src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..summary: Replace per-k ModPow(F[mask], k, MOD) with an incrementally maintained power array, removing the log(k) factor from the dominant loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..currentCost: The k-loop computes ModPow(F[mask], k, MOD) for every k in [0,n] and every mask in [0,2^n): O(n * 2^n * log n) modular multiplications. ModPow does b%=mod, a branch, and a square-and-multiply loop of ~log2(k) iterations each with two 64-bit muls and two %.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..proposedChange: Allocate long* curPow = stackalloc long[size] initialised to 1 (this is F[mask]^0). For each k from 0..n, use curPow[mask] directly as F[mask]^k inside the sum loop, then after using it multiply curPow[mask] = (curPow[mask]*F[mask]) % MOD to advance to exponent k+1. This computes F[mask]^k with one mul/mod per (k,mask) instead of a full ModPow.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..rationale: Drops the inner exponentiation from O(log k) modular muls to amortised O(1) per (k,mask), turning the block from O(n * 2^n * log n) to O(n * 2^n). This is the asymptotically dominant phase of Subset, so the win is real and large for the typical n up to ~20.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..risk: Semantics-preserving: F[mask]^0 = 1 even when F[mask] is 0 (0^0 is treated as 1 here, matching ModPow(0,0,MOD)=1), and ModPow(F[mask],k>0,MOD) with F[mask]=0 gives 0 which the running product also produces. Needs size*8 extra bytes of stackalloc; size = 2^n so memory matches existing F buffer and is fine for the n this brute-force method already requires.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..summary: Replace the bit-by-bit PopCount loop with System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount (single popcnt instruction under Burst).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..currentCost: PopCount shifts and tests one bit per iteration: up to 31 iterations, each a branch, AND, increment, and shift. Called once per mask inside the y[k] loop: n * 2^n invocations.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..proposedChange: Return (int)System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount((uint)mask). Cast to uint is safe because mask is a non-negative subset index < 2^n.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..rationale: BitOperations.PopCount lowers to a single hardware popcnt on x86/ARM under Burst, replacing an ~O(bits) data-dependent branch chain with one instruction; removes a long dependency chain and unpredictable branch.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..risk: Cast to uint required since the intrinsic is defined on unsigned types; mask is always >= 0 here so the bit pattern is identical. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..summary: Hoist popcount out of the k-loop and precompute the (n-pop) sign per mask once, instead of recomputing PopCount for every k.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..currentCost: PopCount(mask) and the (n-pop)%2 parity test are recomputed for every (k,mask) pair = n * 2^n times, though pop depends only on mask.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..proposedChange: Before the k-loop, precompute a sign per mask once (e.g. a byte/sbyte buffer or fold the +/- into curPow handling) using popcount of mask, then in the k-loop just branch on the precomputed sign. Even simpler: track parity incrementally is unnecessary if PopCount is hoisted to a one-time pass over masks.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..rationale: Removes (n-1)*2^n redundant popcount+modulo computations. The sign of each mask is loop-invariant in k.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..risk: Adds a small per-mask buffer (2^n bytes). Behaviour identical. If combined with the curPow change above, ensure the precompute pass runs once before the k-loop.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..summary: stackalloc inside the for-i loop allocates a fresh buffer every iteration; hoist a single max-sized scratch buffer outside the loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..currentCost: long* nextPoly = stackalloc long[polyLen + 1] executes on every iteration of the i-loop (n+1 times). Stack-pointer growth inside a loop is not reclaimed until method return in C#, so this can grow the frame by sum(polyLen+1) ~ O(n^2) longs rather than O(n), and re-zeroes each time.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..proposedChange: Allocate one long* nextPoly = stackalloc long[n + 2] before the loop and reuse it each iteration, zeroing only the [0..polyLen] prefix actually used. Same for any other in-loop stackallocs.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..rationale: Caps stack usage at O(n) longs instead of O(n^2) cumulative, reduces frame size and the risk of stack overflow for larger n, and avoids repeated allocation setup. Burst/IL keeps in-loop stackalloc live for the whole method, so this is a genuine working-set reduction.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..risk: Must zero exactly the prefix that the algorithm reads (0..polyLen) each iteration to preserve the current zero-initialised semantics. polyLen grows to n+1, so buffer size n+2 covers nextPoly[j+1] for j up to polyLen-1.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..summary: Iterate only over set bits of mask and drop the unnecessary long index arithmetic for the adjacency lookup.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..currentCost: Double loop over all i,j in [0,n) testing (mask & (1<<i)) each time, recomputing 1<<i and 1<<j; index computed as (long)i*(long)n+(long)j with three long casts and a 64-bit multiply.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..proposedChange: Loop over set bits: for a copy m=mask, extract lowest set bit i via BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount, then inner-iterate remaining higher set bits; compute index as int i*n+j (no long). Since the whole method requires size=1<<n to fit a positive int (n<=30), i*n+j < n*n <= ~900M fits in int.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..rationale: Skips all clear-bit iterations (work proportional to popcount^2 instead of n^2), eliminates recomputed shifts, and replaces 64-bit index math with 32-bit. Fewer cycles and a shorter dependency chain that Burst handles better.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Chromatic..risk: int index is safe only while n*n stays within int range; n is already bounded by 1<<n being a valid positive int (n<=30), but for n in (23,30] n*n can exceed int max — guard: keep int index only for n<=46340, which always holds here since n<=30 gives max 900M < 2^31. So safe across the entire valid input domain. Same applies to the identical IsIndependentSet in Independence.cs and the adj index in Matching.cs.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Independen.summary: Replace PopCount bit-loop with BitOperations.PopCount and iterate IsIndependentSet over set bits only (same fixes as Chromatic).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Independen.currentCost: Per mask in [0,2^n): IsIndependentSet does n^2 bit tests with recomputed shifts and long index math; PopCount loops bit-by-bit. Hot loop runs 2^n times.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Independen.proposedChange: Use (int)System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount((uint)mask); rewrite IsIndependentSet to walk set bits via TrailingZeroCount and use int i*n+j indexing (n<=30 so product < 2^31).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Independen.rationale: popcnt intrinsic replaces a data-dependent loop; set-bit iteration reduces inner work from n^2 to popcount^2; 32-bit indexing shortens the address-compute chain. All in the 2^n-iteration hot path.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Independen.risk: uint cast for popcount is safe (mask>=0). int index safe for all valid n (n<=30 -> n*n<=900M<2^31). No observable change.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Matching.c.summary: Find the lowest set bit v with BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount instead of a linear scan, and hoist 1<<v.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Matching.c.currentCost: For every mask in [1,2^n), an inner loop scans i=0..n until the first set bit is found (up to n iterations + branch each), recomputing 1<<i each step. This runs ~2^n times.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Matching.c.proposedChange: int v = System.Numerics.BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount((uint)mask); int vbit = 1 << v; int maskWithoutV = mask ^ vbit. mask is always >=1 here so TrailingZeroCount is well-defined (input nonzero).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Matching.c.rationale: Replaces an O(n) branch loop with a single tzcnt/ctz instruction under Burst, removing a variable-length dependency chain from the hot per-mask path; also caches 1<<v.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Matching.c.risk: TrailingZeroCount on uint 0 returns 32, but the loop starts at mask=1 so the argument is always nonzero — safe. uint cast harmless since mask<2^n with n<=30 is positive. adj index (long)v*n+u can also drop to int v*n+u (n<=30 -> <2^31), shaving the 64-bit multiply.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.summary: Precompute power tables of p and q once, replacing per-mask O(edges) probability recomputation and the per-mask bit-count loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.currentCost: CalculateProbability runs two loops totalling O(edges) modular muls for every connected mask, and Run recomputes edgeCount with a bit-by-bit loop per mask. Over 2^edges masks this is O(edges * 2^edges) extra muls plus O(edges * 2^edges) popcount work, all redundant since results depend only on edgeCount in [0,edges].
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.proposedChange: Before the mask loop, precompute qPow[i]=q^i and pPow[i]=p^i for i in [0,edges] (two O(edges) passes). Then per mask use popCnt = (int)BitOperations.PopCount((uint)mask) and prob = (qPow[popCnt]*pPow[edges-popCnt]) % MOD. Note current code multiplies q edgeCount times and p (totalEdges-edgeCount) times, so map accordingly to preserve exact semantics.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.rationale: Reduces the per-mask probability cost from O(edges) to O(1) table lookups plus one mul, cutting total from O(edges*2^edges) to O(2^edges) for the probability work; popcnt intrinsic removes the bit loop. The probability is a pure function of popcount, so caching is exact.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.risk: Must preserve the existing (slightly unusual) mapping: current code raises q to edgeCount and p to totalEdges-edgeCount. Keep that exact assignment in the table lookup. uint popcount cast safe (mask>=0, edges<=30). Table is (edges+1)*8 bytes per array, negligible.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.summary: Add union-by-size/rank and stop re-running Find(parent,0) for the root each iteration; also short-circuit using a component count.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.currentCost: IsConnected rebuilds DSU per mask (O(n) reset) then for the connectivity check calls Find for component count: it computes root=Find(0) then Find(i) for i=1..n-1. Union lacks rank/size so trees can be taller, and the final verification re-Finds every node. Runs 2^edges times.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.proposedChange: Track the number of distinct components while unioning (start at n, decrement on each successful union); the graph is connected iff components==1 after processing edges. This removes the entire final O(n) Find verification loop. Optionally add union-by-size to bound tree height (already have path halving in Find).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.rationale: Eliminates the O(n) post-pass of Find calls per mask (O(n*2^edges) saved) by maintaining component count during union; union-by-size keeps amortised Find near O(alpha). Pure structural improvement to the per-mask hot routine.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Reliabilit.risk: Component-count connectivity is equivalent to the all-same-root check for an undirected graph on n vertices. Must initialise components=n each mask and decrement only when Find(u)!=Find(v). Behaviour identical for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.summary: Precompute a power-of-x table so xPow becomes an O(1) lookup instead of an O(count) loop per valid placement.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.currentCost: For every valid mask, xPow is built by multiplying x together count times: O(count) modular muls, count up to min(n,m). Over up to 2^(n*m) masks this adds O(min(n,m) * 2^(n*m)) redundant muls.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.proposedChange: Before the loop, precompute xPowTable[k]=x^k for k in [0, min(n,m)] (count cannot exceed min(n,m)). Then result = (result + xPowTable[count]) % MOD. count is already returned by IsValidPlacement.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.rationale: Turns the inner exponentiation into a single array load, dropping the dominant placement-counting loop's per-valid-mask cost from O(min(n,m)) to O(1); table build is one cheap O(min(n,m)) pass.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.risk: x is taken mod implicitly via the running product; precompute table the same way ((prev*x)%MOD) to match exactly. Table size min(n,m)+1 longs, tiny. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.summary: Skip cleared mask cells with a set-bit iteration and avoid resetting rowUsed/colUsed fully when few bits are set; also early-out is already present.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.currentCost: For every mask in [0,2^(n*m)), the function clears n+m bool flags then scans all n*m cells testing (mask & (1L<<bit)). Most cells are clear, yet every cell is visited and 1L<<bit is recomputed each step.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.proposedChange: Iterate over set bits of mask via TrailingZeroCount on the 64-bit mask (mask is long): extract each set bit position, derive i=bit/m, j=bit%m (or precompute row/col per bit). This visits only placed rooks (popcount) rather than all n*m cells. Keep the rowUsed/colUsed clears.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.rationale: Reduces inner work from O(n*m) per mask to O(popcount) per mask and removes the recomputed 1L<<bit shift; the conflict/blocked checks then run only on actually-placed cells. Significant since most masks have few set bits on average.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Rook.cs.risk: bit/m and bit%m introduce a divide; if m is not a power of two consider precomputing per-bit (row,col) tables of size n*m to avoid the div, or keep div since it is off the very hottest path. Clearing rowUsed/colUsed still O(n+m) per mask — acceptable. Behaviour identical: same conflict detection, same count. mask is long so use 64-bit TrailingZeroCount ((ulong)mask).

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.summary: Replace the two per-mask ModPow calls with precomputed power tables for x and y, since both exponents are small bounded non-negative integers.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.currentCost: The main loop runs 2^edges iterations, and each iteration calls CalculateTerm which performs two ModPow calls. Each ModPow is an O(log exp) loop of 64-bit multiply+mod. So the inner cost is ~2*2^edges modular exponentiations, dominating runtime (e.g. 256 iterations * 2 modpows for edges=8).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.proposedChange: Before the loop, build two stackalloc tables: long* xPow = stackalloc long[n]; long* yPow = stackalloc long[edges + 1]; fill xPow[0]=1, xPow[i] = (xPow[i-1] * (x mod-normalized)) % MOD for i in 1..n-1, and similarly yPow[0..edges]. Inside the loop replace CalculateTerm's ModPow(x,xExp,..) / ModPow(y,yExp,..) with xPow[xExp] * yPow[yExp] % MOD. Inline xExp/yExp computation (xExp = rkE - rkA, yExp = eCount - rkA).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.rationale: Turns O(2^edges * log(exp)) modular exponentiations into O(n + edges) table setup plus one 64-bit multiply + one mod per mask. The exponents are tiny and highly repeated across masks, so memoizing all reachable powers removes the entire log-exp dependency chain from the hot loop. Cuts the dominant cost by roughly an order of magnitude.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.risk: Requires the exponents to be non-negative and within table bounds. Verified: rkA = n - comps in [0, n-1]; xExp = rkE - rkA in [0, rkE] subset of [0, n-1] because adding edges never increases components (comps >= compsE => rkA <= rkE); yExp = eCount - rkA in [0, edges] because a subgraph's rank rkA <= its edge count eCount and rkA >= 0. So xPow[n] and yPow[edges+1] sizes are sufficient and no negative index occurs. Must normalize base mod MOD (and add MOD if negative) exactly as ModPow does to preserve identical results; x,y are passed as long but the modular reduction must match. Edge case n could be small; xPow needs at least 1 slot (n>=1 guaranteed since stackalloc int[n] already assumes it).

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.summary: Replace the hand-rolled Kernighan PopCount loop with System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount, which Burst and the JIT lower to a single hardware popcnt instruction.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.currentCost: PopCount runs a loop iterating once per set bit (up to edges iterations: m &= m-1; c++), executed once per mask = 2^edges times. Each call is a variable-length, data-dependent branchy loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.proposedChange: Return System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount((uint)m); (m is a mask in [0, 2^edges - 1], always non-negative, so the uint cast is exact). Remove the manual loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.rationale: BitOperations.PopCount is an intrinsic mapping to the POPCNT instruction (Burst recognizes it), replacing a multi-iteration loop with a single fixed-latency, branchless instruction. Removes a data-dependent branch from the hot path and shortens the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.risk: BitOperations.PopCount takes uint/ulong; cast (uint)m is safe because m = mask < 2^edges and edges <= 31 for the 1<<edges size computation to be valid, so m is always non-negative. Behavior identical for all valid inputs. Confirm Burst/target supports BitOperations (it does for popcount); otherwise keep the loop but mark unsigned.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.summary: Hoist the (long)MOD cast and reuse a single modL local; also the compsE/rkE full-graph CountComponents is correct to compute once but the per-mask result modulo and accumulation can avoid repeated casts.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.currentCost: Inside the loop, (long)MOD is recomputed/cast on every iteration in both the accumulation (result + term) % (long)MOD and inside CalculateTerm/ModPow. Repeated widening casts and the redundant module constant materialization add per-iteration overhead across 2^edges iterations.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.proposedChange: Compute long modL = (long)MOD once at the top of Subset and pass/use it everywhere instead of re-casting MOD. Combined with the power-table change, CalculateTerm becomes a tiny inline expression taking modL.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.rationale: Eliminates redundant int->long conversions inside the hottest loop and keeps the modulus in a register. Minor constant-factor win but free and compounds with the table change.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.risk: None; pure refactor, identical arithmetic. Casting MOD once vs many times yields the same value.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.summary: Replace per-mask popcount-style component recount (final loop scanning parent[i]==i) by decrementing a running component counter during unions, removing the second O(n) scan.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.currentCost: Each CountComponents call does: O(n) init, O(edges) union pass with Find, then a separate O(n) scan counting roots (parent[i]==i). The final scan is a full extra pass over parent every call, i.e. 2^edges * n extra reads.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.proposedChange: Initialize int comps = n; in the union pass, when u != v perform the union and decrement comps. Return comps directly, deleting the trailing for-loop that scans for roots. (Union only happens when u != v, which is exactly when two distinct components merge.)
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.rationale: Removes a full O(n) pass per mask, halving the non-union work. Component count is exactly n minus the number of successful unions, which the existing if (u != v) branch already identifies, so the count is maintainable for free inside the existing branch.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.risk: Semantics preserved: a successful union (u != v) reduces distinct components by exactly one; duplicate/self edges (u == v) are skipped and must not decrement. With path-halving Find, roots are correct, so comps stays accurate. Identical result to the root-scan. Negligible risk.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.summary: Iterate masks in Gray-code order to reuse incremental state is NOT applicable (union-find lacks deletion); instead consider that compsE full-graph pass is redundant with mask=size-1 iteration.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.currentCost: compsE is computed via CountComponents(..., size-1, ...) separately, and the loop also evaluates mask = size-1 (the full edge set) inside the main loop, recomputing the same union-find a second time.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.proposedChange: compsE/rkE is needed before the loop for every term, so it must be computed first; but you can skip recomputation when mask == size-1 inside the loop by reusing the already-known compsE (comps for the full mask equals compsE). Branch is cheap (one compare per iteration) but only saves one CountComponents call total, so optionally just leave as-is. Document that Gray-code reuse is impossible because union-find does not support edge deletion.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.rationale: Avoids exactly one redundant CountComponents call (the full-mask one). Marginal at large edge counts; included for completeness so a future reader does not mistakenly attempt Gray-code incremental DSU, which is unsound here.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.GraphPoly/Tutte.cs.risk: Adding a per-iteration branch to save one call is usually not worth it; net could be slightly negative for large 2^edges. Recommend NOT adding the branch and instead leaving compsE computation as the single source. This entry is primarily to flag that the asymptotic 2^edges * (n + edges) bound is essentially tight for the subset-sum Tutte definition; no better asymptotics without switching to deletion-contraction, which changes the algorithm.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.summary: Three stackalloc calls live inside the while(k>0) loop; C# stackalloc is NOT freed per iteration, so the stack grows by (qLen + 2*sz + 2*sz) longs every halving of k until method return.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.currentCost: Per loop iteration: stackalloc long[qLen] + stackalloc long[sz*2] + stackalloc long[sz*2]. The loop runs ~log2(k) times. With k up to 2^62 that is ~62 iterations, each leaking its allocation onto the frame -> ~62*(qLen+4*sz)*8 bytes of stack accumulated. For modest qLen this risks stack overflow and certainly trashes the cache / defeats Burst stack budgeting.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.proposedChange: Hoist all three stackalloc out of the loop, sized once to the worst case: qneg = stackalloc long[qLen]; r = stackalloc long[2*sz]; s = stackalloc long[2*sz] where sz=Max(pLen,qLen) is loop-invariant (pLen and qLen never change across iterations). Reuse the buffers each iteration; FilterPolynomial already writes back into p/q so degrees do not grow.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.rationale: Moving stackalloc above the loop converts O(log k) accumulating allocations into a single fixed-size frame reservation. This bounds stack usage, removes per-iteration frame-pointer arithmetic, and keeps the three buffers hot in cache across iterations. sz, pLen, qLen are provably invariant so one allocation suffices.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.risk: Must confirm pLen/qLen are truly invariant across iterations (they are: only the contents of p and q are overwritten, not the lengths). r and s must be zero-initialized or fully written by ToomCook.Multiply before FilterPolynomial reads them; if Multiply does not clear the upper region, add a clear or rely on existing FilterPolynomial bounds check (parity+2*i < len+sz) which already guards reads. Behavior is otherwise identical.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.summary: Parity tests use signed % 2 on non-negative values where & 1 is exact and cheaper, and 2*i can be strength-reduced.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.currentCost: (i % 2 == 0) in the qneg build, (int)(k % 2L) for parity, and 2*i recomputed inside FilterPolynomial's loop. Signed % by 2 emits sign-correction sequences in IL/JIT vs a single AND.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.proposedChange: Replace (i % 2 == 0) with ((i & 1) == 0); replace (int)(k % 2L) with ((int)k & 1) (k>0 here so non-negative); in FilterPolynomial track an additive index idx = parity, stepping idx += 2 per iteration instead of computing parity + 2*i.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.rationale: i and k are non-negative in these contexts, so & 1 is semantically identical to % 2 but branch/sign-correction free. Incrementing idx removes a multiply per element from the inner filter loop and shortens the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/BostanMor.risk: k is loop-guarded > 0 and i is a non-negative loop counter, so & 1 preserves semantics exactly (the signed-vs-unsigned % caveat does not apply). No behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.summary: Flat index arithmetic recomputes (long)row*(long)n + (long)col with 64-bit multiplies in every inner-loop iteration; row-base offsets are loop-invariant and the casts to long are unnecessary since n*n already fits in int (stackalloc long[(int)(n*n)] requires n*n < 2^31).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.currentCost: Inner Gaussian-elimination loop (lines 91-104) computes (long)r*(long)n+(long)j and (long)rank*(long)n+(long)j for every j with full 64-bit imul. The rank*n term is invariant across j; r*n is invariant across j. Same pattern in BuildQMatrix, SwapRows, ExtractBasis.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.proposedChange: Precompute int row-base offsets once per row (int rankBase = rank*n; int rBase = r*n;) and index Q[rBase + j], Q[rankBase + j]. Use pointer walks (long* rowR = Q + rBase; long* rowRank = Q + rankBase;) to drop the index multiply entirely from the j loop. Since n*n fits in int, use int index math throughout instead of (long) casts.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.rationale: Hoisting r*n / rank*n out of the j loop removes a multiply per element from the hottest loop of the O(n^3) reduction. Pointer-stride access is Burst-vectorization-friendly and shortens the address-dependency chain. int math avoids 64-bit imul on mobile where it can be multi-cycle.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.risk: stackalloc long[(int)byteCount] already casts n*n to int, so n*n < 2^31 is a precondition of the existing code; int index math is therefore safe and preserves behavior. Pure address-computation refactor, no numeric change.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.summary: Inner elimination does (Q[rjIdx] - (factor*Q[rankjIdx]) % MOD + MOD) % MOD with two divisions (modulo) per element; the pivot-row normalization plus per-element double-% can be reduced.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.currentCost: Line 101 performs two 64-bit % MOD per inner iteration (one on the product, one on the final result) -> 2 divisions per element across the O(n^3) loop. Division is the most expensive integer op, especially on mobile ARM where there is no hardware 64-bit divide.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.proposedChange: Since factor and Q[rankjIdx] are both already reduced into [0,MOD), and MOD fits in int, the product factor*Q[rankjIdx] < MOD^2 < 2^62 cannot overflow long. Compute t = (Q[rjIdx] - (factor*Q[rankjIdx]) % MOD); then a single branchless add-if-negative (t += (t >> 63) & MOD) instead of (+ MOD) % MOD. This drops the outer modulo to a conditional add.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.rationale: (x + MOD) % MOD where x in (-MOD, MOD) is exactly the branchless 'add MOD if negative'. Replacing a 64-bit division with a shift+and+add removes one of the two divisions per element in the hottest loop. The arithmetic-shift mask (t>>63) is branchless and Burst-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.risk: Requires factor and the rank-row entries to be in [0,MOD) (they are after normalization on lines 85-89) so the inner % keeps the product term in [0,MOD) and the subtraction result stays in (-MOD, MOD). MOD must fit in 31 bits so MOD^2 < 2^62 (it is an int). If MOD could be > ~3e9 this guard fails; for int MOD it is safe.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.summary: The transpose loop (lines 50-63) effectively copies column i into row i via a tmp buffer that is fully zeroed each outer iteration; the per-j tmp[i] accumulation is degenerate (only tmp[i] is ever written) so the structure is over-complicated and does redundant zeroing.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.currentCost: For each i: zero all n tmp entries (line 52), then accumulate Q[j*n+i] into tmp[i] for all j with a % MOD per add (lines 53-57, though only tmp[i] is touched), then write tmp back to row i (lines 58-62). The tmp zeroing of all n entries plus writing n entries when only one column is read is wasteful.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.proposedChange: This block transposes Q in place. Replace with a direct in-place transpose swapping Q[i*n+j] with Q[j*n+i] for j>i (single pass, no tmp buffer, no zeroing, no modulo since entries are already reduced). If the intent is genuinely a transpose, the stackalloc long[n] tmp and its O(n) zeroing per row are eliminated.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.rationale: An in-place transpose is O(n^2/2) swaps with zero modulo ops and zero scratch, versus the current O(n^2) reads + O(n^2) zeroing + O(n^2) writes + O(n^2) modulo. Removes the n-long stackalloc entirely.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.risk: Must verify the loop's true intent is a transpose (the accumulation onto tmp[i] with %MOD over already-reduced values is identity, so it is). If any aliasing semantics differ for non-reduced inputs, keep the %MOD; but since BuildQMatrix produced reduced entries above, a plain swap preserves values. Validate against existing NUnit tests before landing.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.summary: stackalloc long[(int)byteCount] for the n-by-n Q matrix plus inner stackalloc long[n] buffers in BuildQMatrix/ExtractBasis push O(n^2) longs onto the stack; on mobile this can exceed the thread stack for moderate n and the (int) cast silently truncates if n*n >= 2^31.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.currentCost: Q is n^2 longs = 8*n^2 bytes on the stack (n=256 -> 512KB, overflowing typical 256KB-1MB thread stacks). BuildQMatrix and ExtractBasis add further n-long stackallocs. The (int)byteCount cast can wrap negative for large n with no guard.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.proposedChange: Either document/assert an upper bound on n (named const MAX_N) so the stack budget is provable, or accept a caller-provided scratch pointer (T* workspace) following the library's unmanaged-pointer convention so the O(n^2) buffer can be pooled/persisted rather than re-stackalloc'd per call. Hoist BuildQMatrix's tmp out as part of the same workspace.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.rationale: Moving the O(n^2) buffer off the stack into caller-owned memory removes stack-overflow risk on mobile, enables reuse across calls (no repeated zero-init of n^2 entries), and makes the function's memory footprint explicit and Burst-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.risk: API change (adds a workspace parameter) -- an ergonomics/signature shift; must keep the unchecked Run contract. Purely additive if a workspace overload is introduced alongside the existing one. No numeric behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.summary: Modular reduction uses % MOD per multiply-accumulate in the two hot inner loops where a single deferred reduction or branchless correction would halve the division count.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.currentCost: CalculateDiscrepancy does d = (d + c[j]*s[i-j]) % MOD every j -> one 64-bit division per term. UpdateCoefficients does c[idx] = (c[idx] - (factor*b[j]) % MOD + MOD) % MOD -> two divisions per term. Divisions dominate on ARM.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.proposedChange: In UpdateCoefficients replace the outer (...+MOD)%MOD with branchless add-if-negative: long t = c[idx] - (factor*b[j])%MOD; c[idx] = t + ((t>>63)&MOD). In CalculateDiscrepancy, if MOD^2*L fits in long (i.e. MOD < ~2^31 and L bounded so the running sum < 2^63), accumulate without per-term % and reduce once at the end; otherwise keep per-term but drop to single % since c[j]*s[i-j] with reduced inputs < MOD^2 < 2^62 needs no intermediate correction.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.rationale: Deferring/eliminating the second modulo converts a 64-bit divide into a shift+and+add. CalculateDiscrepancy can batch reductions when the accumulator provably stays below 2^63, cutting L divisions down to one per discrepancy.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.risk: Batching in CalculateDiscrepancy requires sum of up to L terms each < MOD^2 to stay < 2^63: needs L*MOD^2 < 2^63. With int MOD ~2^31 this allows only L up to ~2, so batching is generally unsafe -- instead just guarantee c[j], s[] are pre-reduced into [0,MOD) so a single % per term suffices (the current code already keeps them reduced). The UpdateCoefficients branchless correction is always safe given factor,b[j] in [0,MOD).

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.summary: CopyArray and InitArrays iterate to n with per-element loops; these are memcpy/memset-shaped and the CopyArray(c,tmp,n) on every nonzero discrepancy copies n+1 longs even though only indices [0..L] are meaningful.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.currentCost: CopyArray copies n+1 longs each call; called once per nonzero discrepancy plus once per length-increase. Since only c[0..L] are nonzero, copying the full n+1 each time is up to O(n) wasted per step -> O(n^2) total in the worst case.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.proposedChange: Bound the copy by the live degree: copy only L+1 (or current max degree) entries into tmp, and copy L+1 from tmp into b on the length-update branch. Track the actual populated length instead of always using n. For the bulk zero/copy of full arrays, these are vectorizable element loops Burst will SIMD, so keep the loop form but shrink the count.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.rationale: Reducing copy length from n+1 to L+1 cuts the per-step copy cost proportional to current recurrence length, which is typically far below n early in the scan, lowering the constant factor of the O(n^2) algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Berlekamp.risk: Must ensure b is consulted only up to its populated length in UpdateCoefficients (it iterates j<=L using the L captured at copy time) -- the b[j] for j>copied-length must be zero. Since arrays start zeroed and only [0..L] are written, copying L+1 leaves higher indices at their prior (zero) value only if they were never dirtied; safest is to copy max(prevL, L)+1. Verify against tests.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/DivMod.cs.summary: Inner subtraction loop recomputes the base index i-(lenB-1) every j and applies (... - sub + MOD) % MOD with a modulo where a branchless correction suffices since sub is already reduced.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/DivMod.cs.currentCost: Line 50: temp[i-(lenB-1)+j] = (temp[...] - sub + MOD) % MOD computes i-(lenB-1) per iteration and one 64-bit % per element across the O(lenA*lenB) loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/DivMod.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int base = i-(lenB-1) outside the j loop (or walk a pointer long* row = temp + (i-(lenB-1))). Replace (x - sub + MOD) % MOD with long t = temp[base+j] - sub; temp[base+j] = t + ((t>>63)&MOD), branchless since sub=(q_i*b[j])%MOD is in [0,MOD) and temp entries are in [0,MOD) so t in (-MOD,MOD).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/DivMod.cs.rationale: Removes a repeated subtraction-and-multiply for the index from the inner loop and converts a 64-bit divide to a shift+and+add per element, the dominant cost on mobile. Pointer walk is Burst-vectorization-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/DivMod.cs.risk: Requires temp[*] and sub in [0,MOD); temp is reduced on each update and sub is explicitly %MOD, so t in (-MOD,MOD) and the branchless add-if-negative is exact. q_i*b[j] < MOD^2 < 2^62 for int MOD (no overflow). Safe for int MOD.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.summary: Use Horner's method to halve modular multiplications and shorten the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.currentCost: Per iteration the loop does two 64-bit multiplies and two % MOD reductions: one for poly[i]*xPow and one to advance xPow = xPow*x. That is 2 muls + 2 mods over n iterations, plus the xPow accumulator is a serial dependency that runs in parallel to val.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.proposedChange: Evaluate from the high coefficient down using Horner: long val = 0L; long m = (long)MOD; for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) { val = (val * x + poly[i]) % m; } return val; This removes xPow entirely.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.rationale: Horner does exactly one multiply and one reduction per coefficient (1 mul + 1 mod vs 2+2), eliminates the separate xPow running-product state, and produces a single tight recurrence that Burst can schedule without the second parallel chain. Net ~2x fewer modular ops.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.risk: Result is mathematically identical for all inputs (same polynomial value mod MOD). Requires poly coefficients already reduced into [0,MOD) as the current code assumes (val*x stays < MOD*MOD < 2^63 for MOD up to ~3.0e9, matching the existing accumulation which already relies on poly[i]*xPow < 2^63). No signedness/overflow change versus current code.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.summary: Hoist the (long)MOD cast out of the loop body.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.currentCost: Each iteration casts the int MOD to long for the % operation; even if cheap, it is re-materialized each pass and the int parameter forces sign-extension at every use.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.proposedChange: Cache long m = (long)MOD; once before the loop and use m inside (already folded into the Horner rewrite above).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.rationale: Removes repeated sign-extension materialization and gives the JIT/Burst a single invariant register operand.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/OfflineQu.risk: None; pure invariant hoist, identical semantics.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant m12 % MOD out of the per-element loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.currentCost: Inside the n-iteration loop, result[i] = (a12 + (m12 % (long)MOD) * k3) % (long)MOD recomputes m12 % (long)MOD every iteration, and casts MOD to long twice per iteration. m12, MOD are all loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.proposedChange: Before the loop compute long m = (long)MOD; long m12modM = m12 % m; then result[i] = (a12 + m12modM * k3) % m;. Also hoist the cast of MOD once.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.rationale: Removes one 64-bit division (the % m12) and two sign-extensions from every iteration of the hot CRT combine loop; a 64-bit div is ~20-40 cycles, so this is a large constant-factor win over n elements.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.risk: m12 % MOD is constant across i, so hoisting is exact. m12 = MOD1*MOD2 = 998244353*985661441 fits in long (~9.8e17 < 2^63), so no overflow introduced. Semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.summary: Drop the redundant a1 % m2 reduction when a1 is a residue mod MOD1 < m2.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.currentCost: k2 computes (a2 - a1 % m2 + m2) % m2. a1 is an NTT residue mod MOD1 (998244353) and m2 = MOD2 = 985661441 < MOD1, so a1 % m2 is needed in general. But a3 - a12 % m3: a12 = a1 + m1*k2 can exceed m3, so that one is required.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.proposedChange: Leave a1 % m2 as-is (it is genuinely needed since MOD1 > MOD2). Reject the a1%m2 removal. However, the trailing reductions chain (% m2, % m3) each include an add-then-mod that can use the branchless conditional-subtract form: since (a2 - a1%m2) is in (-m2, m2), replace (x + m2) % m2 with a branchless add-back: long t = a2 - (a1 % m2); t += (t >> 63) & m2; using arithmetic shift to add m2 only when negative.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.rationale: Replaces a 64-bit modulo (after the +m2) with a sign-mask conditional add, eliminating one division on the dependency-critical path per element. (t >> 63) is all-ones when t<0, all-zeros otherwise, so & m2 adds m2 iff negative. Same trick applies to the (a3 - a12%m3 + m3) % m3 numerator before multiplying by inv12.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Ntt.cs.risk: Valid only because a2 - a1%m2 lies in (-m2, m2): both a2 and a1%m2 are in [0,m2), so the difference is in (-m2,m2) and a single add-back fully normalizes. For the m3 term, a3 in [0,m3) and a12%m3 in [0,m3), difference in (-m3,m3), single add-back suffices. Right-shift of signed long is arithmetic in C#/.NET (guaranteed), so >> 63 is portable. Must keep these as the *pre-multiply* normalization; the post-multiply * inv1 % m2 still needs its real modulo.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.summary: Right-size the q/r scratch buffers; remainder length is bounded by lenV, not Max(lenA,lenB)+1.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.currentCost: Two stackalloc buffers of Math.Max(lenA,lenB)+1 longs each are allocated for q and r. In the Euclidean loop the quotient degree is lenU-lenV+1 and remainder degree < lenV, both bounded by max(lenA,lenB). The +1 padding and Max sizing are conservatively correct but the stack footprint is 2*(max+1)*8 bytes held for the whole call.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.proposedChange: Keep q sized to Math.Max(lenA,lenB)+1 (quotient can reach that), but the combined u/v/q/r stack usage can be reduced by noting r never exceeds lenB initially; more importantly, document the bound. If stack pressure matters on mobile, the four buffers (u,v,q,r) total ~4*max longs; consider reusing q's space across iterations (already done) — no change needed unless mobile stack is tight.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.rationale: On mobile, deep stackalloc in an AggressiveInlining method that may be inlined into a caller already holding large stackallocs risks stack overflow; tightening r to lenB and keeping q at max+1 trims one buffer's worst case.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.risk: Quotient length in DivMod can be lenU-lenV+1 which for the first division is lenA-lenV+1 <= lenA, so q must remain max-sized. Only r can be safely capped at lenB (initial divisor length) since subsequent remainders shrink. Verify DivMod.Run never writes past lenB into r before applying; if unsure, leave as-is. Low confidence without DivMod's exact write contract.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.summary: Hoist the (long)MOD cast in the normalization loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.currentCost: The final normalization loop does gcd[i] = (u[i]*inv) % (long)MOD with the int->long cast inside the loop, and ModInv is called with (long)MOD cast separately.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.proposedChange: long m = (long)MOD; once, reuse in ModInv call and the loop: gcd[i] = (u[i] * inv) % m;
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.rationale: Single invariant register operand instead of per-iteration sign-extension; trivial but free.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.summary: Fuse the a -= t*b then swap into the canonical single-temp extended-Euclid form to cut register shuffles.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.currentCost: The loop uses an explicit tmp variable twice and computes a -= t*b before swapping, doing the division t=a/b and then a separate multiply t*b. Standard form computes both quotient and remainder structurally.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.proposedChange: Use: while (b != 0) { long t = a / b; long na = a - t*b; a = b; b = na; long nu = u - t*v; u = v; v = nu; } This removes the tmp aliasing and lets the compiler keep values in registers; optionally use a single divrem if available. Note loop condition can be b != 0L since b stays non-negative here.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.rationale: Fewer named temporaries and a cleaner data-flow graph; the compiler emits one idiv producing quotient and the remainder is the cheap a-t*b. Marginal but removes the double-tmp pattern.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Gcd.cs.risk: b > 0 vs b != 0: in this Euclid b stays non-negative (remainders of positive mod), so b != 0 is equivalent; keep b > 0L if any chance b goes negative. Behavior otherwise identical.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.summary: Skip the final redundant base-squaring after the top exponent bit is consumed.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.currentCost: The loop unconditionally squares basePoly (ToomCook.Multiply + ComputeEffectiveLength + DivMod.Run) every iteration including the last, after the highest set bit has already been multiplied into result. That final square-and-reduce is a full polynomial multiply + division whose output is never used.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.proposedChange: Guard the squaring step: after exponent >>= 1, only square if exponent > 0L. e.g. exponent >>= 1; if (exponent == 0L) break; before the basePoly self-multiply, or move the squaring to the top of the next iteration. Equivalent: restructure to multiply-into-result first, test/shift, break when exponent hits 0, square only when more bits remain.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.rationale: Eliminates one of the most expensive operations in the whole routine (a ToomCook multiply plus a polynomial DivMod) on every PowMod call. For exponents with the top bit anywhere, the last square is pure waste; this is a guaranteed full-multiply saving per call.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.risk: Must ensure result has already absorbed the final bit before breaking. The odd-bit multiply happens at loop top using current basePoly, so breaking after the shift when exponent==0 is safe and preserves output exactly. No semantic change for any exponent >= 1.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.summary: Reuse a single scratch buffer instead of separate q and temp where lifetimes do not overlap.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.currentCost: Four stackalloc buffers of (lenModPoly*2+1) longs each: basePoly, q, r, temp. q and temp are both transient scratch within each step; q holds a quotient that is discarded immediately (only r is used as the reduced result).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.proposedChange: Since the quotient q is never read after DivMod (only r feeds back), q and temp can share storage if DivMod does not need them simultaneously distinct — but DivMod.Run takes temp(dividend), q(quotient out), r(remainder out) concurrently, so they must be distinct during the call. Keep distinct. Instead, narrow buffer sizing: temp only needs lenResult+lenBase-1 and lenBase+lenBase-1 worst cases, both <= 2*lenModPoly-1, so size 2*lenModPoly (drop the +1) is sufficient — saves 4 longs total and is clearer.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.rationale: Minor stack reduction on a hot recursive-ish routine; the main value is correct tight sizing on mobile stack.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.risk: Confirm DivMod/ToomCook never write the +1 guard slot. If any writes the index 2*lenModPoly (e.g., a degree-2k product term), the +1 is load-bearing — in that case leave as-is. Low confidence without ToomCook output-length contract; flag rather than apply blindly.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.summary: ComputeEffectiveLength after every multiply scans from the top for trailing zeros; pass the known exact product length to avoid the scan when no reduction needed.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.currentCost: After each ToomCook.Multiply the code calls ComputeEffectiveLength over the full product span (lenResult+lenBase-1), a backward scan that in the common dense case finds no leading zeros and walks at most a few elements, but is invoked twice per loop iteration.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.proposedChange: If ToomCook guarantees a normalized (no trailing-zero high coefficient) product for nonzero operands, the trim is unnecessary and the exact length lenResult+lenBase-1 can be used directly. Otherwise keep it. Confirm ToomCook's normalization contract.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.rationale: Removes a redundant O(degree) trailing-zero scan per multiply when the product is structurally dense (high coeff = product of two nonzero leading coeffs mod MOD, which is nonzero unless a zero-divisor arises mod composite MOD).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/PowMod.cs.risk: Mod a composite MOD, leading-coeff product can be 0 even with nonzero factors, so trimming IS needed there. Only safe to drop when MOD is prime. Since MOD is a runtime int (possibly composite), keep the trim. Reject for general MOD; viable only behind a prime-MOD precondition.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.summary: Avoid re-indexing offsets[levelStart + i] / sizes[levelStart + i] multiple times per node.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.currentCost: In the paired branch, offsets[levelStart + i] and offsets[levelStart + i + 1] are read for the ToomCook pointer args while sizes are read separately into sa/sb; in the odd branch offsets[levelStart+i] and sizes[levelStart+i] are each indexed once. The levelStart+i address arithmetic is recomputed for each separate array access.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.proposedChange: Hoist the base index once: int li = levelStart + i; then use offsets[li], offsets[li+1], sizes[li], sizes[li+1]. Load offsets[li]/offsets[li+1] into locals oa, ob and pass tree + oa, tree + ob to ToomCook.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.rationale: Removes redundant integer add for the base index and lets the compiler keep the offsets in registers across the multiply-arg setup; fewer reloads from the offsets/sizes arrays.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.risk: None; pure CSE of index arithmetic, identical semantics.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.summary: Strength-reduce the i*2 indexing in the leaf-initialization loop to an additive stride.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.currentCost: The leaf loop computes i*2 three times per iteration (offsets[nodeCount]=i*2, tree[i*2], tree[i*2+1]). i*2 is a shift but it is recomputed and the two tree writes index i*2 and i*2+1 separately.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.proposedChange: Maintain int two_i = 0; incrementing two_i += 2 each iteration; use offsets[i] = two_i; tree[two_i] = (MOD - values[i] % MOD) % MOD; tree[two_i + 1] = 1; (nodeCount == i here so use i directly for offsets/sizes index).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.rationale: Replaces repeated multiply/shift with a single add per iteration and makes the two adjacent tree stores share a base pointer, friendlier to write-combining. nodeCount equals i throughout this loop so it can be dropped in favor of i, removing an increment.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ProductTr.risk: nodeCount must still end at n for the subsequent level loop; setting nodeCount = n after the loop preserves that. Semantics identical. The (MOD - values[i]%MOD)%MOD already correctly handles values[i] in [0,MOD) producing the monic linear factor's constant term; unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..summary: Replace power-accumulation evaluation with Horner's method to halve the multiplies and shorten the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..currentCost: Per coefficient the loop does two multiplies (poly[i]*xPow and xPow*x) and two %, plus it carries an extra xPow state register. Each iteration's xPow depends on the previous xPow (serial mul+mod dependency chain) AND val depends on poly[i]*xPow, so there are two parallel mod-chains of length n.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..proposedChange: Evaluate as val = (val*x + poly[i]) % MOD iterating i from n-1 down to 0: long val = 0; for (int i = n-1; i >= 0; i--) val = (val * x + poly[i]) % MOD; return val<0? val+MOD: val. This removes the xPow variable entirely, doing one multiply + one add + one mod per term.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..rationale: Horner does n multiplies and n mods instead of 2n multiplies and 2n mods, removing the second multiply/mod dependency chain and one live register. On Burst this is a tighter, more vectorization-friendly reduction with fewer latency-bound mod ops (mod/div is the dominant cost here).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..risk: Inputs are reduced mod MOD only at the end of each step; products poly[i]*x*... must not overflow long. Same overflow envelope as the existing code (both assume coefficients and x kept < MOD with MOD small enough that a*b fits in long). Preserves output for all valid inputs; if any poly[i] could be negative the final non-negative normalization keeps result in [0,MOD) matching nothing currently (current code can return negative), so only add normalization if callers expect [0,MOD).

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..summary: Brute-force scan of all x in [0,MOD) is O(MOD * n); for finding all roots over a prime field this is the worst possible asymptotics when MOD is large.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..currentCost: The outer loop tries every field element 0..MOD-1, evaluating an n-term polynomial each time -> O(MOD*n) mod-multiplications. For MOD ~ 1e9 this is intractable; even for moderate MOD it dominates everything.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..proposedChange: For full root enumeration over GF(MOD), use the standard equal-degree / Cantor-Zassenhaus approach: compute gcd(poly, x^MOD - x) to isolate the product of linear factors, then split via gcd(poly, (x+r)^((MOD-1)/2) - 1). This is polynomial in deg(poly)*log(MOD) instead of linear in MOD. Keep the brute-force path only as a fallback for tiny MOD (e.g. MOD <= some threshold where MOD < deg*log(MOD)).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..rationale: Replaces O(MOD) field scanning with O(deg^2 * log MOD) factor-finding, an enormous asymptotic improvement for large prime moduli — the intended hard case. The library already has Gcd/DivMod/PowMod-style primitives (SquareFree uses Gcd.Run, DivMod.Run), so the building blocks exist.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RootFind..risk: Cantor-Zassenhaus is randomized and requires MOD prime; the brute force works for any MOD and is deterministic. Provide the fast path only when MOD is known prime and large, with the existing scan as fallback, to preserve current semantics for composite/small MOD. Larger implementation effort and needs careful testing.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.summary: Use Horner's method for the per-value polynomial remainder instead of accumulating xPow.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.currentCost: Inner loop over polyLen does two multiplies (poly[j]*xPow, xPow*v) and two mods per coefficient, with two serial mod dependency chains, across n outer iterations -> O(n*polyLen) with a 2x constant on the expensive mod.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.proposedChange: For each value v compute r via Horner: long r = 0; for (int j = polyLen-1; j >= 0; j--) r = (r * v + poly[j]) % MOD; This drops the xPow register and one multiply+mod per inner step.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.rationale: Halves multiply and mod count in the hottest inner loop and eliminates a parallel dependency chain plus a live register, improving ILP and cache/register pressure under Burst. Same asymptotics, ~2x constant-factor win on the mod-bound path.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.risk: poly[j] is multiplied into r before reduction; products must fit in long, identical overflow envelope to current xPow*v and poly[j]*xPow products. v is pre-normalized to [0,MOD) as before. Output identical for valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.summary: MOD parameter is int but arithmetic promotes to long repeatedly; widen MOD to long for consistency with sibling APIs (RootFind, RationalInterpolation use mixed int/long).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.currentCost: Each (r + poly[j]*xPow) % MOD and xPow*v % MOD promotes the int MOD to long every iteration (sign-extend), and the API is inconsistent with RationalInterpolation which takes long MOD.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.proposedChange: Change signature to take long MOD (matching RationalInterpolation.Run), removing the repeated int->long conversions and unifying the module's modulus type.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.rationale: Eliminates per-iteration implicit widening and makes the module's modular-arithmetic APIs uniform, aiding discoverability and reducing accidental int-overflow when callers pass a near-2^31 modulus.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Remainder.risk: Pure signature change; callers must pass long. No behavioral change for moduli that already fit in int. Verify all call sites updated.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.summary: Simplify the per-element difference-quotient expression: ModInv already returns a value in [0,MOD), so the extra '% MOD + MOD' reductions are redundant and add ops plus risk a needless extra-wide product.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.currentCost: Line 40 computes (den % MOD + MOD) * (inv % MOD + MOD) % MOD. inv is already in [0,MOD) from ModInv, so 'inv % MOD + MOD' is a wasted mod, add, and pushes the operand up to ~2*MOD, making the product up to ~4*MOD^2 before the final mod. den is also already a small signed value.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.proposedChange: Normalize den once: long dn = den % MOD; if (dn < 0) dn += MOD; then diffs[i] = dn * inv % MOD; (inv is already non-negative and < MOD). This removes two %/+ ops on inv and one on den per element and halves the pre-reduction product magnitude.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.rationale: Fewer mod/add ops per inner element and a smaller intermediate product reduce both cycle count and overflow headroom usage on the inner Thiele pass (which runs O(n^2) total). Mod is the costly op so dropping one per element is a real win.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.risk: Must confirm ModInv's contract: it returns t in [0,MOD) (it normalizes t<0) except the -1 sentinel on non-invertible input. If inv could be -1 (num not coprime to MOD), current code turns it into (-1%MOD+MOD)=MOD-1 silently; the proposed form would use -1 directly, changing behavior on that error path. Guard: keep current handling only if -1 sentinel is reachable, otherwise the simplification is exact. Also den is signed so the dn<0 normalization is required (do not use & here).

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.summary: Hoist the per-iteration stackalloc of 'diffs' out of the while loop and drop the redundant second copy of y into local c.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.currentCost: 'long* diffs = stackalloc long[m-1]' is inside the while loop (lines 34) — stackalloc in a loop either re-bumps the stack pointer each iteration or, more importantly, is a code-smell that can defeat Burst and grows frame reasoning. Also lines 26-27 copy y into a fresh local c[] even though Run already passed a writable copy (c in Run) as y; that is a duplicate n-element buffer and copy.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.proposedChange: Allocate one scratch buffer once before the loop sized [n-1] (max needed) and reuse it each iteration: long* diffs = stackalloc long[n]; Reuse across iterations since only the first m-1 entries are touched. Separately, evaluate whether the local c in ThieleInterpolation can be removed by operating in-place on y (Run passes a private copy already), saving an n-long stackalloc and the copy loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.rationale: Single stackalloc keeps a fixed, Burst-friendly frame and removes per-iteration stack manipulation; eliminating the duplicate c buffer + copy removes an O(n) RAM allocation and an O(n) copy. Lower working set helps mobile cache/stack budgets.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.risk: Reusing diffs is safe because each iteration fully overwrites entries [0,m-2) before reading. Removing c requires confirming Run's 'c' (its stackalloc copy of ys) is exclusively owned and not needed afterward — Run does not read c after the call, so in-place mutation is safe. Verify no aliasing between x and y.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.summary: Track only t and the two r values; newT/t update is fine, but the unconditional 'a % MOD' on entry can be skipped when caller already supplies reduced input, and the final r>1 sentinel branch is on the cold path.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.currentCost: Extended-Euclid loop has a division q = r/newR plus two multiply-subtracts per step (unavoidable), but the entry 'newR = a % MOD; if(newR<0) newR+=MOD' adds a mod+branch even when callers (Thiele) pass num = x[nxt+i]-x[i] which can be large/negative — so the reduction IS needed there. No safe removal without caller guarantee.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.proposedChange: Keep the algorithm; mark ModInv with AggressiveInlining (already present) and ensure the q*newT and q*newR share the single division result (they already do). Optionally compute q once and reuse — already done. Net: this function is essentially optimal; only note that if a caller guarantees 0<=a<MOD the entry reduction can be elided via a separate ModInvReduced overload.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.rationale: Extended Euclidean GCD is asymptotically optimal for modular inverse here; the only constant-factor lever is skipping the entry reduction, which requires a caller contract. Documenting a reduced-input overload avoids one mod+branch per inverse on hot O(n) Thiele inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/RationalI.risk: Removing the entry reduction is only valid if a is guaranteed in [0,MOD); Thiele's num can be negative, so the general ModInv must keep it. Provide the elision only as a separate clearly-named overload to preserve correctness.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/SquareFre.summary: Remove redundant (long) casts and reorder the derivative computation to reduce one mod per term.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/SquareFre.currentCost: Line 17: deriv[i-1] = ((long)i % (long)MOD * poly[i]) % (long)MOD does two mods per coefficient and casts i and MOD to long repeatedly. The (long)MOD casts are redundant once one operand is long; '(long)i % MOD' is usually i itself since i < lenPoly is typically << MOD.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/SquareFre.proposedChange: Compute deriv[i-1] = (long)i * poly[i] % MOD; (single mod). i is a small loop index that fits in long; only reduce i mod MOD if lenPoly can exceed MOD, which it cannot for a degree-<MOD polynomial. Drop the explicit (long) on MOD since the left operand is already long.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/SquareFre.rationale: Saves one mod per derivative coefficient and removes superfluous sign-extension casts, tightening an O(lenPoly) setup loop. Single multiply-then-mod is the standard modular form.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/SquareFre.risk: '(long)i % MOD' differs from 'i' only when i >= MOD; for a polynomial reduced mod MOD the degree (lenPoly-1) is < MOD by construction, so i < MOD and the inner mod is a no-op — safe to drop. If callers can pass lenPoly > MOD, keep the i%MOD. (long)i*poly[i] must fit in long: i < MOD and poly[i] < MOD, same envelope as existing code's intermediate.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Schonhage.summary: This class is a misnomer and a thin pass-through to ToomCook.Multiply; it adds an indirection layer and an inaccurate name with no algorithmic content.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Schonhage.currentCost: Multiply just forwards to ToomCook.Multiply(a,n,b,n,result,MOD). The AggressiveInlining likely elides the call, so no runtime cost, but the name promises an O(n log n) Schonhage-Strassen / NTT path while delivering Toom-Cook (~O(n^1.46)). For large n this is an asymptotic gap hidden behind the API.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Schonhage.proposedChange: Either (a) delete this wrapper and have callers use ToomCook directly, or (b) if the library intends an NTT-based multiplication for large n, implement a real number-theoretic transform here with a degree threshold that dispatches Toom-Cook below and NTT above. At minimum rename/comment so the name matches behavior.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Schonhage.rationale: Removes a misleading indirection and, if a true NTT is added, gives genuine O(n log n) for large-degree products versus Toom-Cook's super-linear exponent — a real asymptotic improvement for the large-n regime this class name targets.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/Schonhage.risk: Pure pass-through removal is API-breaking for callers of SchonhageStrassen.Multiply; do behind a deprecation. Implementing real NTT is a larger change requiring a suitable prime/root and correctness validation; only pursue if large-n inputs are expected. No semantics change if merely renamed/documented.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..summary: Hoist a[i] and the (long)MOD widening out of the inner loop so they stay in registers.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..currentCost: Inner loop runs result[i+j]=(result[i+j]+a[i]*b[j])%(long)MOD. a[i] is re-referenced and (long)MOD is sign-extended every j iteration of the O(lenA*lenB) hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..proposedChange: Before the j loop: long ai = a[i]; long mod = (long)MOD; then use ai and mod in the body. The % stays per-term (required).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..rationale: Removes a redundant load and the int->long sign-extension from the dominant inner loop, shortening the dependency chain and freeing registers for Burst.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..risk: None; pure invariant hoist, identical results. (Pre-existing: a[i]*b[j] can overflow long for large MOD per the unchecked caller contract; unchanged.)

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..summary: Fuse the separate zero-init pass into the multiply pass to stream result[] once instead of twice.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..currentCost: One full pass writes resultLen zeros, then the multiply pass read-modify-writes the same cells: result[] is touched by two memory streams of up to lenA+lenB-1 longs.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..proposedChange: Seed result via direct stores from the first non-zero a-row instead of a +0 accumulate, zeroing only indices that row does not cover, so each result cell is written once. Conservative fallback: keep the zero loop if a[0] may be zero.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..rationale: Halves cache traffic over result[], which matters on bandwidth-limited mobile targets.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..risk: Correctness depends on every result index being zeroed before its first accumulate; rows skipped by a[i]==0 must not leave cells uninitialized. The direct-store seed only works when the seed row is non-zero, so it must be guarded; otherwise keep the zero pass.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..summary: Restructure to one modulo per output coefficient instead of one per term, when accumulator overflow is provably bounded.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..currentCost: An integer division (% ~20-40 cycles) executes for every (i,j) term, O(lenA*lenB) divisions; the division dominates per-term cost over the multiply-add (~3 cycles).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..proposedChange: Compute each output[k] as a column convolution sum acc += a[i]*b[k-i], applying % once per k (with periodic reduction if needed). This drops modulo count from O(n*m) to O(n+m) on the guarded path.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..rationale: Replaces the most expensive op (idiv) on the hot path with a single reduction per output, a potential 2-5x speedup when overflow is bounded.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..risk: (MOD-1)^2 can already approach 2^62 for large int MOD, so summing >1 term overflows long. Must gate on L*(MOD-1)^2 < 2^63 (or insert periodic reductions). Not safe for the general unchecked path without this documented bound; reject otherwise.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..summary: Class named ToomCook but implements O(n*m) schoolbook convolution; either rename or implement real Karatsuba/Toom-3.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..currentCost: Misleading name implies sub-quadratic scaling (Toom-3 ~O(n^1.465)) that the quadratic body does not deliver; callers may assume large-input performance it lacks.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..proposedChange: Either rename to SchoolbookMultiply/NaiveConvolve for API honesty, or implement Karatsuba/Toom-3 splitting with this schoolbook kernel as the base case below a tuned length threshold (e.g. ~32-64).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..rationale: Genuine asymptotic improvement for large polynomials, which is the stated purpose of a ToomCook type; rename alone fixes discoverability.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..risk: Modular Toom-Cook needs modular inverses for the interpolation/exact-division steps and overflow control to preserve exact mod-MOD outputs; nontrivial, must be separately verified, must respect house constraints (stackalloc scratch, no managed types). Rename is zero-risk.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..summary: The per-term % is the specific blocker preventing Burst from vectorizing the multiply-add inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..currentCost: idiv in the inner loop forces scalar execution; the otherwise SIMD-friendly a[i]*b[j] multiply-add cannot be auto-vectorized while % is present per term.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..proposedChange: Widen MOD once (covered by op #1) and, on a reduced-coefficient/bounded path, move % out of the inner loop (op #3) so the multiply-add convolution becomes vectorizable.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..rationale: Identifies idiv as the vectorization blocker; removing it on a guarded path lets Burst SIMD the dominant loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Polynomial/ToomCook..risk: Low for the MOD-widening; the vectorization win is contingent on removing % which carries the overflow caveat in op #3. Do not remove % unconditionally.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.summary: Binom recomputes three full Factorial loops plus a ModPow inverse on every call; callers like Narayana and Lah call it repeatedly, making this O(n) per call with a modular exponentiation each time.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.currentCost: Each Binom does Factorial(n) (n-1 mults), Factorial(k), Factorial(n-k) and a ModPow(den, MOD-2) which is ~log2(MOD) ~30 mod-mults. Narayana calls Binom twice -> recomputes Factorial(n) twice; Lah calls Binom plus its own Factorial(n) again.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.proposedChange: Compute the product form num = n*(n-1)*...*(n-k+1) and den = k! in a single fused loop of min(k, n-k) iterations, then one ModPow inverse: long num=1,den=1; int kk = k<n-k?k:n-k; for(int i=0;i<kk;i++){num=num*((n-i)%MOD)%MOD; den=den*(long)(i+1)%MOD;} return num*ModPow(den,MOD-2,MOD)%MOD. Uses symmetry C(n,k)=C(n,n-k) to bound the loop by min(k,n-k).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.rationale: Replaces three independent O(n) factorial passes (up to 3n-ish mults) with one fused pass of min(k,n-k) <= n/2 iterations, and keeps a single ModPow. Fewer total modular multiplications, shorter dependency chain, better cache behavior (no separate factorial walks).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.risk: Pure refactor; same value modulo MOD for valid 0<=k<=n. MOD must be prime for ModPow inverse, which the existing code already assumes (Fermat inverse). No signed/overflow change: products stay < MOD^2 < 2^63 for MOD up to ~3e9, same as current code.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.summary: Lah computes nf=Factorial(n) then Binom(n-1,k-1) which itself recomputes Factorial(n-1) and Factorial(k-1)/Factorial(n-k), and does two separate ModPow inversions.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.currentCost: Factorial(n) (n-1 mults) + Binom's internal three factorials + two ModPow inversions (~60 mod-mults total).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.proposedChange: Use the closed form Lah(n,k)=C(n-1,k-1)*n!/k!. Compute n!/k! as a single descending product n*(n-1)*...*(k+1) (n-k mults, no inverse needed), combine with one C(n-1,k-1) via the fused Binom from the prior finding. Removes the explicit ModPow(kf,MOD-2) entirely.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.rationale: n!/k! needs no modular inverse (it is an exact integer ratio computable as a contiguous product), eliminating one full ModPow (~30 mod-mults) and one Factorial pass.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.risk: Same result mod MOD for valid 1<=k<=n. Still relies on prime MOD only for the binomial inverse. No overflow change.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.summary: QBinomial calls ModPow twice inside the k-iteration loop to recompute q^(n-1-i) and q^(i+1) from scratch each iteration, turning an O(k) loop into O(k log MOD).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.currentCost: 2*k ModPow calls, each ~log2(MOD) ~30 mod-mults => ~60*k mod-mults, plus a final ModPow inverse.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.proposedChange: Maintain the powers incrementally. q^(n-1-i) for i=0..k-1 is a descending sequence: precompute qHi = ModPow(q, n-1, MOD) once, then divide is hard, so instead iterate i and track qPowHi starting at q^(n-1) and multiply by ModPow(q,-1) is also a ModPow; simplest: compute qPowLow = q (i+1 starts at 1) and multiply by q each iter; for the high term precompute base = ModPow(q,n-1,MOD) once and keep a running qPowHi where qPowHi_{i+1}=qPowHi_i * invq, with invq=ModPow(q,MOD-2,MOD) computed once. Net: 2 ModPow total instead of 2k.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.rationale: Replaces 2k modular exponentiations with 2 (one for q^(n-1) base, one for invq) plus O(k) plain multiplications. Cuts the loop cost from O(k log MOD) to O(k + log MOD).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.risk: Requires q not divisible by MOD for invq to exist (q coprime to prime MOD). If q can be 0 mod MOD, guard or keep the high term as a forward product q^0..q^(k-1) multiplied into a precomputed q^(n-k) base instead of using invq, avoiding the inverse entirely. State this guard; otherwise semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.summary: The hook-length product calls ModPow(hook, MOD-2) once per cell, i.e. n modular exponentiations; these can be batched into a single inverse.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.currentCost: For a partition of n cells, n separate ModPow(hook,MOD-2) calls => ~30*n mod-mults.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.proposedChange: Accumulate the product of all hook lengths into one value H = prod(hook) % MOD across all cells, then return Factorial(n) * ModPow(H, MOD-2, MOD) % MOD. One inverse instead of n.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.rationale: result = n! / prod(hooks); computing prod(hooks) then a single Fermat inverse replaces n exponentiations with 1, reducing ~30*n mod-mults to ~30 + n.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.risk: Requires no hook length to be 0 mod MOD (true for a valid Young diagram and MOD > max hook, which holds since hooks <= n and MOD is a large prime). Same result mod MOD. If MOD could be <= some hook, the original per-term version also fails identically, so no new constraint.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.summary: Eulerian allocates two stackalloc buffers and does a manual copy pass each row; it can use a single in-place buffer updated backward, halving stack and removing the copy loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.currentCost: 2*(k+1) longs stackalloc, plus an explicit ndp->dp copy loop of min(k,nextN)+1 each of the n-1 rows.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.proposedChange: Use one dp buffer and iterate j downward so dp[j] only reads dp[j] and dp[j-1] (both still old at that point): for(int j=Math.Min(k,nextN); j>=0; j--){ long val=(j+1)*dp[j]; if(j>0) val=(val+(long)(nextN-j)*dp[j-1])%MOD; dp[j]=val%MOD; }. Eliminates ndp and the copy loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.rationale: The recurrence A[i][j] = (j+1)A[i-1][j] + (i-j)A[i-1][j-1] reads only j and j-1, so a single backward sweep is safe in-place. Halves stack working set and removes one O(k) pass per row.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Combinatori.risk: Must iterate strictly descending so dp[j-1] is still the previous row's value when read. Loop bound min(k,nextN) preserved. Same outputs.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.summary: EgfMultiply computes fact and ifact (a ModPow per inner iteration) that are never used, and recomputes Binom(i+j,i) (three factorials + ModPow) inside the O(n^2) double loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.currentCost: For each of ~n^2/2 inner iterations: Factorial(i+j), one ModPow(fact,MOD-2) (~30 mod-mults, dead), plus Binom which internally does 3 factorials + a ModPow. Dead code dominates; useful Binom is itself O(n) + ModPow per cell.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.proposedChange: Delete the unused 'fact' and 'ifact' lines entirely. Precompute factorials fact[0..n-1] and inverse factorials invfact[0..n-1] once in O(n + log MOD) (single inverse of fact[n-1] then backward recurrence), then bin = fact[i+j]*invfact[i]%MOD*invfact[j]%MOD. Reduces each inner cell to a few multiplications.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.rationale: Removes a dead ModPow per cell and replaces per-cell Binom (O(n)+ModPow) with O(1) table lookups, dropping total cost from O(n^3 log MOD) to O(n^2). Large asymptotic win.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.risk: Pure dead-code removal for fact/ifact (zero semantic effect). Factorial table approach gives identical binomials mod prime MOD. Need stackalloc for two n-length tables (or reuse), within the unmanaged/stackalloc house rules.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.summary: The derivative buffer der[] is fully computed but only der[k-1] is ever read; computing the whole array is wasted O(n) work and an n-long stackalloc.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.currentCost: O(n) loop filling der[0..n-2] plus n-long stackalloc, of which only index k-1 is used.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.proposedChange: Compute only the needed term: long term = ((long)k % MOD * f[k]) % MOD; then result = term*k%MOD; return result*invK%MOD. Drop the der buffer and the loop. (der[k-1] corresponds to i=k, value (k%MOD*f[k])%MOD.)
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.rationale: Replaces an O(n) pass and an n-element stack buffer with a single O(1) computation; removes the only allocation in the function.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/GeneratingF.risk: der[k-1] is exactly ((long)k % MOD * f[k]) % MOD by the loop's indexing (i=k => der[k-1]). For k in [1,n-1] f[k] is in range. Same output. Guard already present: k<=0 returns 0; ensure k<n so f[k] valid (caller-contract per Run convention).
