src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Prufer.cs.summary: Rank computes an entire first block (the 'pow' loop and the loop that accumulates into 'r') whose results r and the per-iteration pow are never used; only the second Horner loop's 'result' is returned. This is dead, expensive work including a ModPow.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Prufer.cs.currentCost: First loop: n-2 mults to build pow. Second loop: n-2 iterations each doing a ModPow on i==0 (~30 mod-mults) or a modular division pow/n (integer division on longs, NOT modular inverse) and accumulating into unused r. All discarded.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Prufer.cs.proposedChange: Delete the first 'pow' loop and the first accumulation loop entirely; keep only the final Horner evaluation that fills 'result'. The function reduces to: long result=0,pn=1; for(int i=n-3;i>=0;i--){result=(result+(long)seq[i]*pn)%MOD; pn=pn*n%MOD;} return result;
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Prufer.cs.rationale: Removes ~2*(n-2) iterations plus a ModPow that produce values never returned, cutting work roughly in half and eliminating a misleading non-modular 'pow / n' division. The returned value is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Prufer.cs.risk: Confirmed dead: r is local and never returned; the only return path uses 'result'. Pure removal, identical observable output. (Note the deleted code also contained a latent bug—pow/n is not modular—so removing it is strictly safe and clarifying.)

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..summary: The binomial coefficient in the Bell-row recurrence is updated using a ModPow(k+1, MOD-2) modular inverse every inner iteration, when C(i-1,k+1) can be advanced by an exact integer division-free multiplicative step using inverse-factorial tables or by precomputed inverses.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..currentCost: Inner loop over k does a ModPow(k+1,MOD-2) (~30 mod-mults) each iteration => O(n^2 log MOD) for the full Bell triangle.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..proposedChange: Precompute inv[1..n] (modular inverses of 1..n) once in O(n) using the linear inverse recurrence inv[1]=1; inv[x]=(MOD-(MOD/x)*inv[MOD%x]%MOD)%MOD, then binom *= (i-1-k)%MOD then binom *= inv[k+1]. Replaces the per-iteration ModPow with a table lookup.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..rationale: Linear sieve of modular inverses costs O(n) total instead of O(log MOD) per element; turns the row cost from O(n log MOD) to O(n). For the whole triangle O(n^2 log MOD) -> O(n^2).
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..risk: Linear inverse recurrence requires prime MOD (already assumed via Fermat). inv table needs an n-length stackalloc, within house rules. Same values mod MOD. Ensure MOD%x and MOD/x use the prime modulus; valid for 1<=x<=n<MOD.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..summary: The Bell numbers are built via the binomial recurrence (C(i-1,k) sum) which needs modular inverses; the Bell triangle recurrence computes the same b[i] with pure additions and no inverses.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..currentCost: O(n^2) additions plus O(n^2) ModPow inverses (current) for the binomial form.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..proposedChange: Use the Bell triangle: maintain a row where T[0]=last row's last value, T[j]=T[j-1]+prevRow[j-1]; Bell(i)=T[0] of row i. This yields b[0..n] with only modular additions, zero multiplications and zero inverses, in O(n^2) adds.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..rationale: Eliminates all multiplications and all modular inverses from Bell-number generation, leaving only adds — far cheaper per element and Burst-vectorizable, while keeping O(n^2) which is optimal for generating all Bell numbers up to n.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/SubsetBell..risk: Requires one extra n-length row buffer (stackalloc, in-place rolling possible). Produces identical Bell numbers mod MOD. No prime-MOD requirement at all for the triangle, strictly more robust.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.summary: First(n,k) and Second(n,k) generate the entire row via FirstRow/SecondRow (O(n^2) work) just to return a single entry row[k]; if many single-entry queries are made this is wasteful, and the row buffer is discarded.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.currentCost: O(n^2) modular mults to fill row[0..n], then return one element; buffer freed immediately.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.proposedChange: Document that First/Second are O(n^2) single-shot helpers and expose the existing FirstRow/SecondRow (already public) as the batched API for callers needing multiple k; optionally early-out the inner UpdateSecondRow/UpdateFirstRow to stop maintaining indices > k is NOT valid (recurrence needs full row), so the real win is API guidance: prefer FirstRow when more than one k is queried for the same n.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.rationale: No cheaper algorithm exists for a single Stirling number than building the row, so the win is ergonomic/purity: steer batch callers to the row API to avoid recomputing the whole O(n^2) row per k. Prevents quadratic-per-query blowup in loops.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.risk: Ergonomic guidance only; no behavior change. If kept as-is it is already correct. Mark low-priority.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.summary: factor is recomputed via two nested % operations though (i-1) < MOD for all realistic i, making the outer reductions redundant.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.currentCost: ((long)MOD - ((long)(i-1) % MOD)) % MOD per row: two modulo ops where i-1 is a small loop index almost always < MOD.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.proposedChange: long factor = (long)(MOD - (i - 1)); when i-1 < MOD (guaranteed when n < MOD, the normal case), giving the negative-coefficient directly without the inner %; keep the general form only if i-1 can exceed MOD.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.rationale: Removes two modulo operations per row (n total) on a value that is provably in [0,MOD) under the normal n<MOD precondition, replacing with a single subtraction.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Stirling.cs.risk: Valid only if i-1 < MOD (i.e. n <= MOD). Since these tables are stackalloc'd of size n+1 and MOD is a large prime, n<MOD effectively always holds; state this guard. If n could exceed MOD, keep one % on (i-1).

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.summary: Precompute modular inverses of 1..n-1 once instead of calling ModPow inside the O(n^2) double loop, cutting a log(MOD) factor.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.currentCost: Binomial runs the outer loop n times; ComputeBinomialTerm runs an inner loop of up to n2+1 iterations, and every non-terminal iteration calls Combinatorial.ModPow(k+1, MOD-2, MOD). ModPow is O(log MOD) ~= 30 modmuls. Total cost is O(n^2 * log MOD) modular multiplications, all to obtain modular inverses of the integers 1..n2.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.proposedChange: In Binomial, before the outer loop, stackalloc a long* inv of length n (inv of 1..n-1) and fill it with the standard linear-sieve modular-inverse recurrence: inv[1]=1; for i in 2..n-1: inv[i] = (MOD - (MOD / i) * inv[MOD % i] % MOD) % MOD (valid only when MOD is prime, which the Fermat ModPow already assumes). Pass inv into a modified ComputeBinomialTerm and replace the ModPow(k+1,...) call with inv[k+1]. The incremental comb recurrence is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.rationale: Replaces O(n^2 log MOD) work with O(n) precompute + O(n^2) inner work => drops a ~30x log-MOD factor on the dominant term. The linear inverse sieve computes all inverses 1..n-1 in O(n) total, and each inner-loop inverse becomes a single array load instead of a 30-multiply modular exponentiation, also shortening the modmul dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.risk: The inverse sieve requires MOD prime, which is already an implicit precondition of the existing Fermat-based ModPow(.., MOD-2). Requires MOD > n so that no i in 1..n-1 is divisible by MOD (i.e. every i is invertible); for the unchecked Run-style contract this matches the existing assumption that k+1 is invertible mod MOD. inv[i] uses inv[MOD % i] where MOD % i < i, so the table is filled before use. Extra n*8 bytes of stack; acceptable for the same n already stackalloc'd elsewhere in the module.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.summary: Same precomputed-inverse-table optimization as Binomial, plus drop the per-iteration sign branch by alternating a multiplier.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.currentCost: O(n^2 * log MOD) from the inner ModPow(k+1, MOD-2, MOD) call, identical to Binomial. Additionally, each inner iteration evaluates a branch 'long sign = (k % 2 == 0) ? 1L : MOD-1L' which is a data-dependent branch and a signed modulo.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.proposedChange: Hoist a stackalloc inv[] table (filled by the linear inverse sieve) and replace ModPow(k+1,...) with inv[k+1]. For the sign, replace the branch with a toggling value: initialize 'long sign = 1L' before the loop and at the end of each iteration do 'sign = MOD - sign' (i.e. 1 -> MOD-1 -> 1 ...), eliminating the k%2 modulo and the ternary branch.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.rationale: Removes the ~30x log-MOD factor on the dominant term as in Binomial. The sign toggle removes a signed % and an unpredictable branch from every inner iteration, shortening each iteration to straight-line modular arithmetic that Burst schedules better.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.risk: Inverse sieve needs MOD prime and MOD > n (same as Binomial). For the sign toggle, MOD - sign where sign in {1, MOD-1} yields {MOD-1, 1}, matching the original mapping exactly for all k, so semantics are preserved provided MOD >= 2 (true for any valid prime modulus). No overflow: MOD-sign stays within long.

src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.summary: Precompute inverses of 1..n once to remove the ModPow call from the O(n^2) Bell-number double loop.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.currentCost: SetPartition builds the Bell triangle via a double loop: outer i in 1..n, inner k in 0..i-1, each inner iteration calling Combinatorial.ModPow(k+1, MOD-2, MOD). Total O(n^2 * log MOD) modular multiplications just to get inverses of 1..i-1.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.proposedChange: After 'long* bell = stackalloc long[n + 1];', also stackalloc 'long* inv = stackalloc long[n + 1];' and fill inv[1..n] with the linear inverse-sieve recurrence (inv[1]=1; inv[i] = (MOD - (MOD/i)*inv[MOD%i] % MOD) % MOD). Replace the inner 'Combinatorial.ModPow((long)(k + 1), (long)MOD - 2L, (long)MOD)' with 'inv[k + 1]'. The binom incremental recurrence is otherwise unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.rationale: Cuts O(n^2 log MOD) down to O(n) precompute + O(n^2) inner work, removing the ~30x log-MOD factor on the hot path and turning each inverse into a single load. This is the same proven incremental-binomial pattern the function already uses, just sourcing the inverse from a table.
src/IAFahim.Algebra.Sequence/Transform.c.risk: Requires MOD prime (already assumed by Fermat ModPow) and MOD > n so every i in 1..n is invertible. inv[i] depends on inv[MOD % i] with MOD % i < i, so it is computed before use. Adds (n+1)*8 bytes of stack alongside the existing bell buffer; bounded by the same n.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.summary: Marshal.AllocHGlobal does not honor the requested alignment, and the alignInBytes parameter is silently ignored across all overloads.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.currentCost: AllocHGlobal returns memory aligned only to the platform malloc granularity (typically 16 bytes on 64-bit). Callers expecting larger alignInBytes (e.g. 32/64 for SIMD/cacheline) get misaligned pointers, forcing scalar or split loads in downstream Burst-vectorized code (a real per-iteration cycle cost in hot loops that consume these buffers).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.proposedChange: For the alignment-bearing overloads, over-allocate sizeInBytes + alignInBytes, align the returned pointer up via (p + (align-1)) & ~(nint)(align-1), and store the original base pointer in the bytes immediately preceding the aligned pointer so Free can recover it; or document that alignment is not honored. Since alignInBytes is a power of two by Unity convention, the round-up is a single add+and (branchless).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.rationale: Correct alignment lets downstream code use aligned vector loads/stores instead of unaligned or split accesses, and avoids cacheline-straddling reads. The align math itself is branchless add+and.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.risk: Changes the free path (must subtract the stored offset), so it is NOT a drop-in for the current Free which calls FreeHGlobal directly on the same pointer. This is a correctness-coupled change: only safe if Free is updated in lockstep. If callers never request alignment > malloc granularity, this is a no-op and can be skipped. Power-of-two alignment assumed (true for Unity allocators).

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.summary: Marshal.AllocHGlobal / FreeHGlobal are managed P/Invoke calls that Burst cannot compile; on the hot path inside Burst-compiled jobs these allocators are not Burst-compatible.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.currentCost: Any Burst-compiled method that calls these allocators will fail to compile or fall back to managed (Mono) execution, losing all Burst vectorization/codegen for the calling job. This defeats the stated 'runs under Unity Burst' goal for allocation-bearing paths.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.proposedChange: For Burst compatibility use UnsafeUtility.Malloc/Free (or a raw malloc/free via a Burst-callable function pointer) instead of Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal. If this module is intentionally the non-Burst fallback shim, annotate it so callers know allocation must happen outside Burst regions.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.rationale: UnsafeUtility.Malloc is Burst-intrinsified and also takes alignment directly, simultaneously fixing the alignment gap above. Removes the managed transition entirely.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Allocator.risk: This is the NoDeps module that deliberately avoids UnityEngine/Unity.Collections internals, so UnsafeUtility may be unavailable by design. If so, reject; this is a structural/dependency tradeoff, not a free micro-opt. Behavior of allocation size is identical; only the backing allocator changes.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.summary: Allocate ignores the requested alignment, so returned pointers are only guaranteed 8/16-byte aligned by the CRT, not the caller's requested alignment (e.g. 64-byte CacheLineSize).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.currentCost: Marshal.AllocHGlobal(size) returns malloc-aligned memory (typically 16 bytes on 64-bit). Callers passing alignment=CacheLineSize=64 silently receive under-aligned blocks; SIMD/Burst vectorized loads/stores assuming 64-byte alignment can fault on some targets or incur split-load penalties, and false-sharing-avoidance via cache-line padding is defeated.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.proposedChange: Use an aligned allocator: NativeMemory.AlignedAlloc((nuint)size, (nuint)alignment) (paired with NativeMemory.AlignedFree in Free), or implement manual over-allocation + pointer rounding storing the original base just before the aligned pointer. Keep the AllocatorHandle parameter for API compatibility.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.rationale: Honoring alignment lets Burst/SIMD use aligned moves (movaps/vmovaps vs movups) and keeps cache-line padding effective, avoiding false sharing across worker threads. It also prevents potential misaligned-access faults on ARM/mobile for over-aligned types.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.risk: NativeMemory.AlignedAlloc requires its matching AlignedFree, so Free must change in lockstep or you get heap corruption. AlignedAlloc requires alignment to be a power of two and non-zero; guard or document that precondition. Marshal.AllocHGlobal takes IntPtr (cast of long) and can wrap/overflow on 32-bit mobile for size > int.MaxValue; AlignedAlloc takes nuint and is cleaner. This is a behavioral fix, not a pure micro-opt — it changes pointer alignment observably, which is the intent.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.summary: Marshal.AllocHGlobal / FreeHGlobal are managed P/Invoke wrappers that are not Burst-compilable, so any Burst-compiled call path through Allocate/Free falls back to managed or fails compilation.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.currentCost: Marshal.* calls pull in System.Runtime.InteropServices managed marshalling; under Burst these are not supported intrinsics, defeating Burst on the allocation path and preventing the method from being used inside [BurstCompile] jobs.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.proposedChange: Replace Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal with System.Runtime.InteropServices.NativeMemory.Alloc/AlignedAlloc/Free, which Burst recognizes (or with Unity's UnsafeUtility.Malloc when available). These map to raw malloc/free without managed marshalling.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.rationale: NativeMemory.* are thin libc malloc/free intrinsics with no managed marshalling layer, so they are blittable, exception-free on the hot path, and Burst-friendly, keeping allocation usable inside Burst jobs and removing per-call managed transition overhead.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Memory.cs.risk: NativeMemory was added in .NET 6; confirm the target framework / Unity runtime exposes it. Free semantics differ between plain Free and AlignedFree, so the alloc/free pair must match. Behavior (allocate/free a block) is preserved.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Collectio.summary: Align is correct for power-of-two alignment but has no overflow guard; for the unchecked-Run convention this is fine, otherwise note size+alignment-1 can overflow int.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Collectio.currentCost: (size + alignment - 1) & ~(alignment - 1): if size is near int.MaxValue the addition overflows and wraps to a negative/wrong value. No extra cycles spent, but correctness depends on caller staying in range.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Collectio.proposedChange: No code change recommended if this follows the unchecked-Run convention (assume valid input). If a checked variant is desired, document the precondition size <= int.MaxValue - alignment + 1 and that alignment must be a power of two, rather than adding a runtime branch on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Collectio.rationale: The masking approach is already the optimal branchless power-of-two round-up (single add + and). No strength reduction or further simplification is possible; flagging only the overflow precondition for documentation.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/Collectio.risk: None to behavior — this is a documentation/precondition note. Adding a guard would cost a branch on a hot inlined leaf, so it should NOT be added under the perf model.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.summary: Replace the 4-iteration byte-wise FNV loop over a single int with a branchless integer-mix hash, or at least unroll it.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.currentCost: Per call: 4 loop iterations, each doing a byte load from a stack address (&h), an XOR, and a multiply, with a loop counter and compare. This is on the hottest path (called by Add, Remove, Contains, Reallocate per element, ToNativeArray indirectly). The byte-by-byte read through a pointer to a stack local also forces h to be address-taken, defeating register allocation.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.proposedChange: Compute the FNV over the 4 bytes with a fully unrolled fixed sequence (no loop, no pointer): uint hash = FnvOffsetBasis; uint u = (uint)h; hash = (hash ^ (u & 0xFF)) * FnvPrime; hash = (hash ^ ((u >> 8) & 0xFF)) * FnvPrime; hash = (hash ^ ((u >> 16) & 0xFF)) * FnvPrime; hash = (hash ^ (u >> 24)) * FnvPrime; return hash; Or, since the only consumer masks with (BucketCount-1), substitute a single-step integer finalizer (e.g. Knuth multiplicative or an xorshift-multiply mix) which is one multiply instead of four.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.rationale: Removes the loop overhead (counter, compare, branch x4) and removes taking the address of a stack local, letting h stay in a register. The unrolled version is identical bit-for-bit to the current output so it is provably semantics-preserving; the integer-mix variant changes hash distribution but not correctness (still deterministic, still masked into bucket range).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.risk: Unrolled FNV variant: zero semantic change, byte order matches the little-endian pointer walk only on little-endian targets - the current pointer-based code is ALSO little-endian-dependent, so the unrolled (u>>0,8,16,24) form reproduces the exact same values on LE and is therefore strictly equivalent on all real Burst targets (x64/ARM LE). Integer-mix variant changes which bucket a key lands in (still correct, just different distribution) - only adopt if exact hash-value compatibility is not required.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.summary: Add calls Contains (computes hash + walks chain) then recomputes Hash and the bucket index again for insertion.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.currentCost: On every successful Add: Hash(item) computed twice and the bucket index (hash & (BucketCount-1)) computed twice. Hash is a 4-iteration loop, so this doubles the most expensive part of the operation on the common insert path.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.proposedChange: Inline the containment scan into Add: compute uint hash = Hash(item) and int bucket once, walk Buckets[bucket] chain checking Equals; if found return false; otherwise (after a possible Reallocate, which must recompute bucket because BucketCount changes) insert. Note the existing code already has the reallocation hazard handled because it computes bucket AFTER the resize - preserve that ordering: scan first, then if(Length>=Capacity) Reallocate, then recompute bucket from the (possibly new) BucketCount, then insert.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.rationale: Eliminates one full Hash computation and one chain walk per Add (Contains walks the chain, then Add does nothing with that work). Roughly halves the per-insert cost in the no-resize case.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.risk: Must recompute bucket = hash & (BucketCount-1) after Reallocate since BucketCount may grow; the current separate-Contains code accidentally gets this right by computing bucket after the resize. Keep that invariant. hash itself is stable across resize so it can be hoisted; bucket cannot. No observable behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.summary: The power-of-two rounding loop is duplicated in the ctor and Reallocate and uses an O(log n) shift loop instead of a closed-form.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.currentCost: while(powerOf2<bucketCount) powerOf2<<=1; runs ceil(log2(bucketCount)) iterations, duplicated in two methods. Minor, but it is branchy startup/resize cost and code duplication.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.proposedChange: Factor a private static int NextPow2(int v) using a branchless bit-twiddle (v--; v|=v>>1; v|=v>>2; v|=v>>4; v|=v>>8; v|=v>>16; return v+1;) or lzcnt-based form, and call it from both the ctor and Reallocate. Guard v<=1 to return MinBucketCount path.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.rationale: Constant-time, branchless pow2 rounding replaces an O(log n) loop and removes duplicated logic, improving both cycles on resize and maintainability without changing the resulting BucketCount.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.risk: NextPow2(0) must be guarded (the bit-twiddle yields 1 for input 1 after decrement of 0 underflowing) - inputs here are always >= MinBucketCount(16) before rounding, so it is safe, but add the guard if MinBucketCount logic is folded in. Output values identical to the loop for all in-range inputs.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.summary: The two EmptyBucket init loops (Next over capacity, Buckets over BucketCount) are scalar -1 fills that MemSet/MemClear cannot do but a tighter fill or wider stores can.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.currentCost: Two element-by-element int writes of -1. For large capacities this is a long scalar loop that Burst may or may not vectorize well because the value is -1 (not 0, so MemClear is unusable).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.proposedChange: Use UnsafeUtility.MemSet(ptr, 0xFF, byteCount) to fill int arrays with -1 in one call (0xFFFFFFFF == -1 for int). This applies to both the Next init and Buckets init here and the Buckets re-init in Reallocate (lines 287-290, 319-322) and Clear (lines 221-224).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.rationale: 0xFF byte-fill produces -1 for every int, so a single memset replaces the scalar loops with an optimized, vectorized/SIMD bulk fill. Fewer instructions, better memory bandwidth utilization, especially in Clear which is called frequently.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.risk: MemSet fills bytes; for int* the byte 0xFF gives exactly -1, semantics-preserving. Confirm UnsafeUtility.MemSet exists in the target API (it does in Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe); if not, a fallback to a manual byte-fill or keep the loop. No behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.summary: Enumerator stores a copy of T current plus a full NativeHashSet value (which is just a pointer) - the cached current duplicates Keys[entryIndex].
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.currentCost: Enumerator holds a T current field updated in MoveNext, duplicating the value already reachable via set.state->Keys[entryIndex]. For large T this enlarges the enumerator struct and adds a copy per MoveNext.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.proposedChange: Make Current read through directly: public readonly T Current => this.set.state->Keys[this.entryIndex]; and drop the current field (and its assignments in MoveNext/Reset/ctor).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.rationale: Removes sizeof(T) bytes from the enumerator struct and removes a value copy on every MoveNext, shrinking the working set and dependency chain. NativeList's enumerator already does this (reads list[index] on demand).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeHas.risk: Current would reflect the live backing store; for a foreach that does not mutate during iteration this is identical. If a caller reads Current after Remove/Add mid-iteration the lazy read could differ - but mutating during enumeration is already undefined for this container. Match NativeList's on-demand pattern for consistency.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.summary: Constructor always MemClears the initial buffer even though List contents below Length are never read until written.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.currentCost: Every NativeList allocation pays a full MemClear of initialCapacity*ElementSize bytes, even though indices [0,Length) start at 0 and elements are only observable after Add/explicit set. This is wasted bandwidth proportional to capacity at every construction (including the default 16-cap ctor used widely).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.proposedChange: Drop the unconditional MemClear in the ctor. Length starts at 0, so no element in [0,Length) is observable; Add writes before incrementing Length; Resize(...,ClearMemory) already zero-fills the grown region explicitly (lines 256-261). Only paths that expose uninitialized memory are direct this[index] reads beyond Length, which are out-of-contract for an unchecked Run-style API.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.rationale: Removes an O(capacity) memory write from every construction. The buffer is logically empty (Length=0) so clearing it has no observable effect under the documented contract.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.risk: Behavior changes ONLY if a caller reads this[index] for index>=Length on a freshly constructed list and relies on it being zero - that is reading uninitialized/out-of-range data, outside the unchecked contract. If the library guarantees zero-init like Unity's NativeList does NOT (NativeList is always empty at length 0), this matches Unity semantics. Verify no test depends on pre-zeroed capacity; if it must stay, leave as-is.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.summary: ElementSize is a static readonly field (non-const), so every index/Add/Remove reads it from a static field with a beforefieldinit guard rather than a compile-time constant.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.currentCost: Each this[index] get/set, Add, RemoveAt, RemoveRange, Resize multiplies by ElementSize loaded from a static readonly field. Burst can usually constant-fold UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() since T is known at compile time, but routing it through a static readonly field can defeat that folding and adds a static-ctor dependency / potential memory load per use.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.proposedChange: Replace the static readonly field with direct sizeof(T) (legal since T:unmanaged) at each use, or a local const-folded expression. e.g. IntPtr byteOffset = this.state->Buffer + index * sizeof(T); Burst/IL will constant-fold sizeof(T) per specialization.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.rationale: sizeof(T) on an unmanaged generic is a compile-time constant per specialization, enabling strength reduction (index*const becomes a shift when const is a power of two) and removing the static field load and its lazy-init class constructor check. NativeArray already uses UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() inline; this makes NativeList consistent and lets the JIT/Burst fold.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeLis.risk: sizeof(T) for unmanaged T equals UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() in all blittable cases; identical values. No semantic change. Pure win unless the field was deliberately cached to avoid an intrinsic call - under Burst the intrinsic folds away entirely.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeArr.summary: Indexer recomputes UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() inline (fine) but uses IntPtr arithmetic with int index that can be strength-reduced; minor consistency note.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeArr.currentCost: byteOffset = _buffer + index * UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>(). SizeOf<T>() folds to a constant under Burst so index*const becomes a shift for power-of-two T - already good. The only cost is using Unsafe.Read/Write through a reconstructed (void*) each access.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeArr.proposedChange: Optionally expose the element access via ((T*)_buffer)[index] which lets the compiler do typed scaled-index addressing (mov [base + idx*scale]) directly instead of manual byte math plus Unsafe.Read. Functionally identical, often one fewer cast/temp.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeArr.rationale: Typed pointer indexing emits a single scaled-index load/store and avoids the IntPtr-to-void* round-trip, slightly shorter dependency chain. Burst typically lowers both to the same code, so impact is low, but it is cleaner and never worse.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativeArr.risk: None functionally; ((T*)_buffer)[index] is equivalent to the byte-offset Read/Write for unmanaged T. Keep _buffer as IntPtr or cache the T* - behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.summary: Replace the two byte-at-a-time zeroing loops over Keys and Values with a single bulk memclear.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.currentCost: Two scalar loops iterate keysSize and valuesSize BYTES individually (e.g. length*sizeof(TKey) iterations), each a load/store/branch. For length=10000 and 16-byte keys that is 160000 single-byte store iterations that Burst will not auto-collapse to wide stores because the loop bound is a runtime byte count and aliasing is opaque.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.proposedChange: Replace the `for (long i...) keysPtr[i]=0;` and the equivalent values loop with `Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(keysPtr, 0, (uint)keysSize)` (or a memset helper). Since the very next block also writes Next[i]=EmptyBucket in a separate loop, that loop is fine as-is (it writes int sentinels), but the two byte loops should be bulk clears.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.rationale: A single InitBlock/memset is implemented as wide vectorized stores (SIMD/`rep stos`) and is memory-bandwidth bound, vs. the current 1-byte-per-iteration loop which is branch/throughput bound at ~1 byte/cycle. Order of magnitude fewer retired instructions and far better store-port utilization.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.risk: Semantically identical (fills the same byte ranges with 0). keysSize/valuesSize already computed as long; cast to uint is safe only if a single allocation never exceeds 4GB — guard by clearing in a loop chunked to uint, or use a 64-bit memset helper. Otherwise none.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.summary: BucketCount is forced even (length*2 or 16) but bucket index uses %; make BucketCount a power of two and replace % with & (mask).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.currentCost: `(hashCode & 0x7FFFFFFF) % this.state->BucketCount` executes a hardware integer division (~20-40 cycle latency, not pipelined) on every insert during RecalculateBuckets (O(AllocatedLength) divisions) and on every TryGetFirstValue lookup.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.proposedChange: Round bucketCount up to the next power of two in SetAllocatedIndexLength (it is already a free-chosen `length*2`), store `bucketMask = bucketCount-1`, and compute `bucketIndex = hashCode & bucketMask` everywhere (drop the &0x7FFFFFFF since masking with a positive mask already yields a non-negative in-range index).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.rationale: AND is 1 cycle and fully pipelined vs. a multi-cycle non-pipelined DIV. On the hot lookup path and the O(n) rehash this removes the single most expensive instruction. Power-of-two bucket counts keep load factor identical (~2x slots).
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.risk: Changes which bucket a key lands in, but observable map semantics (membership, value retrieval, iteration via Next chains) are unchanged. Must store the mask alongside or derive bucketCount-1; only valid because bucketCount is internally chosen, not caller-supplied.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.summary: Hoist this.state->Next into a local pointer before the probe loop to cut repeated double-indirection through state.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.currentCost: The probe loop reads `this.state->Next[entryIndex]` each iteration: a load of state->Next (pointer chase through state) plus the indexed load. keysPtr/valuesPtr are already hoisted but Next is not.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.proposedChange: Add `int* nextPtr = this.state->Next;` before the while loop and use `nextPtr[entryIndex]`. Same in TryGetNextValue and RecalculateBuckets.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.rationale: Removes one dependent load (state->Next) from the per-iteration dependency chain of a linked-list walk that is already latency-bound on cache misses; shortens the critical path.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.risk: None; state is not mutated inside the loop. Pure read hoist.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.summary: Specialize the byte-wise FNV hash and compare for common small power-of-two key sizes to avoid the per-byte loop.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.currentCost: HashKey loops sizeof(TKey) times with a dependent multiply chain (hash depends on previous hash) — for a 4- or 8-byte key that is 4-8 serialized iterations. CompareKeys does sizeof(TKey) byte compares with early-out branches; for an 8-byte key that is up to 8 branchy compares vs one 64-bit compare.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.proposedChange: In CompareKeys, when sizeof(TKey) is 4/8/16, do a single `*(uint*)`/`*(ulong*)` (or two ulong) equality test instead of the byte loop. sizeof(TKey) is a compile-time constant under Burst so the branch folds away. HashKey is harder to keep bit-identical, so leave its value semantics but consider it lower priority.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.rationale: Burst evaluates sizeof(TKey) at compile time, so the size-dispatch is free and only the matching widened-compare path is emitted: one 64-bit compare replaces an 8-iteration branchy loop, cutting both instruction count and mispredict risk on the hot lookup path.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/NativePar.risk: CompareKeys with widened loads is bit-identical to byte compare for blittable keys (no padding concerns since the same bytes are compared). Do NOT change HashKey's arithmetic if any persisted/cross-call hash identity is assumed; the bucket mapping is internal so a different-but-consistent hash is acceptable, but keep it deterministic.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.summary: Replace the static readonly _elementSize field with sizeof(T) so index math becomes a compile-time constant.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.currentCost: Every indexer, Add, AddRange, RemoveAt, RemoveRange, Resize reads the static field `_elementSize` to compute byte offsets. A static field load is a memory access Burst cannot constant-fold, and the multiply `index * _elementSize` stays a runtime multiply instead of a shift/immediate.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.proposedChange: Use `sizeof(T)` (T is unmanaged, so `sizeof(T)` is legal and a Burst compile-time constant) directly in offset math, or `private static int ElementSize => sizeof(T);`. Remove the static field. For power-of-two element sizes Burst then strength-reduces the multiply to a shift.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.rationale: sizeof(T) folds to a literal at compile time, turning `index * _elementSize` into `index * const` (often a shift), eliminating a static-field load on every element access. Static readonly fields also add a class-constructor/initialization concern that is unnecessary in a Burst struct.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.risk: None functionally — sizeof(T) equals UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() for unmanaged T. Pure win; just changes a runtime read to a constant.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.summary: Index offset `index * _elementSize` uses 32-bit int arithmetic; widen to long/nint to avoid overflow for large lists and to match the 64-bit pointer add.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.currentCost: `_buffer + index * _elementSize` computes `index * _elementSize` in 32-bit int. For a list with length*elementSize > 2^31 (large element types) this overflows silently before the widening add to _buffer. Other methods (AddRange, RemoveRange) already use `(long)`/byte* casts inconsistently.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.proposedChange: Compute offsets as `(nint)index * sizeof(T)` (or `(long)`), matching ReallocateBuffer/AddRange which already cast. Make the offset type consistent across all accessors.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.rationale: Correctness for large buffers and consistency; nint arithmetic also avoids an implicit int->long sign extension juggling and produces the natural LEA addressing. No extra cost for normal sizes.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.risk: Behavior changes ONLY for inputs that currently overflow (already undefined/wrong), so observable behavior for valid in-range inputs is preserved. Low risk.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.summary: Replace the `while (cap < needed) cap <<= 1` growth loop with a branchless next-power-of-two via leading-zero count.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.currentCost: Growing from 4 to a large capacity iterates log2(needed) times with a branch each iteration. Called on every resize past capacity.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.proposedChange: Compute `cap = needed <= 4 ? 4 : 1 << (32 - lzcnt((uint)(needed-1)))` using math.lzcnt/BitOperations-style intrinsic available under Burst, clamped to a 4 minimum.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.rationale: Single LZCNT + shift replaces a data-dependent loop, removing log2(n) branches. Minor but real on the resize path.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeLis.risk: Must reproduce exact same capacities: for needed<=4 return 4; for needed a power of two return needed; for others next power of two. Validate edge needed==0 (returns 4, matching loop) and needed==1 (returns 4). Use needed-1 form to handle exact powers.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeKey.summary: Hoist UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<TValue>()/SizeOf<int>() out of the MemCpy argument list; they are compile-time constants but the repeated calls obscure intent and the int sizeof is a literal 4.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeKey.currentCost: Three MemCpy calls each recompute SizeOf<int>() (and one SizeOf<TValue>()). Under Burst these fold, but `data->KeyCapacity * UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<int>()` is clearer and the same as `data->KeyCapacity * 4`.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeKey.proposedChange: Cache `int sizeOfInt = sizeof(int);` and `int sizeOfTValue = sizeof(TValue);` once; reuse. Cosmetic/defensive — main value is ensuring constant folding is obvious and consistent with CalculateDataSize which already caches them.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeKey.rationale: No asymptotic change; ensures the multiplies use compile-time constants and reduces reliance on the optimizer to dedupe the SizeOf calls. Low impact since Burst likely already folds.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafePar.summary: Hoist this.Buckets, this.Next, this.keys into local pointers before the build loop to avoid repeated field loads through the struct.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafePar.currentCost: The loop reads this.keys[idx], this.Next[idx], this.Buckets[key], this.Buckets[key]= each iteration. Each `this.Field` is a load from the struct's memory (the struct may be behind a pointer via Create), so 3-4 field loads per iteration over count elements.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafePar.proposedChange: Local `int* buckets = this.Buckets; int* next = this.Next; int* k = this.keys;` before the loop, then index those locals. Mirrors how UnsafeKeyedMap.RecalculateBuckets already hoists.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafePar.rationale: Removes redundant struct-field loads from the hot O(count) rehash loop, shortening the per-iteration dependency chain and freeing registers for the load-store of the bucket chain insert.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafePar.risk: None; fields are not reassigned during the loop. Pure read hoist.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.summary: Byte-at-a-time clear loop is ~8x slower than word-wide clear and is not auto-vectorized well; clear in word-sized chunks with a byte tail.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.currentCost: One store + one branch per byte: `size` iterations, each a dependent loop-carried `i++` and a single-byte store. For a typical struct/array clear (hundreds-thousands of bytes) this is an order of magnitude more loop overhead and store-port pressure than necessary.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.proposedChange: Cast to `ulong*` and store 0 in 8-byte strides for `size >> 3` iterations, then clear the remaining `size & 7` bytes with the existing byte loop. e.g. `ulong* q = (ulong*)destination; long n = size >> 3; for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) q[i] = 0UL; byte* p = (byte*)(q + n); for (long j = 0; j < (size & 7); j++) p[j] = 0;`
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.rationale: 8 bytes cleared per store instead of 1, cutting store count and loop branches by 8x and exposing the inner loop to Burst's SIMD widening (vectorized zero stores). The byte tail handles non-multiple-of-8 sizes. Strength-reduces nothing semantically — same bytes written to zero.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.risk: `size >> 3` and `size & 7` are safe because `size` is non-negative by contract (a memory length); for negative `size` the original loop never executes and the new one also never executes (n<=0, tail loop count <=0 via unsigned-intent comparison) so behavior matches for valid input. Word stores assume `destination` is byte-addressable (it is); no alignment requirement on modern targets but Burst-preferred aligned access is the common case.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.summary: Byte-at-a-time fill is ~8x slower than word-wide fill; broadcast the byte to a ulong and store in 8-byte strides with a byte tail.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.currentCost: One store + branch per byte across `size` iterations, same loop-overhead and store-port problem as MemClear, but for arbitrary fill values.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.proposedChange: Broadcast: `ulong v = value; v |= v<<8; v |= v<<16; v |= v<<32;` then `ulong* q=(ulong*)destination; long n=size>>3; for(long i=0;i<n;i++) q[i]=v;` then fill `size & 7` tail bytes with `value`. The broadcast is a handful of hoisted ops outside the loop.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.rationale: 8 bytes per store, 8x fewer loop branches, and Burst can vectorize the uniform `ulong` store into wide SIMD splat stores. The broadcast constant is loop-invariant and computed once.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.risk: Broadcast math is exact for all byte values (each byte of `v` equals `value`). `size>>3`/`size&7` safe for non-negative `size` (contract). Same observable bytes written as the byte loop for valid input.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.summary: Nested byte-copy with recomputed `i*size+j` index has a multiply per inner iteration and copies one byte at a time; hoist the base and copy whole blocks via MemCpy.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.currentCost: Inner body computes `i*size+j` every iteration (a multiply plus two adds) and does a single-byte load/store. Total `count*size` byte ops plus `count*size` multiplies. Index arithmetic dominates for small `size`.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.proposedChange: Hoist the row base out of the inner loop: `byte* dest=(byte*)destination; for(int i=0;i<count;i++){ Buffer.MemoryCopy(source, dest, size, size); dest += size; }` — i.e. delegate each replica to the intrinsic block copy and advance `dest` by `size`, eliminating the inner loop and the per-byte multiply entirely.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.rationale: Removes the `i*size+j` multiply (replaced by a single pointer add per outer iteration), removes the inner branch, and lets `Buffer.MemoryCopy` (an intrinsic Burst lowers to a fast memcpy / wide SIMD) copy each block. Asymptotically same O(count*size) bytes moved but with far lower per-byte overhead and better vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.risk: `Buffer.MemoryCopy` requires non-overlapping src/dest per call, which holds here (source is a distinct `size`-byte block, each dest slot is disjoint). Semantics identical for valid input. If callers ever pass `count<=0` or `size<=0`, both old and new loops are no-ops.

src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.summary: `int i*size+j` index can overflow for large replicate counts; the pointer-advance rewrite also removes this latent 32-bit overflow.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.currentCost: `i * size + j` is computed in `int`; for large `count*size` (>2^31 bytes) the index wraps to a negative/incorrect offset, corrupting memory. Even within the current API this is a hidden 32-bit ceiling.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.proposedChange: Adopting the pointer-advance form above (dest += size) accumulates the offset in a 64-bit pointer rather than a 32-bit index, raising the safe range without changing the signature.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.rationale: Pointer advancement avoids the 32-bit multiply overflow entirely; offset tracked in the native pointer width. Pure robustness/RAM-safety win at zero extra cost.
src/IAFahim.Collections.NoDeps/UnsafeUti.risk: `size` and `count` remain `int` per the existing signature so total still bounded by callers, but intermediate overflow is removed. No behavior change for inputs where `count*size` already fits in int.

src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.summary: Horizon construction is O(F^2) per iteration via per-edge linear face scans; replace with an edge-counting / adjacency pass to make it O(F) (or O(F*E)).
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.currentCost: For each visible face, IsHorizonEdge is called 3 times, and each call scans all faceCount faces (inner loop over fa/fb/fc). With up to MaxFaces=256 faces, that is ~3*F*F integer-compare iterations per EPA iteration, and up to 128 EPA iterations. This nested O(F^2) dominates EPA runtime and is pure pointer-chasing with poor vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.proposedChange: Compute the horizon by edge cancellation instead of repeated full scans. For each visible face, push its 3 directed edges into a small edge list; an edge that borders an invisible face survives, an edge shared by two visible faces cancels. Concretely: collect all directed edges of visible faces, then an edge (u,v) is a horizon edge iff its reverse (v,u) is NOT present among visible-face edges. Detect cancellation by sorting/scanning the visible edge list once (O(Ev log Ev) or O(Ev) with the existing horizonA/horizonB scratch used as a hash-free linear cancel buffer), rather than scanning ALL faces per edge. This removes the dependence on total faceCount and replaces it with dependence only on the (usually small) visible set.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.rationale: The visible face set is typically far smaller than faceCount; horizon edges number O(visible). Edge-cancellation touches each visible edge O(1) (amortized) instead of O(F). This drops the inner work from O(F^2) to ~O(Ev), a large asymptotic win on the hottest EPA loop, and the edge buffer is already allocated.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.risk: Must preserve winding/orientation so AddFace(horizonA[i], horizonB[i], newIdx) produces the same outward faces. Edge-cancel logic must treat (u,v) and (v,u) as the canceling pair exactly as IsHorizonEdge's 'shared edge with an invisible neighbor' rule does. Degenerate/duplicate vertices (collinear supports) could create non-manifold edges; keep the current AddFace len<Epsilon rejection so a spurious face is dropped. Validate against existing NUnit tests since this changes the horizon code path, not the math.

src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.summary: The 'visible' bool[MaxFaces] and horizon int[MaxFaces*EdgesPerFace] buffers are declared inside the EPA iteration loop; hoist their stackalloc to the method top to make frame usage explicit and avoid relying on JIT hoisting.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.currentCost: stackalloc bool[256] plus two stackalloc int[768] appear lexically inside the for(iter) body. C#/Burst hoists loop-invariant stackalloc to the frame, but expressing it in-loop obscures the ~6.5KB stack footprint and risks a stack-growth pattern if the JIT ever fails to hoist.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.proposedChange: Move 'bool* visible = stackalloc bool[MaxFaces];', 'int* horizonA = stackalloc int[MaxFaces*EdgesPerFace];', 'int* horizonB = ...' to the top of PenetrationDepth alongside the other stackalloc buffers, and just reset horizonCount=0 each iteration. The 'visible' array is fully overwritten each iteration so no clearing is needed.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.rationale: Guarantees single-allocation frame layout independent of optimizer behavior, keeps total stack budget visible for mobile, and removes any chance of repeated frame adjustment in the loop.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.risk: None semantically; buffers are fully written before read each iteration (visible[f] set for f<faceCount, horizonCount reset). Pure refactor.

src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.summary: AddFace computes math.length(n) (sqrt) for the degeneracy check AND to normalize; the degeneracy test can use lengthsq to avoid a sqrt on the reject path, and normalization can use rsqrt.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.currentCost: len = math.length(n) is a sqrt. It is used both as the degeneracy gate (len < Epsilon) and the normalizer (n = n/len). The compare-against-Epsilon does not need the true length, and n/len is a divide after a sqrt.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.proposedChange: Compute float lenSq = math.dot(n,n); reject when lenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon (use a named const EpsilonSq). Otherwise n = n * math.rsqrt(lenSq) to combine sqrt+divide into one reciprocal-sqrt multiply. Distance d still uses the normalized n via math.dot(n, vertices[a]).
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.rationale: Removes one sqrt entirely on rejected/degenerate faces and converts the survivor path's sqrt+divide into rsqrt+multiply (fewer cycles, shorter dependency chain). AddFace runs per horizon edge per EPA iteration, so this is a hot leaf.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.risk: rsqrt is an approximation in some math libs but Unity.Mathematics math.rsqrt on float is accurate enough for normals here; if exact parity with math.length is required for test determinism, keep n = n * (1.0f / math.sqrt(lenSq)) which is bit-equivalent restructuring. The Epsilon^2 threshold differs from Epsilon for the length test: with Epsilon=1e-6, EpsilonSq=1e-12; a face with length between 1e-12 and 1e-6 would now pass instead of being rejected. To preserve EXACT behavior keep the gate as lenSq < EpsilonSq only if the intended threshold is on squared length; otherwise gate on math.length still. Recommend: reject when lenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon to keep the same true-length cutoff (sqrt(EpsilonSq)=Epsilon), which is exactly equivalent.

src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.summary: ExpandSimplex line-2 case calls math.length(ab) inside a comparison that can be squared to avoid a sqrt.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.currentCost: math.abs(ab.x) > DirectionThresholdRatio * math.length(ab) computes a sqrt to compare a magnitude against a scaled length. ExpandSimplex runs at most once per PenetrationDepth so impact is low, but the sqrt is avoidable.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.proposedChange: Compare squared quantities: ab.x*ab.x > (DirectionThresholdRatio*DirectionThresholdRatio) * math.lengthsq(ab), with a precomputed const for the squared ratio. Both sides are non-negative so the inequality is preserved.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.rationale: Removes a sqrt from the comparison; squaring both sides preserves ordering since both operands are >= 0.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Epa.cs.risk: math.abs(ab.x) and the RHS are both non-negative, so squaring preserves the comparison exactly. Floating-point rounding of the squared form differs by ULPs from the sqrt form at the exact threshold boundary, which could flip the perturbation-axis choice in a measure-zero case; result is still a valid expansion direction (this is heuristic seeding), so observable collision output is unaffected.

src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.summary: BoxSupport normalizes the direction (normalizesafe = sqrt + divide) only to take its sign; the support point depends solely on the per-component sign of direction, so the normalize is wasted work.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.currentCost: math.normalizesafe(direction) computes lengthsq, rsqrt/sqrt, a 3-wide divide, and a zero-length fallback branch — then only math.sign(n) is used. sign of the normalized vector equals sign of the raw vector for every nonzero length.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.proposedChange: return center + halfExtents * math.sign(direction); dropping the normalizesafe call entirely.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.rationale: math.sign(direction) == math.sign(normalizesafe(direction)) because positive scaling preserves component signs. Eliminates a sqrt, a 3-component divide, and the normalizesafe zero-guard branch from a hot support function called many times per GJK/EPA iteration.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.risk: Edge case: zero direction. normalizesafe returns float3.zero (default) for zero input, so n=0 -> sign=0 -> returns center. math.sign(0)=0 likewise -> returns center. Identical. Component-wise zeros (e.g. direction.x==0) also match: sign(0)=0 in both paths. Behavior is bit-identical for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.summary: SphereSupport does math.length then divides by it; use rsqrt of lengthsq to fold sqrt+divide into one multiply, and reuse the squared length already implied.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.currentCost: len = math.length(direction) (sqrt) followed by (direction/len)*radius (a 3-wide divide then 3-wide multiply). Called directly and twice via CapsuleSupport, so it is a hot leaf.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.proposedChange: float lenSq = math.dot(direction,direction); if (lenSq < EpsilonSq) return center; return center + direction * (math.rsqrt(lenSq) * radius); This computes one rsqrt and folds the radius scale into a single scalar, then one 3-wide multiply-add.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.rationale: Replaces sqrt + vector-divide + vector-multiply with rsqrt + scalar-multiply + vector-multiply-add: fewer total FLOPs, no divide (divide latency >> multiply), shorter dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/MinkowskiDiffe.risk: Threshold changes from len<1e-6 to lenSq<1e-12; sqrt(1e-12)=1e-6 so the cutoff on true length is identical — exactly equivalent. rsqrt approximation: Unity.Mathematics math.rsqrt is full-precision on float for scalar; result matches direction/length to within ULPs. If exact test determinism is required, use direction * (radius / math.sqrt(lenSq)) for bit-stable behavior while still removing the redundant length recompute.

src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Gjk.cs.summary: Distance's simplex handling only ever resolves point and segment cases; ComputeClosestPointToOrigin returns float3.zero for count>=3, silently dropping triangle/tetra closest-point logic, so the loop wastes support evaluations that cannot improve the result.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Gjk.cs.currentCost: When count reaches 3 or 4, ComputeClosestPointToOrigin returns float3.zero, so dir = -zero = zero, the next support(0) is meaningless, and ComputeDistanceToOrigin also returns length(zero)=0 for count>=3. The loop keeps calling supportA/supportB (2 delegate calls per iter, up to 32 iters) producing no useful refinement and can return a wrong 0 distance.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Gjk.cs.proposedChange: Either (a) implement the triangle and tetrahedron closest-point-to-origin cases so the GJK-distance subalgorithm is correct and converges early, or (b) cap simplex growth at 2 and reduce after each step so the segment path is exercised, removing dead support calls. At minimum, cap count and break once the closest feature stops improving to avoid running the full MaxIterations on a no-op path.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Gjk.cs.rationale: Removes up to ~30 redundant delegate-pair evaluations per Distance call on the degenerate path and fixes a latent correctness gap (count>=3 returning 0). Fewer indirect calls (delegates defeat inlining/vectorization) is a real cycle win in addition to correctness.
src/IAFahim.Collision.Gjk/Gjk.cs.risk: This touches Distance's numerical results for inputs whose simplex grows past a segment, so it is NOT purely behavior-preserving — flag as a correctness fix, validate against NUnit distance tests. If strict behavior preservation is mandatory, only apply variant (b)'s early-out when ComputeClosestPointToOrigin would return zero, since that path already yields 0.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.summary: Evaluate a[i] once per iteration and hoist the 2*n loop bound / endpoint.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.currentCost: Each iteration of the descending loop reads a[i] for the `a[i] == 1` decrement test, then reads it AGAIN in `a[i] == 1 && ones >= zeros + 1`. The endpoint 2*n is recomputed as the loop init `2*n - 1` and passed again to UpdateDyckSuffix as `2*n`; n-ones is recomputed.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.proposedChange: Compute `int two_n = n << 1;` once. In the loop read `byte v = a[i];` into a local, branch on `v`. Replace `a[i] == 1` tests with `v == 1`. Pass `two_n` to UpdateDyckSuffix.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.rationale: Removes one redundant memory load per iteration (2n-1 loads saved over the scan) and removes redundant multiply/add of 2*n; fewer dependent loads shortens the per-iteration dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.risk: None. n<<1 == 2*n for all valid n>=1 (no overflow since 2*n indexes a valid buffer). Observable behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.summary: Drop the full O(size^2) zero-fill; only the lower triangle the recurrence reads needs init.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.currentCost: `for (int i = 0; i < size*size; i++) dp[i] = 0;` zeroes the entire (n+2)^2 table even though the recurrence only writes/reads cells with i>=j in 0..n. The zero pass duplicates work the recurrence loop already overwrites, and touches the unused (n+1)-row/column padding.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.proposedChange: Remove the blanket zero loop. Instead, within the existing i/j double loop, the cells skipped by `if (i < j ...) continue;` must read 0 from neighbors: guard the two reads with their existing `i+1<=n` / `j+1<=i` conditions (already present) AND zero only the boundary cells actually read out of range. Simplest safe form: zero just row index n and column index referenced via (i+1)*size+j when i+1>n — i.e., memset only the cells dp[(n+1-based) padding] the recurrence can read, which are the i==n row above-diagonal and j just past i. Concretely keep correctness by zeroing only dp cells for i in [0..n], j in [0..n] with i<j before the recurrence (a triangular ~n^2/2 fill) instead of the full (n+2)^2.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.rationale: size^2 = (n+2)^2 stores vs ~n^2/2 needed halves-to-quarters the init traffic; for repeated Rank/Unrank calls this is on the hot path. Fewer stores, fewer cache lines dirtied.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.risk: Medium correctness risk: the recurrence reads dp[(i+1)*size+j] when i+1<=n and dp[i*size+(j+1)] when j+1<=i; any cell read must be pre-zeroed or previously written. Must prove every read target is either written by an earlier iteration or explicitly zeroed. If unsure, keep the full zero — only adopt with a verified read-set. Triangular fill is the conservative correct subset.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.summary: DP table is identical for every rank with the same n; recomputing it per Rank/Unrank call is wasteful when ranking many objects.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.currentCost: Both RankCatalanObject and UnrankCatalanObject allocate a (n+2)^2 stackalloc and run an O(n^2) PrecomputeCatalanDp on EVERY call. Ranking M objects costs O(M*n^2) plus M table builds, even though the table depends only on n.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.proposedChange: Add public Rank/Unrank overloads that accept a caller-supplied precomputed `long* dp` (built once via a public PrecomputeCatalanDp), turning the per-call cost into O(n). Keep the current self-contained methods as convenience wrappers. This matches the library's explicit-buffer convention.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.rationale: Amortizes the O(n^2) build across many objects: M*O(n) + 1*O(n^2) instead of M*O(n^2). Large asymptotic win for batch ranking/unranking, the common combinatorics use case.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Cat.risk: None to existing callers (additive API). Caller must size dp as (n+2)^2 and build it for the right n; document the contract. Pure/deterministic preserved.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.summary: Both 'enumerators' implement the same plain lexicographic combination successor, not CoolLex or revolving-door (Gray) order; either dedupe or fix to honor the named ordering.

CoolLex should be a single-shift O(1)-amortized loopless order; revolving-door should be a Gray code changing one element per step. As written both are O(t)-per-step lex order — duplicated code and a misleading API.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.proposedChange: Either (a) collapse to one shared lexicographic enumerator and rename honestly, or (b) implement true CoolLex (loopless, O(1) per step via the shift rule) and true revolving-door (single-element Gray successor). Option (b) restores the intended O(1)-per-step cost vs current O(t).

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.risk: Changing the emitted ORDER changes observable behavior; only acceptable because the current order does not match the method name (latent bug). If the order must stay, only the dedupe (a) is semantics-preserving. Flag to maintainer which intent is canonical.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.summary: Populate copies c into res every step, doubling working set and write traffic for identical data.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.currentCost: MoveNext maintains state in `c` and then copies all t elements into `res` via Populate on every step. res is a verbatim duplicate of c, so the caller could read c directly. This is an O(t) copy plus a second t-int buffer per call site.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.proposedChange: Drop res/Populate and let the caller read the combination directly from c (the enumerator's working buffer), matching how HeapPermutationEnumerator exposes `a` directly. If a separate output buffer is a hard API requirement, document that res==c content and skip the copy when the caller passes the same pointer.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.rationale: Eliminates an O(t)-per-step memcpy and a t-int buffer (half the RAM footprint, less cache pressure). Heap/JohnsonTrotter enumerators already expose state in-place, so this also makes the API consistent.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Com.risk: API change: callers currently reading res must switch to c. Behavior of the sequence is unchanged. Low risk if callers are in-tree.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.summary: Finds the largest mobile element by full O(n) scan plus a second O(n) direction-flip scan every step; classic JT tracks position to avoid the search.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.currentCost: Per step: one O(n) loop to locate the largest mobile element (with redundant `dir[a[i]]` lookups and two near-identical branches), then a swap, then a SECOND O(n) loop flipping directions of all larger elements. Total 2n reads/writes per permutation; the position lookup is the avoidable part.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.proposedChange: Maintain an inverse-permutation (value->index) array so the mobile-element position is found in O(1) per value, or use the standard Steinhaus-Johnson-Trotter with a position table; still O(n) worst for the flip pass but removes the search loop. At minimum, hoist `a[i]` into a local and compute `dir[a[i]]` once per i instead of twice.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.rationale: Removes one of two full-array passes per step and redundant repeated `dir[a[i]]` indexed loads; for an enumerator called n! times this constant factor and the search elimination compound dramatically.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.risk: Must preserve the exact JT visiting order. The inverse-array variant needs extra n-int state (ram tradeoff) and careful maintenance on swaps; verify the emitted sequence is unchanged. The local-hoist micro-opt alone is zero-risk.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.summary: O(n) stackalloc for a 2-term linear recurrence that needs only two scalars.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.currentCost: Allocates `long* dp = stackalloc long[n+1]` though dp[i] depends only on dp[i-1] and dp[i-2]. That is n+1 longs of stack and n+1 stores when two rolling scalars suffice.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.proposedChange: Replace the array with two locals: `long prev2=1, prev1=1, cur=1; for(int i=2;i<=n;i++){ cur = prev1 + (long)(i-1)*prev2; prev2=prev1; prev1=cur; } return cur;`
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.rationale: Drops stack working set from O(n) to O(1) and removes n array stores/loads, keeping everything in registers — better for Burst register allocation and avoids stack traffic.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.risk: None. Same recurrence, same long arithmetic; (i-1)*dp[i-2] cast to long preserved. Identical output for all n.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.summary: j = (i+1)%n fixup uses a modulo where a branchless wrap suffices, and the swap-with-neighbor fixup does not guarantee a derangement.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.currentCost: `(i+1)%n` issues an integer division per fixed point. Also semantically: swapping a fixed point with its neighbor can create a new fixed point or fail to derange in general, so the result is not a guaranteed derangement (correctness concern, not just perf).
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.proposedChange: For the modulo: `int j = i+1; if (j==n) j=0;` (single branch, no div) since i in [0,n-1]. Separately, flag that the algorithm should be a rejection-sampling or early-refusal derangement generator if a true uniform derangement is the contract.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.rationale: Replaces a div (10-40 cycles) with a predictable compare+move. The correctness note prevents shipping a non-derangement under a Random*Derangement* name.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.risk: The modulo replacement is exact for i in [0,n-1]. The correctness flag is a behavior question for the maintainer — do not silently change sampling semantics; raise it.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.summary: Hoist a[k] to avoid double-indexing and enable a cleaner branchless accumulation.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.currentCost: `a[a[k]] != k` does a dependent double load (a[k] then a[a[k]]) plus an early-return branch each iteration. Fine, but the inner load can be hoisted.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.proposedChange: `for(int k=0;k<n;k++){ int ak=a[k]; if (a[ak]!=k) return false; } return true;` keeps the early-out. The double indirection is inherent; just name the intermediate so Burst schedules the loads.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.rationale: Minor: makes the dependent-load chain explicit and removes a redundant recompute of a[k]; negligible but free.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Per.risk: None. Identical semantics including early return.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.summary: Linear edge-existence scan makes every duplicate-rejecting graph builder O(E^2); use an adjacency bitset for O(1) membership.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.currentCost: EdgeExists scans all `count` existing edges per probe. RandomConnectedGraph/RandomDAG/RandomBipartiteGraph/RandomRegular call it inside their add loops, so building m edges costs O(m^2) (or worse under rejection). For dense graphs this dominates.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.proposedChange: Maintain an adjacency presence structure: for n up to a few thousand a stackalloc bit array of n*n bits (or a packed upper-triangular bitset of n*(n-1)/2 bits) gives O(1) EdgeExists and O(1) insert. Index undirected edge (u,v) with u<v into the triangular bitset. Pass the bitset pointer through the builders.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.rationale: Turns O(m^2) construction into O(m) amortized plus O(n^2/8) bytes for the bitset — a large asymptotic win for medium/dense graphs, the regime where these builders are slow.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.risk: Extra n^2/8-byte working set (bound n to keep stackalloc safe, or require caller-supplied buffer per house convention). Must mirror the exact undirected/directed matching logic (EdgeExists treats (u,v)==(v,u) for undirected but RandomDAG is directed u<v) — use separate triangular vs full indexing per builder. Preserve the same accept/reject decisions so the emitted graph for a given seed is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.summary: Replace per-element division i/d in the points-fill with an incremental counter, and guard n*d overflow.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.currentCost: `for (i=0;i<total;i++) pts[i] = i/d;` does a division each iteration. Also `int total = n*d;` and `n*d % 2` can overflow int for large n,d (silent wrong result / negative stackalloc size).
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.proposedChange: Fill without division: `int val=0, cnt=0; for(int i=0;i<total;i++){ pts[i]=val; if(++cnt==d){cnt=0;val++;} }`. Compute total as `long` for the overflow check, and clamp/early-return if total exceeds a safe stackalloc bound.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.rationale: Removes a div (10-40 cycles) per of total=n*d elements, replacing it with a compare+increment. Overflow guard prevents negative stackalloc size and UB.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.risk: Division replacement is exact (i/d increments every d steps). The parity test n*d%2 must be done in long to match intended math; behavior changes only for inputs that currently already overflow (undefined today), so this is a strict robustness improvement. Keep the existing `n*d%2!=0` early-return semantics for valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.summary: Hoist the *edgeCount dereference and writeback out of the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.currentCost: Inner loop dereferences `*edgeCount` repeatedly (`outFrom[*edgeCount]`, `outTo[(*edgeCount)++]`). Through a pointer the compiler may not keep this in a register across the n^2 iterations, adding load/store traffic on the hottest loop.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.proposedChange: Use a local `int ec = 0;` for the loop body and write `*edgeCount = ec;` once at the end: `if(XorShift(...)<threshold){ outFrom[ec]=i; outTo[ec]=j; ec++; }`.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.rationale: Keeps the counter in a register across the O(n^2) loop, removing a pointer load+store per accepted edge and aiding Burst vectorization/scheduling of the inner test.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Ran.risk: None for single-threaded use (edgeCount is caller output, written once at end gives same final value). Identical emitted edges and order.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Nec.summary: Cache k-1 and reuse the nextJ scan; the `_n % curJ` / `n % j` divisibility test runs a div per emitted word.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Nec.currentCost: Both routines recompute `_k - 1` / `k - 1` inside the inner `while (w[nextJ]==k-1)` scan each step, and test divisibility with `%` per candidate. For large alphabets/lengths the repeated subtraction and modulo add up.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Nec.proposedChange: Hoist `int km1 = k - 1;` (and `_k-1`) into a local before the scan loops. The `n % j` test is inherent to the FKM algorithm but j only takes divisor values; if n is fixed per enumerator, this is minor — leave the modulo but ensure km1 is hoisted.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Nec.rationale: Removes a redundant subtraction from the hot inner comparison loop; trivial but free and helps the comparison stay register-resident.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Nec.risk: None. k-1 is loop-invariant within a MoveNext call; identical results.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.summary: Replace Math.Max with a branchless update of m[i] in the restricted-growth-string successor
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.currentCost: m[i] = Math.Max(m[i], kappa[i]) is a call/branch per successor step. After kappa[i]++ the relation between m[i] and kappa[i] is constrained: kappa[i] can exceed the old m[i] by at most 1, so the max is effectively a conditional max.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.proposedChange: Since FindSetPartitionSplit stops where kappa[i] != m[i-1]+1, and the increment makes kappa[i] at most m[i]+1, replace with: int ki = kappa[i] + 1; kappa[i] = ki; if (ki > m[i]) m[i] = ki;  or branchless: m[i] += (m[i] < ki) ? 1 : 0 collapses to m[i] = ki when greater. Equivalent to current Math.Max but inlines without the call.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.rationale: Burst inlines System.Math.Max(int,int) to a cmov already in most cases, so the realistic win is removing a managed-method dependency and making the intent (a single +1 ceiling) explicit; the new value can only be m[i] or m[i]+1, allowing m[i] = ki > m[i] ? ki : m[i] to fold to a single predicated move.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.risk: Must preserve exact semantics: m[i] is the running max of kappa[0..i]. The new form keeps m[i] = max(m[i], kappa[i]); correct as long as kappa[i] is the only entry changed since m[i] was last set, which holds here. No signed/overflow concern (values bounded by N).

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.summary: Eliminate the O(K) prefix-sum recomputation in FillCompositionSuffix to make NextComposition O(1) amortized
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.currentCost: FillCompositionSuffix recomputes sum = comp[0..i] every successor call (O(i) per step, O(N*K) over a full enumeration). The composition successor only ever moves one unit from comp[i] to comp[i+1] and zeroes the tail; the value comp[i+1] = N - sum(comp[0..i]) can be derived without re-summing.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.proposedChange: Track the total mass moved into the tail. In NextComposition: after comp[i]-- , the new comp[i+1] equals (old comp[i+1] which is 0 at this point since i is the last nonzero before tail) ... Instead compute the tail value directly: the suffix from i+1 to K-1 must sum to (N - sum(comp[0..i])). Since FindCompositionSplit guarantees comp[i+1..K-2] were all 0 and only comp[K-1] held the remainder, maintain a running 'tail' = N - prefixSum incrementally: when decrementing comp[i], comp[i+1] = previous_suffix_total + 1, then zero comp[i+2..]. Store the suffix-of-i total once rather than re-summing each call.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.rationale: Standard composition (bars-and-stars) successor is O(1) amortized; the current re-sum makes it O(K) per step and O(N choose model) overall, a real asymptotic constant blow-up. Removing the inner sum loop cuts the dominant cost of the enumeration.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.risk: Must keep comp[i+1] = N - sum(comp[0..i]) exactly. The incremental tracking is only valid because the successor structure restricts which cells changed; verify FindCompositionSplit's invariant (only comp[K-1] nonzero in suffix) before relying on it. If invariant is ever violated, fall back to the sum. No overflow (values <= N).

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.summary: Pack the 'First' flag to avoid 3 bytes of struct padding and unify with the int-flag pattern used by SetPartitionState
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.currentCost: CompositionState uses bool First after two ints; on 4-byte alignment the bool consumes 4 bytes (1 used, 3 padding), giving a 12-byte struct. SetPartitionState uses int First (also 12 bytes but no inconsistency).
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.proposedChange: Either keep bool but document it costs a full word, or store First in the high bit / a packed field. For consistency and blittable clarity under Burst, make CompositionState mirror SetPartitionState by using int First, or fold First into a sentinel value of K (e.g. First implied when a separate cheap check holds) so the struct is just {int N; int K;}.
