src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.rationale: Smaller/consistent state structs improve cache density when many enumerators are stored in arrays and remove a bool-vs-int inconsistency that can affect Burst layout assumptions. Marginal but free.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.risk: bool is blittable under Burst but layout differs from int; changing the field type changes the public struct layout (ABI). Only safe if no external code depends on the exact field offsets/size. Behavior unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.summary: Avoid zeroing the whole comp[0..K) then overwriting comp[0]; only zero comp[1..K)
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.currentCost: InitializeComposition does a full loop comp[0..K-1]=0 then comp[0]=N, writing comp[0] twice.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.proposedChange: Set comp[0] = state->N first, then zero comp[1..K-1] (loop from x=1). Saves one redundant store and clarifies intent.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.rationale: Removes a redundant write to comp[0]; trivially fewer ops on the (cold) init path. Cheap and clearly correct.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.risk: None; output identical. Init is called once per enumeration so impact is small.

src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.summary: Rank/Unrank functions are non-functional stubs returning 0/identity, breaking the Run/Try* contract and producing silently wrong results
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.currentCost: RankIntegerPartition/RankSetPartition/RankComposition always return 0; UnrankIntegerPartition returns false with outLen=0; UnrankSetPartition/UnrankComposition return identity/zero regardless of rank. Callers get silently incorrect data with no signal.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.proposedChange: Either implement the real rank/unrank (set-partition ranking via restricted-growth-string + Bell/Stirling tables; composition ranking via combinatorial number system over C(n+k-1,k-1)) or, until implemented, make them explicit: return false / a sentinel and document as unimplemented so callers can't mistake 0 for a valid rank. At minimum keep signatures consistent (some return long, some bool+out).
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.rationale: Not a micro-opt but a correctness/ergonomics issue: stubbed functions that return plausible-looking values are worse than ones that signal 'unimplemented'. A real implementation also enables O(1)-ish unranked random access instead of enumerating.
src/IAFahim.Combinatorics.Generation/Set.risk: If external tests already assert these stub return values, changing them breaks those tests; confirm intended status (TODO vs shipped) before altering. No Burst concern.

src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.summary: Replace O(n^2) insertion sort with an O(n log n) sort (heapsort/introsort) for the coordinate-compression sort phase.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.currentCost: The inner while-loop (lines 14-24) is insertion sort: worst-case and average O(n^2) comparisons/moves. For n in the thousands this dominates everything else and grows quadratically; a reverse-sorted input on n=10000 is ~50M element moves.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.proposedChange: Implement an in-place heapsort (or median-of-3 introsort) over tmp[0..len) instead of the insertion-sort while-loop. Heapsort needs no extra buffer, is branch-light, and is fully Burst-friendly with raw pointers. Keep insertion sort only as the small-n base case (e.g. len <= 16) of an introsort to retain its cache-friendliness for tiny arrays.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.rationale: Lowers asymptotic cost from O(n^2) to O(n log n). For any non-trivial len this is the single biggest win in the module; the dedup pass and the initial copy are already O(n) and negligible by comparison.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.risk: Heapsort is not stable, but coordinate compression only needs sorted unique values, so stability is irrelevant here -> behavior preserved. Must ensure the comparison stays a simple > on int (no overflow). Only worthwhile if len can realistically exceed a few dozen; for guaranteed-tiny len insertion sort is fine.

src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.summary: Fuse the src->tmp copy into the sort/first pass, or use a memcpy intrinsic instead of a scalar element loop.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.currentCost: Lines 12-13 do a scalar element-by-element copy of len ints before sorting, a separate full O(n) pass that the compiler may or may not vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.proposedChange: Replace the scalar copy loop with Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned(tmp, src, (uint)len * sizeof(int)) (or Buffer.MemoryCopy). This issues a single vectorized/rep-movs copy instead of a per-element store loop.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.rationale: A bulk memcpy moves multiple ints per instruction (SIMD/rep movs) and has a tighter dependency profile than a scalar loop, cutting the copy phase cost by a constant factor with no behavior change.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Coordina.risk: None semantically: tmp and src are distinct caller buffers (tmp is scratch). Must confirm Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned is permitted under the project's Burst/house rules (it is unmanaged and intrinsic). len*4 cannot overflow uint for any realistic len.

src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Discreti.summary: Replace O(n^2) insertion sort with O(n log n) in-place heapsort for the in-place discretization sort.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Discreti.currentCost: Lines 13-23 are an in-place insertion sort with worst/average O(n^2) moves; this is the entire cost of the function aside from the O(n) dedup pass.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Discreti.proposedChange: Sort src[0..len) in place with heapsort (no scratch buffer needed, matching this function's in-place contract), falling back to insertion sort only for tiny subarrays as an introsort base case.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Discreti.rationale: Drops the function from O(n^2) to O(n log n) while staying fully in-place, preserving its zero-extra-memory design. Same sorted-unique output.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/Discreti.risk: Stability not required (output is sorted unique ints). The function's distinguishing feature vs CoordinateCompress is in-place operation, which heapsort preserves (no extra buffer). Insertion sort base case keeps small-n cache behavior.

src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.summary: Replace InsertionSort (O(n^2)) called from Run with an O(n log n) sort.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.currentCost: InsertionSort (lines 25-38) is O(n^2); it dominates Run, since Unique and the final BinarySearch mapping loop are O(n) and O(n log u) respectively.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.proposedChange: Implement heapsort/introsort over tmpSorted[0..len) in place of InsertionSort. The signature InsertionSort(int* arr, int len) can stay; just swap the body, or rename to Sort for ergonomic accuracy. tmpSorted is already a dedicated scratch buffer so an in-place heapsort fits perfectly.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.rationale: Sorting is the asymptotic bottleneck of rank compression; O(n log n) makes the total Run cost O(n log n) (sort) + O(n log u) (mapping) instead of O(n^2). Largest single win for large len.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.risk: None to correctness: ranks come from BinarySearch over the sorted-unique array, independent of sort stability. Keep the comparison as plain int > to avoid sign/overflow issues.

src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.summary: Use a bulk memcpy for the src->tmpSorted copy instead of a scalar loop.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.currentCost: Lines 12-13 copy len ints scalar-wise before sorting; a separate O(n) per-element store loop.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.rationale: Single vectorized/rep-movs copy instead of a scalar store loop; constant-factor cycle reduction, no semantic change. src and tmpSorted are distinct buffers.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.risk: Confirm Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned is allowed under Burst/house rules (it is intrinsic and unmanaged). No overflow for realistic len.

src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.summary: The final mapping loop re-runs a full log(u) binary search per element; for inputs with many duplicates or near-sorted access this recomputation can be reduced, and the search itself can be made branchless.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.currentCost: Run's mapping loop (lines 18-19) calls BinarySearch len times, each O(log u) with a data-dependent branch (lines 59-62) that mispredicts ~50% of the time on random data, stalling the pipeline per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.proposedChange: Make BinarySearch branchless: replace the if/else updating lo/hi with a conditional-move form, e.g. lo += (arr[mid] < val ? (mid + 1 - lo) : 0) computed via a mask, so the loop body has no unpredictable branch. Optionally hoist len into a local (already a param) and keep the lo+((hi-lo)>>1) midpoint (good, overflow-safe).
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.rationale: Branchless binary search converts a per-step mispredicting branch into a data-flow conditional move, removing pipeline flushes; over len*log(u) steps this is a real constant-factor win and vectorizes/predicts better under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Compress.Coordinate/RankComp.risk: Must keep first-occurrence (lower-bound) semantics: arr[mid] < val => lo=mid+1 else hi=mid yields the lower bound; the branchless mask must reproduce exactly this to preserve identical rank outputs. The midpoint formula is already overflow-safe; keep it.

src/IAFahim.Compress/CompressValues.cs.summary: Cache src[i-1] in a register across iterations instead of re-loading the previous element each pass.
src/IAFahim.Compress/CompressValues.cs.currentCost: Each loop iteration reads src[i] and src[i-1] from memory (2 loads), where src[i-1] was already loaded as src[i] in the prior iteration. The data-dependent branch (src[i] != src[i-1]) also serializes the compare against a redundant load.
src/IAFahim.Compress/CompressValues.cs.proposedChange: Hoist the previous value into a local: 'int prev = src[0]; for (int i = 1; i < len; i++) { int cur = src[i]; if (cur != prev) { dst[count++] = cur; } prev = cur; }'. This carries 'prev' in a register and issues one load per iteration instead of two.
src/IAFahim.Compress/CompressValues.cs.rationale: Halves the number of loads in the loop body (1 instead of 2) and shortens the compare's dependency chain, since 'prev' is register-resident rather than reloaded. Removes the i-1 address computation. Constant-factor win on a tight scan loop.
src/IAFahim.Compress/CompressValues.cs.risk: Semantics-preserving: 'prev' exactly tracks the value previously compared. len<=1 early-out is unchanged. No signedness/overflow concerns since these are plain int copies and comparisons.

src/IAFahim.Compress/RestoreCompressed.c.summary: Narrowing long->int copy with explicit (int) cast is already Burst-vectorizable; only note is to confirm it is the intended truncation, not saturation.
src/IAFahim.Compress/RestoreCompressed.c.currentCost: Per-element 64->32-bit truncating store; Burst can vectorize the narrowing pack, so cost is near memory-bandwidth bound already.
src/IAFahim.Compress/RestoreCompressed.c.proposedChange: No code change needed for correctness/perf. If callers ever pass values outside int range expecting clamping, that is NOT what this does (it truncates the low 32 bits). Document the truncation contract in a comment so the unchecked Run convention is explicit.
src/IAFahim.Compress/RestoreCompressed.c.rationale: The loop is already optimal for Burst (contiguous load, narrow, store; SIMD pack). There is no asymptotic or constant-factor win to extract; flagging it would be cargo-cult.
src/IAFahim.Compress/RestoreCompressed.c.risk: None for behavior. Truncation (int)long differs from clamping only for out-of-range inputs, which the unchecked Run contract already assumes valid; no change proposed.

src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.summary: Per (i,j) cell the code does TWO full O(2^m) array copies (dp->tmp inside UpdateProfileDpMasks, then tmp->dp in CopyDp). One copy is entirely removable by swapping roles or writing results directly into dp.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.currentCost: Each of the n*m iterations performs: a 2^m copy (line 31), a 2^m relaxation pass, then a second full 2^m copy in CopyDp (line 49). That is 2 * 2^m stores per cell purely for buffer shuffling, i.e. n*m*2^(m+1) extra long stores plus the n*m*2^m loads. CopyDp is pure overhead on top of the copy already done in UpdateProfileDpMasks.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.proposedChange: Drop CopyDp entirely. In UpdateProfileDpMasks the relaxation only ever WRITES tmp[nmask] where nmask = mask^bit (a strictly different slot reachable only from a mask that has the bit set), and READS dp[mask]. Since tmp is seeded as an exact copy of dp, you can instead relax in place on dp itself: for masks with bit set, compute cand = dp[mask]+rowA[j] and do dp[nmask] = max(dp[nmask], cand). Because nmask has the bit clear and mask has it set, iterating mask ascending never revisits a written nmask as a future source (nmask < mask is false in general, but the source dp[mask] for a given mask is never itself a destination in this same j-pass since destinations all have bit==0 and sources all have bit==1). This removes both the tmp seed copy and CopyDp, eliminating the tmp buffer round-trip. If strict equivalence with the two-buffer semantics is required, instead keep tmp but swap the dp/tmp pointers after the pass (pointer swap, O(1)) rather than calling CopyDp (O(2^m)).
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.rationale: Eliminates n*m*2^m redundant long stores (the CopyDp pass) and, in the in-place variant, a second n*m*2^m. For typical m (broad profile DP) 2^m dominates; halving or removing buffer copies is a direct constant-factor win on the hottest loop and improves cache behavior (single buffer stays hot instead of two).
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.risk: The pointer-swap variant is exactly semantics-preserving and lowest risk: after UpdateProfileDpMasks writes into tmp, swap dp<->tmp pointers in Run instead of CopyDp; the returned dp[0] must read from the final live buffer, so track parity (n*m swaps) or swap back once. The fully in-place variant requires verifying no source mask is also a destination within the same j-pass: sources have bit set, destinations have bit clear, so they are disjoint and the transform is safe for this specific recurrence. Reject in-place only if the recurrence is later changed to relax same-parity masks.

src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.summary: Inner mask loop reads dp[mask] twice and tests every mask even though only masks with bit set do work; the long.MinValue guard and double load add an avoidable dependency on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.currentCost: For each of 2^m masks: branch (mask&bit), then dp[mask] is loaded once for the != MinValue test (line 37) and again for the addition (line 39). Half the masks (bit clear) do nothing yet still iterate. rowA[j] is reloaded every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long addV = rowA[j] above the loop (loop-invariant, line 39 reloads it each iteration). Iterate only over masks that have the bit set by stepping: for(int mask=bit; mask<maskCount; mask=(mask+1)|bit) or enumerate submasks; this skips the (mask&bit)==0 half entirely. Load dp[mask] once into a local long cur, test cur!=long.MinValue, then cand=cur+addV — removing the second load.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.rationale: Removes the redundant second load of dp[mask], hoists the rowA[j] load out of the loop, and roughly halves loop trip count by visiting only bit-set masks. Fewer loads shorten the dependency chain and reduce memory traffic on a loop that runs n*m*2^m times.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.risk: Stepping only over bit-set masks changes iteration order but not results (masks without the bit are no-ops in the original). The mask=(mask+1)|bit enumeration must start at mask=bit and is correct for visiting exactly the bit-set masks. addV hoist is unconditionally safe (rowA, j fixed for the call).

src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.summary: BrokenProfileDp is a byte-for-byte duplicate of ProfileDp except for an unused int* state parameter; it adds maintenance/code-size cost with no behavioral difference.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.currentCost: Two identical copies of the same DP (InitializeDp, UpdateProfileDpMasks, CopyDp bodies are identical lines 67-97 vs 20-50). The state pointer is accepted but never read or written, so it is dead surface area. Doubles instruction-cache footprint and any future fix must be applied twice.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.proposedChange: Either remove BrokenProfileDp and route callers to ProfileDp, or, if the distinct name is part of the public API, have BrokenProfileDp.Run forward to ProfileDp.Run (dropping the unused state arg) so the optimized inner loop lives in one place. If state is meant to participate in a true broken-profile recurrence, it is currently a no-op bug; flag for spec review.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.rationale: Single source of truth removes duplicate I-cache pressure and ensures the cycle optimizations above only need to be made once. Removing a dead pointer parameter also clarifies the API.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.risk: If external code depends on the BrokenProfileDp.Run signature including state, keep the signature and forward internally. If state was intended to carry real DP information, deduplication would mask a latent functional bug rather than preserve it — confirm intended semantics before deleting.

src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.summary: subSize is always 0 (Run declares it and never assigns), so dp[vNode*cap+subSize]+valV inside the loop is loop-invariant and should be hoisted; also the i+weightV<cap test wastes iterations that do nothing.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.currentCost: ProcessTreeKnapsackChild recomputes val2 = dp[vNode*cap + subSize] + valV every iteration (line 121) although vNode, subSize(=0), valV are all fixed for the call — a redundant load+add per i. Additionally the loop runs i from min(size,cap)-1 down to 0 but only acts when i+weightV<cap, so iterations with i >= cap-weightV are pure no-ops (a branch with no body).
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long val2 = dp[vNode*cap + subSize] + valV; above the loop. Replace the per-iteration guard by tightening loop bounds: start i at min(min(size,cap)-1, cap-weightV-1) so every iteration does real work, removing the inner branch entirely. Also hoist long* dpU = dp + u*cap; so dp[u*cap+i+weightV] becomes dpU[i+weightV], removing the repeated u*cap multiply/add.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.rationale: Removes a load, an add, a multiply (u*cap and vNode*cap), and a branch from each iteration of a loop that runs O(cap) times per edge across the whole tree (O(V*cap) overall). Tightening bounds eliminates the no-op tail iterations entirely instead of branching through them.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.risk: Hoisting val2 is safe only because dp[vNode*cap+subSize] is not written inside this loop (the loop writes dp[u*cap+...], u != vNode for a child edge). Bound tightening preserves results because skipped iterations had no effect under the original guard; must guard cap-weightV-1 against negative (if weightV>=cap the loop should not run at all) to avoid an out-of-range start index. The dead subSize/size accounting also suggests a latent algorithm bug (sizes never grow as intended) — flag for correctness review separately.

src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.summary: The i*n row base is recomputed inside the k-loop and the long.MaxValue double-guard adds branches; hoist the row pointer and the (k+1)*n stride.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.currentCost: For each k in [i,j): dp[i*n+k] recomputes i*n (line 148) and dp[(k+1)*n+j] recomputes (k+1)*n (line 149) each iteration. Two != MaxValue comparisons plus the compare-and-update form a branch cluster per k. Inner loop runs O(n) per cell, O(n^3) total.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long* rowI = dp + i*n; so d1 = rowI[k]. For d2, note (k+1)*n advances by exactly n each iteration, so keep a running pointer long* colBase = dp + (i+1)*n + j; and add n each step instead of multiplying. This converts two multiplies per k into one add.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.rationale: Removes two integer multiplies per inner iteration (i*n hoisted, (k+1)*n strength-reduced to running add) in an O(n^3) triangle loop — a real per-iteration cycle saving and shorter address-computation dependency chain that Burst can pipeline better.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.risk: Strength-reduction of (k+1)*n to incremental add is exact for the contiguous k step; ensure the running pointer is initialized to (i+1)*n+j and incremented by n in lockstep with k. No semantic change to the MaxValue guard or the min selection.

src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.summary: Inside the k-loop, i*n (constant for the call) is recomputed and k*n is recomputed each iteration; hoist the row base and strength-reduce k*n to a running add.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.currentCost: Per k in [start,end]: dp[i*n+k] recomputes i*n and dp[k*n+j] recomputes k*n (line 200). With the Knuth/Yao opt the k-range is amortized small, but the two multiplies and the double MaxValue guard still execute every iteration of the amortized-O(n^2) total work.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long* rowI = dp + i*n; (d1 = rowI[k]). Maintain a running pointer rowK = dp + start*n + j; incremented by n per k so d2 = *rowK. Hoist into locals to cut the address-computation multiplies to a single add per iteration.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.rationale: Same strength-reduction win as IntervalDp: replaces two multiplies per inner iteration with one add and a hoisted base, shortening the address dependency chain on the dominant inner loop.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.risk: Exact transform: k advances by 1 so k*n advances by n; initialize rowK at start*n+j. opt[i] bestK tracking and the MaxValue guard are unchanged, so the Knuth optimization invariant is preserved.

src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.summary: Inner loop reloads a[i] every j iteration and the a[i]!=INF test is loop-invariant in j; hoist a[i] and its INF check out of the j-loop.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.currentCost: For each (i,j): a[i] is loaded and compared to INF (line 168) inside the j-loop although both are constant across j. That is m redundant loads+compares per i, n*m total wasted.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long ai = a[i]; and the if(ai==INF) continue; check above the j-loop. Inside the loop only test b[j]!=INF and compute ai+b[j]. Optionally hoist long* cBase = c + i; so c[i+j] is cBase[j].
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.rationale: Removes a load and a branch per inner iteration and skips entire rows where a[i]==INF, cutting n*m work to (#finite a)*m. The min-update can stay as written; the dependency chain on c[i+j] is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.DP.General/General.cs.risk: Hoisting a[i] and its INF guard is exactly equivalent because neither a[i] nor the INF constant changes across j, and skipping a fully-INF row produces no writes the original would have made (original would also skip every j for that i). c[i+j] aliasing with a/b is not a concern since they are distinct output/input buffers by contract.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: dp is indexed with (int) casts of long loop counters; the casts add work and force int-domain arithmetic on indices that are already known non-negative longs.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: Each inner-loop access dp[(int)(c - weight)] and dp[(int)c] performs a long->int narrowing conversion (movsxd/cdqe-class), and the subtraction c-weight is recomputed as long then narrowed every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Drive the inner loop with a native-width index (nint/long) and keep dp[idx] in the long domain so no per-iteration (int) cast is emitted. Hoist the read of dp[(int)(c-weight)] vs dp[(int)c]: iterate c from cap down to weight using two running pointers (long* cur=dp+c, long* prev=dp+c-weight) decremented together, eliminating both the subtraction and both casts per iteration.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Pointer-walk form removes one subtraction and two narrowing casts per iteration in the hottest loop (O(n*cap)), shortening the dependency chain to a compare+cmov+store. dp index domain stays identical so addresses are unchanged.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: None for valid input: cap and c-weight are non-negative and < array length by contract, so the int cast was already lossless; pointer form yields identical addresses. Ensure pointers use the same element type (long) to keep scaling correct.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: Branchy max update (if val > dp[c]) prevents Burst from emitting a branchless cmov and may mispredict on adversarial weight/value patterns.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: Per iteration: compare + conditional store with a data-dependent branch; mispredicts flush the pipeline.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Replace 'long val = prev+value; if (val > cur) cur = val;' with 'dp[c] = math.max(dp[c], prev+value);' (branchless). Under Burst, math.max(long,long) lowers to compare+cmov; even hand-written 'cur ^= (cur ^ val) & -(long)(val>cur)' is branchless but math.max is cleaner.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Removes a data-dependent branch from an O(n*cap) loop, converting it to straight-line code Burst can pipeline/vectorize-friendlier. Identical result.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: Semantically identical (max). The XOR-mask trick relies on (val>cur) producing 0/1 then negation to all-ones; prefer math.max to avoid sign/overflow subtlety. No behavior change.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: Loop nesting is inverted vs the cache-friendly form: outer over capacity, inner over items, so w[i]/v[i] are re-streamed for every one of the `cap` capacities, and the (int) casts plus per-iteration w[i] reload dominate.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: O(cap*n) with item arrays w[]/v[] fully re-read cap times (poor temporal locality of the item stream), plus a branch 'if (w[i] <= c)' and three (int) casts per accepted item.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Invert loops to outer-over-items, inner-over-capacity (the standard unbounded form): for each item, for c = w[i] .. cap: dp[c] = max(dp[c], dp[c-w[i]] + v[i]). This streams w[i]/v[i] once per item (kept in registers across the whole inner sweep), removes the per-iteration 'w[i] <= c' branch (loop starts at w[i]), and lets the inner loop use a pointer walk to drop the (int) casts. Result is identical because unbounded knapsack is order-independent over the forward sweep.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Hoists w[i]/v[i] out of the inner loop (loop-invariant for the inner sweep), removes a branch, improves locality of dp[] sequential access, and removes casts. Same asymptotic class but far better constant factor and cache behavior.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: Must keep the FORWARD sweep (c increasing) for unbounded semantics — that is what allows reusing the current item multiple times. Behavior is identical to the current code, which also reuses items within the same c. No overflow change.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: Bounded knapsack uses naive per-cap multiplicity scan: O(cap * maxUse) per item, giving O(n * cap * count) overall. Binary (power-of-two) decomposition reduces it to O(n * cap * log(count)).
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: ProcessBoundedItem's count>1 path runs, for each of cap+1 capacities, an inner loop up to maxUse iterations each doing k*weight and k*value multiplies — O(cap*maxUse) per item, multiplications recomputed every k.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Decompose count into powers of two (1,2,4,...,remainder) and run a standard 0/1 update for each piece with combined weight=p*weight, value=p*value. This turns each item into O(log count) virtual items, each an O(cap) 0/1 sweep: total O(n*cap*log count) instead of O(n*cap*count). Also eliminates the inner k*weight/k*value multiplies (precompute pieceWeight/pieceValue once per piece).
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Asymptotically tighter for count>1 and removes repeated multiplications; the 0/1 sweep is the already-optimized branchless/pointer-walk loop. Standard, provably equivalent bounded-knapsack result.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: Must reuse the existing 0/1 sweep semantics (descending c) for each piece. Watch overflow: p*value can be large — but it is <= count*value which the current code already computes (k*value up to maxUse*value), so no new overflow domain. Equivalent optimal value guaranteed by binary representation completeness.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: The count>1 path iterates c from cap down to 0, but for c < weight the inner UpdateBoundedCap loop body 'c >= k*weight' (k starts at 1) is always false, doing useless iterations.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: For c in [0, weight-1] the outer loop still calls UpdateBoundedCap which immediately fails its guard; that is up to `weight` wasted outer iterations per item plus call overhead (if not inlined).
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Lower bound the outer loop to c >= weight (for (long c = cap; c >= weight; c--)), since no k>=1 can satisfy c >= k*weight when c < weight. If the binary-decomposition rewrite above is adopted this method disappears; otherwise this guard is a free win.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Eliminates up to `weight` no-op outer iterations and their call/guard overhead per bounded item. Identical result.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: None: when c < weight the original inner loop produced no writes, so skipping those c values changes nothing.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: Inner loop recomputes k*weight and k*value each iteration via multiplication.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: Two long multiplies per k (k*weight, k*value) plus the cast (int)(c - k*weight) each iteration.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Strength-reduce to running accumulators: 'long cw = weight, cv = value;' then each iteration use cw/cv and do 'cw += weight; cv += value;'. Replaces two multiplies/iteration with two adds. (Moot if binary decomposition is adopted, which removes this loop entirely.)
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Add is cheaper than imul and shortens the dependency chain; identical values produced.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: None for valid input; accumulator path reaches the same cw=k*weight, cv=k*value values. Overflow domain unchanged (same maximum products as multiply form).

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: A dedicated bool[] DP is used while BitsetSubsetSum already provides a 64x-denser, ~64x-faster bitset variant; the bool variant is redundant and the slowest path for reachability.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: bool* dp uses target+1 bytes and the inner loop processes one capacity per iteration with a data-dependent branch (if dp[s-val]) — O(n*target) byte stores, 64x more memory traffic than the bitset.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: For the reachability (subset-sum boolean) use case, route callers to BitsetSubsetSum (already present), or at minimum document SubsetSum as the simple/reference path. If SubsetSum.Run must stay, make its inner store branchless: 'dp[(int)s] |= dp[(int)(s-val)];' (OR into target) instead of 'if (dp[s-val]) dp[s]=true;', removing the branch.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Bitset form is 64x less RAM and ~64x fewer operations for the identical reachability answer; even keeping the bool form, the branchless OR removes a misprediction-prone branch in the O(n*target) loop.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: Branchless OR is semantically identical for bool (true stays true, only sets when source true). Steering to bitset is an API/ergonomics change for callers, not a behavior change in the result bit.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: Hot shift loop recomputes the carry index check 'j - offset - 1 >= 0' as a branch inside the per-word loop.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: Per word j: a branch 'if (j - offset - 1 >= 0)' guarding the carry-in OR. The guard only fails for the single lowest word (j == offset); branching every iteration to handle one boundary word.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Peel the boundary: run the main loop for j from size-1 down to offset+1 doing the full two-term OR unconditionally (j-offset-1 >= 0 always holds there), then handle j == offset separately with only the 'bits[j] |= bits[0] << shift' term. Removes the per-iteration boundary branch.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Eliminates a branch from the inner O(size) word loop (run n times => O(n*size) overall); the peeled iteration runs once per item. Identical bit result.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: None: the peeled j==offset case omits exactly the carry term that the original guard already skipped (since j-offset-1 = -1 < 0). Word ordering of the OR-into-self descending sweep is preserved, so no read-after-write hazard is introduced.

src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.summary: RunSpaceEfficient is an exact alias of Run (already 1D/space-efficient), implying a distinction that does not exist and risking caller confusion.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.currentCost: Two public symbols with identical behavior; no perf cost but discoverability/maintenance cost and an implied 2D-vs-1D contract that isn't real.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.proposedChange: Either remove RunSpaceEfficient (Run is already the space-efficient 1D form) or document explicitly that Run IS the space-efficient implementation and the alias exists only for API symmetry. Keep the AggressiveInlining alias if external API stability is required.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.rationale: Clarifies the API surface (Run/Try* convention) without a perf model change; reduces the chance a caller assumes RunSpaceEfficient is cheaper.
src/IAFahim.DP.Knapsack/Knapsack.cs.risk: Removing a public method is a source-breaking API change; if external callers depend on it, keep the alias and only add documentation. No runtime behavior change either way.

src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant cost term (a[j+1]-a[i]) out of the inner k-loop and add it once after the loop.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.currentCost: Inside the hot k-loop, every iteration computes a[j+1]-a[i] (two loads + subtract) and adds it into val, even though this term is identical for all k. That is 2 loads + 2 adds per candidate split, plus the comparison only needs the variable part.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.proposedChange: Compute 'long cost = a[j + 1] - a[i];' once before the loop. In the loop compute 'long val = dp[i*n+k] + dp[(k+1)*n+j];' and compare those; after selecting bestK return 'best + cost' (guarding the long.MaxValue sentinel case where bestK==-1 by returning best unchanged). Since cost is added uniformly to every candidate, argmin over (val) equals argmin over (val+cost), so bestK is unchanged and the returned value best+cost is identical.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.rationale: Removes 2 memory loads and 1 add from each inner-loop iteration (the dominant O(n^3)-ish total work via Knuth's O(n^2) split ranges). The two array loads a[j+1], a[i] also no longer pollute the dependency chain of the comparison, shortening the critical path and improving Burst vectorization/ILP.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.risk: If the loop never executes (start>end), best stays long.MaxValue; adding cost would overflow. Guard: only add cost when bestK != -1 (i.e. 'return bestK == -1 ? best : best + cost;'). With the original code this case returns long.MaxValue unchanged, so the guard preserves exact semantics.

src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.summary: Hoist the invariant base index i*n out of the k-loop to strength-reduce address computation.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.currentCost: Each inner iteration recomputes dp[i*n+k] requiring the multiply i*n every time (and i*n+j-1 etc are recomputed for the opt reads). i is fixed for the whole call.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.proposedChange: Compute 'int rowI = i * n;' once and index 'dp[rowI + k]'. Also reuse rowI for 'opt[rowI + j]' / 'opt[rowI + (j-1)]' and the final 'opt[rowI + j] = bestK;'. The (k+1)*n term still varies with k but can be kept as a running offset 'kp1Row += n' incremented each iteration instead of a multiply.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.rationale: Replaces a multiply on the address-generation path per iteration with an add/precomputed base, reducing dependency-chain length and freeing the multiplier unit. Maintaining (k+1)*n as a running accumulator turns a multiply into a single add per step.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.risk: Pure index algebra; identical addresses. n*(k+1) fits in int for realistic n (same as existing code which already does (k+1)*n in int). No overflow change versus current behavior.

src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.summary: Recompute-free bound and fuse: n*n is recomputed every iteration of the clear loop, and the dp=0 clear is redundant work that can be narrowed.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.currentCost: 'for (int i = 0; i < n*n; i++)' recomputes n*n each iteration (Burst likely hoists this, but it is not guaranteed at source level), and it clears dp[i]=0 across the full n*n region even though only the upper-triangular dp[i*n+j] (j>=i) entries are ever read.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.proposedChange: Hoist 'int total = n * n;' before the loop and use it as the bound. Optionally, since dp's diagonal is left 0 and Run only reads dp[i*n+j] for j>=i (all of which are written by ComputeRow or are the len==1 diagonal which stays 0), the dp clear is only needed for entries the algorithm reads; but the simplest safe win is just hoisting total. The opt[i]=-1 init is required as a sentinel.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.rationale: Guarantees the bound multiply is computed once. Linear-pass init is memory-bound; ensuring no per-iteration multiply keeps it purely streaming, which Burst vectorizes (it can emit a vector store of zeros for dp and broadcast -1 for opt if split into two simple loops).
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.risk: Hoisting total is exact. Splitting the combined loop into two separate streaming loops (one zeroing dp, one setting opt=-1) changes write ordering but not final state; both arrays are distinct so no aliasing concern.

src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.summary: Eliminate redundant midpoint recomputation and the wasteful swap-then-store pattern; write the better line directly.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.currentCost: midX is computed as x1+(x2-x1)/2 but 'mid=(l+r)>>1' is also computed and used only in recursion bounds — both are needed, fine. However the swap path does Swap(ref m,ref curMidM); Swap(ref b,ref curMidB); then stores curMid back: that is 6 assignments plus two stores when a direct 'store new line, keep old as the descending line' needs fewer moves.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.proposedChange: Replace the swap+store with branch that picks (loM,loB) = better-at-mid line to store and (hiM,hiB)=other line to recurse with: 'bool better = m*midX+b < curMidM*midX+curMidB; long keepM = better? m:curMidM; long keepB = better? b:curMidB; long passM = better? curMidM:m; long passB = better? curMidB:b; seg[node*2]=keepM; seg[node*2+1]=keepB;' then recurse with passM/passB. This removes the two ref-Swap calls and the conditional double-store, leaving exactly two unconditional stores and branchless selects.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.rationale: Turns a data-dependent swap (two XCHG-like sequences + conditional store) into branchless conditional-move selects plus two unconditional stores, shortening the critical path and removing a branch Burst would otherwise predicate awkwardly. Fewer ref-parameter Swap calls also avoids any aliasing pessimization.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.risk: Must preserve which line continues downward. In the original, after swapping, the line that recurses is the one NOT kept at mid (the displaced m,b). The select formulation keeps that exact assignment, so behavior is identical. Note seg stores were previously skipped when !betterAtMid; making them unconditional rewrites the same values (no change) but adds a store on the no-swap path — if that store-back of identical data is undesirable, guard it with 'if(better)'; recommend keeping the guard to avoid an extra write per node.

src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.summary: midX division can be a shift only if (x2-x1) is known non-negative; current /2 on a signed long is a real divide.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.currentCost: midX = x1 + (x2 - x1) / 2 performs a signed 64-bit division by 2, which the compiler must emit as (val + (val>>63 & 1))>>1 to round toward zero, not a plain arithmetic shift.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.proposedChange: If x2 >= x1 is an invariant of the coordinate domain (it is, since x1<x2 for a valid Li Chao segment), replace '(x2 - x1) / 2' with '(x2 - x1) >> 1'. For a non-negative dividend, >>1 equals /2 exactly.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.rationale: Replaces the signed-division-by-2 fixup sequence (add of sign bit then shift) with a single arithmetic shift, removing 1-2 ops on the recursion's per-node path.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.risk: Only valid if (x2 - x1) >= 0. For signed values this holds iff x1 <= x2, which is the standard Li Chao precondition (the tree spans [x1,x2] with x1<x2). If callers could pass x1>x2, >>1 rounds toward negative infinity and differs; since these are 'Run' unchecked methods assuming valid input, the x1<=x2 invariant makes it safe. State the invariant in docs.

src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.summary: AggressiveInlining on the leaf hot helpers to ensure Burst/JIT inlines across the call boundary.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.currentCost: FindBestSplit and ComputeRow are separate private methods called per cell/row; without inlining hints there is call overhead and lost cross-procedure optimization (the i*n hoist and cost hoist span ComputeRow->FindBestSplit).
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.proposedChange: Annotate FindBestSplit (and optionally ComputeRow) with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]. The using for System.Runtime.CompilerServices is already present.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.rationale: Inlining FindBestSplit into ComputeRow exposes the loop-invariant i*n and the (a[j+1]-a[i]) cost to the enclosing scope, enabling the hoists above and removing per-cell call overhead in the O(n^2)-cells loop.
src/IAFahim.DP.Optimization/Optimization.risk: Inlining a sizeable method can increase code size / I-cache pressure; Burst usually already inlines static unmanaged helpers, so the hint is advisory. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: CanPrune recomputes the suffix-sum of remaining values in an O(n) loop at every node, making the bound computation O(n) per visited node and total O(n * 2^n).
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: CanPrune runs `for (int i = idx; i < n; i++) remaining += value[i];` once per BranchRec call. With up to 2^n nodes, this adds an O(n) factor purely for the bound.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Precompute a suffix-sum array once in Run: `long* suffix = stackalloc long[n + 1]; suffix[n] = 0; for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--) suffix[i] = suffix[i+1] + value[i];` then CanPrune becomes `return curV + suffix[idx] <= bestV;` (O(1)). Pass suffix down the recursion (or store as a pointer param).
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Strips an entire O(n) factor off the dominant recursion: total bound cost drops from O(n * nodes) to O(nodes), plus one O(n) precompute. The suffix sum is loop-invariant across the whole search, so recomputing it per node is pure redundant work.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: Identical results: suffix[idx] equals the original loop sum exactly. Adds n+1 longs of stack (8(n+1) bytes); fine for the small n that branch-and-bound targets. No signedness/overflow change since the additions are the same.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: The 2D tabulation recomputes `int cols = (int)capacity + 1` per row and recomputes `i*cols` and `(i-1)*cols` base offsets inside the inner loop for every column.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: Inner loop over w does index math `dp[i * cols + (int)w]`, `dp[(i-1)*cols + (int)w]`, `dp[(i-1)*cols + (int)(w - weight[i-1])]` — multiple multiplies (i*cols) and (int) casts per cell across (n+1)*(capacity+1) cells.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `long* row = dp + (long)i * cols;` and `long* prev = dp + (long)(i - 1) * cols;` once per row, then index `row[w]`, `prev[w]`, `prev[w - weight[i-1]]`. Also hoist `long wi = weight[i-1]; long vi = value[i-1];`. Since w fits the loop bound, index with the long w directly instead of (int) casting each access.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Removes a multiply and an add per cell (base offsets become loop-invariant pointer adds computed once per row), shrinks the dependency chain, and lets Burst keep the row pointers in registers. Strictly fewer cycles per cell with no behavior change.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: None for valid inputs: row/prev pointers index the same elements. Caller already guarantees capacity fits int (existing code casts to int), so (long)i*cols addressing is safe and equal.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: Bounded knapsack uses naive O(capacity * count) per item; this can be reduced to O(capacity * log(count)) via binary-decomposition into 0/1 items, or O(capacity) via monotonic-deque sliding-window max.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: For each item, the double loop `for w in [capacity..0]` x `for k in [1..count] while k*weight<=w` costs O(capacity*count) and recomputes `k*weight` and `k*value` every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Replace with binary splitting: decompose count into powers (1,2,4,...,rem) and run the standard 0/1 backward update for each piece — O(capacity * log count). For best asymptotics use the monotone-deque grouped-by-residue method to get O(capacity) per item. As a cheap interim win, at least hoist/strength-reduce k*weight and k*value to running adds (`kw += weight; kv += value;`).
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Lowers the dominant factor from count to log(count) (or to 1 with the deque), a genuine asymptotic improvement. The interim strength-reduction alone removes two multiplies from the innermost loop.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: Binary decomposition yields identical reachable (count,value) combinations as the naive loop, so results match. The deque method needs careful residue handling but is a known equivalent. The interim k*weight->running-add must guard against the same loop bounds (k*weight<=w) — keep kw as the running product to compare.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: SubsetSum uses a bool[] DP at O(n*target) bytes/ops while the file already contains BitsetSubsetSum doing the same in O(n*target/64). The bool variant's inner loop is also not strength-reduced.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: bool* dp of size target+1, inner loop `for s in [target..val] if(dp[s-val]) dp[s]=true` — one byte per state, branchy, no word-level parallelism; total O(n*target) byte ops.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: For the boolean reachability question, prefer the existing BitsetSubsetSum path (64x fewer iterations and RAM). If the bool API must stay for ergonomics, at minimum document it as the slow path and consider implementing Run via the bitset internally. Within the bool loop, `(int)val` is recomputed each iteration — hoist `int v = (int)val;` once.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Bitset packs 64 states per word and the OR-shift does 64 transitions per instruction: ~64x fewer cycles and ~8x less RAM than the bool array for identical output. Hoisting the cast removes a per-iteration conversion.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: Output is the same boolean reachability. If callers rely on the bool* buffer being filled (full reachability table), bitset only gives the target bit — so either keep both APIs or expose the table. Treat as ergonomics/dedup suggestion, not a forced replacement.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: The inner search bound `Math.Min(mid, optR)` is recomputed every loop iteration, and `dp[k-1]` / `cost[k+mid]` use casts/index math that can be hoisted.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: `for (int k = optL; k <= Math.Min(mid, optR); k++)` calls Math.Min on every iteration of the search loop, and indexes cost[k+mid] with a recomputed mid offset.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int kEnd = mid < optR ? mid : optR;` before the loop and use `k <= kEnd`. Optionally hoist `long* costBase = cost + mid;` so the body is `costBase[k]`. Replace Math.Min with the branchless/inlined ternary already used elsewhere in the file for consistency.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Removes a function-call/compare from each iteration of the hot search loop (the loop bound is loop-invariant) and turns cost[k+mid] into a single-add index. Pure constant-factor cycle reduction.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: kEnd equals Math.Min(mid, optR) exactly, so iteration range is unchanged. Math.Min(long? no, int) — both int, no overflow on the compare.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: AlienDp takes a managed delegate `Func<long,long,long> dist`, which is a managed type invoked in the innermost loop — this defeats Burst compilation and prevents inlining of the distance function.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: `Func<long,long,long>` is a managed reference type; calling dist(cur, arr[i]) is a virtual delegate invoke per element inside a binary-search-driven O(n log range) loop, with no inlining and a managed allocation/GC dependency. Burst cannot compile methods taking System.Func.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Replace Func<long,long,long> with an unmanaged function pointer `delegate*<long,long,long>` (Burst/function-pointer-friendly), or make AlienDp generic over an unmanaged struct implementing the distance via a constrained interface-free pattern (struct with a static method). This keeps it blittable and Burst-compilable while allowing inlining.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Removes the only managed type on the hot path of this class, enabling Burst codegen and inlining of dist — turning a non-Burstable method into a Burstable one and eliminating per-call delegate dispatch overhead in the innermost loop.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: delegate*<...> requires callers to pass an unmanaged function pointer (semantics identical for the same function). This is an API change but aligns with house constraints (no interfaces/managed types). Same numeric results.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: Both recompute `(1 << n)` (the mask upper bound) and `(1 << i)` every iteration of the inner mask loop, and iterate all masks while only half have bit i set.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: `for (int mask = 0; mask < (1 << n); mask++) if ((mask & (1 << i)) != 0) ...` — recomputes 1<<n per loop test and 1<<i per iteration; processes 2^n masks but skips half via branch, so half the iterations are pure overhead plus a branch misprediction source.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int full = 1 << n; int bit = 1 << i;`. Then iterate only masks with bit set without branching: `for (int high = bit; high < full; high = (high + bit) | bit)` is fiddly; simpler is the standard SOS form `for (int mask = 0; mask < full; mask++) if ((mask & bit) != 0) f[mask] += f[mask ^ bit];` with bit hoisted — or iterate blocks: outer over high bits, inner over low bits stepping by bit, touching only set-bit masks (eliminates the branch entirely and halves loop trips).
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Hoisting removes two shifts per iteration; the block-iteration form removes the per-mask branch and halves the loop count for the set-bit work, improving both cycle count and branch predictor behavior with identical results.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: Standard SOS block iteration visits exactly the masks where bit is set, same as the branch, so f[] updates are identical. Must keep f[mask] += f[mask ^ bit] order (in-place, current bit only) — unchanged.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: cost[i*n+j] is loop-invariant across the k split loop but is re-read (and re-indexed) every iteration; row base pointers for dp can also be hoisted.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: Inner loop `for k: val = (i<k?dp[i*n+k-1]:0) + (k<j?dp[(k+1)*n+j]:0) + cost[i*n+j]` recomputes cost[i*n+j] index+load each k, and recomputes i*n base each iteration.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `long c = cost[i * n + j];` and `long* dpRowI = dp + (long)i * n;` before the loop; inside use `dpRowI[k-1]` for the left term and add `c` once. The right term dp[(k+1)*n+j] still varies by k but its base can be incremented.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Removes a redundant load+multiply-add per k iteration (cost term is constant for fixed i,j) and strength-reduces the left index. Constant-factor win in an O(n^3) hot loop, so the absolute saving scales with n^3.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: c equals cost[i*n+j] for all k, so the sum is identical. Boundary ternaries (i<k, k<j) preserved. No overflow change.

src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.summary: The k-loop indexes a[i*n+k] (row, stride 1, good) but b[k*n+j] (column, stride n) causing a cache miss roughly every iteration; a[i*n+k] base and b column base can be hoisted, and the access pattern is cache-hostile.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.currentCost: b[k*n+j] strides by n longs (8n bytes) each k, so for n beyond a cache-line worth it touches a new line every iteration -> ~n cache misses per (i,j), O(n^3) misses total. a[i*n+k] base i*n is recomputed conceptually each call.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `long* aRow = a + (long)i * n;` (then aRow[k]) and `long* bCol = b + j;` (then bCol[(long)k*n]). For the cache problem, transpose b once into b^T (O(n^2) one-time, O(n^2) scratch) so the inner loop reads bT[j*n+k] sequentially — turning the strided column walk into a linear scan and making it vectorizable by Burst.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.rationale: Transposing b converts O(n^3) strided/cache-missing accesses into sequential ones (huge cache-miss reduction and enables SIMD min/max+add), and pointer hoisting removes per-iteration base multiplies. Asymptotically same O(n^3) compute but dramatically better memory behavior.
src/IAFahim.DP/Dp.cs.risk: Transpose needs an n^2 scratch buffer (caller-provided per house rules, no managed alloc) and produces identical sums (a[i,k]+b[k,j] unchanged). If no scratch is acceptable, the pointer-hoist alone is still a safe, smaller win. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.summary: Convert recursive path-compression find into an iterative two-pass loop to remove call-stack overhead and stack-overflow risk on deep chains.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.currentCost: Recursion: one stack frame per node along the path to root, each with a call/return, argument passing, and a write-back on unwind. Under Burst the recursion is unlikely to be inlined/optimized into a loop, so a chain of length L costs L frames plus L dependency-chained returns. On pathological long chains (e.g. union without union-by-size feeding this find) it can stack overflow.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.proposedChange: Rewrite iteratively: first walk `root = x; while (parent[root] != root) root = parent[root];` then a second walk `while (parent[x] != root) { int next = parent[x]; parent[x] = root; x = next; }` Two linear passes, no recursion, identical final parent[] state and return value.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.rationale: Eliminates per-node call frames and the return dependency chain; both passes are simple pointer-chase loops Burst compiles tightly. Same O(path length) work but lower constant factor and bounded stack usage.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.risk: Observable behavior identical: every node on the path ends pointing directly at root, return value is root. No signedness/overflow concerns.

src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.summary: Convert recursive parity find into an iterative two-pass loop to remove recursion overhead and stack-overflow risk.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.currentCost: Recursion with a post-order side effect: parity[x] ^= parity[p] and parent[x] = root are applied on unwind, so the whole path is held on the call stack (L frames) before any write-back. Deep chains risk stack overflow and the unwind creates a serial dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.proposedChange: Two-pass iterative: pass 1 find root via `r = x; while (parent[r] != r) r = parent[r];` then accumulate parity along the path and compress. Standard approach: walk from x to root summing XOR of edge parities to get total parity-to-root, then second walk re-pointing each node to root and setting parity[node] = (running XOR from node to root). Preserves the same compressed parent[] and parity[] result.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.rationale: Removes L call frames and the unwind dependency chain; pointer-chase loops vectorize/pipeline far better under Burst than self-recursion, which Burst generally cannot turn into a loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.risk: Must reproduce the exact accumulated parity semantics (parity[x] relative to root) so outputs are bit-identical; careful ordering of the XOR accumulation required. No overflow concern (parity is 0/1).

src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.summary: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to the hot leaf find/swap/record helpers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.currentCost: DsuFind.Run, DsuRollbackUnion.FindSimple, Swap, RecordHistory, DsuBipartiteAdd.FindBipartiteRoot etc. are tiny leaf methods called once or twice per union. Without explicit inlining hints, call overhead (arg setup, branch) is paid per invocation; `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;` is already imported but the attribute is unused.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.proposedChange: Annotate the small hot helpers (DsuFind.Run, FindSimple, Swap, RecordHistory, FindBipartiteRoot, RecordBipartiteHistory, UpdateBipartiteMerge) with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)].
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.rationale: Inlining these leaf functions removes call/return overhead and lets Burst/LLVM see across the boundary to keep root indices and size values in registers, eliminating redundant reloads through the int* pointers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.risk: None semantically. Inlining the two find calls in Union duplicates a pointer-chase loop but does not change results; only code size grows slightly.

src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.summary: Hoist parity[a]^parity[b] and use the already-computed roots instead of re-reading parent[ra] for the attach-direction test.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.currentCost: `parity[a] ^ parity[b]` is computed up to twice (the same-root branch and the two merge branches each recompute it). Also `if (parent[ra] == ra)` re-loads parent[ra] from memory even though ra is already a root by construction (DsuParityFind compresses so parent[ra]==ra is always true after the find), making the else-branch effectively dead/asymmetric and the load redundant.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int pab = parity[a] ^ parity[b];` once and reuse. Since ra is always a root after a compressing find, the `parent[ra] == ra` test is always true and the else branch is unreachable for valid input; if union-by-size is not desired here, drop the branch and always do `parent[ra] = rb; parity[ra] = pab ^ w;`. If the asymmetric attach is intentional, document it; otherwise this removes a redundant load and a never-taken branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.rationale: Eliminates a redundant XOR recompute and a redundant memory load plus an always-true branch, shortening the dependency chain on the hot union path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.risk: Must confirm parent[ra]==ra invariant holds (it does given RunPathCompression-style find sets parent[root]=root). If a caller mutates parent between find and union the branch could matter — but within Run it cannot. Verify before removing the branch; the pab hoist alone is unconditionally safe.

src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.summary: DsuRollbackSnapshot.Run is an identity function taking an unused int* history; drop the dead pointer parameter.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.currentCost: `Run(int* history, int histSize)` ignores `history` and returns `histSize` unchanged — a no-op wrapper that still forces the caller to pass and the JIT/Burst to pass an unused pointer argument, and is misleading API surface.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.proposedChange: Either remove the class entirely (callers can read histSize directly) or reduce the signature to `Run(int histSize) => histSize`, dropping the unused int* history parameter.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.rationale: Removes an unused argument from the calling convention and clarifies the API; a snapshot of an append-only history is just its current length, so no work is needed.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.risk: API change — any caller passing history must be updated. Purely mechanical; no behavioral change to the value returned.

src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.summary: Cache *currentHistSize in a local across the rollback loop instead of dereferencing the pointer on every step.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.currentCost: In the `while (*currentHistSize > targetHistSize)` loop, RollbackStep does `*currentHistSize -= 3` and then three `history[*currentHistSize + k]` reads, each re-dereferencing the currentHistSize pointer. The loop condition also re-loads *currentHistSize each iteration. That is repeated pointer indirection that the compiler may not prove non-aliasing against history/parent/size.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.proposedChange: Load `int hs = *currentHistSize;` once, run the loop on the local (`while (hs > targetHistSize) { hs -= 3; int par = history[hs]; ... }`), then write back `*currentHistSize = hs;` after the loop. Inline RollbackStep into the loop body.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.rationale: Removes potential aliasing barrier: the compiler cannot assume *currentHistSize is unchanged by writes through history/parent/size pointers, so keeping it in a local breaks the reload-per-iteration and shortens the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.Dsu/Dsu.cs.risk: currentHistSize must not alias history/parent/size such that an external observer needs the intermediate value mid-loop — it does not, since the final value is the only observable. Write-back after the loop preserves the same end state.

src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.summary: Recomputes prev-branch and child loads redundantly; hoist into locals to halve branches and loads per node.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.currentCost: Per recursive node the expression 'prev != 0 ? leftChild[prev] : 0' and 'prev != 0 ? rightChild[prev] : 0' are each evaluated twice: once when copying children into the new node (lines 12-13) and again when picking the recursion argument (lines 21 or 24). That is up to 4 conditional-load evaluations and 4 branches per node along an O(log range) path. The 'prev != 0' test is also evaluated 3 times.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.proposedChange: At function entry compute 'int hasPrev = prev; long/int pl = prev != 0 ? leftChild[prev] : 0; int pr = prev != 0 ? rightChild[prev] : 0; int ps = prev != 0 ? sumArr[prev] : 0;' once, then reuse pl/pr/ps in both the node copy and the recursion argument. This removes the duplicate pointer loads and collapses the three 'prev != 0' branches into one.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.rationale: Eliminates redundant memory loads (leftChild[prev]/rightChild[prev] read twice -> once) and redundant branches, shortening the dependency chain on the hot recursive path. Each load is a potential cache miss in the persistent-segment-tree node arena, so halving them matters.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.risk: Pure refactor of evaluation order; identical results. prev==0 still yields 0 for all three. No overflow/signedness concern since values are just copied.

src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.summary: AggressiveInlining on a recursive method is ineffective and can bloat codegen; remove it.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.currentCost: The method is self-recursive (lines 20-24), so the JIT/Burst cannot fully inline it; the [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] attribute either no-ops or forces partial inlining that increases I-cache pressure without removing the call.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.proposedChange: Drop [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] from PersistentFenwickUpdate.Run (and likewise PersistentFenwickQuery.Run). Optionally convert the update walk to an iterative loop since it is single-path (only one child recurses), eliminating the call frame entirely.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.rationale: Inlining a recursive function yields no call-elimination benefit; removing the hint avoids speculative code bloat and lets Burst optimize the body normally. Converting the tail-position single-child descent to an iterative while-loop removes per-level stack frames and the recursion dependency.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.risk: Removing the attribute cannot change semantics. An iterative rewrite must preserve node-allocation order and parent-link wiring exactly; verify the new node's left/right pointer is patched after the child id is known.

src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.summary: Recursive query marked AggressiveInlining; remove the ineffective hint.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.currentCost: Self-recursive (lines 39-40); AggressiveInlining cannot eliminate the recursive calls and risks I-cache bloat.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.proposedChange: Remove [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]. The two-child range query genuinely needs recursion (or an explicit stack), so leave the algorithm but drop the hint.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.rationale: No call is eliminated by inlining a recursive method; the attribute only adds codegen pressure.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/PersistentFenwick.risk: None; attribute removal is semantically inert.

src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.summary: Highest-set-bit loop is recomputed; can be derived branchlessly and the total can reuse it, but main win is replacing the O(log n) bit-find loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.currentCost: Lines 69-70 spin a 'while ((bitMask << 1) <= n) bitMask <<= 1;' loop to find the top power of two, costing ~log2(n) iterations/branches before the real descent. The same loop is duplicated in LowerBoundInt64 (line 44).
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.proposedChange: Replace the while-loop with a single highest-bit computation: bitMask = 1 << (31 - lzcnt((uint)n)) when n>0 (Unity.Burst.Intrinsics.X86 / math.lzcnt or a portable de Bruijn). Factor it into a private static helper HighestPowerOfTwoLE(n) shared by both bound methods to remove the duplicated loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.rationale: Strength-reduces an O(log n) prologue loop to a single lzcnt-based O(1) op, and deduplicates identical code so Burst emits it once. lzcnt maps to a single hardware instruction on the targeted PC/mobile ISAs Burst supports.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.risk: Guard n==0 (lzcnt(0) is undefined / yields 32); current methods already handle small n. Must return identical bitMask for the descent. Use (uint) cast to avoid sign issues with 31-lzcnt; behavior identical for all n>=1.

src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.summary: Duplicated implementation of FenwickRangeSum.RunLong; both walk two prefix sums independently though shared tree-walk could be fused for adjacent l,r (minor).
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.currentCost: RangeSumInt64 calls SumInt64 twice (lines 28,30) doing two independent O(log n) ascents from r and l-1, recomputing 'idx & -idx' for overlapping high-order path segments.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.proposedChange: Leave as-is unless a fused dual-walk is desired; the existing two-call form is standard and branch-light. If fusion is wanted, walk both r and l-1 in a single loop subtracting where indices diverge, but the readability/Burst-vectorization tradeoff is marginal.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.rationale: Two separate descents share their common ancestor path; a fused walk avoids re-traversing it. However the saving is at most a few iterations and adds branches, so net win is small.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/Fenwick.cs.risk: A fused implementation risks off-by-one on the divergence point; the current two-call version is provably correct. Recommend NOT changing unless profiled.

src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.summary: FenwickLowerBound.Run omits the 'target <= 0' early-out that Fenwick.LowerBoundInt64 has, giving inconsistent behavior for non-positive targets.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.currentCost: With target <= 0, the descent in FenwickLowerBound.Run still runs the full O(log n) loop and, because 'bit[next] < target' is false for non-negative entries when target<=0, returns 0 anyway but after wasted iterations. The canonical Fenwick.LowerBoundInt64 short-circuits at line 41.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.proposedChange: Add 'if (target <= 0) return 0;' as the first statement to match Fenwick.LowerBoundInt64 and skip the descent. This unifies the two implementations' contracts.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.rationale: Saves the entire descent for the common 'target<=0' query and makes the two API surfaces behaviorally identical, reducing surprise.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.risk: For target<=0 the loop already returns 0 given non-negative values (the documented precondition), so the early-out is semantics-preserving under that assumption. If callers ever pass negative bit entries the early-out would differ, but the non-negative precondition forbids that.

src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.summary: q is computed as idx+1 before mutating idx; the multiply uses int q widened to long. Minor: cache the two BIT loads share index stream and could be interleaved-friendly already.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.currentCost: Line 171 saves q=idx+1, then the loop reads bit1[idx] and bit2[idx] (two pointer loads per level from separate arrays, line 174-175). res1*q at line 177 widens int q to long.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.proposedChange: Keep the algorithm. Optionally hoist q as a long ('long q = idx + 1;') to make the final 'res1 * q' a long*long multiply without an int->long widening cast in the hot return; negligible but free. No structural change recommended otherwise.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.rationale: Avoids a sign-extension instruction on the result path; effectively free and clarifies the 64-bit intent.
src/IAFahim.DS.Fenwick/FenwickOps.cs.risk: None for valid idx within int range; the product res1*q must stay 64-bit which it already is.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.summary: Replace `idx = (idx + 1) % this.Capacity` in the open-addressing probe loops with a branchless/branch wrap to remove an integer division per probe step.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.currentCost: Each probe iteration executes an integer `%` against a runtime `Capacity` that is not a compile-time power of two. Integer division/modulo is ~20-40 cycles on most ARM/x86 cores and cannot be strength-reduced by Burst since Capacity is a runtime value. This is the innermost hot loop of every Add/Find.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.proposedChange: Increment then wrap with a compare instead of modulo: `idx++; if (idx == this.Capacity) idx = 0;` (or the branchless form `idx++; idx -= (idx == this.Capacity ? this.Capacity : 0);`). Since idx starts in [0,Capacity) and increments by exactly 1, it can only ever equal Capacity, never exceed it, so a single equality test is exactly equivalent to `% Capacity`.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.rationale: Removes a full integer-division uop from the dependency chain of every probe step, replacing it with an add + predicated subtract (1-2 cycles). Linear probing typically does many steps near load, so this is a real per-step win.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.risk: Equivalent only because the step is exactly +1 and idx is always < Capacity before the step; holds for both loops here. No signed/overflow concern since Capacity << int.MaxValue.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.summary: `hash % (uint)Capacity` is an unavoidable division per lookup, but the (uint)Capacity cast and reciprocal can be precomputed once at construction.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.currentCost: GetFirstIdx runs once per TryAdd/Find/TryGetValue and does a 32-bit unsigned division by a runtime Capacity. Burst cannot fold this because Capacity is not const.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.proposedChange: Precompute and store `uint capacityU` (and optionally a libdivide-style magic/shift pair) at construction time alongside Capacity, and use it in GetFirstIdx and the wrap. At minimum cache `(uint)this.Capacity` to avoid the repeated cast; ideally store a precomputed multiply-shift reciprocal to turn the modulo into a mul+shift+sub.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.rationale: Division by a value known only at construction can be converted to a multiply+shift using a fixed reciprocal computed once, trading a ~25-cycle div for ~5 cycles on every hash lookup.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.risk: The full reciprocal path adds code/complexity and must be verified for the exact Capacity range; the cheap cast-caching variant is risk-free. Note Capacity could be 0 if TCapacity is too small for one element — division by zero is already a latent issue in current code, unchanged by this.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.summary: The `fixed` pin + pointer arithmetic for Ptr/NumItems/Keys/values is recomputed on every access inside the probe loops; hoist the base pointers into locals once per public call.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.currentCost: `this.Ptr` re-pins `&this.data` and recasts on every single dereference (`this.Ptr[idx]`, `this.Keys[idx]`, `this.NumItems[firstIdx]`, and value base in GetElementAt each recompute `capacity * (...)`). In the do/while loops Ptr is dereferenced once per iteration plus Keys per match, each going through a property getter with a fixed-statement.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.proposedChange: At the top of TryAdd/Find/TryGetValue, take `uint* hashes = this.Ptr; int* numItems = (int*)(hashes + Capacity); TKey* keys = (TKey*)(hashes + Capacity*2);` once, plus the value base pointer, and index those locals in the loop. Hoists the pin, the casts, and the `capacity * stride` multiply out of the per-iteration path.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.rationale: Eliminates a repeated pin + multiply + property-call from the hot probe loop, shortening the dependency chain and helping Burst keep the bases in registers. Pointers into the same fixed struct are stable for the call duration.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.risk: Pinning once for the whole method is semantically identical here since `data` is a struct field that does not move; just ensure all loop accesses use the hoisted locals so no GC-hole assumptions break (unmanaged blittable, so fine).

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.summary: Per-bucket `NumItems` counter array (int per bucket) costs Capacity*4 bytes of the fixed storage and shrinks effective Capacity; reconsider whether it is needed or can be narrowed.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.currentCost: Layout is [uint hash][int numItems][TKey][TValue] per slot, so 4 bytes/slot go to NumItems. CalcCapacity divides total size by (4+4+key+value); the numItems word roughly halves capacity for small key/value types and adds a cache line touch (NumItems[firstIdx]) separate from the hashes array.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.proposedChange: If NumItems counts only collisions-into-this-home-bucket for early-out in Find, it can be a narrower type (byte/ushort) given Capacity is bounded, or removed in favor of probing until an empty slot (uint.MaxValue) as TryAdd already does. Narrowing to byte recovers 3 bytes/slot of capacity and packs counters into far fewer cache lines.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.rationale: Smaller per-slot footprint increases Capacity for the same TCapacity storage (better load factor / fewer probes) and reduces cache pressure; the counters also become contiguous and prefetch-friendly.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.risk: Removing NumItems changes Find's termination from count-based to empty-slot-based, altering probe counts for missing keys (still correct, but different perf profile and full-table-no-empty edge needs the existing do/while wrap guard). Narrowing requires proving max chain length < type max; behavior-preserving only if the counter cannot overflow, so byte/ushort must be chosen against the max possible Capacity.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.summary: Value-base offset `capacity * (sizeof(uint)+sizeof(int)+sizeof(TKey))` is recomputed every value access and uses `sizeof(int)` for the NumItems stride while NumItems is `int*` and hashes are `uint*` — keep the stride constants centralized to avoid drift and recompute.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.currentCost: The constant base offset (independent of idx) is multiplied out on every GetElementAt call; only `idx * sizeOfValueT` actually varies. Also the per-slot stride literal is duplicated between CalcCapacity (sizeof(uint)+sizeof(uint)+...) and GetElementAt (sizeof(uint)+sizeof(int)+...).
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.proposedChange: Precompute the constant value-region base offset once at construction (or hoist per-call) and add only `idx * sizeOfValueT` at access time. Define the per-slot stride as a single computed field used by both CalcCapacity and the offset math to guarantee they agree.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.rationale: Removes a multiply from each value access and removes a duplicated/divergent magic expression, lowering both cycles and maintenance risk.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedHas.risk: sizeof(int)==sizeof(uint)==4 so the two expressions are numerically identical today; centralizing is purely defensive and behavior-preserving. Caching the base offset is safe because Capacity and sizes are fixed after construction.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.summary: `Length` calls `UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>()` at runtime instead of using `sizeof(T)` which Burst/IL can fold to a compile-time constant.
