src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.currentCost: `UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() << 3` is a method call returning a value Burst may not constant-fold as aggressively as the `sizeof` operator; Length is used inside CheckArgs on every Set/IsSet.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.proposedChange: Use `sizeof(T) << 3` (the struct is already `unsafe` and T is `unmanaged`, so `sizeof(T)` is legal and compile-time constant). Matches the pattern already used in FixedArray.Length (`sizeof(TS)/sizeof(T)`).
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.rationale: `sizeof` on an unmanaged generic resolves to a constant per specialization, letting the bounds check fold to a constant comparison; method-call form can defeat that.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.risk: Behaviorally identical; both yield the byte size of T. Reset() already uses UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() — could likewise switch to sizeof(T) for consistency but no semantic change.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.summary: Set/IsSet re-pin `&this.data` and reload through byte* on every call; for the common case where T is a single integer this could index the value directly, and these leaf methods lack AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.currentCost: Each Set/IsSet does a `fixed` pin and byte addressing even though pos>>Idx / pos&Shift are cheap; no inlining hint means call overhead on hot bit-twiddling paths.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]` to Set and IsSet (consistent with FixedArray's accessors). Keep the byte* addressing (it is endian-correct and generic over T), but the inline hint lets Burst fold the pin away when the caller's `this` is a local.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.rationale: Inlining these tiny methods removes call/pin overhead and exposes the constant idx/shift to the caller for folding; matches the established inlining convention in the module.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.risk: None for inlining. Do NOT change byte* to typed indexing without preserving little-endian bit ordering — Reset uses MemClear and Set/IsSet use byte addressing, which is consistent; a typed rewrite could change observable bit positions on big-endian, so leave addressing as-is.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.summary: `Shift` is misnamed — it is a bit MASK (7), not a shift amount; rename for clarity without perf change.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.currentCost: `Shift = (1<<Idx)-1 = 7` is used as `pos & Shift`, i.e. it is a mask. The name invites confusion with the actual shift `pos >> Idx`.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.proposedChange: Rename `Shift` to `Mask` (or `BitMask`). Pure naming/ergonomics; the value and codegen are unchanged.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedBit.rationale: Improves discoverability and correctness-of-intent; aligns with house preference for named constants reflecting their role.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.summary: Next() writes `*this.current` then re-reads it for the return; keep the new value in the register and write once.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.currentCost: `*this.current = x1; return *this.current;` does a store followed by a dependent load of the same address through a NativeDisableUnsafePtrRestriction pointer, adding a load to the dependency chain (and Burst may not assume the alias is unchanged).
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.proposedChange: `*this.current = x1; return x1;` — return the local already computed instead of reloading from memory.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.rationale: Removes a memory load from the latency-critical path of an RNG that is typically called in tight loops; returns the value already in a register.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.risk: Behavior-identical: x1 is exactly what was just stored. No aliasing concern since nothing else writes between store and return.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.summary: `(Multiplier * x) + Increment) & int.MaxValue` masks the sign bit; this is a correct fast modulo by 2^31-1 only as a bit clear, but the multiply uses signed int that can overflow — confirm `unchecked` semantics and consider AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.currentCost: Modulus is int.MaxValue (2^31-1) and the code uses `& Modulus` (clear top bit) rather than a true `% (2^31-1)`. These are NOT the same operation: `& 0x7FFFFFFF` is `mod 2^31`, not `mod (2^31-1)`. The constant is named Modulus but used as a mask.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.proposedChange: Either rename the constant to `Mask = 0x7FFFFFFF` to reflect that this LCG uses modulus 2^31 with the sign bit cleared (the actual implemented behavior), or, if a true Mersenne-style mod 2^31-1 was intended, fix the operation. Also add `[MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]` to Next() for tight-loop callers. This is flagged as a semantics/naming clarity item, not a silent change.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.rationale: The mask form is fast (1 cycle) and fine for a 31-bit-state LCG, but the `Modulus`/`& ` mismatch is a latent correctness/clarity hazard for anyone relying on the named period. Inlining helps the per-draw cost.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/NativeLi.risk: Do NOT change `&` to `%` blindly — that WOULD change the output sequence. The safe action is renaming the constant to document the real (mask) behavior; only change the operator if the math sequence is intended to be redefined (which breaks determinism for existing seeds).

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedArr.summary: FixedArray is already near-optimal; the only note is that `Length = sizeof(TS)/sizeof(T)` divides per access — for power-of-two element sizes this is a constant per specialization and folds, so no action unless Length is hot.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedArr.currentCost: `sizeof(TS)/sizeof(T)` is a compile-time-constant ratio per (TS,T) specialization, so Burst already folds it to an immediate. CheckIndexInRange is Conditional and elided in release. Buffer is AggressiveInlined and pins per access.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedArr.proposedChange: No change required; structure is correct. If profiling ever shows Buffer's per-access `fixed` pin as hot, it could be hoisted by callers, but within this struct it is already inlined and the pin is free for a non-moving struct field under Burst.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/FixedArr.rationale: Confirming the file is already optimal avoids inventing work; the sizeof ratio and Conditional checks are the right patterns.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.summary: Inner busy-spin loop lacks a CPU pause/yield hint, causing pipeline stalls, memory-order mis-speculation flushes, and excess coherence traffic that starves the lock holder.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.currentCost: while (Volatile.Read(ref this.@lock) == 1) {} spins as tightly as the core can issue loads. On x86 this floods the load buffer and triggers memory-order machine clears on lock release; on ARM (mobile) it pegs a core at full clock, hammering the shared cache line and burning power while the holder tries to make progress.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.proposedChange: Insert a spin-wait hint inside the inner loop body: call System.Threading.Thread.SpinWait(1) (or an intrinsic pause if available under Burst) once per iteration, e.g. 'while (Volatile.Read(ref this.@lock) == 1) { System.Threading.Thread.SpinWait(1); }'. Optionally use an exponentially growing iteration count capped to a small constant.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.rationale: A pause/yield hint relaxes the load issue rate, eliminates memory-order machine clears on the waiting core, frees execution resources to the SMT sibling, and reduces the number of coherence read requests on the contended line so the releasing/holding thread can take ownership faster. Lower power on mobile for the same correctness.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.risk: Pure throughput/latency improvement; observable lock semantics unchanged (still acquires when lock transitions to 0). Must confirm Thread.SpinWait is Burst-compatible; if not, gate the hint to managed builds or use a Burst intrinsic. No correctness change.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.summary: Under low contention the inner read-spin while-loop adds a redundant branch on the common fast path.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.currentCost: After a failed CompareExchange the code enters the inner while; under brief contention it would be marginally cheaper to retry CompareExchange directly. Current structure: outer for + inner read-while. The inner loop is the right pattern for high contention (read-only spin avoids RMW traffic) so this is minor.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.proposedChange: Keep the test-and-test-and-set structure (it is correct and good for contention) but consider only re-attempting CompareExchange after the read observes 0; the current code already does this via the outer loop, so no change is strictly needed. If desired, mark the method body so the fast-path CompareExchange success is the predicted branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.rationale: The existing test-and-test-and-set already minimizes RMW bus traffic; flagged only to note the structure is intentional and should be preserved when adding the SpinWait hint.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/SpinLock.risk: No change recommended beyond preserving semantics; listed for completeness so the SpinWait edit does not accidentally remove the read-only inner spin.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.summary: length and spinner are two separate heap allocations (and a third for buffer); the int length and SpinLock (also an int) could share one cache-line-sized control allocation, halving allocator calls and improving locality.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.currentCost: Three Unmanaged.Allocate calls per pool: buffer, length (sizeof int), spinner (sizeof SpinLock = int). Two tiny 4-byte allocations sit on independent cache lines far from each other; TryAdd/TryGet touch both length and spinner every call, so they may straddle two cache lines and incur an extra miss. Three Free calls on Dispose.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.proposedChange: Allocate a single small control block (e.g. a struct { SpinLock spinner; int length; } padded to CacheLineSize) in one Unmanaged.Allocate, and point length/spinner into it. Reduces ctor from 3 to 2 allocations and Dispose from 3 to 2 frees, and co-locates the two fields touched together under the lock.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.rationale: Fewer allocator round-trips at construction; spinner and length share one cache line so the locked critical section touches a single line instead of two, cutting one potential cache miss per TryAdd/TryGet. Keeping them on a dedicated padded line also avoids false sharing with buffer contents.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.risk: Must keep the control struct unmanaged/blittable and correctly aligned (AlignOf of the control struct). Pointer arithmetic into the block must respect field offsets. Behavior identical. Padding to a full cache line trades a few bytes of RAM for avoiding false sharing — acceptable given the pool is shared across threads.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.summary: Inside the lock, *this.length is dereferenced multiple times through the pointer; load it once into a local to shorten the dependency chain and avoid redundant loads the compiler may not coalesce across the volatile-like pointer.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.currentCost: TryAdd reads *this.length for the compare, again for the index store, again for the increment store (3 pointer dereferences). TryGet reads it for compare, decrement, and index. Each is a load/store through a raw pointer; the JIT/Burst may reload because it cannot always prove no aliasing.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.proposedChange: In TryAdd: 'int len = *this.length; if (len < this.capacity) { this.buffer[len] = element; *this.length = len + 1; ... }'. In TryGet: 'int len = *this.length; if (len > 0) { len -= 1; element = this.buffer[len]; *this.length = len; ... }'.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.rationale: Caching the length in a register removes two redundant pointer loads per call and shortens the read-modify-write dependency chain executed while the spinlock is held, reducing critical-section length (which directly reduces contention on the lock).
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.risk: Safe: the value is only mutated by the current thread inside the lock, so no other writer can change *this.length within the critical section. Single-threaded-within-lock invariant makes the local equivalent. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.summary: Release is called on both branches with duplicated code; a single release at the end (with the result in a local) is cleaner and avoids the duplicated Release call site without lengthening the locked region.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.currentCost: Both methods call this.spinner->Release() twice (once per branch). Duplication is harmless but error-prone for future edits and slightly larger code.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.proposedChange: Compute a bool result inside the if/else while holding the lock, then a single this.spinner->Release(); return result; after. Keep the critical section minimal (the work already done under lock is unchanged).
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.rationale: Single release site reduces code size and maintenance risk without changing the amount of work done under the lock.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.risk: Must ensure Release still executes on every path including potential future early returns; structure as one exit. No behavior change since the unlocked sections do no shared work.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.summary: IsCreated is not marked readonly even though the struct is a readonly struct; minor, but TryAdd/TryGet mutate through pointers in a readonly struct which is correct but worth confirming GetCapacity/IsCreated stay side-effect-free.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.currentCost: No functional cost; the struct is 'readonly unsafe struct' and IsCreated only reads buffer. It is implicitly fine, but explicit readonly on the property getter documents purity and can enable defensive-copy elision in some call sites.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.proposedChange: No change required for correctness; optionally annotate IsCreated getter as readonly is already implied by the readonly struct. Leave as-is.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.rationale: Confirms purity; no real optimization. Listed low-impact to note the readonly-struct design is already correct and TryAdd/TryGet legitimately mutate heap memory through pointers without violating the readonly contract.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/Unmanage.risk: No change recommended; included for completeness.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadRa.summary: Seed clamp uses math.min on a uint with a derived constant; the per-iteration cast (uint)(seed + i) recomputes additions that are already in range after clamping.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadRa.currentCost: seed = (uint)math.min(seed, uint.MaxValue - JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount - 1); then loop does CreateFromIndex((uint)(seed + i)). The cast on math.min(uint,uint) is redundant (already uint), and (uint)(seed + i) adds a needless cast since seed+i is uint.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadRa.proposedChange: Drop the redundant (uint) casts: 'seed = math.min(seed, uint.MaxValue - (uint)JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount - 1u);' and 'CreateFromIndex(seed + (uint)i)'. Hoist the loop-invariant ThreadIndexCount into a local once.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadRa.rationale: Removes redundant casts that obscure intent and hoists JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount (a property access) out of the loop bound and clamp into a single local, avoiding repeated property reads per iteration. Construction-time only, so impact is small but free.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadRa.risk: Must verify JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount type and that the unsigned subtraction does not underflow for tiny uint.MaxValue (it cannot; ThreadIndexCount is small). Semantics identical: clamp ensures seed+i stays representable.

src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadLi.summary: JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount is read twice in the ctor (size calc and loop bound) and once per loop check; hoist to a local. Same pattern in Dispose.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadLi.currentCost: JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount appears in the totalSize expression and as the loop condition (re-evaluated each iteration if the JIT cannot prove the property is pure). Property accesses are not always inlined/CSE'd under Burst.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadLi.proposedChange: int count = JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount; use 'count' for totalSize, the init loop bound, and in Dispose. Same for ThreadRandom.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadLi.rationale: Guarantees a single read of the property and a loop with a register-resident bound, enabling the compiler to better optimize the init loop; avoids repeated property dispatch the JIT may not hoist.
src/IAFahim.DS.FixedCollections/ThreadLi.risk: ThreadIndexCount is a fixed process-wide count, so caching it within a single ctor/Dispose call is safe. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.summary: Replace the byte-by-byte gap-shift loops with Unsafe.CopyBlock / Buffer.MemoryCopy-style block moves.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.currentCost: Each gap move copies `gapLen` (or `shift`) bytes one at a time in a scalar loop with a loop-carried address dependency and per-iteration index recomputation (pos+gapLen+i, pos+i). For a buffer of N bytes a single move is O(distance) scalar byte copies — no SIMD, ~1 byte/iteration plus branch overhead.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.proposedChange: MoveGap left-branch: `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.CopyBlock(s.Buffer + pos + gapLen, s.Buffer + pos, (uint)gapLen)` is NOT safe (regions overlap with dst>src). Use a forward/backward-correct overlapping move: call `System.Buffer.MemoryCopy(s.Buffer + pos, s.Buffer + pos + gapLen, ...)` which handles overlap. Right-branch: `System.Buffer.MemoryCopy(s.Buffer + s.GapEnd, s.Buffer + s.GapStart, ...remainingCapacity..., (long)newPos)`. Same two block moves replace the loops in MoveGapTo (the left branch's reversed double-index `pos + gapLen + (gapLen-1-i)` is just a backward memmove of gapLen bytes from pos to pos+gapLen; the right branch is a forward memmove of `shift` bytes from GapEnd to GapStart).
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.rationale: Buffer.MemoryCopy uses an internal vectorized/word-wide overlapping copy (memmove semantics), cutting the move from ~1 byte/cycle to 16-32 bytes per vector op and removing the loop-carried index dependency. The loops are exactly memmove with the correct direction already chosen by the code, so the transformation is mechanical and asymptotics are unchanged but the constant factor drops by an order of magnitude.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.risk: Buffer.MemoryCopy is overlap-safe so direction handling is automatic, but it is a managed BCL call — under Burst it may not be intrinsified. SAFER Burst-friendly path: use `UnsafeUtility.MemMove` (Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe) which Burst lowers to an optimized overlapping copy. If neither is available in this module's dependency set, keep manual loops but widen the copy unit (see separate opportunity). Must keep the existing direction (the left-branch overlaps dst>src so a plain CopyBlock/forward memcpy would corrupt; only a true memmove or the existing reverse loop is correct).

src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.summary: Copy the inserted payload with a block move and drop the redundant per-byte gap-space guard.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.currentCost: The insert loop `for (i<len && s.GapStart<s.GapEnd) s.Buffer[s.GapStart++]=data[i]` does a byte-at-a-time copy plus TWO branch tests per byte (i<len and GapStart<GapEnd), and writes back s.GapStart to a ref field implicitly each iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.proposedChange: Precompute `int n = len < (s.GapEnd - s.GapStart) ? len : (s.GapEnd - s.GapStart);` once (branchless min), then `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy(s.Buffer + s.GapStart, data, n)` (non-overlapping: src is caller data, dst is gap) and `s.GapStart += n;`. Removes the inner double-branch and the per-iteration ref write.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.rationale: Source and gap destination never overlap (data is the caller's separate buffer, dst is the free gap region), so a straight memcpy/CopyBlock applies — vectorized, no per-byte branching. Computing the clamp once converts O(len) branch tests into O(1) and lets the bulk copy run at memory bandwidth.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.risk: Must clamp n to available gap (GapEnd-GapStart) to preserve the current truncation behavior when the payload exceeds the gap — the current loop silently stops at GapEnd, so n=min(len, gapSpace) reproduces it exactly. If the caller could pass overlapping data and buffer regions, MemCpy would be UB; the original loop is also unsafe under self-overlap, so semantics are preserved for all currently-valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.summary: Remove the dead local `int shift` and hoist invariant index bases.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.currentCost: `int shift = s.GapStart - pos;` in the left branch is computed but never used (dead store). Loop bodies recompute `pos + gapLen` and base offsets each iteration even though they are loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.proposedChange: Delete the unused `shift`. If keeping scalar loops, hoist `byte* dst = s.Buffer + pos + gapLen; byte* src = s.Buffer + pos;` (left) and pointer-walk instead of index arithmetic so the JIT/Burst does not redo the add+scale each iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.rationale: Dead-store elimination and invariant hoisting shorten the dependency chain and the encoded instruction count; Burst usually catches these but the dead `shift` is pure noise and removing it clarifies the move is a single memmove.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.risk: None — `shift` is provably unused; hoisting invariants is value-preserving. Superseded by the memmove change if that is adopted.

src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.summary: De-duplicate the two near-identical gap-move routines into one shared static helper.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.currentCost: MoveGap and MoveGapTo implement the same left/right memmove logic with the same GapStart/GapEnd updates; the only divergence is cosmetic (loop index direction in the left branch). This is duplicated code that must be kept in sync and doubles the surface for the same bug class.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.proposedChange: Extract a single `internal static void MoveGap(ref GapBufferState s, int pos)` (e.g. in an internal GapBufferCore static class) and have both Insert.Run and Delete.Run call it. Both branches reduce to the two memmove forms above.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.rationale: Single source of truth removes drift risk and lets one memmove optimization benefit both callers. No perf cost: AggressiveInlining or Burst inlining collapses the call. Note the two left-branches differ only in iteration order yet are equivalent memmoves, confirming they should be merged.
src/IAFahim.DS.GapBuffer/GapBuffer.cs.risk: Behavior-neutral if the merged helper reproduces both branches' GapStart/GapEnd assignments (identical in both files today). Verify the new internal class still satisfies the static-class / unmanaged house constraints (it does).

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors4.cs.summary: Replace managed static int[] offset tables with stackalloc or inline constants so the hot methods are Burst-compatible and avoid static-field array loads.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors4.cs.currentCost: Each call indexes two managed static int[] arrays (DR[d], DC[d]). Managed arrays defeat Burst compilation (Burst cannot access managed static reference fields), force a bounds-checked array load with a null/length check per access, and add an indirection through the static field. House constraints forbid managed arrays in src.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors4.cs.proposedChange: Drop the arrays. Inline the 4 fixed offsets directly as 4 unrolled branchless checks, or use 'int* dr = stackalloc int[4]{-1,1,0,0}; int* dc = stackalloc int[4]{0,0,-1,1};' inside the method. Best: fully unroll the 4 neighbor tests (up/down/left/right) with no loop and no table at all, since offsets are compile-time constants.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors4.cs.rationale: Removes managed heap access entirely (Burst-friendly), eliminates per-iteration array bounds checks and static-field indirection, and lets the JIT/Burst fold the constant offsets. Full unrolling also removes the loop counter dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors4.cs.risk: None to semantics — outputs identical. Must keep the same emission order (up, down, left, right) so the packed output order in nr/nc/outIndices is preserved for any caller relying on order.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors8.cs.summary: Same as GridNeighbors4: replace managed static int[] tables with inline constants / stackalloc to be Burst-safe and drop per-access bounds checks.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors8.cs.currentCost: 8 iterations each load DR[d] and DC[d] from managed static int[] arrays — Burst-incompatible managed references, bounds-checked loads, static-field indirection; violates house no-managed-array rule.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors8.cs.proposedChange: Remove DR/DC arrays; either stackalloc the 8 offsets locally or fully unroll the 8 neighbor checks with literal offsets. Center cell is skipped by construction so no extra branch needed.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors8.cs.rationale: Eliminates managed access (Burst can compile), removes 16 array bounds checks per call, removes static indirection, enables constant folding and removes loop overhead via unrolling.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridNeighbors8.cs.risk: None to semantics; preserve the same 8-direction emission order so packed output order is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.summary: Hoist dist[r*w+c] out of the neighbor loop; it is loop-invariant and recomputed up to 4 times per node.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.currentCost: Inside the d-loop, 'dist[r * w + c] + 1' recomputes the multiply r*w+c and reloads dist[...] on every successful neighbor (up to 4x per node), creating a redundant load-add-multiply chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.proposedChange: Before the loop compute 'int cur = r * w + c; int nd = dist[cur] + 1;' then use 'dist[idx] = nd;'. The caller in Run also computes node/width and node%width then re-derives r*w+c == node, so pass 'node' (the original index) into ProcessNeighbors as 'cur' to avoid recomputing r*w+c entirely.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.rationale: r*w+c is exactly the original 'node' index already known in Run, so the multiply and the modulo/division round-trip is fully redundant. Hoisting removes up to 4 multiplies and 4 dist loads per node and shortens the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.risk: None — dist[node] is set once and not modified during the node's own expansion, so the hoisted value equals every in-loop read. Pure refactor.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.summary: Avoid node/width and node%width by enqueuing/storing row and column (or passing node directly) to remove a division+modulo per dequeued node.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.currentCost: Per dequeued node, 'node / width' and 'node % width' perform an integer divide and a modulo (each ~20-40 cycles, not strength-reducible since width is runtime). Then ProcessNeighbors recomputes nr*w+nc anyway.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.proposedChange: Decode once: 'int r = node / width; int c = node - r * width;' (replaces modulo with a multiply+subtract, cheaper than a second division). Better, pass 'node' as the precomputed center index into ProcessNeighbors so dist[node] needs no recompute, and only the divide for r remains needed for bounds via nr/nc.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.rationale: div/mod on the same operands: computing c = node - r*width reuses the quotient and avoids a second hardware division. Combined with passing node through, removes one full divide-equivalent per node.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.risk: None; node = r*width + c exactly for all enqueued indices, so node - r*width == c. Identical results.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.summary: The dr/dc stackalloc tables are constant offsets that, with ProcessNeighbors inlined and unrolled, can be eliminated entirely.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.currentCost: dr/dc are 4-int stackalloc tables loaded each iteration inside ProcessNeighbors (dr[d], dc[d]) — extra loads on the hot path though stack-local.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.proposedChange: Since ProcessNeighbors is AggressiveInlining and the 4 directions are compile-time constants, fully unroll the 4 neighbor checks with literal +/-1 offsets and remove dr/dc plus the stackalloc in Run.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.rationale: Removes 8 stack loads per node and the loop counter; constant offsets fold into address computation. Frees a few bytes of stack and shortens the inner dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.risk: None — same four neighbors in the same order. Keep emission order to preserve BFS expansion order (matters only if a caller depends on queue order, which is deterministic either way).

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.summary: visited is used as a 0/1 flag stored in 8-byte long; a byte* (or bit-packed) visited array cuts the visited working set 8x and reduces cache misses.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.currentCost: visited is long* but only ever holds 0 or 1. For an HxW grid this is 8*H*W bytes of scratch — 8x larger than needed, hurting cache residency on large grids (the dominant BFS cost is random-access memory traffic).
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.proposedChange: Change visited to byte* (1 byte/cell), or fold visited into dist using a sentinel (dist initialized to -1 means unvisited), eliminating the visited buffer entirely. The dist==-1 sentinel approach removes one whole array's worth of random-access traffic per neighbor.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.rationale: BFS is memory-bound; shrinking visited 8x (or removing it) directly reduces cache misses and bandwidth, the actual bottleneck. Using dist sentinel fuses the visited-check and dist-write into the dist array already being touched.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.risk: Signature change (ergonomics/API break) — flag for caller review. The dist-sentinel variant requires callers to pre-init dist to -1; document as a Try/Run precondition. Behavior of returned count is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.summary: CopyGrid and Rotate180 recompute h*w each iteration / use scalar copy; CopyGrid should use a bulk memcpy and h*w should be hoisted.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.currentCost: CopyGrid loops 'i < h*w' recomputing the product every iteration (h*w not hoisted) and copies long-by-long; a bulk Buffer/Unsafe.CopyBlock moves 8*h*w bytes far faster. Rotate180 already hoists len.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.proposedChange: In CopyGrid hoist 'int len = h*w;' and replace the scalar loop with Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned(dst, src, (uint)(len*sizeof(long))). Rotate90/270 are inherently strided (transpose) and are correct as-is, though blocking/tiling the transpose would cut cache misses on large grids.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.rationale: Bulk copy saturates bandwidth and removes loop overhead; hoisting h*w removes a redundant multiply per iteration. Tiled transpose (e.g. 16x16 blocks) for Rotate90/270 would dramatically reduce TLB/cache misses on the strided dst writes.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/GridBfs.cs.risk: CopyBlock semantics identical for non-overlapping src/dst (rotate assumes distinct buffers already). Tiling adds complexity — propose only if grids are large; keep simple version for small grids.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.summary: Element-wise scalar fill leaves vectorization to chance; for blittable T this can dispatch to a bulk memset-style fill when value bit-pattern is uniform.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.currentCost: Scalar loop 'ptr[i] = value' over width*height. Burst may auto-vectorize, but for 1-byte value patterns or zero a Unsafe bulk fill / memset is unconditionally faster and not dependent on the autovectorizer.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.proposedChange: For sizeof(T)==1 (or when value==default) call a memset equivalent (e.g., Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned for zero). Otherwise keep the loop but mark it clearly vectorizable. At minimum, hoist 'int len = width*height' is already done; consider widening writes for common T sizes.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.rationale: memset/InitBlock saturates memory bandwidth and avoids the per-element store loop; for large grids fill is bandwidth-bound and a bulk primitive removes loop overhead and improves write-combining.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.risk: InitBlock only valid for byte-uniform patterns (zero, or T where all bytes equal). Guard on sizeof(T)==1 or value bit-pattern; general T must keep the loop. Keep AggressiveInlining.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.summary: index++ is already linear; minor: the unused 'value' parameter signals dead state and the getValue.Get could be hoisted per-row if it depends only on y.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.currentCost: 'value' parameter is accepted but never used in RunXY — dead parameter, mild API confusion and a wasted register/arg slot. The double loop with index++ is fine.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.proposedChange: Remove the unused 'value' parameter from RunXY (ergonomics/purity). No behavioral change since it is never read.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.rationale: Removes a dead argument, clarifying the API and matching the functor-driven intent; no caller relies on its value.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/FillGrid.cs.risk: Signature change — API break for callers passing value positionally. Cosmetic/ergonomic only; verify call sites before removing.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/MakeGrid.cs.summary: Replace per-cell multiply (y*width+x) with a running counter; the value being stored equals the linear index itself.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/MakeGrid.cs.currentCost: Each inner iteration computes y*width+x (1 IMUL + 1 ADD) plus index++ (separate counter). The stored value y*width+x is, by construction, identical to the running index that walks the buffer.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/MakeGrid.cs.proposedChange: Drop the nested loops and the multiply entirely: int total = width * height; for (int i = 0; i < total; i++) ptr[i] = i; Since cells are written in row-major order, ptr[index] always receives the value 'index'. This is a single tight loop Burst vectorizes trivially (store of an incrementing vector).
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/MakeGrid.cs.rationale: Eliminates one IMUL per cell and the outer-loop bookkeeping, collapsing two nested loops into one linear pass with a self-incrementing store value. Lower dependency chain and SIMD-friendly (broadcast iota).
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/MakeGrid.cs.risk: Semantics-preserving only because the write order is row-major and value == linear index. width*height must not overflow int (already implied: index is int and ptr[index++] uses the same range, so no new overflow risntroduced). Empty grid (total==0) handled by loop guard.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.summary: Hoist the per-cell destination-index multiply out of the inner loop and strength-reduce to additions.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.currentCost: Clockwise branch: inner loop computes srcIdx = y*width+x and dstIdx = x*height + (height-1-y) every iteration -> 2 IMUL + several ADD/SUB per cell. srcIdx already increments by 1 per x; x*height recomputes a multiply each step.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.proposedChange: For clockwise: precompute outside x-loop: int srcRow = y*width; int dstBase = height-1-y; then inside, maintain dstIdx via additive stepping: starting dstIdx = 0*height + dstBase and adding 'height' each x iteration; srcIdx = srcRow + x increments by 1. Symmetric treatment for the counter-clockwise branch (dstIdx steps by -height with base (width-1)*height + y). Replaces inner IMULs with one ADD each.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.rationale: Strength-reduces x*height (a multiply in the dependency chain of the store address) to a running add, and hoists y*width to once per row. Fewer multiplies, shorter address-computation dependency chain, same memory traffic.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.risk: Pure index arithmetic, identical addresses produced. width*height must fit int as before (unchanged). The scatter store pattern (non-contiguous dst) limits vectorization either way, but the arithmetic reduction is a real constant-factor win.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.summary: Buffer.MemoryCopy of the whole grid into temp is required because output is a scatter into ptr; but the copy could be avoided by writing the rotation directly when a separate dst is acceptable.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.currentCost: Full len*sizeof(T) MemoryCopy of ptr->temp every call (one extra full pass over the grid + a caller-supplied scratch buffer of equal size), purely to break the read/write aliasing of the in-place scatter.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.proposedChange: Offer/add a variant that reads from a caller src and writes the rotated result directly into a distinct dst (no temp, no copy): Run(T* src, T* dst, int width, int height, bool clockwise). The current in-place Run can forward to it after the copy, but callers that already have two buffers skip the MemoryCopy entirely, halving memory traffic and removing the scratch requirement.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.rationale: The MemoryCopy exists only to resolve aliasing for the in-place case. A src!=dst overload removes one full O(len) pass and the scratch allocation for the common transform-into-new-buffer use case.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Rotate.cs.risk: Ergonomic/API addition, not a change to existing semantics. Caller must guarantee src and dst do not overlap for the new overload; document that. In-place behavior of existing Run is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Shuffle.cs.summary: Replace the 2-int stackalloc RNG state with two local ints to avoid pointer-indirected loads/stores on every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Shuffle.cs.currentCost: rng = stackalloc int[2] forces every RNG read/write (rng[0], rng[1]) through memory (stack slot via pointer) inside the hot loop, defeating register allocation. rng[1] is a loop-invariant constant (1103515245) yet stored in a slot.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Shuffle.cs.proposedChange: Use plain locals: uint state = (uint)seed; const uint MUL = 1103515245u; const uint A = 134775813u; per iteration: state = (MUL*MUL + 12345u) ^ (state*A + 1u)... — but note rng[1] never changes, so its term (rng[1]*1103515245+12345) is a compile-time constant. Precompute it once: const int CONST_TERM = unchecked(1103515245 * 1103515245 + 12345); then rng[0] = CONST_TERM ^ (rng[0]*134775813 + 1). Keep rng[0] in a register-resident local int.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Shuffle.cs.rationale: Keeps RNG state in registers (no stack pointer indirection per iteration), and folds the entire rng[1]-dependent expression into one named constant since rng[1] is invariant — removing a multiply and an add from every loop iteration. Strictly fewer ops on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Shuffle.cs.risk: Must reproduce the exact same int sequence to preserve shuffle output. rng[1] is initialized to 1103515245 and never written, so 1103515245*1103515245+12345 (evaluated unchecked, wrapping in int) is bit-identical to the original each iteration. Use 'unchecked' for the constant to match overflow-wrapping. The (int)((uint)x>>16)%(uint)(i+1) modulo must remain unchanged.

src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Reverse.cs.summary: Already optimal two-pointer in-place reverse; no algorithmic change. Only a minor note on unused 'using System'.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Reverse.cs.currentCost: Loop body does len/2 swaps, each a 3-temp exchange — minimal. 'using System;' is unused (no System type referenced).
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Reverse.cs.proposedChange: Leave the algorithm as-is (optimal). Optionally remove the unused 'using System;' to keep the file clean (no codegen impact). For T of size 1/2/4/8 Burst already handles the swap well; no manual SIMD needed since reverse-swap has an inherent cross dependency.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Reverse.cs.rationale: The two-pointer reverse is O(n) with the minimum n/2 swaps and a tight branchless-friendly body. There is no faster approach; flagging it as already-optimal per the high-signal rule.
src/IAFahim.DS.Grid/Reverse.cs.risk: None — no change proposed beyond an optional cosmetic using-removal.

src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.summary: Sift-up does a full 3-way swap each level; replace with hole-carry insertion to halve writes per level.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.currentCost: Per level: one CompareTo plus a 3-assignment swap (read parent, write parent, write child). Each swap moves the inserted value down and back up repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Hold val in a register, only shift the parent down into the child slot when it is greater, and write val once at the final resting position: `T val=...; int i=len; while(i>0){int p=Parent(i); if(ptr[p].CompareTo(val)<=0) break; ptr[i]=ptr[p]; i=p;} ptr[i]=val;`
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.rationale: Eliminates the redundant write of val into ptr[i] at every level (and the tmp read) — each level becomes one CompareTo + one copy instead of CompareTo + three copies. For a sift of depth d this saves ~2d element copies, shortening the dependency chain (each iteration depends only on ptr[p], not on a completed swap).
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.risk: Semantics preserved exactly: standard hole-carry heap insertion produces an identical final array. val must be a local copy taken before the loop (it is the argument, already a copy). No signed/overflow concerns; Parent uses >>1 on non-negative i.

src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.summary: Both the sift-up and sift-down phases use full 3-way swaps; convert to hole-carry to halve element copies.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.currentCost: Sift-up loop and sift-down loop each perform a 3-assignment swap per level (tmp read + 2 writes), plus re-reading ptr[cur]/ptr[smallest].
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Cache `T moved = ptr[len-1]` once, run sift-up comparing parent against `moved` and shifting parents down (ptr[cur]=ptr[p]), then in the sift-down phase compare children against `moved` and shift the smaller child up, writing `moved` to the final hole once. Avoid re-reading ptr[smallest] via a temp holding the current min child value.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.rationale: Same dependency-chain and write-count reduction as HeapPush: one copy per level instead of three. Also removes the repeated ptr[smallest]/ptr[cur] loads since the candidate value is kept in a register across the inner comparisons.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.risk: Behavior identical to swap-based sift. Must preserve the existing guard `if (cur != i) return;` that skips sift-down when the element bubbled up. moved must be read before the array is logically shortened. No overflow/signedness issues.

src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.summary: Dead code: HeapPop declares private Left and Right helpers that are never used.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.currentCost: Two unused private static methods (Left, Right) in HeapPop add source/IL surface and maintenance noise; they duplicate HeapFix's helpers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Delete HeapPop.Left and HeapPop.Right (lines 29-33). HeapPop.Run only computes ptr[0], ptr[len-1] and delegates to HeapFix.Run.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.rationale: Removes dead code; no runtime cost change but reduces complexity and the chance of divergence from the canonical helpers in HeapFix. Cleaner, more discoverable API.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.risk: None — the methods are private and unreferenced within the class. Pure deletion, no behavior change.

src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.summary: Modulo by runtime cap on every push/pop; if cap is constrained to a power of two, replace % with & (cap-1).
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.currentCost: Each deque op executes an integer division (`% cap`) — ~20-40 cycles on mobile ARM, and the worst single instruction in these otherwise trivial ring-buffer ops.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Add power-of-two-capacity variants (or document cap as power-of-two and pass a mask): `*front = (*front - 1 + cap) & (cap - 1)` and `*back = (*back + 1) & (cap - 1)`. Alternatively branchless wrap without division: `int f=*front-1; *front = f<0 ? f+cap : f;` and `int b=*back+1; *back = b==cap ? 0 : b;`.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.rationale: Power-of-two & is a single-cycle AND vs a multi-cycle DIV; the conditional-wrap form is branchless (cmov) and avoids division entirely while supporting arbitrary cap. Both eliminate the per-op divide that dominates these functions.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.risk: The `& (cap-1)` form REQUIRES cap to be a power of two — must be enforced/documented (House 'Run' contract assumes valid caller input, so a power-of-two precondition is acceptable for a new variant). The conditional-wrap form is fully general and preserves semantics for all cap>=1 since each op changes the index by at most 1 (it can never under/overshoot by more than cap).

src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.summary: stackalloc int[len] for the deque can blow the stack for large len; the ring never needs more than windowSize entries.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.currentCost: Allocates `len` ints on the stack (4*len bytes). For large len (e.g. 100k) this is 400KB of stack — risks stack overflow on mobile thread stacks (often 512KB-1MB) and wastes cache footprint.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Size the scratch to the window: `int* deque = stackalloc int[windowSize]` and index modulo windowSize (mask if power-of-two), since a monotonic deque for a sliding window of size w holds at most w indices. Or cap the stackalloc and document a max.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.rationale: Bounds working set by windowSize instead of len, which is typically far smaller. Smaller scratch improves L1 residency and removes the stack-overflow hazard for large inputs.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.risk: Requires converting the linear `deque[back]` indexing into ring indexing (front/back modulo windowSize), changing the `deque[front] <= i - windowSize` staleness check accordingly. Logic must be re-derived carefully; behavior must remain identical. If left linear, the only safe minimal change is asserting len fits the stack.

src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.summary: dst is left unwritten for indices that remain on the stack (no next-greater element), leaving caller-visible garbage.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.currentCost: Indices still on the stack at loop end never get a dst value assigned, so dst[those] retain prior memory contents — an implicit, undocumented contract that the caller must pre-clear dst.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Either document that unmatched positions are untouched and the returned count identifies how many remain, or explicitly write a sentinel (e.g. -1 or len) for remaining stack entries in a final drain loop: `while(top>0) dst[stack[--top]] = SENTINEL;`.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.rationale: Removes hidden caller obligation / nondeterministic output, improving purity and ergonomics. A sentinel drain is O(top) with no asymptotic change and makes output fully determined by input.
src/IAFahim.DS.Heap/Heap.cs.risk: Adds writes; if existing callers rely on dst being untouched for unmatched entries (current behavior), introducing a sentinel changes observable output. Should be a new/explicit variant or documented choice rather than a silent change.

src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.summary: Replace if/else-if cascade on seg with a single switch-free arithmetic dispatch and remove the redundant x>=hpow / y>=hpow re-evaluation
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.currentCost: Run recomputes x>=hpow and y>=hpow inside GetHilbertSegment AND again in the seg==3 tail (line 18). The seg dispatch is a chain of up to 3 branch tests (seg==0,1,2) creating a dependency chain; each recursion level repeats this.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.proposedChange: Compute int gx = x>=hpow?1:0; int gy = y>=hpow?1:0; once, pass them (or derived subtraction) into the segment computation, and reuse gx/gy for the line-18 subtraction (x - gx*hpow). Reorder the seg tests so the most common case is first, or convert the 4-way seg dispatch to a switch which Burst lowers to a jump table.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.rationale: Eliminates two redundant signed comparisons per recursion level and shortens the branch-dependency chain, cutting cycles in the hot recursive path; a jump table replaces a linear branch cascade.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.risk: Must preserve exact seg semantics from GetHilbertSegment (the XOR with rot&2 and rot&1 parity term). gx/gy hoisting is purely a CSE and is semantics-preserving since x,y,hpow are unchanged between the two uses.

src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.summary: Convert tail recursion to an iterative loop to remove call overhead and enable accumulation
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.currentCost: Run is fully tail-recursive (every return is a single recursive call, with seg==3 adding subSize). Even with AggressiveInlining, recursion across `pow` levels cannot be inlined (self-call), so each level pays a call/return + stack-frame cost, and subSize is recomputed via 1L<<(2*pow-2) each level.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.proposedChange: Rewrite as a while(pow>0) loop accumulating `result`: mutate x,y,rot in place and add subSize only on the seg==3 branch. subSize for level p is 1L<<(2*p-2); accumulate by shifting a running base. This is the same structure Encode already uses.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.rationale: Removes per-level call/return and frame setup, turns the function into a flat loop Burst can keep in registers, and lets subSize be tracked incrementally instead of recomputed with a shift each level.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.risk: Behavior identical because the recursion is genuine tail recursion with simple accumulation; care needed to apply the seg==1 argument swap (Run(y,x,...)) and the seg==3 coordinate subtraction in the right order inside the loop.

src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.summary: Make GetHilbertSegment branchless and AggressiveInlined; replace the ((a)==(b)?0:1) and multiply with XOR
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.currentCost: Three ternary branches: two for x>=hpow / y>=hpow and one for the (x>=hpow)==(y>=hpow)?0:1 parity, plus an integer multiply (rot&1)*parity. No inlining attribute on this hot leaf called once per recursion level.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]. Compute int gx=(int)(((ulong)(x-hpow))>>63)... or use comparison results directly: int gx = x>=hpow?1:0 still branches; instead use gx = -(x>=hpow) tricks are not needed — better: parity = gx ^ gy gives exactly the !=  predicate, so replace ((x>=hpow)==(y>=hpow)?0:1) with (gx ^ gy), and replace (rot&1)*parity with ((rot&1) & (gx^gy)) — both operands are 0/1 so AND equals multiply.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.rationale: Removes one branch and one integer multiply per level, replacing them with a single XOR/AND; AND-of-0/1 is a cheaper, branchless equivalent of the multiply. Inlining removes the leaf call overhead.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.risk: gx^gy equals 1 exactly when gx!=gy, matching the != predicate; (rot&1)&(x) equals (rot&1)*x only when both are 0/1, which holds here. Semantics preserved. Comparison-to-0/1 conversions in Burst are already branchless via setcc, so no signed-shift hack is required.

src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.summary: Hoist loop-invariant shift amounts and fold RotateHilbert into the loop branchlessly; precompute (1L<<i)-1 masks
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.currentCost: Per iteration: computes 1L<<(2*i-2), (rx<<1)+ry, and calls RotateHilbert which recomputes (1L<<i)-1 twice and branches on rx. The d += 1L<<(2*i-2) term is a fixed geometric series (sum equals (4^logN-1)/3) computed via a shift every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.proposedChange: Maintain a running `bit = 1L<<(2*i-2)` updated by >>2 each iteration instead of recomputing the shift. Inline RotateHilbert: compute mask=(1L<<i)-1 once, and do the rx==1 conditional reflection branchlessly via mask. Note the d += 1L<<(2*i-2) over all iterations is a constant for given logN — it could be added once as the closed-form ((1L<<(2*logN))-1)/3 outside the loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.rationale: The summed term is loop-invariant in aggregate (closed form), eliminating logN shifts and adds. Running `bit` avoids recomputing 2*i-2 shifts. Inlining RotateHilbert removes a call and the duplicate (1L<<i)-1 computation.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.risk: Closed-form replacement of sum of 1L<<(2*i-2) must use integer floor division ((4^logN-1)/3) which is exact since the sum is an integer; verify for logN up to 31 to avoid 1L<<(2*logN) overflow at logN=32. RotateHilbert reorders x/y but only the rx==1 path reflects, so the swap must still always execute — preserve the unconditional swap after the conditional reflect.

src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.summary: Add AggressiveInlining and compute the reflection mask once
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.currentCost: Called once per Encode iteration without an inlining hint; computes (1L<<i)-1 twice when rx==1.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] and compute long mask=(1L<<i)-1 once, reusing it for both x and y reflection.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.rationale: Removes call overhead in the hot Encode loop and one redundant shift+sub when rx==1.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.risk: Pure refactor; mask reuse is identical arithmetic. The unconditional x/y swap must remain after the conditional reflection.

src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.summary: EncodeRecursive is a non-functional placeholder returning x*h+y — flag as incorrect / dead before optimizing
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.currentCost: Comment says 'Placeholder for real Gilbert curve logic'; it never recurses and returns x*h+y, so GilbertOrder.Encode does not compute a Gilbert curve index. Math.Abs on the sum is wasted work given the placeholder.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.proposedChange: Either implement the real generalized Hilbert (gilbert2d) recursion or mark the API clearly as unimplemented. Do not micro-optimize a placeholder; once implemented, the ax/ay/cx/cy parameters that are currently always 0 should be exploited (the w>=h/h>w split passes constant zeros).
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.rationale: Optimizing a placeholder wastes effort and could entrench wrong behavior; correctness must precede performance. Noting it prevents false confidence in the module.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.risk: This is a correctness/design flag, not a behavior-preserving micro-opt. No change should be applied silently; implementing the algorithm changes observable output (currently wrong) intentionally.

src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.summary: Replace division/modulo by int.MaxValue and blockSize with cheaper ops where blockSize is power-of-two; precompute l/blockSize once
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.currentCost: Encode computes l/blockSize twice (line 69) and multiplies by int.MaxValue (a non-power-of-two odd constant forcing real 64-bit multiply) and uses % indirectly via the sign branch. Decode uses code/int.MaxValue and Math.Abs(code%int.MaxValue) — two expensive 64-bit divides by a non-power-of-two constant.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.proposedChange: Compute int block = l/blockSize once and reuse for both the multiply and the parity test. If blockSize is constrained to a power of two, replace l/blockSize with l>>log2(blockSize). The int.MaxValue radix is awkward; if a power-of-two stride (e.g. 1L<<31) were used instead, code/stride and code%stride become shift and mask. Decode's Math.Abs(code % int.MaxValue) can drop Math.Abs if r is known non-negative.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.rationale: Eliminates one redundant integer division in Encode and replaces div/mod by a constant with shift/mask when the stride is a power of two, removing the slowest integer ops on mobile cores; CSE of l/blockSize saves one div.
src/IAFahim.DS.HilbertOrder/HilbertOrder.risk: Switching the stride from int.MaxValue to a power of two changes the encoded values (observable) and must be a deliberate format change, not silent. The pure CSE of l/blockSize and the power-of-two shift for blockSize are semantics-preserving ONLY if blockSize is guaranteed positive power-of-two; otherwise keep the divide. Signed l/blockSize differs from >> for negative l, so guard l>=0.

src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.summary: Remove the provably-dead null guard at the top of the hottest leaf of Splay.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.currentCost: Every Rotate call (the innermost operation of Splay, executed O(amortized) times per Access) starts with `if (x == null || x->Parent == null) return;` — two pointer loads/compares and a branch on the critical dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.proposedChange: Delete line 57 (`if (x == null || x->Parent == null) return;`). Rotate is private and called only from Splay at lines 104/106/108, where `!IsRoot(x)`/`!IsRoot(p)` already guarantees the argument is non-null with a non-null Parent. The guard is unreachable for valid state. This matches the 'Unchecked Run methods assume valid caller input' house policy for a private hot helper.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.rationale: Eliminates two dependent pointer dereferences and a branch from the inner splay loop. The branch is always not-taken, so it wastes a predictor slot and lengthens the dependency chain before the real rotation work begins; removing it shortens the critical path of the most-executed routine in the structure.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.risk: Only safe because all three call sites pass a node known to be non-root (parent non-null). If Rotate ever becomes public or gains another caller, the guard must return. No semantic change for current callers.

src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.summary: Replace recursive top-down PushTo with an iterative two-pass (collect-up, push-down) loop to kill call-stack overhead and a long return-dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.currentCost: PushTo recurses up the splay tree via `PushTo(x->Parent)` for every level before any Push, once per Splay call. Each recursion frame costs a call/return, spills, and the Push of an ancestor cannot start until the recursive call returns — a strict serialized chain of depth = splay-tree height. It is not tail-recursive (Push follows the call), so the JIT/Burst cannot turn it into a loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.proposedChange: Walk parent pointers upward into a small fixed stackalloc buffer of LctNode* (e.g. capacity ~64, the practical splay depth bound), collecting the path from x up to the splay root while `!IsRoot`, then iterate that buffer in reverse calling Push on each. This converts the recursion to two tight loops with no call frames. Splay already starts with PushTo, so the change is local.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.rationale: Removes O(depth) function-call/return overhead per Splay and replaces a serialized recursion-return chain with two cache-friendly linear scans. Pointers are already being chased to walk up; storing them avoids re-deref and lets the push-down loop run without stack unwinding. Lower instruction count and no recursion guarantees Burst-friendly straight-line codegen.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.risk: Need a depth bound for the stackalloc; splay/LCT preferred-path depth is small but unbounded in theory, so size the buffer conservatively (LCT splay depth stays modest after self-balancing, but a fixed cap technically assumes it). If unbounded depth must be supported exactly, keep a fallback or size to a documented MaxDepth constant. Observable behavior (order of Push calls top-to-bottom) is preserved.

src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.summary: Reconsider AggressiveInlining on the large loop-bearing public methods (Access, MakeRoot, FindRoot, Link, Cut, Query) — inlining them bloats code without benefit and can pessimize I-cache.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.currentCost: Access contains a while-loop that itself calls Splay (which loops and recurses). MakeRoot/FindRoot/Link/Cut/Query each call Access+Splay. Marking these AggressiveInlining forces the compiler to inline multi-block, loop-containing bodies into every caller (e.g. Query inlines MakeRoot which inlines Access...), exploding code size for no inlining win on a non-leaf.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.proposedChange: Drop [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] from Access, MakeRoot, FindRoot, Link, Cut, Query. Keep it only on the genuine hot leaves Update, Push, IsRoot (lines 21,31,47), which are tiny and inline cleanly. Let the compiler decide for the loop-bearing routines.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.rationale: AggressiveInlining is meant for small leaf helpers. Inlining loop-heavy callees increases code size, harms instruction-cache locality on mobile (small I-cache), and provides no register/dispatch savings because the call overhead is negligible relative to the loop work. Removing it shrinks the binary and improves I-cache residency of the inner splay loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.risk: Pure code-gen hint; zero semantic change. Worst case the compiler would have made the same decision anyway. Verify no caller relied on cross-inlining for a measured win (none can be assumed without benchmarks, which match the 'reason theoretically' constraint).

src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.summary: Avoid re-reading x->Left/x->Right after the swap when toggling children's Rev.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.currentCost: After swapping Left/Right, Push re-loads x->Left and x->Right from memory (lines 39,41) to toggle their Rev flags, re-dereferencing pointers it just wrote.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.proposedChange: Hold the original children in locals: `LctNode* l = x->Left; LctNode* r = x->Right;` then write `x->Left = r; x->Right = l;` and toggle `if (l != null) l->Rev = !l->Rev; if (r != null) r->Rev = !r->Rev;` using the locals instead of re-reading the fields.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.rationale: Eliminates two redundant pointer loads from the struct after the store, keeping the child pointers in registers across the swap-and-toggle. Shortens the dependency chain in a routine called on every node visited during PushTo/FindRoot.
src/IAFahim.DS.LinkCut/LinkCut.cs.risk: Semantics identical — toggling Rev on the (now swapped) children is exactly toggling on the original two children regardless of which field they sit in. No aliasing concern since l and r are distinct nodes or null.

src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.summary: Replace O(q^2) selection-style sort with an O(q log q) quicksort like the one already in MoSort.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.currentCost: Nested i/j loops: for every i scans all j>i, swapping. That is q*(q-1)/2 comparisons = Theta(q^2). For q=1e5 this is ~5e9 CompareQueries calls, each doing 3 integer divisions and CompareTo — catastrophic vs the rest of the algorithm which is roughly O((n+q) * n^{2/3}).
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.proposedChange: Implement an in-place iterative/recursive median-of-middle quicksort over the Query3D* array (mirroring MoAlgorithm.MoSort.QuickSort) using CompareQueries (made branch-comparison) as the predicate. Precompute block(L)=L/blk into the comparison via a Less() returning bool to avoid CompareTo. Optionally keep insertion sort only for sub-ranges < ~16 elements.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.rationale: Asymptotic improvement from Theta(q^2) to Theta(q log q). This is the single dominant cost for large q; the sort currently can dwarf the entire Mo traversal.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.risk: Quicksort is not stable, but Mo's sort does not require stability (ties broken fully by the comparator on L-block, R-block, T). Must ensure the comparator gives a total order (it does: L-block, then R-block, then T). Recursion depth worst-case O(q); use median-of-three or the existing left+(right-left)>>1 pivot plus tail recursion on the larger side to bound stack.

src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.summary: stackalloc int[1000001] (~4 MB) on the stack risks stack overflow and is not Burst/mobile-friendly; take freq as a caller-provided pointer.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.currentCost: int* freq = stackalloc int[1000001] allocates ~4,000,004 bytes on the stack per Run call. Default thread stack is ~1 MB; this overflows on most platforms, and on mobile (smaller stacks) it is guaranteed UB. It is also not zero-cost — the runtime zero-inits 4 MB every call.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.proposedChange: Remove the stackalloc and add an int* freq parameter (and a maxVal/freqLen) to Run, matching the rest of the library's convention where the caller owns buffers (MoAlgorithm passes int* freq everywhere). Caller allocates once and reuses, pre-zeroed. Document that freq length must exceed max array/update value.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.rationale: Eliminates a multi-megabyte per-call stack allocation and its mandatory zeroing, removes stack-overflow risk on PC and mobile, and makes the function reusable without re-zeroing 4 MB each call. Aligns with the house buffer-ownership pattern.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.risk: API change (adds parameters) — breaks existing callers, but the current form is effectively broken anyway due to overflow. Caller must guarantee freq is large enough and zeroed; this matches the 'Unchecked Run assumes valid input' convention.

src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.summary: Per-comparison divisions and CompareTo calls are expensive in the hot sort comparator; precompute L/blk and R/blk once per query and compare branchlessly.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.currentCost: Each call does up to 4 integer divisions (a.L/blk, b.L/blk, a.R/blk, b.R/blk) plus int.CompareTo (a non-inlined-by-default method-call producing -1/0/1). In an O(q log q) sort this runs q log q times; divisions are ~20-40 cycles each on mobile ARM.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.proposedChange: Precompute each query's L-block once (store block index in Query3D.Id-adjacent scratch, or compute a parallel int* lblock array before sorting) so the comparator only compares precomputed ints. Replace a.X.CompareTo(b.X) with direct 'if (x!=y) return x<y' bool comparisons (return bool from a Less predicate). If blk is a power of two, L/blk becomes L>>log2(blk) (guard: L>=0, which holds for indices).
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.rationale: Removes repeated divisions (compute L-block n times instead of ~n log n times) and replaces CompareTo call overhead with inlined integer compares, shortening the dependency chain in the innermost sort loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.risk: Shift replacement only valid when blk is a power of two and operands non-negative (array indices are >=0, so safe). Precomputing blocks needs a small parallel buffer or reuse of an existing field; must keep it in sync with any swaps (compute block-of-L, not block index, so it moves with the query).

src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.summary: Run mutates the caller's input arr in place via Apply/RevertUpdate, leaving arr in a non-deterministic final state; document or restore.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.currentCost: ApplyUpdate/RevertUpdate write arr[u.Pos] = NewVal/OldVal, so after Run the input array reflects whatever the last processed query's time was — a hidden side effect on caller data, not a pure query routine.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.proposedChange: Either document explicitly that arr is scratch/clobbered, or restore arr to its original state at the end by reverting curT back to 0 (the time-travel loop already supports this). For determinism, callers re-running Run on the same arr must reset it; making restoration explicit removes that footgun.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.rationale: Removes hidden mutable state leaking into caller buffers; makes Run idempotent/deterministic across repeated calls, which matters for a reusable library routine.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoUpdates.cs.risk: Restoring arr adds O(uCount) work at the end (cheap relative to the main loop). If callers intentionally rely on arr being updated, restoration changes observable behavior — so prefer documenting unless idempotency is desired. No correctness risk to ans[].

src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.summary: Recurse only into the smaller partition and loop on the larger to bound stack depth to O(log q).
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.currentCost: Two unconditional recursive calls QuickSort(left,j) and QuickSort(i,right). Worst-case (already-sorted / adversarial) input gives O(q) recursion depth, risking stack overflow for large q and adding call overhead Burst cannot elide.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.proposedChange: Convert to a hybrid: after partitioning, recurse into the smaller side and tail-loop (while-loop reassigning left/right) on the larger side. Guarantees recursion depth <= log2(q). Optionally cut to insertion sort for ranges < ~16.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.rationale: Bounds stack to O(log q) regardless of input, eliminating worst-case deep recursion and halving call-frame overhead; preserves identical ordering.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.risk: Pure refactor of the same partition scheme — output order unchanged. Must keep the parallel arrays (q,l,r,b) swapped together exactly as now.

src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.summary: The 'queries'/q array (parallel to l,r,b) is permuted by Swap but never read inside the sort; confirm it carries the query id payload, otherwise it is dead work.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.currentCost: Swap permutes q[i]/q[j] on every swap (one extra load/store/temp per swap) but Less and QuickSort never read q. If q holds query ids that callers need reordered alongside l/r/b, this is necessary; if not, it is pure overhead per swap.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.proposedChange: If q is the id payload meant to be reordered with the keys, keep it but document that contract clearly. If it is unused, drop the q parameter and the q[] swap to remove one quarter of the swap cost.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.rationale: Either eliminates ~25% of per-swap memory traffic in the sort, or clarifies a load-bearing-but-unobvious data dependency. Sorts do many swaps in the hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.risk: Removing q changes the public Run signature and would break callers relying on reordered ids — only do this after confirming q is unused downstream. Keeping it has no correctness risk.

src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.summary: Branchless distinct-count update: derive the increment from the pre-increment value instead of an if.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.currentCost: if (freq[val] == 0) (*curDistinct)++; then freq[val]++ — a data-dependent branch per element in the hottest inner loop of Mo's traversal (called O((n+q)*n^{2/3}) times). Mispredicts are common because add/remove order is irregular.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.proposedChange: int f = freq[val]; *curDistinct += (f == 0) ? 1 : 0; freq[val] = f + 1; — or use the comparison result directly: *curDistinct += (int)(f == 0). Symmetrically for RemoveInt: freq[val] = f - 1 then *curDistinct -= (int)((f - 1) == 0). Lets the JIT/Burst emit a setcc instead of a branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.rationale: Removes a frequently-mispredicted branch from the innermost Mo loop, converting it to a branchless conditional add; this loop dominates total runtime.
src/IAFahim.DS.Mo/MoAlgorithm.cs.risk: Semantics identical (the (f==0)?1:0 add equals the conditional increment). Must read freq[val] once into a local to avoid an extra load and to keep the pre/post values consistent. No overflow concern for realistic frequencies.

src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.summary: Replace IComparable<T>.CompareTo virtual-ish call in the hot binary-search loop with a branchless/Burst-friendly comparison and drop AggressiveInlining payoff concerns
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.currentCost: Per loop iteration: one ptr[mid].CompareTo(key) call. CompareTo on a generic T:IComparable<T> is a constrained interface call. For primitive T this is fine, but the comparison-result is only tested with `< 0`, forcing the full 3-way comparison contract each step. Loop also recomputes `hi - lo` each iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.proposedChange: Keep the algorithm but compute mid as `lo + ((hi - lo) >> 1)` instead of `/ 2`. Since `hi - lo >= 0` always (lo < hi guard), the shift is exactly equivalent to the unsigned division by 2 with no signed-rounding hazard. This strength-reduces the divide to a shift on every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.rationale: `(hi - lo)` is provably non-negative inside the `while (lo < hi)` body, so `/ 2` and `>> 1` produce identical results; the shift is 1 cycle vs a multi-cycle IDIV (or a div-by-constant magic-number sequence the JIT/Burst may emit). Saves cycles on every step of an O(log n) loop that runs for every Insert/Erase/Rank.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.risk: Safe: `hi - lo` cannot be negative given the loop guard and len >= 0, so arithmetic-shift == division. No overflow because `lo + (hi-lo)` stays within [0,len]. If a caller ever passed len < 0 (invalid by contract) behavior differs, but unchecked Run methods assume valid input.

src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.summary: Use a bulk memmove for the shift loop instead of element-by-element copy
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.currentCost: The `for (int i = len; i > idx; i--) ptr[i] = ptr[i-1];` loop moves (len - idx) elements one at a time with a dependency chain and bounds-free but still per-element store. For large sets this is the dominant cost of Insert and is not auto-vectorized well because of the descending overlapping copy.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.proposedChange: Replace the manual loop with `Buffer.MemoryMove(ptr + idx + 1, ptr + idx, (long)(len - idx) * sizeof(T))` (or Unity's `UnsafeUtility.MemMove` in the Unity/Burst build). This is an overlap-safe block move.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.rationale: A memmove intrinsic copies in wide SIMD chunks and is far cheaper than (len-idx) individual T-sized stores; it also removes the loop's induction-variable dependency chain. Strict improvement for the shift, same observable result.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.risk: Must use an overlap-aware move (memmove semantics), NOT memcpy, since source/dest regions overlap. `Buffer.MemoryMove` is overlap-safe. T is unmanaged so a raw byte move is valid (no managed refs to track). In Burst, prefer UnsafeUtility.MemMove; Buffer.MemoryMove may not be Burst-compatible, so gate by build.

src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.summary: Use a bulk memmove for the compaction loop instead of element-by-element copy
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.currentCost: The `for (int i = idx; i < len-1; i++) ptr[i] = ptr[i+1];` loop shifts (len-1-idx) elements down one slot, one at a time, with an induction dependency chain; same vectorization limitation as Insert.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.proposedChange: Replace with an overlap-safe block move: `UnsafeUtility.MemMove(ptr + idx, ptr + idx + 1, (long)(len - 1 - idx) * sizeof(T))` (or Buffer.MemoryMove on non-Burst builds).
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.rationale: Block move runs in wide SIMD chunks instead of (len-1-idx) scalar stores, removing the per-element dependency chain. Same observable result.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.risk: Regions overlap (forward shift), so must use memmove not memcpy; both UnsafeUtility.MemMove and Buffer.MemoryMove handle overlap. T unmanaged makes the byte move valid.

src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.summary: Adopt the Try*/Run naming convention and surface whether the operation mutated the set
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.currentCost: Insert returns `len` unchanged on duplicate and `len+1` on success; Erase returns `len` on not-found and `len-1` on success. Callers must compare the returned length against the input length to learn whether anything changed, which is an implicit, easy-to-misuse contract.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.proposedChange: Either keep the length-return fast path but add `TryInsert`/`TryErase` wrappers returning a bool `changed` out-param plus new length, or document the convention explicitly. No change to the hot path; the existing methods can be the unchecked `Run`-style core.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.rationale: Improves discoverability/consistency with the library's Run/Try* convention without altering the per-op cost model. Reduces caller bugs from misreading the sentinel-by-equal-length contract.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.risk: Pure API addition; if implemented as wrappers it has zero effect on existing call sites and no perf impact. Do not change existing return semantics or it breaks callers.

src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.summary: Kth and Rank are trivial wrappers; consider returning by ref / documenting bounds expectation
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.currentCost: `Kth` returns `ptr[k]` by value (a full T struct copy) and does no bounds reasoning by design. For large T (e.g. a big value struct) the by-value return copies the whole struct.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.proposedChange: Add a `ref T KthRef<T>(...)` overload returning `ref ptr[k]` for large-T callers that want to read/mutate in place without copying; keep the value-returning Kth for small primitives.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.rationale: For large unmanaged value types, returning ref avoids a struct copy on read; for primitives the by-value version is already optimal so keep both. Pure win for big-struct element types.
src/IAFahim.DS.OrderedSet/OrderedSet.cs.risk: ref-return exposes mutation of the backing buffer; only safe if the caller does not violate sortedness. Document that mutating through KthRef can break the ordered invariant. No change to existing Kth semantics.

src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.summary: Bounds check in TryGetIndex is provably always-true dead code on the hottest lookup path
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.currentCost: Every TryGetValue / indexer get executes index = key.GetHashCode() & (Size-1) then the comparison (index >= 0 && index < Size) and returns the result. The two comparisons plus the boolean &&, plus the out-param store and branch on the caller side, run on every single lookup.
