src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.proposedChange: Recognize that index = hash & (Size-1) with Size a power of two >= 1 always yields a value in [0, Size-1]. So index >= 0 && index < Size is a tautology. Make TryGetIndex always return true (or inline the mask directly into TryGetValue / the indexer and drop the predicate entirely). TryGetValue already re-validates presence via item.Equals(NullValue), so removing the index range branch does not change observable results.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.rationale: Eliminates two compares, a logical-and, and a conditional branch from the innermost lookup loop. The branch is also nominally a misprediction candidate; removing it shortens the dependency chain (hash -> mask -> load) and lets Burst fold the indexer get into a single masked load + NullValue compare. Asymptotically same, but a real constant-factor win on the dominant operation.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.risk: Relies on the invariant that Size is always a power of two (guaranteed by FindSize starting at 1 and only doing size <<= 1) and that GetHashCode() & (Size-1) is non-negative for any int hash (true: AND with a non-negative mask clears the sign bit, so result is always in [0, Size-1] regardless of hash sign). No signed-% pitfall here because it is already &, not %. Safe.

src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.summary: Precompute and store the (Size-1) mask instead of recomputing size-1 on every IndexFor call
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.currentCost: Each IndexFor(key, size) computes (size - 1) at runtime. On lookups this is a dependent subtract before the AND; in the build loop HasCollisions/constructor it runs once per key per probe.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.proposedChange: Add an internal int Mask field set to Size - 1 at construction. Have the instance IndexFor use key.GetHashCode() & this.Mask directly. Keep the static IndexFor(key, size) only for the FindSize/HasCollisions build phase. This removes the subtract from the steady-state lookup path.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.rationale: Strength-reduces one ALU op out of the lookup dependency chain (hash -> AND vs hash -> SUB -> AND), and removes a recompute that the JIT/Burst may not always hoist since size is passed by value. Storing Mask costs 4 bytes already available via struct padding alignment in many TKey/TValue combos.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.risk: Must keep Mask in sync with Size (only set once at construction; map is immutable after build, so no resync needed). Behavior identical. Minor RAM cost of 4 bytes per map instance.

src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.summary: NativeArray indexer re-fetches keys[i] twice and recomputes the mask each iteration during build
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.currentCost: for loop body does IndexFor(keys[i], size) then this.Keys[index] = keys[i] and this.Values[index] = values[i]. keys[i] goes through the NativeArray indexer (with bounds/safety checks under collections-checks) twice per iteration, and IndexFor recomputes size-1 each iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.proposedChange: Hoist int mask = size - 1; before the loop. Load TKey k = keys[i]; TValue v = values[i]; once into locals, compute int index = k.GetHashCode() & mask;, then store this.Keys[index] = k; this.Values[index] = v;. This halves the NativeArray indexer calls and removes per-iteration mask recompute.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.rationale: NativeArray<T> indexer under ENABLE_UNITY_COLLECTIONS_CHECKS is not free (safety handle check + range check); fetching keys[i] once removes a redundant guarded load and a second GetHashCode-feeding read. Build is one-shot but proportional to key count; this is a clean fused-pass win.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.risk: None; reading the same element into a local is semantically identical. keys.Length read can also be hoisted to a local for the loop bound.

src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.summary: FindSize rebuilds the hash set from scratch for every candidate size, giving O(n log(range)) set operations with repeated allocget churn
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.currentCost: FindSize doubles size from 1 upward; for each candidate it calls HasCollisions which Clear()s the NativeHashSet and re-Add()s all n keys, hashing every key again at every size step. Total work is O(n * number_of_doublings) hash+insert operations, and each Add touches the hash set's internal buckets.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.proposedChange: Precompute all n GetHashCode() values once into a temp stackalloc/Temp buffer (hashes are size-independent), then in HasCollisions only mask the cached hash (hash & (size-1)) instead of recomputing key.GetHashCode() each probe. This removes a full re-hash of every key at every size doubling. For small key counts the doubling count is small, but GetHashCode on large TKey structs can be expensive, so caching the hash is the real saving.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.rationale: GetHashCode() may be a non-trivial function for big unmanaged structs; computing it once instead of once-per-doubling cuts the hash work from O(n * doublings) to O(n). The collision probe then becomes a cheap mask + set-insert.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.risk: Build-time only, not steady-state. Requires a Temp allocation of n ints (already allocating a NativeHashSet of capacity n, so no worse). Behavior identical since hash values do not depend on size.

src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.summary: Single allocation packs Keys then Values contiguously; Values start may straddle a cache line, and offset is recomputable
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.currentCost: keysSize = sizeof(TKey)*count rounds to no alignment, so Values begin at an arbitrary byte offset that can split a TValue across a cache line on the first value, hurting the lookup load. valueOffset is also stored/passed out though it is trivially derivable.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.proposedChange: Align valueOffset up to sizeof(TValue) (or to a small power-of-two like 8/16) so Values is naturally aligned, improving the single hot load in TryGetValue. Since the block is already cache-line-aligned at allocation (JobsUtility.CacheLineSize), only the intra-block Values base needs alignment. This is a one-line round-up: valueOffset = AlignUp(keysSize, max(sizeof(TValue), alignof(TValue))).
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.rationale: Lookups touch exactly one Values[index] load; guaranteeing alignment avoids split-line loads for that access and keeps Burst's vectorized/aligned-load assumptions valid. Costs a few padding bytes once.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.risk: Adds up to (align-1) padding bytes to the allocation. Must keep the same valueOffset used for both write (ctor) and read (lookup) so they stay consistent. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.summary: Indexer get path computes the index twice (once via TryGetValue, value already loaded) - acceptable, but the get could share one masked load
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.currentCost: this[key].get calls TryGetValue which calls TryGetIndex (mask + dead bounds check), loads Values[index], compares to NullValue. The chain is fine, but combined with the dead bounds-check finding the get can collapse to: index = hash & Mask; value = Values[index]; if (value.Equals(NullValue)) throw.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.proposedChange: Once the dead bounds check is removed and Mask is cached, fold the indexer get into a single masked load plus one NullValue compare, dropping the out-param plumbing of TryGetValue for the throwing getter. Keep public TryGetValue as-is for the Try* API.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.rationale: Removes out-param store/load and a redundant boolean return through the inlined call, shortening the getter to load + compare + (unlikely) throw. Pairs with the bounds-check removal for a clean hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.PerfectHashMap/UnsafePerf.risk: Must preserve that the getter throws (under DOTS_DEBUG) exactly when value.Equals(NullValue), matching current TryGetValue semantics. Pure refactor; identical observable behavior.

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.summary: Convert recursive Query into an iterative loop to eliminate per-level call overhead on the hottest path
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.currentCost: Query is O(log n) recursion, invoked once per Find iteration and Find runs in a loop (multiple Query calls per Union). Each segment-tree level costs a full method call: argument marshaling of 8 parameters (root,l,r,idx,parent,lc,rc,size + out s), return-address push, stack frame setup. The out parameter 's' forces a store through a pointer at the leaf. The dependency chain is call -> load lc/rc[root] -> compare -> recurse.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.proposedChange: Rewrite as: int node=root; while(l!=r){ int mid=(l+r)>>1; if(idx<=mid){ node=lc[node]; r=mid; } else { node=rc[node]; l=mid+1; } } s=size[node]; return parent[node]; Keep the public signature identical so callers are unchanged.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.rationale: Tail-style descent has no need for a stack; the loop turns N recursive frames into N cheap iterations with one branch and one pointer load each, shrinking the dependency chain and removing call/return overhead. Burst/JIT may already tail-call-optimize this, but an explicit loop guarantees it and avoids the out-pointer store happening once per leaf only.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.risk: None — observable behavior is identical for all valid idx in [l,r]. The leaf assignment to s happens exactly once (at the leaf) as before. No signed/overflow change: (l+r)>>1 semantics unchanged.

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.summary: Inline the segment-tree descent into Find to fuse the Find loop with Query traversal
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.currentCost: Find calls Query (a full O(log n) traversal) on every loop iteration just to read parent[x] and size[x] for the current x. Each iteration re-enters the tree at root and walks down again. The out-int s is written every iteration but only the final value is used by the caller (sa/sb in Union). So intermediate s stores are wasted work, and every iteration pays full call overhead plus an out-pointer store.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.proposedChange: Inline an iterative descent inside Find's while(true): walk node from root using idx=x to the leaf, set p=parent[leaf]; only write s=size[leaf] when p==x (the terminal iteration), then return. This fuses the two loops, drops the Query call entirely, and removes the per-iteration s store for non-terminal steps.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.rationale: Eliminates one function call per Find iteration and avoids repeatedly storing through the out pointer 's' for intermediate (discarded) values — only the final size matters to callers. Fewer instructions per iteration and a shorter dependency chain; better Burst codegen since there is no out-parameter aliasing to reason about each step.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.risk: Must preserve that s reflects size of the final representative x (the node where parent==x). Guard: only assign s on the returning iteration. Behavior identical to current code, which returns size of the last queried node (the representative). No edge-case change for self-roots (first query returns p==x with its own size).

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.summary: Mark hot leaf descent helpers with [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.currentCost: Query, Swap, and (if kept) the descent helpers are separate methods. Query is called from Find in a tight loop; Swap is called twice in Union. Without an inlining hint the JIT/Burst may keep them as out-of-line calls, adding call/return overhead on the hot Find path.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to Query (once iterative) and to Swap. The using for System.Runtime.CompilerServices is already present.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.rationale: AggressiveInlining on small leaf methods lets Burst fold them into callers, removing call overhead and enabling cross-method register allocation and constant propagation of l/r/mid. Swap is two-temp trivial and benefits from inlining into Union.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.risk: None functionally. Inlining a recursive Query has no effect (recursion isn't inlined), so this hint only pays off if Query is first made iterative (see other opportunity).

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.summary: Branchless size-ordered swap to avoid a mispredictable branch before Update
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.currentCost: if (sa < sb) { Swap(ref ra,ref rb); Swap(ref sa,ref sb); } is a data-dependent branch on union sizes, which is essentially random in DSU workloads and thus frequently mispredicted (~15-20 cycle penalty per misprediction).
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.proposedChange: Replace with branchless conditional select: int lt=-(sa<sb?1:0) is still a branch in C#; instead compute mask via comparison and arithmetic select, or simply ensure (ra,sa) is the larger root using max/min-style select: e.g. int swap=(sa<sb)?1:0; then use it without a control-flow branch is hard in C#. Lower-risk: keep the branch but note it is cold relative to Find/Update cost (each Update is O(log n)).
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.rationale: Removing an unpredictable branch saves misprediction penalties; however the surrounding Find+Update work is O(log n) and dominates, so the swap branch is a small fraction of Union cost.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.risk: C# lacks a clean branchless 2-tuple swap without cmov-style intrinsics; a naive bit-mask select on ra/rb/sa/sb is correct but verbose. Given Update dominates, this is low-impact — only pursue if profiling later shows Union branch cost. Marked low and optional to avoid cargo-cult.

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.summary: Build recursion depth and node count are fine; no scratch buffers, but note stack depth is O(n) due to left-recursion pattern
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.currentCost: Build recurses depth O(log n) for a balanced tree (Build(l,mid) then Build(mid+1,r)), which is acceptable. allocCnt is dereferenced via pointer (*allocCnt) once per node — a load+store through a pointer each call, plus it aliases nothing else so it's cheap. No real RAM waste here.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.proposedChange: Optionally pass allocCnt by ref int instead of int* if callers can supply a ref, avoiding pointer-aliasing assumptions and letting Burst keep the counter in a register across the recursion; or hoist *allocCnt into a local counter threaded by return value. Low priority given correctness and existing pointer-based API.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.rationale: A ref/register-resident counter avoids repeated memory round-trips through allocCnt, but the recursive structure means the increment must be visible across sibling calls, so it must live in memory or be threaded through return values — the current pointer approach is already the simplest correct form.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentDsu/PersistentD.risk: Changing allocCnt from int* to ref int alters the public API signature (ergonomics/breaking) and Burst treats both similarly for an escaping address. Net win is marginal; flag only, do not force. No semantic change if done carefully.

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.summary: Priority hash is computed in 64-bit and contains a dead `>> 0` shift; do the multiply in 32-bit unsigned to make it a single IMUL.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.currentCost: `prio[idx] = (int)((uint)(idx * 2654435761) >> 0)`: `idx` is `int`, literal `2654435761` exceeds int.MaxValue so it binds as `uint`; `int * uint` promotes both operands to `long`, producing a 64-bit IMUL plus a truncating `(uint)` cast, plus a no-op `>> 0`. On a 32-bit-leaning mobile target the 64-bit multiply costs extra cycles per allocation.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Compute purely in 32-bit: `const uint Knuth = 2654435761u;` then `prio[idx] = (int)((uint)idx * Knuth);`. This is a 32-bit IMUL, drops the dead `>> 0`, and names the magic constant. Result bit pattern is identical because (uint)idx * Knuth mod 2^32 equals the low 32 bits of the long product.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.rationale: 32-bit unsigned multiply with wraparound is exactly the low 32 bits of the 64-bit product, so output is bit-identical, but it emits one 32-bit multiply instead of a widened 64-bit multiply + truncate, and removes a no-op shift. Named constant aids readability.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.risk: None for the value: `(uint)idx * 2654435761u` wraps mod 2^32, matching `(uint)(longProduct)`. `idx` is always positive (`++(*allocCnt)`), so `(uint)idx` is the same magnitude. Behavior preserved exactly.

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.summary: Eliminate the two null-child branches in size recomputation by relying on size[0] == 0 (the sentinel node).
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.currentCost: `size[x] = 1 + (left[x] != 0 ? size[left[x]] : 0) + (right[x] != 0 ? size[right[x]] : 0)` performs two compares and two conditional selects/branches on every Update. Update runs once per recursion frame in Split and Merge, i.e. O(log n) times per operation, on the hottest path.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Guarantee `size[0] == 0` once at buffer init (index 0 is the null sentinel and is never written by NewNode/CloneNode), then write `size[x] = 1 + size[left[x]] + size[right[x]];`. The `left[x]`/`right[x]` may be 0 but `size[0]` is 0, so the arithmetic is correct with zero branches.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.rationale: Two extra dependent loads of size[0] (which will be hot in cache) replace four branches/cmovs and shorten the dependency chain to a flat add-tree, which Burst/LLVM schedules better and never mispredicts. Same result for all inputs.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.risk: Requires size[0] to be 0 for the lifetime of the buffers. CloneNode/NewNode start allocation at index 1 (`++(*allocCnt)`) so index 0 is never overwritten; only the initial zero-init of the size buffer must be ensured (stackalloc/calloc already zeroes). State this precondition where buffers are allocated.

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.summary: Make the BST descent branchless on the child selection to cut mispredicts in the search loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.currentCost: `cur = cmp < 0 ? right[cur] : left[cur]` is a data-dependent branch each iteration; comparison-tree descent has ~50% unpredictable direction, so this branch mispredicts heavily over a random key distribution.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Index a 2-wide base instead of branching: since left/right are separate buffers this needs a select, but the select can be expressed branchlessly, e.g. `int* child = cmp < 0 ? right : left; cur = child[cur];` — the pointer select compiles to a CMOV with no control-flow hazard, or compute `cur = left[cur] + ((right[cur]-left[cur]) & -(cmp>>31... ))` only if a single combined child array is introduced. Minimal form: hoist to a CMOV-friendly pointer select.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.rationale: Replacing the control-flow branch with a conditional move removes branch-misprediction stalls in a tight O(log n) loop. The `cmp == 0` early-out remains a branch but is taken at most once.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.risk: Pointer-select CMOV codegen is compiler-dependent; if Burst does not emit CMOV the change is neutral. No semantic change. Combining left/right into one interleaved array would be a larger layout change (separate opportunity) and is not required for this micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.summary: Erase is an unimplemented placeholder that returns the wrong tree; it does not erase anything.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.currentCost: The method splits root at `val` then `return l;` (a comment explicitly says `// Placeholder`). It never removes the matching node and discards the entire `> val` subtree (`r`), so Erase both fails to delete and corrupts the set by dropping all greater elements. This is a correctness defect, not a perf issue, but it is on the public API.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Implement correctly with a three-way split. Split root at the predecessor boundary to isolate `< val`, `== val`, and `> val`. Concretely: split at `val` into (l = <=val, r = >val); then split l at the largest key strictly less than val. Since T only supports CompareTo, do a second split that routes equal keys right, i.e. split l using a `<`-comparator into (lt, eq); then `return Merge(lt, r)` to drop exactly the equal block (or merge eq's children to remove a single occurrence). Reuse existing Split/Merge so it stays O(log n) with one extra split pass.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.rationale: Restores correctness in O(log n) using the existing primitives; no asymptotic regression. The current code is O(log n) but produces wrong output, so any correct implementation at the same complexity is strictly better.
src/IAFahim.DS.PersistentTreap/Treap.cs.risk: Split's comparator is hardcoded to `<= 0` (equal goes left). To separate equals you need a strict-less variant or a sentinel key just below val, which T (only IComparable) cannot synthesize generically. The clean fix is a second Split overload that uses `< 0` for the equal-handling pass. Must decide erase-one vs erase-all semantics; match the intended test contract.

src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.summary: Replace the byte-by-byte copy loop into the Added buffer with a single bounded Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned (memcpy).
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.currentCost: The append loop `for (int i = 0; i < len && s.AddedLen < s.AddedCap; i++) s.Added[s.AddedLen++] = data[i];` executes len iterations, each with a bounds-against-cap branch, a load, a store, and a counter increment. For an N-byte insert this is N branches + N scalar stores; Burst cannot vectorize because the loop has a data-dependent termination condition (the AddedLen<AddedCap test) and an aliased running index.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.proposedChange: Precompute the clamp once: `int copy = len; int remaining = s.AddedCap - s.AddedLen; if (copy > remaining) copy = remaining;` then `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned(s.Added + s.AddedLen, data, (uint)copy); s.AddedLen += copy;`. Use `copy` (not `len`) for newPiece->Length so the truncation semantics match the original loop exactly.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.rationale: A single memcpy is a well-optimized wide/SIMD copy with no per-byte branch; it collapses N iterations into one call and removes the dependency chain on AddedLen. The clamp is computed once instead of tested every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.risk: Must preserve the original truncation behavior: when len exceeds remaining capacity, the old loop stops early and the new Piece->Length must equal the number of bytes actually copied (`copy`), NOT len. The current code already mismatches this by setting Length=len even on truncation; if exact-current-behavior is required this is a behavior change on the overflow edge. If callers guarantee AddedLen+len<=AddedCap (unchecked-Run contract), copy==len always and there is no risk. CopyBlockUnaligned requires non-overlapping src/dst, which holds since data is caller input and Added is internal.

src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.summary: Two near-identical list-traversal-to-position loops are duplicated; both also recompute the same 'find piece containing pos' logic.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.currentCost: The `while (after != null && offset + after->Length <= pos)` walk appears in both Insert and Delete verbatim. Code duplication, not a cycle cost, but it increases maintenance surface and the chance the two drift in edge handling.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.proposedChange: Extract a private static helper `[MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] static Piece* SeekToPos(Piece* head, int pos, out Piece* prev, out int offset)` and call it from both. Mark AggressiveInlining so Burst inlines it back into each caller with zero call overhead.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.rationale: Single source of truth for the seek; AggressiveInlining guarantees the generated code is identical to the current inlined loops, so no perf regression. Improves discoverability and consistency.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.risk: Behavior-preserving only if the helper reproduces the exact loop condition (`<=` not `<`) and updates prev/offset identically. No Burst concern: out-pointer params on unmanaged pointers are blittable and inline cleanly.

src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.summary: Piece is 24 bytes due to 4 bytes of padding before the 8-byte Next pointer; reordering fields packs it to 24 with no padding waste only if fields are grouped, but the real win is narrowing the three ints if buffer/length ranges allow.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.currentCost: Current layout: int BufferIndex(4), int Start(4), int Length(4), Piece* Next(8). On 64-bit the pointer needs 8-byte alignment, so after three ints (12 bytes) there are 4 padding bytes, total 24 bytes per Piece. Each Piece is a node walked by pointer-chasing; at 24 bytes, ~2.6 nodes per 64-byte cache line.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.proposedChange: Keep the int trio contiguous before the pointer (already the case, so the 4-byte pad is unavoidable while Next is a full pointer). If BufferIndex is always 0 or 1 (it is only ever set to 1 or copied from an existing piece originating as 0/1), narrow it to a byte and reorder as `byte BufferIndex; int Start; int Length; Piece* Next` — but padding then reappears. The actual usable win: if the document size fits in 2^31 the ints are fine; consider whether Start/Length could be int (they are). Net: leave as-is unless you can replace Next with a 4-byte index into the piece pool, which drops Piece to 16 bytes (4 nodes/line).
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.rationale: Replacing the raw Piece* Next with an `int NextIndex` into the newPieces/pool array removes the 8-byte pointer and its alignment padding, shrinking Piece from 24 to 16 bytes. That is a 33% reduction in node footprint, improving cache-line density during the pointer-chase traversal which is the dominant cost of every Insert/Delete.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.risk: Significant API change: every `->Next` deref becomes `pool[node->NextIndex]`, and null-termination must use a sentinel index (e.g. -1) instead of null. Requires the whole piece set to live in one contiguous pool addressable by index, which the current newPieces design already implies but s.Head being a raw pointer breaks. Only safe if the entire list (including original Head pieces) is pool-resident. Flagged as a design-level option, not a drop-in.

src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.summary: The middle removal loop reads cur->Length into `removed` then adds it to offset, but offset is not used after the loop except by the final trim check — the running offset bookkeeping can be simplified.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.currentCost: Inside `while (cur != null && offset + cur->Length <= end)` the body computes `removed = cur->Length; ...; offset += removed;`. The `removed` temp and the offset accumulation add a load+add per removed node, and offset is only consumed by the post-loop `offset < end` / `trim = end - offset` computation.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.proposedChange: Drop the separate `removed` temporary: `offset += cur->Length;` directly (the value of cur->Length is already loaded). This is already nearly what the code does; the only real micro-win is `offset += cur->Length;` instead of routing through `removed`, letting the compiler keep one fewer named live value. Marginal.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.rationale: Eliminates a redundant local; reduces register pressure slightly in the unrolled loop. The loop's real cost is the pointer-chase and the dual-condition test, which cannot be reduced without changing the data structure.
src/IAFahim.DS.PieceTable/PieceTable.cs.risk: Behavior-identical; `removed` equals cur->Length and is used nowhere else. Essentially a no-op for an optimizing compiler/Burst, so impact is genuinely low — include only as a readability/register-pressure nit.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Remove dead 'leftBetter' computation comparing an expression to itself.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: Line 139 'bool leftBetter = m * xl + b < m * xl + b;' performs two multiplies and two adds plus a compare, stores into a local that is never read. Pure wasted work on every recursive Add call.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: Delete the entire 'leftBetter' statement (line 139). It is never used and the comparison is always false.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Eliminates 2 IMULs + 2 ADDs + 1 CMP + a register store per node visited in the Li Chao insert recursion, with zero behavioral effect since the variable is dead.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: None. Variable is unused and the RHS has no side effects (m,xl,b are values). Observable behavior is identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Hoist repeated seg[node*2+0]/seg[node*2+1] line loads into locals to cut redundant pointer arithmetic and memory loads.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: After the possible swap, seg[node*2+0] and seg[node*2+1] are re-loaded at lines 152 and 157 (twice each across the two branches), recomputing node*2+0/node*2+1 addresses and reloading memory that holds the current line slope/intercept already settled.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: After the swap block, load 'long sm = seg[node*2+0]; long sb = seg[node*2+1];' once, then use 'm*xl+b < sm*xl+sb' and 'm*xr+b < sm*xr+sb'. Also reuse a single 'long idx2 = node*2;' base index.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Removes redundant address computation (node*2) and 2-4 redundant loads from the L1-resident seg array per visited node; shortens the dependency chain feeding the two branch comparisons.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: None: seg[node*2+0/1] are not written between the swap block and these comparisons, so cached locals are equal to re-reads. Behavior preserved.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Hoist node*2 base index to avoid recomputing the child slot address.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: seg[node*2+0] and seg[node*2+1] each recompute node*2; res = seg[node*2+0]*x + seg[node*2+1] does this twice per call.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: Compute 'long b2 = node*2;' (or int) once and index seg[b2] and seg[b2+1]. Minor but it is on the hot query path.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Saves one shift/add of address arithmetic per query node; trivially correct.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Hoist node*2 into a local to remove duplicate child-index computation across both recursive calls and the combine.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: node*2 and node*2+1 are computed 4 times each (in the two recursive call args and again in 'tree[node*2] + tree[node*2+1]'). Each is a separate shift+add.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: int c = node << 1; recurse with c and c+1; combine 'tree[node] = tree[c] + tree[c+1];'. Optionally [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] is not appropriate (recursive) but the index hoist still helps.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Reduces redundant address arithmetic in a hot tree-build recursion; same emitted loads, fewer index ops, shorter dependency chains.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: None. node*2 == node<<1 for the non-negative node indices used here (root starts at 1, always positive).

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Cache *top in a local across the multi-field history pushes instead of repeatedly dereferencing the top pointer.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: Each leaf/internal record reads *top via pointer multiple times (histNode[*top], histVal[*top], histType[*top], then (*top)++). The pointer-to-int 'top' forces reloads since the compiler cannot prove no aliasing with tree/lazy/histVal pointers.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: int t = *top; histNode[t]=node; histVal[t]=tree[node]; histType[t]=0; *top = t+1; (apply same pattern to all three push blocks and the two extra lazy pushes).
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Burst/.NET cannot assume *top doesn't alias the long*/int* buffers, so each *top use is a real memory load. Hoisting to a local collapses 4 dependent loads/stores into register ops, cutting the critical path of every history append.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: None as long as top does not alias the other buffers (it is a distinct scalar slot by contract). Behavior identical; just fewer reloads.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Same *top-hoist and node*2 child-index hoist as RangeAddInt64.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: Repeated *top dereferences per push and recomputed node*2/node*2+1 in the combine and recursive descent.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: int t=*top; ... *top=t+1; and int c=node<<1; index tree[c], tree[c+1].
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Removes redundant pointer loads and address arithmetic on the point-update path; identical emitted semantics.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: None; node positive, top non-aliasing by contract.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Hoist node*2 child base and avoid recomputing (mid-l+1)/(r-mid) terms; the 'l != r' guard is redundant inside the push-down.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: node*2 and node*2+1 recomputed up to 5 times; the 'if (l != r)' check at line 93 can never be false at that point because the earlier 'ql<=l && r<=qr' full-cover return already handles single-node ranges that fully match, but a leaf reached here with l==r would also have returned via that branch only if covered — leaf push-down does nothing useful. The branch is a predictable but unnecessary test when l==r implies mid==l and the deltas are (1) and (0).
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: long c=node*2; long c1=c+1; reuse c/c1. Keep the l!=r guard only if leaves can reach here; otherwise note that at a leaf l==r the lazy push-down writes lazy[child] out of the leaf's own subtree — confirm leaf never enters this block. Primary safe win: hoist the child index and load lazy[node] once (already done as 'val').
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Fewer address computations and a shorter dependency chain on the recursive sum's hot push-down; lazy[node] is already hoisted, mirror that for child indices.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: Do NOT remove the l!=r guard unless it is proven a leaf cannot reach this push-down with l==r (out-of-subtree child writes would corrupt state). The index-hoist alone is unconditionally safe.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Hoist Math.Min(r, mid-1) and b[mid] out of the inner search loop; precompute the loop bound and the invariant b value.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: Line 194 recomputes Math.Min(r, mid-1) on every iteration of the for-loop, and b[mid] is reloaded each iteration inside 'a[i]*b[mid]'. Both are loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: int hiBound = r < mid-1 ? r : mid-1; long bm = b[mid]; then loop 'for (int i=l; i<=hiBound; i++) { long val = dp[i] + a[i]*bm + c[i]; ... }'.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Removes a branch/min and a redundant load from every inner iteration of the divide-and-conquer DP optimization (the dominant cost of this algorithm), tightening the per-candidate work to one load+mul+two adds+compare.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: None. mid is fixed within the call so b[mid] is invariant; Math.Min(r,mid-1) has no side effects. Branchless or branchy min both fine.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Make the per-element predicate branchless to aid Burst auto-vectorization and remove a data-dependent branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: 'if (cond) count++;' inside the loop is a data-dependent conditional increment; with random interval data the branch mispredicts and it inhibits clean SIMD vectorization of the count.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: count += (starts[i]<=point & point<=ends[i]) ? 1 : 0; using a single bitwise-& of the two comparisons folded to an int, e.g. 'count += ((starts[i]<=point) & (point<=ends[i])) ? 1 : 0;' (and the 4-way & for RectangleStabbing). This pattern lets Burst emit a vector compare + masked add.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Branchless accumulation removes misprediction penalty and is the canonical shape Burst vectorizes into packed compares and horizontal-add, cutting the linear scan cost by a SIMD-width factor.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: Use bitwise & (not &&) only on the boolean comparison results to avoid short-circuit branches; comparisons have no side effects so eager evaluation is safe. Semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.summary: Cache *top in a local across the three decrements in the rollback loop body.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.currentCost: Each undo does histVal[--(*top)], histNode[--(*top)], histType[--(*top)] — three read-modify-writes through the 'top' pointer per record, each a dependent load+store of *top.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.proposedChange: int t=*top; ... read histVal[t-1], histNode[t-2], histType[t-3]; *top = t-3; (mirroring the actual 3-slot stride). Hoist *top once per iteration in Run's while loop and once in UndoLast.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.rationale: Collapses three dependent pointer-memory RMWs into register arithmetic plus one final store, shortening the loop-carried dependency chain that gates rollback throughput.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/RollbackSeg.c.risk: Must preserve the exact 3-decrement stride and ordering currently used so the same slots are read and the same final *top results. This is a behavior-preserving rewrite of the existing index pattern only; do not alter which slots are read.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/Retroactive.c.summary: File contains only empty stub methods; no optimization possible until implemented.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/Retroactive.c.currentCost: Six empty static void methods with no bodies; unused 'using System;' / 'using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;' add nothing.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/Retroactive.c.proposedChange: No perf action. Optionally drop the unused usings for cleanliness; otherwise leave until the algorithms are implemented.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackSeg/Retroactive.c.rationale: Nothing executes, so there is nothing to make faster or leaner.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.summary: Rollback rebuilds the heap with a full O(targetSize) build-heap (Floyd) plus appends entirely NEW swap records to the SAME history buffer instead of UNDOING the recorded swaps. This is both asymptotically wasteful and a likely correctness/state bug: history grows on rollback and heapIdx/priority invariants are not actually reverted to the snapshot state.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.currentCost: O(targetSize) build-heap on every rollback regardless of how few operations occurred since the snapshot; plus each HeapifyDown writes 4 ints/swap into history via currentHistSize, mutating the undo log during an undo. Undo of K recorded swaps should be O(K), not O(n).
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.proposedChange: Replace the build-heap loop with a true history-replay undo: while (*currentHistSize > /*history offset for targetSize*/) { decrement by 4; read (i, smallest, heapIdxI, heapIdxSmallest); swap ptr[i]/ptr[smallest] back and restore heapIdx entries }. Track the history offset corresponding to a snapshot (return both heapSize and histSize from Snapshot) so Rollback unwinds exactly the swaps performed since the snapshot. Do not append to history during Rollback.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.rationale: Undoing the exact recorded operations is O(K) in the number of swaps since the snapshot versus O(n) for a full rebuild; for incremental rollback (the whole point of an undoable structure) K << n. It also avoids the dependency-chain and store traffic of writing 4 ints per swap into history on the undo path, and keeps the heap's secondary indices (heapIdx, and the value-vs-priority correspondence) exactly consistent with the snapshot.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.risk: This is a semantics CHANGE relative to the current implementation, but the current implementation does not appear to restore the snapshot state correctly (it appends to history and only re-heapifies a truncated array, which can leave heapIdx/priority associations differing from the pre-op state). Must confirm against intended semantics and tests before applying. If a full rebuild is genuinely intended, at minimum stop writing to history during Rollback (pass a throwaway/no-op histSize or a separate counter) to avoid corrupting the undo log.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.summary: Less<T> is constrained where T : unmanaged, IComparable<T> but never uses T — it only compares priority[a] < priority[b]. The unused IComparable<T> constraint propagates through HeapifyDown/HeapifyUp/Rollback and forces an interface constraint that is pure dead weight for Burst and the JIT.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.currentCost: Every heap method carries an IComparable<T> generic constraint that is never exercised; interface constraints can pessimize generic specialization and add no value since comparison is on int priority, not on T.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.proposedChange: Drop IComparable<T> from Less, HeapifyDown, HeapifyUp, and Rollback, leaving where T : unmanaged. The body priority[a] < priority[b] is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.rationale: Fewer constraints means simpler, more Burst-friendly generic specialization and no risk of interface-dispatch codegen. The value T is only ever moved (ptr[i] swaps), never compared, so IComparable<T> is provably unnecessary.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.risk: Pure API/constraint narrowing; observable behavior identical. Only risk is source-compat for external callers that relied on the constraint signature, which is internal to this library.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.summary: Init takes an unused 'capacity' parameter and Rollback takes an unused 'sizeOfT' parameter. Dead parameters mislead callers and waste an argument register/stack slot at the call site.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.currentCost: Two unused parameters across the public API; each call passes a value that is computed/loaded for nothing, and they obscure the actual contract (the structure only stores a single int size at *mem).
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.proposedChange: Remove 'int capacity' from Init and 'int sizeOfT' from Rollback (or document why they exist if reserved). Signatures become Init(void* mem) and Rollback(void* mem, int targetSize).
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.rationale: Eliminates per-call argument setup for values never read and clarifies the API. The methods' bodies already ignore these parameters, so removal is behavior-preserving for the stored state.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.risk: Source-breaking signature change for callers; if the parameters are intentionally reserved for a future variable-stride layout, keep them but mark intent. No runtime semantics depend on them today.

src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.summary: Union reloads parity[a]/parity[b] and recomputes the pa>pb branch structure twice (once per parity-equal branch). The two branches differ only in the parity value written (1 vs 0), which equals (parity[a]==parity[b]) ? 1 : 0.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.currentCost: Duplicated branch body and an extra top-level branch on (parity[a]==parity[b]); parity[a] and parity[b] are read multiple times forming a longer dependency chain before the merge.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.proposedChange: Compute int newParity = (parity[a] == parity[b]) ? 1 : 0; then a single pa>pb branch: if (pa > pb) { parent[pa] = pb; parity[pa] = newParity; } else { parent[pb] = pa; parity[pb] = newParity; }. Cache parity[a]/parity[b] into locals once.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.rationale: Collapses two nearly identical branch bodies into one, halving the merge-logic code size (better I-cache/branch-predictor behavior) and reducing redundant loads of parity[a]/parity[b]. Fewer distinct branch targets.
src/IAFahim.DS.RollbackStack/RollbackSta.risk: Behavior-identical: the original writes exactly 1 when parities equal and 0 when they differ, which newParity reproduces. No edge cases since parity values are 0/1. Verify against tests.

src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.summary: Update redundantly re-derives child sizes via two null-checked Size() calls; inline the null checks into a single branchless-friendly accumulation and mark the recomputation cheaper.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.currentCost: Update calls Size(n->Left) and Size(n->Right), each = 1 branch (null test) + 1 load (n->Size). Two separate conditional loads with a data-dependent branch each, executed on EVERY node touched during SplitAt and Merge (the hot path).
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.proposedChange: Inline: 'RopeNode* l = n->Left; RopeNode* r = n->Right; int s = 1; if (l != null) s += l->Size; if (r != null) s += r->Size; n->Size = s;'. Optionally compute branchlessly when pointers are non-null on the common path. Keeps AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.rationale: Avoids two out-of-line-eligible Size() call frames and lets the compiler keep l/r in registers (they are re-loaded again by callers like Merge right after). Fewer redundant loads of Left/Right which were just written by the caller.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.risk: None — identical result. Size() is already inlined so the win is modest, but it removes the dependency on Size's exact codegen and enables register reuse of l/r.

src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.summary: SplitAt is unbounded recursion (depth = tree height); under Burst on mobile this risks stack overflow and is not tail-call-optimized. Convert to an iterative split using the standard treap zig-zag pointer-chasing loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.currentCost: Recursion depth ~O(height) = O(log n) expected but O(n) worst-case for an adversarial/degenerate treap. Each frame spills root, k, left, right to the stack; Burst cannot guarantee TCO. On mobile thread stacks (often 512KB-1MB) a degenerate rope can fault.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.proposedChange: Rewrite SplitAt iteratively: walk from root maintaining the two 'attach point' double-pointers (RopeNode** for the growing left and right spines), updating sizes on the way back via an explicit ascent, or accumulate along the descent. Each merge/split in treaps has a well-known iterative form using two result spines.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.rationale: Removes recursion frames entirely -> no stack-overflow risk, smaller per-op cost (no call/ret, no frame setup), Burst-friendly straight-line loop that can keep the cursor pointers in registers. Same O(height) work, lower constant.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.risk: Iterative treap split must preserve exact Update ordering (sizes updated bottom-up). Must keep identical attach semantics so the resulting tree shape and all node Sizes match the recursive version. Verify against the recursive version with tests before shipping.

src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.summary: Merge is unbounded recursion mirroring SplitAt's risk; convert to the iterative two-pointer treap merge to remove frames and stack-overflow risk under Burst.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.currentCost: Recursion depth up to O(height); each frame setup + the post-call Update forms a long dependency chain (each Update waits for the recursive Merge to return). On a degenerate tree this is O(n) deep on a constrained mobile stack.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.proposedChange: Iterative merge: maintain a cursor double-pointer; at each step compare priorities, advance into a->Right or b->Left, record the attach point; on completion walk the recorded spine back updating Size. Avoids recursion and the serialized return-then-Update chain.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.rationale: Eliminates call/ret overhead and frame spills, removes stack-overflow risk, and lets sizes be fixed in one ascending pass instead of interleaved with returns — shorter critical dependency chain, better for Burst straight-line codegen.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.risk: Must reproduce exact priority tie-break (a->Priority > b->Priority chooses a; equal goes to b) and identical Update bottom-up order so resulting Sizes are byte-identical. Tie-break direction is observable; preserve '>' (not '>=').

src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.summary: Collect is recursive in-order traversal writing one byte per node; recursion depth O(height) risks stack overflow and is slow. Convert to an iterative in-order walk (Morris or explicit cursor) writing into buf.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.currentCost: O(m) nodes but O(height) recursion depth, plus a call frame per node carrying buf and ref idx. The ref int idx forces a memory-resident counter passed by address across every frame, blocking it from staying in a register.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.proposedChange: Iterative in-order traversal: use Morris traversal (O(1) extra space, temporarily rethreads Right pointers and restores them) OR, since the subtree is small and bounded by len, an explicit stackalloc cursor stack sized to the known height. Keep idx as a local int in a register, return the count.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.rationale: Removes per-node call frames and the by-address idx, keeping the write index in a register -> tighter store loop into buf that Burst can keep dense. No recursion -> no stack-overflow risk. Morris keeps RAM at O(1).
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.risk: Morris mutates Right pointers transiently — must fully restore them before Merge re-attaches mid, and is not safe if interrupted/concurrent. Explicit-stack variant avoids mutation but needs a height bound; size the stackalloc to a safe max or compute height first. Ensure idx advances in identical left-root-right order.

src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.summary: RopeNode is 32 bytes due to padding around 'byte Value'; the int Size/Priority and byte fields leave 7 bytes of padding. Layout is already near-optimal but Priority width can likely shrink.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.currentCost: sizeof(RopeNode)=32 on 64-bit: Size(4)+Priority(4)+Value(1)+pad(7)+Left(8)+Right(8). Each node is a separate allocation; 32B is half a 64B cache line so two nodes per line — acceptable but the 7 padding bytes are pure waste.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.proposedChange: Leave field order (Size, Priority before pointers is already cache-friendly: hot Size loads precede pointer loads). Cannot reclaim the padding without shrinking pointers. If Priority's range is bounded (treap priorities are random ints), no change. Document that the struct is intentionally 32B/cache-line-friendly so future edits don't add fields that push it past 32B.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.rationale: Keeping the node at exactly 32 bytes guarantees two-per-cache-line and 8-byte pointer alignment with no false sharing within a node. The current layout already puts the frequently-read Size first.
src/IAFahim.DS.Rope/Rope.cs.risk: None as-is; this is a guard against regressions. Do NOT reorder Value before the ints (would not help) and do NOT add a 5th field that breaks the 32B boundary. Narrowing Priority to short would NOT shrink the struct (padding absorbs it), so it's not worth the range risk.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..summary: Recompute of `prev != 0` and the four `prev != 0 ? x[prev] : 0` ternaries hoist to a single branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..currentCost: Each Run call evaluates `prev != 0` 5-6 times (lines 27,28,29,30,36/39). On the hot O(n log n) build path this is 5-6 dependent compares + selects per node, plus redundant `leftChild[prev]`/`rightChild[prev]` loads that are reloaded again inside the recursive branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..proposedChange: Compute `int hasPrev = prev; int pl = prev != 0 ? leftChild[prev] : 0; int pr = prev != 0 ? rightChild[prev] : 0;` once at top, then `leftChild[node]=pl; rightChild[node]=pr; cnt[node]=(prev!=0?cnt[prev]:0)+addCount; ...`. Reuse pl/pr in the recursive call: `leftChild[node]=Run(pl, lo, mid, ...)`. This removes the duplicate `leftChild[prev]` load and folds the repeated branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..rationale: Reduces the per-node dependency chain (one compare feeding many selects) and eliminates a redundant memory load (leftChild[prev]/rightChild[prev] read twice). Fewer loads = fewer chances of cache stalls along the recursion spine of length log(hi-lo).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..risk: Semantics identical: prev==0 path already yields 0 for child reads. No signed/overflow concern.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..summary: Recursive persistent update can be converted to an iterative loop, removing log-depth call overhead and stack spills.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..currentCost: Recursion of depth ceil(log2(hi-lo+1)) per inserted element; each frame passes 10 pointer/scalar args, causing register spill/reload and call/return overhead in Burst-compiled code.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..proposedChange: Rewrite as a while loop walking lo/hi/mid, allocating each node and linking parent->child as it descends, since the recursion is purely tail-structured (only one of left/right recurses). Keep a running `parentChildSlot` pointer to patch.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..rationale: Eliminates per-level function-call prologue/epilogue and argument marshaling; the path is strictly linear (single child recursion), so no real recursion is needed. Burst will keep all state in registers.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..risk: Must preserve allocation order (node ids must match recursive version if any caller depends on ids) — node allocation order is identical when iterating top-down, so ids match. Verify no caller relies on call-stack ordering.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..summary: Redundant `lRoot != 0`/`rRoot != 0` re-evaluation across recursion; precompute child indices once.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..currentCost: Lines 70-71 / 83-84 evaluate `lRoot != 0` and `rRoot != 0` twice each (once for left child, once for right child) plus the loads leftChild[lRoot], rightChild[lRoot] etc. The compare result is recomputed per branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..proposedChange: Hoist `int ll = lRoot!=0?leftChild[lRoot]:0; int lr = lRoot!=0?rightChild[lRoot]:0; int rl = rRoot!=0?leftChild[rRoot]:0; int rr = rRoot!=0?rightChild[rRoot]:0;` after the leaf/cover checks, then pass ll/rl to the left recursion and lr/rr to the right.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..rationale: Halves the number of `!=0` compares per internal node and groups the four child loads so the compiler can issue them without interleaved branches, shortening the dependency chain on the dual-tree descent.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..risk: Behavior-preserving; both children are always visited here (no short-circuit savings lost). No overflow concern.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..summary: Hot leaf-ish recursive Run methods lack [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] and `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices` is imported but unused.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..currentCost: The CompilerServices using is present (line 3) but no attribute is applied, unlike DualSegment which uses it consistently. Recursive methods cannot be fully inlined, but small wrappers (Kth/Count/Sum entry) called once per query benefit from inlining into callers.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..proposedChange: Either remove the unused `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;` to match house cleanliness, or apply [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] where it actually helps (it will not help self-recursive methods, so prefer removal for the recursive ones).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..rationale: Dead using adds noise; recursion defeats inlining so attribute would be cargo-cult here. Removing keeps signal high and matches the no-dead-import convention.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/ChairmanTree..risk: None; purely cosmetic / does not change codegen for recursive methods.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/DualSegment.c.summary: `idx & -idx` lowest-set-bit isolation is already optimal; the only win is removing the redundant `using System` (unused) — code is otherwise tight.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/DualSegment.c.currentCost: BIT update/query loops are O(log n) with `idx & -idx` which lowers to a single neg+and. The `using System;` (line 3) is unused. AggressiveInlining is correctly applied.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/DualSegment.c.proposedChange: Remove `using System;`. No algorithmic change — the Fenwick walk is already canonical and branch-minimal.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/DualSegment.c.rationale: This file is essentially optimal: power-of-two-free, branchless inner loop, narrow Int32 variants provided. Only the dead using is removable.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.summary: Repeated `node * 2` and `node * 2 + 1` recomputation; compute `int lc = node << 1; int rc = lc + 1;` once per call.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.currentCost: RunInt32 computes `node * 2` 3x and `node * 2 + 1` 3x (lines 16-18). RangeAddInt32, RangeSetInt32, PushInt32, PushSetInt32, LazySegmentUpdate all recompute these multiple times per node, every recursion level over the whole tree.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.proposedChange: At the top of each method (after leaf check) compute `int lc = node << 1; int rc = lc + 1;` and reuse for both tree[] indexing and lazy[] indexing. Replace all `node * 2`/`node * 2 + 1`.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.rationale: Removes 2-4 redundant integer multiplies/adds per node visited; on a full O(n) build and O(log n) per update this is a constant-factor across every node. Shifts also avoid imul latency where the JIT/Burst doesn't strength-reduce inside complex expressions.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.risk: node*2 == node<<1 for all non-negative node ids (1-based tree, always positive). Safe; no overflow vs original since identical arithmetic.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.summary: Duplicated push logic across LazySegmentApply.PushInt32 and LazySegmentPush.Run (byte-identical); and lazy[node] is reloaded ~5 times.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.currentCost: PushInt32 (lines 67-78) and LazySegmentPush.Run (lines 98-109) are identical code maintained twice. Inside, lazy[node] is loaded 5 times (lines 72,73,74,75 + the !=0 check). The `* (mid-l+1)` and `* (r-mid)` recompute segment widths.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.proposedChange: Cache `int lz = lazy[node];` once; branch `if (lz != 0 && l != r)`; reuse lz for all four updates. Consolidate the two duplicate push implementations into a single call so only one is maintained and inlined. Optionally cache `int lc=node<<1, rc=lc+1`.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.rationale: Cuts 4 redundant memory loads of lazy[node] to 1 register read per push; removes duplicated code reducing icache footprint and maintenance risk. Push is on every update/query descent, so this is hot.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.risk: Identical results; lazy[node] is not mutated between reads except the final reset, so caching is safe.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.summary: `(l + r) >> 1` can overflow for large indices; ChairmanTree uses the safe `l + ((r - l) >> 1)`. Inconsistent and a latent bug, not slower.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.currentCost: Lines 15,38,61,71,84,102,126,148 use `(l + r) >> 1`. For l,r near int.MaxValue/2 this overflows to a negative mid, corrupting recursion. Not a perf issue but a correctness/consistency divergence from ChairmanTree's `lo + ((hi-lo)>>1)`.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.proposedChange: If segment indices can ever exceed ~2^30, switch to `l + ((r - l) >> 1)` to match ChairmanTree and avoid overflow; otherwise document the bounded-input assumption. Same cycle count either way.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.rationale: Same instruction count (add+shift vs sub+shift+add is one extra add, negligible) but removes a latent overflow. Consistency with the rest of the module.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.risk: For typical segment-tree sizes (l,r < 2^30) current code is correct; only flag/guard if large-index use is intended. No behavior change for in-range inputs.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.summary: bool* hasLazy uses 1 byte per node; acceptable, but recursive Run methods lack inlining hints on the small leaf helpers (Pull).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.currentCost: LazySegmentPull.Run is a tiny leaf (one add) called once per internal node on every update but is a separate non-inlined static method (no attribute). LazySegmentPush.Run likewise.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to LazySegmentPull.Run and LazySegmentPush.Run so the trivial pull/push fold into the recursive updater, removing call overhead per node.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.rationale: Pull is a single memory add; the call/return overhead dominates the work. Inlining it eliminates that overhead at every internal node of the update path.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LazySegmentTr.risk: None functionally. Push is small enough that inlining its branch is a net win; verify it does not bloat the recursive method past Burst inline thresholds (it is small).

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/KineticDS.cs.summary: All methods are empty stubs — no implementation to optimize; unused `using` directives present.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/KineticDS.cs.currentCost: KineticTournamentBuild/Update/Winner, KineticSegmentTreeBuild/Query are empty bodies. `using System;` and `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;` are unused. No optimization possible until implemented.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/KineticDS.cs.proposedChange: No perf action. Remove the two unused usings for cleanliness, or implement the data structure. Flagging that this module is non-functional, not a hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/KineticDS.cs.rationale: Cannot optimize absent code; reporting state so the orchestrator knows the file is a stub.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LiChaoTree.cs.summary: Methods are empty stubs; only Line.Eval is real. Line struct is blittable/Burst-friendly already. Unused usings.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LiChaoTree.cs.currentCost: PersistentLiChaoAdd/Query, DynamicLiChaoRollback, LiChaoRollback, DivideConquerHullOptimization, OnlineChtAdd/Query are empty. Line.Eval (M*x+C) is one fma-shaped expression, already optimal. `using System;` and CompilerServices unused.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LiChaoTree.cs.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] to Line.Eval (hot leaf when implemented) and remove unused usings. No other action until the tree is implemented.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LiChaoTree.cs.rationale: Line.Eval will be the innermost hot operation of any Li Chao / CHT query; marking it inline ensures it folds into query loops. The rest is unimplemented.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/LiChaoTree.cs.risk: None; Eval is pure (M*x+C), deterministic, blittable.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.summary: Per-node insertion sort makes build O(n log n * n) worst case; replace with bottom-up merge of children.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.currentCost: Each internal node copies its sub-range from arr then runs MergeSortTreeShared.Sort (insertion sort, O(len^2)). For a leaf-segment of length len the parent re-sorts len elements from scratch. Across all levels this is O(sum over nodes of len^2). For the root node alone that is O(n^2), dominating everything; total build is Theta(n^2) worst case (reverse-sorted input).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.proposedChange: Build bottom-up: leaves are single elements (already sorted), and each internal node's sorted array is the merge of its two already-sorted children's arrays (standard 2-way merge, O(len)). Recurse to children first, then merge nodes[2*node+1] and nodes[2*node+2] into nodes[node]. This makes per-level work O(n) and total O(n log n).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.rationale: Merge-sort-tree construction is canonically O(n log n) via merging sorted children. The current code throws that away by re-sorting each node from the raw array with an O(len^2) insertion sort, turning the whole build into O(n^2). Merging two sorted runs is a linear single pass with sequential memory access (cache-friendly, Burst-vectorizable).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.risk: Output arrays must be identical (each node holds the multiset of its range, sorted ascending). Merge must be stable-equivalent for equal keys but since values are plain ints and only sortedness matters, any merge order is fine. Must ensure the merge writes into nodes[node] which is a distinct pool region from the children, so no aliasing. Recursion order changes (children before parent merge) but Run's contract (final node arrays sorted) is preserved.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.summary: Insertion sort is O(len^2); if kept, only needed for leaves (len==1) — otherwise unused after bottom-up merge.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.currentCost: O(len^2) comparisons/moves per call. Called once per node on the full range length, including the root with len==n.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.proposedChange: After switching Build to bottom-up merge, Sort is no longer called on multi-element ranges and can be deleted (leaves of length 1 are trivially sorted). If a general sort is still desired elsewhere, replace insertion sort with a non-recursive heapsort or introsort for O(n log n) worst case.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.rationale: Removes the quadratic primitive entirely from the hot build path; dead-code elimination also shrinks the Burst-compiled module.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.risk: Only safe to delete if Build no longer depends on it. If any external caller uses MergeSortTreeShared.Sort it must be retained; it is internal so callers are confined to this module.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.summary: Branchy binary search has a data-dependent branch per step; a branchless variant cuts mispredicts in the hot Kth loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.currentCost: Each loop iteration has an unpredictable `if (a[mid] <= val)` branch (~log2(len) per call). MergeSortTreeKth.Run calls CountLessEqual ~30 times (1<<30 range), each doing UpperBound at every covered node — so this branch executes O(30 * log n * log n) times per Kth query, with high misprediction rate on random data.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.proposedChange: Use a branchless lower/upper-bound over a half-open window: maintain `int* base = a; int len = n;` and loop `while (len > 1) { int half = len >> 1; base += (base[half-1] <= val ? half : 0); len -= half; }` with the conditional add expressed via a mask (`int take = -(base[half-1] <= val); base += take & half;`). Keep AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.rationale: Converts a hard-to-predict branch into a data-dependent pointer add the compiler can render as a cmov/select, removing pipeline flushes. Burst/LLVM lowers the masked add to branchless code. Memory access pattern is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.risk: Must reproduce exact UpperBound (first index with a[i] > val) and LowerBound (first index with a[i] >= val) semantics including empty (n==0) and all-elements-match cases. The masked form `take & half` relies on take being 0 or -1 (all-ones); verify the comparison yields a full mask. Off-by-one in the window reduction is the main correctness hazard — needs careful unit coverage against the current versions.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.summary: Value-space binary search over a fixed 1<<30 range re-walks the whole segment tree ~30 times; persistent-tree / fractional-cascading walk would cut a log factor.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.currentCost: Run does ~30 iterations of value bisection, each calling CountLessEqual which descends O(log n) tree nodes doing an UpperBound (O(log n)) each. Total ~30 * log n * log n binary searches per Kth query, all re-decomposing the same [ql,qr] into the same O(log n) canonical nodes every iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.proposedChange: Hoist the [ql,qr] canonical-node decomposition out of the value-bisection loop: precompute once the up-to-2*log n covering node indices into a small stackalloc int buffer, then each value-bisection step only does UpperBound on that fixed set instead of re-running the recursive CountLessEqual decomposition. This removes the repeated range-overlap branching and recursion overhead (the dominant constant factor).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.rationale: The set of canonical segment-tree nodes covering [ql,qr] is invariant across the 30 value-bisection iterations. Computing it once and reusing eliminates ~29 redundant tree descents and their qr<l / r<ql comparison branches, replacing recursion with a flat loop over <=2*log n cached node ids — better ILP and no call overhead.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/MergeSortTree.risk: Requires a stackalloc buffer sized to 2*ceil(log2 n) ints; bound must be guaranteed by caller's n. The decomposition must enumerate exactly the same nodes CountLessEqual's full-cover branch hits. Behavior identical; only intermediate work removed.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.summary: Five separate `prev != 0 ? ... : 0` ternaries recompute the same predicate; branch once and copy.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.currentCost: Lines 11-15 evaluate `prev != 0` five times and do five conditional loads. The predicate is identical each time; the compiler may not fully CSE the branch across five distinct array bases, costing redundant compares and poor branch grouping per node creation (every update allocates O(log n) nodes).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.proposedChange: Replace with a single branch: `if (prev != 0) { leftChild[node]=leftChild[prev]; rightChild[node]=rightChild[prev]; sumArr[node]=sumArr[prev]; lazyArr[node]=lazyArr[prev]; cntArr[node]=cntArr[prev]; } else { leftChild[node]=0; rightChild[node]=0; sumArr[node]=0; lazyArr[node]=0; cntArr[node]=0; }`. Since pools are not guaranteed zero-initialized the else must still clear.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.rationale: One predictable branch instead of five evaluations of the same condition; the copy block is a straight run of loads/stores the compiler can schedule densely. Reduces instruction count on the per-node hot path of every persistent update.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.risk: Semantically identical only if the else-branch zeroing matches the original (each ternale yields 0 when prev==0). Must keep the zero-store else block — do not assume node memory is pre-zeroed. No observable change.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.summary: Redundant `node != 0` re-test on line 43 after the function already returned for node==0 on line 42.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.currentCost: Line 42 returns when `node == 0`. Line 43 then computes `inherited + (node != 0 ? lazyArr[node] : 0)` — but node is provably non-zero here, so the ternary and its branch are dead work executed on every non-trivial query node.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.proposedChange: Replace line 43 with `long lazy = inherited + lazyArr[node];`. The `node != 0` guard is unreachable-false-removed by the early return above.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.rationale: Eliminates a per-node compare-and-select that can never take the zero path, shrinking the dependency chain before the recursive split. Pure constant-factor win on the query hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentLaz.risk: None — line 42's early return guarantees node != 0 at line 43. Strictly behavior-preserving.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.summary: `prev == 0 ? 0 : left[prev]` recomputed though the prev!=0 copy block already loaded those values.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.currentCost: In Build, lines 11-15 (under `if (prev != 0)`) copy left[prev]/right[prev]/tree[prev] into node. Then lines 23-24 recompute `prev == 0 ? 0 : left[prev]` and `prev == 0 ? 0 : right[prev]`, re-loading left[prev]/right[prev] and re-evaluating the prev predicate. Same pattern in Update lines 50/52.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.proposedChange: Hoist `int lp = prev != 0 ? left[prev] : 0; int rp = prev != 0 ? right[prev] : 0;` once near the top, store into left[node]/right[node], and pass lp/rp to the recursive calls. This both populates the node and feeds recursion from registers instead of re-reading memory and re-branching.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.rationale: Removes a duplicate memory load and a duplicate branch per recursion level on the persistent build/update hot path (O(log n) nodes per operation). Values come from registers already in flight, shortening the dependency chain to the recursive call.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.risk: Must preserve that when prev==0 the recursive child arg is 0 and left[node]/right[node] end up correct (they are overwritten by the returned child id afterward anyway). Behavior identical; pure CSE.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.summary: Two byte-identical query functions; consolidate to one to reduce code size and improve I-cache/inlining.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.currentCost: PersistentSegmentQuery.RunInt32 (lines 60-67) and DynamicSegmentQuery.Run (lines 96-103) have identical bodies. Burst compiles both, doubling generated code for the same operation and splitting the instruction cache footprint.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.proposedChange: Have one delegate to the other (or expose a single shared internal query and keep thin public wrappers). Wrappers marked AggressiveInlining so call sites pay nothing.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.rationale: Less duplicated machine code improves instruction-cache locality on mobile and keeps a single optimized version. No behavioral change since bodies are identical.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/PersistentTre.risk: Purely organizational; must keep both public entry points for API stability (ergonomics) — make one forward to the other rather than deleting. Zero semantic change.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegTreeOnTree.summary: sumArr is int; on accumulation-heavy DSU-on-tree merges int sums can overflow — consider widening or documenting bound.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegTreeOnTree.currentCost: sumArr is int*. Merge accumulates sumArr[aRoot] += sumArr[bRoot] and Update adds val repeatedly. For large n with many merges the running sum can exceed int range, silently wrapping (Burst has no overflow checks).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegTreeOnTree.proposedChange: If counts/sums can exceed 2^31, switch sumArr to long* (as PersistentLazySeg already does). If the design guarantees sums fit in int, document the invariant with a named constant/comment so callers know the safe bound; otherwise widen.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegTreeOnTree.rationale: Prevents silent wraparound corruption on large inputs — a correctness concern, not just perf. Matches the long-based design already used in PersistentLazySeg for the same family of structures.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegTreeOnTree.risk: Widening to long doubles sumArr memory traffic and cache footprint; only do it if overflow is actually reachable for intended n. This is a semantics/correctness flag, not a guaranteed speedup — keep int if the caller contract bounds sums to int range.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.summary: Dead ternary: `res == -1 ? -1 : res` always returns res
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.currentCost: One redundant compare + conditional-select (cmov or branch) on every top-level call, plus reader confusion.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.proposedChange: Replace `int res = RunNode(...); return res == -1 ? -1 : res;` with `return RunNode(tree, 1, 0, n - 1, r, &target);`. Both branches of the ternary yield `res`, so it is a provable no-op.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.rationale: Eliminates a compare and a conditional move/branch; identical output for all inputs since both arms are `res`.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.risk: None. Pure simplification; observable behavior identical. (Note: this differs from MaxRight.Run where the ternary maps -1 -> n and is meaningful; do not apply the same removal there.)

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.summary: `long* target` indirection forces target to memory across the hot descent loop; pass/return by value to keep it in a register
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.currentCost: Taking `&target` in Run() forces the local onto the stack. Each `*target` read in the `while` loop is a memory load and each `*target -= ...` is a load+store, defeating register allocation on the hottest path (one such access per tree level, O(log n) per call).
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.proposedChange: Refactor RunNode to take `long target` by value and return the residual when it returns -1. E.g. signature `int RunNode(int* tree, int node, int lo, int hi, int l, long* targetOut)` is the current shape; instead thread target as a value parameter and, for the descent loop, keep a local `long t = target;` operating purely on `t` (no dereference), writing back only when needled by the recursive accumulation path. Concretely: in the while loop replace all `*target` with a local `long t` initialized once from the pointer and stored back only on the early-return-(-1) accumulation branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.rationale: Burst/LLVM keeps a value-typed local in a register; pointer aliasing through `long*` prevents that and inserts a load/store per level. Removing the indirection in the tight while loop cuts ~1 load (+1 store on the subtract branch) per level.
