src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.risk: Must preserve the side-effecting subtraction semantics: when a subtree is fully consumed (`tree[node] < target`), the caller's residual `target` must be decremented exactly as today so sibling subtrees see the reduced target. Any refactor must still write the residual back before returning -1 from a fully-scanned subtree; only the in-loop dereferences (which never cross a call boundary) are safe to localize.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.summary: Recomputed `node * 2` and `node * 2 + 1` child indices; hoist to locals to shorten the dependency chain
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.currentCost: In Build/Set the left child index is computed up to 3x (`node*2` in recurse arg and in `tree[node*2]`), right child 2x. Each is a shift+(add). The compiler usually CSEs these, but making them explicit guarantees a single computation and clarifies intent.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.proposedChange: Add `int left = node << 1; int right = left | 1;` once after computing mid, then use `left`/`right` for both the recursive calls and the `tree[left] + tree[right]` combine. `left | 1` is equivalent to `left + 1` since left is even (node<<1), and OR can issue on more ports than ADD.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.rationale: Single computation of each child index; `right = left | 1` is branch/carry-free and may relieve the ALU add port. Shortens the read-after-write chain feeding the final `tree[node] = ...` store.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.risk: `left | 1` equals `left + 1` only because `node << 1` is always even — true here for all `node >= 0` (valid tree nodes are >= 1). If `node` could be negative the shift is still well-defined for the index arithmetic the code already relies on, so no new constraint beyond what the code assumes. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.summary: Disjoint-range test `qr < l || ql > r` is evaluated at every recursion node before the containment test; cheap but the two-branch short-circuit can be made branch-lighter and the call elides a frame when out of range higher up
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.currentCost: Each node does up to two compares with a short-circuit OR (a branch), then a two-compare AND for containment. For a point/narrow query most descended nodes hit the disjoint test, paying a mispredict-prone branch per visited node.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.proposedChange: Keep semantics but order so the common containment fast-path is reachable with fewer branches, or compute the disjoint condition branchlessly: `if (((uint)(qr - l) | (uint)(r - ql)) ...)` style is unsafe with overflow here, so prefer leaving logic but marking these leaf recursive helpers `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` is NOT applicable (recursive). Instead, hoist `node<<1`/`(node<<1)|1` as in the Build/Set item to share the child-index computation across the two recursive calls.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.rationale: The only safe, real win here is sharing the child-index arithmetic (same as the hoist item); a branchless disjoint test risks signed overflow on `qr - l` for extreme indices, so it is rejected.
src/IAFahim.DS.SegmentTree/SegmentTree.c.risk: Branchless overflow-based range test is REJECTED: `qr - l` / `r - ql` can overflow for int indices near int.MIN/MAX, changing results. Only the child-index hoist is safe and is already captured above.

src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.summary: Hoist the per-iteration shift in the loop bound and precompute the inner span constant.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.currentCost: The loop condition `i + (1 << j) <= n` recomputes `1 << j` on every iteration of the inner build loop. Across all O(n log n) build iterations this is an extra shift plus the add in the bound test each time, lengthening the dependency chain of the loop-control path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int span = 1 << j;` (or `int limit = n - (1 << j);`) once before the loop and use `for (int i = 0; i <= limit; i++)`. `half` is already hoisted; do the same for the full-block width.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.rationale: Strength-reduces a loop-invariant shift+compare to a single compare against a precomputed bound, shortening the loop-control dependency chain and helping Burst keep the inner copy/min loop tight and vectorizable.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.risk: None. `1 << j` is loop-invariant; `n - (1 << j)` cannot underflow because the outer loop guarantees `(1 << j) <= n`. Observable behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.summary: Replace the element-by-element copy of level 0 with a bulk memcpy.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.currentCost: `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) table[i] = arr[i];` is a scalar load/store loop. Burst may autovectorize it, but it is plainly a contiguous blittable copy that does not need a hand loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.proposedChange: Use `Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned(table, arr, (uint)(n * sizeof(int)))` (and the long variant) or `UnsafeUtility.MemCpy` to copy the whole level-0 row in one call.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.rationale: A dedicated memcpy uses the widest available stores and is a single intrinsic call, eliminating loop overhead and guaranteeing wide moves rather than relying on the autovectorizer to recognize the copy idiom.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.risk: Low. Source and destination are distinct, non-overlapping blittable buffers, so CopyBlock semantics match the loop exactly. Must ensure `n * sizeof(...)` does not overflow int for very large n (cast to long/uint as needed).

src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.summary: Eliminate the per-element integer division `i / bSize` in the build scan and hoist the block-count expression.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.currentCost: The main scan does `int bIdx = i / bSize;` for every one of the n elements — an integer divide per element, the most expensive integer ALU op. Also `(n + bSize - 1) / bSize` is recomputed in the init-loop bound each iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.proposedChange: Walk blocks instead of dividing: precompute `int blockCount = (n + bSize - 1) / bSize;` once for the init loop, then build mins with a nested loop `for (int b = 0, base = 0; base < n; b++, base += bSize) { int end = base + bSize; if (end > n) end = n; int m = int.MaxValue; for (int i = base; i < end; i++) if (arr[i] < m) m = arr[i]; block[b] = m; }` which removes the division and the redundant init pass entirely.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.rationale: Replaces n integer divisions with simple additions and fuses the init (setting MaxValue) and the min-accumulation into one pass, halving memory traffic over `block` and removing the divide chain. bSize is data-dependent (sqrt(n)) so it is NOT a power of two and cannot be turned into a shift; converting to a counter is the only divide-free route.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.risk: None for valid input. The block boundary clamp `end > n -> end = n` exactly reproduces the partial final block; result per block is identical. Local `base`/`end` are int and bounded by n.

src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.summary: Hoist `(bl + 1) * blockSize` and `br * blockSize` out of loop bounds; use branchless min in the scalar tails.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.currentCost: The first tail loop recomputes `(bl + 1) * blockSize` in its bound each iteration, and `br * blockSize` is recomputed for the third loop's start. The three inner loops use a data-dependent branch `if (arr[i] < res) res = arr[i];` which can mispredict on adversarial inputs.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int leftEnd = (bl + 1) * blockSize; int rightStart = br * blockSize;` once. Replace `if (x < res) res = x;` with branchless `res = x < res ? x : res;` (cmov/min pattern) in all three scan loops, matching the build code's already-branchless style.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.rationale: Removes a multiply from each iteration of the first tail and converts unpredictable data-dependent branches to a branchless select that Burst lowers to a min instruction, eliminating mispredict penalties and aiding vectorization of the block-sweep loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.risk: None. Loop bounds are invariant within the call; ternary min is semantically identical to the if-update for ints (no NaN concerns).

src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.summary: Replace the hand-rolled 5-branch software log2 with a hardware bit-scan intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.currentCost: This is a leaf called on every disjoint-sparse query (the per-query critical path). It executes up to five dependent compare-and-conditional-shift steps, a long serial dependency chain, where a single lzcnt/bsr instruction suffices.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.proposedChange: Under Burst, compute `31 - math.lzcnt(value)` (Unity.Mathematics) for floor-log2 of a nonzero uint, or use `System.Numerics.BitOperations.Log2` which Burst/JIT lowers to LZCNT/BSR. Keep the current software version only as a non-Burst fallback if needed.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.rationale: Collapses a ~5-step branchy dependency chain into one hardware instruction, drastically cutting latency on the query hot path and removing branches the predictor must track.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.risk: Caller guarantees value != 0 here (l != r implies l ^ r != 0), matching lzcnt's nonzero-input domain, so 31-lzcnt is exact. If the project forbids Unity.Mathematics in this module, the intrinsic must be confirmed available; otherwise keep the manual version. No semantic change for the guaranteed nonzero input.

src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.summary: Hoist the repeated `j * n` row-offset multiply out of the inner accumulation loops.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.currentCost: Inside both descending and ascending inner loops, every store recomputes `table[j * n + i]` — a multiply `j * n` per element across the full O(n log n) build. The row base is invariant for the entire level j.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.proposedChange: Precompute `long* row = table + (long)j * n;` (or `int rowBase = j * n;`) once at the top of the `for j` body and index `row[i]` / `row[mid]` in all four store sites. Likewise `arr` reads are already direct.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.rationale: Removes one integer multiply from every table write in the build, replacing `base + i` index math with a single add against a hoisted pointer; shortens the address-calculation dependency chain and is a pattern Burst keeps in registers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.risk: None. `j * n` is invariant within each outer iteration; pointer form must use a 64-bit offset (`(long)j * n`) to avoid int overflow for very large tables, otherwise identical addressing.

src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.summary: Avoid recomputing `j * n` twice and `1 << j` in the two table index expressions.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.currentCost: `table[j * n + l]` and `table[j * n + r - (1 << j) + 1]` each evaluate `j * n` (two multiplies) and one shift on the per-query hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int span = 1 << j; long* row = table + (long)j * n;` then `left = row[l]; right = row[r - span + 1];`. Use a branchless `return left < right ? left : right;` (already branchless).
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.rationale: Folds two multiplies into one hoisted pointer add and reuses the shift, trimming the query's address-math dependency chain; AggressiveInlining is already present so this directly benefits the caller.
src/IAFahim.DS.Sparse/Sparse.cs.risk: None. Pure index-arithmetic refactor; use 64-bit offset for the pointer to avoid overflow on large n. Output identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.summary: Hoist GetUnsafeBucketData() out of the two separate calls; it is invoked twice per Execute, each call re-fetching the same bucket struct.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.currentCost: Two calls to this.Map.GetUnsafeBucketData() (lines 118-119), each returning a struct and reloading keys/values base pointers. The accessor is not guaranteed to be free; it copies a UnsafeParallelHashMapBucketData struct each time.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.proposedChange: Call var bucketData = this.Map.GetUnsafeBucketData(); once, then int* keys = (int*)bucketData.keys; int* values = (int*)bucketData.values; — exactly as SpatialHexMap.QuantizeJob already does at lines 158-160.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.rationale: Removes one redundant struct-returning call and the associated field loads per worker invocation. Burst may already CSE this, but the source-level duplication is unnecessary and the sibling files already use the single-call form, so this also unifies the pattern.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.risk: None; identical observable behavior. GetUnsafeBucketData returns the same data for both fields within one Execute.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.summary: length, start, end and the index==Workers-1 tail correction are loop-invariant per Execute but the per-element bounds branch (math.any(quantized >= QuantizeWidth)) prevents vectorization; the design intent (skip vs throw) differs from siblings but the divide-by-Workers chunking recomputes Positions.Length/Workers and %Workers redundantly.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.currentCost: Positions.Length / Workers and Positions.Length % Workers are two integer divisions; division is ~20-40 cycles on mobile ARM. Done once per Execute (acceptable) but the same division pair is recomputed in every sibling QuantizeJob too.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.proposedChange: Compute int total = Positions.Length; int q = total / Workers; int start = index * q; int end = (index == Workers - 1) ? total : start + q; — replacing the separate add of (total % Workers) with a direct assignment to total on the last worker, eliminating one division.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.rationale: The last-worker branch end = start + q + (total % Workers) equals total exactly (since start = (Workers-1)*q and (Workers-1)*q + q + total%Workers = Workers*q + total%Workers = total). Replacing with end = total removes the modulo division entirely on the hot last-chunk path and is provably identical.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.risk: None: algebraically exact for all positive Workers. Guard: Workers is math.max(1, ...) at call sites so Workers>=1; division by zero impossible.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.summary: Division by quantizeStep per entity can be turned into a multiply by a precomputed reciprocal stored on the struct.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.currentCost: Quantized does (position + halfSize) / step — two FP divisions (componentwise float2 / float) per entity in the hot loop. Division is not pipelined; ~10-20 cycles each on ARM.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.proposedChange: Add a precomputed float invQuantizeStep = 1f/quantizeStep (computed once in the SpatialMap constructor) and pass it into QuantizeJob / Quantized, replacing /step with *invStep: new int2(math.floor((position + halfSize) * invStep)). Apply identically to SpatialMap, SpatialKeyedMap, LocalSpatialMap (PartialSpatialMap.Quantized) ReadOnly paths.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.rationale: Converts a per-entity vector division into a per-entity vector multiply by a value computed once at build setup. floor of a product vs quotient differs only by fast-math rounding which Burst already permits. Large entity counts make this a real build-time win.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.risk: Reciprocal multiply can produce a value epsilon below an integer where true division gave exactly the integer, flipping floor() to the cell below on boundary-aligned positions. Burst fast-math already makes this non-bit-exact, so within existing tolerance; if exact floor on grid-aligned coordinates is contractual, reject. Must change all four Quantized variants consistently to keep maps interchangeable.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.summary: Quantized and Hash are duplicated verbatim across four files (SpatialMapUtility, PartialSpatialMap, SpatialKeyedMap, with the hex variant differing); consolidating removes divergence risk and ensures one place to apply the reciprocal optimization.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.currentCost: Four near-identical static Quantized/Hash implementations. No runtime cost, but any perf fix (e.g. reciprocal) must be applied 3-4 times and can drift (e.g. SpatialMap casts size to float at line 22 but SpatialKeyedMap/LocalSpatialMap do not, line 29/32).
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.proposedChange: Extract the grid Quantized/Hash into a single internal static helper used by SpatialMap, SpatialKeyedMap and PartialSpatialMap. Note the existing inconsistency: SpatialMap.cs line 22 uses (float)size/quantizeStep while SpatialKeyedMap line 29 and LocalSpatialMap line 32 use size/quantizeStep (int division before ceil) — these produce DIFFERENT quantizeSize for the same inputs and should be reconciled.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.rationale: Single source of truth lets the reciprocal/strength-reduction land once and stay correct; also surfaces a real latent bug where integer size/quantizeStep truncates before math.ceil, under-sizing the map versus the float version.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap.cs.risk: Behavior-changing if you 'fix' the int-vs-float divide; flag for human decision — SpatialMap (float div) and SpatialKeyedMap/LocalSpatialMap (int div) currently compute different sizes. Pure refactor of identical bodies is safe; reconciling the divide is a semantics change requiring sign-off.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/LocalSpatialMa.summary: Eliminate the redundant modulo on the tail worker by assigning end = Positions.Length directly.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/LocalSpatialMa.currentCost: Positions.Length % Workers is an extra integer division (~20-40 cycles on ARM) executed on the last worker's Execute.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/LocalSpatialMa.proposedChange: Replace the if (index == Workers-1) { end += Positions.Length % Workers; } block with end = (index == Workers-1) ? Positions.Length : end; (or compute end as Positions.Length on the last worker), removing the % division.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/LocalSpatialMa.rationale: start + length + (Length % Workers) on the last worker algebraically equals Positions.Length, so the modulo result is redundant. Removes a division from the per-Execute setup.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/LocalSpatialMa.risk: Exact for Workers>=1, guaranteed by math.max(1, JobWorkerCount) at the call site.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialKeyedMa.summary: Same redundant tail modulo; assign end = Positions.Length on the last worker.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialKeyedMa.currentCost: One integer modulo (Positions.Length % Workers) per last-worker Execute, ~20-40 cycles on mobile.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialKeyedMa.proposedChange: end = (index == Workers - 1) ? Positions.Length : start + length; removing the modulo.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialKeyedMa.rationale: Algebraic identity start+length+(total%Workers)==total on the last chunk makes the modulo redundant.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialKeyedMa.risk: Exact for Workers>=1 (guaranteed by math.max(1, JobWorkerCount)).

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..summary: Same redundant tail modulo; assign end = Positions.Length on the last worker.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..currentCost: One integer modulo per last-worker Execute.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..rationale: Identity start+length+(total%Workers)==total on the last chunk.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..summary: Precompute the inverse of outerRadius once and multiply, instead of two divides by outerRadius per quantize call (plus the /3f).
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..currentCost: Each Quantized call does two divisions by outerRadius (q and r lines 204-205) plus a division by 3f for the y term. Division is the single most expensive scalar FP op (~10-20+ cycles, not pipelined). This runs once per entity in the hot QuantizeJob loop and again per query.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..proposedChange: Store invOuterRadius = 1f/outerRadius alongside outerRadius (compute once in the constructor/ReadOnly and pass it in, or compute float inv = math.rcp(outerRadius) at the top of Quantized). Then q = (Sqrt3Over3 * position.x - position.y * (1f/3f)) * inv; r = ((2f/3f) * position.y) * inv;. The /3f is already foldable to a constant multiply (1f/3f) which Burst with fast-math does, but making it explicit guarantees it.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..rationale: Replaces 2-3 hardware divides per call with 1 reciprocal + multiplies. With many entities this is a large constant-factor win in the build loop. Burst's default fast-math usually converts /const to *recip(const), but division by the runtime variable outerRadius is NOT automatically reciprocal-folded unless the value is hoisted, so storing inv as a precomputed field is the real win.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..risk: math.rcp / 1f/x is a different rounding than true division and can shift a borderline math.round() result to an adjacent hex cell. Acceptable only if the library tolerates fast-math (Burst default already enables it, so observable results are already non-IEEE-exact). If bit-exactness across this change is required, reject; otherwise precompute the field which keeps a true reciprocal once and is the safer variant.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..summary: math.distance computes a sqrt that is partly undone; restructure to avoid the sqrt when the cell is outside the radius is not possible, but the max(0, d-r) then square pattern still needs the sqrt — however the squaring of (d-r) can be reformulated to avoid one multiply, and the early-out branch avoids the subtract.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..currentCost: math.distance does a sqrt (dot+sqrt). Then max(0, d - outerRadius), then multiply. sqrt is ~15-30 cycles on mobile. Called per candidate cell during range queries.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..proposedChange: Compute float distSq = math.distancesq(position, center); float rSq = outerRadius*outerRadius; if (distSq <= rSq) return 0f; float d = math.sqrt(distSq); float m = d - outerRadius; return m*m;. This skips sqrt entirely for cells whose center is within outerRadius (the common near-cell case where result is 0).
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..rationale: distancesq avoids sqrt; the sqrt is only computed for cells actually outside the inner radius. For a typical neighborhood query many candidate cells are at or near the query point, so a meaningful fraction take the branchless distSq<=rSq early-out and skip the expensive sqrt.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..risk: Branch adds a predictable compare; for fully-outside workloads it is pure overhead (one compare + one square of outerRadius). rSq can be hoisted if outerRadius is a field. Semantics identical: max(0,sqrt(distSq)-r)^2 == 0 exactly when distSq<=r^2.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..summary: The y component and yDiff are only needed for the branch selection; the cube-coordinate reconstruction can drop one round and one abs by noting only the largest-diff axis is corrected.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..currentCost: Three math.round, three math.abs, and a 3-way branch per quantize. y = -x - z and ry = round(y) plus yDiff are computed unconditionally even though ry is overwritten in two of three branches.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..proposedChange: Keep as-is for clarity, OR: since rx,ry,rz must satisfy rx+ry+rz==0 and only the coordinate with the largest rounding error is recomputed, you can compute xDiff,yDiff,zDiff branchlessly via math.select to pick which axis to fix, avoiding the dependent branch mispredicts. E.g. compute all three corrected candidates and select. Marginal.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..rationale: Removes a 3-way unpredictable branch (cube rounding error distribution is data-dependent and hard to predict) in favor of branchless select, helping pipeline on mobile. Constant-factor only.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..risk: Must preserve the exact tie-break order (xDiff>yDiff && xDiff>zDiff, else yDiff>zDiff, else z). math.select reformulation must replicate the same strict-inequality precedence or a tie lands on a different axis, changing the chosen hex for points exactly on a cell boundary. Low impact; only worth it if branch profiling shows misprediction.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..summary: Two math.all calls over separate comparisons can be fused into a single unsigned-range test.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..currentCost: local = axial - boundsMin; then math.all(local >= 0) && math.all(local < boundsSize) — two vector compares, two horizontal all-reductions, one boolean AND with a short-circuit branch.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..proposedChange: Cast to unsigned: bool inside = math.all((uint2)local < (uint2)boundsSize); — a single comparison treats negative local (which wraps to large uint) as out-of-range, folding the >=0 and <size checks into one math.all.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..rationale: Classic branchless range check: (uint)(x) < (uint)n is true iff 0<=x<n. Halves the compares and removes the short-circuit branch. Used in the debug ValidatePosition path (Conditional), so impact is mostly on the public ReadOnly.IsWithinBounds used in query loops.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialHexMap..risk: Requires boundsSize components to be non-negative (always true: boundsSize = max-min+1 >= 1). Signed-to-unsigned reinterpret of local is the intended trick; correct for all int2 inputs given non-negative bounds. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.summary: GetUnsafeBucketData() is invoked twice to fetch keys and values from the same bucket struct.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.currentCost: Two calls to Map.GetUnsafeBucketData() (lines 120-121), each returning the full UnsafeBucketData struct, before the hot loop. The struct fetch and its internal pointer copies are duplicated.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.proposedChange: Cache the struct once: 'UnsafeParallelHashMapBucketData bucketData = this.Map.GetUnsafeBucketData(); long* keys = (long*)bucketData.keys; int* values = (int*)bucketData.values;'
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.rationale: Removes a redundant property/method evaluation that copies a multi-pointer struct. One fetch instead of two; both pointers come from the same snapshot, identical result.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.risk: None. The bucket data does not change between the two calls; both reads return the same pointers. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.summary: Hash recomputes width*depth every call; it is loop-invariant within QuantizeJob.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.currentCost: '(long)quantized.z * width * depth' performs an extra 64-bit multiply (width*depth) per entity. In QuantizeJob the width/depth pair is constant for the whole job.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.proposedChange: Precompute the slab stride once. Either pass a single 'long widthDepth' (= QuantizeWidth*QuantizeDepth as long) into the job and add a Hash overload 'Hash(int3 q, int width, long widthDepth)' returning 'q.x + (long)q.y*width + (long)q.z*widthDepth', or compute 'long widthDepth = (long)QuantizeWidth * QuantizeDepth;' once before the loop in Execute.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.rationale: Eliminates one 64-bit multiply per entity by hoisting the invariant stride. Same arithmetic result.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.risk: None if widthDepth is computed as (long)width*depth to match current promotion order. Current expression is '((long)z * width) * depth' — ensure the precomputed stride uses 64-bit math to avoid 32-bit overflow for large width*depth; (long)QuantizeWidth*QuantizeDepth preserves the value range and ordering.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.summary: Per-element division and modulo to compute the worker's [start,end) range; these are loop-setup constants but use div/mod that could be moved into job scheduling.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.currentCost: 'Positions.Length / Workers' and 'Positions.Length % Workers' execute once per Execute call (once per worker), plus the 'index == Workers-1' branch. Minor, but the chunking math is recomputed for every worker invocation.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.proposedChange: Compute base length and remainder once when building the job (store them as fields, e.g. ChunkLength and Remainder) so Execute only does 'start = index*ChunkLength; end = start + ChunkLength + (index==Workers-1 ? Remainder : 0)'. Alternatively distribute the remainder across the first 'Remainder' workers to balance load instead of dumping it all on the last worker.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.rationale: Removes a div and a mod from each Execute. The remainder-on-last-worker scheme also creates a load imbalance (last worker does up to Workers-1 extra items); spreading it improves parallel wall-clock for large counts.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.risk: Low. Precomputing div/mod is semantics-preserving. The load-balancing variant changes which worker processes which index but not the final map contents (values are written by absolute index). Verify the IJobFor index range (workerCount, 1) still maps one Execute per worker.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.summary: Upper-bound cull only checks quantized >= QuantizeWidth; negative quantized components (positions below -halfSize) are not culled and produce negative-component hashes.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.currentCost: 'math.any(quantized >= this.QuantizeWidth)' guards the high edge only. A position with any component < -halfSize yields a negative quantized lane, a negative/colliding hash, and a written entry that escapes the intended grid.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.proposedChange: If out-of-low-bound positions are possible, extend the cull to 'math.any(quantized < 0) || math.any(quantized >= this.QuantizeWidth)' (or 'math.any(quantized >= QuantizeWidth | quantized < 0)' as a single branchless mask). If callers guarantee positions are always within [-halfSize, halfSize), leave as-is and document the precondition.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.rationale: Branchless combined bound mask is one comparison pair feeding math.any; prevents malformed keys without adding a second branch. Improves robustness with no extra branch when fused into one any().
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.risk: This CHANGES behavior for currently-unguarded negative inputs (they would now be skipped instead of stored with a bad hash). Only adopt if the current acceptance of negative cells is a latent bug; if Build is treated as unchecked/valid-input-only, reject to preserve observable behavior.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.summary: Positions[entityInQueryIndex] uses the safe NativeArray indexer in the hot loop, incurring bounds/safety overhead in editor and an extra layer Burst must elide.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.currentCost: Each iteration indexes NativeArray<T> via the managed-style indexer reading .Position. In safety builds this is a bounds check; even with safety off it is an indirection Burst must lower.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.proposedChange: Obtain the raw pointer once: 'T* pos = (T*)this.Positions.GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr();' then 'float3 position = pos[entityInQueryIndex].Position;'. Job is already unsafe, so this fits the existing pattern (mirrors the keys/values raw-pointer usage).
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.rationale: Removes per-iteration safety-check indirection and gives Burst a clean linear pointer access it can vectorize/prefetch, consistent with the raw keys/values writes already in this loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMap3.cs.risk: Loses the safety-system bounds check in editor builds; correct only because start/end are derived from Positions.Length. Requires Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe using. Behavior identical for valid ranges.

src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMapUtil.summary: Per-element float division by step in the hottest loop; step is loop-invariant and could be a precomputed reciprocal multiply.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMapUtil.currentCost: '(position + halfSize) / step' executes a 3-lane float divide per entity inside QuantizeJob.Execute. Division has ~3-6x the latency/throughput cost of multiplication on PC and especially on mobile ARM NEON.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMapUtil.proposedChange: Hoist 'float invStep = 1f / this.QuantizeStep;' out of the loop (or store an invQuantizeStep field computed once in the ctor) and change Quantized to multiply: 'new int3(math.floor((position + halfSize) * invStep))'. Keep a step-based overload for SpatialMapReadOnly3 if exact reciprocal differs.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMapUtil.rationale: Replaces N vector divides with one reciprocal plus N vector multiplies. Multiply is significantly cheaper and pipelines better; the divisor is constant across the whole job.
src/IAFahim.DS.SpatialMap/SpatialMapUtil.risk: 1/step then multiply is not always bit-identical to direct divide; math.floor could land on a different integer cell for values exactly on a quantization boundary. If exact-divide semantics must be preserved, restrict this to the Build/QuantizeJob path where cell assignment tolerance is acceptable, or document the boundary tolerance. Reject if bit-exact cell parity with the readonly query path is required.

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.summary: Avoid recomputing x->Size in Update(x); it equals p's pre-rotation Size.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.currentCost: Two full Update() calls per Rotate, each doing 2 null-checks + 2 child-size loads + 2 adds. Rotate is the hottest primitive (called O(depth) times per Splay).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.proposedChange: Capture the rotated node's new size cheaply: x occupies p's old slot and its subtree is exactly p's old subtree, so x->Size = (old p->Size). Read int oldPSize = p->Size before mutating, call Update(p) (recompute, since p lost a subtree), then set x->Size = oldPSize instead of calling Update(x).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.rationale: x's subtree after a single rotation contains exactly the same node set as p's subtree before the rotation, so its size is invariant. Replacing Update(x) (2 branches + 2 loads + 2 adds) with a single stored-int assignment removes ~6 ops and a dependency chain per rotation.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.risk: Correct only because Update(p) must run BEFORE assigning x->Size if Update(x) were to read p->Size — but here we read oldPSize first, so ordering is safe. Sum field (in the SplayRevNode variant) is NOT invariant under this trick only if Sum changed; for plain Splay there is no Sum so it is fully safe. Note this exact same opportunity applies to SplayRangeReverse.Rotate for both Size and Sum (Sum is also subtree-invariant, so x->Sum = oldPSum too).

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.summary: IsLeftChild(x)==IsLeftChild(p) redundantly re-derives parent relationships already in hand (p, g).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.currentCost: Each loop iteration calls IsLeftChild(x) and IsLeftChild(p); each call reloads x->Parent / p->Parent and compares ->Left==node. That is 2 pointer loads + 1 compare per call, 2 calls = ~6 ops, despite p and g being local.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.proposedChange: Compute the two booleans directly from the already-loaded locals: bool xLeft = (p->Left == x); bool pLeft = (g->Left == p); then 'if (xLeft == pLeft) Rotate(root, p); else Rotate(root, x);'. This is inside the g!=null branch where g is known non-null.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.rationale: Eliminates redundant x->Parent and p->Parent dereferences (p==x->Parent and g==p->Parent are already loaded), shortening the dependency chain to two cheap compares against cached pointers. Improves Burst's ability to keep values in registers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.risk: Semantics identical: IsLeftChild(x) is exactly p->Left==x given p=x->Parent (and p!=null since we are in the loop), and IsLeftChild(p)==g->Left==p given g=p->Parent!=null in this branch. No behavior change.

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.currentCost: x->Parent != null && x->Parent->Left == x reloads x->Parent on the second clause (unless the JIT/Burst proves no aliasing, which it generally cannot across a pointer write).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.proposedChange: Load once: SplayNode* p = x->Parent; return p != null && p->Left == x;
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.rationale: One fewer memory load on a method called on every splay/rotate step. Burst cannot assume x->Parent is loop-invariant across writes, so the explicit local removes the second dependent load.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/Splay.cs.risk: None; pure read, single-threaded. Same value.

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.summary: Update(x) recomputes Size and Sum that are invariant under a single rotation (equal p's pre-rotation values).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.currentCost: Update(p)+Update(x) per Rotate: each Update does 4 null-checks + 4 field loads (2 Size, 2 Sum) + several adds. Doubled work since x's aggregates are derivable.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.proposedChange: Before mutating, capture int oldPSize = p->Size; long oldPSum = p->Sum; call Update(p) to recompute p (it lost a subtree), then set x->Size = oldPSize; x->Sum = oldPSum; instead of Update(x).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.rationale: After one rotation, x's subtree is exactly p's old subtree, so both Size and Sum are unchanged. Replaces a full Update (8+ loads/adds + 4 branches) with two register-to-memory stores, cutting the per-rotation aggregate cost roughly in half.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.risk: Must read oldPSize/oldPSum before any pointer rewiring and before Update(p). Sum is a plain additive aggregate so it is subtree-invariant; Key is not touched. Behavior preserved. The lazy Rev flag is unaffected (Push already applied along Splay path before rotations).

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.summary: Redundant null guard: Rotate checks x==null || x->Parent==null but every caller (Splay loop) already guarantees x and x->Parent are non-null.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.currentCost: Two branches at the top of every Rotate call; Splay only calls Rotate from inside 'while(!IsRoot(x))' and after loading p=x->Parent (non-null), so the guard never trips.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.proposedChange: Drop the guard in the hot Rotate, or keep a Debug-only assert. Since Rotate is private and only called from Splay where non-null is established, the check is dead on the hot path. (Matches the 'Unchecked Run' house convention.)
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.rationale: Removes two never-taken branches per rotation, shortening the instruction stream and helping Burst’s straight-line codegen.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.risk: Only safe because Rotate is private and the sole caller Splay guarantees x!=null and x->Parent!=null (it dereferences p=x->Parent unconditionally). If a future external caller appears this guard would need restoring. Note Splay.cs Rotate already omits this guard, so this also unifies the two implementations.

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.summary: Recursive PushAll uses O(depth) stack frames; convert to an explicit top-down pass without recursion.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.currentCost: PushAll recurses parent-ward then pushes on unwind, costing one call frame per ancestor (O(tree height), up to O(n) for a degenerate splay tree before balancing). Recursion also blocks Burst (Burst cannot compile recursive functions).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.proposedChange: Walk up to the root collecting nodes into a fixed stackalloc SplayRevNode* buffer (height bounded by current depth) then Push them top-down in a loop; or, since Splay immediately rotates x to root, push along the descent in Kth (already done) and push x's ancestors iteratively. Replace recursion with an iterative two-pointer/stack loop.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.rationale: Eliminates per-frame call overhead and, critically, makes the function Burst-compilable (Burst rejects recursion). An iterative version also has better i-cache behavior and no risk of deep-recursion stack growth.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.risk: Must preserve top-down push order (root first) since Rev flags must propagate parent-to-child before children are read. A stackalloc buffer needs a safe upper bound on height; for a splay tree height is unbounded in the worst case, so use a heap-free growable scheme or push during the upward walk only if order is corrected. Get ordering wrong and reversals corrupt — verify carefully.

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.summary: Update loads each child pointer twice (once for Size, once for Sum).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.currentCost: x->Left is tested/loaded for both l and ls; x->Right for both r and rs. That is 4 redundant null-compares and the JIT may reload the child pointer.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.proposedChange: Load children once: SplayRevNode* L = x->Left; SplayRevNode* R = x->Right; int l = L!=null?L->Size:0; long ls = L!=null?L->Sum:0; etc. Better, fold: x->Size = (L!=null?L->Size:0)+(R!=null?R->Size:0)+1; x->Sum = (L!=null?L->Sum:0)+(R!=null?R->Sum:0)+x->Key; reusing the same L/R locals.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.rationale: Halves the null-check count (2 instead of 4) and lets Size and Sum reuse the same loaded child pointer and the same branch predicate, reducing dependency chain length and branch count in a function called twice per rotation.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.risk: None; pure recompute from current child state, single-threaded. Identical result.

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.summary: zig/zag predicate recomputes child relations available from cached p,g.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.currentCost: bool zig = (g->Left==p)==(p->Left==x): fine, but g may be re-dereferenced; combined with the Rotate guard removal the dependency chain can be tightened.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.proposedChange: Keep the zig computation (already uses cached p,g) but pair it with removing Rotate's redundant null guard (separate item) so the inner Rotate calls are branch-lean. Optionally hoist bool pLeft = (p->Left==x) once and reuse.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.rationale: Marginal: keeps the well-written predicate but ensures the rotations it drives are not re-validating non-null pointers. Mostly realized via the Rotate-guard removal.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeReverse.c.risk: None on its own; this is a coordination note with the Rotate-guard item rather than an independent change.

src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeQuery.cs.summary: Kth in SplayRangeQuery calls SplayRangeReverse.Push (which can flip Rev) during a read-only sum query path; confirm intent and consider sharing one Kth implementation.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeQuery.cs.currentCost: Two near-identical Kth implementations exist (one in SplayRangeQuery, one private in SplayRangeReverse), each calling Push and re-deriving left size. Duplicate code, and the query path performs lazy Rev pushes (writes) during what is semantically a read.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeQuery.cs.proposedChange: Factor a single internal static Kth(SplayRevNode* root, int k) in SplayRangeReverse and reuse it from SplayRangeQuery to avoid divergence; load cur->Left once for the size read (same single-load fix as Update).
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeQuery.cs.rationale: Removes duplicated logic (maintenance + i-cache) and applies the load-once micro-opt to the descent loop. Pushing is required for correctness (Rev must be resolved before reading subtree sizes), so it stays.
src/IAFahim.DS.Splay/SplayRangeQuery.cs.risk: Push is intentional and must remain (size/sum are only valid after lazy reversal is pushed down). Pure refactor + single-load; no semantic change. Just ensure accessibility (internal) since house rules forbid exposing extra public surface unnecessarily.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.summary: Update calls SizeOf(Left)/SumOf(Left) and SizeOf(Right)/SumOf(Right) as four separate calls, each re-loading the same child pointer and re-doing the null check twice per child.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.currentCost: Per Update: 2 loads of node->Left, 2 loads of node->Right, 4 null-compares. Update is called on every Merge/Split/Insert/Erase recursion frame, so this is the hottest leaf in the library.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Cache the child pointers once and fold size+sum: `TreapNode* l = node->Left; TreapNode* r = node->Right; int ls = l == null ? 0 : l->Size; long lsum = l == null ? 0 : l->Sum;` (same for r). Reading l->Size and l->Sum off one already-loaded l also keeps both fields in the same cache line.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.rationale: Halves the child-pointer loads and null branches (4 compares -> 2), and l->Size / l->Sum share a 64B cache line so the second access is free once l is dereferenced. Fewer dependency-chain stalls on the pointer chase. Burst will fold the two null checks into one predicated load.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.risk: None. Pure local CSE; identical results including the node==null early-out which is preserved. node==0 case unchanged.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.summary: bool Rev sits between int Size and long Sum, causing alignment padding before Sum, inflating the node and reducing nodes-per-cache-line.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.currentCost: Key(4),Priority(4),Size(4),Rev(1)+3pad,Sum(8),Left(8),Right(8): the Rev byte forces 3 pad bytes before the 8-byte Sum, wasting space on the hottest pointer-chasing struct.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Reorder fields to put all 4-byte ints together and the bool last (or as a packed byte): Key,Priority,Size, then Sum,Left,Right, then bool Rev at the end. This eliminates the mid-struct padding.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.rationale: Tighter packing = more nodes per 64B line during Merge/Split traversal, directly cutting cache misses on the dominant cost of a treap.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.risk: Reorders public struct layout (ABI change). Semantics unchanged. Only safe if external initializers use named-field init, not positional/blittable-copy that assumes current order.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.summary: Kth is recursive but is a strict downward traversal (tail-recursive in both branches), so it needlessly consumes stack frames per level.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.currentCost: One call frame per tree level (O(log n) frames); recursion prevents Burst from keeping state in registers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Rewrite as an iterative loop like Rank/Find: `while (root != null){ Push(root); int ls = SizeOf(root->Left); if (k<ls) root=root->Left; else if (k==ls) return root; else { k -= ls+1; root=root->Right; } } return null;`
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.rationale: Eliminates call/return overhead and stack frame setup per level; keeps k and root in registers. Same O(log n) work, lower constant factor and no recursion depth pressure. Matches the iterative convention already used by Find/Rank.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.risk: None. Identical traversal and Push order. Note Push mutates (lazy reversal), so the iterative version must Push each visited node exactly as the recursion did — preserved.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.summary: Split (key-ordered) is recursive only down one spine; it can be iterated, but more impactfully it recomputes Update on the way back which is unavoidable. The recursion itself is single-path and could be unrolled to a loop with pointer-to-pointer threading.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.currentCost: One frame per level; Update per level on return. Recursion frames add call overhead Burst cannot always elide.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Leave Split recursive ONLY if Burst fails to flatten it; otherwise convert to iterative top-down split threading TreapNode** cursors, then a single bottom-up Update pass. Lower priority than the Update CSE above.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.rationale: Removes per-level call overhead. Marginal vs the Update CSE win, included for completeness.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.risk: Iterative split with lazy Push is subtle; the recursive form is correct and clear. Only refactor if measured frame overhead matters — house style and correctness favor leaving as-is. Low confidence, low impact.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.summary: RangeQuery is a read (returns Sum) but mutates the tree via two Splits/Merges and re-roots *root; it is not pure and does O(log n) structural writes per read.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.currentCost: Same split/merge write churn as TreapRangeMin.QueryMin for a read-only operation.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.proposedChange: Provide a non-destructive sum-fold over the key range [l,r] (BST-ordered descent accumulating SumOf over fully-covered subtrees), Pushing lazy only along the path. Keep the existing split/merge version if callers depend on the re-root.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.rationale: Eliminates structural mutation on reads, lowers write traffic and cache pressure, and makes the query deterministic/purer (no topology change).
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/Treap.cs.risk: Lazy (Rev) must be pushed along the descent to read correct subtree sums; result identical. Larger refactor; verify with tests. Low-medium confidence.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.summary: Same redundant child re-load pattern as Treap.Update: Size(Left)+Sum(Left) and Size(Right)+Sum(Right) load each child pointer twice and null-check it twice.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.currentCost: 4 child-pointer loads and 4 null-compares per Update; called on every Split/Merge frame in AffineRange/QuerySum.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `TreapAffineNode* l = n->Left, r = n->Right;` once, then compute size and sum from the cached pointers with a single null test each.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.rationale: Cuts pointer loads and branches in half and exploits cache-line locality of Size/Sum within one node. Same win as Treap.Update; this is the per-frame hot leaf.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.summary: Merge Pushes BOTH a and b unconditionally at entry, but only one of them is descended into per call; pushing the non-chosen node propagates its lazy one level deeper than necessary, doing extra Apply work.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.currentCost: Two Push calls per Merge frame; the loser's Push (e.g. Push(b) when a wins) pushes b's lazy to b's children even though b is returned intact as a subtree root — extra Apply(Left)/Apply(Right) writes that were not required for correctness of this merge step.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.proposedChange: Push only the node being descended into: in the a-wins branch Push(a) before touching a->Right; in the b-wins branch Push(b) before touching b->Left. The other node needs no push because Merge does not read/restructure its children at this frame.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.rationale: Halves Push (and thus Apply) work per Merge frame, removing speculative lazy propagation. Fewer writes, shorter dependency chains.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapAffineRange.cs.risk: Subtle correctness: must confirm the un-pushed node's lazy stays consistently pending for later access. Standard treap merge only needs to push the node whose child link is rewritten. Verify against tests before applying — medium-low confidence; if any caller relies on both being pushed, reject. Same pattern in TreapImplicit/TreapRangeMin/TreapRangeReverse Merge.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.summary: Update duplicates child pointer loads/null-checks across Size() and Sum() helpers for both children.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.currentCost: 4 loads + 4 null compares per Update, on every Merge/SplitBySize frame.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.proposedChange: Cache `TreapImplicitNode* l = n->Left, r = n->Right;` once; derive size and sum from the cached pointers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.rationale: Halves redundant loads/branches; Size and Sum of a child sit in one cache line so the fused read is near-free after the first deref.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.summary: ApplyLazy computes (long)n->Size * lazy with a sign-extending widening of an int that is always >= 1; fine, but the n->Lazy += lazy / HasLazy = true store happens even when accumulating onto a node that will be immediately overwritten by a deeper push. Minor: the cast is correct and needed.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.currentCost: One int->long widen + multiply + two stores per lazy application. Correct as-is.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.proposedChange: Keep the cast (it is required to avoid 32-bit overflow). No change to math. Optional: mark struct field ordering so HasLazy/Rev bytes pack (see layout opportunity) to keep Lazy/Sum on one line with Value for this read-modify-write.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.rationale: The arithmetic is already minimal; the only real lever here is struct packing addressed separately. Listing to confirm the (long) cast must stay.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.risk: Removing the (long) cast would overflow for Size*lazy beyond 2^31 — do NOT remove it.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.summary: Two separate bool fields (Rev, HasLazy) placed before the 8-byte-aligned pointers force 6+ bytes of padding; the struct is larger than necessary, hurting cache density of the node pool.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.currentCost: Layout (Sequential): int Priority(4), int Size(4), long Value(8), long Sum(8), long Lazy(8), bool Rev(1), bool HasLazy(1) -> 6 bytes pad to align Left -> Left(8), Right(8). Total 56B but with the two bools costing an aligned 8B slot. On a 64B line, fewer nodes per line than needed.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.proposedChange: Pack the two bools into a single byte flags field (bit0=Rev, bit1=HasLazy), or at minimum group both bools adjacent (already are) and move them to the very end after Right so the trailing pad is shared. Combining into one `byte Flags` removes one bool's footprint and lets Push test/set bits with masks.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.rationale: Smaller node -> more nodes per cache line -> fewer misses during the pointer-chasing Merge/Split. Bit flags also let Push check 'any lazy work pending' with a single nonzero test instead of two bool loads.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapImplicit.cs.risk: Changes field layout / public struct ABI. Bitwise flag access must preserve exact toggle semantics (Rev = !Rev becomes Flags ^= REV_BIT). Acceptable only if no external code reads .Rev/.HasLazy directly. Burst-blittable preserved.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.summary: Update calls Size(Left), Min(Left), Size(Right), Min(Right) separately, loading each child pointer twice and null-checking twice; the min fold is already branchy.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.currentCost: 4 child loads + 4 null compares, plus 3 compares for the nested-ternary min, every frame.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.proposedChange: Cache `TreapMinNode* l = n->Left, r = n->Right;`. Compute lmin = l==null?MaxVal:l->Min and rmin similarly from the cached pointer (reusing l->Size from the same line). Keep the existing nested-ternary min (it is already branchless-friendly for Burst's select), or write it as math.min-style chained selects.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.rationale: Removes duplicate pointer chasing and null branches; l->Size and l->Min share a cache line. Lower dependency-chain latency on the pointer load.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.risk: None. min semantics preserved (MaxVal sentinel for null children unchanged).

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.summary: QueryMin (read-only) performs two Splits and two Merges, mutating the whole tree spine (allocating lazy work, O(log n) writes) just to read a range min; a read query should not restructure the tree.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.currentCost: 2 splits + 2 merges = ~4*O(log n) node writes and Update recomputations per query, plus Push side-effects, for a pure read.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.proposedChange: Add a non-destructive range-min walk: descend with implicit-index bounds [lo,hi] accumulating Min over fully-covered subtrees (classic order-statistic range fold), applying pending lazy along the path without splitting. Same idea applies to QuerySum in Treap/TreapImplicit/TreapAffine.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.rationale: Converts a structural O(log n)-write operation into an O(log n)-read walk: no Merge/Update churn, far fewer writes, better cache behavior, and it is purer (query no longer mutates topology). Same asymptotic depth but a large constant-factor and write-traffic reduction for the common read-heavy workload.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeMin.cs.risk: Must still Push lazy along the descent path to read correct values, so it is not fully side-effect-free unless lazies are applied read-only. Behavior (returned min) identical. Larger change; verify against existing NUnit tests. Medium confidence.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeReverse.c.summary: Same redundant Size(Left)/Sum(Left), Size(Right)/Sum(Right) double-load-and-null-check pattern.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeReverse.c.currentCost: 4 child loads + 4 null compares per Update, every Split/Merge frame in Reverse.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeReverse.c.proposedChange: Cache child pointers once: `TreapRevNode* l = n->Left, r = n->Right;` then fused size+sum per child.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeReverse.c.rationale: Halves loads/branches and exploits Size/Sum cache-line locality.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeRotate.cs.summary: Double modulo k normalization can be reduced to a single integer division-remainder plus one branchless add for the negative case.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeRotate.cs.currentCost: Line 10 `k = ((k % len) + len) % len;` performs TWO integer remainder operations (idiv is ~20-40 cycles each on typical x86/ARM cores) on a non-power-of-two `len`. The second `%` exists only to map the value back into [0,len) after adding len.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeRotate.cs.proposedChange: Replace with one remainder then a conditional add: `k %= len; if (k < 0) k += len;`. Since after `k %= len` the value lies in (-len, len), a single `k += len` (guarded by k<0) already lands it in [0, len) — the outer `% len` is provably unnecessary. The branch can be made branchless: `k += len & (k >> 31);` (arithmetic shift produces 0 or -1 mask; only valid because k > -len so adding len once suffices, and len fits comfortably so no overflow).
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeRotate.cs.rationale: Eliminates one full integer-division/remainder instruction (the second `%`), the most expensive integer op on both PC and mobile, from every Rotate call. Halves the idiv latency on the normalization path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeRotate.cs.risk: Behavior-preserving for all int k and len>=1: after `k%=len`, k in (-len,len); the single `+len` mask maps negatives into [0,len) exactly as the double-mod did. The branchless `k>>31` form assumes 32-bit int and len small enough that k+len cannot overflow int (guaranteed since k<len<=array size). If len could be a power of two it is still correct (no special-casing needed).

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.summary: Push is a hot non-recursive leaf called inside both Split and Merge but lacks AggressiveInlining, unlike the sibling helpers.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.currentCost: Push (lines 43-49) is invoked on every Split node (line 57) and twice per Merge (lines 78-79). It is non-recursive (it only mutates the node and its two children) yet is a separate non-inlined call, adding call/return overhead and a register spill barrier inside the hottest tree-traversal loops. Apply, which it calls, IS inlined, but Push itself is not.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to Push (matching the attribute already on Size/Sum/Update/Apply/Merge). The early-out `if (n == null || n->LazyAdd == 0) return;` keeps the inlined body tiny in the common (no-lazy) case.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.rationale: Inlining a tiny, non-recursive leaf into Split/Merge removes call overhead, lets Burst/LLVM fold the n==null and LazyAdd==0 checks with surrounding code, and shortens the dependency chain in the dominant traversal path. The body is small (one branch + two Apply calls), so code-bloat risk is minimal.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.risk: None to semantics; Push is non-recursive so inlining cannot blow up like a recursive inline. The corresponding Push in TreapRangeReverse (also non-recursive, also un-inlined) is the same pattern and could get the same treatment for consistency.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.summary: Update recomputes Size and Sum via four null-checked helper calls that reload child pointers and re-test null redundantly.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.currentCost: Update (lines 30-31) calls Size(n->Left), Size(n->Right), Sum(n->Left), Sum(n->Right) — four calls, each loading the child pointer and branching on null, so n->Left and n->Right are tested for null twice and dereferenced up to twice. In Split/Merge, Update runs on every node touched on the path (O(log n) per op), so this redundancy is on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.proposedChange: Cache the children once and combine: `TreapSumNode* l = n->Left; TreapSumNode* r = n->Right; int ls = l==null?0:l->Size; int rs = r==null?0:r->Size; long lsum = l==null?0:l->Sum; long rsum = r==null?0:r->Sum; n->Size = 1+ls+rs; n->Sum = n->Value+lsum+rsum;` — or, since Size and Sum live in the same cache line as the node, load l->Size and l->Sum together under a single null test: `if(l!=null){ls=l->Size;lsum=l->Sum;}`.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.rationale: Reduces the per-node null branches from 4 to 2 and the child-pointer loads from 4 to 2, and loads Size+Sum of each child together (same struct, likely same cache line) so the second access is a guaranteed L1 hit. Shortens the dependency chain and removes two predictable-but-nonzero branches per Update on every path node.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.risk: Semantics identical; the inlined Size/Sum helpers already do the same null->0 mapping. Only caveat: ensure the manual null checks keep the exact `n==null` short-circuit — but Update already guards n==null at line 29, so l/r checks are the only ones needed. Burst will likely already do some of this; the win is guaranteeing it and tightening the cache behavior.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.summary: TreapSumNode is 8 bytes larger than necessary due to Priority/Size field ordering leaving the layout already tight, but Priority could share with Size packing is not the issue — the real note is cache-line footprint of the hot fields.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.currentCost: TreapSumNode is Priority(4)+Size(4)+Value(8)+Sum(8)+LazyAdd(8)+Left(8)+Right(8) = 48 bytes (Sequential, naturally aligned, no padding). Split/Merge/Push touch Size, Sum, LazyAdd, Left, Right — but Value is only needed by Update/Apply. The hot traversal fields (Size, Left, Right) span from offset 4 to 47, crossing into the second half of the struct.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.proposedChange: Reorder fields so the traversal-hot fields cluster at the front: Left, Right, Size, Priority, then Sum, LazyAdd, Value. This keeps Left/Right/Size (read on every Split/Merge step) within the first 16-20 bytes, improving the odds a single cache line prefetch covers the pointer-chase set. Keep [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] and explicit types.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.rationale: Pointer-chasing treaps are latency-bound on cache misses; clustering the fields read during traversal (Left, Right, Size) at the front of the struct maximizes useful bytes per fetched cache line and can reduce effective miss cost. Same total size (48B), zero RAM increase, pure layout win.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.risk: Layout reorder is observable only via interop/serialization that assumes field order; within this unmanaged-pointer library nothing depends on offsets, so behavior is preserved. Apply the identical reorder to TreapRevNode for consistency if desired. Low impact because the struct already fits well within typical 64B lines; benefit is marginal unless nodes straddle line boundaries.

src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.summary: AddRange and QuerySum recompute the window length r-l+1 and perform two splits then two merges; the merge nesting allocates no scratch but the call pattern can hoist the length and avoid a redundant Merge null path.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.currentCost: Both AddRange (line 97) and QuerySum (line 108) compute `r - l + 1` inline and call Split twice + Merge twice (`Merge(left, Merge(mid, right))`). The inner Merge(mid,right) then outer Merge(left,...) each re-run Push on a/b. No correctness issue, but `r-l+1` is recomputed and the merge order forces Push(mid) and Push(left) sequentially.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int len = r - l + 1;` into a named local and pass it to the second Split for clarity/consistency with Rotate. This is primarily ergonomics/consistency; the merge structure is already optimal (left-leaning rebuild). No functional change to the split/merge counts.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.rationale: Marginal: avoids one redundant add and matches the `len` naming convention used in Rotate, improving readability and giving the JIT/Burst a single SSA value. The dominant cost is the O(log n) Split/Merge tree work, which is already minimal.
src/IAFahim.DS.Treap/TreapRangeSum.cs.risk: None — pure local hoist, identical semantics. Listed as low because the arithmetic saving is negligible; include only if consistency with Rotate's `len` convention is desired.

src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.summary: Hoist the per-node base index `cur * 27` into a local instead of recomputing `cur * 27 + c` (and `cur * 27 + 26`) multiple times per iteration.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.currentCost: Each loop body computes `cur * 27 + c` at least once, and on the insert path computes `cur * 27 + c` twice (read at line 14, write at line 18). 27 is not a power of two, so each is a full imul + add. TrieDelete recomputes `p * 27 + c` 26 times in the child-scan plus `p * 27 + pc` again.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int base = cur * 27;` once at the top of each iteration and index `trie[base + c]`, `trie[base + 26]`. In TrieDelete's inner scan, hoist `int pbase = p * 27;` before the `for (c...)` loop so the multiply is done once per path node instead of once per child.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.rationale: Removes redundant imul instructions from the hot per-character loop and the 26-iteration child scan. The base address is a loop invariant within each node visit; computing it once shortens the dependency chain feeding every array access.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.risk: None. Pure CSE of an integer expression; identical results. `cur`/`p` are non-negative node ids so no overflow concern beyond what already exists.

src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.symbol: BinaryTrieInsert.Run / BinaryTrieErase.Run / BinaryTrieMaxXor.Run / BinaryTrieMinXor.Run / PersistentTrieInsert.Run / PersistentTrieQuery.Run
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.summary: Hoist `cur * 3 + 1` (the children base) into a local; currently `cur * 3 + 1 + b` / `+ 3` are recomputed and several loads are issued twice.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.currentCost: Stride-3 means `cur * 3` is a lea/imul recomputed per access. BinaryTrieMaxXor loads `trie[cur*3+1+want]` twice (test at line 159, use at line 162); MinXor loads `trie[cur*3+1+want]` twice (lines 183 and 185). BinaryTrieErase recomputes `path[i] * 3 + 1 + b` for both the read (line 142) and the conditional write (line 144), and re-derives the bit with `(val >> (bits-1-i)) & 1`.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.proposedChange: Per iteration compute `int childBase = cur * 3 + 1;`, then index `trie[childBase + b]`. In Max/MinXor, load `int chosen = trie[childBase + want];` once into a local and branch on `chosen != 0`, reusing `chosen` for the assignment to `cur`. In BinaryTrieErase, hoist `int pbase = path[i] * 3 + 1;` and load the child node id once.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.rationale: Eliminates a redundant memory load (the same trie slot read twice) and redundant address arithmetic in the bit-walk loops. Halving the load count on the chosen branch shortens the critical dependency chain that determines the next `cur`, which is the loop's latency bottleneck.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.risk: None for the address hoist. For the double-load elimination: the trie array is not aliased/modified between the two reads within these query methods, so caching the value is semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.summary: Convert the recursive subtree sum into an explicit stack-based (or pointer-stack) iterative DFS to make it Burst-friendly and avoid call-frame overhead.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.currentCost: Recursion across up to N nodes incurs a call/return per visited node, with the trie row spilled to the stack frame; Burst does not inline/optimize recursion well and recursive functions defeat its vectorization and can blow the stack on deep/wide tries. Each call also recomputes `cur * 27`.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.proposedChange: Replace recursion with an explicit `int* stack = stackalloc int[STACK_CAP];` worklist DFS: push `cur`, while stack non-empty pop `n`, add `trie[n*27+26]` to sum, and push each non-zero child `trie[n*27+c]`. Hoist `int base = n*27;` per pop. Document STACK_CAP as a named constant sized to max trie node count, consistent with the stackalloc[256]/[64] pattern already used in this file.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.rationale: Removes per-node call/return overhead, turns the traversal into a tight loop Burst can compile cleanly, and bounds stack usage to an explicit named cap rather than implicit recursion depth. Same total work, far lower constant factor and no recursion hazard.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.risk: Must size STACK_CAP for the worst-case live frontier (a worklist can hold more than tree depth). Caller-provided trie node count bounds it; if unbounded, this is a behavioral constraint to document. Output sum is identical.

src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.summary: Reuse the already-stored child index instead of rescanning all 26 child slots to test 'has any child', and reuse the bit/char already known.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.currentCost: The cleanup loop scans up to 26 slots per path node (`for c in 0..26`) to detect any remaining child. After deleting one child this is an O(26) scan per level; across a full backtrack it is O(26 * pathLen).
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.proposedChange: Track, alongside `path[i]`, the child slot index that was descended into (store `c` per level in a parallel `int* pathC = stackalloc int[256];`). When pruning, you still must confirm no OTHER child exists, so the 26-scan cannot be fully removed — but you can early-skip the slot just zeroed and avoid re-deriving `pc = s[i]-'a'` (already known as pathC[i]). Hoist `int pbase = p*27;` (see first item) so the scan indexes `trie[pbase+c]`.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.rationale: Removes the redundant `s[i]-'a'` recomputation and the redundant multiply per scanned slot; storing the descended slot avoids recomputing it. The 26-scan itself is required for correctness (need to know if a sibling subtree survives), so only constant-factor cleanup is available here.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.risk: Low. Must keep the existing semantics: prune only when the node has zero children. Storing pathC adds 1KB of stackalloc (256 ints) — acceptable given path[] is already 256 ints; ensure total stackalloc stays within budget.

src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.summary: Document/exploit that the alphabet stride is 27 (not 32); a 26-wide alphabet padded to 32 (power-of-two stride) would turn `cur * 27` into `cur << 5` and `+ 26` slot handling, trading 5 wasted ints/node for branchless shift indexing.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.currentCost: Stride 27 forces an integer multiply on every node access across all trie operations. The count slot lives at index 26.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.proposedChange: If memory budget allows, change the node stride to 32 (children 0..25, count at slot 26 or 31) so `cur * 32` strength-reduces to `cur << 5`. This converts every `cur * 27` in the file into a shift. Gate behind a named constant `NODE_STRIDE` so the choice is explicit and the +26/+31 count index is consistent across all five classes.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.rationale: Replaces a multiply with a single shift on the hottest address computation in every trie operation. Cache cost: 32 vs 27 ints per node is +18% node size, which may increase cache misses on large tries — hence this is a tradeoff, not a free win.
src/IAFahim.DS.Trie/Trie.cs.risk: Changes the on-array layout, so the trie buffer size and `++trie[0]` node-allocation accounting must be updated coherently across ALL classes (Insert/Delete/Find/PrefixCount) and any caller. Behavior is preserved only if every accessor uses the same stride. Marked low impact because the multiply may already be folded into a lea on the target ISA and the extra RAM can hurt mobile cache.

src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.summary: Unconditional MemClear forces an O(length) zeroing write pass on every allocation, even when the caller immediately overwrites the whole buffer.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.currentCost: UnsafeUtility.MemClear(Ptr, byteCount) touches every byte of the allocation (length * sizeof(T) stores), evicting useful cache lines and adding a full memory-write pass that callers who fully initialize the array (e.g. copy-from, fill, compute-into) pay for nothing.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.proposedChange: Add an overload / parameter mirroring Unity's convention: `UnsafeArray(int length, Allocator allocator, NativeArrayOptions options)` and only call MemClear when `options == NativeArrayOptions.ClearMemory`. Keep the existing 2-arg ctor delegating with ClearMemory for source compatibility, or add an explicit `bool clear` named-constant-driven path. Hot callers then pass UninitializedMemory and skip the pass.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.rationale: Eliminates an entire length-proportional store pass and its cache pollution for the common 'allocate then fully write' pattern; this is the standard NativeArray/UnsafeList design for exactly this reason. Pure constant-factor on small arrays but asymptotically the dominant cost when the caller's own init is also O(length).
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.risk: Semantics change ONLY for callers that rely on zero-initialization; the default path must remain clearing to preserve observable behavior. Document that UninitializedMemory yields garbage contents. No Burst/blittability impact (NativeArrayOptions is a plain enum).

src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.summary: `this = default;` zeroes the whole struct and is then immediately followed by writing all three fields, doubling writes to Length/Allocator/Ptr.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.currentCost: `this = default` issues a struct-wide zero store (Ptr=0, Length=0, Allocator=0) and the next three lines overwrite the same slots, so each field is written twice. The struct is tiny (8+4+4 bytes) so the win is small but the zeroing is redundant.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.proposedChange: Drop `this = default;` and assign every field directly: `Length = length; Allocator = allocator; Ptr = (T*)AllocatorManager.Allocate(...);`. All instance fields are definitely assigned, so the struct ctor is fully initialized without the default-zero step.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.rationale: Removes one redundant struct-wide store; each field is written exactly once. Fewer instructions on the allocation hot path.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.risk: None for behavior: every field is unconditionally assigned afterward, so removing the default-zero is observably identical. Only required because C# struct ctors must definitely-assign all fields — direct assignment already satisfies that.

src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.summary: `this = default;` in Dispose does a struct-wide zero store even when Ptr was already null.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.currentCost: On every Dispose, `this = default` writes the full struct. For a struct passed by value/copied this is dead work, and it forces nulling Length/Allocator that callers cannot observe after disposal.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.proposedChange: Set only `Ptr = null;` after Free (so a double-Dispose is still safe via the null check) instead of `this = default;`. Length/Allocator do not need clearing for correctness.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.rationale: Single pointer store instead of a full-struct zero; keeps the idempotent double-free guard (Ptr null check) intact with strictly less work.
src/IAFahim.DS.UnsafeArray/UnsafeArray.c.risk: Behavior differs only if external code reads Length/Allocator after Dispose and expects 0 — disposed-object field reads are already undefined by convention, so this is semantics-preserving for valid usage. Keep `Ptr = null` to preserve the existing double-Dispose safety.

src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.summary: Fuse the bitmap-write pass and the rank prefix-sum pass into a single loop per level.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.currentCost: Per level the algorithm walks the n elements twice: once in ComputeBitmapsAndCountOnes (read data, shift, write bitmaps[i], count ones) and once in FinalizeLevel (read bitmaps[i-1], accumulate into ranks[i]). The second pass reloads bitmaps values that were just written, doubling memory traffic over the n*log inner work and incurring store-to-load forwarding/cache pressure on the bitmaps array.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.proposedChange: Compute the prefix sum inline while writing bitmaps: keep a running 'acc' initialized to 0, set ranks[offset+i]=acc before/while writing bit=(data[i]>>b)&1, then acc+=bit. After the loop ranks[offset+n]=acc and mids[b]=acc (the final running total IS the ones count). This eliminates the separate FinalizeLevel pass and the separate 'ones' counter entirely.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.rationale: Halves the per-level passes over n (one streaming pass instead of two), removes the redundant bitmaps re-read, and folds the ones-count and prefix-sum into the same accumulator so the loop becomes a single fused streaming kernel that Burst can vectorize/scalar-pipeline more tightly. Asymptotically still O(n*log) but ~2x fewer memory-bound iterations.
