src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.risk: Must preserve the exact ranks definition: ranks[offset+i] = prefix sum of bits over [0,i) (i.e. ranks[offset]=0, ranks[offset+n]=ones). Writing ranks[i] from the running acc before adding the current bit reproduces this exactly. mids[b]=ones still holds since acc==ones at loop end. bitmaps[offset+n]=0 sentinel must still be written. No signed/overflow concern: bit is 0/1, acc<=n.

src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.summary: The bitmaps array is dead after build for Kth queries — it can be dropped, or stored as packed bits, to shrink the working set by ~4x or eliminate it.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.currentCost: bitmaps is allocated as int[log*(n+1)] storing only 0/1 values (4 bytes each, 31 bits wasted per element). WaveletMatrixKth.Run never reads bitmaps — it uses only rankPtr and mids. So bitmaps is build-only scratch that nonetheless persists in the caller-provided buffer, inflating RAM and cache footprint on mobile.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.proposedChange: Two options: (a) If callers only need Kth, treat bitmaps purely as transient and compute ranks/mids directly (per the fusion above), so the persistent structure is just ranks[log*(n+1)] + mids[log]. (b) If a bit array is genuinely needed for rank/select queries, store it as packed uint64 words (n/64 words per level) and derive rank via blockRank + popcount, cutting bitmaps storage ~64x and making rank cache-friendly.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.rationale: Smaller working set means fewer cache lines touched during build and queries — directly fewer cache misses on memory-bound traversal. Option (a) removes an entire log*(n+1)*4-byte buffer; option (b) is the standard succinct-bitvector layout the empty SuccinctWavelet stubs imply is intended.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.risk: Behavior-preserving for Kth (it ignores bitmaps). If any future/external API exposes bitmaps as output, dropping it changes the contract — verify no caller reads bitmaps. Packed-bit option requires rewriting rank as word-popcount and must keep the n+1 prefix semantics; popcount path must stay branchless/Burst-friendly.

src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.summary: Restructure the per-bit branch to a branchless select and hoist rankPtr[ri+1]/rankPtr[li] reads (each currently loaded up to twice).
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.currentCost: Inside the log-iteration loop: GetCountInLevel reads rankPtr[ri+1] and rankPtr[li]; then on the taken branch UpdateIndicesZero re-reads the same rankPtr[li] and rankPtr[ri+1], or UpdateIndicesOne re-reads them. That is up to 4 dependent loads where 2 suffice. The if/else is also data-dependent on query values, so it is poorly predictable and serializes the dependency chain across the (typically ~20-30) levels.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.proposedChange: Load r0=rankPtr[li] and r1=rankPtr[ri+1] once per iteration. leftCount=r1-r0. Compute both candidate (li,ri) pairs from r0,r1,mids[b] and select with a branchless mask: int take=(k>=leftCount); k-=take*leftCount; val|=take<<b; li = take? mid+(li-r0) : r0; ri = take? mid+(ri-r1+1)-1 : r1-1; using arithmetic-mask selection (e.g. (-take) masks) to stay branchless.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.rationale: Cuts redundant rank loads roughly in half on the hot per-level path and removes a hard-to-predict branch from a long serial dependency chain, shortening the critical path per level and helping Burst emit conditional-move/predicated code instead of branches. Constant-factor but applied across log iterations per query.
src/IAFahim.DS.WaveletMatrix/WaveletMatr.risk: Must reproduce exact index updates: zero-branch li=r0, ri=r1-1; one-branch li=mid+(li-r0), ri=mid+(ri-r1+1)-1; val|=1<<b only when taken; k-=leftCount only when taken. Branchless masking must use correct signed arithmetic (take is 0/1; -take is 0 or -1 for AND-masks). Verify no overflow in mid+(...) — same range as current code, so safe.

src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameTheory.cs.summary: Replace the linear bit-scan loop for mex with a hardware trailing-zero-count of the complemented mask.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameTheory.cs.currentCost: A data-dependent loop `while ((seenMask & (1 << mex)) != 0 && mex < 31) mex++` executes one branch + one shift + one AND per set low bit, with a serial dependency chain (mex feeds the next shift). For a dense mask this is up to 31 iterations of mispredictable branches in the hot BFS loop (called once per node).
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameTheory.cs.proposedChange: Compute mex branchlessly: `int mex = math.tzcnt(~seenMask);` (Unity.Mathematics) or `System.Numerics.BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(~seenMask)`. The complement turns the lowest unset bit of seenMask into the lowest set bit, so tzcnt yields mex directly in 1-3 cycles. Because seenMask is a 32-bit int, ~seenMask always has at least the sign/high bits set when low 31 are full, so tzcnt returns 31 when bits 0..30 are all set — matching the original `mex < 31` cap exactly (original stops at mex==31; tzcnt(~mask) returns at most 31 here as well only if bit31 is the first zero — see risk).
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameTheory.cs.rationale: tzcnt is a single low-latency instruction and removes the per-bit branch and the serial shift dependency, collapsing an O(mex) loop into O(1). Burst lowers math.tzcnt to the native TZCNT/RBIT+CLZ instruction on x86/ARM.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameTheory.cs.risk: Edge case at the 31 cap: original returns at most 31 (it stops incrementing once mex==31 regardless of bit 31). tzcnt(~seenMask) returns the index of the first zero bit, which could be 31 only if bits 0..30 are all 1; if bit 31 is also 1 then ~seenMask==0 and tzcnt returns 32, diverging from the original's 31. Guard: clamp with `math.min(math.tzcnt(~seenMask), 31)` to preserve the original ceiling. Grundy values that large are non-physical for valid DAGs, but the clamp keeps observable behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameDp.Run.summary: Replace the inner mex linear scan with trailing-zero-count of the complemented 64-bit mask.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameDp.Run.currentCost: `int g = 0; while ((seen & (1L << g)) != 0) g++;` is a serial, data-dependent loop run once per i (n times), up to 64 iterations each with a branch and 64-bit shift. This dominates the per-cell cost for dense reachability sets.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameDp.Run.proposedChange: Use `int g = math.tzcnt(~(ulong)seen);` (or `BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount((ulong)(~seen))`). This returns the smallest g with bit g unset, i.e. the mex, in one instruction.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameDp.Run.rationale: Collapses an O(mex) per-cell loop into O(1) branchless tzcnt; removes mispredicted branches and the serial shift chain in the hot DP loop. Burst vectorizes/lowers tzcnt natively.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GameDp.Run.risk: If all 64 bits of seen are set, ~seen==0 and tzcnt(0)==64; the original loop would shift `1L << 64` which is undefined/UB (shift count masked to 0 in C#), so the original is already broken for the all-bits-set case. The proposed version returns 64 deterministically, which is strictly more correct; for all valid inputs (mex < 64) behavior is identical. Cast to ulong to avoid sign-extension of the complement.

src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.summary: Zero the `seen` scratch with a bulk memset instead of an element-by-element loop.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.currentCost: `int* seen = stackalloc int[n]; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) seen[i] = 0;` is an n-iteration scalar store loop. stackalloc memory is not auto-zeroed here, so the clear is needed, but a scalar loop is slower than a vectorized clear.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.proposedChange: Use `Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(seen, 0, (uint)(n * sizeof(int)));` or `UnsafeUtility.MemClear(seen, (long)n * sizeof(int))`. Both lower to a vectorized/rep-stos memset under Burst.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.rationale: A single bulk memset issues wide SIMD/rep stores (16-32 bytes/iter) versus 4 bytes/iter scalar, roughly 4-8x fewer store uops and better cache streaming for large n. Also removes the loop branch overhead.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.risk: None for correctness — clears the same bytes. Ensure the byte count uses the element size (sizeof(int)=4). InitBlockUnaligned is Burst-friendly and unmanaged-safe.

src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.summary: Hoist the decrement/compare and mark UpdateNeighbor / FindMex AggressiveInlining as hot leaf methods.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.currentCost: UpdateNeighbor and FindMex are private leaf calls inside the BFS hot loop. Without inlining hints the JIT/Burst may keep call overhead (arg marshalling of 6 pointers/refs for UpdateNeighbor).
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to `FindMex`, `UpdateNeighbor`, and `InitializeQueue`. These are tiny, single-use leaves; inlining removes the call/ret and lets Burst keep `rear`/`seen` in registers across the loop body.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.rationale: Eliminates call overhead and enables register allocation across the fused loop body; the `ref int rear` becomes a register update rather than a memory round-trip through a callee.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/GrundyDAG.Run.risk: None semantically. Inlining a method taking `ref` is always safe; only code-size grows slightly, negligible for single call sites.

src/IAFahim.GameTheory/Minimax.Run.summary: Branchless update of best/alpha (and best/beta) to shorten the dependency chain in the move loop.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/Minimax.Run.currentCost: `if (val > best) best = val; if (best > alpha) alpha = best;` are two dependent conditional branches per move. In alpha-beta these branches are data-dependent and often mispredict, stalling the search.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/Minimax.Run.proposedChange: Use branchless max/min: `best = math.max(best, val); alpha = math.max(alpha, best);` in Maximize and `best = math.min(best, val); beta = math.min(beta, best);` in Minimize. Keep the `if (beta <= alpha) break;` cutoff branch (it must remain a branch for early exit).
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/Minimax.Run.rationale: math.max/min on long lower to a compare+cmov (or SSE/NEON min/max), removing two mispredictable branches per iteration and shortening the latency of the best/alpha update chain that gates the cutoff test.
src/IAFahim.GameTheory/Minimax.Run.risk: Semantics identical: max/min reproduce the exact assignments. Only the cutoff `beta <= alpha` stays branchy (required for correctness of pruning). No overflow concern — values are bounded game evaluations, and long.MinValue/MaxValue seeds compare correctly with cmov.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Replace (ni+1)%n / (nj+1)%n with branch-free wrap to avoid a 64-bit integer division per caliper step.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: Two `% n` operations per call inside the Run while-loop; n is arbitrary so Burst emits a full idiv (20-90 cycles each on the hot path), executed O(n) times.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Compute next index with conditional increment: `int nni = ni + 1; if (nni == n) nni = 0;` (same for nnj). Indices are always in [0,n) and advance by exactly 1, so modulo is never needed.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: idiv is one of the most expensive integer ops; replacing it with a compare+cmov/branch removes a long-latency instruction from the inner caliper loop. Burst can turn the if into a branchless select.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: None. ni,nj are seeded from FindExtremePoints in [0,n) and only ever incremented by these statements, so they stay in [0,n); +1 can reach at most n, handled by the == n reset.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Eliminate the three `% n` operations in the per-iteration calipers loop (ni, j advance, nj inside IsFurther) with conditional wraps.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: `ni = (i+1)%n` once per outer iter, `j = (j+1)%n` per inner advance, and `nj = (j+1)%n` recomputed on every IsFurther call — all 64-bit idiv on arbitrary n.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: ni: `int ni = i + 1; if (ni == n) ni = 0;`. j advance: `int jn = j + 1; if (jn == n) jn = 0; j = jn;`. In IsFurther pass nj in or compute `nj = j + 1; if (nj == n) nj = 0;`. All values stay in [0,n).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Removes idiv from both the outer loop and the inner while, the hottest part of the rotating-calipers scan, replacing each with a compare and conditional move.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: None: every index is monotonically incremented by 1 from a value in [0,n), so the ==n reset is exactly equivalent to %n.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Avoid recomputing nj's wrap and redundant subtractions by hoisting; merge IsFurther's edge-vector computation with the loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: IsFurther recomputes `(j+1)%n` and four subtractions every inner-loop probe; called repeatedly while advancing j.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Track j's successor index incrementally alongside j in Run (advance both together), and pass the precomputed edge deltas, so IsFurther only does the cross product. Mark IsFurther AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Shortens the dependency chain in the inner while and removes redundant modulo+subtract recomputation across consecutive probes.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: None functionally; just reindexing. Keep cross-product sign test identical (>0).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Replace the two edge-delta precompute loops' `(k+1)%n` with a wrap-on-equal, and drop the resX/resY scratch buffers by writing directly to rx/ry.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: `(k+1)%n1` and `(k+1)%n2` are idiv per edge in the two setup loops. Additionally resX/resY are stackalloc'd then copied to rx/ry in a final O(m) loop — 2*(n1+n2) longs of redundant stack and a full copy pass.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: For deltas use `int kn = k+1; if (kn==n1) kn=0;`. Write resX[m]/resY[m] directly into rx[m]/ry[m] throughout, removing resX/resY stackalloc and the final copy loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Removes idiv from setup, eliminates 2*(n1+n2)*8 bytes of stack, and removes an entire O(m) copy pass plus its cache traffic. Output is written exactly once.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: Caller supplies rx/ry sized >= n1+n2 (already required since m can reach n1+n2). Writing in-place is safe because rx/ry are distinct output buffers, not aliased with inputs. Edge wrap is exact since k ranges [0,n).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Solve builds the y-strip array yt but never compares strip points, so it returns only the min of the two halves and is both O(n) wasted work and arguably incorrect; the strip merge is missing.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: The loop `for(i=l;i<r;i++) if((x[i]-mx)^2<d) yt[k++]=y[i];` fills yt but no pairwise distance over the strip is computed; result d is just min(left,right). Per node this is O(n) pure overhead with zero effect on the answer.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Either (a) if the intent is a correct divide-and-conquer closest pair, sort/scan yt and check up to ~7 neighbors to fold strip distances into d; or (b) if behavior must be preserved as-is, delete the dead yt loop and the yt buffer entirely to reclaim n longs of stack and an O(n log n) pass.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: As written the strip loop is dead computation; removing it is a strict win. If correctness is desired, the standard 7-neighbor strip scan restores true O(n log n) closest-pair with the same asymptotics but a correct result.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: Option (b) preserves current observable output exactly while removing work. Option (a) CHANGES output (fixes a likely bug) — only apply if the current result is known-wrong by design intent; flag for maintainer decision.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Insertion sort is O(n^2); for the closest-pair driver this dominates and defeats the divide-and-conquer's O(n log n) intent.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: O(n^2) comparisons/moves to sort by x before Solve; on large n this is the bottleneck and a long dependency chain of shifts.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Replace with an in-place O(n log n) sort over the parallel (sx,sy) arrays (e.g. heapsort or an iterative bottom-up mergesort using the existing yt buffer as scratch). Keep raw-pointer, no managed types.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Drops the dominant cost from quadratic to n log n, matching the algorithm's intended complexity; especially important on mobile where large-n quadratic passes blow the cycle budget.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: Must keep sx and sy permuted together identically. Heapsort avoids extra allocation; mergesort can reuse yt scratch. No semantic change to the sorted order (ascending x).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Hoist repeated `*r * *r` and the squared-distance-to-center recomputation; cache center coords in locals to avoid repeated pointer loads/stores.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: Inner loops reload *cx,*cy,*r through pointers every iteration and recompute `*r * *r` and `(*cx-x[i])^2+(*cy-y[i])^2` multiple times; pointer aliasing forces Burst to re-load on each access.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Read cx,cy,r into local longs at each level, compute `long r2 = r;` once per loop (r already stores squared radius here) and compare `dx*dx+dy*dy > r2`; write back to *cx,*cy,*r only when they change. Recompute the radius expression into a local instead of inline twice.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Removes redundant loads/stores through potentially-aliased pointers (rx/ry/cx/cy may not be marked restrict), shortens dependency chains, and avoids recomputing the same multiply. Burst keeps locals in registers.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: cx,cy,r point to caller storage possibly distinct from x,y; caching in locals and writing back at change-points preserves semantics. Note *r already holds squared radius (set to 0 or to squared dist), so `*r * *r` in the comparisons squares an already-squared value — verify this matches intended semantics before changing; keep the exact same expression to preserve behavior.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Potential overflow/semantics caveat: comparisons use `*r * *r` where *r is already a squared distance, so the test is dist^2 > (r2)^2 = r^4-scale, which both magnifies overflow risk and is dimensionally inconsistent.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: `*r * *r` with *r ~ coordinate^2 produces coordinate^4 magnitudes, risking long overflow for moderately large coords and comparing dx^2 (coordinate^2) against r^4 (inconsistent units).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: If intended radius-squared semantics: store r as squared distance and compare `dx*dx+dy*dy > r` (single square), not `> *r * *r`. Confirm with tests; this is a correctness/units fix, not a pure micro-opt.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Correct dimensional comparison both removes a multiply and dramatically lowers overflow magnitude (coordinate^2 vs coordinate^4).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: CHANGES observable behavior; only apply if current `*r * *r` is a bug. Flag for maintainer — do not apply blindly since 'Run' may be assumed correct by design.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Fuse the two O(n) polygon passes into one and replace `(i+1)%n` with a conditional wrap.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: Two separate loops over the polygon each compute `j=(i+1)%n` (idiv per vertex); the boundary loop and the shoelace area loop iterate the same edges separately, doubling vertex/coordinate loads and cache traffic.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Single loop: `int j = i+1; if (j==n) j=0;` then accumulate both `boundary += Gcd(|dx|,|dy|)` and `area += x[i]*y[j] - x[j]*y[i]` together. Removes idiv and halves coordinate loads.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: One pass instead of two halves memory traffic over x[],y[]; conditional wrap removes idiv. The two accumulations are independent and order-invariant, so fusing is safe.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: None. Both sums are commutative/associative over the same edge set; j wrap is exact for i in [0,n). dx,dy for Gcd use Math.Abs as before.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Euclidean Gcd uses `%` (idiv) per step; for the common axis-aligned/short edges a binary GCD avoids division, and an early-out when one operand is 0 avoids the loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: Each Gcd call does repeated `a % b` (idiv) until b==0; called once per polygon edge.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Add fast path: `if (a==0) return b; if (b==0) return a;` (axis-aligned edges where dx or dy is 0 return immediately). Optionally a binary-GCD (subtract/shift) variant to avoid idiv entirely, since dx,dy>=0 here.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Axis-aligned polygon edges are extremely common and hit the zero fast-path with no division; binary GCD trades idiv for shifts/subtracts which are cheaper and Burst-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: Inputs are non-negative (Math.Abs applied at call site), so unsigned/binary-GCD reasoning is valid. Result identical to Euclidean GCD; gcd(0,x)=x preserved.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.summary: Hoist the three repeated coordinate-difference subexpressions (by-cy, cy-ay, ay-by) reused in both the determinant and ox; reuse to cut redundant subtracts.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.currentCost: `(by-cy)`, `(cy-ay)`, `(ay-by)` are each computed twice (once in d, once in ox numerator); similarly cx-bx etc. for oy. Extra subtracts and longer dependency chain before the two divides.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.proposedChange: Compute `long bcy=by-cy, cay=cy-ay, aby=ay-by, cbx=cx-bx, acx=ax-cx, bax=bx-ax;` once and reuse in d, ox, oy numerators.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.rationale: Removes ~3 redundant 64-bit subtractions and shortens the critical path feeding the two divisions (which can't start until numerators are ready).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Advanced/GeometryAd.risk: None; pure CSE, identical arithmetic and integer-division results.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Replace O((r-l)^2) selection sort with O(r-l) average quickselect (nth_element) to find the median along the axis.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: Partition runs a full selection sort of the [l,r] subrange: an outer loop over every position with an inner scan, i.e. Theta((r-l)^2) comparisons and swaps, even though only the median index (l+r)>>1 and the partition invariant are needed. Called once per KD-tree node, so BuildKdTree is Theta(n^2) overall instead of Theta(n log n).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: Implement a quickselect/nth_element on the (l,r) range targeting k=(l+r)>>1, comparing pts[idx*2] when axis==0 else pts[idx*2+1], swapping both coordinate longs together. Stop once the k-th element is in place; return k. BuildKdTree already only consumes tree[node]=m and the two halves, which after nth_element still satisfy left<=pivot<=right along the axis.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Quickselect partitions in O(range) expected work per node, giving the standard O(n log n) KD-tree build versus the current O(n^2). For large point sets this is the dominant asymptotic win; it also reduces total swaps and memory traffic over the points array.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: nth_element does not fully sort each half, but the KD-tree query only relies on the axis-split invariant (everything in the left subtree has axis-coordinate <= pivot), which quickselect preserves, so the resulting tree answers nearest-neighbor identically. Worst-case quickselect is O(n^2) on adversarial/duplicate input; use median-of-three or a deterministic pivot if adversarial input is a concern. Coordinate pair must be swapped atomically (both *2 and *2+1) exactly as the current swap does to keep points consistent.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Cache points[idx*2]/points[idx*2+1] (and the next/cand coords) into locals to kill repeated pointer loads and duplicated distance subexpressions.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: dist computes (points[idx*2]-px) twice and (points[idx*2+1]-py) twice from memory; the next-branch and cand-branch each recompute their squared distance with two repeated loads + repeated subtractions. Each recursion level re-dereferences the same array slots multiple times, lengthening the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: Introduce long ix=points[idx*2], iy=points[idx*2+1]; compute long dx=ix-px, dy=iy-py; dist=dx*dx+dy*dy. Do the same for the next and cand indices (load each coord once, subtract once, square once). Optionally factor a static AggressiveInlining helper SqrDist(long ax,long ay,long px,long py) to reuse for idx/next/cand.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Removes redundant loads and arithmetic on the hot recursive path, shortening the critical dependency chain and reducing total integer ops per node. Burst/JIT may already CSE some of this, but the array-index form through a pointer is not always provably aliasing-free, so explicit locals guarantee the elimination.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: Pure refactor of identical arithmetic; results bit-identical. No overflow change since the same long multiplications are performed.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Hoist the axis-dependent child selection and avoid recomputing node*2 / node*2+1 expressions.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: node*2 and node*2+1 are computed in the child selection, then again (conditionally) for the second-subtree recursion via (axis==0?node*2+1:node*2). The axis==0 branch is evaluated twice (for val and for the second child).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: Compute int lo=node*2, hi=node*2+1 once. Select child/other with the px<val test and axis already known: e.g. int child = px<val?lo:hi; the pruning recursion uses the sibling of child directly (the opposite of the first choice) rather than recomputing axis==0?hi:lo.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Eliminates one redundant shift/add and one redundant axis comparison per node; trims the dependency chain on a hot recursive traversal.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: Must preserve exact child-selection semantics: first descent goes to the px<val side; the pruning pass must visit the OTHER side. Confirm the sibling-of-child equals the original (axis==0?node*2+1:node*2) for all axis/px<val combinations before substituting, otherwise nearest-neighbor results change.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Replace two per-point integer divisions with reciprocal-free index math and hoist invariant subexpressions; or document the signed-divide assumption.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: The per-point loop does two signed int divisions ((ys[i]-minY)/cellH and (xs[i]-minX)/cellW) plus a multiply by gridSize and an array RMW, per point. Integer division is ~20-40 cycles on many mobile cores and is the bottleneck of this loop. cellW/cellH/gridSize are loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: If callers guarantee xs[i]>=minX and ys[i]>=minY (true by construction since minX/minY are the array minima), the differences are non-negative, so the divisions are unsigned-equivalent and could use a precomputed multiply-shift reciprocal (magic-number division) for cellW/cellH, or at minimum hoist gridSize into a local. Keep cellW/cellH in registers. For the common case where gridSize is a power of two, the maxX-minX division can also be turned into a shift, but cellW itself is data-dependent so the per-point divide generally remains.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Fixed divisors known before the loop can be strength-reduced to multiply+shift, removing the long-latency divide from the hot per-point path; hoisting gridSize avoids reloading it. This is the single most expensive operation in the build loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: Magic-number division is only valid because the dividends are provably non-negative here (minX/minY are the minima from FindMinMax), so signed vs unsigned semantics coincide; if that invariant could ever be violated (e.g. callers pass external minX), the reciprocal trick must use the signed form. cellH/cellW are >=1 so no divide-by-zero. Net behavior must equal the original integer division for all valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Compute the sx1<sx2 comparison once and select lo/hi branchlessly instead of evaluating the ternary twice.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: loX and hiX each re-evaluate the predicate sx1[i]<sx2[i]; that is two loads of sx1[i] and sx2[i] plus two comparisons per iteration where one suffices.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: int a=sx1[i], b=sx2[i]; int lt=a<b?1:0 (or branchless: int loX = b ^ ((a^b) & -(a<b?1:0)) style min/max). Compute loX/hiX from the single comparison. Reuse the loaded a,b.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Halves the comparisons and the redundant loads in the per-segment loop; branchless min/max also removes a mispredictable branch, which Burst vectorizes more readily.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: Behavior identical for all int inputs; branchless min/max on signed ints is overflow-safe here since no subtraction-based form is required (use ternary-select or Math.Min/Max). Keep ty1/ty2 assignment order exactly as-is.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Insertion sort of the index array is O(n^2); reuse the library's existing O(n log n) index/key sort if n can be large.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: SortByX is insertion sort over order[] keyed by xs[order[]], Theta(n^2) worst/average for random input, with each comparison doing an extra indirection xs[order[j]].
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: For large n, replace with an O(n log n) sort (the repo already has QuickSort/Selection partition primitives) sorting indices by key. For tiny n keep insertion sort (good cache/branch behavior); a size threshold gives the best of both.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Removes quadratic blowup on large vertex sets; the extra double-indirection per comparison makes the quadratic constant factor worse than a plain sort, so the asymptotic improvement compounds.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: Must remain a stable-or-equivalent ordering only if downstream relies on stability; the current insertion sort is stable, so if outX/outY ordering of equal-x points is observable, choose a stable O(n log n) or document that ties may reorder. If n is always small by design, this opportunity is not worth taking.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Hoist x1[i]/y1[i]/x2[i]/y2[i] out of the inner j-loop to avoid reloading them every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: The inner loop reloads x1[i], x2[i], y1[i], y2[i] from memory for every j although they are invariant across the inner loop; Math.Max/Min are called against these repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: Before the inner for-j loop, load int xi1=x1[i], yi1=y1[i], xi2=x2[i], yi2=y2[i] into locals and use those in the Max/Min calls.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Removes four pointer loads per inner iteration (O(n^2) loads -> O(n)), shrinking memory traffic in the hot double loop and freeing the comparator inputs to stay in registers.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: Pure hoist of provably loop-invariant reads; identical results. No aliasing concern since the loop only reads these arrays.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.summary: Restructure the min/max scan into branchless updates / separable x and y passes to improve Burst auto-vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.currentCost: The single fused loop has four data-dependent branches per element (if x<minX, x>maxX, y<minY, y>maxY) interleaving xs and ys access; conditional-update branches inhibit SIMD min/max reduction.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.proposedChange: Use branchless min/max (minX = xs[i]<minX?xs[i]:minX etc., which Burst lowers to vector min) keeping the fused pass, or split into two contiguous passes over xs and ys so each is a clean min/max reduction Burst can vectorize with packed min/max.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.rationale: Branchless min/max maps to single SIMD/scalar min-max instructions and is unconditional, so Burst can vectorize the reduction; the current branch form is data-dependent and unpredictable, costing mispredictions on random data.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Arrangement/Arrange.risk: Min/max selection semantics are identical to the comparisons used; ties resolve the same way. Splitting into two passes doubles loop overhead but each pass is contiguous-stride friendly; keep fused+branchless if a single pass is preferred. No overflow concern (no subtraction).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.summary: Eliminate the duplicate Math.Cos(lat2) transcendental call via common-subexpression elimination.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.currentCost: Math.Cos(lat2) is evaluated twice (line 12 in y, line 13 in x). The method also re-derives Math.Sin(lat1), Math.Cos(lat1), Math.Sin(lat2), Math.Cos(dLon) — currently 6 distinct trig evaluations but cos(lat2) is computed twice for a total of 7 trig calls.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.proposedChange: Hoist into locals: double sinDLon = Math.Sin(dLon); double cosDLon = Math.Cos(dLon); double sinLat1 = Math.Sin(lat1); double cosLat1 = Math.Cos(lat1); double sinLat2 = Math.Sin(lat2); double cosLat2 = Math.Cos(lat2); then y = sinDLon * cosLat2; x = cosLat1 * sinLat2 - sinLat1 * cosLat2 * cosDLon. This removes the second cos(lat2) evaluation (7 trig -> 6).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.rationale: Math.Cos is a libm transcendental costing tens to ~100+ cycles. The JIT/Burst cannot CSE it because it is not provably side-effect-free/pure to the optimizer, so the duplicate call is emitted as-is. Manual CSE guarantees a single evaluation, saving one full cos per call in a hot leaf.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.risk: None. Math.Cos is deterministic for a given input, so reusing the value is bit-identical to recomputing it. Pure refactor, identical IEEE result.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.summary: Same branchless normalization and TwoPi constant as CartesianAzimuth.Run.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.currentCost: Duplicate if (angle < 0.0) angle += 2.0 * Math.PI pattern: a data-dependent branch plus a runtime 2.0 * Math.PI literal multiply after Atan2.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.proposedChange: Introduce a shared private const double TwoPi = 2.0 * Math.PI (or a small internal helper static method NormalizeTwoPi(double) tagged AggressiveInlining shared by both azimuth files) and use a ternary select for the add. Centralizing also improves ergonomics/consistency between the two azimuth implementations.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.rationale: Removes a mispredictable branch and a redundant runtime multiply; a shared inlined normalizer keeps the two Run methods consistent without cost.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalAz.risk: Same as CartesianAzimuth: select is value-identical to the branch for all inputs. -0.0 handling matches. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/CartesianAz.summary: Make the [-pi,pi] -> [0,2pi) normalization branchless to remove a data-dependent branch on the Atan2 result.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/CartesianAz.currentCost: if (angle < 0.0) angle += 2.0 * Math.PI is a branch whose direction depends on the runtime Atan2 output, so it can mispredict (~50% taken depending on input distribution) and creates a control dependency right after a long-latency Atan2.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/CartesianAz.proposedChange: Compute branchlessly: long bits = BitConverter.DoubleToInt64Bits(angle); double mask = (double)((bits >> 63)); but cleaner under Burst: double add = angle < 0.0 ? (2.0 * Math.PI) : 0.0; angle += add; — the ternary lowers to a conditional-move (no branch). Also hoist 2.0 * Math.PI into a const TwoPi field to avoid the literal multiply.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/CartesianAz.rationale: A cmov/select removes a mispredictable branch and the dependent control flow, keeping the pipeline straight after Atan2. Precomputing TwoPi as a named constant removes a runtime multiply.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/CartesianAz.risk: Behavior-identical: ternary select yields the same value as the if for all inputs including angle == -0.0 (-0.0 < 0.0 is false, matching the current branch). Whether the JIT actually emits cmov is not guaranteed; if it keeps a branch the change is neutral, never worse.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalDi.summary: Replace 2*atan2(sqrt(a), sqrt(1-a)) with 2*asin(sqrt(a)) to drop one sqrt and convert atan2 to asin.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalDi.currentCost: Line 16 computes Math.Sqrt(a), Math.Sqrt(1.0 - a), and Math.Atan2 — two sqrt plus one atan2 (atan2 is among the most expensive libm routines).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalDi.proposedChange: double c = 2.0 * Math.Asin(Math.Sqrt(a)); This removes the second sqrt(1-a) and replaces atan2 (2-arg) with asin (1-arg), which is typically cheaper.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalDi.rationale: For the haversine, 2*asin(sqrt(a)) is mathematically identical to 2*atan2(sqrt(a), sqrt(1-a)) since a in [0,1]. Saves one sqrt and trades atan2 for the generally cheaper asin, shortening the dependency chain after the sqrt.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Azimuth/SphericalDi.risk: Precision tradeoff: the atan2 form is the numerically robust standard precisely because asin(sqrt(a)) loses precision as a -> 1 (near-antipodal points). For non-antipodal use this is fine and faster, but if the library intends full antipodal accuracy this changes observable output in the last ULPs near a==1. ONLY adopt if antipodal-precision is not a requirement; otherwise reject. Also clamp a to [0,1] is unnecessary here since a is already in range by construction (unchecked Run assumes valid input).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.summary: Replace per-iteration `(i + 1) % n` integer modulo with the rotating-index idiom used in PolygonContains.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.currentCost: One 64/32-bit integer division (idiv, ~20-40 cycle latency, not pipelined) per vertex per call, because `n` is a runtime value (not a power of two), so the JIT/Burst cannot strength-reduce the modulo. For an n-gon that is n divisions in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.proposedChange: Restructure as `for (int i = 0, j = n - 1; i < n; j = i++) { area += x[j]*y[i] - x[i]*y[j]; }` (shoelace with previous index j), or hoist `int j = 0; for i: j = i+1; if (j==n) j=0;`. This removes the div entirely, replacing it with a copy/compare-branch that predicts perfectly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.rationale: idiv is one of the most expensive integer ops; eliminating one per loop iteration converts an O(n) chain of long-latency divisions into O(n) cheap adds/multiplies. The j=i++ trailing-index form is already proven in PolygonContains in this same file, so it is idiomatic here.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.risk: Must preserve sign of the accumulated cross sum. The shoelace sum's sign is taken as abs at the end (`if (area<0) area=-area`), so re-ordering i/j swaps the sign of every term uniformly and the final abs makes it identical. Only valid because the result is the absolute area; verify the term reorder keeps the same magnitude (it does: sum over edges is rotation-invariant).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.summary: Eliminate the per-iteration `(i + 1) % n` modulo with a wrap-on-compare next index.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.currentCost: One integer division per vertex to compute `j = (i + 1) % n`, in addition to the real centroid math. Same non-power-of-two idiv penalty as PolygonArea.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.proposedChange: Use `int j = 1; for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { ...use x[i],x[j]...; j++; if (j == n) j = 0; }` so the wrap is a predictable compare+conditional-move/branch instead of a division. Reads x[i],y[i],x[j],y[j] into locals once to also cut redundant pointer loads.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.rationale: Replaces a long-latency idiv per iteration with a single increment and a well-predicted branch (taken exactly once per call). For polygons with many vertices this is a measurable constant-factor reduction in the centroid hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.risk: Semantics-preserving: the only use of j is to index the next vertex with wraparound at n, which the increment-and-reset reproduces exactly. The final `cx*3/area` division and the area!=0 guard are unchanged. Caller must still pass n>=1 (already assumed by the unchecked Run contract).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.summary: Hoist the shared subexpression in the crossing test to cut one multiply per crossing edge.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.currentCost: Per edge that straddles py, computes `rhs = xi*dy + (xj - xi)*(py - yi)` then `px*dy`. The two multiplies plus the add form the per-edge work; `dy = yj - yi` and the comparison `(yi>py)!=(yj>py)` are recomputed each edge.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.proposedChange: Keep current structure but factor `px*dy < xi*dy + (xj-xi)*(py-yi)` into `(px - xi)*dy < (xj - xi)*(py - yi)`, which is algebraically identical and uses two multiplies instead of three (drops the separate `xi*dy` term).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.rationale: Reduces the multiply count in the inner test from three (px*dy, xi*dy, (xj-xi)*(py-yi)) to two ((px-xi)*dy and (xj-xi)*(py-yi)), shortening the dependency chain on the hot crossing path with no change in the comparison's truth value.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.risk: Sign-of-inequality preservation: moving xi*dy to the left as (px-xi)*dy keeps the same inequality direction only when dy is unchanged sign-wise on both sides, which it is (dy multiplies both sides identically here, but note we are NOT dividing — we subtract xi*dy from both sides, so the inequality direction is fully preserved regardless of dy's sign). Use 64-bit longs as now; (px-xi) and (py-yi) stay within long range given inputs already used in long multiplies.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.summary: Ccw.Run is a byte-for-byte duplicate of Orientation.Run; collapse one into a forwarding call to remove duplicate code/icache footprint.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.currentCost: Two separate identical method bodies (Ccw and Orientation) each emit the same cross-product + sign logic, duplicating code size and instruction-cache footprint; SegmentIntersect/OnSegment call Orientation, leaving Ccw a redundant copy.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.proposedChange: Make `Ccw.Run` body `return Orientation.Run(ax, ay, bx, by, cx, cy);` (still AggressiveInlining, so zero call overhead after inlining), keeping the public API intact while having a single source of truth.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.rationale: With AggressiveInlining the forwarding call inlines to the identical machine code, so runtime cost is unchanged while source duplication and standalone code size shrink. Purely a maintainability/footprint win with no perf regression.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.risk: None to observable behavior: identical inputs map to identical outputs. Only consideration is that Ccw must keep the same signature/return convention (-1/0/1), which forwarding preserves exactly.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.summary: Return branchless sign of the cross product instead of two compares-and-branches.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.currentCost: Two conditional branches (`if cross>0`, `if cross<0`) to produce -1/0/1. On the hot path inside SegmentIntersect (4 calls) and OnSegment, mispredictable branches on data-dependent sign.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.proposedChange: Compute sign branchlessly: `return (int)((cross > 0 ? 1 : 0) - (cross < 0 ? 1 : 0));` which Burst/JIT typically lowers to setcc/conditional-moves, or use `(int)(((ulong)(-cross) >> 63)) ... ` style sign extraction. Concretely `int s = (cross >> 63) | (int)((-(ulong)cross) >> 63 ... )` — simplest portable form is `return (cross > 0 ? 1 : 0) - (cross < 0 ? 1 : 0);`.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.rationale: Eliminates two data-dependent conditional branches in a leaf function called up to 4x per SegmentIntersect and inside polygon-adjacent geometry, replacing them with branchless setcc/cmov which avoids branch-misprediction stalls when orientation sign is unpredictable.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Basic/GeometryBasic.risk: Must produce exactly -1/0/1 for negative/zero/positive cross including the case cross == long.MinValue (where -cross overflows): the `(cross>0)-(cross<0)` form avoids any negation and is overflow-safe, so prefer that form over any `-cross` bit-trick. No overflow in cross itself is a pre-existing caller assumption (unchecked Run).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.summary: Replace unguarded recursive QuickSort (O(n^2) worst case + O(n) recursion depth) with median-of-three pivot and tail-recursion-on-smaller-half, or an introsort/heapsort fallback.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.currentCost: Partition always picks items[right] as pivot. BVH centroids fed to BuildNode are frequently already partially sorted along an axis from the parent's sort, which is the pathological input for last-element-pivot quicksort: O(n^2) comparisons and O(n) recursion depth. With stackalloc'd items and deep meshes this can blow the native stack and degrades the whole Build from O(n log n) to O(n^2).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.proposedChange: In Partition, choose pivot via median-of-three (items[left], items[mid], items[right]) and swap it to items[right] before the scan. In QuickSort, after partitioning recurse only into the smaller subrange and loop (while) on the larger one (tail-call elimination), guaranteeing O(log n) stack depth. Optionally cap depth at 2*log2(n) and fall back to heapsort for true introsort worst-case bounds.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.rationale: Median-of-three removes the sorted-input pathology that is specifically common here (sibling ranges inherit parent ordering). Tail-recursion-on-smaller-half bounds recursion depth to O(log n) regardless of pivots, preventing native stack overflow. Restores guaranteed O(n log n) build.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.risk: Sort is not stable, but the current sort isn't either, and BVH split ordering only needs a consistent total order on the chosen axis, so observable build output (tree shape) may differ only when centroids tie on the split axis — equivalent valid BVH. If strict bit-identical tree output must be preserved, keep the same comparison and only add median-of-three + tail-loop (these still change tie-break ordering); to preserve exactly, restrict to the tail-recursion-on-smaller-half change alone, which keeps identical partition results and only reduces stack depth.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant axis branch out of the inner comparison loop; index the float3 component once instead of branching per element.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.currentCost: The inner loop runs `if(axis==0)... else if(axis==1)... else...` on every iteration (n-1 times per partition, across O(n log n) total compares). axis is invariant for the whole call, so this is a fully predictable-but-still-decoded branch chain plus a load of all three lanes' selection each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.proposedChange: Split Partition into three specialized inner loops selected once by axis (or read the lane via pointer: `float pivotC = ((float*)&pivotValue.Centroid)[axis];` and `float c = ((float*)&items[j].Centroid)[axis];` computed with axis hoisted). Simplest: `switch(axis)` once around three otherwise-identical scan loops so the compare is `items[j].Centroid.x < pivotX` with no per-iteration branch.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.rationale: Removes a 2-3 way branch and redundant lane selection from the innermost hot loop of the build. Three monomorphic loops let Burst keep the pivot component in a register and potentially vectorize the scan. Strictly fewer instructions per comparison.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.risk: None — pure refactor, identical comparison semantics. Pointer-indexing into float3 by lane assumes float3 is 3 contiguous floats with no padding before/between lanes (true for Unity.Mathematics float3, StructLayout Sequential), otherwise use the switch-of-three-loops form which has zero layout assumptions.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.summary: Recursion + per-node full AABB rescan does redundant work; precompute triangle AABBs once and combine, and hoist triIdx*3.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.currentCost: Each BuildNode rescans every triangle in its range (3 vertex fetches + min/max each) to compute the box. A triangle in a leaf at depth d has its vertices loaded ~d times across the d ancestor nodes, so total bbox work is O(n log n) vertex fetches with repeated `indices[triIdx*3+j]` index math and gather loads (cache-unfriendly indirect addressing through indices then vertices).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.proposedChange: In Build, while computing centroids, also compute and store each triangle's min/max AABB (extend CentroidSortItem or a parallel stackalloc float3 pair). Then BuildNode combines child boxes bottom-up: compute leaf boxes directly, and for internal nodes set node->Min/Max = min/max of Left and Right child boxes after the recursive calls, eliminating the per-node O(range) rescan entirely (build bbox cost drops from O(n log n) to O(n)). At minimum, hoist `int base3 = triIdx*3;` so the j-loop uses base3+0/1/2.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.rationale: Combining child boxes makes per-node box O(1) instead of O(range), removing the dominant repeated indirect gather loads (the main cache-miss source in build). Hoisting base3 removes a multiply per inner iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.risk: Bottom-up combination is mathematically identical (union of child boxes == union of all contained triangles) given the leaf boxes are the triangle boxes — produces bit-identical Min/Max. Extra stackalloc for per-triangle boxes raises peak stack by ~24 bytes/triangle; if triangleCount can be large this risks stack overflow and should instead reuse the caller-provided buffers or document a size cap. The hoist-only variant has zero risk.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.summary: Use math.cmax/cmin for the longest-axis selection instead of chained scalar branches.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.currentCost: `axis` selection uses two dependent branches and `math.max(size.x,size.y)`; `maxDim` then recomputes `math.max(size.x, math.max(size.y, size.z))`. The max of size is computed twice and axis uses branches.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.proposedChange: Compute `float maxDim = math.cmax(size);` once (single horizontal max). Keep axis via branches if exact tie-break must match, or derive axis = select using comparisons against maxDim. Reuse maxDim for both the Epsilon test and avoid recomputing the y/z max.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.rationale: cmax is a single reduction Burst lowers to a couple of shuffles+maxps; removes the duplicated max computation and shortens the dependency chain before the Epsilon branch.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.risk: axis tie-break semantics must be preserved exactly (current code: y beats x on strict >, z beats max(x,y) on strict >). cmax only replaces maxDim; if you also rederive axis from maxDim the tie-break can differ (e.g. when two axes equal the max). Keep the existing 2-branch axis selection and only replace maxDim with cmax to stay bit-identical.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.summary: Recursive traversal lacks closest-child-first ordering and best-distance AABB culling; add tEnter-based child ordering and pass bestDist into the AABB test.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.currentCost: RaycastNode always descends Left then Right and tests AABB intersection only for hit/miss, ignoring the current bestDist. It will fully traverse a subtree whose nearest entry tEnter is already beyond a triangle hit found in the other subtree, doing wasted AABB and triangle tests. Native recursion also adds call overhead per node.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.proposedChange: Have RayAABBIntersection return tEnter (out param). Descend into the child with smaller tEnter first, and skip a child whose tEnter >= *bestDist. Convert recursion to an explicit stackalloc'd node-index stack to remove call overhead and enable the early-out before pushing. This is standard front-to-back BVH traversal.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.rationale: Closest-first + tEnter<bestDist pruning is the core BVH speedup: it cuts visited nodes from O(n) toward O(log n) for typical closest-hit queries by abandoning subtrees that cannot contain a nearer hit. Returning tEnter reuses the slab computation already done.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.risk: Must preserve closest-hit semantics: only prune when tEnter strictly exceeds the current bestDist (use >= since a hit exactly at tEnter cannot be nearer than an existing equal/closer hit — but to be safe against ties use > to avoid dropping equal-distance triangles if exact tie behavior matters). Reordering child visitation changes which of two exactly-equidistant triangles wins (currently Left-first); if a deterministic tie-winner is part of observable behavior, keep a tie-break that prefers Left on equal t. NaN handling in the AABB test must still reject.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.summary: Replace per-lane scalar invDir branching with vectorized reciprocal + select; drop the redundant NaN checks given the comparison already rejects NaN.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.currentCost: invDir is built with three independent scalar ternary chains (math.abs + compare + select per lane), defeating SIMD. Then two math.isnan calls guard a comparison that, for IEEE, already returns false when tEnter/tExit is NaN (NaN<=x and x>=0 are both false).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.proposedChange: Compute invDir = 1f/direction as a vector, then `invDir = math.select(invDir, math.select(-1e6f, 1e6f, direction>=Zero), math.abs(direction) <= Epsilon);` using float3 selects (branchless, SIMD). Drop the two isnan branches and rely on `tEnter <= tExit & tExit >= Zero` returning false on NaN. Use & instead of && to make it branchless.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.rationale: Vectorized reciprocal + select keeps the slab test fully in SIMD with no scalar lane extraction, and removes two branches plus two isnan ops from the hottest leaf in raycast (called per node visited). Fewer instructions, better Burst vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.risk: IEEE semantics: if direction has a true 0 lane, 1f/0f = +/-Inf rather than the +/-1e6f the current code substitutes; the slab math with Inf still yields correct enter/exit for axis-aligned-miss rays, BUT 0*Inf=NaN can occur when (boxMin-origin) is exactly 0 on a zero-direction axis, and the current 1e6f hack avoids that. To preserve exact behavior keep the 1e6f substitution (do it via select, not raw reciprocal) — then the isnan checks become provably dead and can be removed safely. Only remove isnan if the substitution guarantees finite invDir; otherwise keep one combined isnan guard.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.summary: Hoist triIdx*3 index base and gather the three vertices via one base pointer to cut repeated multiplies and index loads.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.currentCost: Computes `indices[triIdx*3]`, `indices[triIdx*3+1]`, `indices[triIdx*3+2]` with the multiply repeated three times in source (likely CSE'd by Burst but not guaranteed across the array index expressions).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.proposedChange: `int* tri = indices + triIdx*3; float3 v0=vertices[tri[0]]; float3 v1=vertices[tri[1]]; float3 v2=vertices[tri[2]];` Make this consistent with the same pattern in Build/BuildNode.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.rationale: Single multiply + pointer adds; removes ambiguity for the optimizer and shortens the address-computation dependency chain in the per-triangle hot path. Also improves readability/consistency.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Bvh/BvhTree.cs.risk: None — identical addresses computed; pure strength-reduction/readability. Assumes indices is a valid contiguous int array (already required by the unchecked Run contract).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.summary: Use Horner's method to evaluate the cubic, cutting vector multiplies and shortening the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.currentCost: Computes tt = t*t and ttt = tt*t, then p = Half*(a + b*t + c*tt + d*ttt). That is 3 vector scalar-multiplies on b,c,d plus 3 vector adds plus the final Half scale, and a long serial chain (ttt depends on tt depends on t).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.proposedChange: Evaluate as p = Half * (a + t*(b + t*(c + t*d))). This is 3 fused multiply-adds (math.mad / mad pattern Burst lowers to FMA) plus the Half scale, and avoids materializing tt and ttt entirely.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.rationale: Horner form removes the precomputation of tt and ttt (2 scalar muls) and replaces 3 independent scalar*vector + 3 adds with 3 mads. On Burst this maps to vectorized FMA on float3, fewer instructions and a balanced/shorter critical path, lowering latency per evaluation. Evaluate is the hottest leaf (called per LUT sample and per output sample).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.risk: Floating-point result changes in the last ULP because mad/FMA rounds once vs separate mul+add, and reassociation reorders rounding. If bit-exact parity with the current expression is required by tests, this is observable; otherwise mathematically equivalent. Reject if exact-bit reproducibility is a contract.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.summary: Provide a combined position+tangent entry point so the shared coefficients b, c, d are computed once.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.currentCost: Callers that need both a point and its tangent at the same t call Evaluate then EvaluateTangent, each independently recomputing b = p2-p0, c = 2p0-5p1+4p2-p3, and d = p3-p0+3(p1-p2) (roughly a dozen vector ops duplicated).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.proposedChange: Add a static method EvaluateWithTangent(p0,p1,p2,p3,t, out float3 pos, out float3 tangent) that computes a,b,c,d once and produces both pos = Half*(a + t*(b + t*(c+t*d))) and tangent = Half*(b + t*(2c + 3t*d)). Keep the two existing methods for callers needing only one.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.rationale: Eliminates duplicate computation of b, c, d (the bulk of the work) when both outputs are needed, halving coefficient setup. This mirrors how CubicBezier.UniformSample evaluates position and tangent at the same t.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.risk: Pure additive API; no behavior change to existing methods. The out form must reproduce the same arithmetic ordering to stay bit-identical, or accept last-ULP differences from any Horner refactor. Low risk.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.summary: Remove unused usings and unused named constants to reduce surface and avoid confusion.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.currentCost: using System; is imported but unused. Constants Zero (0f), and arguably the full set, exist; in Evaluate/EvaluateTangent only Half, Two, Three, Four, Five are referenced. Zero and One appear unused.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.proposedChange: Drop using System; and any const not referenced (Zero, One if unreferenced). Verify each const has a use before removing.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.rationale: No runtime cost (consts are compile-time), but trimming dead declarations keeps the file lean and prevents accidental misuse. Pure hygiene.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CatmullRom.cs.risk: None functionally. Only confirm the consts are truly unreferenced before deletion.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.summary: Replace the Bernstein-basis evaluation with the Horner/expanded power-basis form to cut multiplies and shorten the chain in the hottest leaf.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.currentCost: Computes u, uu, uuu, tt, ttt (5 scalar muls) then p = uuu*p0 + 3*uu*t*p1 + 3*u*tt*p2 + ttt*p3: that is many scalar muls to form the 4 Bernstein weights plus 4 scalar*vector products and 3 vector adds. Called SampleCount(128) times in IntegrateArcLength and again per output sample in UniformSample, so it dominates both.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.proposedChange: Precompute power-basis coefficients once is not possible per-call without p inputs, but per call use Horner on the expanded cubic: c0=p0; c1=3*(p1-p0); c2=3*(p0-2*p1+p2); c3=-p0+3*p1-3*p2+p3; then p = c0 + t*(c1 + t*(c2 + t*c3)) (3 vector mads). Alternatively, if many points are sampled for the SAME control points (IntegrateArcLength/UniformSample), hoist c0..c3 out of the loop and pass them to an inner evaluator so they are computed once instead of per sample.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.rationale: Hoisting c0..c3 out of the 128-iteration loops turns ~12 vector coefficient ops per sample into 3 mads per sample, computing the coefficients once per curve instead of 128+count times. This is a large constant-factor win on the dominant inner loop, with better FMA vectorization under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.risk: Last-ULP differences from reassociation/FMA versus the current Bernstein expression; reject only if bit-exact parity is contractually required. The two power-basis evaluations are mathematically identical to the Bernstein form for all t.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.summary: IntegrateArcLength duplicates UniformSample's LUT-building loop; the total length is exactly lut[SampleCount]. Share one inner routine.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.currentCost: IntegrateArcLength runs a 128-iteration loop summing math.distance, and UniformSample runs the identical loop to build lut. The arc length is precisely lut[SampleCount] that UniformSample already computes, so callers wanting both length and samples pay for the loop twice.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.proposedChange: Factor a private BuildArcLengthLut(p0..p3, float* lut) that fills lut[0..SampleCount] and returns lut[SampleCount]. Have IntegrateArcLength call it into a stackalloc (or a length-only variant that skips storing), and UniformSample call it directly, then reuse the returned total instead of re-reading. Removes the duplicated distance-accumulation logic.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.rationale: Eliminates a redundant 128-iteration sqrt-heavy loop (math.distance does a sqrt each step) when both arc length and uniform samples are needed; also centralizes the sampling so the Horner/hoisting win above is applied in one place.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.risk: If IntegrateArcLength must avoid the extra SampleCount+1 floats of stack, keep a length-only overload that accumulates without storing. Behavior identical. Low risk.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.summary: Precompute the shared difference vectors and use the power-basis derivative to reduce multiplies, and hoist for the per-curve sampling loops.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.currentCost: tangent = 3*uu*(p1-p0) + 6*u*t*(p2-p1) + 3*tt*(p3-p2) computes u, uu, tt and three scalar*vector terms each call; called once per output sample in UniformSample.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.proposedChange: The derivative of the Horner cubic p = c0 + t(c1 + t(c2 + t c3)) is c1 + t*(2*c2 + 3*t*c3). Reuse the same hoisted c1,c2,c3 from Evaluate so tangent needs only 2 mads plus the 2c2/3c3 scaling (which can also be hoisted as d1=c1, d2=2*c2, d3=3*c3 once per curve). Provide an evaluator that takes the hoisted coefficients.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.rationale: Sharing c1..c3 between position and tangent and precomputing the derivative coefficients d2=2c2, d3=3c3 once per curve removes per-sample reconstruction of the basis, leaving 2 mads per tangent. Cuts work in UniformSample's per-sample tangent path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.risk: Last-ULP differences from the algebraically-equivalent power-basis form; reject if bit-exact parity required. Otherwise identical for all t.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.summary: Replace per-target binary search over the LUT with a single linear merge pass, since target distances are monotonically increasing.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.currentCost: UniformSample calls FindT once per output sample; each FindT does an O(log SampleCount) binary search restarting from [0,SampleCount]. Total O(count * log 128).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.proposedChange: Since targetDist = i*targetStep is strictly increasing in i, maintain a running cursor index into lut that only advances forward across the whole output loop (a two-pointer merge). Each lut entry is visited at most once overall, giving O(count + SampleCount) instead of O(count log SampleCount), with branch-predictable forward scans Burst handles well.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.rationale: Monotone queries against a sorted prefix-sum array are the classic case where a forward merge beats repeated binary search: it removes the log factor and the binary search's data-dependent, hard-to-predict branches, replacing them with a sequential, prefetch-friendly scan.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.risk: Must preserve the same low/high bracket and interpolation factor that the current binary search selects (low is the largest index with lut[low] < targetDist, clamped within [0,SampleCount]); replicate the segmentLength>0 guard and edge handling exactly so output t values are identical. Moderate care to match boundary semantics, but no float change when brackets match.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.summary: Remove unused using System and unused constants; consider Run/Try naming consistency for UniformSample.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.currentCost: using System; is unused. UniformSample silently returns on count<=0 (a Try-style contract) while sibling Run methods assume valid input; the convention is mixed.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.proposedChange: Drop using System;. Optionally rename UniformSample to follow the library's Run/Try* convention (e.g. an unchecked RunUniformSample assuming count>=1, plus the guard living in a Try wrapper) to match house API style.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.rationale: Hygiene and discoverability; aligns with the documented Run/Try* convention without changing the perf model. No runtime cost.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Curve/CubicBezier.c.risk: Renaming is a public-API change; only do it if it matches the established convention and callers are updated. The using removal is risk-free.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.summary: v1 == positions[i+1]-positions[i] is identical to diff already computed in the tangents pass; c1 = dot(v1,v1) is the squared length recomputed from scratch every iteration. Precompute and reuse.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.currentCost: Each loop iteration recomputes v1 = pNext - pI (3 subs) and c1 = dot(v1,v1) (3 mul + 2 add). The first tangent pass already computed diff = positions[i+1]-positions[i] and len = length(diff) (which includes a sqrt of exactly this quantity). c1 here equals len*len.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.proposedChange: Store the per-segment squared length (lenSq) in a small stackalloc float* segLenSq[count-1] during the first pass (segLenSq[i] = math.lengthsq(diff)), or reuse the already-known diff. In the main loop set v1 = pNext - pI only if needed, and c1 = segLenSq[i]. Better: since v1 is used as a reflection plane vector and c1 is its squared length, both come directly from the tangent pass.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.rationale: Removes 3 subtractions and a 5-op dot product per iteration (O(count) saved), plus eliminates a redundant data dependency chain on positions loads. The squared length was effectively already computed (len = sqrt(lengthsq)) in the tangent pass.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.risk: lenSq must be the exact same float bit pattern as dot(v1,v1) to preserve the c1 > Threshold branch outcome. math.lengthsq(diff) == math.dot(diff,diff) == dot(v1,v1) since v1==diff, so bit-identical. Costs (count-1)*4 bytes extra stackalloc; acceptable, or fold into reusing diff directly. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.summary: (Two / c1) and (Two / c2) are scalar divides on the hot path; combine each with its dot product into a single reciprocal-scaled scalar to cut the dependency chain and hoist the constant.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.currentCost: Per iteration up to two divisions: (Two / c1) and (Two / c2). Division is ~20-40 cycle latency on mobile ARM and is on the critical dependency path. Each reflection also forms (Two/c)*dot(...)*v as three separate scalar/vector mults.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.proposedChange: Compute float s1 = (math.dot(v1,nI) + math.dot(v1,tI)) ... no — keep separate dots but fold: float inv1 = Two / c1; uI = nI - (inv1*math.dot(v1,nI))*v1; tIL = tI - (inv1*math.dot(v1,tI))*v1; (inv1 computed once, already partially done). The real win: compute the scalar coefficient k = inv1*dot first (scalar), then k*v1 (one vector mul), reducing to 1 div + 2 scalar muls + 2 vector muls per reflection instead of recomputing Two/c1 implicitly twice.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.rationale: Hoisting inv1 = Two/c1 to a single named scalar shares one divide across the two reflections of plane v1 (currently the source reads (Two / c1) twice on lines 85-86, which the compiler may or may not CSE under fast-math off). Explicit hoist guarantees one divide and shortens the chain.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.risk: Burst with default (non-fast) float math may treat (Two/c1) as a strict op; manual CSE is safe and bit-identical since both expressions are textually equal. Reordering dot/scale must keep the same rounding: k=inv1*dot then k*v1 vs inv1*dot*v1 is the same left-to-right association already used; preserve order to stay bit-exact.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.summary: nI is read from outUp[i] (memory) each iteration, but nNext written to outUp[i+1] in the previous iteration is exactly that value — carry it in a register instead of round-tripping through the output pointer.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.currentCost: Each iteration does float3 nI = outUp[i]; a 12-byte load from the caller's outUp buffer that was just stored the previous iteration (store-to-load forwarding, but still a memory dependency and pointer arithmetic per iter).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.proposedChange: Maintain a loop-carried local float3 nPrev initialized to n0 before the loop; use nPrev in place of outUp[i]; at the end set nPrev = nNext. This removes the dependent load from outUp[i] and the indexed address computation.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.rationale: Eliminates a 12-byte load and address calc per iteration and breaks the artificial dependency on the just-written output, helping Burst keep the normal in registers across iterations and aiding vectorization/scheduling.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.risk: None semantically: nPrev holds exactly what outUp[i] would; outUp is still written. Pure register reuse. Only caveat: if caller aliases outUp with positions/tangents (it must not for correctness anyway), behavior is unchanged because we still write outUp[i+1] identically.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.summary: tangents stackalloc float3[count] (12*count bytes) can overflow the stack for large count and is the only scratch buffer; the per-iteration tangent could be derived on the fly, or the buffer narrowed/guarded.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.currentCost: stackalloc float3[count] = 12*count bytes on the stack. For count in the thousands (e.g. dense curves) this risks stack overflow on mobile (typical 512KB-1MB thread stacks: ~40k-80k points). The buffer stores normalized tangents that are mostly consumed sequentially (tI and tNext for adjacent i).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.proposedChange: Either (a) document/guard a max count, or (b) restructure to keep only tCur and tNext as loop-carried locals: compute tNext from positions[i+1]-positions[i+2] inside the loop, removing the O(count) scratch buffer entirely and dropping RAM to O(1). The last-segment duplication (tangents[count-1]=tangents[count-2]) becomes a simple branch on the final iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.rationale: Drops working set from O(count)*12 bytes to O(1), eliminating the stack-overflow failure mode and improving cache behavior (no scratch buffer traffic). tangents are only ever used as tI (current) and tNext (next), so two registers suffice.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.risk: Must preserve exact tangent values including the len>Threshold fallback to (0,0,1) and the final-segment duplication. Recomputing tNext each iter adds one normalize per iter but removes count normalizes from the prepass and all buffer load/store traffic — net neutral on math, strictly better on RAM. Order of operations must stay identical for bit-exact tangents.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.summary: The orthonormalization fallback logic (pick alternate axis when tangent/normal nearly parallel, then cross + normalize) is duplicated between the count==1 path and the count>1 prelude with subtly different structure; unify into one inlined helper to reduce code size and divergence risk.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.currentCost: Lines 21-36 (count==1) and 47-67 (prelude) implement near-identical Gram-Schmidt-with-fallback against different reference vectors. Duplicated branch-heavy code inflates instruction footprint (I-cache pressure on mobile) and risks the two paths drifting.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.proposedChange: Extract a private static [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] BuildFrame(float3 tangent, float3 normalHint, out float3 right, out float3 up) that does the parallel check + fallback axis selection + cross/normalize, and call it from both sites. Keeps Burst-friendliness (by-value float3, out params, no managed types).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.rationale: Single source of truth for the orthonormal-frame construction, smaller code, easier to keep bit-identical. AggressiveInlining preserves the current inlined cost.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.risk: count==1 uses fwd=(0,0,1) as the seed tangent and a different fallback ordering ((0,1,0) then keep) than the prelude (alt=(0,1,0) then (0,0,1)). The helper must reproduce each call site's exact branch sequence and normalize order to remain bit-exact; if the two cannot be reconciled without changing rounding, keep separate. Low impact, refactor-only.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.summary: bNext = normalize(cross(tNext, nNext)) normalizes a cross product whose operands are already unit and (after the reflections) nearly orthogonal; the normalize may be droppable or cheaper, and the dependency chain shortened.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.currentCost: Per iteration: normalize(cross(tNext,nNext)) = cross (6 mul, 3 sub) + length (dot+sqrt) + reciprocal + 3 muls. The sqrt+div is the longest-latency op in the loop body.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.proposedChange: After nNext=normalize(nNext), tNext is unit and nNext is unit. If they are guaranteed orthogonal, cross is already unit and normalize is redundant. They are NOT exactly orthogonal here (nNext came from reflections, not re-orthogonalized against tNext), so instead Gram-Schmidt nNext against tNext first (nNext -= dot(tNext,nNext)*tNext; normalize) which both improves frame orthogonality AND lets bNext = cross(tNext,nNext) skip its normalize. Net: replaces one sqrt-normalize with one dot+mul+sub, often a latency win.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.rationale: Trades a sqrt-bearing normalize for a cheaper Gram-Schmidt step while also producing a more orthonormal frame. Removes one sqrt from the critical path per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Frame/ParallelTrans.risk: This CHANGES output bits (re-orthogonalizing nNext against tNext alters nNext and bNext slightly). It improves orthonormality but is NOT bit-preserving, so it must be gated as an opt-in/behavioral improvement, not applied silently. Only adopt if the library treats frame orthonormality tolerance as the contract rather than exact bits. Flagged low because of the semantics caveat.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.summary: Replace O(n^2) selection-style sort with O(n log n) sort (e.g. iterative/median-of-three quicksort already used elsewhere in the repo).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.currentCost: Double nested loop over all m+4 planes: ~ (count^2)/2 angle comparisons and up to count^2/2 full HalfPlane (40-byte) struct swaps. For m=1000 inputs that is ~500k comparisons and potentially hundreds of thousands of struct copies on the hot path of Run.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.proposedChange: Sort by Angle using a pointer-based quicksort (the repo already has QuickSort patterns in BvhTree.cs and PowerfulNumbers.cs). Sort an index array or swap whole HalfPlane structs in O(n log n). Optionally precompute keys (Angle) into a separate double* to compare scalars and minimize struct touching.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.rationale: Asymptotic improvement from O(n^2) to O(n log n) comparisons. For n in the hundreds-to-thousands this is the dominant cost of Run; selection sort here is strictly worse and Burst cannot rescue an O(n^2) algorithm.
