src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.risk: Quicksort is not stable; UniquePlanes already disambiguates equal-Angle planes by keeping the smaller D, so a stable order is not required, but verify tie-handling: if two planes share an Angle, UniquePlanes keeps the one with smaller D regardless of their relative sorted order, so correctness is preserved under any consistent ordering.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.summary: The four bounding-box sentinel angles are computed with Math.Atan2 on constant arguments at runtime instead of named compile-time constants.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.currentCost: Four Math.Atan2 calls (atan2 is ~tens of cycles each) on constant inputs every Run invocation: Atan2(0,-1)=PI, Atan2(0,1)=0, Atan2(-1,0)=-PI/2, Atan2(1,0)=PI/2.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.proposedChange: Replace with named constants: PI, 0.0, -PI/2, +PI/2 (use Math.PI). Keeps identical values, removes four transcendental calls per Run.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.rationale: Eliminates redundant runtime computation of compile-time-known transcendentals; pure constant folding the compiler may not perform across the Math.Atan2 intrinsic boundary under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.risk: None; the values are exactly the standard atan2 results for these axis directions (Math.Atan2(0,-1) is exactly Math.PI, etc.), bit-identical to the library constants used.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.summary: IsOutside recomputes the full Intersect (including a division) for pairs (a,b) that are re-tested across the convex-hull deque loop, and Intersect uses two divides where one reciprocal suffices.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.currentCost: In the i-loop, the back/front while-loops repeatedly call IsOutside on the same neighbor pairs, each performing Intersect = 1 division (no det guard here, but div ~20-40c) then a dot product. Adjacent re-tests recompute the same intersection.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.proposedChange: Compute reciprocal invDet once in Intersect and multiply (1 div + multiplies instead of 2 divs). Optionally cache the back-pair / front-pair intersection across consecutive predicate calls as suggested for MaximumInscribedCircle. Mark IsOutside and Intersect AggressiveInlining (Intersect is private leaf; IsOutside is too) to remove call overhead in the tight deque loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.rationale: Fewer divisions on the critical path and reduced call overhead via inlining of the leaf helpers used in the hottest loop of Run.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/HalfSpaceInter.risk: Reciprocal-multiply is ~1 ulp different from two divides, so NOT bit-identical; the > p.D + 1e-9 epsilon comparison tolerates this, but if exact reproducibility is contractual, keep two divides and only add inlining (which is exact). Inlining alone is fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.summary: Redundant Intersect recomputation inside the deque maintenance loops; the same (prev,curr) intersection at a fixed mid is recomputed multiple times per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.currentCost: For each of 60 binary-search iterations and each i, both the pop-back and pop-front while-loops call Intersect (2 muls + 1 div + abs + 2 divs) on (q[tail-2],q[tail-1]) / (q[head],q[head+1]) repeatedly. The final trailing while-loop likewise. A division (~20-40 cycles latency) dominates, multiplied by 60 * n * (loop iterations).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.proposedChange: Cache the intersection point for the current back-pair and front-pair so it is computed once per deque change rather than once per predicate evaluation. More importantly, hoist invariant work: c[prev]+mid and c[curr]+mid are recomputed; precompute c[i]+mid once per i. Consider that nx,ny,c do not change across iterations, only mid shifts c uniformly, so the intersection x,y for a fixed pair scales predictably — but at minimum, avoid recomputing Intersect for an unchanged pair within the same while-loop body.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.rationale: Removes repeated expensive divisions inside the innermost loop. Division has the longest latency of the ops here and sits on the critical dependency chain of the predicate.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.risk: Must preserve exact floating-point results; caching the computed (x,y) for a given (prev,curr,mid) is bit-identical, so semantics are preserved. Reordering of c[i]+mid additions is exact since it is the same single addition hoisted, not a reassociation.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.summary: Strength-reduce (i + 1) % n in the normal-precompute loop to a branchless/incremental next-index.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.currentCost: The modulo runs n times in the setup loop. Integer division/modulo is ~20-40 cycle latency and n is not generally a power of two, so & cannot be used.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.proposedChange: Replace nxt = (i + 1) % n with an incremental counter: process i in 0..n-1 with nxt starting at 1 and wrapping to 0 only on the last iteration (nxt = i + 1; if (nxt == n) nxt = 0;), or special-case the last edge (i = n-1 -> nxt = 0) outside the loop. Branchless: int nxt = i + 1 - ((i + 1 == n ? 1 : 0) * n) is unnecessary; the single compare-and-set is cheaper than a div.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.rationale: Replaces a hardware divide with a single predicted compare/conditional-move per iteration, shortening the dependency chain in the setup pass.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.risk: None; produces identical indices for all i in [0,n-1]. Setup loop is O(n) and runs once, so impact is bounded, hence medium not high.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.summary: The det near-zero guard branch (Math.Abs(det) < 1e-12) sits on the hot path of a method called many times per binary-search iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.currentCost: Each call evaluates Math.Abs and a compare/branch before the divisions. In the inner deque loops this branch is evaluated O(60 * n * loop) times. For well-conditioned convex polygons det is essentially never near zero, so the branch is almost always not taken but still costs a compare and a poorly-predictable guard.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.proposedChange: If callers guarantee non-degenerate adjacent edges (convex, distinct normals), provide an unchecked Intersect variant for the hot deque path and keep the guarded version for setup/extraction. Alternatively compute 1.0/det once and multiply (replaces two divides with one divide + two multiplies), since both x and y divide by the same det.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.rationale: Reciprocal-and-multiply turns 2 divisions into 1 division + 2 multiplications (div ~20-40c vs mul ~3-5c), a clear win on the critical chain. The unchecked variant removes a branch from the hottest loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MaximumInscrib.risk: Reciprocal multiply slightly changes rounding vs two separate divides (1 ulp), so it is NOT bit-identical; acceptable only if the binary-search tolerance (60 iterations) absorbs sub-ulp differences. State this explicitly: propose the reciprocal form only if exact bit-reproducibility is not contractually required. The unchecked variant requires the caller-guarantees-valid-input convention to hold.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.summary: FixNeighbors contains commented-out/dead reconstruction logic and a SetNeighbor call whose arguments do not match the documented original algorithm; it appears semantically broken/incomplete, which is both a correctness risk and dead-code cost.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.currentCost: The method iterates all faces (O(faceCount)) per inserted point and calls SetNeighbor with (faces[f].C, faces[f].A, nextF), while inline comments admit uncertainty ('Error in previous logic?', 'Re-checking original logic: u = faces[f].B; v = faces[f].A'). head is keyed by u via head[u]=newF in TryCreateNewFace but FixNeighbors reads head[faces[f].A] and head[faces[f].B], so the horizon-edge stitching likely links the wrong faces.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.proposedChange: Reconcile the head-map convention: TryCreateNewFace stores head[u]=newF for new face edge (u,v); FixNeighbors should, for each new face, look up the adjacent new face sharing the opposite directed edge (head[v]) and SetNeighbor accordingly, matching the standard incremental-hull horizon stitching. Remove the dead comment block. Verify against a unit test with a known polytope.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.rationale: Beyond perf: incorrect neighbor links corrupt the face adjacency used by subsequent ProcessPoint visibility deletion via Volume sign, which can either crash (out-of-range face index in SetNeighbor/TryCreateNewFace) or silently produce a non-convex result. Correct linking is a prerequisite before any micro-opt; the dead code also bloats the inlined body.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.risk: This is a semantics-changing fix, not a behavior-preserving micro-opt — flag for review and test coverage. Must validate that head is fully reset between points (it is reset in the second loop) and that no stale head entries leak across ProcessPoint calls.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.summary: The collinearity test recomputes each cross-product component twice (squared inline) instead of storing it once.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.currentCost: Line 66 computes (dy1*dz2 - dz1*dy2), (dz1*dx2 - dx1*dz2), (dx1*dy2 - dy1*dx2) and then squares each by writing the full subexpression twice, doubling the multiply/subtract work for the magnitude test. Also dx1,dy1,dz1 (the p1-p0 delta) are recomputed every loop iteration though they are loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.proposedChange: Hoist dx1,dy1,dz1 out of the i-loop (they depend only on p0,p1). Compute cx,cy,cz once each, then return cx*cx+cy*cy+cz*cz > 1e-15. This halves the cross-product arithmetic and removes redundant per-iteration recomputation of the fixed edge vector.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.rationale: Fewer multiplies/subtracts per iteration and a shorter dependency chain; loop-invariant hoist of the p1-p0 delta removes 3 subtractions per iteration. Runs once at setup so impact is low, but it is a free, exact win.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.risk: None; squaring a precomputed value is bit-identical to squaring the inline subexpression, and hoisting an invariant is exact.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.summary: head[] is fully re-initialized to -1 over all n entries before the insertion loop, but only the entries touched by TryCreateNewFace need resetting; current FixNeighbors already resets touched entries, making the n-wide init partially redundant.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.currentCost: Line 41 writes -1 to head[0..n-1] (O(n) memory writes, cache-line traffic) once. FixNeighbors resets only faces' A/B entries after each point. The full n-wide clear is needed only for the very first point's correctness if any vertex index can exceed touched set.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.proposedChange: Keep the single initial clear (it is O(n) once and cheap relative to the build), but ensure FixNeighbors' reset covers exactly the entries set in this round so no second full clear is ever needed. This is mostly a verification item; the bigger concern is that head is indexed by vertex id (size n) yet new faces reference p which is also < n, so n entries are required — confirm no over/under-clear. No change if already correct.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.rationale: Avoids any redundant full-array clears across the n insertion iterations; touching only dirtied entries keeps head mostly hot in cache and avoids O(n) writes per point.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHull3D.c.risk: Must guarantee every head entry written during a point's processing is reset before the next point, otherwise stale newF indices cause mis-linking. Tie this to the FixNeighbors correctness fix; do not change clearing semantics without the adjacency fix landed.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHullTric.summary: The bad-line test casts to double for the cross-multiplication, losing exactness and adding int->double conversions; Int128 (or a 128-bit mul) gives exact comparison and avoids float conversion on every pop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHullTric.currentCost: Per pop in the while-loop: two long->double conversions of products plus a double multiply/compare. double has 53-bit mantissa, so (b3-b1)*(m1-m2) with 64-bit operands overflows precision and can mis-decide near-collinear lines, and the int->float conversions add latency.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHullTric.proposedChange: Use System.Int128 (Burst-blittable, no allocation) for the cross products: compare (Int128)(b3-b1)*(m1-m2) <= (Int128)(b2-b1)*(m1-m3). This is exact and avoids FP conversions. If Int128 is unavailable under the target Burst version, keep double but document the precision domain.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHullTric.rationale: Removes per-iteration float conversions and yields exact integer comparison, eliminating a class of incorrect hull pops for large coordinate magnitudes; integer 128-bit multiply is typically as fast as or faster than the convert+fp-mul path on modern cores.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/ConvexHullTric.risk: Int128 changes results only where the double comparison was already wrong (precision loss), so for in-range inputs behavior is preserved and for out-of-range it becomes MORE correct — verify Burst supports System.Int128 in the target Unity version; if not, this is rejected. Watch subtraction overflow: b3-b1 etc. of two longs can overflow 64-bit; promote operands to Int128 before subtracting to be fully safe.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.summary: Recomputes identical Cross/Dot calls multiple times per iteration; cache the base-edge results.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.currentCost: Each loop iteration calls Cross(...,t) and Cross(...,t+1) inside the while condition AND again to compute height; Dot(...,ri), Dot(...,l) computed in both the while-loop guards and again in the width calc. Cross/Dot each do 4 mul + several sub. The two while loops re-evaluate Cross(...,xs[t],ys[t]) / Dot(...,xs[ri]) on the fixed t/ri endpoint every comparison even though it only changes when t/ri advance. This is the inner hot loop of an O(n) rotating-calipers pass.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.proposedChange: Hoist the base point and edge vector once per i (px=xs[i],py=ys[i],ex=xs[nxt]-px,ey=ys[nxt]-py). Then compute support values as projections: cross_t = ex*(ys[t]-py)-ey*(xs[t]-px) etc., keeping a running 'current' value for t/ri/l so the while guard reuses the cached current instead of recomputing Cross(...,xs[t]). After each advance, update current. Reuse the final cross_t for the height computation (line 62) and the final Dot values for the width computation (line 63) instead of calling Cross/Dot a third time.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.rationale: Cuts redundant 4-mul Cross/Dot evaluations: currently ~5-6 Cross/Dot calls per iteration plus per-advance recomputation of the stationary endpoint; caching the stationary endpoint value removes one full Cross/Dot per while-iteration, and reusing the final values removes 3 more calls per outer iteration. Fewer multiplies, shorter dependency chains.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.risk: Pure arithmetic re-association of the same expressions; identical IEEE results if the exact same subtraction/mul ordering is preserved. Must keep operand order (x2-x1)*(y3-y1)-(y2-y1)*(x3-x1) to be bit-identical; if reordered, results differ by rounding — to stay strictly semantics-preserving keep the expanded form matching Cross/Dot exactly.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.summary: Replace `(t + 1) % n` advance with a branchless/cheap wrap since the index only ever increments by 1.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.currentCost: Inside the calipers while-loops, `t = (t + 1) % n` executes an integer division (DIV ~20-40 cycles, not vectorizable) on every advance. n is runtime so Burst cannot strength-reduce to a mask. Same for ri, l, and the outer `nxt = (i+1) % n`.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.proposedChange: Since t increments by exactly 1, replace with `int tn = t + 1; if (tn == n) tn = 0; t = tn;` (or branchless `t = t + 1; t = t == n ? 0 : t;`). Same for ri, l, and nxt = i+1>=n?0:i+1. The `(t+1)%n` used to read the lookahead point also becomes a precomputed `t+1==n?0:t+1`.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.rationale: Removes integer DIV from the hottest inner loops, replacing it with add + compare + cmov. On mobile ARM, idiv is especially expensive (10-12+ cycles, non-pipelined); a predicated select is ~1-2 cycles.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/RotatingCalipe.risk: Semantics identical only because the incremented value is always in [1, n] (advance is always +1 from a value in [0,n-1]); the simple wrap is exact. Verified: every modulo argument here is prev/cur index +1, never a larger jump.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.summary: O(n^3) total: every event does a full O(activeCount) scan recomputing all IntersectTime values; use an incremental candidate update or a min-heap of edge events.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.currentCost: The while(activeCount>2) loop runs O(n) times; each iteration scans `for i in 0..nextId` (which grows to ~2n) and calls IntersectTime for every non-deleted edge — O(n) per event -> O(n^2) total just for re-scanning, and nextId keeps growing so the scan walks deleted nodes too. Worst case work is quadratic-to-cubic in n.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.proposedChange: Maintain edge collapse times in a binary min-heap (stackalloc array) keyed by IntersectTime(i, next). After an event, only the two new edges (prevI->newNode and newNode->nextJ) change, so push just those and lazily skip stale/deleted heap entries on pop. This makes the algorithm O(n log n) instead of O(n^2/n^3). At minimum, avoid scanning [0,nextId): keep an explicit linked-list walk over only active nodes starting from any live head, giving O(activeCount) per event without touching deleted slots.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.rationale: Replaces a per-event full rescan (touching all created-and-deleted nodes up to 2n) with O(log n) heap maintenance. Removes the dominant asymptotic cost; also improves cache behavior by not streaming deleted entries.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.risk: Heap version changes tie-break ordering when multiple events share minT; original picks the lowest-index i. To preserve exact output, break heap ties by node index. The cheaper linked-list-only walk fully preserves semantics (same min selection) with no behavioral change and is the safe minimum.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.summary: IntersectTime is recomputed for every surviving edge on every event though only edges adjacent to the last collapse changed.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.currentCost: Even keeping the O(n) scan, IntersectTime (several abs/div/branches) is evaluated for all ~activeCount edges each of the ~n events. Only the new node's two incident edges change their collapse time between events; all others are invariant.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.proposedChange: Store the computed collapse time t on each Node (add a double field, e.g. CollapseT) when the node is created/updated. The per-event scan then just reads node.CollapseT to find the min instead of recomputing IntersectTime. Recompute only for prevI and the newly inserted node after each event.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.rationale: Turns O(events * activeCount) IntersectTime evaluations into O(events) recomputations plus O(activeCount) cheap field comparisons per scan — far fewer divides and branches in the hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.risk: Adds 8 bytes to Node (scratch buffer grows). Must invalidate/recompute the cached time for the two nodes whose Next pointer changed (prevI and newNode) so a stale time is never used; otherwise output diverges. Pairs naturally with the heap change.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.summary: Node carries an unused `Id` field and a `bool Deleted` that wastes layout padding.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.currentCost: Node is { int Id; 8 doubles; int Prev; int Next; bool Deleted; }. Id is written (lines 76,138) but never read. The trailing bool forces 7 bytes of padding to 8-byte align the struct in the scratch array; over a 2n-sized scratch buffer that is wasted cache footprint.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.proposedChange: Drop the Id field entirely (the array index already identifies the node). Pack Deleted into a sentinel instead of a bool (e.g. set Next = -1 to mark deleted, or use the sign bit of Prev), eliminating the bool and its padding. This shrinks Node and improves the density of the scan over scratchNodes.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.rationale: Smaller Node => more nodes per cache line during the per-event scan (the bottleneck), fewer bytes to initialize, lower mobile memory pressure. Removing Id removes two dead stores per node creation.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/StraightSkelet.risk: Must add explicit StructLayout if relying on field order for the deleted-sentinel; check no caller reads Node.Id or Node.Deleted outside this file. The struct lacks [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] though it imports InteropServices — add it to guarantee blittable layout for Burst.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.summary: `% an` / `% bn` on runtime moduli inside the merge loop, plus redundant recomputation of edge deltas that could be incremental.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.currentCost: The while loop computes `(i+1)%an`, `i%an`, `(j+1)%bn`, `j%bn` every iteration — 4 integer DIVs per step over (an+bn) steps. Since i only ranges 0..an and the indices step by 1, the modulo is only needed to wrap the single +1 lookahead.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.proposedChange: Track current indices ic=i (clamped) and the wrapped next index incrementally: maintain inext where inext = i+1==an?0:i+1 updated only when i advances. Replace `i % an` with i when i<an (the only time deltas are used in the dual-branch), and use the precomputed wrapped lookahead. Replace the four `%` with add+compare wraps.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.rationale: Removes 4 idiv per merge step. idiv is ~20-40 cycles and serializes; add/cmp/cmov replacement is a few cycles. The merge loop is the whole cost of the algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.risk: Need care: when i==an the code path uses i<an guard so deltas with i%an wrap to 0 are still computed but unused in that branch; replacing %an with conditional wrap must reproduce the same value (i%an for i in [0,an]). Since i never exceeds an, `i==an?0:i` is exact; keep that guard precise.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.summary: Uses two stackalloc scratch buffers and a copy-back; the cyclic rotation can be done in place via reversal or gcd-cycle rotation.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.currentCost: Allocates 2*n doubles of stack (tx,ty) and does a full copy into them then back — 2n reads+writes of scratch plus 2n for copy-back, i.e. ~4n memory ops and 2n*8 bytes stack. The `(minIdx+i)%n` also does n integer DIVs.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.proposedChange: Rotate-left by minIdx in place using the three-reversal trick (reverse[0,minIdx), reverse[minIdx,n), reverse[0,n)) on x and y, or a juggling/gcd cycle rotation. No scratch buffer, ~n swaps total, and no modulo.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.rationale: Eliminates 2*n*8 bytes of stackalloc and the copy-back pass, halving memory traffic, and removes n idiv from the index computation. Lower stack pressure matters for Burst inlining (Reorder is AggressiveInlining'd into Convex).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.risk: In-place reversal preserves the exact rotated sequence (same doubles, same order) so output is bit-identical. Must reverse x and y with the identical index pattern to keep pairs aligned. Slightly more code but no managed/exception surface.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.summary: Negate-and-reverse done in two passes over the b buffer; fuse into one pass.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.currentCost: First loop negates all bn entries into nbx/nby; second loop reverses them via swaps. Two sweeps of the bn-length buffers (2*bn reads/writes for negate + bn swaps for reverse).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.proposedChange: Single pass: for i in [0,bn) write nbx[i] = -bx[bn-1-i]; nby[i] = -by[bn-1-i]; producing the negated+reversed array directly with bn writes and no separate swap loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.rationale: One sweep instead of two; eliminates the swap loop's reads/writes and its `bn/2` branch. Fewer total memory operations and a cleaner straight-line loop Burst can vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Hull/MinkowskiSum.c.risk: Output array identical (negation and reversal commute element-wise). bn writes vs original two-phase; verify mid-element handling — the fused form is exact for all bn including odd lengths where the original swap loop skipped the center (center gets negated in pass 1 there; fused negates it too).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.summary: Signed distance assumes denormalized plane normal and recomputes sqrt of |n| every call; offer a fast path / document the convention.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.currentCost: One sqrt + 5 mults + 1 div per call. Callers passing an already-normalized (nx,ny,nz) still pay the full sqrt(nx*nx+ny*ny+nz*nz) of ~1.0.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.proposedChange: Add a sibling Run-style overload PointPlaneDistanceNormalized(px,py,pz,nx,ny,nz,d) that returns px*nx+py*ny+pz*nz+d with no sqrt, for the common case where the plane normal is unit length. Keep the general method but mark it as 'unnormalized'.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.rationale: sqrt is ~15-20 cycles and a long-latency op on the critical path; for the very common unit-normal case it is pure waste. Removing it leaves a short FMA chain that Burst vectorizes/pipelines well.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.risk: Different method, not a behavior change to the existing one. Caller must guarantee unit normal; document this. No overflow/sign caveat.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.summary: Axis selection recomputes Math.Abs of the three direction components up to 4 times and re-reads *ldx/*ldy/*ldz through the pointer repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.currentCost: Up to 6 Math.Abs calls and many pointer dereferences across the branch chain (lines 40-42). *ldx,*ldy,*ldz are read via pointer each time instead of from registers.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.proposedChange: Compute ax=Math.Abs(*ldx), ay=Math.Abs(*ldy), az=Math.Abs(*ldz) once into locals, then branch on ax,ay,az. Also cache the dir components into locals before the dirSq computation so the cross-product results are written once and reused from registers.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.rationale: Hoists redundant abs and removes pointer aliasing reloads: the compiler cannot assume *ldx is unchanged across calls without restrict semantics, so each *ldx reread is a real load. Locals cut ~5 loads and 3 abs ops, shortening the dependency chain before the divide.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.risk: Pure reordering; identical results. lpx/lpy/lpz may alias ldx/ldy/ldz only if caller passes overlapping pointers, but the existing code already reads ld* after the cross-product write, so caching matches current behavior.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.summary: Unused 'axis' parameter forces an extra argument load and obscures intent.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.currentCost: Each of the 3 call sites passes a literal axis (0/1/2) that the body never reads (line 45), costing an argument setup that the inliner usually elides but which still bloats the signature.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.proposedChange: Remove the int axis parameter from SolvePoint and drop the 0/1/2 literals at call sites.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.rationale: Dead parameter elimination: fewer argument moves if not fully inlined, and clearer signature. No functional effect.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Plane.cs.risk: None; parameter is provably unused in the body.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.summary: Tangent branch (disc<1e-12) recomputes -b/(2.0*a); and the citardauq path divides by 2.0*a twice via separate constant divides.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.currentCost: Two divides by (2.0*a) implied; the disc<1e-12 path computes 2.0*a fresh. r*r, b*b, 4.0*a*c form a moderate dependency chain feeding sqrt.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.proposedChange: Hoist double inv2a = 0.5 / a (one divide) and reuse it: tangent t = -b*inv2a. Keep the numerically-stable citardauq form for the two-root case (q/a and c/q are already good). Precompute double rr = r*r once.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.rationale: Replaces a long-latency divide in the tangent branch with a multiply by a precomputed reciprocal; 0.5/a is computed once and shared. Divides are ~20-30 cycles on mobile FPUs, mults ~4.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.risk: 0.5/a vs -b/(2.0*a): floating-point result can differ in the last ULP. Acceptable for a geometric tangent root, but if exact bit-reproducibility with the current build is contractual, reject. State the ULP caveat.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.summary: dx/d, dy/d, dz/d are each computed twice (once for center, once for normal) — six divides where three suffice; r1*r1 and r2*r2 also recomputed.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.currentCost: Lines 77-85 perform dx/d, dy/d, dz/d twice = 6 divides total. r1*r1 appears at lines 73 and 74; r2*r2 at line 73. Each divide is ~20-30 cycles.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.proposedChange: Compute double invD = 1.0/d once, then nxv=dx*invD, nyv=dy*invD, nzv=dz*invD into locals; write *nx=nxv etc. and *cx=x1+a*nxv etc. Precompute double r1r1=r1*r1, r2r2=r2*r2 and reuse in the 'a' formula and hSq.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.rationale: Cuts 6 divides to 1 (reciprocal) plus 6 mults, and removes 1 redundant square. This is the dominant cost in this routine; on mobile the divide reduction alone is a large win and shortens the dependency chain feeding the output writes.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.risk: Multiply-by-reciprocal differs from direct divide by up to ~1 ULP per component. If bit-exact reproducibility is required reject; otherwise geometrically negligible. Behavior (return value, sign) unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.summary: Early-reject tests use d=sqrt(dSq) but could be done on squared quantities, deferring the sqrt until after rejection.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.currentCost: sqrt(dSq) at line 67 is always paid even when the spheres are clearly separated/contained and the function returns false at lines 69-71.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.proposedChange: Rewrite the separation test d > r1+r2 as dSq > (r1+r2)^2 and containment d < |r1-r2| as dSq < (r1-r2)^2 (both sides non-negative), with epsilon folded appropriately, so sqrt is only computed once the pair is confirmed intersecting.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.rationale: Avoids a long-latency sqrt on the common rejection paths in broad-phase-style usage. Squared comparisons are exact-sign equivalent since all operands are non-negative.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Intersect/Sphere.cs.risk: Epsilon semantics shift: 'd > r1+r2+1e-12' is not identical to 'dSq > (r1+r2+1e-12)^2' at the boundary. To preserve exact behavior, compare dSq against (r1+r2)*(r1+r2) plus a derived tolerance, or keep the epsilon in linear space by only skipping sqrt on the clearly-true squared rejections and falling back. Flag as needing careful epsilon handling; reject if epsilon boundary must match bit-for-bit.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.summary: Hoist the inNormals/outNormals null check and the forward-vector computation out of the per-vertex hot path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.currentCost: Every iteration computes f = SafeNormalize(lerp(f0,f1,t), ...) — a lerp, a math.length (sqrt), a branch, and a divide — but f is used ONLY inside the `if (inNormals != null && outNormals != null)` block. When normals are not requested, all of that work plus the two pointer loads f0/f1 are pure waste, executed vertexCount times.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.proposedChange: Compute `bool hasNormals = inNormals != null && outNormals != null;` once before the loop. Move the f0/f1 loads and the `float3 f = SafeNormalize(...)` inside the `if (hasNormals)` block so they are skipped entirely in the position-only case.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.rationale: Removes one lerp + one sqrt + one divide + one branch + two float3 loads per vertex on the common position-only path. The null pointers are loop-invariant, so the branch itself is also hoisted (Burst can hoist, but making it explicit guarantees the dead f computation is gone).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.risk: None. f only feeds nDeformed inside the normals branch; behavior is identical for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant `(float)(pathCount - 1)` conversion and reuse it.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.currentCost: `float floatIdx = u * (float)(pathCount - 1);` recomputes the int subtraction and int->float conversion every iteration, and `pathCount - 1` is also recomputed for math.min.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.proposedChange: Before the loop: `int lastIdx = pathCount - 1; float lastIdxF = (float)lastIdx;`. Use `u * lastIdxF` and `math.min(idx0 + 1, lastIdx)` inside the loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.rationale: Removes one int sub + one int->float cvt per vertex (cvt has non-trivial latency on some targets) and shortens the dependency chain feeding floatIdx.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.summary: Premultiply scale.x into r and scale.y into upVec instead of scaling per-component-per-vertex.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.currentCost: `vDeformed = p + vLocal.x * r * scale.x + vLocal.y * upVec * scale.y` does two extra scalar*float3 multiplies (r*scale.x, upVec*scale.y) per vertex, where scale is loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.proposedChange: Fold scale into the basis: `float3 rS = r * scale.x; float3 upS = upVec * scale.y;` then `vDeformed = p + vLocal.x * rS + vLocal.y * upS;`. Note r and upVec are still needed unscaled for the normal computation, so keep both. Net change: replaces (vLocal.x * r) * scale.x with (vLocal.x) * rS, i.e. moves the scale multiply off the per-vertex scalar onto the already-needed normalized basis — but since r/upVec are computed per vertex too, this is a wash unless the position branch is split from normals. Lower the priority accordingly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.rationale: Reduces the dependency chain for the position write by precombining the scale; marginal because the basis is per-vertex here. Mainly a readability/chain-length win.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.risk: Floating-point reassociation: (vLocal.x * r) * scale.x vs vLocal.x * (r * scale.x) can differ in the last ULP. Acceptable for mesh deformation but technically not bit-identical; flag if strict reproducibility is required.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.summary: Advance a triangle pointer by 3 instead of recomputing i*3, i*3+1, i*3+2.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.currentCost: Per triangle: three integer multiplies-by-3 (or one mul + two adds) to compute the index offsets `indices[i*3]`, `indices[i*3+1]`, `indices[i*3+2]`.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.proposedChange: Iterate with a moving pointer: `int* tri = indices; for (int i = 0; i < triangleCount; i++, tri += 3) { int idx0 = tri[0]; int idx1 = tri[1]; int idx2 = tri[2]; ... }`. This strength-reduces the address arithmetic to a single +=3.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.rationale: Removes the per-triangle multiply and turns three independent index expressions into three consecutive loads from one base, which the address-generation unit handles for free.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.risk: None; same elements accessed in the same order.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.summary: Replace math.length + divide in the final normalize pass with rsqrt on length-squared (with matching guard).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.currentCost: Final loop does `len = math.length(n)` (a sqrt) then `n / len` (a vector divide), per vertex.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.proposedChange: `float lenSq = math.lengthsq(n); n = lenSq > EpsilonSq ? n * math.rsqrt(lenSq) : new float3(0,1,0);` with `const float EpsilonSq = Epsilon*Epsilon`.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.rationale: rsqrt + multiply is cheaper than sqrt + divide on most targets (rsqrt is a single hardware estimate path Burst vectorizes; divide is high-latency). lengthsq avoids the sqrt entirely in the guard.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.risk: math.rsqrt is an approximation, so the normalized output differs from v/length(v) by a small relative error — NOT bit-identical. Acceptable for rendering normals but observably different; only apply if approximate normals are acceptable. Guard threshold must use EpsilonSq = Epsilon*Epsilon to preserve the same fallback boundary (len > Epsilon <=> lenSq > Epsilon^2 for nonnegative len).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.summary: Use lengthsq for the guard and rsqrt for the normalize to avoid sqrt+divide.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.currentCost: `len = math.length(v)` (sqrt) then `v / len` (divide) on every call (3x per deformed vertex when normals on, plus r/up always).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.proposedChange: `float lenSq = math.lengthsq(v); return lenSq > EpsilonSq ? v * math.rsqrt(lenSq) : fallback;`
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.rationale: Eliminates a sqrt and a vector divide in favor of rsqrt+multiply per call; SafeNormalize is a hot leaf called 2-3x per vertex.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Mesh/MeshProjection.risk: rsqrt is approximate => result not bit-identical to v/length(v). Guard must use EpsilonSq=Epsilon*Epsilon to keep the same fallback boundary. Only apply if approximate unit vectors are acceptable for deformation/lighting.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/CoverTree.c.summary: Nearest is a brute-force linear scan mislabeled as a cover-tree query; it also ignores the actual tree links (Next/Level) and silently caps at 1024 nodes, producing WRONG results beyond that.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/CoverTree.c.currentCost: O(n) scan but loop bound is 'i < root + 1', tying the search range to the numeric value of the root index rather than the node count n, plus a hard '&& i < 1024' cap. For root!=n-1 or n>1024 the answer is incorrect, not just slow.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/CoverTree.c.proposedChange: Pass the real node count n into Nearest (or iterate i<n) and remove the 1024 cap, OR implement an actual cover-tree descent using Level/Next so the query becomes sub-linear. At minimum fix the loop bound to scan all n candidates so semantics are correct before optimizing.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/CoverTree.c.rationale: A genuine cover tree gives expected O(c^12 log n) nearest-neighbor queries vs the current O(min(root+1,1024)). Even keeping brute force, scanning n instead of root+1 removes a correctness-vs-index coupling bug and the magic cap.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/CoverTree.c.risk: This changes observable output for inputs where root != n-1 or n > 1024. If the cap/root-coupling is considered 'by-design valid input', this is a behavior change; flag to owner. The Level/Next fields are currently dead (Build sets Level=0, Next=-1 and Nearest never reads them), so the struct also wastes 8 bytes/node.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.summary: BallTree.Build never sets Left/Right (leaves all -1), so Nearest's recursion is dead and Nearest degenerates to inspecting only the root node — it is neither a ball tree nor a correct nearest search.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.currentCost: Build writes Left=Right=-1 for every node, so NearestRec returns immediately on both children; Nearest effectively returns root always. The radius field R is computed as 0 and never used. This is O(1) but returns wrong answers for n>1.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.proposedChange: Either build an actual ball-tree hierarchy (split on widest spread, set R to the bounding radius, populate Left/Right) and prune in NearestRec using 'if (sqrt(d_to_center) - R >= sqrt(bd)) return;', or if a linear scan is intended, loop i in [0,n) in Nearest. As-is the recursion and R are pure overhead.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.rationale: A real ball tree prunes subtrees via the triangle inequality giving expected O(log n) queries; current code is O(1)-but-wrong. If kept flat, removing R and the unused recursion shrinks Node from 40 to 32 bytes and removes two dead recursive calls per query.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.risk: Behavior-changing: fixes incorrect nearest results for n>1. Confirm with owner whether the flat/degenerate behavior is intended. R removal changes struct layout/ABI.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.summary: Nearest uses non-tail recursion (NearestRec on Left then Right) which Burst cannot tail-call optimize and which, given the dead links, is pure overhead today.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.currentCost: Two recursive calls per node create stack frames and a call dependency chain; with no pruning this is a full traversal when links exist.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.proposedChange: If a real ball tree is implemented, convert NearestRec to an explicit stackalloc'd index stack with triangle-inequality pruning (push the nearer child last); this is Burst-friendly (no recursion) and prunes subtrees. If the flat-scan interpretation is chosen, drop recursion entirely for a simple loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.rationale: Burst does not guarantee recursion optimization; an explicit stack avoids call overhead and enables pruning, turning a full O(n) traversal into expected O(log n) with the radius bound.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/BallTree.cs.risk: Tied to the Build fix above; only meaningful once Left/Right/R are populated. Explicit-stack version must reproduce the same nearest result (ties broken by first-seen as the current 'd < bd' does).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.summary: Build uses an O(count^2) selection-style bubble sort at every recursion level, making tree construction O(n^2 log n) instead of O(n log n).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.currentCost: The nested i/j loops fully sort each subarray with ~count^2/2 comparisons and swaps per node; summed over levels this is O(n^2 log n). For n in the thousands this dominates everything.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.proposedChange: Replace the full sort with an in-place quickselect (nth_element) on the chosen axis to partition around 'mid' in expected O(count). You only need the median positioned and elements partitioned around it, not a total order. This reduces build to expected O(n log n).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.rationale: Median-of-the-array is all the kd-tree needs; quickselect gives expected linear partition per node, turning the per-level cost from O(n^2) into O(n) and total build from O(n^2 log n) to O(n log n).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.risk: Quickselect tie-handling must keep left subtree size == mid and elements < pivot on the left to preserve identical tree shape; with duplicate coordinates the exact node assignment may differ from the stable bubble sort. If exact tree identity matters for downstream tests, use a deterministic pivot and stable partition.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.summary: Each recursion allocates two fresh stackalloc index buffers (leftIndices/rightIndices) and copies into them, causing O(n log n) extra stack traffic and risking stack overflow on deep/large n.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.currentCost: Per node: stackalloc[mid] + stackalloc[rightCount] plus two copy loops. Stackalloc inside a recursive method accumulates frames (it is NOT freed until the method returns), so total live stack is O(n log n) worst case — a real overflow hazard for large n under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.proposedChange: Partition the single 'indices' array in place around the median (as quickselect does) and recurse on the [0,mid) and (mid,count) slices of the same buffer via pointer offset + length, eliminating both per-call stackallocs and the copy loops.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.rationale: In-place partitioning removes all auxiliary allocation and the copy passes, cuts stack growth from O(n log n) to O(n) for the index array (single buffer) plus O(log n) recursion frames, and improves cache locality.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.risk: Must ensure the in-place partition leaves the left half entirely before mid and right half after, matching the recursion contract. Recursion depth still O(log n) after balanced median selection; guard against degenerate depth if quickselect picks bad pivots (use median-of-three).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.summary: axis is 'depth % 2' and the inner swap test branches on 'axis == 0' / 'axis == 1' separately every comparison.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.currentCost: depth % 2 is a modulo (compiler likely lowers to AND, but not guaranteed under all paths), and the comparison evaluates two independent if-branches per (i,j) pair inside the hot O(count^2) loop, adding a redundant compare.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.proposedChange: Compute 'axis = depth & 1' (power-of-two mask, always valid for non-negative depth). Hoist the axis decision out of the inner loop by selecting the coordinate pointer once: 'double* key = (axis == 0) ? xs : ys;' then compare 'key[indices[j]] < key[indices[i]]'. Combined with quickselect this disappears, but even with the current sort it removes a branch per comparison.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.rationale: & 1 is a single-cycle mask vs a potential div/rem; selecting the key pointer once turns two per-iteration branches into a straight-line compare, shortening the dependency chain in the innermost loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/KdTree.cs.risk: depth is always >= 0 so '& 1' is exactly '% 2' here — safe. Pointer-select keeps identical comparison semantics.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.summary: Both run textbook O(n^2) Prim with a fresh inner loop that recomputes full pairwise distances; the two methods are ~95% duplicated and recompute xs[u],ys[u] each v-iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.currentCost: Inner update loop reloads xs[u]/ys[u] every iteration (compiler may hoist, but under pointer aliasing it may not) and recomputes Math.Abs / multiply for every unvisited v each of n outer steps: O(n^2) distance evals. Code duplication doubles maintenance surface.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.proposedChange: Hoist 'double xu = xs[u]; double yu = ys[u];' above the v-loop so the per-v body uses locals (breaks aliasing assumptions, lets Burst keep them in registers and vectorize). Optionally unify the two methods via a metric flag or a templated inner distance to remove duplication while keeping the unchecked perf path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.rationale: Hoisting kills two pointer loads per inner iteration (2*n^2 loads removed) and gives Burst alias-free locals it can SIMD-widen across v. The distance form (abs-sum vs squared) is the only real difference.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.risk: Pure constant-factor win, semantics identical. Unifying methods must not introduce a per-iteration branch on the metric inside the inner loop (use two specialized inner loops or a compile-time switch) or you trade the load saving for a branch.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.summary: O(n^2) dense Prim is used even though MST in the plane under L1/L2 can be built from a sparse Delaunay/L1-Delaunay graph in O(n log n).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.currentCost: Selection of the next vertex (O(n) scan) times n iterations = O(n^2) time and the algorithm touches every pair. For large point sets this is the dominant cost.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.proposedChange: For Euclidean, the MST is a subgraph of the Delaunay triangulation (O(n) edges); build Delaunay (O(n log n)) then run Kruskal/Prim on the sparse graph for O(n log n) total. For Manhattan/rectilinear, use the classic 8-octant (Guibas-Stolfi / Zachariasen) sweep that yields O(n) candidate edges in O(n log n).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.rationale: Reduces an inherently O(n^2) all-pairs Prim to O(n log n) by exploiting planar MST sparsity — a genuine asymptotic improvement for the 2D case these functions target.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.risk: Large implementation effort and adds substantial code; ties/degenerate collinear points need careful handling to keep the exact same MST weight (MST weight is unique only when all edge weights distinct). If downstream relies on the specific edge set, the chosen-edge identity may differ even when total weight matches. Provide as opt-in rather than replacing the unchecked O(n^2) path.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.summary: dist[] stores squared distances and Math.Sqrt is taken only once per accepted edge — already good; but totalWeight accumulation reads back outW[edgeCount] from memory after writing it.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.currentCost: 'outW[edgeCount] = Math.Sqrt(dist[u]); totalWeight += outW[edgeCount];' writes then reloads through the pointer, a store-to-load that can stall and defeats keeping the value in a register.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.proposedChange: Compute into a local: 'double w = Math.Sqrt(dist[u]); outW[edgeCount] = w; totalWeight += w;'
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.rationale: Removes a dependent load right after a store (store-forwarding stall / aliasing barrier) and lets the sqrt result stay in a register for the add.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Mst.cs.risk: None; identical result. Pure local-variable refactor.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.summary: The flat index '(long)(i-1)*Y*Z + (long)(j-1)*Z + (k-1)' recomputes Y*Z and the i/j partial products inside the innermost k-loop on every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.currentCost: Per innermost iteration: two long multiplies plus adds, and Y*Z is recomputed at every (i,j,k). These are loop-invariant relative to inner loops.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.proposedChange: Hoist 'long yz = (long)bit->Y * bit->Z;' once; hoist 'long iBase = (long)(i-1)*yz;' in the i-loop; hoist 'long ijBase = iBase + (long)(j-1)*bit->Z;' in the j-loop; inner index becomes 'ijBase + (k-1)'. Same for Sum.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.rationale: Moves invariant multiplies out of the BIT's innermost loop (which runs O(log per dim) but the multiplies are on the critical address-gen path), reducing the inner body to one add and one load/store.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.risk: None; arithmetic is associative over long here and values are identical. Y*Z fits in long as already cast.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.summary: Init zeroes Tree with a scalar element-by-element loop instead of a bulk clear.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.currentCost: O(x*y*z) scalar stores with loop overhead; Burst may auto-vectorize but a memset is guaranteed wide.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.proposedChange: Use 'Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(bit->Tree, 0, (uint)(bit->Size * sizeof(long)))' (or a Burst-friendly memset) to zero the whole buffer in one call.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.rationale: Bulk zeroing issues wide stores / uses the platform memset, beating a scalar loop and shortening code; fewer loop-branch overheads.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Bit3D.cs.risk: Size*sizeof(long) must not overflow uint — Size is int (x*y*z); for very large grids Size*8 could exceed uint. Guard: ensure (long)Size*8 <= uint.MaxValue, else fall back to loop. Behavior otherwise identical (all-zero).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.summary: Octant index computed twice per point (count pass + scatter pass); cache it in a stackalloc byte buffer and reuse.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.currentCost: GetOctIdx is called once in the counting loop (line 33) and again in the scatter loop (line 35) for every point in [start,end). That is 2 calls x (3 compares + 3 ORs) per point per recursion level, i.e. O(n) redundant index recomputation at every tree level (O(n log n) total wasted GetOctIdx evaluations and 2x redundant loads of xs/ys/zs).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.proposedChange: Allocate `byte* oct = stackalloc byte[n];` alongside tx/ty/tz. In the first loop store `byte o = (byte)GetOctIdx(...); oct[i-start]=o; counts[o]++;`. In the scatter loop read `int idx = oct[i-start];` instead of recomputing. This also removes the second set of xs[i]/ys[i]/zs[i] loads needed only for the index.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.rationale: Halves the GetOctIdx work and eliminates one full re-read of the three coordinate streams per node, trading 6 FP compares/point for one byte load/store. Fewer cycles and fewer dependent loads in the hottest build loop; byte buffer is tiny and stays in L1.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.risk: None to semantics — identical partition. Adds n bytes of stack per recursion frame; n shrinks down the tree so peak extra stack is bounded by root n. Keep `byte` (0..7 fits).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.summary: stackalloc of tx/ty/tz uses the full [start,end) span at every recursion level, compounding stack usage along the deepest path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.currentCost: Each BuildRec frame that partitions allocates 3*n doubles (24*n bytes) of scratch where n=end-start. Along a recursion path the live frames stack their scratch; worst case the sum over the path can approach 24*N*maxDepth bytes of stack in pathological splits, risking stack overflow for large N on mobile (small thread stacks).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.proposedChange: Allocate the tx/ty/tz scratch once in Build() sized to the root n (or accept a caller-provided scratch pointer per the Try*/Run convention) and pass it down, reusing the same buffer at each level since partition is done before recursing into children.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.rationale: Caller-provided or once-allocated scratch caps scratch RAM at 24*N bytes total instead of growing per recursion frame, removing a mobile stack-overflow hazard and reducing stack-probe/touch cost.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.risk: Scratch is consumed before BuildChildren recurses, so a single shared buffer is safe (no overlap between a parent's partition and its children's). Must size to root n. Changes Build signature if exposed as a scratch param (ergonomics tradeoff).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.summary: Recomputes mx,my,mz which were already computed (as x+size/2 etc.) by the caller for PartitionOctants.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.currentCost: PartitionOctants is called with x+size/2, y+size/2, z+size/2 (line 25), then BuildChildren recomputes mx=x+half, my=y+half, mz=z+half (line 41) where half==size/2. Two extra adds (size/2 already equals half). Minor but per-node.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.proposedChange: Compute `double half = size/2, mx = x+half, my = y+half, mz = z+half;` once in BuildRec and pass mx/my/mz into both PartitionOctants and BuildChildren, dropping the recompute and the inner `x + size/2` expressions.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.rationale: Removes 3 redundant adds and a divide-vs-half mismatch per internal node; tightens the per-node dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.risk: size/2 and half are bit-identical (same double divide), so midpoints are identical — fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.summary: Leaf detection does 8 child-pointer compares even though the build already stores Count; recursion also re-checks each child >=0 after the all-negative test.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.currentCost: Every visited node runs an 8-way `Ci<0` AND chain (line 57) to detect a leaf, then on internal nodes re-tests each `Ci>=0` (lines 59-66). A leaf node here is exactly one with end-start<=1 or depth>=maxDepth; the node already carries Count and could carry an explicit leaf flag, avoiding the 8-compare scan on the hot query path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.proposedChange: Mark leaves at build time (e.g. set C0=-2 sentinel or a dedicated IsLeaf via reusing sign of Count) and test a single condition for the leaf fast-path; for internal nodes the per-child `>=0` guard is still needed but the leaf scan is removed.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.rationale: Replaces an 8-term boolean reduction at every node with one branch on the common leaf path, shortening the query's per-node critical path in a recursive hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Octree.cs.risk: Must pick a sentinel that cannot collide with valid node indices (>=0). Adds one store at build time. Behavior identical if the leaf predicate matches the original all-children-negative condition exactly.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.summary: Axis-selecting ternary (xs/ys/zs choice) is re-evaluated inside the innermost partition compare loops, putting two nested branches on every comparison.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.currentCost: Lines 36,40,41 select the coordinate array via `axis==0?xs:(axis==1?ys:zs)` for the pivot and for every i/j comparison inside the inner while loops. axis is invariant for the whole BuildRec call, yet the two-way/three-way branch executes per comparison — O(n log n) redundant axis branches and indirect array selection that defeats clean vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.proposedChange: Hoist `double* a = axis==0?xs:(axis==1?ys:zs);` once at the top of BuildRec, then compare `a[idx[i]] < pivot` etc. This collapses the per-compare ternary to a single pointer load.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.rationale: Removes 1-2 branches per comparison in the median-partition inner loop and exposes a single contiguous gather (a[idx[*]]) the JIT/Burst can schedule better; strict win in the build hot path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.risk: axis is constant within a BuildRec frame, so hoisting is exact. None to semantics.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.summary: Median selection uses a full quickselect-style partition loop per node giving O(n log n) average but O(n^2) worst case and re-partitioning already-ordered data.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.currentCost: BuildRec runs a Hoare-style partition repeatedly to drive the median to position k at every level. With adversarial / pre-sorted input the partition degrades toward O(n) per level over O(n) levels = O(n^2) build, and the work is not reused across levels.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.proposedChange: Either pre-sort indices per axis once and build via index splitting (classic kd-tree build with presorted arrays, O(n log n) deterministic), or use a median-of-three / introselect pivot to bound the worst case. At minimum, median-of-three pivot selection for the partition.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.rationale: Bounds the asymptotic build cost and removes the pathological O(n^2) on sorted/clustered point sets common in spatial data.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.risk: Changing pivot strategy changes which equal-key element lands at the node but not query correctness (range queries over kd-tree are order-insensitive). Presorted-build is a larger rewrite; median-of-three is low-risk.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.summary: Per-node axis dispatch via depth%2 ternary chain; depth%2 and the val/min/max selection can be replaced by branchless or alternating-axis recursion.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.currentCost: Each QueryRec node computes `depth%2`, then three ternaries to pick val/minV/maxV (lines 81-84). depth%2 is a modulo (compiles to and on non-negative depth) plus 3 conditional selects per visited node on the recursive query hot path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.proposedChange: Pass the already-known axis (toggle 0/1) instead of depth, and select coordinate via a small branchless pattern: for 2D, `bool xAxis = (depth&1)==0; double val = xAxis?n->X:n->Y;` — or specialize two mutually-recursive functions (QueryX/QueryY) eliminating the per-node axis test entirely.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.rationale: depth%2 -> depth&1 is a safe strength reduction (depth>=0); specializing axis removes the selection branches, shortening the per-node path in a tree traversal that can visit many nodes.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/RangeTree.c.risk: depth is always >=0 so &1 == %2 exactly. Specialization duplicates code (complexity tradeoff) but is semantics-identical.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.summary: Build3D/Query3D silently ignore the z coordinate and bounds, returning 2D results — a correctness/semantics trap rather than a perf win.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.currentCost: Build3D (line 101) forwards to Build2D dropping zs entirely; Query3D (line 107) drops z1/z2. Any caller treating this as a real 3D interval/segment structure gets wrong results — and the unused z parameters mislead the API.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.proposedChange: Either implement true 3D (carry z interval into Node and test z overlap in Query) or rename/remove the 3D entry points so the API does not advertise unsupported behavior. If 3D is intentionally out of scope, drop the methods to avoid dead-parameter confusion.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.rationale: Purity/ergonomics: the function is not doing what its name promises; fixing or removing it prevents silent wrong answers and clarifies the API contract.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.risk: This is a semantics correction, not a behavior-preserving micro-opt — flag for owner decision. If callers currently rely on the 2D-forwarding behavior, removing it is breaking.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.summary: Child Min/Max merge re-loads nodes[Left]/nodes[Right] up to four times each through repeated indexing.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.currentCost: Lines 62-71 access nodes[rootIdx].Left and nodes[nodes[rootIdx].Left].Min/.Max via chained indexing multiple times (e.g. nodes[nodes[rootIdx].Left].Min appears in both the compare and the assign). Each is a dependent pointer-add + load; the compiler may not prove no-alias to fold them.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.proposedChange: Cache `int lft = nodes[rootIdx].Left;` then `Node* lc = &nodes[lft];` and read `lc->Min`/`lc->Max` once into locals before the compares. Same for Right. Also hoist `nodes[rootIdx]` into `Node* self = &nodes[rootIdx];`.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.rationale: Collapses repeated address computations and loads into single local reads, shortening the dependency chain of the bottom-up merge done at every internal node.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.risk: Pointers are stable for the duration (no reallocation), so caching addresses is safe. Semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.summary: Inner partition loop reloads xs[idx[i]]/xs[idx[j]] with double indirection per comparison; same hoist as RangeTree applies.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.currentCost: Lines 35,39,41 do nested gather xs[idx[*]] each comparison. The double indirection (idx then xs) per compare is a long dependency chain repeated O(n) per level.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.proposedChange: Within this single-axis build, the values being partitioned are always xs[idx[*]]; this is already minimal, but the pivot `xs[idx[k]]` is reloaded as the loop may move idx[k]. Hoisting pivot into a local `double pivot` (already done) is fine; ensure idx[i]/idx[j] indices are read into locals once per swap rather than re-indexed. Minor.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.rationale: Reduces redundant array indexing in the partition swap; small constant-factor.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/SegmentTree.risk: Low impact; only worth it alongside the RangeTree change for consistency. Semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.summary: Computes Math.Sqrt for every one of the O(n^2) pairs; if S is used only for separation comparisons the sqrt can be deferred or avoided.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.currentCost: Inner loop runs Math.Sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy) for all n(n-1)/2 pairs. sqrt is ~15-20+ cycle latency and serializes the loop; for n=1000 that is ~500k sqrts.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.proposedChange: If downstream consumers compare/threshold distances, store squared distance (dx*dx+dy*dy) in S and compare against squared thresholds, eliminating sqrt entirely. If the true distance is required, at least the loop is embarrassingly parallel — structure dx/dy as SoA spans so Burst can vectorize the multiply-add, and only sqrt the surviving pairs.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.rationale: Dropping sqrt removes the dominant per-pair latency in an O(n^2) kernel; squared-distance comparisons are monotonic so thresholding is exact without the root.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.risk: Changing S to squared distance changes the observable field value — only valid if all consumers are updated to expect squared (state guard: confirm no caller reads S as Euclidean distance). If S must remain true distance, keep sqrt but vectorize.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.summary: This is a brute-force all-pairs enumeration (O(n^2) pairs), not a Well-Separated Pair Decomposition, which produces O(n) pairs via a split-tree.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.currentCost: Emits every pair: count = n(n-1)/2 = O(n^2) pairs and O(n^2) work and output RAM. A real WSPD over a fair-split tree yields O(n) pairs for fixed separation s in O(n log n) build time.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.proposedChange: Implement the actual WSPD: build a fair-split / kd tree, then recursively emit well-separated node pairs using the separation ratio s, producing O(s^d * n) pairs. This matches the class name Wspd and slashes both time and the pairs[] output size from quadratic to near-linear.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.rationale: Genuine asymptotic improvement (O(n^2)->O(n log n) time, O(n^2)->O(n) output) and correct WSPD semantics; the separation parameter s is currently stored but never used to prune, confirming the current code is a placeholder.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Wspd.cs.risk: Large algorithmic change and changes output (set of pairs and their meaning) — flag for owner. Current code ignores s for pruning, so output differs from a true WSPD; treat as feature-completion, not a behavior-preserving micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.summary: Allocates four full-size stackalloc child buffers (4*count ints) at every recursion level, compounding stack along the deepest path.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.currentCost: Lines 83-86 stackalloc c0..c3 each of size `count` ints = 16*count bytes per frame. Along a recursion path these live frames sum; with degenerate splits (all points to one quadrant) the deepest path can allocate ~16*count bytes at many levels, a mobile stack-overflow risk and heavy stack touching.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.proposedChange: Partition in place into the existing indices buffer using counting/offsets (compute the 4 quadrant counts, prefix-sum to 4 offsets, scatter into a single shared scratch of size count, then recurse on contiguous sub-ranges) — mirrors the Octree PartitionOctants pattern. One scratch buffer of size n total instead of 4*count per frame.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.rationale: Cuts scratch from 4*count-per-frame to a single n-sized buffer reused across the recursion, removing the quadratic-ish stack growth and improving cache locality of the index stream.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.risk: Must compute quadrant of each point once and reuse for scatter (store a 2-bit/byte tag) to keep one pass; partition is consumed before child recursion so a shared buffer is safe. Semantics-preserving if quadrant test matches lines 91-94 exactly (note the <= / > boundary handling).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.summary: Quadrant classification uses an if/else-if chain that re-tests xs[p]<=midX and ys[p]<=midY redundantly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.currentCost: Lines 91-94: the chain tests (x<=midX && y<=midY), then (x>midX && y<=midY), then (x<=midX && y>midY). xs[p] and ys[p] are loaded and compared to midX/midY up to 2-3 times per point across the branch chain.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.proposedChange: Compute each comparison once: `int q = (xs[p] > midX ? 1 : 0) | (ys[p] > midY ? 2 : 0);` then index by q (0..3) to select the child bucket, matching the branchless GetOctIdx pattern already used in Octree.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.rationale: One load+compare per axis per point and a branchless bucket index instead of a re-testing if/else cascade; consistent with the Octree design and friendlier to Burst.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.risk: Must map q to the same buckets as the original: original c0 = (x<=midX,y<=midY), c1=(x>midX,y<=midY), c2=(x<=midX,y>midY), c3=(x>midX,y>midY). With q = (x>midX)|((y>midY)<<1) the mapping is exactly c[q]; boundary (<= vs >) preserved. Semantics-identical.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.summary: AggressiveInlining on the recursive BuildRecursive and on Build is ineffective and may bloat code.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.currentCost: BuildRecursive (line 42) is self-recursive; the JIT/Burst cannot inline a recursive method, so the attribute is a no-op at best and can mislead. Build itself is large and called once per tree, so inlining yields no benefit.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.proposedChange: Remove [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] from BuildRecursive and from the top-level Build/Build2D/Build3D entry points across these files; reserve it for small hot leaf helpers (GetOctIdx-style) only.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.rationale: Avoids code-size bloat / icache pressure from forcing inline on large or recursive methods where it cannot help; keeps inlining where it actually reduces call overhead (leaf classifiers).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Spatial/Quadtree.cs.risk: Purely an attribute cleanup; no semantic change. Verify no caller depends on inlining for a measured win (none expected for build entry points).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.summary: Restart ear search from the removed vertex instead of from index 0 each iteration; track a clip count instead of re-evaluating the whole polygon repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.currentCost: After every ear is clipped, the for-loop restarts at i=0 and re-tests already-rejected vertices via IsEar (which itself is O(activeCount)). Combined with maxIterations = activeCount*activeCount, the worst-case is O(n^3) point-in-triangle tests, and the common case re-scans a large prefix of still-reflex vertices every clip.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.proposedChange: After clipping vertex i, do not `break` back to i=0. Continue scanning from the neighborhood of the removed vertex (a single pass index that wraps), and bound total work by a counter of consecutive failed ear tests equal to activeCount (no ear in a full lap -> bail). This keeps the same outputs (first-found ear at each step in scan order is unchanged when you resume at the same position) but removes the repeated rescans of the leading reflex run.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.rationale: Standard ear-clipping resumes near the modified vertex because removing an ear only changes the convex/reflex status of its two neighbors. Re-testing the whole prefix each time is wasted work; resuming locally turns the typical case from O(n^2)-with-large-constant rescans into far fewer IsEar calls without changing which triangle list is produced for convex-scan order.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.risk: Output order of triangles can change if you resume at a different scan position; to PRESERVE the exact current triangle list, keep resuming the scan at the same vertex position the ear was found (i clamped into the shrunk array) rather than at 0 — that yields the identical first-found-ear sequence the current code produces, just without re-scanning [0..i). Verify against existing NUnit tests.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.summary: Eliminate the O(n) array shift on each ear removal by using a doubly-linked-list of indices in the stackalloc buffer.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.currentCost: On every successful ear, the inner `for (k=i; k<activeCount-1; k++) activeIndices[k]=activeIndices[k+1]` shifts up to activeCount elements, i.e. O(n) memmove per clip, O(n^2) total just for compaction.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.proposedChange: Replace the compacted array with prev[]/next[] arrays (two int* stackalloc of size mergedCount) forming a circular linked list. Removing vertex v becomes next[prev[v]]=next[v]; prev[next[v]]=prev[v] — O(1). Iterate via next[] pointers. activeCount is a simple decrement.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.rationale: Removing the per-clip O(n) shift drops total compaction cost from O(n^2) to O(n). The neighbor lookups (prev/next) also become array reads instead of `(i-1+activeCount)%activeCount` and `(i+1)%activeCount` modulo ops, removing a div from the hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.risk: More stackalloc (2*mergedCount ints) — bounded and small, still within the no-managed-alloc constraint. Must keep IsEar's containment scan iterating over the live list (follow next[] for activeCount steps) so the same vertices are tested; output triangle order must be validated identical against tests since traversal order is preserved.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.summary: Only run the expensive IsValidBridge check on the closest candidate(s), not on every pair that beats the running min distance.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.currentCost: The double loop is O(mergedCount * holeSize) distance evals, and for every pair whose distSq < current min it calls IsValidBridge, which is itself O(mergedCount + holeSize) segment-intersection tests. Early in the scan minDistSq drops frequently, so IsValidBridge runs many times: worst case O(mergedCount * holeSize * (mergedCount + holeSize)).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.proposedChange: First pass: find the globally-nearest (outer,hole) pair by distance only (no bridge test) — pure O(mergedCount*holeSize), no early IsValidBridge. Then validate that single best bridge; if it fails, fall back to scanning remaining pairs in increasing-distance order validating until one passes. This reduces IsValidBridge invocations from potentially O(mergedCount*holeSize) down to ~1 in the common (non-degenerate) case.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.rationale: Bridge validity rarely fails for the nearest pair in well-formed polygons, so deferring the O(n) intersection test until after the cheap distance minimization avoids the vast majority of intersection sweeps. Same chosen bridge for the common case; identical final result.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.risk: Tie-breaking: the current code picks the first pair (in i,j scan order) achieving the strict-min that also passes IsValidBridge; a deferred scheme can select a different valid bridge when multiple pairs share equal/near distance, changing the merged polygon and thus triangle output. To preserve semantics exactly, only skip IsValidBridge for pairs that cannot become the strict minimum (distSq >= current best); pairs that DO lower the min must still be validated in the same order — so the safe form keeps the early-out `if (distSq < minDistSq)` but is otherwise unchanged. The fully-deferred form is a behavior change and must be gated/tested.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.summary: Hoist edge-vector subtractions out of PointInTriangle's per-point loop by precomputing the triangle's three edge directions once per ear test.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.currentCost: PointInTriangle recomputes Direction(p,a,b), Direction(p,b,c), Direction(p,c,a) for every active vertex p. Each Direction does 2 subtractions + 2 mults + 1 sub. The triangle vertices a,b,c are constant across the whole containment loop, yet the cross-product is recomputed from scratch each call.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.proposedChange: Precompute edge vectors e_ab=(b-a), e_bc=(c-b), e_ca=(a-c) once in IsEar before the loop. Inside the loop compute the sign tests as cross(e_ab, p-a), cross(e_bc, p-b), cross(e_ca, p-c). This reuses the constant edge deltas and only varies (p - vertex) per iteration, shaving redundant subtractions of the fixed endpoints.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.rationale: Removes recomputation of the constant edge differences (b-a etc.) for every interior-point test; in a near-convex polygon the containment loop runs ~activeCount times per ear, so the saved subtractions accumulate. Burst vectorizes the per-point (p - vertex) float2 ops well.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.risk: Must keep the exact same Epsilon comparison semantics (d1<-Epsilon / d>Epsilon) and the same multiplication/subtraction ordering to avoid float rounding differences that could flip a borderline containment result. Reorder must reproduce identical float expression `(dx)*(dy2)-(dy)*(dx2)` term-for-term to be bit-identical; if exact bit-reproduction isn't guaranteed, mark as a numeric-tolerance change and validate.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.summary: Replace the `(i+1)%count` wrap with a rolling 'previous point' variable to drop the modulo and one vertex re-load per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.currentCost: Loop does `next=(i+1)%count` (an integer division each iteration) plus two indexed vertex loads (vertices[indices[i]] and vertices[indices[next]]); consecutive iterations re-load the same point twice.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.proposedChange: Carry currPt across iterations (seed with the last vertex as the initial 'prev'), compute the shoelace term against the stored previous point, and avoid the modulo by handling the wrap once. Each iteration then does one new load instead of two and no division.
