src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.rationale: Removes a div and halves the vertex loads in the signed-area sweep. Pure constant-factor win but the sum is identical (shoelace is order-independent on which adjacent pair, just keep the same pairing).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.risk: Floating-point summation order must stay identical to keep the same accumulated `area` value and thus the same `area < 0` result on borderline (near-degenerate) polygons. Keep the addition order i=0..count-1 with the same (next - curr)*(next + curr) term to remain bit-identical.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.summary: Strength-reduce the `(i+1)%mergedCount`, `(j+1)%holeSize`, `(bestHole+k)%holeSize` modulo wraps in hot loops to a compare-and-reset.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.currentCost: These loops do an integer division (`%`) every iteration purely to wrap the last index back to 0; division is multi-cycle and serializes the dependency chain on each segment test.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.proposedChange: Use `int next = i + 1; if (next == count) next = 0;` (branch predicts perfectly — taken once per loop) instead of `% count`. For the `(bestHole + k) % holeSize` copy loop, maintain a running index that decrements/wraps once.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.rationale: A predictable single branch (mispredicted at most once per loop) is cheaper than an integer division every iteration on both PC and mobile ARM where idiv is slow. Indices are always in [0,count), so the conditional reset is exactly equivalent to the modulo.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Triangulation/EarCl.risk: None for non-negative operands — `i+1` is always in [1,count] so `==count -> 0` reproduces `%count` exactly. No signed-negative concern here since all operands are non-negative. (Do NOT apply a similar &-mask trick: counts are not power-of-two.)

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.summary: Build is O(n^4): O(n^3) candidate triangles each checked against all n points. The InCircle test loop dominates and is fully redundant for the vast majority of triangles.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.currentCost: Three nested loops over n produce ~n^3/6 triangles, and IsDelaunay scans all n points per triangle => O(n^4) double-precision cross/incircle work. For n=200 that is ~5.3e9 InCircle evaluations.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.proposedChange: Replace the brute-force generator with an incremental/Bowyer-Watson or divide-and-conquer Delaunay (O(n log n) expected). If the brute-force form must stay, at minimum break IsDelaunay early (already does) and skip InCircle when t lies outside the triangle's axis-aligned bounding box (precompute min/max x,y of u,v,w once and test before the full predicate).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.rationale: Lowering asymptotics from O(n^4) to O(n log n) is the single largest possible win here; even a bbox pre-filter removes the majority of 8-mul/6-sub InCircle calls because most of the n points are far from any given small triangle.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.risk: Full algorithm swap changes code substantially but preserves the output triangle set for non-degenerate inputs; the bbox pre-filter is exactly semantics-preserving (a point outside the triangle bbox can still be inside the circumcircle, so the bbox test must only be used to skip points that are also provably outside the circumcircle — therefore reject bbox-skip as unsafe; keep only the algorithmic swap or accept it as not equivalent). Mark bbox-skip as INVALID; recommend only the asymptotic replacement.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.summary: The `if (TryAddTriangle(...)) { }` empty-body call in Build discards the return value and reads as dead code; TryAddTriangle mutates cnt via ref as its real effect.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.currentCost: An empty if-statement guard adds a branch the JIT/Burst must prove dead; reduces readability of the hot triple loop.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.proposedChange: Call TryAddTriangle as a statement (drop the `if (...) {}`) or rename to a void AddTriangleIfDelaunay since the bool is unused by the caller. Keeps cnt-by-ref semantics identical.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.rationale: Removes a no-op branch from the innermost loop body and clarifies that the side effect (cnt increment) is the contract, aiding Burst's branch elimination.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.risk: None; the return value is already ignored, so behavior is identical.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.summary: xs[i],ys[i],xs[j],ys[j],xs[k],ys[k] are reloaded from memory repeatedly across TryAddTriangle and the IsDelaunay loop; the three triangle vertices are loop-invariant for the entire inner n-scan.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.currentCost: Each InCircle call re-indexes xs[u],ys[u],xs[v],ys[v],xs[w],ys[w] (6 pointer loads) per t; over the n-loop that is 6n redundant loads of values that never change.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.proposedChange: Hoist xu=xs[u], yu=ys[u], ... once before the IsDelaunay loop and pass scalars into InCircle, so only xs[t],ys[t] are reloaded per iteration. Equivalently inline the three vertex coords as locals in IsDelaunay.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.rationale: Cuts per-iteration memory traffic from 8 loads to 2, shortening the dependency chain feeding the predicate and improving Burst vectorization/register allocation.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Delaunay.cs.risk: None; values are read-only during the scan, pure data movement.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Fortune.cs.summary: Fortune.Build is a non-functional skeleton: it copies inputs to outputs and returns n with no Voronoi/sort logic, despite AggressiveInlining and an O(N log N) claim in comments.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Fortune.cs.currentCost: Ships an inlined no-op that misleads callers (returns vertices == input points) and the [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] forces a copy loop to be inlined into every caller with zero benefit.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Fortune.cs.proposedChange: Either implement the actual sweep or drop AggressiveInlining (a loop-of-n copy should never be force-inlined) and mark the method clearly as unimplemented. If kept as a passthrough, replace the manual copy loop with two Buffer.MemoryCopy calls for xs->outX and ys->outY.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Fortune.cs.rationale: Buffer.MemoryCopy on blittable doubles is a single vectorized memcpy versus an element-wise scalar loop; removing AggressiveInlining avoids code-bloat at call sites for a non-hot copy.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/Fortune.cs.risk: MemoryCopy preserves exact bytes for the n doubles; behavior identical. Removing AggressiveInlining has no observable effect.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.summary: BuildKD calls a full QuickSort over [left,right] at every recursion level, making construction O(n log^2 n) at best and O(n^2 log n) worst-case; only the median (nth element) is actually needed.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.currentCost: QuickSort sorts the entire subrange to find one median, then recurses; each level re-sorts already-partially-sorted data. Worst case (sorted/duplicate-heavy input) degrades to O(n^2) per level due to last-element pivot.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.proposedChange: Replace QuickSort+take-middle with quickselect (nth_element / introselect) to partition around the median in expected O(subrange) without fully sorting; this yields O(n log n) total build. Also use median-of-three or randomized pivot to avoid the O(n^2) adversarial case on sorted input.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.rationale: Median selection is O(m) expected vs O(m log m) for a full sort; summed over the recursion tree this drops build cost by a log factor and removes the catastrophic sorted-input blowup from the fixed last-element pivot.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.risk: Quickselect leaves the subrange unsorted except the partition invariant, which is exactly what BuildKD needs (it only reads pts[mid] and recurses on the two halves). Median index choice must match left+(right-left)/2. Randomized pivot makes build nondeterministic in element order but the resulting tree's correctness (nearest-neighbor results) is unaffected; if determinism is required, use median-of-three instead of randomization.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.summary: The comparison axis `(depth % 2 == 0)` is recomputed for every element in the partition loop although depth is constant for the whole call.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.currentCost: A modulo (or its branch) plus a select per inner-loop iteration; for m elements that is m redundant depth%2 evaluations, and the branch inside the hot loop hinders vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.proposedChange: Compute `bool byX = (depth & 1) == 0;` once before the loop and branch on it; or better, hoist the axis test out of the loop entirely by writing two specialized loop bodies (compare .X vs compare .Y) selected once. Replace `% 2` with `& 1` regardless.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.rationale: depth & 1 is a single AND vs a div-based modulo; hoisting the constant axis decision out of the loop removes a per-iteration branch and lets Burst vectorize each comparison branch cleanly.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.risk: depth is non-negative so `& 1` equals `% 2` exactly. Hoisting the boolean is pure; specializing the two loops preserves identical comparisons.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.summary: nodes[node].Left and nodes[node].Right are reloaded multiple times (DistToBox arg, comparison, and SearchIfBetter arg), and DistToBox re-reads the whole child node struct after node!=-1 was already implied.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.currentCost: Repeated `nodes[node].Left/.Right` indexed loads (KDNode is 56 bytes; .Left/.Right live at offsets that may straddle cache lines) and a redundant node!=-1 reload chain per recursion.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.proposedChange: Cache `int l = nodes[node].Left; int r = nodes[node].Right;` once at the top of SearchNearest and pass those locals to DistToBox/SearchIfBetter. Read the current node into a local KDNode (or a ref) once instead of re-indexing nodes[node] in UpdateBest, DistToBox, and the comparisons.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.rationale: Reduces repeated 56-byte-struct pointer indexing and shortens dependency chains in the recursive hot path; helps register allocation in Burst.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.risk: None; nodes are immutable during search, so caching child indices and the node struct is semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.summary: KDNode stores X,Y redundantly with the point AND four bounds doubles (MinX/MinY/MaxX/MaxY); the struct is 56 bytes, hurting cache density during traversal where only X,Y,Left,Right and bounds-for-pruning are touched.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.currentCost: 56 bytes/node means ~1.14 nodes per 64-byte cache line; nearest-neighbor descent touches X,Y,Left,Right (UpdateBest+children) on the way down and bounds only when deciding to recurse, so every node access pulls bounds it may not need.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.proposedChange: Consider splitting hot fields (X,Y,Idx,Left,Right = 28 bytes) from cold bounds into a parallel array (SoA), so the descent walks a denser hot array and only loads bounds when DistToBox is actually called. Alternatively store bounds as float if the precision budget allows (halves bounds footprint).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.rationale: Smaller hot stride => more nodes per cache line => fewer misses on the pointer-chasing descent, the dominant cost of KD search on large point sets.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/NearestNeig.risk: SoA split changes the API/layout (callers build nodes differently) — an ergonomics/breaking-change tradeoff, flag as design-level. float bounds change pruning precision: DistToBox would compare a slightly looser/tighter box distance, which can change which subtrees are pruned and thus is NOT guaranteed semantics-preserving for ties; reject float-bounds unless exact-double results are not contractual. SoA split with double bounds IS semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.summary: Dijkstra uses a lazy binary heap that pushes a new node on every relaxation without decrease-key, so the heap can grow to O(E) entries; combined with the stale-entry skip this is correct but does extra heap work.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.currentCost: Each successful relaxation does a fresh Push (O(log heapSize)) and the heap may hold up to E nodes, so pq must be sized E and Pop discards stale entries (the `top.Dist > dist[top.V]` continue).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.proposedChange: This lazy approach is the standard pointer-free choice and is fine; the only concrete win is documenting the required pq capacity (E+1) and short-circuiting Push when nd >= current best-known dist[dst] (goal-bounded pruning) since Run has a dst. Optionally stop pushing nodes whose tentative dist already exceeds dist[dst].
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.rationale: Goal-bounded pruning skips heap insertions for paths already longer than the best known to dst, reducing heap operations on graphs where dst is found early.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.risk: Pruning on nd >= dist[dst] is only valid with non-negative weights (true for Euclidean visibility weights) and only after dst has been settled; before dst is reached dist[dst] is MaxValue so the prune is inert. Must keep weights non-negative; flag this assumption.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.summary: Heap sift uses explicit Swap (3 moves per step) while sifting; a hole-based sift (carry the moving element, shift the path, write once) halves memory writes per level.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.currentCost: Each sift level executes Swap = 3 struct copies (PQNode is 16 bytes => 48 bytes moved/level). Over log n levels that is 3 log n copies of the moving node.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.proposedChange: Replace swap-based sift-up/sift-down with hole-based: hold the inserted/replacement PQNode in a register, shift parents/children into the hole, and write the held node once at the final position. Also `(i-1)/2` and `2*i+1/2*i+2` are already shift-friendly; leave as-is (compiler lowers to shifts).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.rationale: Hole-based heap moves the carried element once instead of swapping at every level, reducing 16-byte struct copies by ~2x in the heap hot path that dominates Dijkstra.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.risk: None functionally; standard heap transformation preserving the exact same node ordering and pop sequence (ties resolved identically as long as comparisons stay <= / <).

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.summary: Run returns dist[dst] after the loop, but if dst is unreachable dist[dst] stays double.MaxValue; the early `top.V == dst` return is good, but the trailing return reads dist[dst] redundantly when the early return already covers the reachable case.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.currentCost: Negligible, but the design relies on InitializeGraph rebuilding the CSR adjacency from the COO edge list on every Run call (O(n+e) setup per query).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.proposedChange: If Run is called repeatedly on the same graph with different src/dst, split InitializeGraph's adjacency construction (head/next/toEdge/weight) from the per-query dist reset, so the CSR is built once and reused; only dist[] needs reinitializing per query. Expose a BuildAdjacency + RunOnPrebuilt pair.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.rationale: Avoids rebuilding the entire edge adjacency O(e) on every shortest-path query, which is pure repeated work when the graph is static across queries (the common Voronoi/visibility-graph use case).
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/ShortestPat.risk: API change (ergonomics). Behavior identical per call; the split must reset dist[] each query to MaxValue. Flag as an API addition, not a replacement, to preserve the existing one-shot Run.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.summary: Build is O(n^3): O(n^2) vertex pairs, each IsVisible scans all n polygon edges; plus IsVisible calls IsInside (another O(n)) per pair.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.currentCost: n^2/2 pairs x (n edge-intersection tests + n-point-in-polygon test) => ~n^3 SegmentsIntersect/Dir evaluations with 4 Dir (4 mul,2 sub each) per intersection test.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.proposedChange: For the segment-intersection sweep this is near the practical floor for a naive visibility graph, but the per-pair IsInside midpoint test is redundant work that can be folded: the `Math.Abs(j-i)==1 || (i==0 && j==n-1)` polygon-edge check is cheap and should be tested FIRST (short-circuit before the O(n) IsInside). Currently IsInside is evaluated even for adjacent polygon edges that are trivially visible.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.rationale: Reordering the `||` so the O(1) adjacency tests run before the O(n) IsInside call skips a full point-in-polygon scan for the ~n polygon-boundary edges and any pair where adjacency already proves visibility; C# || short-circuits, so this is a pure reordering win.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.risk: None: || is short-circuit, the three operands are side-effect-free, and OR is commutative for booleans, so result is identical while skipping IsInside whenever an adjacency test is already true.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.summary: ox[i],oy[i],ox[j],oy[j] are loaded into x1..y2 (good), but the midpoint visibility/IsInside is computed even when an earlier SegmentsIntersect already returned false-positive paths; also Dist in Build recomputes sqrt for every edge.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.currentCost: Per visible pair, Dist does a Math.Sqrt; the edge weight could in some consumers be kept squared. More concretely, the k-loop recomputes (k+1==n)?0:k+1 wrap each iteration and re-reads ox[k],oy[k] twice.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.proposedChange: Cache ox[k],oy[k] into locals once per k iteration (used by SegmentsIntersect args). Keep the wrap index but compute it via branchless `kn = k+1; if (kn==n) kn=0;` (already minimal). Leave Dist's sqrt unless the consumer (ShortestPath) can operate on squared weights — it cannot, since Dijkstra sums edge lengths, so sqrt is required; do not remove it.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.rationale: Caching ox[k]/oy[k] removes duplicate pointer indexing feeding SegmentsIntersect; the sqrt is genuinely needed for additive path costs so flagging it as keep avoids a cargo-cult removal.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.risk: Caching is pure. Explicitly NOT removing sqrt because squared distances are non-additive and would break Dijkstra correctness in ShortestPath.

src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.summary: IsInside performs a division per edge inside the crossing test, and adds a 1e-12 epsilon to the denominator on every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.currentCost: One double division per polygon edge per call; division is ~10-20x the latency of a multiply and is on the O(n) point-in-polygon hot path called O(n^2) times from IsVisible.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.proposedChange: Rewrite the crossing test to avoid division using the standard sign-comparison form: instead of `x < (ox[l]-ox[k])*(y-oy[k])/(oy[l]-oy[k]) + ox[k]`, cross-multiply by (oy[l]-oy[k]) and flip the inequality based on the sign of the denominator. This removes the divide and the epsilon hack.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.rationale: Cross-multiplied ray-casting eliminates a per-edge division (replaced by a multiply and a sign-dependent compare), substantially cheaper on the O(n^3)-reached inner test.
src/IAFahim.Geometry.Voronoi/VisibilityG.risk: Cross-multiplication changes behavior at the exact epsilon-guarded degenerate case (horizontal edges where oy[l]==oy[k]); the original `+1e-12` avoids div-by-zero, but the `(oy[k]>y)!=(oy[l]>y)` guard already excludes horizontal edges from the test, so the denominator is provably non-zero there and the epsilon is inert — making the division safe to replace exactly. Must preserve the inequality direction by branching on sign(oy[l]-oy[k]); verify tie-handling (strict < vs <=) matches original.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.summary: Fuse the three sequential init loops over [0,n) into one loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.currentCost: Three separate full passes over n elements (tin, low, isArticulation), three loop-counter setups and three traversals of the same index range, with poor locality since the three arrays are distinct.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.proposedChange: Replace the three loops with a single `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { tin[i] = 0; low[i] = 0; isArticulation[i] = 0; }`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.rationale: One loop instead of three removes two branch/counter overheads per element fold and lets the compiler keep `i` in a single induction register; the stores still hit three arrays but the loop bookkeeping is amortized once. low[] does not even need zeroing for correctness (it is always written by Dfs before being read since tin[u]=low[u]=++timer runs first), so the low loop could be dropped entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.risk: low[] is set in Dfs before any read, so zeroing it is dead work; removing it is safe only because every reachable vertex gets visited (the outer loop covers all components). Keep zeroing tin and isArticulation. No semantic change from fusing.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.summary: Collapse the two dependent `low[v]` comparisons against tin[u] into a nested branch to avoid re-comparing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.currentCost: After the recursive call, the code does `if (low[v] > tin[u])` then independently `if (low[v] >= tin[u] && p != -1)`. Two compares of the same pair low[v]/tin[u] plus a separate p!=-1 test on every tree edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.proposedChange: Load `int lv = low[v]; int tu = tin[u];` once, then `if (lv >= tu) { if (lv > tu) { bridgesU[bridgeCount]=u; bridgesV[bridgeCount]=v; bridgeCount++; } if (p != -1) isArticulation[u] = 1; }`. Also hoist `int hu = head[u]` and read tin[u]/low[u] into locals reused across the loop, writing low[u] back once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.rationale: Strict `>` implies `>=`, so nesting removes one redundant comparison on the common branch and shares the loaded operands, shortening the dependency chain. Caching tin[u]/low[u] in registers avoids repeated pointer dereferences of the same cell inside the hot edge loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/BridgeAndArtic.risk: Behavior identical: lv>tu still sets a bridge; lv>=tu with p!=-1 still sets articulation. Must write low[u] back to memory after the loop if cached, and re-read after the recursive call is unnecessary since recursion does not touch low[u] (only the caller does).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.summary: Fuse the three-array init loop and combine the leaves/isolated scan with degree computation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.currentCost: Init loop writes tin,low,comp in one pass (already fused) but comp degree pass plus a separate scan over compCount to count leaves/isolated is two passes over component data. Also degree[] is zeroed in its own loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.proposedChange: Zero degree[] inside the same allocation-adjacent loop, and after ComputeComponentDegrees the leaves/isolated counting loop is unavoidable, but `leaves / 2` and `(leaves + 1) / 2` divides by 2 on a provably non-negative int can be `leaves >> 1` and `(leaves + 1) >> 1`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.rationale: Signed `/2` emits an extra add-of-sign-bit sequence (test sign, conditionally add 1, then shift) because the compiler must round toward zero for negatives. leaves and isolated are counts (>=0), so `>>1` is one instruction and identical for non-negative operands.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.risk: Strength reduction `x/2 -> x>>1` only matches for x>=0; leaves is a count incremented from 0 so always >=0, and leaves+1>=1>=0. Safe. Burst/Roslyn may already do this; if leaves were ever negative the results would differ, but it cannot be.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.summary: Hoist comp[u] out of the inner edge loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.currentCost: Inner loop reads comp[u] on every edge via `comp[u] != comp[to[e]]` and `degree[comp[u]]++`, dereferencing comp[u] up to 3 times per edge though u is loop-invariant in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.proposedChange: In the outer loop body load `int cu = comp[u]; int hu = head[u];` once, then inner loop: `if (cu != comp[to[e]]) degree[cu]++;`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.rationale: comp[u] is invariant across the entire inner edge traversal; hoisting removes a load and an address computation per edge, and `degree[cu]` indexes off a register instead of re-loading comp[u]. Fewer cache touches of comp[] in the hot adjacency walk.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/Biconnectivity.risk: None: comp[u] and head[u] are not modified inside the inner loop. Pure hoist.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.summary: Convert recursive root-to-node push into an iterative two-phase walk to remove call overhead and stack growth.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.currentCost: PushAll recurses up to the splay-tree root before pushing down, one stack frame per ancestor. Called at the start of every Splay (the hottest LCT primitive), so recursion depth equals the access path length and adds call/return overhead per node on every splay.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.proposedChange: Walk up collecting the path into a stackalloc int buffer (sized to log-bounded splay depth, or reuse a caller-provided scratch), then PushDown in reverse order. Alternatively, since AggressiveInlining cannot inline self-recursion, an explicit loop removes the un-inlinable recursive call entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.rationale: Self-recursive methods are never inlined despite the attribute, so each PushAll level pays a real call. An iterative version keeps everything in one frame, shortens the dependency chain, and avoids per-frame prologue/epilogue. Same node visitation order is preserved (collect upward, apply downward).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.risk: Must preserve exact order: PushDown applied from topmost ancestor down to x (current recursion does parent-first then self). A stackalloc inside a hot leaf called per-splay could be costly if re-allocated; better to thread a reusable scratch pointer or bound with a fixed small buffer. Splay depth is amortized O(log n) but worst-case O(n); buffer must be sized n to stay safe, or keep recursion if stack scratch is unacceptable.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.summary: Pack the struct: the single `byte Rev` forces padding, inflating each node from a tight layout and worsening cache density.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.currentCost: Sequential layout is Parent,Left,Right (int x3 =12), Rev (byte), Val,Sum,LazyCover (int x3). The byte at offset 12 is followed by an int needing 4-byte alignment, so 3 bytes pad after Rev -> struct size 28 bytes with a wasted padding slot. With per-node random access in splay/access, fewer bytes per node means more nodes per cache line.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.proposedChange: Reorder so the byte sits at the end after all ints: Parent,Left,Right,Val,Sum,LazyCover (24 bytes) then byte Rev -> still padded to 28 for array stride, but consider folding Rev and LazyCover into a single byte flags field (Rev bit0, LazyCover bit1) reducing logical state and enabling 24-byte stride, or store Rev/LazyCover as bytes adjacent so both share the same padding window.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.rationale: Both Rev and LazyCover are 0/1 flags; merging them into one byte bitfield removes a 4-byte int (LazyCover) and clusters the flag byte, allowing a 24-byte struct (3 cache lines per 8 nodes vs current). Smaller stride = fewer cache misses in the pointer-chasing splay loop, which dominates LCT cost.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.risk: PushDown/ApplyCover/MakeRoot read/write Rev and LazyCover independently; bitfield merge requires masking (`flags & 1`, `flags ^= 1`, `flags |= 2`) which is cheap but must preserve the other bit. Rev^=1 toggling must mask to bit0 only. Verify no code assumes LazyCover is a full int. Blittability preserved (still unmanaged).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.summary: Redundant Splay(v) after Access(v) in the cycle branch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.currentCost: In the else branch: `Access(nodes, v); Splay(nodes, v);`. Access already ends with `Splay(nodes, u)` on its argument (Access splays its parameter as its final step), so v is already at the root of its splay tree; the explicit Splay(v) repeats work.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.proposedChange: Remove the explicit `Splay(nodes, v)` line; Access(v) already leaves v splayed (root of its auxiliary tree) so nodes[v].Sum is valid.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.rationale: Access's final statement is `Splay(nodes, u)` on the accessed node, guaranteeing v is splayed to the top with PushUp applied. The second Splay is a no-op walk plus a PushAll/PushUp pass, pure overhead on every cycle-closing edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Bridges/DynamicBridges.risk: Must confirm Access(v) leaves v as the splay-root with Sum aggregated over the represented root path to v — it does, since the loop's final Splay(u) and PushUp establish that. If any future change makes Access not splay its argument, this breaks. Behavior currently identical; low risk but verify against the LCT invariant that Sum on v reflects the whole path.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.summary: FindCentroid is purely tail-recursive (it returns the recursive call directly); convert to an iterative while-loop to eliminate call-frame overhead and unbounded stack growth.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.currentCost: Each descent step is a full method call: spill/reload of 9 pointer/int arguments, return-address push, and a frame that the JIT/Burst may not tail-call-optimize. On a centroid path the descent can be O(depth) frames deep.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.proposedChange: Replace the body with: keep p,u as locals; in an outer `while(true)` loop scan edges of u, and on finding the heavy child set p=u, u=v, and `continue` the outer loop instead of recursing; if no heavy child found, `return u;`. No recursion at all.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.rationale: Removes one call frame per descent level: fewer pushed/popped registers, no return-address management, and bounded O(1) stack. Burst/JIT cannot be relied on to perform tail-call elimination, so doing it by hand is a guaranteed win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.risk: None to semantics — identical descent order and return value. Pure mechanical transform of a tail call.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant `total / 2` out of the edge loop and drop the redundant `sz[v] > 0` test.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.currentCost: `total / 2` (an IDIV-class op on signed int) is recomputed on every edge iteration inside the for-loop, and `sz[v] > 0` is evaluated as a separate branch on every edge even though it is implied by `sz[v] > total/2`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int half = total / 2;` (or `int half = total >> 1;`) once before the loop, then test only `if (v != p && removed[v] == 0 && sz[v] > half)`. Drop `sz[v] > 0` entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.rationale: One division instead of degree-many divisions per node; one fewer branch per edge. `sz[v] > 0` is dead: every non-removed reachable node has sz>=1 after ComputeSizes, and `sz[v] > total/2` with total>=0 already implies sz[v]>=1, so removing it changes nothing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.risk: `total >> 1` equals `total / 2` only for non-negative total; total is a subtree size and always >= 1 here, so the shift is safe, but keeping `/ 2` is equally correct and avoids any signedness doubt. The `sz[v] > 0` removal relies on sizes being >= 1, which the algorithm guarantees.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.summary: Remove the unused `temp`/`int*` parameter (and the unused `n` parameter) threaded through ComputeSizes and FindCentroid.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.currentCost: `temp` is never read or written in ComputeSizes or FindCentroid, yet it is passed on every recursive call, consuming an argument register/stack slot per frame. `Build` allocates `int tempStorage` and `Decompose` passes `&n` purely to satisfy the signature. `n` is likewise unused by both recursive helpers.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.proposedChange: Delete the `int* temp` parameter from ComputeSizes and FindCentroid (and remove `int tempStorage`/`&n` at the call sites). Also drop the unused `int n` parameter from both helpers since neither references it.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.rationale: Fewer arguments per recursive call means fewer registers spilled/restored and a smaller frame in the hottest loops of the module, plus a cleaner, less error-prone API (the current `&n` aliasing in Decompose is a latent footgun if temp ever becomes live).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.risk: None — both parameters are provably dead in the called bodies. Pure signature cleanup; observable behavior unchanged. Public Build/Decompose signatures need not change if desired, but the internal helpers should shed the dead params.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.summary: ComputeSizes and Decompose recurse to O(tree-depth); on degenerate (path-like) trees this is O(n) deep and can overflow the stack on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.currentCost: ComputeSizes recurses one frame per tree node along the deepest path. A linear chain of n nodes yields n nested frames; on constrained mobile stacks this risks a hard crash, and deep recursion also thrashes the stack cache.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.proposedChange: Replace ComputeSizes with an explicit-stack post-order traversal using a stackalloc'd `int*` (parent/iterator stack) sized to n, accumulating sz[u] on pop. Decompose can similarly use an explicit work stack of subtree roots instead of recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.rationale: Converts unbounded native-call-stack usage into bounded, caller-controlled scratch memory with O(1) frame overhead, removing the stack-overflow failure mode and giving predictable memory cost — important for a Burst/mobile target.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.risk: Higher implementation complexity and needs an n-sized scratch buffer (caller-supplied or stackalloc); must preserve the exact post-order accumulation so sz values match. Only worth it if deep/degenerate trees are in scope; for shallow balanced trees the current recursion is fine.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.summary: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to the leaf helpers once they are de-recursed, and note the unused using.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.currentCost: `using System;` and the AggressiveInlining import are present but no method is annotated; while recursive, inlining is pointless, but after FindCentroid becomes a loop it is a small pure leaf worth inlining into Build/Decompose.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.proposedChange: Once FindCentroid is iterative, mark it (and the size helper if iterative) with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]; remove the unused `using System;`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.rationale: Inlining a small loop body into Build/Decompose removes a call boundary and lets Burst keep pointer args in registers across the fused region. Dropping the unused namespace import is a trivial cleanliness win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Centroid/Centroid.cs.risk: Inlining a recursive method is rejected by the compiler, so this must follow the de-recursion change; otherwise no effect. Negligible risk.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Decrement.summary: Type dispatch uses if/else-if on a small dense int set; an unhandled type silently no-ops.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Decrement.currentCost: Two sequential branch comparisons (==0 then ==1) per query iteration; documents nothing about type 2+.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Decrement.proposedChange: Keep the branch structure (it is already minimal), but reorder so the more frequent query path is tested first if profiling shows query-heavy workloads, or leave as-is. No code change strictly needed; the main observation is the silent no-op for type>1 is by design under 'unchecked Run'.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Decrement.rationale: Branch order can matter for predictor warmup, but with only two arms and data-dependent types the win is negligible. This is essentially already optimal.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Decrement.risk: None; reordering arms is semantics-preserving only if exactly one arm matches per type, which holds.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.summary: Depth-limited reachability is a recursive DFS with no visited set, so it re-expands shared subgraphs exponentially (O(branching^maxDepth)).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.currentCost: A node reachable via multiple paths within maxDepth is re-explored once per path; worst case is exponential in maxDepth, and there is no memoization of 'already proven unreachable within remaining budget'.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.proposedChange: Replace with an explicit-stack/queue BFS bounded by maxDepth using a caller-provided visited bitset (byte* or ulong* seen, plus a best-remaining-depth array so a node visited with greater remaining budget can be revisited). Signature becomes Run(int* head,int* next,int* to,int u,int v,int maxDepth, int* bestDepth) where bestDepth[node] stores the max remaining depth a node was reached with, initialized to -1. Skip a node when bestDepth[node] >= remainingDepth. This bounds work to O(V+E) per query instead of exponential.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.rationale: Pruning re-expansion collapses exponential blowup to linear in reachable subgraph size; on dense or highly connected graphs this is the dominant cost. BFS with explicit stack also removes deep recursion (stack-overflow risk) and is Burst-friendlier than recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.risk: Requires an extra caller-allocated buffer (changes API/RAM). The bestDepth pruning preserves the 'reachable within maxDepth' answer exactly because revisiting only with strictly greater remaining budget can never miss a shorter path. If keeping recursion, at minimum convert tail to iterative to avoid stack-depth issues on mobile.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.summary: Recursive call defeats Burst inlining and risks deep call stacks on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.currentCost: Self-recursion cannot be inlined; each level pushes a full frame; AggressiveInlining on a recursive method is a no-op.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.proposedChange: Convert to an iterative DFS using a stackalloc/caller-provided int* stack of (node,depth) pairs. Drop AggressiveInlining since it cannot apply to recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.rationale: Iterative traversal eliminates per-frame prologue/epilogue cost and lets Burst optimize a flat loop; also removes mobile stack-overflow exposure for large maxDepth.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicRe.risk: Need a bounded scratch stack sized to maxDepth*maxBranching worst case; same traversal order can be preserved by using LIFO. Semantics preserved.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.summary: Init fills an n*n byte matrix with a per-element branch (i==j) instead of bulk-zeroing then setting the diagonal.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.currentCost: n*n iterations each with a branch and a recomputed i*n+j index; the inner j-loop recomputes i*n each iteration unless the compiler hoists it.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.proposedChange: Use Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(reach, 0, (uint)(n*n)) to zero the whole matrix in one vectorized memset, then a single loop 'for(int i=0;i<n;i++) reach[i*n+i]=1;' to set the diagonal. Replace inner index i*n+j by maintaining a running 'int row=i*n;' pointer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.rationale: Bulk memset is SIMD/rep-stos fast and branchless; the diagonal pass is O(n) instead of folding a branch into all n^2 elements. Removes n^2 conditional moves and the multiply from the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.risk: InitBlock requires byte fill value semantics (0 is fine). Behavior identical: zero everywhere then diagonal=1 equals (i==j) pattern.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.summary: AddEdge recomputes the row base index i*n / v*n inside hot loops and uses byte comparisons that prevent wide vectorization of the inner OR-merge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.currentCost: Inner loop indexes reach[i*n+j] and reach[v*n+j] recomputing bases each element; the j-loop is a scalar byte conditional store that Burst struggles to vectorize because of the branch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.proposedChange: Hoist 'byte* rowV = reach + v*n;' once before the i-loop, and 'byte* rowI = reach + i*n;' once per i. Replace the branchy inner loop 'if(rowV[j]!=0) rowI[j]=1;' with a branchless merge 'rowI[j] |= rowV[j];' (since reach values are 0/1, OR equals the union and never sets a false bit). This is vectorizable. Even better: pack the reachability matrix as ulong* bitsets (n bits per row, ceil(n/64) words) and do word-wise 'rowI[w] |= rowV[w];' over only the v-row's set columns, cutting the inner loop by ~64x and shrinking RAM 8x.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.rationale: Branchless OR over contiguous rows is the textbook Burst-vectorizable pattern (SIMD OR + store). Bitset packing reduces both memory traffic (8x fewer bytes) and inner iterations (64x) and is the standard transitive-closure representation; it also speeds the outer reach[i*n+u] test via bit indexing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.risk: Branchless OR is exact because operands are guaranteed 0/1 and union is monotonic. Bitset packing changes the storage layout, so Init/AddEdge/CanReach must all switch to bit indexing (reach[row + (col>>6)] & (1UL<<(col&63))); the (col&63) mask is valid since shift counts are unsigned-bounded. CanReach return becomes a bit test. This is an API/layout change but observable reachability answers are identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.summary: Inner j-loop runs over all n columns even when the v-row is sparse.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.currentCost: For each predecessor i, the loop scans all n columns of rowV testing each; columns where rowV[j]==0 do nothing yet still cost a load+branch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.proposedChange: Precompute the list (or bitset) of columns j where reach[v*n+j]!=0 once before the i-loop, then for each qualifying i only iterate that column set. With the bitset representation this falls out naturally (iterate set words). Without bitsets, build a small int* colList of length k once and loop k instead of n per i.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.rationale: Turns the per-i inner cost from O(n) to O(k) where k = out-reach count of v; the v-row is constant across the i-loop so its nonzero columns are a loop invariant that is currently re-scanned for every i.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/DynamicTr.risk: Needs a caller-provided scratch buffer for the column list (RAM/API change). Result identical since the set of j with rowV[j]!=0 is fixed during the call.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.summary: CompareTo calls int.CompareTo four times (each a method call returning -1/0/1) inside the quicksort hot path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.currentCost: Each int.CompareTo is a branch returning a normalized sign; the sort calls CompareTo O(q log q) times and only ever checks <0 / >0, so the normalization is wasted work and the four sub-calls add call overhead Burst may not fully inline.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.proposedChange: Inline the comparisons with plain subtraction-free branch chain: 'if (U != o.U) return U < o.U ? -1 : 1;' etc., avoiding the nested int.CompareTo calls. Better: since the sort only needs ordering, provide a branch-lean comparator. Also note SortEdgeEvents could compare on a packed key. If U,V,Type,Time all fit known bit-widths, pack into a single long key (e.g. (U<<48)|(V<<32)|(Type<<? )...) and compare longs in one instruction, eliminating the four-field chain entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.rationale: Removing four method calls per comparison and replacing the multi-field chain with a single packed-long compare cuts the comparator to one or two instructions, directly reducing the dominant cost of an O(q log q) sort.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.risk: Packing requires that each field fits its allotted bits (e.g. node ids < 2^16, Time < 2^32); must assert/guarantee bounds or the key ordering breaks. Inlining U<o.U is exact and signed-safe for int. Time tie-break must remain last in the packed order to preserve the existing total order.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.summary: Plain quicksort with median-of-one (middle element) pivot has O(q^2) worst case and recurses on both partitions without tail-elimination on the larger side.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.currentCost: Adversarial or already-sorted-with-duplicates inputs (common here: many equal U,V keys) can degrade toward O(q^2); recursion depth can reach O(q) causing stack pressure on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.proposedChange: Recurse into the smaller partition and loop on the larger (tail-call elimination) to bound stack depth to O(log q). Optionally add an insertion-sort cutoff for small subranges (<= 16) to cut overhead. Since the data is keyed and bounded, an LSD radix sort on the packed long key would give O(q) deterministic time and is fully Burst-vectorizable/branchless.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.rationale: Tail elimination caps recursion stack; insertion-sort cutoff removes quicksort overhead on tiny ranges; radix on a packed key removes comparison branches entirely and is linear, which matters when q is large and keys are dense/duplicated (the worst case for this pivot).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.risk: Radix needs a scratch buffer (RAM) and a stable pass to preserve the Time tie-break ordering; must verify stability to keep identical output order where keys tie. Tail-elimination and insertion cutoff are behavior-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.summary: MatchEvents repeatedly dereferences sorted[i].U/.V/.Id inside the inner scan and reloads sorted[i] fields each j iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.currentCost: Inner loop condition reloads sorted[i].U and sorted[i].V every iteration and indexes sorted[j] plus match[sorted[j].Id]; the struct is 20 bytes so each access is a non-trivial load.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.proposedChange: Hoist 'int ui=sorted[i].U, vi=sorted[i].V, idi=sorted[i].Id;' before the inner loop and compare against those locals. Cache 'EdgeEvent ej = sorted[j];' once per inner iteration to avoid multiple pointer-indexed field loads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.rationale: Hoisting loop-invariant field loads removes redundant memory reads from the inner comparison chain; register-resident comparands shorten the dependency chain and help Burst keep the loop tight.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.risk: None; sorted[i] is not modified inside the loop, so caching its fields is exact.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.summary: EdgeEvent stores Time and Id as separate ints but InitializeEvents always sets Time==Id (both = i).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.currentCost: 20-byte struct with a redundant field; the sort copies q*20 bytes (scratchE -> scratchS) and the comparator carries an extra field. Id and Time are identical at construction.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.proposedChange: Drop the duplicate field and use the single index for both roles (it is set to i in both places and MatchEvents/BuildIntervals use them interchangeably as the original query index). Struct shrinks to 16 bytes, improving cache density and halving... reducing the memcopy and making EdgeEvent a clean 16-byte (4xint) blittable that may pack into SIMD lanes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.rationale: 16 bytes vs 20 improves array density (more events per cache line: 4 vs 3 per 64B line) and cuts the Buffer.MemoryCopy volume; fewer fields also simplifies the comparator. Confirm Time and Id are never assigned different values anywhere before removing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/FullyDyna.risk: Must verify no code path sets Time != Id; in the shown code both are i. If any caller or helper relies on them diverging this breaks — guard by auditing all writers before merging the fields.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.summary: Find does full path compression in two passes (find root, then rewrite), doubling pointer traversals; path-halving achieves near-identical amortized bounds in one pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.currentCost: First while-loop walks to root, second while-loop walks the same chain again rewriting parents: two traversals of the path per Find call.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.proposedChange: Replace with single-pass path halving: 'while (i != parent[i]) { parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]; i = parent[i]; } return i;'. One traversal, each node points to its grandparent.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.rationale: Path halving gives the same O(alpha(n)) amortized complexity as full compression but in a single pass with half the memory traffic and a shorter dependency chain per Find — a measurable win since Find is the hottest leaf across all connectivity operations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.risk: Path halving does not fully flatten to the root immediately, so the exact parent[] contents differ from full compression — but Find/Connected/Union outputs (root identity, connectivity answers) are identical for all inputs. Only matters if a caller inspects intermediate parent[] structure, which it should not.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.summary: Init writes parent and size in one loop with two stores; size is a constant fill that could be memset-vectorized, and parent is an iota that Burst can vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.currentCost: n iterations doing parent[i]=i and size[i]=1 interleaved; the constant size fill is not expressed as a bulk memset.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.proposedChange: Keep parent[i]=i in its own tight loop (Burst can vectorize an iota with a base+index vector add), and fill size via a single bulk fill of 1s. Splitting the two stores avoids interleaving a varying store with a constant store and lets each loop vectorize cleanly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/Increment.rationale: Separating the iota write from the constant write gives Burst two homogeneous, vectorizable loops instead of one mixed-store loop; the constant size fill becomes a streamable broadcast store.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.summary: activeIndices stackalloc stays live on the stack during both recursive subcalls even though it is dead after the nextEdges copy, doubling peak stack working set per recursion level.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.currentCost: At each of O(log T) recursion levels, two arrays are stackalloc'd: activeIndices (int[edgeCount]) on line 26 and nextEdges (EdgeInterval[activeEdges], 16 bytes/elem) on line 37. activeIndices is only used to build nextEdges (lines 37-38) and is never read again, yet because it is allocated in the same stack frame as the two recursive Solve calls (lines 40-41), its memory cannot be reclaimed until the frame returns. Peak stack = sum over the active root-to-leaf path of (4*edgeCount + 16*activeEdges) bytes per frame, with the activeIndices portion being pure waste below the current level.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.proposedChange: Split the body so the descent (the two recursive Solve calls plus the final Rollback) lives in a separate helper method that takes nextEdges/activeEdges as parameters. Build activeIndices + nextEdges in the current frame, then tail-call the helper. Because activeIndices is local to the building frame and not to the recursing frame, its 4*edgeCount bytes are released before recursion descends. Concretely: private static void Descend(int l,int mid,int r, EdgeInterval* nextEdges,int activeEdges, ... ) { Solve(l,mid,...); Solve(mid+1,r,...); } and have the else-branch call Descend after building nextEdges. activeIndices can also be reduced from int[edgeCount] to building nextEdges directly (see separate item).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.rationale: Reduces peak stack depth on mobile (small thread stacks, e.g. 512KB-1MB) by eliminating the per-frame activeIndices array from every ancestor frame on the recursion path. With deep time ranges and large edgeCount this is the difference between fitting and a stack overflow, and it improves L1/L2 locality of the live working set.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.risk: Pure refactor; no semantic change. Must ensure the helper still calls Rollback for the current level — keep Rollback in Solve after Descend returns (initialHistory is captured in Solve's frame), not inside Descend, so rollback ordering is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.summary: activeIndices is an indirection buffer used only to materialize nextEdges; the active EdgeInterval values can be written directly, eliminating one O(edgeCount) scratch buffer and one extra gather pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.currentCost: ProcessIntervalEdges fills activeIndices[activeEdges++]=i (line 54), then Solve does a second pass nextEdges[i]=edges[activeIndices[i]] (line 38) — a random-access gather through the index array. Two buffers (activeIndices int[edgeCount] + nextEdges EdgeInterval[activeEdges]) and two passes over the active set.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.proposedChange: In the partial-overlap branch, instead of recording the index, copy the struct directly into a caller-provided EdgeInterval* nextEdges buffer: nextEdges[activeEdges++] = edges[i]. Stackalloc nextEdges once as EdgeInterval[edgeCount] (upper bound) before calling ProcessIntervalEdges, pass it in, and drop activeIndices entirely. This removes the int[edgeCount] buffer and the gather loop on lines 37-38.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.rationale: Eliminates an O(edgeCount) stack buffer and a second O(activeEdges) random-access gather pass, replacing it with a single sequential streaming copy that Burst vectorizes and that has perfect spatial locality (sequential read of edges, sequential write of nextEdges). Fewer cache lines touched, fewer cycles.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.risk: nextEdges must be sized to edgeCount (the upper bound on active edges), not activeEdges, since activeEdges is not known until after the scan. Slightly larger single allocation, but it replaces the activeIndices allocation 1:1 and removes a separate buffer, so net stack use is lower. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.summary: Each loop iteration re-reads edges[i].StartTime/.EndTime/.U/.V via repeated indexed pointer dereferences; loading the struct once into a local reduces address computation and aliasing concerns for Burst.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.currentCost: Lines 51-54 dereference edges[i] up to four times (StartTime twice, EndTime twice, plus U/V on the Union path). The compiler may not prove edges does not alias parent/size/history (all int*), forcing reloads across the Union call boundary.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.proposedChange: Hoist once per iteration: EdgeInterval e = edges[i]; then test e.StartTime/e.EndTime and call Union(parent,size,e.U,e.V,...). The 16-byte struct loads into registers/stack once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.rationale: Removes redundant indexed loads and breaks the aliasing dependency between the edges read and the parent/size writes inside Union, letting Burst keep the comparison operands in registers. Fewer address computations per iteration in the hottest loop of the algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.risk: None — edges[i] is not mutated in the loop, so reading once is equivalent. Copy is 16 bytes, cheaper than the repeated dereferences it replaces.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.summary: mid is recomputed but the real win is that full-span edges unioned at this level are needlessly reconsidered by children; they are already correctly excluded — confirming no change needed there. The genuine note is recursion base-case ordering.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.currentCost: Line 36 computes mid = l + (r-l)/2 — already overflow-safe and correct. No issue.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.proposedChange: No change to mid. (Documenting that the (r-l)/2 form is already the correct overflow-safe choice and should NOT be 'simplified' to (l+r)/2 or (l+r)>>1, which would overflow for large time indices.)
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.rationale: Guards against a future cargo-cult 'optimization' to (l+r)>>1. Keep as-is.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.risk: None; this is a no-op recommendation to preserve the existing correct form.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.summary: size[u] is loaded and stored each iteration through the int* even though the rollback inverse only needs size[v]; the load of size[u] before subtracting is required, but the dependency chain through size can be shortened by reading both into locals.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.currentCost: Lines 58-61 per popped op: read history[historyCount].U and .V, read size[v], read+write size[u], write parent[v]. The size[u] -= size[v] is a read-modify-write through the pointer; if Burst cannot prove size and parent and history do not alias, it must serialize.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.proposedChange: Load the op once: RollbackOp op = history[historyCount]; int u = op.U; int v = op.V; size[u] -= size[v]; parent[v] = v; This loads the 8-byte op in one access instead of two indexed dereferences and gives the compiler clean non-aliasing locals.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.rationale: Reduces two indexed history dereferences to one 8-byte load and clarifies the dependency chain so Burst can pipeline the size update and the parent store. Constant-factor win in the rollback loop, which runs once per union ever performed across the whole divide-and-conquer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.risk: None — purely reads the same fields; semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.summary: history write does two separate field stores; writing the struct once via a local lets Burst coalesce into a single 8-byte store, and the rootI/rootJ swap can be branchless.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.currentCost: Lines 44-46 do history[historyCount].U = rootI; history[historyCount].V = rootJ; historyCount++ — two indexed stores recomputing the same address. The swap on lines 38-41 is a data-dependent branch on size comparison.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.proposedChange: Write the op as one struct: history[historyCount] = new RollbackOp { U = rootI, V = rootJ }; historyCount++; (or assign to a local op then store). For the swap, keep the branch (it is well-predicted by union-by-size and a branchless cmov over two int pairs offers little here), but at minimum coalesce the two history field stores into one 8-byte store.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.rationale: One 8-byte store vs two 4-byte indexed stores with recomputed base+offset addressing reduces address-generation uops in the hot Union path (called once per full-span edge at every recursion level).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.risk: None — RollbackOp is [StructLayout(Sequential)] with two ints, so a whole-struct store is layout-equivalent to the two field stores. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.summary: Find deliberately omits path compression to remain rollback-compatible; this is correct and must be preserved — flagging so it is not 'optimized' by adding compression.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.currentCost: Line 27 walks parent chain with no compression: O(log n) per find under union-by-size. Tempting to add path-halving for speed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.proposedChange: Do NOT add path compression / path halving to Find. The DSU is rollbackable only because Union records exactly the structural changes it makes; path compression would mutate parent[] without recording it in history, breaking Rollback's invariant. Keep Find read-only.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.rationale: Preserves the rollback invariant that the entire offline-dynamic-connectivity algorithm depends on. Union-by-size already guarantees O(log n) find depth, which is the correct bound for a rollbackable DSU.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Connectivity/OfflineDy.risk: Adding compression would silently corrupt the parent array across rollbacks (parent[v]=v restore would not undo compressed pointers), producing wrong connectivity answers. This item is a guard, not a change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.summary: Skip the full inner i-loop by iterating only over the unset bits that are ready, and precompute (1<<i) reuse.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.currentCost: For every reachable mask the inner loop runs n iterations doing a bit-test, an unset-check, and a full dependency-mask compare (adjMask[i] & mask) == adjMask[i]. That is O(2^n * n) with two branches per i regardless of whether the bit is set. For dense masks most i are already set and waste the iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.proposedChange: Compute 'int free = (maxMask - 1) & ~mask;' once per mask, then loop 'while (free != 0) { int bit = free & -free; int i = math.tzcnt(bit); if ((adjMask[i] & mask) == adjMask[i]) dp[mask | bit] += dp[mask]; free &= free - 1; }'. This visits only the unset bits (no wasted iterations on set bits) and replaces (1<<i) with the already-isolated 'bit'.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.rationale: Iterating set bits via free&-free / free&(free-1) processes exactly popcount(~mask) candidates instead of always n, removing the '(mask & (1<<i))==0' branch entirely and the redundant 1<<i shift in the dp index. tzcnt is a single Burst intrinsic. Fewer branches shorten the dependency chain and the loop trip count drops for dense masks.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.risk: Behavior identical for all valid inputs (n <= 31 so 1<<n is well-defined as currently assumed). 'bit & -bit' is safe on the positive int 'free'. Requires Unity.Mathematics for math.tzcnt; if unavailable, a de Bruijn table or intrinsic equivalent is needed. No signedness hazard since free is built from (maxMask-1) which is positive for n<31.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.summary: The dp zero-init loop can be a single memset-style clear.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.currentCost: The explicit 'for (i<maxMask) dp[i]=0' is a scalar store loop of 2^n longs (8*2^n bytes), not auto-recognized as a block clear in all Burst configs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.proposedChange: Replace the manual zeroing loop with 'Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(dp, 0, (uint)(maxMask * sizeof(long)))' (or UnsafeUtility.MemClear). Then set dp[0]=1.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.rationale: A bulk clear maps to vectorized/wide stores (or rep stosb) instead of one 8-byte store per iteration, reducing the init cost and instruction count before the main DP. The main DP loop dominates, so impact is low, but it is a free, semantics-identical win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/CountTopologicalOr.risk: maxMask*sizeof(long) must not overflow uint; for n<=28 it is fine, and the algorithm is already infeasible well before that. Observable result unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagCountingPaths.c.summary: Accumulate into a local long and branchlessly saturate, instead of read-modify-write on pathCount[u] each edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagCountingPaths.c.currentCost: Each edge does a load of pathCount[u], an overflow-guard compare/branch, and a store back to pathCount[u]. The store-to-load dependency on the same memory location each iteration serializes the inner loop and adds a hard-to-predict branch per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagCountingPaths.c.proposedChange: Hoist accumulation: 'long acc = pathCount[u]; for (e...) { long add = pathCount[v]; long sum = unchecked(acc + add); acc = (acc > long.MaxValue - add) ? long.MaxValue : sum; } pathCount[u] = acc;'. Better, since pathCount values are non-negative, detect saturation branchlessly via 'sum < 0' (sign-bit of overflow for non-negative operands) using a select: 'acc = sum < 0 ? long.MaxValue : sum;'.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagCountingPaths.c.rationale: Keeping the running sum in a register removes the per-edge memory store and its store-forwarding dependency, and 'sum < 0' is a correct overflow test when both operands are non-negative (two non-negative longs overflow exactly when their wrapped sum becomes negative), turning the guard into a branchless cmov. Shorter dependency chain and one store at the end instead of per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagCountingPaths.c.risk: Requires that pathCount[v] and the running acc stay non-negative and never reach exactly long.MaxValue from a legitimate (non-saturated) sum boundary; since inputs are counts >=1 and saturation clamps at MaxValue, the 'sum < 0' test matches the original semantics. The original clamps to MaxValue once exceeded and stays there because further adds keep overflowing — identical behavior preserved. Use unchecked to avoid Burst overflow traps.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.summary: Eliminate the first child-counting pass and the separate gather pass by stackalloc'ing once at max degree, fusing into a single edge walk.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.currentCost: Per node u the code walks the adjacency list three times: once to count children, once (after stackalloc) to gather child hashes, then sorts. Three list traversals (pointer-chasing 'next[e]', cache-unfriendly) where two could be one. The stackalloc inside the loop also re-grows the stack frame per node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.proposedChange: Hoist a single 'ulong* childHashes = stackalloc ulong[maxDeg]' outside the i-loop (maxDeg = max out-degree, computable once or passed in), then per node do one walk that both counts and gathers: 'int childCount=0; for(e...) childHashes[childCount++]=hashes[to[e]];'. This removes the dedicated counting pass and the per-node stackalloc.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.rationale: Cuts adjacency traversals from 3 to 2 per node (count+gather fused), and a single hoisted stackalloc avoids repeatedly adjusting the stack pointer and re-zeroing concerns inside the loop. Fewer pointer-chase passes means fewer cache misses on next[]/to[].
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.risk: Requires knowing max out-degree up front to size the hoisted buffer; if not available, computing it needs one O(E) prepass — still cheaper than per-node recount if reused. Stackalloc sizing must cover the largest degree to avoid overflow. Output hashes unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.summary: Insertion sort of child hashes is O(d^2) per node; for high-degree nodes a sort-free order-independent combine avoids sorting entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.currentCost: The canonical hash sorts children with insertion sort (O(d^2)) purely to make the FNV combine order-independent. For nodes with large out-degree d this dominates and is quadratic.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.proposedChange: If the only purpose of sorting is order-independence of the child-hash combine, replace sort+FNV with a commutative/associative mix (e.g. sum, XOR-with-mixing, or sum of a per-child avalanche-hashed value) so children can be combined in any order without sorting. E.g. 'acc += mix(hashes[v]);' then finalize. This makes the per-node cost O(d) instead of O(d^2) and removes the buffer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.rationale: An order-independent reduction (sum/xor of well-mixed child hashes) gives the same canonical property the sort was providing, dropping per-node work from O(d^2) to O(d) and eliminating the childHashes buffer and stackalloc entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagHashCanonical.c.risk: This CHANGES the produced hash values (different algorithm) and collision profile, so it is only valid if the hash output is internal/canonical-only and no caller depends on the exact bit pattern. Plain XOR cancels duplicate children and plain sum is weak; must use an avalanche mix per child to preserve collision resistance. Reject if exact current hash values are part of the contract.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.summary: DagKthPath.Run and DagLexicographicKthPath.Run are byte-identical; one is redundant.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.currentCost: Two separate static classes with identical bodies (the lexicographic variant only differs by a comment assuming sorted adjacency). Duplicated code doubles maintenance and binary/IL surface with zero behavioral difference.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.proposedChange: Collapse to a single implementation: have DagLexicographicKthPath.Run forward to DagKthPath.Run (the algorithm is identical; lexicographic ordering is solely a precondition on adjacency-list order, not on the traversal code). Keep both public entry points for discoverability/API clarity but share the body via [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] delegation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.rationale: Removes duplicated logic so a future correctness/perf fix applies to both. Inlined forwarding compiles away under Burst, so no runtime cost. Purely an ergonomics/maintainability win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.risk: None to runtime semantics: the two bodies are character-for-character identical aside from a comment, so the lexicographic guarantee is entirely a caller-side adjacency-ordering precondition. Keep the distinct class names so the documented precondition stays discoverable.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.summary: The k<=pathCount[v] selection loop already saturates well; only minor: hoist nothing, but note 'while(true)' is fine and loop is optimal.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.currentCost: Each step walks the adjacency list subtracting pathCount[v] until the target child is found; this is inherent O(pathLen * avgDegree) and already minimal. No redundant recomputation present.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.proposedChange: No structural change. Confirm pathCount[v] loads are the only memory traffic; they are. Leave as-is. (Reported only to record that the file is essentially optimal and no further opportunity should be invented.)
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagKthPath.cs.rationale: The greedy descent is asymptotically optimal for kth-path extraction and already branch-light. Manufacturing micro-opts here would be cargo-cult.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.summary: Hoist row base and the reach[i*n+k] guard out of the inner j-loop in the Floyd-Warshall closure.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.currentCost: The triple loop recomputes i*n+k, k*n+j, i*n+j every inner iteration (3 multiplies + adds per j) and re-reads reach[i*n+k] (loop-invariant in j) for all n inner iterations even when it is false, in which case the whole j-loop does nothing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.proposedChange: In the k/i/j closure: compute int iN = i*n and int kN = k*n once per i; load bool rik = reach[iN+k] once per (k,i); if (!rik) continue to skip the entire j-loop; else inner loop does reach[iN+j] |= reach[kN+j] using precomputed iN/kN bases. This removes ~2 multiplies/iter and skips n inner iterations whenever rik is false (the common sparse case).
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.rationale: Reduces the inner-loop arithmetic to a single add for indexing and eliminates an entire O(n) inner pass for every (k,i) where i cannot reach k. In a sparse DAG closure most (i,k) pairs are unreachable, turning many n^2 row scans into a single branch — a large constant-factor and often near-quadratic-per-k reduction. Branchless OR (|=) also keeps Burst happy.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.risk: Pure index/control-flow reassociation; identical writes. reach[i*n+j] stays monotonically set to true, so converting the if to |= preserves results. n*n must fit int (already assumed via the (int)totalBytes cast).

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.summary: Hoist i*n in the reduction pass and precompute m*n indexing; the m-loop also re-multiplies repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.currentCost: The final reduction loop computes i*n+j, i*n+m, m*n+j with full multiplies inside the innermost m-loop (reach[i*n+m], reach[m*n+j]) for every m, despite i*n being invariant across j and m, and i*n+m being a simple increment over m.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.proposedChange: Compute int iN = i*n once per i; reuse for adjMatrix[iN+j] and reach[iN+m] (the latter is reach[iN + m], a base-plus-index load). Keep m*n as int mN accumulated by += n across the m-loop instead of multiplying. Also skip the m-loop early when adjMatrix[iN+j] is false (already guarded) — fine as is.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.rationale: Removes a multiply per m iteration (replaced by an add) and a multiply per j iteration, shrinking the dependency chain in the hottest loop. reach[iN+m] becomes a contiguous-stride read that Burst can prefetch/vectorize the comparison over.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.risk: Pure strength reduction of address arithmetic; no behavioral change. mN += n stays within int as long as n*n fits int, already assumed.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.summary: stackalloc bool[n*n] can blow the stack for moderate n; scratch buffer should be caller-provided.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.currentCost: reach is stackalloc bool[n*n]. For n=1024 that is 1 MiB on the stack, for n=4096 it is 16 MiB — far over typical thread/Burst stack limits, causing stack overflow rather than a graceful failure. It also forces re-zeroing/copy work each call.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.proposedChange: Follow the module convention of caller-provided scratch: add a bool* reach parameter (or byte*/ulong* bitset) to Run so the n*n buffer is allocated/owned by the caller and reused across calls. Document size = n*n. This matches DagReachabilityCompressed/DagMinimumPathCover which already take all working buffers as pointers.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.rationale: Removes a per-call O(n^2) stack allocation that is both a correctness hazard at scale and a hidden cost; lets callers reuse one buffer across many reductions, eliminating repeated allocation and improving cache residency. Consistent with the rest of the DAG API.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.risk: Signature change (API/ergonomics) — breaks current callers. Behavior identical given a correctly-sized buffer; caller must pre-copy or the copy loop stays in Run.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.summary: Use a bitset (ulong*) instead of bool[n*n] for the reachability scratch to cut working set 8x and improve cache behavior.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.currentCost: reach uses one byte per cell (n*n bytes). The Floyd-Warshall closure is memory-bound; a byte matrix wastes 7/8 of each cache line versus a packed bitset and prevents word-parallel OR.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.proposedChange: Store reach as ulong* with ulongsPerNode = (n+63)>>6 words per row. The closure inner j-loop becomes a word-parallel OR: for each (k,i) with bit (i,k) set, OR row k into row i over ceil(n/64) words instead of n byte compares. This is the same trick already used in DagReachabilityCompressed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.rationale: Cuts the closure from O(n^3) scalar byte ops to O(n^3/64) word ops and shrinks the scratch 8x, drastically reducing cache misses on the dominant pass. Burst vectorizes the ulong OR loop well.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagTransitiveReduc.risk: Larger change: bit indexing (word = j>>6, mask = 1UL<<(j&63)) and the reduction pass must read individual bits. Semantics preserved if bit set/test matches the bool semantics. Pairs naturally with the caller-provided-buffer change above.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagReachabilityCom.summary: Hoist offset recomputation and use a local pointer for the destination bitset row in the edge loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagReachabilityCom.currentCost: offset = u*ulongsPerNode is recomputed once per u (fine), but inside the edge loop bitsets[offset + w] is re-indexed from the base each of ulongsPerNode iterations per successor; vOffset = v*ulongsPerNode is a multiply per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagReachabilityCom.proposedChange: Hoist ulong* dst = bitsets + offset once per u. Per edge compute ulong* src = bitsets + v*ulongsPerNode once, then inner loop dst[w] |= src[w]. This presents the OR as a clean pointer-stride loop the Burst auto-vectorizer recognizes, and removes repeated base+offset add chains.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagReachabilityCom.rationale: Shortens the address-computation dependency chain in the innermost OR loop and makes the contiguous ulong OR trivially vectorizable (it already is, but pointer form is the canonical vectorizable shape). dst pointer is loop-invariant across all edges of u, so it is hoisted above the edge loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagReachabilityCom.risk: Pure address-arithmetic refactor; identical loads/stores. No overflow concern beyond existing v*ulongsPerNode which already fits the indexing model.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagPathCoverRestor.summary: Branchless path count avoids a data-dependent branch per node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagPathCoverRestor.currentCost: Per node: nextInPath[i] = match[i]; if (match[i] == -1) numPaths++; — the increment is a data-dependent conditional branch over n nodes, mispredicting on irregular match patterns.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagPathCoverRestor.proposedChange: Read int m = match[i] once (avoids two loads of match[i]); set nextInPath[i] = m; accumulate numPaths += (m == -1) ? 1 : 0 (or numPaths -= (m >> 31) style is unsafe for general -1; use the comparison-to-int form which Burst lowers to a branchless setcc add).
