src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagPathCoverRestor.rationale: Removes a mispredictable branch and one redundant load of match[i] per iteration, turning the loop into a straight-line accumulate that Burst can vectorize (sum of (m==-1) predicates). Constant-factor but the loop is pure n work.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagPathCoverRestor.risk: (m==-1) as int is well-defined and equals the branch's effect. Avoid bit-hacks on the sign bit since only the exact value -1 should count, not all negatives.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagMinimumPathCove.summary: Run is a non-functional stub: it never computes the bipartite matching, so it always returns n.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagMinimumPathCove.currentCost: matching is initialized to 0 and never updated; the documented Hopcroft-Karp augmentation is absent. head/next/to/dist/queue parameters are unused. Result is always n - 0 = n, which is wrong for any DAG with edges.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagMinimumPathCove.proposedChange: Implement Hopcroft-Karp (or Kuhn) augmenting-path matching using the provided head/next/to adjacency, match (size 2n for split L/R or two arrays), dist and queue (BFS layering) buffers, then return n - matching. Use AggressiveInlining only on leaf helpers, not the whole driver.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagMinimumPathCove.rationale: Correctness first; once implemented, Hopcroft-Karp gives O(E*sqrt(V)) which is the right asymptotic for min path cover via Dilworth, vastly better than naive O(V*E) Kuhn on dense inputs and the intended use of the dist/queue buffers.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagMinimumPathCove.risk: This is a functional gap, not a micro-opt: current output is incorrect. Implementing it changes (fixes) behavior by design. Must respect house constraints (pointers, no exceptions).

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagLongestAntichai.summary: Run is a non-functional stub: returns n instead of the longest antichain.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagLongestAntichai.currentCost: reachabilityMatrix and the Dilworth relationship are not used; the function returns n unconditionally, which is correct only when the DAG has no comparable pairs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagLongestAntichai.proposedChange: Compute the answer as min path cover of the transitive closure (Dilworth): build the bipartite graph from reachabilityMatrix (i->j edge when reachable, i!=j) and return n - max_matching via DagMinimumPathCover. Accept the required matching scratch buffers as parameters to stay allocation-free and Burst-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagLongestAntichai.rationale: Provides the correct asymptotic algorithm (matching-based, O(V^2.5) region) rather than a constant. Reuses the matching routine so the closure-to-antichain pipeline is consistent across the module.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/DagLongestAntichai.risk: Functional gap, not a perf tweak — current result is wrong for non-trivial inputs. Fixing it changes behavior by design and depends on DagMinimumPathCover being implemented first.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.summary: Replace the full O(2^n) zeroing loop and skip-if-zero pattern; the initial dp clear over maxMask entries is a separate pass that can be fused, and the dp!=0 guard adds a branch per mask.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.currentCost: A full pass `for (i<maxMask) dp[i]=0` over 2^n longs before the DP, plus a per-mask `if (dp[m] != 0)` branch in the main loop. For n=20 that is ~1M-entry zero pass plus 1M branch mispredict candidates.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.proposedChange: Keep the zeroing (it is required since dp is caller-provided scratch), but hoist `(1 << i)` computations and note the bit work below. The dp!=0 guard is correct to keep (most masks unreachable in sparse DAGs), so leave it. The concrete win: in UpdateDpForMask/FindKthNode precompute `bit = 1 << i` once per i and reuse, and iterate only over the complement bits using `(~m) & ((1<<n)-1)` via De Bruijn / TrailingZeroCount instead of scanning all n bits and testing `(m & bit)==0`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.rationale: Iterating set/unset bits with `Bmi1.TrailingZeroCount`/`math.tzcnt` and `m & (m-1)` clearing turns the inner per-mask loop from O(n) unconditional iterations into O(popcount) iterations touching only relevant bits, removing the `(m & (1<<i))` mask test branch entirely and shortening the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.risk: tzcnt intrinsic must be Burst-supported (it is via Unity.Mathematics math.tzcnt / Burst lowers it). Behavior identical: same nodes visited in same numeric order if you iterate complement bits ascending. For FindKthNode order matters (it scans i high->low and subtracts cnt); must preserve that exact descending traversal to keep the same kth selection, so use a high-to-low bit iteration (e.g. iterate set bits via 31-lzcnt) — verify ordering matches before applying.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.summary: Hoist `1 << i` and avoid recomputing `dp[m]` load; the predecessor-ready test `(adjMask[i] & m) == adjMask[i]` reloads adjMask[i] twice.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.currentCost: Per i: two array loads of adjMask[i], two shifts `1<<i` (one in the mask test, one in `dp[m | (1<<i)]`), and a fresh `dp[m]` read inside the loop though dp[m] is loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.proposedChange: Hoist `long base = dp[m];` before the loop. Compute `int bit = 1 << i;` once. Load `int req = adjMask[i];` once into a local and test `(req & m) == req`. Then `dp[m | bit] += base;`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.rationale: Removes a redundant memory load (dp[m]) from the hot inner loop, halves the shift count, and lets the compiler keep req in a register — fewer uops and a shorter dependency chain. Over 2^n * n iterations this is a measurable constant-factor win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.risk: None — purely local CSE/hoisting, identical results. dp[m] is not aliased with dp[m|bit] since bit is not set in m, so reading base once is safe.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.summary: Hoist `1 << i` (computed twice per iteration) and reuse the `m ^ (1<<i)` value, which is computed twice when the branch is taken.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.currentCost: Per i: `1 << i` evaluated twice in the condition (`(m & (1<<i))` and `(m ^ (1<<i))`), and `m ^ (1<<i)` recomputed again on the `dp[m ^ (1<<i)]` load when taken.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.proposedChange: `int bit = 1 << i; int sub = m ^ bit;` once, then test `(m & bit) != 0 && (adjMask[i] & sub) == adjMask[i]` and use `dp[sub]`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.rationale: Removes 2-3 redundant ALU ops per iteration and a redundant xor on the hot path, shortening the dependency chain feeding the dp load.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/KthTopologicalOrde.risk: None — algebraically identical, sub == m^bit reused safely.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.summary: Recursive DFS uses the call stack; for Burst/mobile an explicit stack avoids per-edge call overhead and deep-recursion stack-overflow risk on long DAG paths.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.currentCost: Each forward edge to an unvisited node is a function call (frame setup, register spill, return). On a path graph of length L this recurses L deep, risking stack overflow and incurring call overhead per node; Burst does not always inline/flatten recursion well.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.proposedChange: Convert Dfs to an iterative search over an explicit `int* stack` (caller-provided, like visited). Push curr, on pop iterate its adjacency list pushing unvisited targets; early-out when target found. Mark visited[curr]=runId on push. Same reachability test (does v reach u).
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.rationale: Eliminates recursive call frames -> fewer cycles per node and bounded, predictable stack usage (cache-friendly contiguous stack buffer) instead of native call stack. Burst optimizes flat loops far better than recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.risk: Requires adding an `int* stack` parameter (API change) and a capacity assumption (size n) — acceptable under the unchecked-Run convention. Must preserve visited semantics: mark before exploring to avoid revisiting. The `head[curr]!=0` sentinel relies on edge index 0 being unused; ensure the iterative version keeps the same e!=0 terminator. Behavior (returns true iff v reaches u) preserved.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.summary: Dereference `*edgeCount` once into a local; it is read three times and written once via the pointer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.currentCost: `*edgeCount` is loaded for `to[*edgeCount]`, `next[*edgeCount]`, `head[u]=*edgeCount`, then `(*edgeCount)++` — four pointer dereferences where aliasing may force reloads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.rationale: Pointers may alias (to/next/head/edgeCount are all int*); the compiler must conservatively reload *edgeCount after each pointer store. Caching in a local guarantees a single load and a single store, removing 3 redundant memory accesses.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/IncrementalCycleDe.risk: None unless edgeCount aliases to/next/head (it must not for correctness — they are distinct buffers by contract). Identical observable behavior.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/MinimumEquivalentD.summary: This is not a correct transitive reduction and the row/column access pattern is cache-hostile; hoist row base pointers and fix iteration to be cache-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/MinimumEquivalentD.currentCost: Inner loop writes `adjMatrix[i*n + k]` and reads `adjMatrix[j*n + k]` while the i loop strides by n (column-major-ish on i*n+j read). `i*n`, `j*n` recomputed; `adjMatrix[i*n+k]` indexed with a multiply-add per element. The single-step transitive removal also only removes length-2 shortcuts, which is a correctness concern for a general transitive reduction (needs reachability closure), but treating it as the intended length-2 reduction: the memory access pattern is the perf issue.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/MinimumEquivalentD.proposedChange: Hoist `bool* rowI = adjMatrix + i*n;` and `bool* rowJ = adjMatrix + j*n;` outside the k loop. Reorder loops to i outer, j middle, k inner so rowI and rowJ are sequential and the k loop streams two contiguous rows (`rowI[k] = rowI[k] && !rowJ[k]` style) — vectorizable by Burst. Replace the branch `if (rowJ[k]) rowI[k]=false;` with branchless `rowI[k] = (bool)(rowI[k] & ~(byte)rowJ[k]);` to let Burst SIMD it.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/MinimumEquivalentD.rationale: Streaming two contiguous rows is cache-line friendly and SSE/NEON-vectorizable; removing the data-dependent branch removes mispredicts and enables Burst to emit packed AND-NOT over the row. Hoisting i*n/j*n removes a multiply per inner iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/MinimumEquivalentD.risk: Loop reorder changes the order writes happen but each `adjMatrix[i*n+k]=false` is idempotent and independent across (i,k) for fixed pass, so result is identical for the length-2 removal semantics. NOTE: flag separately that single-pass removal is not a full transitive reduction for chains longer than 2 — verify intended semantics before relying on it.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/OnlineTopologicalO.summary: Cache `*edgeCount` in a local for the same aliasing reason as IncrementalCycleDetection.AddEdge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/OnlineTopologicalO.currentCost: `*edgeCount` dereferenced 4 times across to/next/head stores and the increment, with potential reloads due to pointer aliasing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/OnlineTopologicalO.rationale: Single load + single store instead of repeated dereferences the compiler cannot prove non-aliasing for.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/OnlineTopologicalO.risk: None under the contract that edgeCount points to a distinct location from to/next/head. The function is a stub (reordering not implemented), so this is the only live path.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.summary: Hoist the per-i bit value (1 << i) inside the forward DP inner loop instead of recomputing it twice per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.currentCost: Lines 19 and 21 each evaluate `1 << i` separately, so the hot inner loop (executed up to 2^n * n times) issues two shift instructions plus re-derives the same value for the mask-test and the dp index. The dependency chain redundantly recomputes a value that is invariant within the iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.proposedChange: Inside `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)` compute `int bit = 1 << i;` once, then use it for both `(mask & bit) == 0` and `dp[mask | bit] += dp[mask];`. Optionally also hoist `long cur = dp[mask];` after the `dp[mask] == 0` check to avoid reloading dp[mask] on every i.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.rationale: Removes one shift per inner iteration and shortens the dependency chain; `dp[mask]` becomes a single register load reused across all n iterations rather than reloaded n times. In a 2^n*n loop these are the dominant constant factors.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.risk: None. `bit` is exactly the value already computed inline; identical results for all inputs. `1 << i` for i in [0,n) with n small is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.summary: Hoist (1 << i) in the backward reconstruction loop, where it is computed three times per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.currentCost: Lines 36 and 42 evaluate `1 << i` three times (`currentMask ^ (1 << i)` appears at line 36 twice via the masked test and at line 42). The reconstruction runs n*n times and recomputes the same shift and the same XOR `currentMask ^ bit` redundantly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.proposedChange: Inside the inner `for (int i = n - 1; i >= 0; i--)` compute `int bit = 1 << i;` and `int prevMask = currentMask ^ bit;` once, then use `(currentMask & bit) != 0`, `(adjMask[i] & prevMask) == adjMask[i]`, `dp[prevMask]`, and on the hit set `currentMask = prevMask;`. This also reuses the single `dp[prevMask]` load for the `count` comparison.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.rationale: Collapses three shifts and two XORs into one each, and reuses prevMask for both the predecessor-subset test and the dp index, cutting the per-iteration op count roughly in half on the selection hot path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.risk: None. prevMask = currentMask ^ bit equals the inline expression; on the break path `currentMask ^= (1 << i)` is exactly `currentMask = prevMask`.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.summary: Reuse maxMask to derive the full mask instead of recomputing 1 << n.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.currentCost: Line 10 computes `1 << n` into maxMask; line 26 recomputes `1 << n` for `(1 << n) - 1`. One redundant shift.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.proposedChange: Replace `int currentMask = (1 << n) - 1;` with `int currentMask = maxMask - 1;`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.rationale: maxMask already holds `1 << n`; subtracting 1 yields the all-bits-set mask without a second shift. Trivial but free.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.risk: None. maxMask == 1 << n by construction, so maxMask - 1 == (1 << n) - 1 exactly.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.summary: Document/guard the 32-bit Lemire-style ranged random which silently breaks when the topological-order count reaches 2^32.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.currentCost: Line 32 `(long)((state * (ulong)total) >> 32) + 1` uses a 32-bit-fraction multiply-high to map the uniform `state` into [1,total]. This is correct only while `total < 2^32`. For larger n the number of topological orderings (up to n!) exceeds 2^32; then `(ulong)state * (ulong)total` can exceed 2^64 and wrap, producing r outside [1,total]. If r > total the reconstruction inner loop never finds a match and `order[step]` is left unwritten (silent garbage), and even without wrap the distribution is truncated/biased.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.proposedChange: Either (a) document the invariant `total < 2^32` (i.e. n small enough that the order count fits 32 bits) as a Run precondition, or (b) for full range use a 64-bit reduction: draw a 64-bit random `rng` and compute `r = (long)(((unsigned __int128)rng * (ulong)total) >> 64) + 1` (emulate via Math.BigMul / mulhi). Given the unchecked-Run convention, (a) is sufficient and zero-cost.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.rationale: Makes the determinism/range contract explicit so callers don't feed n that overflows the 32-bit ranged-random, which is a correctness (not perf) hazard. No behavior change for in-domain inputs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/RandomTopologicalO.risk: This is a contract/clarity note, not a code rewrite. The 64-bit variant changes the produced random sequence, so it must NOT be applied if exact reproducibility of current output is required; only the documentation option is fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.summary: Remove AggressiveInlining from this self-recursive method; inlining a recursive function yields no benefit and can bloat codegen.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.currentCost: Line 7 marks a directly self-recursive method (line 28 calls Run) with MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining. Recursion cannot be fully inlined, so the attribute either no-ops or causes one level of inline expansion that increases code size and instruction-cache pressure without removing call overhead.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.proposedChange: Drop the `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` attribute on Run (keep it on genuine leaf helpers only).
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.rationale: AggressiveInlining is for hot non-recursive leaf methods. On a recursive enumerator it cannot eliminate the dominant recursive call cost and only risks larger code/I-cache footprint on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.risk: None functionally; identical results. Pure codegen/size consideration.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.summary: Optional frontier of indegree-zero nodes to avoid rescanning all n nodes at every recursion level.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.currentCost: Each recursion level does `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (indegree[i] == 0)`, an O(n) scan, giving O(n) per emitted prefix. For dense enumeration the total work has an extra n factor versus tracking the available (indegree==0) set incrementally.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.proposedChange: Maintain an explicit stack/list of currently-available nodes (indegree just reached 0), pushing successors that hit zero during the decrement pass and restoring it on backtrack, so each level iterates only over the live frontier rather than all n nodes. Implement with a caller-provided `int*` scratch buffer to stay within the no-managed-collections constraint.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.rationale: Replaces the per-level O(n) rescan with O(frontier) iteration; reduces constant/asymptotic factor when n is large but the frontier is small.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DAG/TopologicalSortAll.risk: Backtracking must restore the frontier exactly (order-independent enumeration must still visit each candidate once per level) — easy to introduce duplicate or missed orderings. Adds a scratch buffer and code complexity; only worthwhile for large n. For small n the current simple scan is cheaper and clearer, so this is low priority.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.summary: Recursive treap Split/Merge are marked AggressiveInlining but recursion cannot be inlined; the attribute is dead and the call-frame/dependency-chain overhead dominates these hot O(log n) operations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.currentCost: Each Split/Merge level is a real call: argument marshalling of EttNode* + ints, out-param indirection (out nodes[root].Right writes through a pointer), a return, plus a PushUp call after unwinding. AggressiveInlining on a self-recursive method is ignored by the JIT/Burst.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.proposedChange: Remove [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] from Split and Merge. Convert both to iterative form: Split with an explicit descent recording the path then fixing Parent/PushUp on the way back using a small stackalloc int* path buffer (depth bounded by treap height ~ O(log n)); Merge can be rewritten as an iterative loop that walks down choosing the higher-priority root and stitching, then PushUp up the recorded spine.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.rationale: Eliminates per-level call overhead and the long return-dependency chain, shortens the critical path, and lets Burst keep the hot fields in registers across levels instead of re-spilling for each recursive frame. Iterative form also removes the misleading inline hint.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.risk: Must preserve exact treap shape and PushUp order (PushUp happens post-order on the touched spine). The out-params write directly into nodes[root].Right/Left during recursion; the iterative version must reproduce that same parent-pointer fixup order. Treap height is randomized O(log n) so a fixed stackalloc must be sized to a safe max (e.g. 64) or the existing recursion depth bound.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.summary: Reroot takes `ref uint randState` but never reads or writes it; the parameter is dead and forces every caller (Link) to thread randomness state that is not consumed here.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.currentCost: A ref parameter is passed by address; Burst must keep randState addressable (cannot fully enregister it) across the Reroot calls in Link, and the API misleads callers into thinking Reroot consumes randomness.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.proposedChange: Remove the `ref uint randState` parameter from Reroot. Update its two call sites in Link to call Reroot(nodes, u) / Reroot(nodes, v). Optionally drop randState from Link signatures that no longer need it beyond the two NextRand calls (keep it only where NextRand is actually invoked).
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.rationale: Removes a pointless by-ref argument from a hot path, enabling the compiler to keep the PRNG state in a register in Link, and clarifies the API (purity/ergonomics).
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.risk: Pure signature change; observable behavior identical since the parameter is unused. Must update all call sites in the same module to keep it compiling.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.summary: Link performs up to five separate O(log n) root/index tree-walks (GetRoot x2 before Reroot, GetRoot x2 inside the two Reroots, then GetRoot x2 again on lines 180-181, then GetIndex). Several are redundant given Reroot's postcondition.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.currentCost: Each GetRoot/GetIndex is a pointer-chasing walk to the treap root (cache-miss-heavy). After Reroot(u), u is the leftmost element so GetRoot(u) re-walks a tree whose root we could have captured; rootU/rootV on lines 180-181 repeat work Reroot already implied.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.proposedChange: Have Reroot return the new root (the value of Merge(r,l)) so Link can reuse it directly instead of calling GetRoot(nodes,u)/GetRoot(nodes,v) again on lines 180-181. Also fold the initial connectivity check: since Reroot is about to run anyway, capture rootU=GetRoot(u) once and compare to GetRoot(v) before rerooting, reusing rootU as the Reroot input.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.rationale: Cuts two to three full root-to-leaf pointer-chasing walks per Link, each of which is a chain of dependent loads likely to miss cache. Fewer redundant O(log n) traversals on a hot structural-update path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.risk: Must confirm Reroot's returned root equals what GetRoot(u) would yield afterward (Merge(r,l) returns the merged root; verify it is the tree containing u). Connectivity early-out semantics must remain identical (still returns without modifying when already connected).

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.summary: EttNode is 8 ints/uints + 2 longs + padding; field order (mixing 4-byte and 8-byte fields) forces alignment padding, inflating the struct beyond the minimum 48 bytes and worsening cache density for large node arrays.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.currentCost: Sequential layout: Parent,Left,Right(int) Priority(uint) Size(int) [4 bytes] then Val,SubSum(long) Twin(int). The trailing int Twin after two longs likely adds 4 bytes tail padding; total ~56 bytes/node, so fewer nodes per 64-byte cache line during treap walks.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.proposedChange: Group the five 4-byte fields together and the two 8-byte longs together: order as Val, SubSum (longs first, 8-byte aligned), then Parent, Left, Right, Size, Priority, Twin (six 4-byte fields = 24 bytes). Total 16+24 = 40 bytes with no internal padding.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.rationale: Removes alignment padding (56 -> 40 bytes, ~28% smaller working set), increasing nodes per cache line and reducing cache misses across the pointer-chasing GetRoot/GetIndex/Split walks that dominate runtime.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.risk: StructLayout(Sequential) means field order is the memory layout; any external code that memcpys or interops by field offset would break. Within this library all access is by named field so it is safe, but verify no serialization depends on current offsets.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.summary: Repeated `nodes[u].Field` and especially nested `nodes[nodes[root].Left].Size` re-evaluate the base+index*stride address arithmetic and reload through a non-cached pointer on every field touch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.currentCost: E.g. PushUp reads nodes[u].Left and nodes[u].Right then nodes[l].Size, nodes[l].SubSum, nodes[u].Val etc.; Split reads nodes[root].Left twice plus nodes[nodes[root].Left].Size. Each `nodes[idx]` recomputes idx*sizeof(EttNode) and the compiler may not prove aliasing to cache the load.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.proposedChange: Introduce local `EttNode* p = nodes + u;` (and `EttNode* lp = nodes + l;` once l != -1) at the top of PushUp, Split, Merge, GetIndex and access fields via p->Field / lp->Size. Compute child Size/SubSum once into a local instead of re-indexing nodes[nodes[root].Left] twice.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.rationale: Hoists address arithmetic and deduplicates dependent loads, shortening the dependency chain on the hottest leaf method (PushUp runs after every Split/Merge level). Burst then keeps the node base pointer in a register and indexes once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/EulerTour.risk: Through-pointer writes alias the same memory as reads; must keep load/store ordering identical (do not cache a field across a write that the algorithm later re-reads through nodes[..]). Pure address-arithmetic hoisting is semantics-neutral as long as no intervening write invalidates the cached child index.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.summary: PushAll is recursive with [AggressiveInlining]; the attribute is ineffective on recursion and the recursion depth equals splay-tree depth, adding call overhead before every Splay.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.currentCost: PushAll(nodes,u) recurses up to the splay root calling itself per level, then PushDown on unwind. AggressiveInlining is ignored. Each frame re-passes nodes* and reloads nodes[u].Parent.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.proposedChange: Rewrite PushAll iteratively: walk up from x to the splay-root collecting the path into a stackalloc int* buffer (depth bounded by splay height), then PushDown from root down to x in reverse. Remove the AggressiveInlining attribute from PushAll.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.rationale: PushDown must be applied top-down (root first) before a splay; an explicit stack does this without per-level call frames, shortening the dependency chain and removing the misleading inline hint. Iterative form is more Burst-friendly (no recursion to defeat optimization).
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.risk: Must preserve strict top-down PushDown order (root pushed before descendants) since lazy Add/Rev tags must propagate downward before rotations; reversing the collected path is required. Path buffer must be sized to a safe max splay depth.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.summary: Access(nodes,v) already ends by calling Splay(nodes,u==v) on its argument, so the immediately following Splay(nodes,v) in PathAdd/PathMin/PathMax/PathQuery/Cut/Link is a redundant second splay of the same node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.currentCost: Access(...) returns after `Splay(nodes,u)` where u is its argument v; the caller then calls Splay(nodes,v) again. The second Splay re-runs PushAll + the while-loop (which immediately sees IsRoot true) + a redundant PushUp — pure overhead on every path query/update.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.proposedChange: Drop the explicit `Splay(nodes, v)` calls that directly follow `Access(nodes, v)` in PathAdd, PathMin, PathMax, SubtreeQuery-adjacent paths, Cut, and Link (and the analogous ones in TopTree). If a guaranteed post-Access splay is needed, document that Access leaves its argument splayed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.rationale: Removes one full Splay (PushAll walk + PushUp) per high-level operation. Since Access guarantees its argument is the splay-tree root and splayed, the second Splay is a no-op loop with wasted PushAll/PushUp.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.risk: Must verify Access truly leaves v at the root and fully splayed in every code path (it calls Splay(nodes,u) as its last statement with u being the loop's start node == v). If any caller relies on the second Splay re-pushing lazy state, confirm Access's final Splay already did so. Reject for Cut if its Splay(v) targets a different node than Access's argument.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.summary: LctNode mixes one byte (Rev) among ints and longs; sequential layout pads Rev to 4/8-byte boundaries, wasting space and reducing cache density of the node array used in pointer-chasing splays.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.currentCost: Order Parent,Left,Right(int 12B) Rev(byte) then long Val forces 3 bytes padding after Rev to align Val to 8; total struct is larger than necessary, fewer nodes per cache line during Access/Splay walks.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.proposedChange: Reorder: put all longs first (Val, LazyAdd, PathMin, PathMax, PathSum, VirSum, AllSum = 56B), then ints (Parent, Left, Right, PathSize = 16B), then byte Rev last (occupying tail padding that would exist anyway). Net layout has no interior padding.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.rationale: Packs Rev into otherwise-wasted tail padding and groups by alignment, minimizing struct size and improving cache-line occupancy for the cache-miss-bound tree traversals.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/LinkCutTr.risk: Sequential layout is the in-memory contract; safe only because all access here is by named field. Verify no external interop/serialization depends on offsets.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.summary: Same recursive-PushAll-with-AggressiveInlining anti-pattern as LinkCutTree; recursion defeats the inline hint and adds per-level call overhead before every Splay.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.currentCost: PushAll recurses to the splay root then PushDown on unwind; AggressiveInlining is ignored on recursive methods; each frame reloads nodes[u].Parent and re-passes the base pointer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.proposedChange: Convert PushAll to an iterative top-down push using a stackalloc int* path buffer (collect path up to root, PushDown in reverse). Remove the AggressiveInlining attribute.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.rationale: Eliminates recursion call frames on the hot splay-preamble path and removes the ineffective inline attribute; iterative form is more amenable to Burst optimization and keeps the base pointer in a register.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.risk: Must preserve strict root-first PushDown ordering for correct lazy Add/Rev propagation; reverse the collected path. Buffer sized to safe max splay depth.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.summary: Hot leaf methods repeatedly index nodes[x] / nodes[nodes[x].Right] etc., re-evaluating base+index*sizeof and reloading through pointers the compiler cannot prove non-aliasing; caching the node pointer per call shortens dependency chains.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.currentCost: Rotate reads nodes[x].Parent, nodes[y].Parent, nodes[y].Left, nodes[x].Right/Left multiple times; Access does nodes[x].VirSum += nodes[nodes[x].Right].AllSum with double indirection recomputed. Each `nodes[i]` is an address-multiply.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.proposedChange: Cache `TopTreeNode* px = nodes + x;` (and py = nodes + y, pz = nodes + z) at the start of Rotate/Access/Splay and access via px->Field. In Access, load `int rx = px->Right;` once and reuse for the AllSum read and the subsequent assignment.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.rationale: Removes redundant index arithmetic and dependent double-loads on the structures' hottest inner methods, shortening critical paths and helping Burst register-allocate the base pointer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.risk: Through-pointer writes alias reads; must not cache a field value across an intervening write the algorithm re-reads. Caching the *pointer* (not stale field values) is always safe; caching field values requires confirming no aliased store in between.

src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.summary: Init zeroes every field individually in a loop; for the many zero-valued fields this is more stores than necessary and is not the memset pattern Burst/JIT vectorize best.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.currentCost: Per node, ~9-11 individual field stores including several literal zeros (Val, LazyAdd, PathSum, VirSum, AllSum, Rev, etc.). The all-zero fields could be bulk-cleared; only Parent/Left/Right = -1 and PathSize/Size = 1 are non-zero.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.proposedChange: Zero the whole region once with Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(nodes, 0, (uint)(n * sizeof(TopTreeNode))) (a vectorizable memset), then in a tight loop set only the non-zero fields: Parent=Left=Right=-1 and PathSize/Size=1 (and Twin=-1 for ETT). This splits the work into one bulk clear plus a few stores per node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.rationale: Replaces many scalar zero-stores with one wide memset the compiler vectorizes, reducing total store traffic and instruction count on initialization of large node arrays.
src/IAFahim.Graph.DynamicTrees/TopTree.c.risk: InitBlock requires the region be exactly the struct array with no managed/GC content (true: unmanaged blittable struct) and correct byte length via sizeof. -1 is not all-bits-zero so those fields still need explicit init; ensure they are set after the memset. Semantics identical to the field-by-field version.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.summary: Hoist redundant nodes[cur] / nodes[temp] field reloads in the two suffix-link walk loops by caching the node index instead of re-indexing repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.currentCost: Each suffix-walk iteration recomputes nodes[cur].Len then nodes[cur].Link via two separate indexed loads from the Node* array. Node is 12 bytes; the two accesses touch the same cache line but issue two distinct address computations and loads per iteration. The walk can iterate O(string length) times in the worst case over the whole build.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.proposedChange: Inside the while(true) walk, load the Node once: 'Node* p = &nodes[cur]; int curLen = p->Len; if (i - curLen - 1 >= 0 && s[i-curLen-1]==c) break; cur = p->Link;'. Same for the temp-walk with '&nodes[temp]'. This reuses one base-address computation for both Len and Link reads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.rationale: Folds two array-index address calculations into one pointer, and lets the compiler keep Len and Link reads adjacent off the same register-held base, shortening the per-iteration dependency chain in the hottest loop of the algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.risk: None. Identical reads, same order, no aliasing concern since nodes are not written inside the walk loops.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.summary: Avoid the redundant final FindTransition for the suffix link by capturing the matching transition target during the temp-walk, mirroring the standard eertree optimization.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.currentCost: For every newly created node with Len != 1, the code walks suffix links to find 'temp', then calls FindTransition(temp, c, ...) which re-scans temp's adjacency list from scratch to locate the c-transition — a list traversal that duplicates work and adds an extra O(alphabet-degree) scan plus a non-inlined-cost lookup per new node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.proposedChange: The suffix link of newNode is the node reached by following the c-transition from the first proper suffix-palindrome that can be extended by c. Since FindTransition is already the lookup, the only safe constant-factor win is to read nodes[temp].FirstNext into a local before the call so the AggressiveInlining body starts from a register-held head; alternatively keep as-is. If an additional invariant holds that the transition always exists at temp (it does by eertree construction), the -1 branch in FindTransition can be skipped for this call via a dedicated FindTransitionExisting helper returning next[e].To without the terminal -1 check.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.rationale: By construction the c-transition from temp is guaranteed to exist when setting the suffix link, so the terminal 'return -1' path is dead for this call; a specialized lookup removes one loop-exit branch test per scanned edge and the unreachable tail.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.risk: Specialized helper must only be used at line 45 where existence is guaranteed by eertree invariants; using it elsewhere would loop past the list end. Behavior preserved only under that guarantee.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.summary: Node and Next structs use int fields where index/length ranges are bounded by string length; narrowing or documenting blittability is fine, but no free win without a known max length.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.currentCost: Node is 12 bytes (3x int), Next is 12 bytes (3x int). For long inputs both arrays scale with len, so working set is ~24*len bytes. On mobile this affects cache footprint of the adjacency scans in FindTransition.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.proposedChange: If callers can guarantee len < 2^31 (always true for int* indexing) the types are already minimal for correctness; no change unless a 16-bit/typed length cap is introduced. Leave as-is. Optionally add [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] documentation intent — already the default for unmanaged structs, so this is a no-op for layout.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.rationale: The structs are already tightly packed with no padding (3 ints = 12 bytes, 4-byte aligned). There is no provably safe narrowing without a documented length bound from callers.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.risk: Narrowing int->short would break for strings longer than 32767 distinct nodes; reject without an explicit caller contract.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.summary: Replace the 'new Next { ... }' struct-initializer store with direct field writes to avoid a temporary struct construct-then-copy.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.currentCost: 'next[nextCount] = new Next { Char = c, To = newNode, Next = nodes[to].FirstNext };' may materialize a temporary Next on the stack and copy 12 bytes into the array slot, plus reads nodes[to].FirstNext separately, then writes nodes[to].FirstNext.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.proposedChange: Write fields directly: 'int head = nodes[to].FirstNext; Next* e = &next[nextCount]; e->Char = c; e->To = newNode; e->Next = head; nodes[to].FirstNext = nextCount++;'. This caches the FirstNext read once and stores straight into the array slot.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.rationale: Direct field stores into the target slot eliminate the potential temporary-struct copy and reuse the single FirstNext load for both the edge's Next field and the head update, trimming one indexed access.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.risk: None under Burst — same final memory state. Burst typically already lowers the initializer this way, so the win may be zero post-optimization; harmless either way.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.summary: Linear adjacency-list scan in FindTransition is the dominant per-character cost; for large alphabets it is O(degree) and not vectorizable due to pointer-chasing via next[e].Next.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.currentCost: FindTransition follows a singly-linked list through next[e].Next, a data-dependent load chain that Burst cannot vectorize or prefetch; each hop is a cache-miss candidate. Called twice per character (transition probe + suffix-link lookup).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.proposedChange: If the alphabet is small and known (e.g., bounded by a named constant ALPHABET), replace per-node linked lists with a direct nodes-by-alphabet table indexed as transitions[node*ALPHABET + c], turning FindTransition into a single O(1) indexed load with no pointer chase. This trades RAM (ALPHABET*nodeCount ints) for eliminating the dependent-load chain.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.rationale: Direct-indexed transition table converts a pointer-chasing O(degree) scan into one branchless O(1) load, removing the serial dependency chain and making the hot lookup cache-predictable — a genuine asymptotic improvement per lookup when alphabet is bounded.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eertree/Eertree.cs.risk: Only valid when the alphabet is small/bounded by a compile-time constant; for large/unbounded int alphabets the table blows up RAM and the linked-list form is preferable. Must keep current form as the general path; this is an alternate specialization, not a drop-in replacement.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: Hierholzer inner loop never advances curHead past edges it skips via `continue`, so used edges at the front of each adjacency list are rescanned on every revisit — turning the traversal into O(V*E) worst case instead of O(E).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: On line 30-40, when `edgeUsed[e] != 0` the loop `continue`s without moving `curHead[u]`. A vertex revisited d times rescans up to d already-used edges each time -> O(sum of degree^2) total edge scans.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.proposedChange: Always advance the cursor when skipping a dead edge: replace `if (ec > 0 && edgeUsed[e] != 0) continue;` with logic that does `curHead[u] = next[e];` before `continue` (i.e. monotonically advance curHead even for used edges). Since each undirected edge is consumed exactly once and the cursor only moves forward, every edge slot is visited O(1) times -> O(E) total.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.rationale: Monotone cursor advancement is the standard linear-time Hierholzer formulation; it removes the repeated O(degree) rescans, reducing asymptotic work from O(V*E) to O(E) and improving cache behavior (each next[] cell read once).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.risk: Must advance curHead BEFORE the break for the live-edge case as well (already done) and BEFORE continue for the dead-edge case. Correctness preserved because once an edge is marked used it never needs to be revisited; the cursor never needs to point back at it. This also lets the `ec > 0` guard (next item) be removed since stale edgeUsed entries are simply skipped-and-advanced.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: The `ec > 0 &&` guard on the edgeUsed test exists only to avoid reading an unzeroed edgeUsed buffer on the very first edge; it adds a branch to every inner-loop iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: Line 32 `if (ec > 0 && edgeUsed[e] != 0) continue;` evaluates `ec > 0` on every edge scan for the entire traversal, purely to handle the first-edge cold-buffer case.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.proposedChange: Zero `edgeUsed` once up front (a single tight `for` over the used range, like the directed version does on line 70) and drop the `ec > 0` term, leaving `if (edgeUsed[e] != 0) continue;`. ec then only needs to remain if used elsewhere (it is not read after), so `ec` and its increment can be removed entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.rationale: Removes a per-iteration comparison and a per-push increment from the hot loop, and removes a live integer from the dependency chain. The one-time zeroing is amortized O(E) and predictable/vectorizable.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.risk: Only the edge slots actually reachable need zeroing; zero the same n*4 range the directed path uses to stay safe. edgeUsed[e]!=0 for paired edges still set via e^1, so semantics identical. Note: edgeUsed[e^1]=1 means each physical edge is one logical edge; behavior unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: Parity test `deg[i] % 2 == 1` uses signed modulo; degrees are non-negative so a bitmask is equivalent and cheaper.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: Line 16 emits signed-remainder codegen (a div/mul/sub or a sign-correcting sequence) per vertex.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.rationale: `& 1` is a single AND instruction with no sign-correction; Burst lowers it to a clean masked test and it vectorizes/branch-predicts identically.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.risk: `%2==1` and `&1!=0` diverge only for negative operands; deg[] is a pure accumulation of non-negative increments so it is always >= 0. Safe.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: Degree is computed in a separate full pass over all adjacency lists solely to count odd-degree vertices, but only the parity of each degree is needed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: Lines 10-16: a stackalloc int[n] plus a full O(E) pass building exact degrees, then an O(n) pass extracting parity. The exact magnitudes are discarded.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.proposedChange: Track parity directly: use a byte/bit buffer (or accumulate XOR) so the degree pass writes `parity[u] ^= 1` and the second pass tests parity[i] directly; this also shrinks the scratch buffer from int[n] to byte[n]. Alternatively fold the odd-count accumulation so the int[n] `deg` buffer is avoided entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.rationale: Halves/quarters the scratch working set (int[n] -> byte[n]) reducing stack pressure and cache footprint on mobile, and removes storing full counts that are immediately reduced to a single bit.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.risk: XOR-parity accumulation gives identical odd/even classification. Keep the buffer in the same stackalloc style (byte* via stackalloc byte[n]) to satisfy the unmanaged/raw-pointer house rule.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: Same non-advancing-cursor rescan as the undirected version: skipped used edges are not stepped over, giving O(V*E) worst case.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: Lines 80-88: `if (edgeUsed[e] != 0) continue;` leaves curHead[u] untouched, so every revisit of u rescans already-consumed prefix edges. Total work O(sum of outdeg^2).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.proposedChange: Advance the cursor unconditionally when skipping: set `curHead[u] = next[e];` before the `continue` so the head only ever moves forward. Each directed edge is then examined O(1) times -> O(E) traversal.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.rationale: Linear Hierholzer; eliminates repeated prefix rescans. Since directed edges are single (no e^1 pairing), once edgeUsed[e]=1 the slot is permanently dead and the cursor can safely skip past it forever.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.risk: None for correctness: a used directed edge never becomes live again, so advancing past it loses nothing. Preserves output path order.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: `m` (total edge count) is computed in a dedicated O(E) pass but is never read afterward — it is dead computation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: Lines 72-74 run a full second traversal of every adjacency list accumulating `m`, an extra O(E) pass plus a live local, with no subsequent use of `m` (return is pathLen).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.proposedChange: Delete the `int m = 0;` declaration and its counting double-loop. If a validity check on the result was intended (Eulerian path should have m+1 vertices), it is currently absent, so removing the unused pass changes nothing observable.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.rationale: Removes an entire O(E) scan and its memory traffic for zero functional benefit.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.risk: None — `m` is provably unused (no read between assignment and method end). If a future caller wants validation, reintroduce a single `outdeg`-sum reduction instead of re-walking lists.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: indeg/outdeg are read only to find the unique start/end via `outdeg-indeg`; the difference can be computed once and the two int[n] buffers collapsed to one.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: Lines 51-62 keep two stackalloc int[n] buffers but only their per-vertex difference is consulted (==1 / ==-1). The classification loop recomputes `outdeg[i]-indeg[i]` twice per vertex.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.proposedChange: Maintain a single `int* netdeg = stackalloc int[n]` updated as `netdeg[to[e]]--; netdeg[u]++;`, then in the scan compute `int d = netdeg[i];` once and branch on `d`. Halves the degree scratch and removes the duplicate subtraction.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.rationale: Cuts scratch RAM from 2*int[n] to int[n] (relevant on mobile stack budgets) and removes one redundant subtraction per vertex in the classification pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.risk: `outdeg-indeg` net value is identical whether stored as two arrays or one net array; start/end selection unchanged. Overflow not a concern (degree bounded by E, same as before).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.summary: edgeUsed is zeroed with a scalar loop over n*4 entries; a bulk clear is cheaper and the directed graph only needs m flags, not n*4.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.currentCost: Line 70 zeroes n*4 ints one at a time. n*4 may also over- or under-allocate relative to actual edge-id range depending on the indexing convention.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Eulerian/Eulerian.cs.proposedChange: Use a single bulk clear (Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned / a memset-style fill Burst recognizes) over the actually-used edge-id span, or size the buffer to the true max edge id. Prefer a byte buffer (stackalloc byte[edges]) since edgeUsed only stores 0/1.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/BfsLayerGraph.cs.summary: Hoist level[u] into a local inside the per-node edge loop to avoid repeated dependent loads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/BfsLayerGraph.cs.currentCost: Inside the inner edge loop, level[u] is re-read (line 22) every time a frontier node is found, and level[u] cannot be cached across iterations by the JIT because the loop writes level[v] (alias-unknown through pointers).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/BfsLayerGraph.cs.proposedChange: After 'int u = q[qh++];' add 'int lu = level[u] + 1;' and use 'level[v] = lu;'. u is the dequeued node, never written during its own expansion, so level[u] is loop-invariant for the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/BfsLayerGraph.cs.rationale: Removes one pointer load plus an add from the hot inner branch; Burst cannot prove level[u] is not aliased by the level[v] store, so it must reload without the manual hoist. The value is provably invariant because v != u for all reachable v in a simple BFS expansion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/BfsLayerGraph.cs.risk: None. u is dequeued once; its level is set before enqueue and never rewritten, so caching level[u]+1 is exact.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/BfsLayerGraph.cs.risk: Delegation must preserve each caller's auxiliary writes (it[] in DinicBfs). Keep Run unchecked-input contract. Low risk if signatures match.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/DinicCurrentArc.c.summary: Init takes 'ptr' and 's' parameters that are never used; drop them.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/DynamicTreeMaxFlo.summary: stackalloc for q is inside the outer while loop, re-allocating n ints every BFS phase.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/DynamicTreeMaxFlo.risk: None functionally. This is a correctness/robustness fix: leaving it in-loop is a latent stack-overflow bug on large phase counts.

Verify against existing tests before adopting.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.summary: Sift-up does full 3-way swaps each step; use hole-punching (shift parent down, place value once) to halve memory writes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.currentCost: Lines 26-29 perform a full swap (read+write of Dist, V, and two Pos updates) at every level of the sift-up. That is ~6 array writes per level; on a heap of size m the path is O(log m) levels, and this runs once per edge relaxation in Dijkstra — the dominant cost of min-cost flow.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.proposedChange: Hole technique: hold the inserted (d, v) in registers; while parent's Dist > d, move parent down into the hole (Dist[idx]=Dist[p]; V[idx]=V[p]; Pos[V[idx]]=idx; idx=p). After the loop, write Dist[idx]=d; V[idx]=v; Pos[v]=idx once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.rationale: Reduces per-level writes from ~6 to ~3 and removes the redundant Pos updates for the moving element until the final placement; fewer stores, shorter dependency chain. Classic heap optimization.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.risk: None to semantics; standard hole-based sift. Must ensure the final single Pos[v]=idx write covers the inserted element's position.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.summary: Sift-down uses full swaps; apply the same hole technique, and strength-reduce idx*2+1 to a running child index.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.currentCost: Lines 53-56 do full 3-way swaps each level (~6 writes/level). Lines 46-49 recompute idx*2+1 and idx*2+2 (two multiplies/adds) per level. Pop runs once per settled vertex in Dijkstra.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.proposedChange: Hole-punch sift-down: keep the moved last element in registers, move the smaller child up into the hole each level, write once at the end. Compute 'left = (idx<<1)+1' (shift not multiply) and 'right = left+1' to avoid the second multiply.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.rationale: Halves store traffic and shortens the dependency chain; shift+add replaces multiply for child index. Both are in the inner loop of the heaviest algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.risk: None; idx is non-negative so <<1 equals *2 exactly. Standard transformation.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to PushOrUpdate and Pop; they are hot leaf-ish methods called per relaxation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.currentCost: Neither heap method is marked for inlining; the call overhead (arg setup, no register promotion of Size/pointers across the call) repeats once per edge relaxation and per pop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.rationale: Lets Burst/JIT promote the heap struct fields into registers at call sites in the Dijkstra loops, cutting per-call prologue/epilogue. Hot, small-ish methods.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.risk: Pop/PushOrUpdate are moderately sized; inlining may bloat code. Low risk under Burst which manages this well; measure I-cache if concerned.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.summary: to[e] and dist[u] are re-loaded/recomputed multiple times per edge in the relax loop.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.proposedChange: Hoist 'long du = dist[u];' after Pop (it equals d, already available — use d directly). Per edge: 'int w = to[e]; long nd = d + cost[e]; if (cap[e] > 0 && nd < dist[w]) { dist[w] = nd; parent[w] = u; parentEdge[w] = e; pq->PushOrUpdate(w, nd); }'.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.rationale: Removes 3 redundant to[e] loads and one redundant add per edge; reuses 'd' from Pop instead of reloading dist[u]. Note: dist[u] cannot be hoisted by the compiler because dist[to[e]] stores may alias, so manual hoist is required.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.risk: Using 'd' for dist[u] is valid only because the 'if (d != dist[u]) continue;' guard (line 383) ensures d == dist[u] at this point. Correct and exact.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.summary: dist[u]+pot[u] is recomputed per edge though both are invariant for u; hoist the partial sum.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.proposedChange: At RelaxEdges entry compute 'long baseU = dist[u] + pot[u];' once, then per edge 'long nd = baseU + cost[e] - pot[to[e]];'. Also hoist 'int v = to[e];' before the pot[v] load (already done) and reuse for dist[v]/parent[v].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.rationale: Removes one long add per edge; dist[u] and pot[u] are not written inside this loop (only dist[v], v!=u in any relax that changes state, and pot is untouched here), so the partial sum is invariant.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.risk: None. pot is read-only in RelaxEdges; dist[u] is only overwritten if some edge relaxes u itself (self-loop), which cannot improve dist[u] since reduced cost of a non-negative... but to be exact: a self-loop edge u->u with negative reduced cost is impossible under valid potentials, so baseU stays correct. If self-loops with cap>0 are possible in input, recompute is identical because nd<dist[u] would fail. Safe.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.summary: Recursive DFS re-reads to[e], level[to[e]], cap[e]-flow[e] up to three times per edge; cache once. Also recursion limits Burst.

This is the Dinic blocking-flow hot path. Additionally, recursion (line 103) is harder for Burst to optimize and risks deep stack on long paths.

Also hoist 'int lu1 = level[u] + 1;' before the loop. Longer term: convert to an explicit-stack iterative DFS to remove recursion for Burst.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.risk: Micro-hoist: none (u, e fixed in iteration; level[u] not written in this frame). Iterative rewrite: larger change, must faithfully reproduce current-arc advancement and partial-push return semantics — validate against tests.

Remove the nn*2 slack unless a specific off-by index requires it; if a guard is needed, +2 (for the e^1 of the highest edge) suffices, not nn*2.

Use edgeId (possibly +1 rounding) to be safe. Note Run returns 0 unconditionally (line 229) — the function appears incomplete; verify intended behavior before tuning.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/Flow.cs.summary: Initial O(V+E) scan to find maxEdge just to zero flow; if edge count is known or flow is caller-zeroed this whole pass is removable, and to[e] reloads in path loops can be cached.

In the path loops, cache 'int pe = parent[u];' once and reuse for cap[pe], flow[pe], flow[pe^1], to[pe^1].
