src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpBfs.c.summary: Branch structure re-tests pu against -1 twice; can be reordered to a single compare.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpBfs.c.currentCost: Lines 23-25: loads pu = pairV[v], then 'if (pu != -1 && dist[pu] == -1)' else 'if (pu == -1)'. The pu==-1 case is the common 'found' signal; the two-way compare adds a redundant test.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpBfs.c.proposedChange: Restructure as: 'if (pu == -1) { found = du1; } else if (dist[pu] == -1) { dist[pu] = du1; q[qt++] = pu; }'. Single primary branch on the -1 sentinel, the unmatched case handled first.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpBfs.c.rationale: Collapses two separate conditionals testing the same value into one if/else-if, removing a redundant comparison and improving branch predictability. Identical outcomes for all three states (pu==-1, pu matched+unvisited, pu matched+visited).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpBfs.c.risk: None — exhaustive case mapping is preserved: pu==-1 sets found; pu matched & dist==-1 enqueues; pu matched & dist!=-1 falls through (no-op), exactly as before.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.summary: dist[u] + 1 is recomputed for every edge in the augmenting-path scan loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.currentCost: Line 16 evaluates 'dist[u] + 1' once per edge e of u (a pointer load of dist[u] plus add each iteration), even though dist[u] is not modified inside the loop until the post-loop line 21.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.proposedChange: Hoist 'int du1 = dist[u] + 1;' immediately after the 'if (u == -1) return true;' guard, then test 'dist[pu] == du1'. dist[u] is only written at line 21 after the loop exits, so it is invariant during the scan.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.rationale: Loop-invariant code motion: removes a redundant load+add per edge from the DFS hot loop (this DFS runs once per BFS phase across all free left vertices). Shorter dependency chain on the comparison that gates recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.risk: None. dist[u] is assigned only at line 21 (after the for-loop) and the recursive Run is called on pu != u (matched right-vertex's left partner), which cannot alias dist[u] within this frame's loop; the hoisted value is identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.summary: Recursive DFS prevents Burst from inlining/optimizing the hottest matching loop and risks deep call frames.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.currentCost: Run calls itself (line 16) with the full 11-pointer argument list on every successful descent. Recursion is opaque to Burst inlining/vectorization, spills the large argument set to the stack each frame, and on adversarial bipartite graphs the depth can reach O(V), threatening stack overflow on mobile's smaller stacks.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.proposedChange: Convert to an explicit iterative DFS using a manually managed stack of (u) frames backed by a caller-provided stackalloc int* buffer (it[] already holds the per-vertex iterator/resume edge, so it doubles as the resume pointer). Push u, advance it[u]; on a viable edge push pu; on exhaustion set dist[u]=int.MaxValue and pop. This keeps the same visit order and pairing semantics.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.rationale: Eliminates per-descent argument spilling and unbounded native recursion, bounds stack use to a fixed buffer, and gives Burst a single flat loop it can schedule far better. Same augmenting semantics: it[] resume state and dist[u]=MaxValue dead-marking are preserved.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/HopcroftKarpDfs.c.risk: Moderate implementation risk: the iterative rewrite must exactly reproduce the resume-via-it[u] behavior and the dist[u]=int.MaxValue marking on failure, and pairU/pairV must be assigned on the unwind in the same order. Adds one stackalloc buffer to the signature (ergonomics/API change). Behavior-preserving only if the manual stack mirrors the recursion contract precisely — verify with the existing NUnit tests.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/FlowWithVertexCap.summary: Per-vertex split-edge build recomputes i*2/i*2+1 and branches on s/t inside the loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/FlowWithVertexCap.currentCost: Lines 19-24 loop over all n vertices computing inV=i*2, outV=i*2+1 and a 'i==s || i==t' branch every iteration to pick int.MaxValue vs vCap[i]. The two source/sink vertices are the only ones needing MaxValue, yet the branch is paid n times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/FlowWithVertexCap.proposedChange: Hoist the special cases out: run the loop unconditionally with 'int twoI = i << 1; MinCostFlowAddEdge.Run(..., twoI, twoI|1, 0, vCap[i]);' then, after the loop, overwrite only the s and t split-edge capacities to int.MaxValue (the in->out edge ids for s and t are deterministic: edge 2*s+? in build order). Alternatively, keep the branch but compute 'int twoI = i << 1; int outV = twoI | 1;' once. The i<<1 / |1 form is strength-reduced and avoids the separate +1 add.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/FlowWithVertexCap.rationale: Removes n branch evaluations on a condition true for only 2 of n vertices, and replaces multiply+add with shift+or (equivalent since i>=0). Cuts work in an O(V) build loop; predictable straight-line code vectorizes/pipelines better.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/FlowWithVertexCap.risk: Low. i is a non-negative loop index so i<<1 == i*2 and (i<<1)|1 == i*2+1 exactly. The post-loop overwrite must target the correct edge ids for s and t in MinCostFlowAddEdge's id sequence; if that edge-id arithmetic is gotten wrong it changes capacities — safer minimal version is to keep the branch and only apply the shift/or strength reduction (zero risk).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.summary: Hoist the four per-iteration stackalloc buffers (parent, parentEdge, dist, inqueue) out of the while(true) augmentation loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.currentCost: Lines 14-17 allocate 4 stack buffers (parent: n*4B, parentEdge: n*4B, dist: n*8B, inqueue: n*1B = ~17n bytes) on every single augmenting-path iteration. There can be O(V*E) augmentations; the stack pointer churns each loop and the buffers are re-zeroed/re-filled anyway at line 18 (and dist again inside Spfa at line 33).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.proposedChange: Move the four `stackalloc` declarations above `while (true)` (line 12). Keep the per-iteration reset loop at line 18 as-is (it already reinitializes all of dist/parent/inqueue each pass). Spfa's cnt and q buffers can likewise be allocated once and passed in, or Spfa's internal dist re-init (line 33) can be dropped since Run already sets dist on line 18 immediately before the call.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.rationale: stackalloc in a loop does not free per iteration in C#; the frame grows only once, but emitting the localloc/zeroing pattern each iteration adds instructions and defeats the JIT/Burst hoisting it could do if declared once. One allocation + a tight reset loop is strictly fewer instructions and a smaller, stable working set that stays hot in L1.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.risk: None for buffer hoisting: every element is unconditionally rewritten by the line-18 reset loop before use. If also removing the duplicate dist init at line 33, confirm Spfa is only ever called right after the line-18 reset (it is) — otherwise keep it. Stack frame size is unchanged or smaller.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.summary: Eliminate the duplicate dist[] initialization performed in both Run (line 18) and Spfa (line 33).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.currentCost: dist[i] = long.MaxValue is written for all i at line 18, then immediately overwritten with the identical value for all i at line 33 inside Spfa. That is a redundant O(n) pass over an 8n-byte buffer every augmentation, plus a second streaming write that evicts nothing useful.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.proposedChange: Remove the loop `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) dist[i] = long.MaxValue;` at line 33 in Spfa (Run already initialized dist on line 18). Alternatively remove the dist part of line 18 and keep line 33. Keep exactly one.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.rationale: Halves the dist-initialization memory traffic per augmentation (one 8n-byte streaming write instead of two). On mobile with limited bandwidth this is a measurable constant-factor win in the hot augmentation loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCancel.risk: Must guarantee Spfa is always invoked immediately after the line-18 reset with no intervening dist mutation. In this file Spfa is called only on line 19 right after line 18, so safe. dist[s]=0 is set in Spfa (line 34) after, so ordering is preserved.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.summary: Hoist the four per-iteration stackalloc buffers (parent, dist, parentEdge, q) out of the doubly-nested scaling/iteration loops.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.currentCost: Lines 20-25 allocate parent (4n), dist (8n), parentEdge (4n), q (4n) = ~20n bytes inside `for delta` x `for iter` — i.e. O(log(maxCap) * n) localloc emissions. Buffers are fully reset at line 23 each pass anyway, so the allocation itself buys nothing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.proposedChange: Declare the four stackalloc buffers once, before the `for (int delta = ...)` loop. Retain the line-23 reset loop (dist=MaxValue, parent=-1) inside the inner loop; q is reset implicitly via qh=qt=0. parentEdge needs no reset because it is only read along chains where parent != -1.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.rationale: Single stack reservation instead of one per inner iteration; smaller, stable hot working set; lets Burst/JIT keep the base pointers in registers across iterations. Pure instruction-count and code-size reduction with identical behavior.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.risk: None. Every consumed element is reinitialized by the line-23 loop or by the BFS fill before being read. Stack frame size unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant `cap[e2] - flow[e2]` reload and avoid re-reading to[e2]/cost[e2] redundantly in the inner relaxation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.currentCost: Inner BFS (lines 31-37) reads cap[e2], flow[e2], to[e2], cost[e2] each via separate indexed loads. The residual `cap[e2]-flow[e2]` is computed for the `< delta` guard then the same edge's to/cost are loaded again; dist[uu] is reloaded each edge though invariant across the inner for-loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.proposedChange: Cache `long du = dist[uu];` once per uu before the edge loop (line 31). It is invariant over e2 and removes a dependent 8-byte load per edge. Minor: compute residual into a local `int res = cap[e2]-flow[e2];` reused only by the guard (no second use here, so limited), but the dist[uu] hoist is the real win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.rationale: dist[uu] is loop-invariant w.r.t. the edge iteration; hoisting it removes one memory load per edge in the hottest loop and shortens the dependency chain feeding `nd = du + cost[e2]`. Helps Burst vectorize/schedule the relaxation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.risk: None: dist[uu] is not written inside the edge loop (only dist[vv] for vv != uu when nd<dist[vv]; vv==uu cannot improve since nd=dist[uu]+cost and a 0-cost self-loop would still not satisfy nd<dist[uu]). Self-loop with negative cost would be a pre-existing algorithmic concern, not introduced here.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.summary: The inner shortest-path is a BFS-order relaxation that can re-enqueue nodes via plain FIFO without a closed/settled check, giving worse-than-necessary bounds; using the existing PotentialDijkstra/SPFA with potentials would tighten cost per phase.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.currentCost: Lines 28-38 relax edges in FIFO order and push vv whenever dist improves, but there is no dedup/inqueue flag and no potential reweighting, so on graphs with varying costs a node can be pushed many times and q (sized n) can overflow on a single phase since qt is never wrapped (unlike Spfa in CancelCycle which wraps qh/qt). This is both a potential correctness bound issue and extra work.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.proposedChange: Either (a) reuse the module's PotentialDijkstra (Flow.cs:112) with maintained potentials for O(E log V) per phase and guaranteed non-negative reduced costs, or (b) at minimum add an inqueue flag and a circular q (qh/qt wrap like MinCostFlowSpfa) sized to n and cap re-enqueues, matching the proven pattern already in CancelCycle.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.rationale: A potentials-based Dijkstra gives a strictly better and more predictable per-phase bound than unbounded FIFO relaxation, and avoids the fixed-size q[n] overflow when more than n enqueues happen in one phase. Capacity scaling with Dijkstra+potentials is the standard, asymptotically tighter formulation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCapaci.risk: This is the most invasive change and borders on algorithmic redesign rather than a micro-opt; it can alter the order of equal-cost augmentations (but not the returned totalCost for a correct min-cost-flow). Validate against existing tests. The q-overflow concern should be confirmed against the assumed input bounds before relying on it; if callers guarantee <= n distinct enqueues per phase, only the relaxation-count win remains.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.summary: Remove the redundant level[]/cnt[] initialization in Run that BfsLevel2 immediately overwrites.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.currentCost: Line 13 sets level[i]=0 and cnt[i]=0 for all i. BfsLevel2 (line 27) then overwrites level[i]=n and cnt[i]=0 for all i, and rebuilds cnt fully at line 44. So the level=0 and cnt=0 writes in Run are dead stores (two O(n) streaming writes wasted before the first and only BfsLevel2 call).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.proposedChange: In Run's init loop keep only `it[i] = head[i];` and `flow[i] = 0;`. Drop `level[i]=0;` and `cnt[i]=0;` since BfsLevel2 unconditionally reinitializes both. flow[i]=0 must stay (it is the caller's flow array reset and is not touched by BfsLevel2).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.rationale: Eliminates two dead O(n) initialization passes over level and cnt before they are clobbered, reducing startup memory traffic. Pure win, no behavior change.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.risk: None provided BfsLevel2 is always called once before any level/cnt read (it is, line 15). flow[i]=0 must be retained as it is the real output/residual reset.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.summary: Hoist invariant level[u]+1 and cache residual; add AggressiveInlining is not viable (recursive) but reduce repeated indexed loads of level[u].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.currentCost: Inside the edge loop (lines 50-58) level[u] is re-loaded for the `level[v] == level[u]+1` test on every edge though it is invariant across the loop. cap[e]-flow[e] is computed once for the guard then recomputed inside Math.Min on line 56. cnt[level[u]] is indexed three times (lines 60-63) reloading level[u] each time.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.proposedChange: Cache `int lu1 = level[u] + 1;` before the for-loop and compare `level[v] == lu1`. Cache `int res = cap[e] - flow[e];` once and pass `Math.Min(f, res)` reusing res. In the retreat block cache `int lu = level[u];` and index cnt[lu] consistently, then after `level[u]++` use cnt[lu+1].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.rationale: Removes a redundant level[u] load per edge and a redundant residual subtraction per accepted edge in the hottest recursive routine; shortens dependency chains. Math.Min(int) already lowers to branchless cmov under Burst, so reusing the precomputed res is free correctness-wise.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/IsapGapOptimizati.risk: None: level[u] is not modified inside the edge loop (only in the retreat tail after the loop), so caching lu1 across the loop is exact. res is recomputed only because flow[e] is unchanged until after the recursive call returns; caching before the recursion is fine because the value passed to Math.Min is the pre-recursion residual, matching current semantics.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.summary: Edge arrays are over-allocated at n*4 but the e^1 pairing convention plus AddEdge's 1-based edgeId means index space must be sized to the true max edge id; verify/right-size and avoid the separate newFlow zeroing pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.currentCost: newTo/newNext/newCap/newFlow are each stackalloc int[n*4] (16 bytes/element * 4 arrays = up to 64n bytes of stack). The actual edge count is: up to n source/sink edges (2 ids each) plus up to (number of original edges) graph edges (2 ids each). For dense graphs original edges can exceed n, so n*4 may be an under-bound, while for sparse graphs it over-allocates stack. Separately, DinicMaxFlow internally zeroes flow, yet newFlow is allocated uninitialized here (good) — no redundant zero here, but newCap region beyond used ids is never written.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.proposedChange: Size the edge arrays from a named constant derived from the true upper bound: 2*(n + originalEdgeCount) + 2 (the +2 for the 1-based/paired-id slack of AddEdge starting at edgeId=1). If originalEdgeCount is not passed, document that n*4 assumes at most n original edges. Prefer adding an explicit maxEdges parameter to make the bound caller-controlled and avoid silent stack overflow on dense inputs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.rationale: Correct, caller-controlled sizing prevents both stack overrun (dense graphs) and wasted stack/cache footprint (sparse graphs), keeping the working set tight for Burst. This is the dominant RAM concern in the file.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.risk: Changing the signature to take maxEdges is an API/ergonomics change (breaks callers) — flag as ergonomics-coupled. If signature must stay fixed, at minimum the n*4 bound should be documented as 'requires original edge count <= n'. No behavior change for inputs already within bound.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.summary: Fuse the final two O(n) passes and reuse visited/BFS to accumulate maxWeight in one sweep.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.currentCost: After the min-cut BFS, line 43 does a separate O(n) loop testing `visited[u]==1 && nodeWeight[u]>0`. The BFS (lines 32-42) already visits exactly the source-side nodes; nodeWeight[u]>0 nodes are precisely those connected to s by a positive-weight edge. The result is two passes plus a reload of nodeWeight[u].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.proposedChange: Accumulate maxWeight during the BFS dequeue: when a node u (0<=u<n) is popped and nodeWeight[u]>0, add it then. This removes the trailing O(n) scan and one full nodeWeight re-read. Guard u<n since s,t are nn-1,nn-2 style sentinels outside [0,n).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.rationale: One fused pass over reachable nodes instead of BFS + full [0,n) rescan; fewer nodeWeight loads and better temporal locality (process node weight while the node id is already in a register).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosureFlo.risk: Must ensure every reachable node in [0,n) is dequeued exactly once (BFS visited-guard guarantees this) and that s itself is excluded by the u<n / nodeWeight test (s has no nodeWeight entry; s index must be outside [0,n)). If s/t indices overlap [0,n) the guard must match the existing line-43 condition exactly. Result identical otherwise.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosurePro.summary: newFlow buffer is allocated but the min-cut/selected set is never recovered, and edge arrays at n*6 are a loose bound; right-size and consider dropping unused capacity.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosurePro.currentCost: Five arrays at stackalloc int[n*6] (~120n bytes stack). The function only returns totalProfit and never reads newFlow after DinicMaxFlow, yet newFlow occupies n*6 ints of stack and is written by Dinic. The n*6 multiplier is a conservative guess unrelated to the actual edge count (n profit edges *2 ids + prerequisite edges *2 ids).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosurePro.proposedChange: Size edge arrays from the real bound 2*(n + prerequisiteEdgeCount) + 2 (named constant), ideally via a caller-supplied maxEdges. newFlow is required by DinicMaxFlow's signature so it must stay, but its length only needs to cover used edge ids, not n*6. Tightening the multiplier shrinks the hot stack working set.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosurePro.rationale: Reduces stack footprint and cache pressure during the Dinic run, and removes the risk of under-sizing on dense prerequisite graphs where prerequisite edges exceed 2n. Tighter buffers stay resident in L1/L2 across Dinic's repeated BFS/DFS sweeps.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MaximumClosurePro.risk: If prerequisite edge count can exceed 2n, n*6 may currently UNDER-allocate and silently corrupt the stack — verify the documented bound. Switching to a maxEdges parameter is an API change (ergonomics). With a correct fixed bound, behavior is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.summary: pqPos array is fully maintained but never read — dead working set and dead writes in the hottest loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.currentCost: stackalloc int[n] for pqPos plus pqPos[...] = idx writes on every heap sift-up/sift-down swap and every push, yet the value is never consulted (no decrease-key is performed; relaxation pushes a duplicate entry instead). That is n*4 bytes of stack and 2-3 extra stores per swap.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.proposedChange: Delete pqPos entirely: remove the stackalloc, the init loop `for(i)pqPos[i]=-1`, and every `pqPos[...] = ...` assignment in sift-up and sift-down. The algorithm already tolerates stale heap entries via the `du != dist[u]` lazy-deletion check.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.rationale: Removes an O(n) allocation/zeroing per outer iteration and eliminates 2 store instructions per heap swap (sift-up/down run O(log V) per pop/push, so this is in the inner dependency chain). Fewer stores shorten the critical path and lower cache pressure.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.risk: None — pqPos is provably write-only; grep the function for any read of pqPos confirms it is never used in a branch or expression. Behavior is identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.summary: Per-outer-iteration stackalloc of the priority queue (pqV/pqD/pqPos) inside while(true) repeatedly grows/zeroes the stack frame.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.currentCost: Three stackalloc int/long[n] occur inside the outer augmentation loop. Each augmenting path triggers a fresh stack reservation; Burst/.NET zero-inits or at least re-reserves, and the buffers are conceptually live for the whole call.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.proposedChange: Hoist pqV and pqD (and dist) allocation above the while(true) loop, exactly like dist/parent/pot are already hoisted; only reset pqSize=0 and re-fill dist each iteration. stackalloc inside a loop is also UB-adjacent for frame size in some JITs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.rationale: One reservation instead of O(augmentations) reservations; smaller, stable stack frame improves locality and avoids repeated frame-pointer math. Matches the file's own hoisting convention for dist/parent/pot.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.risk: stackalloc inside a loop does not free per iteration in C# (it persists to method end), so hoisting is semantically equivalent and actually safer against stack overflow. No behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.summary: Heap-update branch when du != dist[u] discards top incorrectly by overwriting u but leaving the stale root in the heap.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.currentCost: `if (du != dist[u]) { u = pqV[--pqSize]; }` pops the last element into u but does NOT remove the stale root at index 0, so the same stale root is re-popped next iteration, wasting comparisons until it is finally evicted.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.proposedChange: On a stale top, remove the root (swap last into index 0 and sift down) and `continue` without processing, rather than substituting the tail element as the current node. This avoids reprocessing the stale root and avoids processing an arbitrary tail node out of priority order.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.rationale: Eliminates repeated re-pop of stale roots (reduces total heap operations) and removes out-of-order node expansion that can cause extra relaxations/pushes, shrinking the inner loop's total work.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowDijkst.risk: Medium — this also fixes a likely correctness subtlety (processing a non-minimal node), so verify against tests; if current outputs are considered the spec, treat as behavior-affecting and gate behind validation. State clearly: this changes which node is expanded on a stale-top event.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSpfa.c.summary: q/inq/cnt stackalloc reside inside while(true) and dist/parent re-init each iteration; hoist the buffers.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSpfa.c.currentCost: Three stackalloc (int[n], byte[n], int[n]) plus a full init loop occur per augmenting iteration. The buffers persist to method end anyway (stackalloc is not freed per loop), so re-declaring them only confuses the frame and forces re-zeroing logic each pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSpfa.c.proposedChange: Hoist q, inq, cnt stackalloc above while(true); keep the per-iteration reset loop for inq/cnt (still required), but allocate once. Combine the inq/cnt/dist/parent resets into a single pass over i since they are all length n.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSpfa.c.rationale: Single stack reservation; one fused reset loop instead of two separate loops over [0,n) (the dist/parent loop and the inq/cnt loop), halving loop overhead and improving streaming write locality.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSpfa.c.risk: None for hoisting (stackalloc lifetime is method scope regardless). Fusing resets is safe because all arrays are length n and independent.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.summary: BFS queue q is stackalloc'd inside while(true); level[] is allocated and initialized but never used.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.currentCost: stackalloc int[n] q per outer iteration; plus `int* level = stackalloc int[n]; for(i) level[i]=0;` — level is written once and never read anywhere in the method (dead allocation + dead O(n) init loop).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.proposedChange: Remove the level array and its init loop entirely. Hoist q stackalloc above the while(true) loop and reset qh/qt per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.rationale: Eliminates a full O(n) stackalloc plus its zeroing loop that produce nothing, and reduces outer-loop allocations to one. Pure dead-code removal is a guaranteed win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.risk: None — level is provably unused (write-only); removing it cannot change outputs.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.summary: Repeated reduced-cost subexpression pot[u]-pot[v] and cost[e] recompute; hoist pot[u] out of the edge loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.currentCost: Inside the per-node edge scan, `dist[u] + cost[e] + pot[u] - pot[v]` recomputes dist[u]+pot[u] for every outgoing edge of u.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.proposedChange: Hoist `long base = dist[u] + pot[u];` once per node before the edge loop, then `long nd = base + cost[e] - pot[v];`. Same hoist applies in Spfa and Dijkstra inner loops.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.rationale: Removes one add and one load (dist[u], pot[u]) per edge from the inner loop, shortening the dependency chain of the relaxation test.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowPrimal.risk: None — dist[u] and pot[u] are invariant across u's edge scan (not mutated inside the loop body for the current u).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.summary: d/p/eid/q stackalloc'd inside the second while(true); hoist and fuse the init.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.currentCost: Four stackalloc int[n] (d,p,eid,q) plus a 3-field init loop occur each augmenting iteration. Persisted to method end regardless, so re-declaring per pass is wasted frame churn.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.proposedChange: Hoist d, p, eid, q above the second while(true); keep only the per-iteration reset of d (and p/eid as needed). Note p/eid only need reset where d is reset, and d acts as the visited guard, so resetting d[i]=0 alone suffices for correctness (p/eid are only read along the t->s path where d==1).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.rationale: One allocation instead of O(augmentations); and the reset can be narrowed to just `d[i]=0` because p[]/eid[] are only consulted for nodes with d==1 on the recovered path, removing two of three stores per init element.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.risk: Low — must confirm p/eid are never read for a node with d==0; the path walk starts at t (d[t]!=0) and follows p[] which only points to enqueued (d==1) nodes, so unread entries are never touched. Verify before dropping p/eid resets.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.summary: BFS does two separate adjacency passes per node (forward residual then reverse positive-flow) doubling pointer-chasing over the same edge list.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.currentCost: For each dequeued node uu, the code walks `for(e=head[uu]...)` twice: once filtering `cap[e]-flow[e]>0`, once filtering `flow[e]>0`. That is two full traversals of the linked adjacency list (two cache-miss-laden pointer chases) per node per BFS.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.proposedChange: Merge into a single pass: for each e, treat it as usable if its residual `cap[e]-flow[e] > 0` (note the reverse edge e^1 already represents pushed flow as residual capacity in this representation). Verify the edge model: if reverse residual is captured by e^1's cap-flow, the second `flow[e]>0` pass is redundant; otherwise fold both conditions into one `if (cap[e]-flow[e] > 0 || flow[e] > 0)` over a single traversal.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.rationale: Halves the number of linked-list traversals per BFS node, which is the dominant cache-miss source here; fewer next[e] dependency-chain loads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowNetwor.risk: Medium — depends on whether the graph uses paired residual edges (e^1) or stores forward/backward separately. If reverse residual is already via e^1, the second loop double-counts reachability harmlessly but wastes cycles; merging conditions in one pass preserves the visited set exactly. Validate edge representation before applying.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.summary: bucket, inBucket stackalloc'd inside while(true); plus three separate O(n) init loops that can be fused.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.currentCost: Per outer iteration: stackalloc int[n] bucket and inBucket inside the loop, plus separate loops `for(i)bucket[i]=-1`, `for(i)inBucket[i]=0`, and earlier `for(i)dist[i]=long.MaxValue`. Three passes over [0,n).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.proposedChange: Hoist bucket and inBucket above while(true). Fuse the bucket/inBucket reset into a single loop (both length n). dist reset stays separate only because it is long vs int, but it can share the same index loop too.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.rationale: One stack reservation instead of per-iteration; fewer loop-overhead instructions by fusing inits; better write locality streaming two arrays per index.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.risk: None for hoisting/fusing — independent arrays, same length, lifetime already method-scoped.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.summary: Redundant recomputation of residual cap[e]-flow[e] (computed in the continue-guard then again for Math.Min) and rcost components.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.currentCost: In the bucket loop, `cap[e]-flow[e]` is computed in the guard `if (cap[e]-flow[e] <= 0) continue;` and recomputed in `Math.Min(excess[u], cap[e]-flow[e])`. Same in Dijkstra/PrimalDual/Spfa the residual is recomputed in the augment min-pass and again in the apply-pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.proposedChange: Cache `int res = cap[e] - flow[e];` once per edge and reuse for both the guard and the push amount. In the augment loops, the structure already separates passes (acceptable), but within the bucket scan reuse the single res value.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.rationale: Removes one load-load-sub per qualifying edge in the hot scan; shortens the dependency chain feeding Math.Min.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.risk: None — flow[e] is not mutated between the guard and the Math.Min within the same edge iteration, so the cached value is identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.summary: Shortest-path relaxation loop only relaxes edges with rcost<0, which makes it a partial Bellman-Ford that may not converge to true distances; potential update may be suboptimal causing extra outer iterations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.currentCost: The first inner while loop guards relaxation with `if (rcost < 0 && dist[v] > dist[u] + rcost)`. Restricting relaxation to negative-reduced-cost edges means non-negative residual edges never tighten dist, so `potential` updates can be incomplete, potentially increasing the number of outer scaling iterations (each O(V+E)).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.proposedChange: Relax on the standard condition `dist[v] > dist[u] + rcost` (drop the rcost<0 precondition) so the potential function is the true reduced-cost shortest path, matching the textbook cost-scaling/SPFA potential maintenance used in the sibling files. This typically reduces total outer iterations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.rationale: Correct potentials reduce the number of negative-cost relaxation rounds in the bucket phase and overall outer loops, lowering aggregate O((V+E)) passes — an algorithmic constant-to-iteration-count win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.risk: High — this changes the computed potentials and therefore the augmentation order and possibly the iteration count and intermediate state. Only valid if final min-cost flow value is unchanged (it should be for a correct MCMF). Must be validated against existing tests; treat as behavior-affecting, not a blind micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.summary: parent and parentEdge arrays are allocated but never used in this algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.currentCost: `int* parent = stackalloc int[n]; int* parentEdge = stackalloc int[n];` are declared but never read or written anywhere in the cost-scaling routine (it uses bucket-based pushing, not path parent tracking).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.proposedChange: Remove the parent and parentEdge stackallocs from MinCostFlowCostScaling.Run.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.rationale: Frees 2*n*4 bytes of stack frame and removes two reservations; reduces frame size and cache footprint with zero functional effect.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowCostSc.risk: None — both are provably unused in this method (copy-paste residue from the path-based variants).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.summary: stackalloc of pqDist/pqV/pqPos inside the while(true) augment loop accumulates stack across iterations
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.currentCost: Three stackalloc[n] (long+int+int = 16*n bytes) are placed inside the outer while(true) loop (lines 21-23). C# stackalloc inside a loop is NOT freed at end of each iteration; the stack pointer only resets at method return. With up to O(E) augmenting iterations, the stack grows by 16*n bytes per iteration, risking stack overflow on mobile and trashing cache locality.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist the three pqDist/pqV/pqPos stackalloc buffers (and reuse a single allocation) out above the while(true) loop, alongside dist/parent/parentEdge/pot. Reset pqSize=0 and reinitialize pqPos[i]=-1 at the top of each iteration instead of re-allocating.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.rationale: Eliminates unbounded stack growth: O(n) fixed stack instead of O(E*n). Also avoids re-touching fresh (cold) stack pages every iteration, improving cache behavior.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.risk: None semantically; the buffers are fully reinitialized each iteration (pqSize=0, pqPos reset loop already present). Must keep the pqPos[i]=-1 init and pqSize=0 reset at iteration start.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.summary: PushHeap never decrease-keys; duplicate vertices can overflow the n-sized heap buffers
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.currentCost: PushHeap always does i=(*pqSize)++ and writes a new slot (lines 55-56), ignoring pqPos[v]. When an edge relaxes an already-queued vertex (the common Dijkstra case), a second copy is pushed. pqV/pqDist/pqPos are only stackalloc[n], so more than n live entries overflow the buffer (out-of-bounds writes / corrupt pqPos). PopMin sets pqPos[minV]=-1 but Run never re-checks staleness, so stale entries are also popped and re-relaxed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.proposedChange: Adopt the existing MinHeap.PushOrUpdate decrease-key pattern from Flow.cs: if pqPos[v]!=-1 update in place and sift, else insert. This bounds the heap at n entries and removes redundant pops. Alternatively switch Run to delegate to PotentialDijkstra/MinHeap which already implements this correctly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.rationale: Caps heap size at n (no overflow, smaller working set), removes duplicate-entry pops, and reduces total sift operations from O(E log E) toward O(E log V). Lower asymptotic constant and removes a latent buffer-overflow.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.risk: Behavior-preserving for valid graphs once bounded; current code is arguably already incorrect for any vertex relaxed twice. Verify pqPos is consistently maintained on both push and pop paths (PopMin already maintains it).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.summary: n*2 loop bound recomputed and no early-exit when t popped
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.currentCost: Line 11 recomputes n*2 each iteration of the init loop (trivial but trivially hoistable). More importantly, the Dijkstra inner while(pqSize>0) (lines 27-41) drains the entire heap even after t is finalized; the sibling PotentialDijkstra.Run breaks as soon as u==t.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int twoN=n<<1 for the flow-init loop. Add 'if (u==t) break;' after PopMin to stop once the target distance is finalized (Dijkstra guarantees finality on pop).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.rationale: Early t-break stops processing the remainder of the heap on every augmenting phase, cutting relax/sift work substantially on large graphs. Matches the optimization already present in PotentialDijkstra.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.risk: Safe only because pot update on line 43 guards dist[i]<long.MaxValue; vertices not finalized keep dist=MaxValue and are skipped, so pot stays consistent. Confirm no later code depends on dist[] of non-target vertices beyond the pot update (it does not).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.summary: Hot leaf heap methods lack AggressiveInlining and use mul instead of shift for child index
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.currentCost: PushHeap/PopMin are called O(E log V) times but are not marked AggressiveInlining (call overhead per relax). PopMin computes i*2+1, i*2+2 (lines 81) via multiply.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to PushHeap and PopMin. Replace i*2+1 with (i<<1)+1. (Parent (i-1)>>1 is already shift-based.)
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.rationale: Inlining removes call/spill overhead on the hottest inner operations; shift is one cycle vs a multiply on some mobile ARM pipelines. Both are pure constant-factor wins on the tightest loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinCostFlowSsp.cs.risk: None; i>=0 so <<1 equals *2 exactly. Burst already inlines aggressively, so the win is mainly for non-Burst/JIT paths.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.summary: Redundant repeated pointer dereferences of to[e] and reachable indexing in BFS and cut-scan
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.currentCost: In the BFS loop (lines 21-23) to[e] is read up to three times per edge and visited[to[e]] indexed twice. In the cut-scan (lines 28-31) visited[to[e]] and to[e] are re-read. Each is a separate load the compiler may not coalesce across the cap/flow load fence.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.proposedChange: Cache int v=to[e]; once per edge in both loops and reuse v for visited[v] / cutV[cnt]=v. Also hoist int diff=cap[e]-flow[e] used in the condition.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.rationale: Fewer dependent loads on the hot edge-iteration path; lets the compiler keep v in a register and improves the chance of vectorization-friendly straight-line code. Pure constant-factor but on every residual edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.risk: None; values are loop-invariant within the edge body and not mutated between reads.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.summary: visited init loop separate from declaration; could use direct zeroing
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.currentCost: visited is stackalloc[n] then zeroed via an explicit loop (line 14). For large n this is a scalar byte store loop the compiler may not turn into a block clear.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.proposedChange: Keep the loop but note it is the only zeroing needed; alternatively document that callers needing speed can rely on Burst lowering. Minor: the q buffer is sized n which is correct since each vertex enqueued once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumSTCutAll.c.rationale: Marginal; flagged only for completeness. The scalar byte-clear is the lone avoidable overhead and is bounded by n.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.summary: newTo/newNext/newCap/newFlow oversized at n*4 and one buffer (newFlow only needs edgeId entries)
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.currentCost: Four arrays stackalloc[n*4] (lines 12-15) = 4*4*n*4 bytes = 64*n bytes of stack plus newHead. The actual edge count is 2*(n source/sink edges) + 2*(original edge count) entries; n*4 covers only n original edges. If the input graph has more than ~n edges this UNDER-allocates (latent overflow); if fewer, it over-allocates. newFlow needs exactly edgeId+1 entries, not n*4.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.proposedChange: Size buffers from the real edge budget: 2*(n + E) + 2 where E is the original edge count passed in or counted in one pass. At minimum, size newFlow to edgeId after construction (or pass E in). Document the edge-count assumption as a named constant.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.rationale: Correct, tight allocation: removes both the overflow risk for dense graphs and wasted stack for sparse ones; smaller working set improves cache residency of the Dinic passes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.risk: Requires knowing E. Safe fix: count edges in one O(V+E) pass before allocating, or add an E parameter (ergonomics). Do not silently keep n*4 if callers can exceed n edges.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.summary: Final inClosure write uses a redundant ternary on an already-boolean byte
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.currentCost: Line 42: inClosure[u] = (byte)(reachable[u] == 1 ? 1 : 0). reachable[u] is already exactly 0 or 1, so the compare+select is dead work per node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.proposedChange: Write inClosure[u] = reachable[u]; directly (both are byte and reachable holds only 0/1).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.rationale: Removes a compare and a conditional-select per vertex; straight copy is more vectorizable by Burst.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.risk: None provided reachable is only ever assigned 0 or 1 (it is: init 0, set 1). Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.summary: newCap[e]-newFlow[e] and newTo[e] reloaded multiple times in BFS
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.currentCost: Lines 36-38 read newTo[e] up to three times and recompute the residual. Same pattern as MinimumSTCutAll.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.proposedChange: Cache int v=newTo[e]; and the residual once per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/MinimumWeightClos.rationale: Fewer dependent loads on the residual-BFS hot path.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.summary: Rebuilds the entire flow network from scratch n times inside the outer loop; the graph is identical except one i->t edge
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.currentCost: For each i in [0,n) the method: re-zeros newHead (nn), re-adds all source/sink weight edges (O(n)), re-adds ALL original graph edges (O(V+E)), then runs a full DinicMaxFlow. Total O(n*(V+E) + n*Dinic). The only per-i difference is the single 'i->t cap=inf' edge (line 19) and the sink t==i target. This is the Picard-Queyranne parametric structure where the base network is built ONCE and only the s/t connections change.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.proposedChange: Build the base residual network (weight edges + original edges) ONCE outside the i-loop. Per iteration, only attach/detach the single i->t edge and reset flow, or use the monotonic parametric max-flow property (PQ closure) to derive all n cuts from a SINGLE max-flow on the canonical s-t network plus a reachability decomposition, instead of n independent max-flows.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.rationale: Eliminates n-1 full graph reconstructions (O(n*(V+E)) -> O(V+E)) and, with the true Picard-Queyranne algorithm, replaces n max-flow computations with one, turning O(n*MaxFlow) into O(MaxFlow). This is the dominant cost; the asymptotic improvement is large for any non-trivial n.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.risk: Behavioral equivalence must be verified: the current loop returns the minimum cutVal over all i, which the single-network PQ formulation also yields, but the reduction requires care (flow reset between attachments, and DinicMaxFlow mutates cap via residuals). Validate against the existing NUnit tests before landing; if full PQ is too invasive, at least hoist the one-time base-graph construction and deep-copy/reset only cap/flow per iteration.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.summary: Four n*6 buffers stackalloc'd INSIDE the i-loop accumulate stack across iterations
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.currentCost: newHead/newTo/newNext/newCap (lines 14-17) — newTo/newNext/newCap are stackalloc[n*6] (3*4*6*n=72*n bytes) plus newHead, all INSIDE the for(i) loop. As in MinCostFlowSsp, loop stackalloc is not freed per iteration; stack grows ~72*n bytes * n iterations -> O(n^2) stack, near-certain overflow for moderate n on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.proposedChange: Hoist all four buffer stackallocs above the for(i) loop and reset (zero newHead, reset edgeId) at the top of each iteration. Combined with building the base graph once (previous item), most of the reset disappears too.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.rationale: Converts O(n^2) stack consumption into O(n) fixed. Prevents stack overflow and avoids re-faulting cold stack pages every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.risk: None semantically once newHead is re-zeroed and edgeId reset each iteration; the buffers are fully overwritten before use within the iteration.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.summary: newTo/newNext/newCap sized n*6 may under-allocate for dense input graphs (edge count not bounded by n)
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.currentCost: Edges added: 1 (i->t) + up to n (weight edges) + 2*(original edges) per direction. With original edge count E, total residual entries = 2*(1 + n + E). n*6 only suffices when E <= ~2n. Dense graphs overflow these buffers (OOB writes during construction).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.proposedChange: Size from actual E (count once or pass as parameter): 2*(n + E + 1). Use a named constant for the per-node edge multiplier and assert/encode the assumption.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.rationale: Removes latent buffer overflow for dense graphs and right-sizes the working set for sparse ones.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.risk: Requires E. Pair with the build-once refactor where E is naturally available from the single construction pass; do not keep the magic n*6 if callers can exceed it.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.summary: DinicMaxFlow writes into caller's flow buffer but flow is never reset between iterations
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.currentCost: Line 28 calls DinicMaxFlow.Run(... flow) reusing the caller-provided flow array across all n iterations without re-zeroing. DinicMaxFlow itself does not zero flow on entry (Flow.cs line 330-345). Stale residual flow from iteration i-1 leaks into iteration i, making the result order-dependent and impure.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.proposedChange: Zero the relevant flow entries (0..edgeId) at the start of each iteration, or use a hoisted local newFlow buffer reset per iteration rather than the shared flow param.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.rationale: Makes each iteration's max-flow independent and the function deterministic/pure for a given input, eliminating hidden cross-iteration state.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PicardQueyranneCl.risk: This is a correctness fix, not just perf — verify current test expectations; if tests pass today it may be by accident of the inf i->t edge. Resetting flow per iteration is the semantically safe behavior the cut formula assumes.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.summary: Cache head[u] once and hoist flow[head[u]] reload in Push; eliminate redundant pointer-arithmetic loads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.currentCost: Push reads head[u] three times (lines 61,63) and flow[head[u]] twice on line 61 plus once on line 63 (two indexed loads through the same address). Each head[u] is a dependent load (base+index) feeding another dependent load flow[head[u]], creating a long dependency chain executed on every push.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.proposedChange: int hu = head[u]; int f = flow[hu]; int push = Math.Min(excess[u], cap[hu] - f); excess[u] -= push; excess[v] += push; flow[hu] = f + push; flow[hu ^ 1] -= push;
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.rationale: Reduces 3 loads of head[u] to 1 and 2 loads of flow[head[u]] to 1, shortening the load-dependent chain and cutting memory-uop count on the hottest leaf method. Burst keeps hu/f in registers.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.risk: None. Observable behavior identical: flow[hu] is written exactly once with the same final value (f+push); v and n are unused by the original body so still ignored. Note the original already ignores the e/v passed in (uses head[u]); this change preserves that exact (buggy-but-intended-unchecked) behavior.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.summary: Hoist height[u] into a local across the per-edge loop; it is read up to 3x per edge and only changes after the loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.currentCost: Inside the edge loop (lines 33-43) height[u] is loaded on lines 33, 37, 38 for every incident edge. height[u] is loop-invariant within the edge scan (only mutated on line 46 after the loop), so each iteration re-loads it from the stack array.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.proposedChange: int hu = height[u]; count[hu]++; for(...) { int v2 = to[e]; if(flow[e^1]>0 && hu>height[v2]+1) count[hu]--; else if(flow[e]>0 && hu==height[v2]+1){ Push(...); if(excess[u]==0) break; } }
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.rationale: Removes 2 redundant dependent loads of height[u] per edge in the inner scan, freeing load ports and shortening the comparison dependency chain. height[v2] still loaded once as required.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.risk: None. height[u] is provably invariant during the edge loop (only line 46 mutates it, after the loop). count[hu] indexes the same slot consistently.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.summary: The outer while loop (lines 25-52) dequeues v then unconditionally rebuilds the entire BFS/discharge from t every iteration, doing O(outer * (n+E)) redundant full passes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.currentCost: Line 27 reads v (never used). Lines 28-29 zero count[] and reset the queue to {t} on EVERY outer iteration, so the inner while (30-51) re-discharges the whole frontier from scratch each time. The outer loop's queue (q) is simultaneously reset to t inside, so qh/qt bookkeeping at the outer level is dead — the outer loop effectively just repeats the same inner sweep until convergence, an O(n+E) pass per outer turn with no carried state.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.proposedChange: Restructure so the active-vertex queue carries between sweeps (as PushRelabelGlobalRelabel does) instead of re-seeding {t} and re-zeroing count each outer pass; or at minimum drop the dead 'int v = q[qh++]' read and the dead outer qh/qt manipulation. Verify against the test suite since the current control flow is convoluted.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.rationale: Eliminating repeated full-graph re-discharge changes the constant/asymptotic factor of the gap variant from repeated O(n+E) sweeps to incremental work proportional to actual relabels/pushes, matching standard gap-heuristic push-relabel.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.risk: High-risk refactor: the current outer/inner queue interplay is subtle and possibly already incorrect (the unused v, the per-iteration count reset). Must be gated behind the NUnit Flow tests; do not land without green tests. Flagged as opportunity, not a blind rewrite.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.summary: ptr[] is allocated and initialized (lines 20-21) but never read anywhere in the gap variant.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.currentCost: stackalloc int[n] plus an O(n) init loop writing head[i] into ptr[i], consuming n*4 bytes of stack and n stores per call, with zero subsequent reads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.proposedChange: Delete the ptr declaration and its initialization loop (lines 20-21).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.rationale: Removes a dead n-element stack buffer and an O(n) write loop from every call: less stack pressure (matters on mobile/Burst stack budgets) and fewer cache lines touched at startup.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.summary: Fuse the four separate per-index initializations on line 13 — they already are fused, but the count[] re-zero on line 28 runs inside the outer loop and can be hoisted/avoided.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.currentCost: Line 28 'for(i) count[i]=0' executes once per outer-loop iteration, an O(n) memset repeated for every dequeued v, even though the inner sweep recomputes count from scratch each time.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.proposedChange: If the outer loop is kept as-is, replace the explicit zeroing loop with Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned over count (n*4 bytes) which Burst lowers to vectorized stores; or, after the restructure above, this becomes unnecessary.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.rationale: A vectorized clear of n ints is faster than a scalar store loop and avoids per-element loop overhead; better still is eliminating the repeated clear via the structural fix.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGap.cs.risk: None for the InitBlock substitution (same zeroed result). The structural elimination depends on the line-25 refactor and must be test-gated.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.summary: In the discharge inner loop, to[e] is loaded twice and the height comparison recomputes; cache v's height and hoist height[u].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.currentCost: Lines 50-57: v=to[e] then height[v] (line 52) and excess[v] (lines 56,57) each re-index. height[u] (lines 52) reloaded per edge though invariant across the ptr walk for a fixed u. Within one discharge of u, height[u] only changes between outer relabel passes, not inside the while(ptr[u]!=0) loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.proposedChange: Hoist int hu = height[u]; before the while(ptr[u]!=0) loop and use hu in the comparison height[u]==height[v]+1 -> hu==height[v]+1. Keep v=to[e] single-load (already single). Optionally hold int eu = excess[u] in a local and write back once at break/exit to avoid repeated excess[u] load/store.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.rationale: height[u] is invariant during a single u-discharge, so hoisting removes one dependent load per edge. Keeping excess[u] in a register across the inner pushes removes a load+store pair per push from the chain that feeds Math.Min.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.risk: Low. height[u] is not mutated inside the discharge while-loop (only set in the global-relabel pass at line 41), so hoisting is safe. If excess[u] is registerized, must store it back before any path that re-reads excess[u] (the line-65 convergence check is after the discharge loop, so write-back at loop exit suffices).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.summary: BFS relabel loop loads to[e] twice per qualifying edge (lines 35 and 37).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.currentCost: Lines 35-37: 'if (flow[rev] > 0 && dist[to[e]] == -1) { dist[to[e]] = dist[u] + 1; q[qt++] = to[e]; }' computes to[e] three times (two reads in line 35-37 dist index, one for q store).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.proposedChange: int w = to[e]; if (flow[rev] > 0 && dist[w] == -1) { dist[w] = dist[u] + 1; q[qt++] = w; }
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.rationale: Collapses 3 loads of to[e] to 1 in the BFS hot edge loop; to[] is a separate cache stream so each saved load is a real memory-uop saving across the global-relabel passes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.risk: None — to[e] is pure load of immutable edge data; single read is equivalent.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.summary: dist init (line 26) and the dist->height copy (line 41) are two separate O(n) passes that can be fused, and height re-derivation can avoid the branch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.currentCost: Line 26 sets dist[i]=-1 (O(n)); after BFS line 41 does 'height[i] = dist[i] >= 0 ? dist[i] + 1 : 0' (O(n) with a branch/select per element). Two full sweeps over n plus a conditional select.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.proposedChange: Keep line 41 but note dist[i]>=0?dist[i]+1:0 is branchless via Burst select already; alternatively store height directly during BFS (height[t]=1, height[w]=dist[u]+2...) and memset height/dist with Unsafe.InitBlock. Initialize unreachable heights to 0 with one InitBlockUnaligned then overwrite reached nodes, removing the per-element ternary.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.rationale: Folding the -1 sentinel pass and the height-derivation pass reduces two O(n) memory sweeps to roughly one, lowering cache traffic each global-relabel iteration (which runs many times).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.risk: Low. Must preserve that unreachable-from-t nodes get height 0 (line 41 's else branch). Writing height during BFS requires initializing all height[i]=0 first via InitBlock to match the else=0 semantics exactly.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.summary: Convergence check (line 65) rescans all n vertices for residual excess every global-relabel pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.currentCost: Lines 64-66 do an O(n) scan over excess[] after each discharge phase to detect any active vertex. With many global-relabel iterations this is O(passes*n).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.proposedChange: Track an active-count or set a 'producedActive' flag during the discharge loop (incremented when a vertex is enqueued with excess>0 and decremented when fully discharged) so the outer loop can terminate without the full rescan, or break early as soon as the first active vertex is found (already breaks on first, so impact is bounded).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.rationale: Avoids a full O(n) excess sweep per outer pass; for sparse-active graphs the active set is far smaller than n.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Flow/PushRelabelGlobal.risk: Low-to-medium: maintaining an accurate active counter across pushes is error-prone (a vertex can gain/lose excess multiple times). Must be test-gated; the early-break already caps worst case so this is a minor win.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.summary: Cache f[u] to avoid loading it twice when seeding slow/fast.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: Lines 10-11 read f[u] twice from memory (slow = f[u]; fast = f[f[u]]). The second f[u] is a redundant dependent load that the JIT/Burst may or may not CSE through a raw pointer because aliasing with the comp/output is not provable in general; the value is also re-fetched for the inner f[...] step.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: int fu = f[u]; int slow = fu; int fast = f[fu]; This computes f[u] once and reuses it for both seeds.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: Removes one dependent load on the hot setup path and shortens the dependency chain for the first fast step. f[u] is loop-invariant for the seed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.risk: None. f is read-only here; no writes occur between the two reads of f[u], so the value is identical. Pure semantics preserved.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.summary: Unused parameter n in the signature.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: n is accepted but never used. It costs an extra argument register/stack slot at the call site and misleads callers into thinking bounds are checked or used.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: Drop the int n parameter, or keep it only for signature symmetry with the other Functional* Run methods if the family must stay uniform. If kept for consistency, document that it is intentionally unused (unchecked Run).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: Fewer arguments marshalled; clearer contract. Burst/JIT will already discard it, so this is purely an API/clarity win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.risk: Removing it breaks signature uniformity across the FunctionalGraph* family. If the family relies on a common signature shape (e.g. dispatch tables), keep n and just note it. No behavior change either way.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.summary: O(k) walk can be reduced to O(n) by exploiting eventual periodicity of a functional graph (rho structure), since n is available.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: for (long i = 0; i < k; i++) curr = f[curr]; performs exactly k dependent pointer chases. k is a long, so for large k this is unbounded work even though the trajectory from u repeats with period <= n. Each iteration is a serial cache-miss-prone dependent load.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: First walk at most n steps; detect entry of the cycle and its length L (e.g. via Floyd / Brent or tortoise-hare reusing FunctionalGraphCycleEntry). Let mu be the tail length (steps until cycle). If k <= mu, just walk k steps. Otherwise walk mu steps to the cycle entry, then take ((k - mu) % L) more steps. Total work O(mu + L) = O(n) instead of O(k).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: Trajectories in a functional graph are eventually periodic with period L <= n. Reducing k modulo L collapses arbitrarily large k to at most n + n steps, an asymptotic improvement from O(k) to O(n) whenever k > n.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.risk: Changes the performance model, not the result; output is identical for all valid k. Net loss when k < ~2n (the cycle-detection overhead dominates), so guard with: if (k <= n) use the simple loop, else use the rho-reduction. % on (k - mu): k>=mu and L>0 guarantee non-negative operands, so no signed-% surprise. Requires f to define a valid successor for every visited index (already assumed by unchecked Run).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: n is passed but unused in the current O(k) implementation; it costs an argument slot and signals an unenforced contract.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: If the rho-reduction above is NOT adopted, n is dead and could be dropped. If the reduction IS adopted, n becomes load-bearing (bounds the detection walk) and should stay. Decide together with the complexity change.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: Either remove dead arg for a leaner call, or give it a real use via the periodicity optimization.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.risk: Dropping it breaks family signature uniformity; see CycleEntry note. No behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.summary: O(k) weighted walk can be reduced to O(n) using cycle periodicity plus a precomputed full-cycle weight sum.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: for (long i = 0; i < k; i++) { sum += w[curr]; curr = f[curr]; } chases k dependent links and accumulates k loads from w. Unbounded in k despite the trajectory repeating every L <= n steps with a fixed per-cycle weight sum.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: Walk the tail (mu steps) accumulating w, reaching the cycle entry. Compute cycleSum = sum of w over the L cycle nodes once. For the remaining r = k - mu steps: add (r / L) * cycleSum, then walk r % L more steps adding their w. Total O(mu + L) = O(n). Guard: if (k <= n) keep the simple loop to avoid setup overhead.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: The weight accumulated per full cycle traversal is constant, so full laps can be multiplied instead of walked. Drops O(k) to O(n) for k > n, the dominant case for large k.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.risk: Result identical for all valid k. Overflow caveat: (r / L) * cycleSum and the running sum are long; if the original O(k) sum could already overflow long, the reduced form overflows identically (two's-complement multiply/add are associative under wraparound), so observable behavior is preserved only if callers tolerate the same wraparound — which the straight loop already exhibits. r/L and r%L use non-negative operands (r>=0, L>0), so no signed-division edge case. Requires w and f valid over visited indices (already assumed).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.summary: Two interleaved dependent loads (w[curr] then f[curr]) form one long dependency chain per step; minor reordering does not break it but the chain is inherent to the simple loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: Each iteration: load w[curr], add, then load f[curr] to advance. curr is carried, so f[curr] is on the critical path; w[curr] can issue in parallel but both index the same register. Throughput is bound by the f[curr]->curr->f[curr] chain (~load latency per step).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: If staying with the O(k) loop, the only real win is the complexity reduction above; there is no branchless or strength-reduction trick that shortens an inherently serial pointer chase. Do not add speculative unrolling — the dependency on curr prevents ILP. Flagged only to record that the per-step cost is latency-bound and cannot be improved without the algorithmic change.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: Documents that micro-opts here are cargo-cult; the genuine lever is asymptotic, not constant-factor.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.risk: None proposed; this is an explicit non-opportunity to prevent wasted effort.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.summary: Unimplemented stub: returns 0 unconditionally; not an optimization target.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: Body is `return 0;` regardless of f, n, comp. No algorithm present, so there is nothing to optimize; AggressiveInlining on a constant-return stub is harmless but meaningless.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: No optimization possible until implemented. When implemented (weakly connected components of a functional graph = union-find or cycle-root labeling over the f-pointers), the natural O(n) approach is to label each node by its cycle root using the CycleEntry machinery and a single pass writing into comp; design it in-place over comp with no scratch buffer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: Flagging that this file is a placeholder so reviewers do not mistake it for finished hot-path code.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.risk: None; reporting state only. Changing the stub would change behavior by definition.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.summary: Unimplemented stub: returns -1 unconditionally; not an optimization target.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.currentCost: Body is `return -1;`. No traversal of f for u and v occurs, so there is no work to optimize.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.proposedChange: No optimization possible until implemented. When implemented (first common node of the two trajectories from u and v in a functional graph), an O(n) approach computes depth-to-cycle for each via tortoise-hare, aligns the longer tail, then advances both pointers in lockstep; or detect shared cycle and compare entry points. Keep it allocation-free over raw pointers; n bounds the walk.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Functional/FunctionalG.rationale: Flagging placeholder status so it is not treated as live hot-path code.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.summary: MinHeap does three separate AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal heap allocations per Dijkstra invocation; this is called once per unmatched vertex (O(n) times), so O(n) malloc/free round-trips dominate the constant factor.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.currentCost: 3 AllocHGlobal + 3 FreeHGlobal per min_cost_augment call, called up to n times => up to 3n mallocs and 3n frees, each a kernel/CRT round-trip, plus an O(n) Pos init loop each time.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.proposedChange: Replace the three AllocHGlobal buffers with caller-provided scratch (stackalloc in WeightedBlossom.Run, sized 3*n: long[n] for Dist, int[n] for V, int[n] for Pos) and pass pointers into MinHeap. Since min_cost_augment already stackallocs dist/parent of size n, allocate the heap buffers once in Run and reuse across all n augment calls, re-initializing Pos to -1 (or better, lazily via a generation counter) each call.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.rationale: Eliminates 3n malloc/free syscalls, removes try/finally overhead, and keeps the heap working set in stack/registers improving cache locality. Reusing one buffer across iterations turns O(n) allocations into O(1).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.risk: stackalloc size n*(sizeof(long)+2*sizeof(int)) per Run is fine for moderate n but can overflow the stack for very large n; if n is unbounded keep a single AllocHGlobal pair reused across the outer loop instead of per-augment. Pos must be reset to -1 between augment calls (Pop sets visited entries to -1, but un-popped entries remain stale), so a full re-init or generation-stamp is required for correctness.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.summary: Inner relaxation recomputes the loop-invariant base term dist[u]-potentials[u] every iteration and indexes w[u*n+j] with a multiply that can be hoisted to a running pointer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.currentCost: Per inner iteration: load dist[u], load potentials[u], one subtract that is invariant across j; plus an integer multiply u*n inside the address computation for w.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.proposedChange: Hoist 'long baseU = dist[u] - potentials[u];' and 'long* wRow = w + (long)u * n;' before the j-loop, then 'long ndist = baseU + wRow[j] - potentials[j];'. This removes one subtraction and the u*n multiply from every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.rationale: Strength-reduces the index multiply to a single pointer add per row and shortens the per-iteration dependency chain by one subtraction. Over n calls x n vertices x n edges this is O(n^3) iterations, so each removed op is meaningful.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.risk: None; arithmetic is associative for the integer additions here and (long)u*n avoids 32-bit overflow on large n (the original u*n is int and could overflow for n where u*n exceeds int range; widening is a strict improvement, guard worth noting).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.summary: The 'if (i == j) continue;' branch in the hot O(n^2) relaxation per augment can be eliminated by structuring the loop to skip i without a per-iteration test, or by relying on dist[i]=0 making the self-edge non-improving.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.currentCost: One compare+branch per inner iteration (n per call, n*n per augment, n^3 overall) purely to skip the source vertex.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.proposedChange: Drop the 'i == j' guard entirely: since dist[i] starts at 0 and w[u*n+i]-potentials[u]-potentials[i] for the reduced cost is non-negative under valid potentials, ndist for j==i will not be < dist[i]=0, so the update is naturally skipped. If non-negativity is not guaranteed, split the loop into [0,i) and (i,n) to avoid the branch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.rationale: Removes a predictable-but-nonzero branch from the innermost loop, helping Burst vectorize the relaxation as a straight-line reduction over j.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.risk: Removing the guard is only safe if reduced edge costs to the source are non-negative (true after Johnson-style potential maintenance with no negative cycles). If that invariant is not certain, use the loop-splitting variant which is unconditionally equivalent.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.summary: Heap parent/child index math uses '/2' and '*2+1'; '/2' on a known-nonnegative idx can be a shift, and the sift loops recompute child indices.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.currentCost: (idx-1)/2 emits a signed division-by-2 sequence (sign-correcting) rather than a shift; left=idx*2+1/right=idx*2+2 recompute multiplies.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.proposedChange: Use '(idx - 1) >> 1' for the parent (idx>=1 in that branch so non-negative) and 'int left = (idx << 1) + 1; int right = left + 1;' to derive right from left.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.rationale: Signed '/2' on a value the compiler cannot prove non-negative emits extra add+shift for rounding; an explicit '>>1' on a provably non-negative value is one shift. Deriving right=left+1 saves a multiply.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.risk: '>>1' is only equivalent to '/2' for non-negative operands; idx>0 in PushOrUpdate's loop and idx>=0 in Pop guarantee (idx-1)>=0 and idx>=0, so the substitution is exact. Burst likely already does this, so impact is low.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.summary: Blossom contraction uses O(n) full-array scans (GetLca clears inPath[0..n), UpdateBases rewrites base_ across all n) inside the augmenting-path search, giving an O(n^3)+ overall worst case typical of array-based blossom.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.currentCost: GetLca does an O(n) inPath clear per odd-cycle encounter; UpdateBases does an O(n) base_ rewrite per contracted vertex; both run inside FindAugmentingPath which itself runs n times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.proposedChange: Track only the vertices actually touched during the current BFS (a small worklist) to clear inPath, and maintain base_ via a union-find (path-compressed) structure so contraction is near-O(alpha) amortized instead of O(n) per step. This lowers the blossom matching from ~O(n^3) toward O(n*m*alpha(n)).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.rationale: The dominant cost in array-based blossom is the repeated full-width base_/inPath sweeps; union-find with path compression is the standard asymptotic improvement and also reduces cache traffic by avoiding full-array passes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Blossom.cs.risk: This is an algorithmic rewrite, not a micro-opt; must preserve exact matching results and the same edge-iteration order to keep deterministic output. Union-find base tracking needs careful reset between sources. Higher implementation risk; propose only if blossom is a hot path.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/AssignmentAuc.summary: Run is a stub that only initializes match/prices and never reads cost or runs the auction; the AggressiveInlining hint and cost/n parameters imply an unimplemented algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/AssignmentAuc.currentCost: No algorithmic work performed; 'cost' parameter is unused, so callers get a no-op that returns nothing meaningful.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/AssignmentAuc.proposedChange: Either implement the auction relaxation or mark the method clearly as initialization-only. If kept as init, the two init loops can be fused into one loop over i setting both match[i]=-1 and prices[i]=0 to halve loop overhead.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/AssignmentAuc.rationale: Fusing the two independent O(n) init passes into one halves loop bookkeeping and improves cache behavior; currently there is only one loop already, so the main signal is that the algorithm body is missing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/AssignmentAuc.risk: Behavioral: implementing the algorithm changes outputs by design. The loop-fusion note does not apply (already a single loop); flagged primarily because the file appears to be an unfinished stub.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.summary: minv and used are stackalloc'd inside the per-row loop, allocating n+1 longs and n+1 ints on every one of the n iterations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.currentCost: Lines 18-21: `long* minv = stackalloc long[n+1]` and `int* used = stackalloc int[n+1]` execute once per outer i loop (n times). Stack pointer advances n*(n+1) longs + n*(n+1) ints worth of stack across the loop, which the JIT/Burst typically does NOT reclaim until method exit, causing O(n^2) stack growth and risking stack overflow for moderate n.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.proposedChange: Hoist both allocations above the `for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)` loop: `long* minv = stackalloc long[n+1]; int* used = stackalloc int[n+1];`. Keep the two existing re-init loops (`minv[j]=long.MaxValue`, `used[j]=0`) inside the i-loop where they already are so each row starts fresh.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.rationale: Eliminates O(n^2) cumulative stack reservation, replacing it with a single O(n) allocation reused across rows. Same memory traffic for the re-init writes (already present), but the working set is one buffer that stays hot in cache instead of marching down the stack.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.risk: Semantics-preserving only because both buffers are fully re-initialized at the top of each i-iteration (minv to LONG_MAX, used to 0). Verified: every entry index 0..n is rewritten before use, so no stale data leaks between rows.
