src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.summary: Loop-invariant u[i0] reload and redundant base-offset recomputation in the inner j loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.currentCost: Line 48: `a[(i0-1)*n + (j-1)] - u[i0] - v[j]` recomputes `(i0-1)*n` and reloads `u[i0]` for every j in 1..n. This is the hottest inner loop of the algorithm (O(n^3) total executions).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.proposedChange: Before the loop: `long ui = u[i0]; long* arow = a + (long)(i0 - 1) * n - 1;` (the -1 folds the (j-1) index). Then inside: `long cur = arow[j] - ui - v[j];`. Hoists the multiply and the u[i0] load out of the loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.rationale: Removes one integer multiply, one add, and one dependent load from each of the n inner iterations, shortening the dependency chain feeding `cur` and freeing the compiler to keep `ui`/`arow` in registers. Pure constant-factor win on the dominant O(n^3) path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.risk: `(long)(i0-1)*n` must be computed in 64-bit to match the existing `(i0-1)*n` index arithmetic for large n*n; using a long* base pointer preserves identical addressing. No behavioral change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.summary: used[] stores only 0/1 but is typed int (4 bytes); a byte buffer cuts its footprint and cache pressure 4x.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.currentCost: `int* used = stackalloc int[n+1]` plus all reads/writes in UpdateMinvAndWay and ApplyDelta touch 4-byte slots for a boolean flag, occupying 4(n+1) bytes of the hot working set alongside minv.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.proposedChange: Change `used` to `byte* used = stackalloc byte[n+1]`, set `used[j0] = 1`, test `used[j] != 0`. Adjust the helper signatures from `int* used` to `byte* used`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.rationale: Quarters the bytes touched by the used array, improving L1 residency for the inner scan and reducing total stack working set. Byte loads/stores compile to the same cost as int on the flag check.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.risk: Pure flag semantics (only 0/1 ever stored and only compared !=0), so narrowing is provably safe. Requires updating helper method signatures consistently.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.summary: Allocates a full n*n scratch matrix solely to negate the cost matrix before delegating to HungarianMin.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.currentCost: Line 86-87: `long* maxA = stackalloc long[n*n]` plus an O(n^2) negation pass. This doubles the matrix storage on the stack (n*n longs = 8*n^2 bytes) purely to flip signs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.proposedChange: Cannot negate in place without mutating the caller's `a`. Document that the n*n stackalloc is inherent, but the negation pass can be fused or, better, expose a sign/transform flag inside HungarianMin so max-assignment reuses the input directly. Minimum change: note that for large n this stackalloc may overflow the stack and a caller-provided scratch pointer would be safer ergonomically.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.rationale: Avoiding the duplicate n*n buffer halves peak stack memory for the max variant, which matters on mobile where stack budgets are tight (e.g. n=256 is 512KB just for maxA).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Hungarian.cs.risk: Negating in place would mutate caller input (breaks purity); only acceptable if API contract changes. The flag-based approach inside HungarianMin preserves semantics but is a larger refactor. Flag, don't silently change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.summary: seen[] is fully re-zeroed (O(nRight)) before every left vertex even though most entries are untouched by the previous augmenting search.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.currentCost: Lines 15 and 45: `for (int i=0;i<nRight;i++) seen[i]=0` runs nLeft times = O(nLeft*nRight) just clearing the visited array, often dwarfing the actual DFS work in sparse graphs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.proposedChange: Replace the boolean seen[] with a timestamp/iteration-stamp array: `int* seen = stackalloc int[nRight]` initialized to 0 once, plus an `int stamp` incremented per left vertex. Test `seen[v] == stamp` instead of `!= 0`, and write `seen[v] = stamp`. Drop the per-vertex clear loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.rationale: Converts O(nLeft*nRight) clearing into O(nRight) one-time init plus O(1) stamp bump per vertex. For sparse bipartite graphs the augmenting paths touch far fewer than nRight nodes, so this removes the dominant overhead.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.risk: stamp could theoretically overflow after 2^31 left-vertex iterations; for any realistic n this never happens, but guard by re-zeroing seen and resetting stamp to 1 if stamp hits int.MaxValue. Otherwise behavior is identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.summary: BFS queue q is stackalloc'd inside the per-component start loop, causing repeated O(n) stack reservations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.currentCost: Line 144: `int* q = stackalloc int[n]` sits inside `for (int start...)`, so across components the stack pointer marches by n ints per component (not reclaimed until method return), O(n*components) cumulative stack reservation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int* q = stackalloc int[n];` above the `for (int start = 0; start < n; start++)` loop. qh/qt are reset to 0 per component already, so no re-init needed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.rationale: Single O(n) allocation reused across all components instead of one per component; avoids unbounded stack growth and keeps one queue buffer hot in cache.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.risk: None: q is logically reset by qh=qt=0 each component and fully overwritten before read. Semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.summary: Recursive augmenting-path DFS passes 5-6 pointer arguments and recurses, which Burst handles but with call overhead and a stack-depth risk up to O(nLeft).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.currentCost: Each recursive TryKuhn call re-passes head,to,next,matchRight,seen; deep alternating paths recurse up to nLeft frames. Recursion also blocks some Burst inlining/vectorization of the leaf scan.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] is not viable for the recursive call, but converting to an explicit augmenting-path loop with a parent-pointer / iterative DFS over a stackalloc'd frame array removes recursion depth risk and the repeated argument marshaling.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.rationale: Iterative DFS bounds stack to a single stackalloc buffer and lets Burst keep the pointer args in registers across the inner edge scan, reducing per-edge call overhead on the O(V*E) path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/Kuhn.cs.risk: Iterative rewrite must faithfully reproduce the matchRight reassignment order on path success; non-trivial refactor, so verify against existing NUnit tests. Behavior must remain identical for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.summary: Repeated recomputation of the womanRank row base `w*n` (and `m*n`) within rank comparisons.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.currentCost: Line 46: `womanRank[w*n + m] < womanRank[w*n + m2]` computes `w*n` twice. Line 41 recomputes `m*n` for manPref. Minor but on the hot proposal loop which runs O(n^2) times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.proposedChange: Hoist `int* wrow = womanRank + (long)w * n;` then compare `wrow[m] < wrow[m2]`. Similarly cache `int* mrow = manPref + (long)m * n;` in ProcessProposal.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.rationale: Removes one integer multiply per comparison and shortens the address-computation dependency chain on the O(n^2) proposal path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.risk: Index arithmetic must use the same width as existing `w*n` (int) to avoid changing results for very large n; use long base offset to be safe. No behavioral change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MaximumBipart.summary: Method is an unimplemented stub that unconditionally returns 0; AggressiveInlining on an empty body is meaningless and the API is non-functional.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MaximumBipart.currentCost: Returns 0 regardless of input. No algorithm present, so there is nothing to optimize until implemented; the [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] attribute is dead.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MaximumBipart.proposedChange: Either implement b-matching (max-flow / capacity-scaled Hopcroft-Karp over the existing CSR head/to/next representation) or remove the stub. The capacitiesLeft/capacitiesRight signature suggests a Dinic-style b-matching; reuse the HopcroftKarp machinery in Kuhn.cs with per-vertex capacities.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MaximumBipart.rationale: No cycle/ram win is possible on an empty function; flagging so it is not mistaken for optimized code. If implemented, sharing the CSR traversal helpers avoids duplicate graph-walk code.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MaximumBipart.risk: Not an optimization of existing behavior; it is a correctness/completeness gap. Implementing changes observable behavior (currently always 0), so it must be coordinated with callers/tests.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MinimumCostBi.summary: Unimplemented stub returning 0; nothing to optimize until an actual min-cost-flow / SSP algorithm exists.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MinimumCostBi.currentCost: Always returns 0. The cost and capacity pointers are unused. AggressiveInlining attribute on an empty body is dead.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MinimumCostBi.proposedChange: Implement via successive-shortest-paths (SPFA/Bellman-Ford with potentials -> Dijkstra) min-cost max-flow over the CSR graph, reusing the head/to/next layout. Until then there is no perf surface.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MinimumCostBi.rationale: Empty body has no cycles or memory to tune; flagging to prevent it being counted as optimized. A potentials-based SSP gives O(F * E log V) which is the right asymptotic target for this signature.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/MinimumCostBi.risk: Implementation changes observable output (currently always 0); coordinate with tests. Not a semantics-preserving micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.summary: Method is an unimplemented stub; the actual Gale-Shapley algorithm body is absent, so no algorithmic optimization is possible until it is written.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.currentCost: Two O(n) and O(m) init loops set matchMen[i]=-1 and matchWomen[j]=-1. The pref/numPref/n/m parameters are accepted but completely unused; no matching is performed and unstable/incomplete output is always returned.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.proposedChange: Implement the Gale-Shapley deferred-acceptance algorithm for incomplete preference lists (proposer pointer per man, rank-inverse table for women to make 'prefers' an O(1) comparison instead of an O(list) scan). The two existing init loops are already optimal as the array-clear preamble.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.rationale: There is currently nothing to strength-reduce or vectorize beyond the two -1 fills, which Burst already lowers to a vectorized store loop. The only meaningful win is implementing the algorithm with an inverse-rank table so each acceptance test is O(1), giving overall O(n*m) instead of O(n*m^2).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableMarriag.risk: Low risk for the observation itself. When implemented, building an inverse-rank table costs extra O(n*m) RAM (int* of size n*m); under the no-managed-array house rule the caller must supply that scratch buffer or it must be stackalloc'd, which is unsafe for large m on mobile stack limits. Flag scratch ownership in the API.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableRoommat.summary: Method is an unimplemented stub; Irving's stable-roommates algorithm body is absent. It always returns false after clearing match[].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableRoommat.currentCost: Single O(n) loop sets match[i]=-1, then unconditionally returns false. The pref parameter is unused; a stable matching is never computed even when one exists, so the result is always wrong for solvable instances.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableRoommat.proposedChange: Implement Irving's two-phase algorithm (phase 1 proposals with inverse-rank lookup; phase 2 rotation elimination). Keep the existing match[] clear loop as the preamble; it is already an optimal vectorizable fill.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableRoommat.rationale: No constant-factor or branchless win exists in a one-line clear-and-return stub. The genuine improvement is implementing Irving's O(n^2) algorithm using an inverse-rank table so 'prefers a to b' is an O(1) integer compare rather than an O(n) list scan.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Matching/StableRoommat.risk: Low for the observation. Implementation will require O(n^2) scratch (inverse-rank and/or rank-position tables); under house constraints this must be a caller-provided int* buffer, not a managed array. Note n^2 ints may exceed stackalloc safety on mobile for large n.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.summary: Hoist dp[u] out of the inner adjacency loop and fuse the final max scan into the main DP pass to eliminate a redundant full read of dp[].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.currentCost: Inner loop re-reads dp[u] from memory on every edge (dp[u] + 1 recomputed each iteration), and a separate trailing loop re-reads all n entries of dp[] for the max, doubling memory traffic over dp.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.proposedChange: Inside the i-loop, load `long du1 = dp[u] + 1;` once before the edge loop and compare `if (du1 > dp[v]) dp[v] = du1;`. Track the running max in the same outer pass: after the edge loop (or when finalizing dp[u]) update `if (dp[u] > max) max = dp[u]`. Note dp is processed in topological order so dp[u] is final when visited; fold the max update there to drop the second loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.rationale: Removes one add per edge from the dependency chain, and eliminates an O(n) second pass that re-streams dp[] from memory (extra cache traffic). Fewer instructions in the hottest loop and one fewer full array sweep.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.risk: dp[u] is final at visit time only if 'order' is a valid topological order (guaranteed by the unchecked Run contract). Max-folding into the main loop preserves the result as long as dp[u] is not later increased; under a valid topo order it never is. If callers could pass dp with negative initial values and n==0, max stays 0 as before.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.summary: Use a 1-byte visited marker instead of long[n], and skip the explicit zero-init loop by relying on stackalloc-then-clear of the narrower buffer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.currentCost: visited is stackalloc long[n] = 8*n bytes plus an n-iteration zero loop. Only a 0/1 flag is stored, so 7 of every 8 bytes are wasted, increasing cache footprint for the functional-graph walk.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.proposedChange: Declare `byte* visited = stackalloc byte[n];` and clear with `Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(visited, 0, (uint)n);` (or a byte loop). Compare/set with byte 0/1. This shrinks the working set 8x.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.rationale: Smaller working set means fewer cache lines touched during the random `cur = next[cur]` chase, which is the dominant cost in a functional-graph traversal. A single InitBlock is also cheaper than a per-element long store loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.risk: Semantics identical (flag only ever 0 or 1). Burst supports Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned; if disallowed, keep a byte loop. n must fit stackalloc as before (already assumed).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.summary: Hoist dp[u] in ProcessScc and recompute the relax candidate once per neighbor.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.currentCost: ProcessScc computes `dp[u] + sum[v]` twice per edge (once in the comparison, once in the assignment) and re-loads dp[u] every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.proposedChange: At the top of ProcessScc load `long du = dp[u];` once, then per edge compute `long cand = du + sum[v];` and do `if (cand > dp[v]) dp[v] = cand;`. dp[u] is finalized before processing (Kahn order) so the single load is safe.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.rationale: Removes a redundant add and a redundant memory load per edge in the relaxation loop, shortening the dependency chain on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.risk: dp[u] is not mutated after u is dequeued in a valid Kahn topological order (guaranteed by inDeg==0 enqueue), so hoisting is semantics-preserving. No overflow change (same arithmetic).

src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.summary: Hoist the per-u bitset row base pointer and self-bit out of the inner word loop, and load the v-row base once per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.currentCost: Inner OR loop recomputes `u * bitsetSize + j` and `v * bitsetSize + j` each iteration (two multiplies folded into addressing, but base `u*bitsetSize` is invariant across all edges and words and is re-derived every word). Self-bit write also recomputes u*bitsetSize+(u>>6).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.proposedChange: Per u: `long* urow = bitsets + (long)u * bitsetSize;` then `urow[u >> 6] |= 1L << (u & 63);`. Per edge: `long* vrow = bitsets + (long)v * bitsetSize;` then `for (j) urow[j] |= vrow[j];`. This turns the inner loop into a straight two-pointer OR that Burst can vectorize (SIMD OR over the word array).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.rationale: Eliminates the repeated `u*bitsetSize` index math from the innermost loop and exposes a contiguous urow[j] |= vrow[j] pattern that auto-vectorizes to packed 256-bit ORs, dramatically cutting the cost of the O(edges * bitsetSize) reachability merge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.risk: Use a wider index (long or nint) for `u * bitsetSize` to avoid 32-bit overflow when n and bitsetSize are large; current code already risks int overflow in `u * bitsetSize + j`, so widening is a strict improvement. Behavior otherwise identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.summary: Skip the entire j-row when closure[i*n+k]==0 and hoist row base pointers, converting Floyd-Warshall into a guarded row-OR that vectorizes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.currentCost: The innermost loop tests `closure[i*n+k] != 0` for every j even though it is invariant across the whole j-loop, and recomputes i*n+j and k*n+j addressing each iteration. When closure[i*n+k]==0 the inner j-loop still runs n iterations doing nothing useful.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.proposedChange: Restructure: `int* krow = closure + (long)k*n;` then for each i: `if (closure[(long)i*n+k]==0) continue; int* irow = closure + (long)i*n; for (j) if (krow[j]!=0) irow[j]=1;`. This hoists the k-reachability test out of j and makes the inner loop a vectorizable masked-set over two contiguous rows.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.rationale: Removes an invariant branch from the innermost loop (n*n*n -> only runs inner loop for reachable (i,k) pairs) and replaces strided index math with sequential pointer walks the optimizer can SIMD. Same O(n^3) worst case but far fewer effective iterations and instructions per iteration on sparse closures.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.risk: Use long/nint for i*n and k*n to avoid int overflow for n above ~46340 (current `n*n` and `i*n+k` already overflow there; widening fixes a latent bug). Result identical: setting irow[j]=1 only when both bits set matches the original conjunction.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.summary: Offer a bitset variant (already present as WarshallBitset) and document/redirect; the int-per-cell version is 64x more memory and cycles than necessary.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.currentCost: Stores one int (4 bytes) per matrix cell and does scalar work per cell: O(n^3) scalar ops and O(n^2) ints = 4*n^2 bytes. WarshallBitset already packs 64 cells per long and ORs 64 at a time.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.proposedChange: If callers can supply packed bit rows, prefer WarshallBitset.Run (O(n^3/64) word-ops, n^2/8 bytes). For the int API, at minimum apply the row-skip+vectorize change above. Consider naming consistency so the bitset form is the discoverable default.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.rationale: Bit-packing reduces both memory (8x to 64x vs int) and reduces the transitive-closure inner loop to word-parallel ORs (up to 64x fewer operations), a genuine constant-factor-to-asymptotic-per-word win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.risk: Different input representation (packed bits vs int matrix); this is an API/ergonomics suggestion, not an in-place rewrite. Keep the int version for callers that need it.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.summary: Hoist row base pointers in PerformBitwiseOr and mark it AggressiveInlining so the k-row and i-row become two-pointer vectorizable ORs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.currentCost: PerformBitwiseOr recomputes `i*words + j` and `k*words + j` per word inside the loop, and is a separate non-inlined method call invoked per (i,k) reachable pair.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` and rewrite body as `long* irow = cls + (long)i*words; long* krow = cls + (long)k*words; for (j) irow[j] |= krow[j];`. Also hoist `k*words` base in the caller. Using nint/long indexing avoids overflow.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.rationale: Converts strided addressing into sequential dual-pointer OR that Burst vectorizes to packed 256-bit ORs, and inlining removes call overhead in the inner Warshall loop. The (closure[i*words+kW] & kMask) guard already correctly skips non-reachable rows; this only speeds the work that remains.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Misc/GraphMisc.cs.risk: Widen i*words and k*words to long/nint to prevent int overflow for large n*wordsPerRow (latent bug in current code). Semantics unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.summary: Remove AggressiveInlining from the recursive Dfs method; it cannot be inlined into itself and the attribute only risks code-size bloat at the (single) call site in Find.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.currentCost: [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] on a self-recursive method. The JIT/Burst cannot inline a directly recursive call, so the hint is at best ignored and at worst inflates the one non-recursive call site, hurting I-cache.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.proposedChange: Drop the AggressiveInlining attribute on Dfs (keep the method otherwise identical). Same for the public Find wrapper, which is also not a hot leaf.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.rationale: Inlining hints are only useful on small hot leaf methods. A recursive traversal is neither; removing the hint avoids speculative code duplication and keeps the hot recursion body compact in I-cache.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.risk: None — purely a compilation hint; observable behavior is unchanged. Burst still compiles the recursion normally.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.summary: Hoist low[u] into a local register across the neighbor loop instead of re-reading and re-writing low[u] through the pointer on every relaxation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.currentCost: Inside the for-loop, 'low[u]' is loaded and conditionally stored via the pointer up to deg(u) times. Because low is aliased (the recursive call writes low[v]), the compiler must reload low[u] after each recursive call, creating a memory dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.proposedChange: int lowU = low[u]; iterate using lowU for the min updates (if (low[v] < lowU) lowU = low[v]; / if (tin[v] < lowU) lowU = tin[v];), then write low[u] = lowU once after the loop and use lowU in the 'low[u] == tin[u]' test. Note the recursive Dfs(v,...) call may itself read low[v] (fine) but never reads low[u], so hoisting is safe.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.rationale: Keeps the running minimum in a register, eliminating per-edge load/store of low[u] and breaking the store-to-load alias dependency the compiler otherwise must assume. Fewer memory ops and a shorter dependency chain in the hottest loop of Tarjan.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.risk: Must confirm no callee reads low[u] mid-loop — it does not (children only touch low[v] for their own v). The single post-loop store preserves identical final values. Safe.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.summary: The init loop writes four arrays (tin, low, inStack, sccId) per index; tin and low are both zeroed and could be cleared with a single contiguous memset-style fill if laid out adjacently, but at minimum sccId=-1 is the only non-zero write.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.currentCost: Per-element scalar stores of 0 to tin/low/inStack plus -1 to sccId. Three of the four are zero-fills that Burst could vectorize, but interleaving them with the -1 store and different element widths (int vs byte) prevents a clean wide store.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.proposedChange: Split into homogeneous fills: zero tin[0..n], zero low[0..n], zero inStack[0..n] (byte), then set sccId[0..n] = -1 in separate tight loops. Each loop is then trivially vectorizable / lowerable to a memset by Burst.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.rationale: Separate same-type, same-value fills let Burst emit wide SIMD stores or memset intrinsics, whereas the interleaved mixed-width loop forces scalar stores. Lower instruction count over n elements.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/TarjanScc.cs.risk: None — same values written. Minor: trades one loop for four, but each is memset-shaped; net win for large n, negligible for small n.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.summary: Remove AggressiveInlining from recursive Dfs1 and Dfs2; recursion cannot be inlined and the hint only risks bloat.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.currentCost: Both Dfs1 and Dfs2 are self-recursive yet tagged AggressiveInlining, which the compiler cannot honor for the recursive edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.proposedChange: Delete the [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] attribute on Dfs1 and Dfs2.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.rationale: Same as TarjanScc: inlining hints belong on small hot leaves, not recursive traversals; removal avoids speculative duplication.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.summary: inDegree and outDegree are two separate stackalloc int[sccCount] buffers initialized in one loop, but the per-edge update touches both; pack them as interleaved pairs (or a single int[2*sccCount]) to improve locality, or better, fuse the zero-init since both are already done in one loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.currentCost: Two distinct allocations and two distinct cache lines touched per cross-edge in the degree loop: inDegree[toComp]++ and outDegree[fromComp]++ hit unrelated addresses, doubling potential cache misses across the m-edge scan.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.proposedChange: Allocate int* degree = stackalloc int[2*sccCount]; store in/out for component k at degree[2*k] and degree[2*k+1]. Then the increments for a single edge's two components are still two lines, but the zero-init is one contiguous memset and component-local in/out share a line. Alternatively keep two arrays but this is the locality-oriented option.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.rationale: Interleaving keeps a component's in/out degree on the same cache line, and a single contiguous buffer zero-inits as one memset-shaped loop. Fewer distinct lines resident during the hot m-edge accumulation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.risk: Index arithmetic (2*k) must be applied consistently in the accumulation and the final zeroIn/zeroOut scan. Behavior identical. Low risk; verify all four index sites updated.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.summary: The final degree-counting loop recomputes comp[u[i]] and comp[v[i]] for every edge, redoing the same indirection already available from the forward adjacency built earlier; also two init loops (head/revHead and a separate visited loop and a separate comp loop) can be fused.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.currentCost: Three separate O(n) init passes (head/revHead together, visited, comp) each re-walking 0..n; and an O(m) pass that does two dependent loads comp[u[i]] then comp[v[i]] per edge. Multiple passes over the same index range waste cache warmups.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.proposedChange: Fuse the visited[i]=false and comp[i]=-1 initializations into the existing head/revHead init loop (all are length-n) — one pass over 0..n setting head=-1, revHead=-1, visited=false, comp=-1. Leave the O(m) degree pass as is unless interleaving with the buildup; the main win is collapsing three n-length passes into one.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.rationale: One fused n-length pass replaces three, cutting loop overhead and cold-cache re-traversal of parallel arrays. Each array is still written once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.risk: comp must be initialized before Dfs2 (it is, and fusing keeps it before). visited must be set before Dfs1 (also preserved). Order of independent stores is irrelevant. Safe.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.summary: Final return uses a branch for max(zeroIn, zeroOut); make it branchless.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.currentCost: return zeroIn > zeroOut ? zeroIn : zeroOut; is a single comparison/branch — trivial, but it is the one spot a branchless max trivially applies.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.proposedChange: Use a branchless max: int diff = zeroIn - zeroOut; return zeroOut + (diff & ~(diff >> 31)); or simply rely on math.max if available. Both zeroIn and zeroOut are small non-negative counts so no overflow.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.rationale: Avoids a (well-predicted) branch at the single return. Marginal, but real and free of correctness caveats given non-negative bounded counts.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/SccAugmentation.cs.risk: Both operands are counts in [0, sccCount], so zeroIn - zeroOut cannot overflow int; sign-shift trick is valid. Negligible benefit — listed for completeness only.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.summary: Find uses recursive path compression with AggressiveInlining (which cannot apply to recursion); convert to an iterative two-pass path-compression to avoid call overhead and stack growth, and drop the misleading inline hint.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.currentCost: Recursive Find on the DSU is called per edge and per BFS neighbor (Find(parent, to[e])). Each Find is a recursion with a write-back; deep chains cost call frames. The AggressiveInlining hint is inert on the recursive call.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.proposedChange: Make Find iterative: walk to root with a local loop (int r = i; while (parent[r] != r) r = parent[r];), then a second loop to compress (while (parent[i] != r) { int nxt = parent[i]; parent[i] = r; i = nxt; }). Remove AggressiveInlining or keep only on the now-small iterative leaf.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.rationale: Iterative path compression has the same amortized inverse-Ackermann complexity but no per-level call frame, shorter dependency chains, and is Burst-friendly (no recursion to a non-inlinable callee). Hottest DSU primitive called O(edges + BFS-visits) times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.risk: Must preserve full path compression semantics (all nodes on path point to root) to keep amortized bounds; the two-pass form does exactly that. Observable parent[] end-state equals the recursive version's. Safe.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.summary: Union does parent[rootI] = rootJ with no union-by-rank/size; combined with path compression the DSU loses the near-constant amortized guarantee and can degrade Find chains, directly slowing AddEdge's per-edge Find and the contraction loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.currentCost: Unbalanced union can create long parent chains before compression kicks in, increasing Find cost across the many Find calls in the BFS (Find(parent, to[e]) per edge traversed) and in the contraction loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.proposedChange: Add a rank or size array (caller-provided int* to honor the no-hidden-state rule) and attach the smaller tree under the larger in Union. Init alongside parent in Init. This keeps Find chains shallow.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.rationale: Union-by-rank/size + path compression gives O(alpha) amortized; without rank, worst-case Find chains grow, raising the cost of the per-edge Find calls that dominate AddEdge. Asymptotic/amortized improvement on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.risk: Changes the signature/Init contract (adds a rank buffer) — an API change the caller must adopt; flag as ergonomics-affecting. Behavior of SCC results is identical (DSU connectivity unchanged); only internal tree shape and speed differ. Medium risk due to signature change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.summary: In the contraction loop, Union(parent, node, rootU) recomputes Find(parent, rootU) for every visited node even though rootU is fixed; hoist Find(parent,rootU) once and union each node's root into it directly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.currentCost: The loop calls Union qt times; each Union does Find(node) and Find(rootU). rootU's root is invariant across the loop but is re-derived each iteration (and rootU is already a root at loop start, though compression during the loop can move it).
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.proposedChange: Since rootU is a DSU root at the start and the loop only attaches others under it (parent[rootI]=rootJ direction), compute the target root once: keep merging into rootU and set parent[Find(parent,node)] = rootU directly, recomputing only node's root. If union-by-rank is added this needs care, but for the current attach-into-rootU semantics the rootU Find is redundant.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.rationale: Removes qt redundant Find(rootU) calls in the contraction loop, each of which (with current unbalanced DSU) may walk a chain. Cuts work proportional to visited-set size per cycle contraction.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SCC/OnlineScc.cs.risk: Current Union always points rootI under rootJ; calling Union(node, rootU) attaches node's root under rootU's root. Inlining as parent[Find(node)] = rootU is equivalent ONLY while rootU remains a root — it does, because nothing is ever attached above it in this loop. Verify before applying; without rank this holds. Low-medium risk.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: Hoist the per-edge base pointers dists+u*k and dists+v*k out of the inner k-loop and avoid recomputing u*k+i and v*k indices repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: Inner loop over i recomputes dists[u*k+i] twice (the != MaxValue test and the +w) and InsertIfBetter recomputes v*k+j and v*k+l on every probe/shift. Each index is a multiply (u*k) plus add per access; with k iterations per edge per relaxation step this is O(n*k*m*k) multiplies.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Compute long* du = dists + (long)u * k; long* dv = dists + (long)v * k; once per edge. Pass dv (or v's base) into InsertIfBetter instead of v so it indexes dv[j]/dv[l] with no multiply. In Run cache long dui = du[i]; if (dui == long.MaxValue) continue; then InsertIfBetter(k, dv, dui + w).
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Replaces a multiply-add address computation with a single base+offset per access, shrinks the dependency chain (one load of du[i] reused), and removes the duplicate load of dists[u*k+i]. Same arithmetic results, just hoisted/CSE'd manually since the unmanaged pointer aliasing may block the compiler from doing it.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: u*k and v*k must not overflow int; promote the base offset to long (cast u/v to long before multiply) to match a potential n*k that already overflows in the dists init loop. Observable behavior unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: i*k+? init bound n*k is computed as int and used both as loop guard count and step guard; guard against int overflow and mark InsertIfBetter AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: for (i=0; i<n*k; i++) recomputes n*k each iteration (cheap but a multiply in the guard), and the outer step loop guard n*k re-multiplies every step. InsertIfBetter is a hot leaf called n*k*m times but is a separate call (Burst usually inlines, but explicit attribute guarantees it).
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Hoist int nk = n * k; (or long to be safe) before the loops and reuse it. Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to InsertIfBetter so the early-return fast path (cand >= all dists[v*k]) is inlined into the caller.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Removes a redundant multiply from each loop guard and guarantees the leaf insert is inlined, eliminating call overhead and enabling the cand comparison to share registers with the caller's loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: n*k could overflow int for very large graphs; if so the dists buffer itself is already mis-sized, so behavior is unchanged relative to current code. Inlining a loop-containing method can increase code size on mobile but is standard for hot leaves.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: Move the stackalloc of d[n] and v[n] OUT of the pLen loop and reset them per iteration instead of re-allocating each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: stackalloc long[n] and bool[n] are inside the for-i loop, so the stack pointer is bumped pLen times. While stackalloc in a loop is typically hoisted by the JIT, under Burst/IL it is not guaranteed and can grow the frame or re-zero unpredictably; semantically each iteration fully reinitializes both buffers anyway.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Hoist long* d = stackalloc long[n]; bool* v = stackalloc bool[n]; above the for-i loop. Keep the existing for-j reset of d[j]=MaxValue, v[j]=false at the top of each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Guarantees a single fixed-size frame allocation regardless of pLen, removes repeated stack-pointer adjustment, and makes the working set explicit and constant. Behavior identical because both buffers are fully overwritten each iteration before use.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: None functionally; the reset loop already initializes every slot. Only consideration is that stackalloc size n is unchanged so frame size is identical to a single iteration's current allocation.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: The relaxation inner loop scans ALL m edges per settled vertex (O(n*m) per source) and filters eu[e]==cur, making Dijkstra effectively O(n^2 + n*m) with an O(n) array min-select. The dominant cost is the per-vertex full edge scan; an adjacency CSR would cut it to O(m) total edge work.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: For each of the up-to-n settled vertices, the code loops e=0..m testing eu[e]==cur; that is n*m edge inspections per source, repeated pLen times -> O(pLen * n * m). The array-based extract-min adds O(n^2) per source.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Precompute a CSR adjacency (head[] + next-style offsets) once before the pLen loop (or accept it as input) so relaxation only touches the out-edges of cur. Even without CSR, swap the e-loop and j-loop is not valid here; the real win is indexing cur's out-edges directly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Reduces relaxation from O(n*m) to O(m) per source (each edge relaxed once when its tail is settled), turning total work from O(pLen*n*m) to O(pLen*(n^2 + m)). Large asymptotic win on dense edge lists.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: Requires building adjacency structure (extra stackalloc/buffer of size n+1 and m). Must skip pEdges[i] correctly within the adjacency scan. The unchecked Run contract assumes valid input; CSR build adds a one-time O(m) pass. Behavior preserved: same shortest distances excluding edge pEdges[i].

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: In the relaxation loop, d[cur] and the index i (pEdges[i]) are loop-invariant across the e-loop; hoist d[cur] and pEdges[i] into locals, and short-circuit-order the && so the cheap e!=skip test runs first (it already does, but eu[e]==cur should precede the addition).
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: The condition e != pEdges[i] && eu[e] == cur && d[cur] + ew[e] < d[ev[e]] reloads d[cur] and pEdges[i] every edge, and computes d[cur]+ew[e] which involves a memory load of d[cur] each time.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Before the e-loop: long dcur = d[cur]; int skip = pEdges[i]; then test if (e != skip && eu[e] == cur) { long nd = dcur + ew[e]; int tv = ev[e]; if (nd < d[tv]) d[tv] = nd; }.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Removes redundant loads of d[cur] (potential aliasing prevents the compiler from caching it across the d[ev[e]] store) and pEdges[i] from the hot edge loop; computes ev[e] once. Fewer loads per edge shortens the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: d[cur] is not modified inside the e-loop (cur is already settled/visited), so caching dcur is safe. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: Hoist a[i*n+k] out of the k-loop is not possible (varies with k), but hoist the row base a + i*n and the running min; more importantly the branchy MaxValue guard inside the hot k-loop blocks Burst vectorization. Restructure to hoist row pointers and reduce index multiplies.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: Inner loop recomputes a[i*n+k] and b[k*n+j] with full multiplies (i*n and k*n) every k, and has two MaxValue branches plus a branchy min. The k*n+j stride for b is column-walked, a poor (strided) access pattern, and i*n+k for a is sequential. The branch on != MaxValue per element defeats SIMD.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Hoist long* arow = a + (long)i * n; before the j-loop. The b access b[k*n+j] is column-strided; this is min-plus matmul -- consider transposing b once into a scratch bt (bt[j*n+k]) so both inner accesses are sequential, enabling a vectorizable arow[k] (cmp/add/min) reduction. Replace the if(v<min) with branchless min = math.min(min, v) after computing v (MaxValue+w overflow guarded as below).
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Sequential access on both operands turns the inner reduction into a SIMD-friendly load/add/min pass; branchless min removes a mispredict-prone branch. This is the classic cache-blocking/transpose win for matrix-like O(n^3) kernels and is the hottest loop in the file.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: Removing the MaxValue guard requires that long.MaxValue + (finite w) not wrap to a small value and corrupt min; must keep a guard or use saturating add. Safer form: keep the != MaxValue checks but transpose b for sequential access only (no semantic change). Transpose needs O(n^2) scratch (n*n longs) -- a real RAM cost to weigh; if scratch is unacceptable, at minimum hoist arow and the b column base.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: The two separate != long.MaxValue checks can be collapsed: if a[i*n+k]==MaxValue the whole row contribution for that k is skippable, but more cheaply, precompute whether arow[k]==MaxValue once and skip; for b[k*n+j] the check is per-(k,j) and unavoidable without transpose.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: Per innermost iteration: two comparisons against MaxValue, an add, a compare-and-store for min. The a-side check a[i*n+k] is invariant across j (it only depends on i,k) yet is re-tested for every j in the current i,j,k ordering -- actually with j outer of k it is re-tested n times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Reorder is hard due to the min reduction, but cache long aik = arow[k]; once per k and test aik==MaxValue to early-continue. Since j is the middle loop and k innermost, aik is loaded fresh each k anyway -- the win is caching aik in a register for the add and comparison rather than two memory accesses.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Eliminates one redundant memory load of a[i*n+k] per inner iteration (it is read implicitly twice: the guard and the add). Register reuse shortens the chain.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: None; aik is read-only in the loop. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: Hoist the row/column base pointers dist+i*n, dist+v*n out of the j-loop and cache the invariant sum d_iu+newW; the inner test reloads dist[v*n+j] and dist[i*n+j] with full multiplies each j.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: Inner j-loop computes dist[v*n+j] (multiply v*n), dist[i*n+j] (multiply i*n), and d_iu+newW+d_vj every iteration. v*n and i*n are invariant across j but recomputed; d_iu+newW is invariant across j but recomputed each j.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Before the j-loop: long* vrow = dist + (long)v * n; long* irow = dist + (long)i * n; long base = d_iu + newW; then for j: long d_vj = vrow[j]; if (d_vj != MaxValue) { long c = base + d_vj; if (c < irow[j]) irow[j] = c; }.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Removes two multiplies per inner iteration (replaced by base+j sequential addressing) and one redundant add (d_iu+newW computed once per i instead of per j). Sequential vrow[j]/irow[j] access is also cache- and SIMD-friendlier.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: i*n / v*n must not overflow int; cast to long before multiply for safety on large n (the dist buffer is n*n so n is bounded by addressable memory). Behavior identical -- base+d_vj == d_iu+newW+d_vj.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: In the Bellman-Ford-style DP, recompute of dp[(k-1)*n+eu[e]] (loaded twice: guard and add) and the index multiplies (k-1)*n and k*n per edge; hoist row base pointers prevRow=dp+(k-1)*n and curRow=dp+k*n once per k.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: For each k and each edge: dp[(k-1)*n+eu[e]] is read twice (guard + add), plus k*n+ev[e] index for the store. (k-1)*n and k*n are invariant across the e-loop but recomputed each edge. Total m*n edge iterations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Per k iteration: long* prevRow = dp + (long)(k-1) * n; long* curRow = dp + (long)k * n; then per edge: long du = prevRow[eu[e]]; if (du != MaxValue) { long val = du + ew[e]; int te = ev[e]; if (val < curRow[te]) curRow[te] = val; }.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Caches the double-read of dp[(k-1)*n+eu[e]] into du, removes two multiplies per edge by hoisting the row bases, and computes ev[e] once. Shortens dependency chain in the hot DP loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: k*n and (k-1)*n must not overflow int; cast to long. dp is sized (n+1)*n so n bounded. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.summary: In the final Karp min-mean reduction, dp[n*n+v] is recomputed/reloaded for every k and the division uses runtime double divide; hoist dp[n*n+v] into a local and replace the divide-in-loop with a comparison reformulation to avoid n divisions per vertex.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.currentCost: For each vertex v, the k-loop does up to n double divisions (double)(dp[n*n+v]-dp[k*n+v])/(n-k) and reloads dp[n*n+v] (index n*n+v) each k. Division is ~20-40 cycles; n divisions per vertex * n vertices = O(n^2) divides.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.proposedChange: Hoist long dpNV = dp[n*n+v]; before the k-loop (it is invariant). The divide is harder to remove exactly while preserving the same max-of-ratios result; if exactness allows, note that comparing ratios a/(n-k) cross-multiplied changes semantics with mixed signs, so keep the divide but at minimum hoist dpNV and the row index k*n+v base pointer (kcol stride is n). Cache the n*n base once: long* lastRow = dp + (long)n*n;.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.rationale: Removes a redundant load of dp[n*n+v] per inner iteration and the n*n multiply; the loop becomes lastRow[v] - dp[k*n+v] with one hoisted multiply. The divide remains but its operands are cheaper to fetch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.ShortestPath/ShortestP.risk: Cross-multiplying to eliminate the divide is NOT safe here: (n-k) varies and dp differences can be negative (NegativeInfinity init avoided, but values can be negative), so reordering ratio comparisons via cross-multiply changes results. Therefore only hoist the invariant load/base, do not remove the divide. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.summary: Precompute per-vertex net score (outDeg-inDeg) once instead of recomputing two subtractions with four indexed loads per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.currentCost: For each of m edges: 4 dependent array loads (outDeg[eu[i]], inDeg[eu[i]], outDeg[ev[i]], inDeg[ev[i]]) plus 2 subtractions. The score of a vertex is recomputed every time the vertex appears on an edge endpoint (degree times).
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.proposedChange: After building inDeg/outDeg, fold them into a single 'score' array in-place: reuse outDeg as score via score[v]=outDeg[v]-inDeg[v] in one O(n) pass (write into outDeg buffer, no extra stackalloc). Then in the edge loop read sU=score[eu[i]], sV=score[ev[i]] (2 loads, 0 subtractions per edge).
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.rationale: Reduces the hot edge loop from 4 loads + 2 subs to 2 loads + 0 subs per edge, and converts repeated per-edge recomputation into one O(n) precompute pass. Fewer dependent loads shortens the critical dependency chain feeding the branch on line 17.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.risk: None. score[v]=outDeg[v]-inDeg[v] is exact integer arithmetic; values fit in int (degrees <= m). Reusing the outDeg buffer is safe because inDeg is read before outDeg[v] is overwritten only for the same index in the same iteration. Observable output (remove[] and count) is identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.summary: Replace explicit zero-init loops over stackalloc buffers with a single bulk clear, and hoist repeated eu[i]/ev[i] loads into locals.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.currentCost: Lines 11, 28, 31, 75 perform scalar element-by-element zeroing loops. stackalloc memory is not pre-zeroed, so init is required, but the scalar loop is not vectorized as well as a bulk memclear and emits per-element store + index increment + compare.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.proposedChange: Use Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned (System.Runtime.CompilerServices, already imported) to zero the buffers in one call, e.g. Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(inDeg, 0, (uint)(n*sizeof(int))). Also cache int u=eu[i], v=ev[i] into locals in tight loops (lines 12, 16-17, 29) to avoid reloading the same pointer-indexed value multiple times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.rationale: InitBlockUnaligned lowers to a tight vectorized/rep-stos-style clear that Burst recognizes, beating a scalar loop for the common case. Caching eu[i]/ev[i] removes redundant loads and lets the compiler keep the value in a register across the two endpoint computations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.risk: InitBlockUnaligned writes raw bytes; for int 0 and bool false the zero byte pattern is correct on all targets. Byte length must use sizeof(int)/sizeof(bool); off-by-one on the n+1 sized buffers must include the +1. Behavior identical when sizes match exactly.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.summary: Hoist the repeated t[e] and mR[t[e]] chained loads into a single local per edge in both BFS and DFS inner loops.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.currentCost: Line 41 evaluates mR[t[e]] up to three times per edge (condition, dist write target, queue push) — each is a two-level dependent load t[e] then mR[...]. Line 47 evaluates t[e] and mR[t[e]] multiple times per edge similarly. These are pointer-chasing dependent loads on the hottest path of Hopcroft-Karp.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.proposedChange: In TryBfs inner loop: int te = t[e]; int r = mR[te]; then use r. In TryDfs: int te = t[e]; int r = mR[te]; reuse r in the condition and the recursive call; on success assign mR[te]=u; mL[u]=te.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.rationale: Each hoist removes 2-3 redundant dependent memory loads per edge visit. Hopcroft-Karp does O(E*sqrt(V)) edge visits, so on dense transitive-closure inputs (Dilworth feeds up to n^2 edges) this is the dominant inner loop; cutting its dependency chain directly reduces stall cycles.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.risk: None within an iteration: mR[t[e]] is not written inside the BFS loop body, and in DFS it is only written on the success path after the value is consumed, so caching is value-equivalent. Recursion may mutate mR for other indices but te/r refer to the current edge only.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.summary: Recursive DFS defeats Burst inlining/optimization and risks deep stack; convert to an explicit iterative augmenting-path search using a stackalloc stack.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.currentCost: TryDfs is self-recursive (line 47). Burst cannot inline recursion and recursion can blow the native stack for long augmenting paths (depth up to n); each call also re-passes 7 pointer args. On mobile the limited stack makes deep recursion a hard hazard.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.proposedChange: Rewrite the augmenting-path DFS iteratively: maintain an explicit edge-iterator stack (stackalloc int for current edge pointer per level, depth <= n) and walk it, performing the mR/mL assignment on unwind. This is the standard iterative Hopcroft-Karp augment.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.rationale: Removes function-call overhead per node, lets Burst keep the whole search in one frame with registers, and bounds stack usage deterministically (one stackalloc proportional to n) instead of unbounded native recursion. Better instruction cache behavior and no per-call argument marshaling.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.risk: Must preserve exact matching semantics (same augmenting path chosen: first eligible edge in adjacency order). Iterative version must restore dist[u]=int.MaxValue on failure exactly as line 48 does. Careful equivalence testing needed; this is a larger refactor than the micro-opts.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.summary: Avoid materializing the dense transitive-closure edge list (up to n^2 edges) and the O(n^2) extra stackalloc; pass the closure bitmatrix directly into a matching that iterates it row by row.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.currentCost: Lines 61-64 count tcE (up to n^2) closure edges, stackalloc two int[tcE] arrays (up to 2*n^2*4 bytes on the stack), fill them, then MinimumPathCoverDag rebuilds adjacency lists (another t[m+1], nx[m+1] of size n^2). For n=1000 that is ~4MB of stackalloc for tceu/tcev alone — a stack-overflow risk on mobile, plus full duplicate storage of edges already present in tc.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.proposedChange: Add an overload of MinimumPathCoverDag that consumes the n x n bool* tc directly: build the bipartite adjacency by scanning tc rows (vertex u's neighbors are columns j with tc[u*n+j]) instead of an explicit edge array. Eliminates tceu/tcev and the tcE counting pass; the closure matrix already encodes every edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.rationale: Removes an O(n^2) stack allocation and two O(n^2) fill/count passes, and removes duplicate edge storage (the closure is already in tc). Same asymptotic matching cost but far smaller working set and no second materialization of the dense edge set, improving cache locality and removing the mobile stack-overflow hazard.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.risk: MinimumPathCoverDag currently builds reverse adjacency (h indexed by eu+1). The tc-row scan must reproduce the same neighbor ordering the matching relies on; Hopcroft-Karp result (path cover size) is order-independent in value, so width is preserved, but the new code path needs validation that it indexes 1-based vertices consistently with the existing convention.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.summary: Replace the per-bit bool transitive-closure (O(n^3) with branch per element) by a bit-packed (ulong word) Warshall closure, giving 64x fewer inner iterations and branchless OR.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.currentCost: Lines 58-60 and 94-96: classic Warshall over bool* tc. Inner loop does, for each (i,k) with tc[i*n+k], a full j-loop of n branches (if tc[k*n+j]) plus a byte store. That is O(n^3) byte operations with a data-dependent branch on every inner element — poor for Burst vectorization and 1 byte per bit of memory.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.proposedChange: Store the closure as ulong* rows of ceil(n/64) words. The inner step becomes: if bit(i,k) set, then row_i |= row_k (a word-wise OR over ceil(n/64) ulongs, no per-element branch). Use math/intrinsics-friendly OR loop Burst vectorizes. Memory drops from n^2 bytes to n^2/8 bytes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.rationale: Reduces inner work by ~64x (one ulong OR covers 64 columns), removes the data-dependent inner branch entirely (branchless |=), and shrinks the matrix 8x improving cache residency. This is the standard bitset-Warshall and is the single biggest win for both classes since closure dominates their runtime on dense graphs.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.risk: Bit indexing must be exact (word = c>>6, mask = 1UL<<(c&63)). The tail word beyond n must stay zero so spurious high bits never set tc[i*n+j] for j>=n. The public bool* tc buffer signature would change (or a conversion step added); callers (MaximumAntichain reads tc[(u-1)*n+j], TransitiveReductionDag reads tc[eu*n+k]) must be updated to bit-test accessors. Larger change; counting (line 61) becomes popcount.

src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.summary: Hoist eu[i]*n and ev[i] out of the k-loop redundancy check; the row base tc[eu[i]*n] is recomputed every k iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.currentCost: Line 101: per edge, the k-loop of length n recomputes eu[i], ev[i], and the products eu[i]*n (for tc[eu[i]*n+k]) and indexes tc[k*n+ev[i]] (k*n recomputed each k). eu[i] and ev[i] are reloaded from memory inside the inner loop n times per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.proposedChange: Before the k-loop: int u=eu[i], v=ev[i]; bool* rowU=tc+u*n; Then inner loop tests k!=u && k!=v && rowU[k] && tc[k*n+v]. Precompute the row pointer to drop one multiply per inner iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.rationale: Removes the eu[i]*n multiply and the eu[i]/ev[i] reloads from the O(n) inner loop run for each of m edges (O(m*n) savings). rowU[k] is a single-add address vs base+u*n+k each time. Pure strength reduction with no semantic change.
src/IAFahim.Graph.SpanningTrees/Spanning.risk: None. u, v, rowU are loop-invariant across k; tc is not mutated during this loop (closure already complete). Output keep[] and count identical. (If the bit-packed closure opt is adopted, this hoist applies to the word-test variant instead.)

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.summary: Replace the per-bit ascent loop over all logN bits with a bit-iteration over only the set bits of diff using Bmi1/trailing-zero extraction, and strength-reduce the repeated `u * logN` index multiply into a cached row base pointer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.currentCost: First loop runs logN iterations regardless of how many bits are set in diff, each doing a `(diff>>j)&1` test plus a multiply `u*logN+j`. The branch `if(((diff>>j)&1)!=0)` is data-dependent and frequently mispredicts. The multiply u*logN is recomputed every iteration even though u only changes on taken branches.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.proposedChange: Iterate only over set bits: `while (diff != 0) { int j = System.Numerics.BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(diff); u = ancestors[u * logN + j]; diff &= diff - 1; }`. This removes the branch entirely (each iteration is a guaranteed lift) and runs popcount(diff) times instead of logN. Keep the second (LCA-narrowing) loop as-is since it must scan all levels high-to-low.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.rationale: diff often has far fewer set bits than logN, so popcount(diff) <= logN iterations with zero branch mispredicts. `diff &= diff-1` clears the lowest set bit branchlessly; TrailingZeroCount maps to a single TZCNT/CTZ instruction Burst emits. Removes the data-dependent branch that the current `&1` test creates.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.risk: Pure cycle/branch reduction; identical output. diff = depth[u]-depth[v] >= 0 after the swap so it is non-negative; the unsigned-style bit tricks are safe on the non-negative value. BitOperations is Burst-compatible; if unavailable, the same can be done with an intrinsic. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.summary: In the second loop, hoist the two row bases `ancestors + u*logN` and `ancestors + v*logN` and recompute them only when u/v change, instead of computing `u*logN+j` and `v*logN+j` four times per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.currentCost: Each of the logN iterations computes `u*logN+j` and `v*logN+j` up to four times (the compare reads both, and on a taken branch both are reread to assign). That is up to 4 integer multiplies + adds per level.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.proposedChange: Cache `int* au = ancestors + u*logN; int* av = ancestors + v*logN;` and use `au[j] != av[j]`; on a taken branch set `u = au[j]; v = av[j];` then refresh `au`/`av`. The multiply only happens when u/v actually change (at most logN times total across the loop instead of per-read).
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.rationale: Reduces redundant address arithmetic and the dependency chain length per iteration; the multiply by logN (not a power of two in general) is a real multiply Burst cannot fold cheaply. Fewer multiplies per level lowers the critical path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.risk: None to semantics — same reads/writes, just fewer recomputations of the same address. Pointer arithmetic stays in-bounds for valid ancestors layout.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.summary: The two nested binary-lifting fill loops are an exact duplicate of BinaryLiftBuild.Run; delegate to it to remove code duplication and keep a single optimized implementation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.currentCost: Lines 29-34 duplicate BinaryLiftBuild.Run (lines 75-80) byte-for-byte, so any index-strength-reduction must be applied twice and risks drift.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.proposedChange: Replace the duplicated loops in LcaBuild.Run with `IAFahim.Graph.Tree.BinaryLiftBuild.Run(n, root, parent, ancestors, logN);` (root param is unused by BinaryLiftBuild so it is harmless), guaranteeing both paths share the same hot code.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.rationale: Single source of truth for the O(n*logN) lift table build; lets one set of micro-optimizations (below) cover both call sites. No asymptotic change but eliminates divergence risk and shrinks code/icache footprint.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.risk: Behavior identical (same loop). Confirm inlining still occurs under Burst; if Burst won't inline a cross-class call on a hot build path, alternatively keep duplication but apply the strength-reduction to both. Ergonomics/maintenance win primarily.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.summary: Strength-reduce the address arithmetic in the O(n*logN) inner loop: walk row pointers with `+= logN` instead of recomputing `i*logN+j` and `i*logN+(j-1)`, and read the previous column once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.currentCost: Inner loop body `ancestors[i*logN+j] = ancestors[ancestors[i*logN+(j-1)]*logN+(j-1)]` does three multiplies by logN per element across n*logN elements. logN is a runtime value (not a power of two), so each is a genuine IMUL on the critical path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.proposedChange: For each j, set `int* col = ancestors + (j-1);` then loop i with `int* row = ancestors; for(i) { int mid = row[j-1]; row[j] = ancestors[mid*logN + (j-1)]; row += logN; }`. This removes the `i*logN` multiply (replaced by a single add per i) and reuses `row[j-1]` instead of re-deriving it. Only the unavoidable `mid*logN` multiply remains.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.rationale: Cuts ~2 of 3 multiplies per inner-loop element over an O(n*logN) hot build, and shortens the dependency chain (the row base is loop-carried by addition). Sequential `row += logN` is also more vectorizer/prefetcher friendly than scattered `i*logN+j`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.risk: Identical writes and reads, in-bounds for the existing flat [n*logN] layout. Pure cycle win; apply the same transform to LcaBuild if not delegating.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.summary: Iterate only the set bits of k and stop early, instead of always looping logN times with a per-bit branch.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.currentCost: Always logN iterations, each with a data-dependent `((k>>j)&1)!=0` branch and an `node*logN+j` multiply even on non-taken bits.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.proposedChange: `while (k != 0) { int j = System.Numerics.BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(k); node = ancestors[node*logN + j]; k &= k - 1; }`. Branchless per-step (each step is a guaranteed lift), popcount(k) iterations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.rationale: Fewer iterations (popcount(k) <= logN) and no branch mispredict; the multiply only executes on real lifts. Same intrinsic mapping as the LcaQuery suggestion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.risk: k is assumed valid/non-negative per the unchecked Run convention. If a negative k were passed the original would also misbehave; for k>=0 outputs are identical. Burst-compatible intrinsic.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.summary: Fuse the degree-initialization-to-zero pass into the degree-counting pass, and compute degree by counting edges in the same scan rather than two separate O(n)/O(n+m) passes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.currentCost: Three sequential passes: zero degree[] (n), count degree by scanning adjacency (n+m), then scan for leaves (n). The zeroing pass is redundant because the counting loop fully overwrites each degree[u].
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.proposedChange: Drop the `for(i) degree[i]=0;` pass and instead set `degree[u]` directly: `for(u){ int d=0; for(e=head[u];e!=0;e=next[e]) d++; degree[u]=d; if(d<=1) q[qt++]=u; }`. This fuses zero-init, counting, and leaf-seeding into one pass over nodes+edges.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.rationale: Eliminates one full O(n) write pass and one O(n) leaf-scan pass by fusing them into the counting loop, improving cache locality (degree[u] written once) and reducing total memory traffic.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeBasic.cs.risk: None — degree[u] is unconditionally assigned before its first read, and leaf seeding order within the same u-range is identical to the original separate loop. Same q contents and order.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant `total / 2` out of the centroid scan and precompute it once.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.currentCost: Inside the for-i loop, `size[to[e]] > total / 2` (in the inner edge loop) and `(total - size[u]) <= total / 2` both recompute the integer division `total/2` repeatedly — once per edge examined plus once per node — over potentially many nodes/edges.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int half = total / 2;` once after the BFS sizing pass, then compare against `half` everywhere. Division is one of the most expensive integer ops; this removes O(edges) redundant divides.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.rationale: Integer division is ~20-40 cycles on many targets and cannot be folded by the JIT/Burst since `total` is runtime. Hoisting it to a single divide removes it from the hot inner edge loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.risk: None — total is unchanged inside the loop, so total/2 is loop-invariant; identical result.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.summary: The `size[u]=1` BFS sizing pass writes size for every reachable node but the subtree-size semantics are never actually computed (all sizes stay 1), making the > total/2 child test trivially false; verify intent — if sizes are meant to be subtree sizes a post-order accumulation is missing, otherwise the inner child-size loop can be dropped.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.currentCost: Lines 51 sets size[u]=1 for all nodes; the inner loop at line 56 then compares size[to[e]] (always 1) > total/2. For total>2 this branch is always false, so the entire inner edge scan is dead work unless subtree sizes were intended to be filled elsewhere.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: If subtree sizes are required, add a reverse-order accumulation `for(i=qt-1;i>0;i--) size[parent[q[i]]] += size[q[i]];` (needs a parent array like CentroidFind) before the centroid scan. If single-size semantics are truly intended, delete the inner `for(e...)` child check as provably-false and keep only `(total-size[u])<=total/2`.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.rationale: Either removes an entire O(edges) dead inner loop, or fixes a latent correctness gap. As written the child-mass test contributes nothing for total>2, so it is pure wasted cycles.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.risk: This changes observable output ONLY if the current result is already wrong; must confirm against tests/intended centroid definition before removing. Flag as needs-verification rather than a blind micro-opt. Standard centroid definition requires true subtree sizes, so the accumulation fix is the likely-correct path.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.summary: Returning the centroid set as `centroids |= (1 << u)` in a single int caps usable node indices at 31 and silently corrupts for u>=32; this is both a RAM/encoding and correctness limitation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.currentCost: `1 << u` is undefined/wrapping for u>=32 (shift count masked mod 32), so any tree where a centroid has index >=32 produces wrong bits. The whole API is implicitly limited to n<=31 nodes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Change the contract to write centroids into a caller-provided `int* outCentroids` (and return count), matching the TreeCenter pattern in TreeBasic.cs. This both removes the 32-node ceiling and aligns ergonomics with the existing center/center-count convention.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.rationale: Removes an undefined-behavior shift and a hidden node-count cap; consistent Run(... int* out)->count signature improves discoverability and matches TreeCenter.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.risk: API/signature change (breaking) — observable output representation changes from bitmask to array+count. Not a drop-in micro-opt; propose as an API correction. For n<=31 the bitmask values currently match, so a guard/comment is the minimum if the signature must stay.

src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.summary: The parameter `n` and array `depth`/`parent` are fine, but the unused parameter `n` aside, note `0, n-1` segment bounds are recomputed per call into SegmentTreeQuery; cache the segment root span once and mark the method AggressiveInlining-friendly leaf for the hot path loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.currentCost: Inside the while loop, each SegmentTreeQuery.RunInt64 call re-passes `1, 0, n-1` constants; the while loop walking chains is the hot path of HLD queries and the cross-class call may not inline.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to SegmentTreeQuery.RunInt64 (in its own file) so the per-chain query inlines into this loop, removing call overhead on the O(log n) chain hops. No change here beyond ensuring the callee is inlinable.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.rationale: HLD path queries do O(log n) chain hops each issuing a segment-tree query; inlining the leaf query removes call/return and argument-marshaling overhead on a hot path that runs per query.
src/IAFahim.Graph.Tree/TreeAdvanced.cs.risk: Inlining a recursive segment-tree query may bloat code; verify the callee is iterative or that Burst handles it. If RunInt64 is recursive, inlining the entry frame only is still a minor win. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.summary: Byte-by-byte zeroing of the DP buffer is ~8x slower than word-wide clearing and defeats vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.currentCost: A scalar loop writing one byte per iteration over a buffer of 2*(1<<maxBagSize)*8 bytes. For maxBagSize=20 that is ~16M single-byte stores on the allocate path and (1<<maxBagSize)*8 bytes cleared every path step inside the main loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.proposedChange: Clear in long-sized strides: cast to long* and write 0 over size>>3 elements (size is always a multiple of sizeof(long) here since both call sites pass dpSize and (1L<<maxBagSize)*sizeof(long)). Better: replace the helper with Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned / a long* loop, which Burst can widen to vector stores.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.rationale: Zeroing 8 bytes per iteration cuts the store count and loop overhead 8x and lets Burst emit SIMD stores; byte loops it cannot vectorize as cleanly. The buffer length is provably a multiple of 8 at both call sites, so no tail handling is needed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.risk: Only safe because both call sites pass byte counts that are exact multiples of sizeof(long); if a caller ever passes a non-multiple, add a byte tail. dp is freshly AllocHGlobal so alignment is fine for long stores.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.summary: The old-mask -> new-mask remap recomputes the bagElements vertex-match table for every mask, an O(2^oldSize * newSize * oldSize) cost that is mask-independent.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.currentCost: For each of 2^oldSize masks, an inner double loop over newSize x oldSize comparing bagElements to build newMaskBase. The match between old index k and new index j does not depend on mask, only on which bit k is set.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.proposedChange: Precompute once per path step a small int[] mapping each old bit index k to its corresponding new bit index (or -1), via one O(newSize*oldSize) pass into a stackalloc int[oldSize]. Then per mask, build newMaskBase by iterating set bits of mask and OR-ing (1<<map[k]). This removes the inner newSize*oldSize work from the per-mask loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.rationale: Hoists a loop invariant (the index correspondence) out of the 2^oldSize loop, dropping per-step cost from O(2^oldSize * newSize * oldSize) to O(newSize*oldSize + 2^oldSize * popcount). Big asymptotic constant-factor win on the hottest loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.risk: Must preserve the original semantics where multiple old elements could map to the same new bit (original OR-accumulates). Using a per-old-index map keyed on the FIRST match preserves behavior only if each old element matches at most one new element; if duplicates are possible, build a per-new-bit old-mask instead. Guard: bag elements are distinct within a bag (standard tree-decomposition invariant), so the 1:1 map is valid.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.summary: The 'isNew' detection rescans the old bag for every new vertex j; the whole introduce phase repeats adjacency work that could be precomputed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.currentCost: For each new vertex j, a linear scan over oldSize to set isNew, then for each non-set mask a scan over newSize calling AreAdjacent (itself a linked-list walk) repeatedly for the same (u,v) pairs across different masks.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.proposedChange: Precompute per step: (a) the isNew flags in one O(newSize*oldSize) pass, and (b) an adjacency bitmask adj[j] over the newSize bag bits via one O(newSize^2) AreAdjacent pass. Then canAdd reduces to (mask & adj[j]) == 0, a single AND instead of a per-bit AreAdjacent linked-list traversal inside the mask loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.rationale: AreAdjacent is an O(degree) pointer chase; calling it inside the 2^newSize x newSize loop dominates. Reducing the inner test to one bitmask AND removes the dominant cost and the dependency chain through pointer loads.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Path.risk: Adjacency bitmask only fits when newSize <= bag-bit width (it does: masks are already 1<<newSize ints). Self-pairs (j vs j) must be excluded, which the original already does via the j-bit-clear precondition.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.summary: The bit-compaction (removing bit fIdx from mask) is recomputed bit-by-bit for every mask, O(2^oldSize * oldSize) when it can be O(2^oldSize) with a low/high mask split.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.currentCost: For each of 2^oldSize masks, an inner loop over oldSize bits reconstructs nextM by shifting out bit fIdx. That inner loop is pure mask arithmetic independent of dp values.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.proposedChange: Compute nextM branchlessly: int low = m & ((1<<fIdx)-1); int high = (m >> (fIdx+1)) << fIdx; int nextM = low | high; This drops the inner oldSize loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.rationale: Removes an O(oldSize) inner loop from the 2^oldSize loop, turning per-mask compaction into a handful of shifts/ANDs and eliminating a data-dependent branch (i != fIdx) per bit. Pure strength reduction, Burst-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.risk: fIdx is found via a prior scan and is in [0,oldSize); (1<<fIdx)-1 is well-defined for fIdx<31. oldSize is a bag size (small), so no overflow. Behavior is identical: bits below fIdx kept, bit fIdx dropped, bits above shifted down by one.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.summary: Per-mask weight sum recomputes popcount-weighted sums from scratch; it can be built incrementally over masks via the lowest-set-bit trick.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.currentCost: For each of 2^sz masks an inner loop over sz bits accumulates weights[bEl[...]] — O(2^sz * sz). The same per-bit weights are re-fetched and re-summed across masks.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.proposedChange: Precompute w[i]=weights[bEl[u*mBS+i]] into a stackalloc long[sz] once, then compute wt[m] = wt[m & (m-1)] + w[lowestSetBitIndex(m)] using the standard subset-sum DP so each mask costs O(1). Use math.tzcnt / BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount for the index.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.rationale: Reduces join weight computation from O(2^sz * sz) to O(2^sz), and removes repeated indirect loads of weights[bEl[...]] (two pointer chases per bit). The recurrence has a short dependency chain and vectorizes/pipelines well.
