src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.risk: Needs a scratch long[2^sz] for wt, or fold it into the existing cur write to avoid extra RAM. tzcnt is Burst-intrinsic. m & (m-1) clears the lowest set bit; wt[0]=0 base case. Semantics identical since addition is associative.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.summary: The dispatch uses a chain of int comparisons on type[u]; the recompute of (long)u*maskSize and 1<<bSz[0] are minor but the if-chain is the only per-node branch cost.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.currentCost: Four sequential if/else int compares per node; curDp pointer computed even for non-LEAF nodes where it is unused.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.proposedChange: Move the curDp computation into the TYPE_LEAF branch only (it is only used there), and consider a switch on type[u] so Burst can emit a jump table. maskSize is already hoisted; keep it.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.rationale: Avoids one multiply+add (long u*maskSize) on every non-leaf node, and a switch jump table is O(1) dispatch vs an averaged 2.5-compare if-chain. Constant-factor only, but on every nice-tree node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.risk: None semantically; curDp is only read in the LEAF branch. Switch vs if-chain is purely codegen and Burst handles both.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.summary: mid, lChild, rChild and segment lengths are recomputed; the two lengths (mid-start+1) and (end-mid) are used multiple times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.currentCost: In the assign branch both child writes recompute (mid-start+1) and (end-mid); the add branch recomputes them again. lChild/rChild are fine but the length subexpressions repeat up to 4 times.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.proposedChange: Hoist int leftLen = mid - start + 1; int rightLen = end - mid; once at the top and reuse in both the assign and add branches.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.rationale: Removes redundant integer subtraction/recomputation in a function called on every internal node touched by a query/update (the segment-tree hot path). Pure CSE; trivially safe.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.risk: None; values are identical within the call since start/end/mid are constant.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.summary: After the chain-climb loop, depth[u] and depth[v] are each loaded twice to compute l and r.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.currentCost: Two ternary expressions both evaluate depth[u] < depth[v], loading depth[u] and depth[v] twice and computing the same predicate twice; same pattern duplicated in PathAssign and PathSumQuery.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.proposedChange: Compute the predicate once: bool uShallower = depth[u] < depth[v]; int l = uShallower ? pos[u] : pos[v]; int r = uShallower ? pos[v] : pos[u]; Apply identically in PathAssign and PathSumQuery.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.rationale: Eliminates a duplicate memory load pair and duplicate compare; lets the compiler emit a branchless cmov on a single condition. Tiny but on every path operation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.risk: None; depth/pos are not mutated between the two reads.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.summary: node*2 and node*2+1 are recomputed three times in build/update methods; minor CSE plus consistency with the bit-shift style used for mid.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.currentCost: BuildSumTree, SumTreeAdd, SumTreeAssign, SumTreeQuery, BuildMaxSubarrayTree, MaxSubarrayTreeAssign each recompute node*2 and node*2+1 multiple times (recursive calls plus the final merge/read).
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.proposedChange: Introduce int lc = node << 1; int rc = lc | 1; once per method and reuse. (node<<1)|1 == node*2+1 for non-negative node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.rationale: Modest CSE that also documents the child-index pattern; reduces repeated address arithmetic in the segment-tree recursion. Compilers usually CSE this already, so impact is low, but it tightens the dependency chain feeding the recursive calls.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Heav.risk: node is always >=1 (root is 1), so <<1 and |1 are exact equivalents of *2 and *2+1; no signed-shift hazard.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.summary: QSort recurses on both partitions without tail-recursion elimination or median-of-three guard, risking O(n^2) time and O(n) stack depth on adversarial/sorted query orders.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.currentCost: Recurses into both [left,j] and [i,right]; worst case (already-sorted or many-equal queries, common in Mo where many queries share a block) gives O(q^2) comparisons and O(q) recursion depth — stack pressure under Burst and on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.proposedChange: Recurse into the smaller partition and loop on the larger (tail-call elimination) to bound stack to O(log q); the pivot is already mid-of-three-ish but consider it stays. Comparisons stay the same but worst-case stack becomes O(log q).
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.rationale: Bounding recursion depth to O(log q) prevents stack overflow on large q and reduces call overhead; tail-loop on the bigger side is the standard safe quicksort. Mo's queries frequently cluster by block, which is exactly the near-sorted input that hurts naive quicksort recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.risk: Must keep both partitions sorted; converting one recursion to a while-loop preserves output order. No semantic change to the sort result. Compare() ordering is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.summary: Compare passes MoQuery by value (20 bytes) and uses Int32.CompareTo, where a plain subtract-sign would be cheaper and avoids the struct copy.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.currentCost: Each comparison copies two 20-byte MoQuery structs by value and calls CompareTo (a method call returning -1/0/1). Called O(q log q) times inside QSort's inner while loops.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.proposedChange: Take parameters by 'in' (in MoQuery a, in MoQuery b) to avoid the copy, and replace a.R.CompareTo(b.R) with (a.R<b.R?-1:(a.R>b.R?1:0)) or, since QSort only checks <0 and >0, return (a.R - b.R) style comparisons guarded against overflow, or branch directly. R/BlockId are inputs bounded by n so a.R-b.R cannot overflow int when both are non-negative array indices.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.rationale: Removes per-comparison 40-byte stack copies and the CompareTo call overhead in the tightest sort loop; 'in' keeps the value-type semantics while passing by reference. Burst inlines the AggressiveInlining-tagged method but still benefits from avoiding the copy.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.risk: a.R - b.R is only safe from overflow because L/R are Euler-tour indices in [0,2n) and non-negative; if that invariant is not guaranteed, keep the explicit two-way compare instead of subtraction. 'in' parameters are always safe here.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.summary: onPath is zero-initialized with an explicit loop; stackalloc byte[n] can be zeroed in bulk and the init loop removed.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.currentCost: A scalar for-loop writes n bytes to clear onPath after stackalloc (which is not guaranteed zeroed). One byte per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.proposedChange: Use 'byte* onPath = stackalloc byte[n];' followed by Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(onPath, 0, (uint)n), or in C#7.3+ 'stackalloc byte[n]' assigned to a Span and cleared. Burst lowers InitBlock to a fast memset.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.rationale: Replaces an n-iteration scalar clear with a single vectorized memset, shrinking setup cost; negligible RAM change but removes a hot-ish init loop before the main Mo loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/MoAl.risk: None; semantics identical (all zero). n is the vertex count, a valid stackalloc size as already assumed.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Nice.summary: This is an explicitly-documented placeholder/dummy that ignores nearly all inputs and always emits a single LEAF node; not a real algorithm to optimize.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Nice.currentCost: No meaningful computation; many parameters (tdHead/tdTo/tdNext/bag arrays) are unused. The [AggressiveInlining] on a non-hot stub bloats call sites slightly.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Nice.proposedChange: Either implement the real O(N) general->nice conversion, or, until then, drop [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] from this large multi-parameter stub so it is not force-inlined, and mark unused parameters to silence warnings. No micro-opt applies until the real body exists.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Nice.rationale: Inlining a large parameter-heavy method with no hot body only increases code size at every call site without benefit. This is a correctness/placeholder flag rather than a perf win.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Nice.risk: Flagging only: removing AggressiveInlining has no behavioral effect. Implementing the real algorithm is out of scope for a semantics-preserving micro-opt and must not silently change the current (placeholder) output contract.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.summary: Byte-at-a-time clear loop is ~8x slower than necessary and defeats Burst vectorization on a potentially huge buffer.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.currentCost: One store per byte: dpSize iterations of a 1-byte write with a long-typed loop counter. dpSize = niceNodesCount * 2^maxBagSize * (capacity+1) * 8 bytes, which for non-trivial inputs is tens of MB to GB. A scalar byte loop issues 8x more store-uops than a long-width loop and is hard for Burst/the JIT to auto-vectorize cleanly due to the byte granularity.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.proposedChange: Clear in long-width strides since dpSize is always a multiple of sizeof(long) (it is computed as count*...*sizeof(long)). Rewrite as: long* lp = (long*)ptr; long n = size >> 3; for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) lp[i] = 0L;  Even better, call the platform's bulk-zero primitive (Unity's UnsafeUtility.MemClear / memset) which uses SIMD/rep-stos. Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] is NOT appropriate here (large loop), but a wide-store loop is.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.rationale: 8x fewer store-uops, the long-stride loop is trivially vectorizable by Burst into 16/32-byte SIMD stores, and a memset intrinsic uses rep stos / streaming stores that avoid polluting cache. size is guaranteed a multiple of 8 because the expression ends in * sizeof(long), so the >>3 division is exact with no tail remainder.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.risk: Safe: size is always a multiple of sizeof(long) by construction, so no leftover-byte tail handling is needed. Use a shift (>>3) not division. dp comes from AllocHGlobal which is at least pointer-aligned, so long-width stores are aligned. If the helper is ever called with a non-8-multiple size elsewhere, a tail byte loop guard would be required, but there is currently only this one caller.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.summary: dpSize multiplication can overflow long silently and the cleared allocation is never read, so the whole alloc+clear is dead work in the current stub.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.currentCost: dpSize = (long)niceNodesCount * (1L << maxBagSize) * (capacity+1) * 8. With maxBagSize up to ~31 the 1L<<maxBagSize term alone is 2^31; multiplied by niceNodesCount and (capacity+1) this overflows 63-bit range for realistic tree-decomposition widths, producing a negative/wrapped size passed to (nint)AllocHGlobal. Separately, in the current code dp is allocated, zeroed (O(dpSize) writes), and then never read before returning 0 -- pure wasted cycles and a large transient memory spike on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.proposedChange: (1) When the DP is actually implemented, avoid materializing the full niceNodesCount * 2^maxBagSize * (capacity+1) table at once: standard nice-tree-decomposition knapsack DP only needs the table(s) of the current node and its child/children live at any time (post-order), so allocate per-active-node and free as you go -- reducing peak RAM from O(niceNodesCount * 2^w * cap) to O((children+1) * 2^w * cap). (2) Compute dpSize in a way that detects overflow or assert maxBagSize is small; prefer indexing math that keeps the 2^maxBagSize and (capacity+1) factors as int strides. (3) Until the body is implemented, the alloc+memclear is dead and should be removed so the stub does not allocate/clear gigabytes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.rationale: Peak working set on mobile is the binding constraint; a full 3D DP table is exponential in bag size and need not be resident all at once for a tree DP. Eliminating dead alloc+clear removes an O(dpSize) cost entirely. Overflow-safe sizing prevents UB.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.risk: Behavioral: removing the alloc changes nothing observable now (function returns 0 regardless) but obviously the real DP must be written; flag as design guidance, not a drop-in micro-opt. The per-node allocation strategy changes memory lifetime, not outputs. Overflow guard only triggers on inputs that already produce UB today.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.summary: Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal and try/finally are not Burst-compatible and add managed-interop overhead on the hot allocation path.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.currentCost: Marshal.AllocHGlobal and Marshal.FreeHGlobal are managed P/Invoke wrappers that Burst cannot compile; the try/finally also introduces an exception region that Burst does not support. This forces the whole method off the Burst path despite the [AggressiveInlining] and unsafe pointer style.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.proposedChange: Use Unity's UnsafeUtility.Malloc/Free with an Allocator (e.g. Allocator.Temp/TempJob) instead of Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal, and replace try/finally with a straight-line free at the single return point (the method has one logical exit). This keeps the routine Burst-compilable and removes managed interop and the EH frame.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.rationale: Burst-compiled allocation via UnsafeUtility maps to native malloc without managed marshalling; dropping try/finally removes an unwind region Burst rejects, letting the whole function (and its memclear loop) be Burst-vectorized. Fewer instructions on entry/exit and no managed transition.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.risk: Behavioral-neutral for valid input. Without try/finally, an exception between alloc and free would leak -- but house rules forbid exceptions on the hot path and Run methods assume valid input, so straight-line free is acceptable. Requires Unity.Collections.LowLevel.Unsafe dependency; if this module must stay engine-agnostic, keep a manual free at the single exit instead of try/finally rather than switching allocators.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.summary: if/else-if chain on nodeType should be a switch (jump table) and the loop is a candidate for branch-predictable dispatch once implemented.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.currentCost: The per-node dispatch is a linear if/else-if chain over 4 contiguous constant types (0..3). The compiler may turn it into sequential compares (up to 3 branches for TYPE_JOIN) rather than a single jump table, costing extra compares/branches per node for niceNodesCount iterations.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.proposedChange: Replace the if/else-if cascade with switch (type) { case TYPE_LEAF: ...; case TYPE_INTRODUCE: ...; case TYPE_FORGET: ...; case TYPE_JOIN: ...; }. Since the cases are dense 0..3 constants, the compiler/Burst emits a computed-goto jump table: one indexed branch instead of up to three compares.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.rationale: Constant per-node dispatch cost drops from up to 3 dependent compare/branch pairs to a single jump-table indirection; types are dense so a jump table is ideal. Lower branch-misprediction pressure in a hot post-order loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeDecomposition/Tree.risk: None: switch over the same constants is semantically identical to the if-chain. Burst handles dense switch as a jump table. Purely a readability+dispatch improvement; effect is negligible until the case bodies do real work.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.summary: Run does two full DFS traversals of the tree (CanonicalHashRooted then AutomorphismCountRooted); the symmetry counting can read subHash that the first pass produces, but the two passes can be fused or the second can be made to compute hashes inline, eliminating one O(n) traversal plus its per-node insertion-sort of child hashes.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.currentCost: Two recursive DFS walks over all n nodes. CanonicalHashRooted sorts childHashes at every internal node via O(k^2) insertion sort, then AutomorphismCountRooted re-sorts the same child hashes again via another O(k^2) insertion sort. So each internal node pays the child-sort cost twice and the tree is traversed twice end to end.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.proposedChange: Have AutomorphismCountRooted compute and store subHash[u] itself in post-order (it already visits children before the parent and already has childHashes in hand), so CanonicalHashRooted is not needed as a separate pre-pass. Then Run becomes a single traversal: TreeHashing.AutomorphismCountRooted(root,-1,head,to,next,subHash,mod) where that routine fills subHash bottom-up. This removes one of the two DFS walks and one of the two per-node child sorts.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.rationale: Both passes already sort the identical multiset of child sub-hashes at each node; computing the canonical hash during the automorphism post-order reuses that sorted array, halving traversal count and removing n redundant SplitMix/sort operations. Fewer cycles, smaller dependency chain, same outputs because subHash[v] for a child is fully computed before the parent reads it in post-order.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.risk: Requires editing TreeHashing.AutomorphismCountRooted (in IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries, a dependency module) so it is consistent with CanonicalHashRooted's hash formula (h=h*1000003+SplitMix64(child); final SplitMix64(h); leaf=SplitMix64(1)). AutomorphismCount (the centroid entry point) also relies on CanonicalHashRooted being run first to fill subHash before AutomorphismCountRooted; that path must keep correct ordering. If TreeQueries is out of scope for edits, this opportunity cannot be applied without cross-module change. Pure refactor preserves observable results only if the hash formula is replicated exactly.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.summary: stackalloc ulong[n] uses n as the allocation size but Run never validates that root is in [0,n); subHash is indexed by node id (subHash[u]) in CanonicalHashRooted, so node ids must be < n. This is fine for an unchecked Run by design, but the AggressiveInlining on a method that does a stackalloc of dynamic size n and two deep recursive calls yields no inlining benefit and may bloat any caller.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.currentCost: AggressiveInlining is applied to a method whose body is a dynamic-sized stackalloc plus two non-inlinable recursive DFS calls. The attribute cannot meaningfully inline the recursion or the stackalloc, so it only risks code-size growth at call sites with zero cycle benefit.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.proposedChange: Drop [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] from Run. Keep AggressiveInlining only on true hot leaf methods (e.g. SplitMix64). Run is a heavyweight entry point, not a leaf.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.rationale: AggressiveInlining is a code-size/icache tradeoff justified only for tiny hot leaves. Inlining a frame that contains a variable-length stackalloc forces the alloca into the caller's frame and bloats every call site without removing any real call overhead, since the dominant cost is the recursive traversal that stays out-of-line. Removing it reduces caller code size and icache pressure.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeIsomorphism/Rooted.risk: None to correctness. Behavior is identical; only the inlining hint changes. Burst/JIT may already ignore the hint for stackalloc-containing methods, so worst case is a no-op.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.summary: Replace the O(n^2) keyroot identification with the standard O(n) Zhang-Shasha rule.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.currentCost: Nested loop over all (i,j) pairs comparing lm[j]==lm[i] to clear keyroot flags: O(n1^2)+O(n2^2) work plus an early-break that still leaves quadratic worst case. This is the dominant preprocessing cost and grows quadratically with tree size.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.proposedChange: A node in post-order is a keyroot iff no later (higher post-order index) node shares its leftmost-leaf value. Compute in one O(n) pass: keep a stackalloc'd byte[n+1] 'seen' indexed by leftmost-leaf id, iterate i from n down to 1; kr[i]=1 if seen[lm[i]]==0, then set seen[lm[i]]=1. This sets a keyroot exactly for the highest post-order index of each distinct lm value, identical to the current result.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.rationale: Each node's leftmost leaf lm[i] is in [1..n]; the topmost node per lm value is the keyroot. A single reverse scan with an O(1) membership array gives the same set in O(n) instead of O(n^2), removing the asymptotic bottleneck of TreeEditDistance preprocessing.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.risk: Must use a fresh zeroed seen array (stackalloc + manual zero or a generation counter) per tree. Semantics identical: current code clears kr[i] for the earlier index whenever a later j shares lm, leaving only the maximal-index node set; the reverse scan picks exactly that node. kr[n]=1 is preserved since n is first visited with lm[n] unseen.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.summary: Hoist/memoize the repeated CountChildren/CollectChildren and rooted-embed recursion across the r2 loop; immutable tree1 structure is recomputed every outer iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.currentCost: EmbeddingCheck calls EmbeddingCheckRooted(0,-1,r2,-1,...) for every r2 in [0,n2). Each call recomputes CountChildren and CollectChildren for tree1 nodes (which never change across r2) and re-runs the full O(n1*n2*matching) recursion from scratch, with no memoization across roots.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.proposedChange: Hoist tree1's root child count/collection (independent of r2) outside the loop. Further, memoize EmbeddingCheckRooted boolean results keyed by (u1, directed-edge of u2) in a stackalloc'd table so directed-subtree-embed results are reused across r2 roots sharing the same tree2 orientation. Even just hoisting CountChildren(u1,p1) removes one adjacency walk per recursive node per r2.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.rationale: CountChildren walks the whole adjacency list of a node every call; it is called twice per EmbeddingCheckRooted node and again inside CanMatchChildren's recursion. Across n2 outer roots this is pure repeated work on immutable structure. Caching directed subtree-embed results collapses redundant recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.risk: Full memoization needs a table cleared per outer-root where orientation differs; correctness requires keying on the directed edge (parent,node) for tree2 since rerooting changes child sets. The hoist of tree1 root child collection is a no-semantic-change low-risk win; the memo table is medium-risk and must be validated for the rerooted-parent orientation.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.summary: Eliminate the separate CountChildren pre-pass; it walks each node's adjacency list twice (count then collect).
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.currentCost: CanonicalHashRooted calls CountChildren (full adjacency walk) to size the stackalloc, then CollectAndSortChildHashes walks the same list again. Two passes over next[] per node = doubled pointer-chasing on the recursion's hottest structure. AutomorphismCountRooted has the same double-walk pattern.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.proposedChange: Since the graph is a tree, size childHashes from a precomputed degree array (passed in from CSR construction) and collect+recurse in one pass, removing CountChildren entirely. Where no degree array exists, over-allocate to a known max-degree bound and track idx.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.rationale: Each CountChildren is an extra full list traversal per recursive node; for a deep recursion this is a second cache-cold walk of next[]/to[]. Folding count into the collection pass (using a degree bound for sizing) halves the traversals.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.risk: stackalloc needs a bounded size; using degree[u] (exact for a tree minus parent) is safe; over-allocation by max degree wastes stack but is safe. Collection order before SortUlong must stay adjacency order, which it does, so the hash is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.summary: Insertion sort of child hashes is O(k^2) per node; for star-like / high-degree nodes this makes canonical hashing quadratic.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.currentCost: SortUlong is insertion sort, O(k^2) in the number of children k. A node with k = n-1 children (star center) costs O(n^2). Called per node in CanonicalHashRooted and AutomorphismCountRooted.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.proposedChange: Keep insertion sort for small k (cache-friendly, low overhead) but switch to an in-place unmanaged heapsort/introsort over the ulong* buffer when k exceeds a threshold (e.g. 16-32). Caps worst case at O(k log k) with no managed allocation.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.rationale: Insertion sort is optimal only for tiny/near-sorted inputs. A degree-n star makes a single node pay O(n^2), turning the whole hash quadratic. A threshold-guarded heapsort keeps the common small-degree case fast while bounding the pathological case to O(k log k).
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.risk: Sort must remain a total order on raw ulong values (used for hash-combination order and symmetry-factor equality runs). Any correct ascending sort preserves adjacency of equal keys, which is all the equality-run logic needs.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.summary: stackalloc int[cc1*cc2+1] buffers and all-pairs EmbeddingCheckRooted recursion are allocated/recomputed at every recursion level with no reuse; risks stack overflow on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.currentCost: stackalloc int[cc1*cc2+1] twice (bTo,bNext) at every node of the embedding recursion, and the i*j loop calls EmbeddingCheckRooted for every child pair, each recursively re-allocating its own cc1*cc2 buffers. Deep recursion multiplies stack use by depth*O(cc1*cc2), and pair results are recomputed with no memo.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.proposedChange: Pass a caller-provided scratch arena instead of stackalloc-in-recursion so RAM stays flat with depth. Memoize the boolean EmbeddingCheckRooted(child1,u1,child2,u2) results across the i,j loop and sibling subproblems via a reusable byte table, avoiding recomputing identical (subtree1, oriented-subtree2) embeddability.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.rationale: stackalloc inside a recursive function multiplies stack use by recursion depth; on mobile (small stacks) this is a real overflow / working-set risk. A shared arena keeps memory flat and avoids repeated zeroing of bHead, and memoization removes duplicated all-pairs recursion.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeHashin.risk: Replacing stackalloc-in-recursion with a shared arena changes memory lifetime, not results; the arena must be sized to worst-case depth*width. Memo keys must include tree2 orientation (parent direction) since rerooting changes child sets. Behavior-preserving if keys are exact.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeDp.cs.summary: Avoid recomputing Math.Max(dp0[v],dp1[v]) and re-walking the adjacency list; fold dp1 computation into the existing child loop of DfsMatching.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeDp.cs.currentCost: DfsMatching first loop computes dp0[u] += Math.Max(dp0[v],dp1[v]) over all children, then FindMaxMatchingCandidate walks the same adjacency list AGAIN recomputing Math.Max(dp0[v],dp1[v]) for every child. Two passes over head/to/next (extra pointer-chasing/cache misses) plus a redundant Max per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeDp.cs.proposedChange: The candidate term simplifies: dp0[u] - Max(dp0[v],dp1[v]) + dp0[v] + edgeWeight[e] = dp0[u] + (dp0[v] - Max(dp0[v],dp1[v]) + edgeWeight[e]). Since dp0[u] is constant across candidates, in the first loop accumulate maxExtra = Math.Max(maxExtra, dp0[v] - Math.Max(dp0[v],dp1[v]) + edgeWeight[e]); then dp1[u] = dp0[u] + Math.Max(0, maxExtra). Removes the second adjacency walk entirely.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeDp.cs.rationale: One pass instead of two over the edge list halves pointer-chasing through next[] (the main cache-miss source in tree DP) and removes one Math.Max per edge. dp0[u] is loop-invariant once the loop finishes, so factoring it out is exact.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeDp.cs.risk: maxCand starts at 0 (empty matching at u), so the fused form must keep dp1[u] = dp0[u] + Math.Max(0, maxExtra); for a leaf maxExtra stays at a sentinel <=0 giving dp1=dp0=0, matching current. dp0[u] must be fully accumulated before adding, so compute dp1 after the loop. long arithmetic preserved.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeCentro.summary: Hoist n/2 (the centroid threshold) out of the per-node IsCentroid loop and inline IsCentroid.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeCentro.currentCost: IsCentroid is called once per node in the n-iteration loop; each call recomputes n/2 (a signed integer division the JIT/Burst does not strength-reduce to a shift for signed n) and incurs a non-inlined call (IsCentroid lacks AggressiveInlining).
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeCentro.proposedChange: Compute int half = n >> 1; once before the loop (n is a vertex count, always >= 0, so >>1 == /2 exactly). Inline the body: int rem = n - size[i]; int mc = maxChild[i] > rem ? maxChild[i] : rem; if (mc <= half) centroids[centroidCount++] = i; Removes one div and one call per node.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeCentro.rationale: n is loop-invariant, so n/2 is recomputed n times for no reason; hoisting yields a single shift. For non-negative n, n>>1 is bit-identical to n/2, turning a division into a 1-cycle shift. Inlining removes call overhead on the hot scan.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreeCentro.risk: n>>1 differs from n/2 only for negative n; n is a vertex count and always non-negative here, so the result is identical. No observable behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreePathCo.summary: Make the boundary-segment-merge decrement branchless to shorten the dependency chain in the hot segment-tree merge.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreePathCo.currentCost: Merge runs on every Build/Update/Query node combine (O(log n) per op, called heavily). The 'if (left.RightColor==right.LeftColor && left.RightColor!=0) res.SegCount--;' is a data-dependent branch that mispredicts on alternating-color inputs, stalling the merge dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreePathCo.proposedChange: Compute an int 0/1 decrement from comparison results and subtract unconditionally: int dec = (left.RightColor == right.LeftColor & left.RightColor != 0) ? 1 : 0; res.SegCount = left.SegCount + right.SegCount - dec; expressed so the codegen is cmp+and+sub with no conditional jump. The SegCount==0 neutral-element early returns stay as branches (they select a whole node).
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreePathCo.rationale: Converting the rare-decrement branch into an unconditional subtract of a 0/1 mask removes a potential mispredict per merge and keeps SegCount on a single straight-line dependency chain, which Burst/LLVM can fold into a cmp+sub.
src/IAFahim.Graph.TreeQueries/TreePathCo.risk: Only the interior decrement becomes branchless; the SegCount==0 guards must remain branches. The mask must reproduce exactly: decrement iff RightColor==LeftColor AND RightColor!=0, and must yield 0/1 (not -1) before subtracting.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.summary: Per-vertex adjacency is found by scanning the entire edge list (O(m) per call), making Kuhn O(V*m) augment attempts instead of O(V*E) over a CSR adjacency.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.currentCost: Each TryKuhn(u) loops `for i in 0..m: if leftU[i]!=u continue`. With V augmenting searches, each touching up to V recursion levels, total edge-scan work is O(V^2 * m). For dense bipartite graphs this is an order of magnitude worse than the textbook O(V*E).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.proposedChange: Build a CSR adjacency (head/to/next or rowStart[]+colIdx[]) once at the top of Run from (leftU,rightV), then iterate only the true neighbors of u: `for e = head[u]; e!=0; e=next[e]`. The build is O(m); each Kuhn step then visits deg(u) edges, not m.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.rationale: Reduces inner-loop trip count from m to deg(u); summed over the algorithm this drops the asymptotic from O(V^2*m) to O(V*E). Far fewer comparisons and far better cache locality since neighbors are contiguous.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.risk: Requires extra stackalloc/scratch for the CSR arrays (size n+1 and m). Output (matchL/matchR, return count) is identical. Caller-allocated scratch may be preferable to keep within house pointer conventions.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.summary: Hopcroft-Karp's claimed O(E*sqrt(V)) is destroyed: every Bfs and Dfs neighbor expansion scans all m edges with `if eu[i]!=u continue`.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.currentCost: Bfs runs O(phases) ~ sqrt(V) times, each dequeue scans all m edges -> O(V*m) per phase, O(V*sqrt(V)*m) total. Dfs likewise scans m per node. This is dramatically worse than the algorithm's design complexity.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.proposedChange: Precompute CSR adjacency from (eu,ev) once in Run and have Bfs/Dfs walk only neighbors of u. Add a per-vertex iterator pointer (current-edge array, like Dinic) so Dfs does not re-scan dead edges within a phase.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.rationale: Restores O(E*sqrt(V)). The current-edge pointer also avoids re-examining already-failed edges, eliminating repeated work inside a phase.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.risk: Needs CSR scratch (n+1, m) plus an iterator array reset each Bfs phase. Behavior/outputs unchanged. The iterator-pointer optimization must reset per phase, not per Dfs, to stay correct.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.summary: The Konig BFS alternating-tree walk scans all m edges per dequeued vertex (`if eu[i]!=u continue`), giving O(V*m) instead of O(V+E).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.currentCost: `while qh<qt { for i in 0..m: if eu[i]!=u continue ... }` is O(m) per vertex over a BFS that can touch all left vertices -> O(V*m).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.proposedChange: Reuse the same CSR adjacency suggested for the matching routines to expand only u's true neighbors.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.rationale: Linear-in-edges traversal instead of quadratic; same cover output (coverL/coverR, coverSize).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.risk: Shares the CSR-build dependency. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.summary: BFS queue `int* q = stackalloc int[n]` is allocated inside the per-component `for start` loop in IsBipartite/ColorBipartite, accumulating stack across components.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.currentCost: C# stackalloc inside a loop is not freed per iteration; over up to n components this can reserve up to n*n*4 bytes of stack, a real overflow hazard on mobile/Burst for large disconnected graphs.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int* q = stackalloc int[n]` above the `for start` loop (reset qh/qt per component). The queue is overwritten each component, so a single allocation suffices.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.rationale: Bounds stack use to O(n) instead of O(n^2) worst case; one allocation instead of up to n. No behavioral change since qh/qt are reset each component.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.risk: None semantically — queue contents are reinitialized per component. Safe, mechanical hoist.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.summary: Two-coloring uses `1 - color[u]`; `color[u] ^ 1` is a cheaper, branch-free toggle.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.currentCost: `1 - color[u]` is a subtraction with a constant; XOR with 1 is one ALU op and pairs better, and for {0,1} domain is provably equivalent.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.rationale: Single XOR instead of load-immediate + subtract; trivially equivalent over the {0,1} color domain used here.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBipartite.cs.risk: Only valid because colors are strictly 0/1 (guaranteed: start=0, propagated via toggle). Safe.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.summary: Each edge relaxation does a linear scan of the blocked-edge list to test if (u,v) is blocked, making relaxation O(blockCount) per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.currentCost: Inside the per-edge loop: `for b in 0..blockCount: if blockedU[b]==u && blockedV[b]==v`. Over a Dijkstra run this is O(E*blockCount) extra comparisons, and Yen calls Dijkstra O(k*pathLen) times.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.proposedChange: Yen already maintains boolean arrays blockedU[]/blockedV[] indexed by node (set in the spur loop, lines 320/334-337). Pass those node-indexed boolean maps into Dijkstra and test `blockedFromU[u] && blockedToV[v]` in O(1) — but since multiple (u,v) pairs may be blocked, instead keep a per-source-node blocked-target structure: mark blocked targets in a reusable `int* blockEpoch` stamped with u so the test is a single compare. At minimum, early-out when blockCount==0 (currently still enters the loop body bookkeeping).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.rationale: Removes an inner O(blockCount) scan from the hottest loop in Yen; turns blocked-edge test into O(1). Blocked sets are tiny but the scan runs per relaxed edge across many Dijkstra invocations.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.risk: Must preserve exact blocking semantics: only the specific (u,v) directed pairs are blocked, not all edges out of u. An epoch-stamped per-u target set preserves this; a naive node-only boolean would over-block and change results. Reset/epoch handling must be correct.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.summary: The Dijkstra/A* heap heap-allocates three buffers via Marshal.AllocHGlobal on every construction; Yen and AStar create a fresh RemMinHeap per call (Yen: once per Dijkstra, i.e. O(k*pathLen) times).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.currentCost: Each RemMinHeap(n) does 3 AllocHGlobal + an O(n) Pos init, and Dispose does 3 FreeHGlobal. In YenKShortestPaths every spur Dijkstra allocates/frees the heap — hundreds of malloc/free pairs and O(n) inits, plus AllocHGlobal is a syscall-grade allocator hostile to Burst and to mobile fragmentation.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.proposedChange: Switch the heap to caller-provided scratch pointers (stackalloc or pre-allocated by the top-level Run), making PushOrUpdate/Pop operate on borrowed memory. Reset only the Pos entries actually touched (track a dirty list) instead of O(n) full clears per construction.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.rationale: Eliminates all per-call heap allocation on the hot path, removes Marshal interop (which Burst cannot compile), and replaces O(n) re-init with O(touched). Major win for Yen's inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.risk: Changes RemMinHeap's lifetime model and the signatures of AStar/Dijkstra to take scratch. Burst currently cannot compile Marshal.AllocHGlobal at all, so this is also a correctness/compilability fix. Must ensure Pos is fully -1 before reuse (epoch or dirty-list reset).

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.summary: Sift-up/down swap each level fully (3-way temp swap of Dist and V plus two Pos writes per level); a hole-based shift avoids per-level swaps.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.currentCost: Each sift level does: read parent, compare, then swap Dist (3 ops), swap V (3 ops), write Pos[V[p]] and Pos[V[idx]]. Over log(n) levels that's ~8*log(n) memory ops per push/pop, with the intermediate Pos writes immediately overwritten on the next level.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.proposedChange: Use the classic 'hole' technique: cache the incoming (d,v), shift parents/children down into the hole without swapping, and write the cached element plus its Pos exactly once at the final position. Mark Pop's leaf method and PushOrUpdate with [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] since they are tiny hot leaves.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.rationale: Halves the data movement per level (one shift vs three-element swap) and removes redundant intermediate Pos updates, shortening the dependency chain in the tightest loop of every Dijkstra/A*.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.risk: Logic must keep heap invariant identical; only the final landing slot updates Pos. Inlining a recursive-free leaf is safe. Outputs identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.summary: Component merging uses an O(n) relabel loop per accepted edge instead of union-find, and totalWeight adds bestW[i] (wrong index) where the cheapest edge was stored under cu/cv.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.currentCost: Inside the accept loop: `for j in 0..n: if comp[j]==cu comp[j]=cv` is O(n) per merge, and comp[u[i]] lookups give no path compression, so the whole routine is O(n*m + n^2) per round over up to n rounds. Plus `totalWeight += bestW[i]` indexes by component-slot i, not the cu/cv where the chosen edge's weight lives.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.proposedChange: Replace comp[] with a DSU (parent + Find with path halving, union by rank). Accumulate totalWeight from the actually chosen best edge's weight (bestW[cu]) at the point of acceptance, not bestW[i].
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.rationale: DSU drops merge cost from O(n) to near-O(1) amortized, giving the textbook O(m*log n) Boruvka. Using the correct weight slot is a correctness fix that also removes ambiguity.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.risk: The bestW[i] vs bestW[cu] discrepancy is a likely existing bug — flag rather than silently 'optimize'; verify against tests before changing. DSU change is purely structural and preserves the MST produced (modulo tie-break order).

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.summary: An expansion loop with nested while/for that always `break`s after one iteration and produces no effect — dead/incomplete code that still costs a scan.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.currentCost: The `for i in 1..n { ... while(...) for k ... break; }` block runs an O(n) (worst O(n^2)) search whose only statement-effect is the unconditional `break` at line 160; it computes nothing used. Pure wasted work each recursion level.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.proposedChange: Either remove the dead block or implement the real contracted-edge expansion. Until then it adds asymptotic cost to every recursive ChuLiuEdmonds call without contributing to result[].
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.rationale: Removing a provably-effect-free O(n^2) loop is a direct cycle saving at every recursion depth.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.risk: Correctness concern: the expansion appears unfinished, so result[] reconstruction may be wrong. Flag and verify against tests; do not treat as a safe micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.summary: These routines use C# local functions with recursion capturing outer pointers; recursive local-function closures and deep recursion are problematic under Burst and risk stack overflow on large graphs.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.currentCost: Local-function `void Dfs(...)` captures head/to/next/disc/low/etc.; Burst either cannot compile capturing local functions cleanly or boxes the display class. Deep recursion (depth up to n) also overflows mobile stacks.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.proposedChange: Convert the recursive DFS to an explicit iterative DFS using a caller- or stack-allocated state stack (vertex + edge-iterator), passing pointers explicitly instead of capturing. This is the same pattern Hierholzer already uses.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.rationale: Makes the code Burst-compilable (no closure/display-class), removes call overhead, and bounds stack to an explicit O(n) buffer instead of unbounded native recursion — critical on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphRemaining.cs.risk: Iterative rewrite must faithfully reproduce the post-order low[] updates and bucket/edge-stack bookkeeping; non-trivial. Verify against tests. Behavior must match for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.summary: Hardcoded `stackalloc int[20000]` for flow plus a full O(20000) zeroing every outer iteration, independent of actual edge count.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.currentCost: `int* flow = stackalloc int[20000]` is 80 KB of stack (risks stack overflow under Burst, and blows L1). The reset `for j in 0..20000: flow[j]=0` runs n-1 times = O(20000*n) writes regardless of real m. Also `bool* vis = stackalloc bool[n]` is allocated inside the loop (stackalloc in a loop does not free per iteration in C#, so this leaks stack frame space up to n*n bytes).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Size flow by the real edge count (pass m or 2*m+2) instead of 20000; reset only the used entries. Hoist `bool* vis = stackalloc bool[n]` out of the for loop to a single allocation. Zero only `flow[1..edgeCount]`.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.rationale: Cuts stack footprint from fixed 80 KB to O(edges), removes O(20000*n) redundant zeroing, and stops the in-loop stackalloc from accumulating. Big cache and cycle win, and removes a Burst stack-overflow hazard on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.risk: Need the true edge-array length threaded into the signature (currently absent). Hoisting vis is safe because Bfs reinitializes vis[i]=false at its start. Behavior identical for valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.summary: Hardcoded `stackalloc int[20000]` for the DFS stack regardless of graph size.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.currentCost: 80 KB fixed stack allocation; on a small graph this is wasted, on a large one (edges > ~20000) it silently overflows. Burst on mobile has tight stack budgets.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Size the stack by the actual upper bound: the Euler circuit visits each edge once, so stack depth is bounded by (number of edges + 1). Thread the edge count in and use `stackalloc int[edgeCount + 1]`.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.rationale: Right-sizes stack to the problem, eliminating both waste and overflow risk; tighter working set improves cache behavior.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.risk: Requires an edge-count parameter. The circuit buffer is caller-allocated already, so this only affects the internal stack. Semantics unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.summary: Blossom contraction relabels bases with a full O(n) scan per shrink step, inflating Contract to O(n^2) per blossom.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.currentCost: `for i in 0..n: if base_[i]==oldBaseU || base_[i]==oldBaseMv base_[i]=lca` runs inside the while-walk up the blossom, so a single Contract is O(blossomLen * n).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Defer base reassignment: collect the vertices on the blossom path and relabel them in one pass after the walk, or use a union-find over bases so base lookups stay near-O(1) and the explicit relabel scan disappears.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.rationale: Removes the nested O(n) scan from each contraction step; brings blossom matching closer to its standard O(V^3) (or better) bound instead of an inflated constant.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.risk: Must keep base_ semantics consistent for the subsequent GetLca/relax logic. Union-find variant changes how base_ is read everywhere; the deferred single-pass relabel is the lower-risk option. Verify against matching tests.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.summary: Allocates an n*n scratch matrix to hold the negated cost, doubling the working set for a pure transform.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.currentCost: `long* maxCost = stackalloc long[n*n]` is 8*n^2 bytes of stack on top of the caller's cost matrix; for n in the hundreds this is large stack pressure and a full O(n^2) copy.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Two options: (a) require the caller to pass scratch, or (b) since HungarianMin only reads cost[(i)*n+j], pass a small bias (maxVal) and a flag so HungarianMin computes (maxVal - cost) on the fly, avoiding the materialized matrix entirely. At minimum fuse the two loops (find maxVal and copy) — currently maxVal is found in the same double loop, then a second full O(n^2) pass negates; the negation pass cannot start until maxVal is known, but the initial copy is redundant since you could store cost directly and subtract in the second pass reading original cost.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.rationale: Eliminates an 8*n^2-byte stack buffer and one O(n^2) copy pass; reduces cache footprint for the subsequent Hungarian solve.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.risk: On-the-fly negation requires threading a transform into HungarianMin (API change). The fuse-only variant is safe and behavior-preserving. Result formula `(long)n*maxVal - result` unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.summary: Preference-rank inverse table is indexed with `w*n + mID`; multiply per access can be strength-reduced, and the two classes are byte-identical duplicates.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.currentCost: Every womanRank/receiverRank access recomputes `idx*n + other` (a multiply) in hot proposal loops. Two near-identical implementations also double code size / icache.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Hoist row-base pointers (`long* row = womanRank + w*n`) outside inner loops where w is fixed, turning index math into a single add. Collapse GaleShapley to delegate to StableMarriage (the proposerIsMan flag is unused in the body) to remove duplicate code.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.rationale: Removes a multiply from the per-access address computation in the rank-table build loops and reduces instruction-cache duplication.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.risk: Ergonomics/icache only; outputs identical. Confirm proposerIsMan truly has no behavioral effect before collapsing (it is written nowhere in the shown body).

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.summary: MergeNodes calls UpdateWeightsAfterPhase with add=null (a no-op guarded by `add != null`), so the merge does no weight folding — flag as dead/incorrect code rather than optimize.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.currentCost: UpdateWeightsAfterPhase's body `if (vis[to[e]]==phase && add != null) add[last]+=...` can never execute since add is always null here; the call is pure overhead and the intended merge bookkeeping is missing.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.proposedChange: Remove the dead call or implement the real Stoer-Wagner merge (fold t's incident weights into s). As-is the routine likely produces wrong min-cuts; do not micro-optimize until the algorithm is corrected.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.rationale: Eliminating provably-dead branches removes wasted edge-scan cycles; correcting the merge is required for the result to be meaningful.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphAdvanced.cs.risk: This is a correctness flag, not a semantics-preserving micro-opt. Verify intended behavior against tests before changing; reported here so the dead branch isn't mistaken for live hot code.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBasic.cs.summary: Edge-add helpers take an unused `int* edgeCount` parameter, and AddEdge/AddDirectedEdge are byte-identical; AggressiveInlining is missing on these tiny hot leaves.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBasic.cs.currentCost: The unused `edgeCount` parameter forces callers (BuildAdjacency passes `&m`) to materialize an address and occupies an argument register on every call. Without inlining, BuildAdjacency pays a call per edge.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBasic.cs.proposedChange: Drop the unused edgeCount parameter, collapse AddDirectedEdge into AddEdge (identical bodies), and mark Run with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] so BuildAdjacency's per-edge call is inlined into a few pointer writes.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBasic.cs.rationale: Removes a dead parameter and a redundant address-of in the build loop, and inlining a 4-statement leaf eliminates call overhead across all m edges.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphBasic.cs.risk: Signature change is an API break for callers; mechanical. Inlining a tiny pointer-only leaf is safe and Burst-friendly. Outputs identical.

src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.summary: Replace parent/child index arithmetic (idx-1)/2 and idx*2+1 with shifts.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.currentCost: Each sift step computes (idx - 1) / 2 (signed integer division, ~20+ cycle latency, not strength-reduced because idx is signed and div semantics differ for negatives) and idx*2+1 / idx*2+2 (a multiply). In a binary heap these run O(log n) times per push/pop, and Prim does O(m) pushes plus O(n) pops.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.proposedChange: parent = (idx - 1) >> 1; left = (idx << 1) + 1; right = left + 1. idx is always >= 0 here (heap indices), so >>1 is identical to /2 and right=left+1 avoids a second multiply.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.rationale: Signed /2 emits an extra add+shift sequence to handle the rounding-toward-zero of negatives; an unsigned-safe >>1 on a known-nonnegative value is a single shift. Multiplies become shifts. Shortens the dependency chain on the hot heap path.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.risk: idx is provably >= 0 throughout (it starts at Size++ or 0 and only moves to parent/child indices), so >>1 == /2 exactly. No signed-negative hazard. Pure micro-opt, semantics preserved.

src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.summary: O(m^2 * alpha) recomputation of MST-minus-one-edge; replace with single MST + max-edge-on-path queries.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.currentCost: The second loop reruns a full Kruskal-style union pass for every one of m skipped edges: O(m) edges each doing Find, giving O(m^2 alpha(n)). For dense graphs this is the dominant cost of the whole function.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.proposedChange: Compute the MST once, build the tree, and for each non-tree edge (u,v) find the maximum-weight tree edge on the u-v path (via the already-present DFS/LCA-style max-edge query used elsewhere in MstVariants). Second-best MST weight = best + min over non-tree edges of (w(e) - maxPathEdge). This is O(m log n) or O(m + n) versus O(m^2).
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.rationale: Standard second-best-MST algorithm. Removes a full Union-Find rebuild per candidate edge, turning a quadratic outer loop into a single linear/near-linear pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.risk: Must replace the max tree edge being removed (not just any), and handle the case where the candidate edge connects same path correctly. Need to ensure ties and the 'exactly one different edge' semantics match the current brute-force result. Behavior must be validated against existing tests; if equivalence is uncertain, keep brute force. Correctness-sensitive change.

src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.summary: Insertion-sort comparator uses ew[i] instead of ew[idx[j]] consistently; also key indexes the wrong array vs Kruskal's SortEdges.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.currentCost: In the first block the insertion sort sets key = ew[i] (raw index i) while comparing ew[idx[j]] and placing idx[j+1]=i. This sorts by original positions' weights, not by a stable permutation the way MinimumSpanningTreeKruskal.SortEdges does (key = ew[idx[i]]). It still produces a valid sorted order here because it inserts i directly, but the comparison key ew[i] vs ew[idx[j]] mixes indexing conventions and is fragile.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.proposedChange: Use key = ew[idx[i]] and ki = idx[i] exactly as MinimumSpanningTreeKruskal.SortEdges does, for consistency and to avoid an extra indirection mismatch. No asymptotic change but removes a correctness-adjacent inconsistency.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.rationale: Consistency with the proven SortEdges path; the current mixed indexing happens to work only because idx[i]==i at the start of each insertion, which is an implicit invariant easy to break.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.risk: Behavior-preserving only if idx[i]==i holds when the comparison starts (it does, since idx is identity-initialized and insertion sort processes left-to-right). Confirm before applying; this is an ergonomics/robustness fix, not a speedup.

src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.summary: Dead 'if (ProcessKruskalEdge(...)) { }' wrapper and a bool return that is never used.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.currentCost: ProcessKruskalEdge returns bool but the caller does `if (ProcessKruskalEdge(...)) { }` — an empty if with an unused result. Costs nothing at runtime after JIT/Burst but is misleading and the bool return forces the method not to be a clean void.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.proposedChange: Make ProcessKruskalEdge return void and call it directly: ProcessKruskalEdge(idx[i], ...). Cleaner API, no behavior change.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.rationale: Pure readability/ergonomics; removes a confusing empty-branch idiom. Burst already elides it so no perf delta, but it improves maintainability without touching the perf model.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.risk: None — the return value is provably unused.

src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.summary: SecondBestMst.Find lacks path compression and union-by-rank; repeated Find on long chains is O(n) each.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.currentCost: SecondBestMst.Find walks parent pointers with no compression, and its Union is `parent[pu]=pv` with no rank/size — chains can degrade to O(n) per Find. Within the O(m) inner rebuild (already quadratic), this adds another factor on pathological inputs.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.proposedChange: Use the path-halving Find + union-by-rank/size already implemented elsewhere (MstVariants uses path-compressing Find local functions). At minimum apply path halving: while(parent[x]!=x){parent[x]=parent[parent[x]]; x=parent[x];}.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.rationale: Brings amortized Find to near-O(alpha(n)) instead of worst-case O(n), reducing the constant on the already-heavy second-best loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Mst.cs.risk: None for correctness — DSU with compression yields identical connectivity results; only performance changes. If SecondBestMst is replaced per the complexity finding above, this becomes moot.

src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.summary: O(m^2) selection/bubble sorts of edges; replace with the O(m^2 worst but typically far better) insertion sort already used in Kruskal, or a real O(m log m) sort.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.currentCost: These methods sort edges with a nested-for selection sort: for i, for j>i, compare and swap. That is always Theta(m^2) comparisons regardless of input. For m edges this dominates and does not vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.proposedChange: Replace each selection sort with an index-based insertion sort (matching MinimumSpanningTreeKruskal.SortEdges) for small m, or better, a non-recursive radix/heaps-free in-place heapsort over a stackalloc index buffer for O(m log m). At minimum, insertion sort is O(m) on already-near-sorted data and never worse in constant factor than this selection sort.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.rationale: Selection sort always does ~m^2/2 comparisons AND up to m^2/2 swaps; insertion sort does ~m^2/4 comparisons and far fewer writes on partially ordered data; heapsort gives a true asymptotic win for large m. Fewer memory writes = fewer store-buffer stalls.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.risk: Sort must remain stable/total-order-equivalent for the lexicographic variant (LexicographicMst uses a 3-key comparator: weight, min(u,v), max(u,v)). Any replacement must preserve that exact tie-break ordering or Kruskal picks different edges. For plain-weight variants any correct sort is fine.

src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.summary: O(n*m) linear edge search to recover each chosen parent edge; precompute a (parent,child)->edge map once.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.currentCost: After ChuLiuEdmonds, for each of up to n result vertices it scans all m original edges (inner for e=0..m) to find the matching (parent,child) edge. That is O(n*m) just for output reconstruction.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.proposedChange: Build the adjacency once (or a hash-free bucket: head/next arrays keyed by parent node, like the rest of the codebase) so each result[i] lookup is O(deg) instead of O(m). Total becomes O(m + sum deg) = O(m).
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.rationale: Turns the reconstruction from O(n*m) to O(m). Reuses the head/to/next CSR pattern already pervasive in this module, so it stays Burst-friendly with raw pointers.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.risk: Must pick the same edge the original linear scan would (first matching by edge index) to preserve identical resultEdges output when parallel edges exist. Bucket build should insert in ascending edge order or iterate to keep first-match semantics.

src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.summary: Recomputes (n-1)*(n-1) and i*dim repeatedly; hoist dim and row offsets out of inner loops.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.currentCost: The init loop bound (n-1)*(n-1) is recomputed every iteration of the for-condition. Matrix accesses laplacian[i*dim+k], laplacian[pivot*dim+k], laplacian[j*dim+k] recompute the row-base multiply i*dim, pivot*dim, j*dim inside k-loops. Power() (modular inverse) is called once per pivot row.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int total=(n-1)*(n-1) before the init loop. In Gaussian elimination cache long* rowI=laplacian+i*dim, rowJ=laplacian+j*dim, rowPivot=laplacian+pivot*dim and index by [k] so the multiply is done once per row, not once per element.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.rationale: Removes a multiply from each inner-loop iteration (O(dim) saved multiplies per row -> O(dim^2) per elimination step). Pointer-walking the row is also more vectorization/prefetch friendly under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.risk: None — pure addressing reassociation, identical results. Note the modular arithmetic and Power(...Mod-2...) Fermat inverse already assume Mod prime, which holds (1e9+7).

src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.summary: exp%2 and exp/=2 on a known-nonnegative long; use &1 and >>1.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.currentCost: Loop does exp % 2 == 1 and exp /= 2 each iteration. Signed long % and / are expensive and not auto-strength-reduced because exp is signed.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.proposedChange: (exp & 1L) == 1L and exp >>= 1. exp is always >= 0 (starts as Mod-2 > 0, only halved), so shifts are exact.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.rationale: & and >> are single-cycle versus multi-cycle signed div/rem. Runs ~30 iterations per call, called once per pivot row in ArborescenceCount.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.risk: exp is provably nonnegative for all callers (Mod-2). If a future caller passes negative exp the behavior would differ, but current usage is safe; note the guard in risk.

src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.summary: Per-iteration stackalloc of head/next/to/edgeId/cycleEdges inside the while(deg<k) and inner eAdd loops risks stack growth and re-zeroing every pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.currentCost: Inside the while loop, for each candidate eAdd, the code stackallocs head[n], next[2n], to[2n], edgeId[2n], cycleEdges[n] and rebuilds the tree adjacency from scratch (O(n) zero + O(m) build) for every candidate edge every improvement round. stackalloc inside a loop in C# does NOT free per-iteration; it accumulates until method return, so this can blow the stack for large n*k.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.proposedChange: Hoist these buffers to a single stackalloc before the loops and re-init only the needed prefix each pass. Build the tree adjacency once per while-iteration (it only changes when an edge is swapped), not once per eAdd candidate.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.rationale: Avoids unbounded stack accumulation (correctness/robustness on mobile with small stacks) and removes redundant O(m) adjacency rebuilds per candidate edge — large constant-factor and a real stack-overflow risk reduction.
src/IAFahim.Graph/MstVariants.cs.risk: Must re-zero the reused buffers' used prefix each pass to preserve semantics. Hoisting the adjacency build requires confirming inTree only changes between while-iterations, not within the eAdd scan (it does not). Local functions capturing pointers must still see the hoisted buffers.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.summary: Zero-init loop for indeg can be a single memset-style clear; q init loop can fuse with indeg pass partially.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.currentCost: for i: indeg[i]=0 is a manual scalar loop. Burst will likely vectorize it, but it is a separate pass over n before the edge-counting pass.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.proposedChange: Use Unsafe.InitBlock / a memclear over indeg (n*sizeof(int) bytes) for the zeroing, which Burst lowers to a vectorized/memset path. The subsequent 'find indeg==0' queue-seed pass is inherently separate and fine.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.rationale: A bulk clear is fewer instructions and better memory bandwidth utilization than a scalar store loop when Burst does not fully vectorize. Minor but free.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.risk: None; InitBlock(ptr, 0, n*sizeof(int)) is exactly equivalent to the per-element zero loop. Same pattern applies to the many for-loop initializations across these files.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.summary: Recursive DFS risks stack overflow and is not the iterative pattern used elsewhere; Tarjan/Kosaraju recursion depth is O(n).
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.currentCost: FirstDfs, SecondDfs, and TarjanScc.Run recurse to depth O(n). On a path graph of large n this overflows the (small, on mobile) native stack, and deep recursion defeats Burst inlining/optimization. IterativeDfs in GraphTraversal.cs already shows the explicit-stack pattern the codebase prefers.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.proposedChange: Convert these DFS routines to explicit-stack iterative form (stack + per-frame edge iterator), mirroring IterativeDfs.Run. For Tarjan, push (node, edgePointer) frames and emulate the post-order lowlink update.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.rationale: Eliminates O(n) native recursion depth (robustness on mobile), keeps everything in one Burst-compiled function with no call overhead per node, and matches the established iterative convention for ergonomics.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.risk: Iterative Tarjan must faithfully reproduce lowlink propagation order and SCC pop sequence; this is a nontrivial rewrite and must be validated against the recursive output (component ids/order). Higher correctness risk — gate behind tests.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.summary: Duplicate-edge check scans the condensed adjacency list per edge -> O(E * avgCondDeg); could use a per-source visited stamp.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.currentCost: For every original edge crossing components, it walks the entire condensed adjacency list of cu looking for cv (the 'exists' linear scan). Worst case this is O(E * D) where D is condensed out-degree, i.e. quadratic in dense condensations.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.proposedChange: Use a stamp array seen[sccCount] (stackalloc int) and a monotonically increasing token per source component cu: when processing all edges grouped by cu, mark seen[cv]=token and skip if already == token. Avoids the inner adjacency walk. Requires iterating edges grouped by source component or resetting the stamp when cu changes.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.rationale: Replaces the per-edge linear adjacency scan with O(1) stamp test, dropping the dedup cost from O(E*D) to O(E). Classic visited-token trick, allocation-free.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTopo.cs.risk: Must reset/advance the token correctly when cu changes; since edges are iterated by u (not grouped by cu), need either a token keyed by cu or a 2D-free scheme. Output edge ordering must remain identical (first-seen insertion). Validate ordering.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.summary: Recursive DFS with O(n) depth; prefer the iterative variant already present.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.currentCost: Recursive Run recurses to depth O(n); same native-stack-overflow and Burst-inlining concerns as the Kosaraju/Tarjan note. The codebase already ships IterativeDfs.Run which is the safe equivalent.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.proposedChange: Either document Dfs.Run as small-graph-only, or provide the timer (discovery/finish time) semantics inside IterativeDfs so callers can use the iterative version exclusively. Avoid recursion on the hot/large-n path.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.rationale: Removes O(n) recursion depth, avoids per-call frame setup, keeps Burst happy.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.risk: IterativeDfs currently does not produce the in/out 'time' stamps that Dfs.Run does; adding them must replicate the pre/post increment timing exactly. Behavior parity required.

src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.summary: Deque wrap-around uses branchy if(dh>=n)dh=0 / if(dh<0)dh=n-1; fine, but dist[u]+w recomputed and compared twice.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.currentCost: Inside the relax loop, dist[u] is reloaded and dist[u]+w computed; the comparison dist[v] > dist[u]+w then the assignment dist[v]=dist[u]+w recomputes the sum. Minor redundant add. The circular-buffer index wrap is branchy but predictable.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long du = dist[u] before the edge loop (loop-invariant), and compute long nd = du + w once, compare and store nd. Keeps the add off the critical path's second use.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.rationale: Removes a redundant add and a redundant load of dist[u] across all out-edges of u. dist[u] is invariant for the whole inner loop since u is popped and not relaxed against itself.
src/IAFahim.Graph/GraphTraversal.cs.risk: None — dist[u] is not modified within its own out-edge relaxation loop (no self-loops would change it before use in a way that affects correctness since we use the popped snapshot). Standard SPFA/0-1 BFS hoist.

src/IAFahim.Graph/Planar.cs.summary: Dijkstra implemented as O(n^2 + n*m) with linear min-scan and full edge rescan per settle; use the existing MstMinHeap-style binary heap.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Planar.cs.currentCost: PlanarShortestPath and FacePotentialSolve do an O(n) linear scan to pick the min unvisited vertex each of n iterations, and inside settle they scan ALL m edges to find incident ones (since there is no adjacency list). That is O(n^2 + n*m).
src/IAFahim.Graph/Planar.cs.proposedChange: Build a CSR adjacency (head/to/next/weight) once like the rest of the module, and use the indexed binary heap (MstMinHeap is internal but the pattern is reusable) to get O((n+m) log n). For planar graphs (m = O(n)) this is O(n log n) versus O(n^2).
src/IAFahim.Graph/Planar.cs.rationale: Removes both the O(n) min-scan and the O(m) per-vertex edge rescan, giving a genuine asymptotic improvement on the planar (sparse) graphs this file targets.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Planar.cs.risk: Heap operates on long distances; FacePotentialSolve uses double potentials and would need a double-keyed heap variant. Must preserve tie-break/visit order if any downstream logic depends on it (Dijkstra distances are order-independent, so safe). Adding adjacency build must not change which equal-distance node is 'settled' in a way that affects outputs (it does not for distances).

src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.summary: Inner Dijkstra scans all m edges per popped vertex instead of using an adjacency list, making each of the n single-source runs O(V * (V + E_scan*m)).
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.currentCost: For every Pop (up to nodes processed) the loop `for (int i=0;i<m;i++){ if(eu[i]!=u) continue; ... }` walks the entire edge array. Per source that is O(P * m) where P is pops; over n sources O(n * V * m). For a graph with m edges this is far worse than Johnson's intended O(n * (E + V log V)).
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.proposedChange: Build a CSR/linked adjacency over (eu,ev,ew) once before the s-loop (head[n], to[m], next[m], w[m] in stackalloc/single allocation) and in the inner Dijkstra iterate `for (int e=head[u]; e!=...; e=next[e])` like the other Dijkstra variants, instead of the linear `eu[i]!=u` filter.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.rationale: Replaces an O(m) membership scan per vertex pop with O(deg(u)) neighbor iteration, restoring Johnson to its asymptotic E*V + V^2 log V cost. The reduced-weight formula at the edge is unchanged, so outputs are identical.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.risk: Must preserve the existing (unusual) reduced-cost expression `d + ew[e] + h[s] - h[v]` exactly when porting to the adjacency walk; adjacency build must store the original ew alongside to/next. No signedness change.

src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.summary: Heap allocates three separate Marshal.AllocHGlobal blocks (and three FreeHGlobal) per Dijkstra/Johnson invocation; Johnson does this n times inside its loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.currentCost: 3 syscalls-class allocations + 3 frees per heap lifetime. In Johnson.Run a fresh SpMinHeap is created and disposed inside the `for (int s...)` loop => 3n allocations + 3n frees. Marshal.AllocHGlobal is also a managed interop call that does not play well with Burst hot paths.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.proposedChange: Either (a) coalesce the three arrays into one AllocHGlobal of size n*(sizeof(long)+2*sizeof(int)) with pointer offsets (1 alloc/free instead of 3), or (b) since every caller already knows n and the heap is single-threaded scratch, pass caller-provided stackalloc buffers (Dist/V/Pos) into the heap and drop Marshal entirely. In Johnson, hoist the heap (and its buffers) outside the s-loop and reset Size/Pos per source.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.rationale: Fewer allocations cut per-call overhead from 3 (or 3n) heap ops to 1 (or 0 with stackalloc), removes managed interop from the Burst path, and improves locality by keeping the three arrays contiguous.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.risk: stackalloc variant requires n small enough for stack; library already uses stackalloc[n] elsewhere so consistent. Hoisting in Johnson requires resetting Pos[]=-1 and Size=0 each source; must re-init Pos fully to avoid stale positions.

src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.summary: Innermost loop recomputes i*n, k*n and re-reads dist[i*n+k] every j iteration; the i*n+k term is loop-invariant in j.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.currentCost: Per j iteration: two multiplies (i*n, k*n) plus an extra load of dist[i*n+k]. Over the triple loop that is O(n^3) redundant multiplies and loads on the hottest loop in the library.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `long dik = dist[i*n+k];` and `int inBase = i*n; int knBase = k*n;` outside the j-loop (dik is already guarded non-MAX by the line-290 continue), then inner body uses `dist[knBase+j]`, `nd = dik + dist[knBase+j]`, compare/write `dist[inBase+j]`. Also hoist k*n outside the i-loop where j uses knBase.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.rationale: Removes a multiply and a redundant memory load from the n^3 inner loop, shortening the dependency chain and freeing the load/store ports; classic Floyd-Warshall hoist that Burst will then vectorize more readily.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.risk: None semantically: dik is invariant once i,k fixed; the existing `continue` already guarantees dist[i*n+k] != MAX so caching its value before the j-loop is exact.

src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.summary: Dijkstra.Run and DijkstraSparse.Run have byte-identical bodies (lines 83-110 vs 115-142); DijkstraDense is the only behaviorally distinct variant.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.currentCost: Two literal copies of the same heap-Dijkstra increase code size (icache pressure, more to maintain/verify) with zero behavioral difference; a future fix to one can silently diverge.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.proposedChange: Have DijkstraSparse.Run forward to Dijkstra.Run (or extract a single internal static helper both call). Keep the three public class names for API stability, but a single implementation behind them.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.rationale: Eliminates duplicated machine code and the divergence hazard without changing any observable output; smaller code footprint helps icache on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.risk: Pure refactor; must keep public signatures identical so callers are unaffected. No perf regression since forwarding is a tail call Burst inlines.

src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.summary: h[s] is loop-invariant within the inner Dijkstra edge loop but is re-read and re-added on every edge relaxation.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.currentCost: Line 360 `nd = d + ew[i] + h[s] - h[v]` reloads h[s] for each edge of each pop; h[s] is constant for the whole s iteration.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `long hs = h[s];` once at the top of the `for (int s...)` body and use `nd = d + ew[i] + hs - h[v]`.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.rationale: Removes one load + keeps a register-resident constant in the relaxation inner loop, shortening the arithmetic dependency chain by one operand fetch.
src/IAFahim.Graph/ShortestPath.cs.risk: None: h[] is not modified during the s iteration, so caching h[s] is exact.

src/IAFahim.Graph/Tournament.cs.summary: Euler-circuit DFS uses a fixed `stackalloc int[1024]`; the explicit stack can hold up to m+1 entries, so this both wastes stack for tiny graphs and silently corrupts/overflows for m >= 1024.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Tournament.cs.currentCost: Always reserves 1024 ints (4 KB) regardless of m, and has no bound for m>=1024 — a latent correctness/overflow bug as well as a fixed cost that is too big for small m and too small for large m.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Tournament.cs.proposedChange: Pass m (or n) down and size the stack as `int* stack = stackalloc int[m + 1];` (an Eulerian walk pushes at most one node per directed half-edge plus the start). Allocate once in EulerianOrientation and reuse across the per-component calls rather than re-stackallocing inside the loop.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Tournament.cs.rationale: Right-sizes the buffer to the true bound (m+1), removing the magic 1024, eliminating overflow for large graphs, and cutting stack footprint for small graphs; reusing one buffer avoids repeated stack frame growth across components.
src/IAFahim.Graph/Tournament.cs.risk: Must thread m into ProcessEulerianCircuit. The m+1 bound is the standard Hierholzer stack bound; verify against the half-edge encoding (ve indexed by e/2). Reusing the buffer requires resetting only the stack pointer, not the contents.
