src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.proposedChange: Delete 'using System;' (nothing in the file references the System namespace directly).
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.rationale: Cleaner, keeps the file's surface explicitly Burst-friendly (only Unity.Mathematics + CompilerServices), avoids accidental use of managed System types.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.risk: None; purely a no-op removal if truly unused (confirmed: no System.* references in the file).

src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.summary: Reformulate magnitude with dot + rsqrt to remove sqrt and the chain of scalar divisions (same as 2D).
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.currentCost: math.length(delta)=sqrt(dot) then four divisions (1/dist, 1/radius, /(dist*dist), final /dist). In 3D the float3 divides are also 3-wide. Long sqrt->divide dependency chain on the hot gradient path.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.proposedChange: float d2 = math.dot(delta,delta); gate 'd2 > radius*radius || d2 < 1e-12f'; float invDist = math.rsqrt(d2); float coeff = strength * (invDist - invRadius) * invDist*invDist*invDist; return coeff * delta; (invRadius = 1.0f/radius hoisted; radius*radius and 1e-12f as named constants).
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.rationale: Identical algebra to the 2D case: result = strength*(1/dist - 1/radius)/dist^3 * delta = strength*(invDist - 1/radius)*invDist^3*delta. rsqrt + multiplies replace sqrt + four divides; especially valuable in ComputeGradient's repulsor loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.risk: rsqrt approximation: not bit-identical to sqrt path (~1 ULP); flag if exact reproducibility required. Squared radius gate equivalent for radius>=0; 1e-12f=(1e-6f)^2 matches original lower cutoff.

src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.summary: Normalize via strength*rsqrt(dot)*delta instead of length + float3 divide.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.currentCost: math.length(delta) sqrt; then 'strength*delta/dist' is a 3-wide vector divide. sqrt->divide dependency chain, called once per attractor in ComputeGradient.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.proposedChange: float d2 = math.dot(delta,delta); if (d2 < 1e-12f) return float3.zero; return (strength * math.rsqrt(d2)) * delta;
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.rationale: delta/dist is normalize; one rsqrt + scalar*vector multiply replaces sqrt + vector divide, shortening the chain and removing a 3-wide division per attractor.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.risk: rsqrt precision (not bit-identical). d2<1e-12f equals original dist<1e-6f gate (non-negative both sides).

src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.summary: Add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] is not appropriate here, but mark ComputeGradient's hot leaf callers consistent; primary win is ensuring the per-element kernels stay inlined into the loops.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.currentCost: ComputeGradient is the per-position hot path that GradientDescent calls every iteration; Attractive/Repulsive are already AggressiveInlining so the loops should fuse, but ComputeGradient itself has no inlining hint and is called once per descent step with a large argument list passed by value.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.proposedChange: Consider [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] on ComputeGradient so the float3-by-value argument marshalling is elided when inlined into GradientDescent, letting Burst keep position and accumulator in registers across the attractor/repulsor loops.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.rationale: Inlining ComputeGradient into GradientDescent removes the by-value passing of position and the many scalar params per step and exposes the whole step to Burst's vectorizer/register allocator as one body. Fewer call-boundary spills on the hottest path.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.risk: Inlining a large method can increase code size / register pressure; Burst may already inline it heuristically, so the attribute is a hint not a guarantee. No semantic change. Validate it does not hurt I-cache on mobile.

src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.summary: rsqrt-based normalize for 'grad/gradLen' and squared-distance tolerance checks (same as 2D).
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.currentCost: Per step: math.length(grad) sqrt + 'grad/gradLen' 3-wide divide; plus math.length(pos-attractors[0]) sqrt each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.proposedChange: float g2 = math.dot(grad,grad); if (g2 < tol2) break; float invLen = math.rsqrt(g2); pos = pos + grad*(invLen*stepSize); target check via math.dot(pos-attractors[0], ...) < tol2; hoist tol2 = tolerance*tolerance and float3 a0 = attractors[0] out of the loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.rationale: Removes one sqrt+divide for direction and two sqrt per iteration for the comparisons by working in squared space; multiplies replace divides. Hoisting a0 avoids repeated pointer deref.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.risk: tolerance>=0 required for squared comparison equivalence (true for a tolerance). rsqrt approximation can shift a near-threshold convergence by one iteration, perturbing stepCount at the boundary; keep math.length if exact step-count reproducibility is contractual.

src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.currentCost: Dead using directive; no System.* symbol is referenced.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.rationale: Keeps the file's dependency surface minimal and explicitly Burst-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Math.PotentialField/Potentia.risk: None; confirmed no System namespace usage in the file.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.summary: Recompute of sqrt: twistLen = length(v) then twistLen*twistLen squares back what sqrt just rooted
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.currentCost: twistLen = math.length(v) costs a sqrt; then line 30 computes twistLen*twistLen + w*w and another math.sqrt for twistMag. The first sqrt's result is squared away, so it is pure waste (one sqrt + one mul) on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.proposedChange: Compute float twistLenSq = math.lengthsq(qv*dot-equivalent vector) once. Use twistLenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon for the early-out comparison, and twistMag = math.sqrt(twistLenSq + twist.value.w * twist.value.w). This removes the first math.length sqrt entirely; twistLen is never needed as a length, only as a squared term.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.rationale: Eliminates one sqrt (high-latency, ~12-20 cycle dependency) and one multiply per call. The squared early-out threshold Epsilon*Epsilon=1e-12f is a compile-time constant, so the comparison cost is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.risk: twistLen < Epsilon becomes twistLenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon, which is exactly equivalent for non-negative lengths (length is always >= 0), so semantics are preserved. Note twistLenSq must be the squared length of the SAME vector (twistPart components), which equals dot*dot since twistAxis is assumed unit; but to be safe compute lengthsq of the twistPart float3 to avoid assuming twistAxis is normalized.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.summary: math.length(projection) for atan2 first arg incurs a sqrt that atan2 magnitude does not strictly need but is required by the formula
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.currentCost: twistLen = math.length(projection) computes a sqrt; projection = dot*twistAxis. If twistAxis is unit, length(projection) == abs(dot), avoiding both the float3 scalar-multiply and the sqrt.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.proposedChange: If twistAxis is documented unit (precondition), replace twistLen = math.length(dot*twistAxis) with twistLen = math.abs(dot). This drops a float3 mul (3 muls) and a sqrt, leaving Two * atan2(abs(dot), w).
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.rationale: length(dot * unitAxis) = |dot| * length(unitAxis) = |dot|. Removes 3 multiplies plus a sqrt per call.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/SwingTwistDe.risk: Only valid if twistAxis is guaranteed unit-length by the API contract (same assumption FromTwistAngle already makes by not normalizing twistAxis). If twistAxis may be non-unit, keep length(projection). State the unit-axis precondition or guard.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionSl.summary: Separate math.sin/math.cos calls plus redundant sin(theta)/sinTheta0 division can be fused
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionSl.currentCost: Lines 30-34 call math.sin(theta) and math.cos(theta) separately (two transcendental evaluations of the same angle), plus math.sin(theta0). s1 = sinTheta/sinTheta0 is computed, then s0 = cos(theta) - d*sinTheta/sinTheta0 recomputes the same sinTheta/sinTheta0 ratio instead of reusing s1.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionSl.proposedChange: Use math.sincos(theta, out float sinTheta, out float cosTheta) to get both from one call. Compute float invSin0 = One / sinTheta0 once; s1 = sinTheta * invSin0; s0 = cosTheta - d * s1. This reuses s1 in the s0 expression (currently d*sinTheta/sinTheta0 redivides).
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionSl.rationale: math.sincos computes sin and cos together cheaper than two independent calls. Replacing two divisions (sinTheta/sinTheta0 appearing twice) with one reciprocal multiply shortens the dependency chain and removes a divide.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionSl.risk: math.sincos and reciprocal-multiply give bit-results within normal float tolerance of the original; this path already excludes near-parallel quaternions (d > 1-Epsilon returns early), so sinTheta0 is bounded away from zero and the reciprocal is safe. No observable behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.summary: Separate sin/cos and a divide that can be a reciprocal-multiply
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.currentCost: len = math.length(axis); n = axis/len does a float3 divide (3 divides via vector div); then math.sin(halfAngle) and math.cos(halfAngle) are two separate transcendental calls.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.proposedChange: Use math.sincos(halfAngle, out float s, out float c) for one combined evaluation. Replace axis/len with axis * (One/len) so the per-component operation is a multiply; or fold the scale: float scale = s / len and return new quaternion(axis.x*scale, axis.y*scale, axis.z*scale, c), removing the explicit normalize vector entirely.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.rationale: sincos is cheaper than independent sin+cos. Folding 1/len and s into one scalar 'scale' replaces a float3 divide plus a float3 multiply-by-s with a single float3 multiply, cutting the vector op count.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.risk: Folding s/len is algebraically identical to (axis/len)*s. The len < Epsilon early-out is preserved. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.summary: Half-angle products c.x*c.y, s.x*s.y, etc. recomputed across the four components
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.currentCost: The four-component construction recomputes shared subproducts: c.x*c.y appears in z and w; s.x*s.y appears in z and w; c.x*s.y, s.x*c.y, c.y*c.z patterns repeat. Each is a separate multiply emitted unless the compiler CSEs aggressively.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.proposedChange: Precompute the 6 distinct pair products once: float cxcy=c.x*c.y, sxsy=s.x*s.y, cxsy=c.x*s.y, sxcy=s.x*c.y (and reuse), then build the four outputs from these and the third-axis c.z/s.z. This guarantees CSE rather than relying on the optimizer.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.rationale: Reduces the multiply count in the quaternion construction by reusing shared products, shortening the dependency chain feeding the constructor.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.risk: Pure algebraic factoring; identical floating-point result if grouped to preserve the original multiply order. Burst likely already CSEs this, so impact is low and mainly a readability/guarantee win.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.summary: length+divide pattern can use rsqrt to replace sqrt-then-divide with one reciprocal-sqrt multiply
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.currentCost: len = math.length(q) does sqrt(dot); then inv = One/len is a divide; then 4 multiplies. That is one sqrt plus one divide on the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.proposedChange: Compute float lenSq = math.lengthsq(q.value); guard lenSq < Epsilon*Epsilon; inv = math.rsqrt(lenSq); multiply the four components by inv. Replaces sqrt+divide with a single rsqrt.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.rationale: rsqrt is a single hardware-friendly op replacing the sqrt then reciprocal-divide sequence, cutting one high-latency divide off the chain.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.risk: math.rsqrt may use a lower-precision estimate on some targets, slightly changing the last ULPs of the normalized result versus 1/sqrt. If exact bit-parity with the current sqrt-then-divide is required by tests, keep One/math.sqrt(lenSq) instead (still saves nothing over current). The Epsilon guard must become Epsilon*Epsilon on lenSq to preserve the same cutoff.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.summary: normalizesafe(cross) computed before the degenerate-input lengthsq(r) check, and four /s divides per branch
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.currentCost: r = normalizesafe(cross(up,f)) normalizes r, then math.lengthsq(r) < Epsilon checks degeneracy AFTER normalization. normalizesafe already returns 0 for degenerate cross, so lengthsq(r) is ~0 only when normalizesafe bailed; computing the full normalize then re-measuring its squared length is wasteful. Each of the four trace branches also performs three or four scalar /s divisions.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.proposedChange: Compute crossUF = math.cross(up, f); test math.lengthsq(crossUF) < Epsilon BEFORE normalizing to early-out on degenerate input, then r = normalize(crossUF). In each branch replace the repeated '/ s' with a precomputed float invS = One / s and multiply, e.g. (m21 - m12) * invS, and s * Half stays.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.rationale: Moves the cheap degeneracy test (lengthsq, no sqrt) ahead of the expensive normalize so degenerate inputs skip normalization entirely; reordering also tests the raw cross magnitude which is the true degeneracy signal rather than the post-normalize length. Replacing 3 divides with 1 reciprocal + 3 multiplies per branch shortens the critical path.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.risk: Behavior is preserved only if the degeneracy threshold maps correctly: current code checks lengthsq of the normalized r against Epsilon; checking lengthsq of the raw cross is the more correct degeneracy test but uses a different magnitude scale, so the Epsilon constant for the raw-cross test should be chosen to match intent (raw cross can be tiny yet valid for near-unit inputs). Safer minimal change: keep the normalize but hoist invS in each branch (pure win, no threshold change). The reorder is the higher-impact but threshold-sensitive part.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.summary: sinHalf = sqrt(1-w*w) then divide by sinHalf; can be reciprocal-multiply, and acos(w) shares w
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.currentCost: sinHalf = math.sqrt(One - w*w); then axis = xyz / sinHalf is a float3 divide (3 divides).
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.proposedChange: Compute float invSin = One / sinHalf once after the Epsilon guard and multiply: axis = new float3(x,y,z) * invSin. Replaces 3 component divides with 1 reciprocal + 3 multiplies.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.rationale: Vector divide-by-scalar becomes reciprocal-then-multiply, removing two of the three divide-latency operations.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.risk: Algebraically identical; the sinHalf < Epsilon guard already ensures the reciprocal is finite. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.summary: Branch for abs() can be branchless math.abs
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.currentCost: After clamp, an if (d<0) d=-d branch computes absolute value with a conditional, creating a predictable-but-present branch.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.proposedChange: Replace the if-block with d = math.abs(d) (or fold: d = math.abs(math.dot(...)) then clamp to [0,1]). Branchless, one instruction.
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.rationale: math.abs is a single bitwise/instruction op with no branch, removing a conditional from the leaf method that may be called in tight loops (e.g. per-bone angle checks).
src/IAFahim.Math.Quaternion/QuaternionOp.risk: math.abs(d) is identical to the if-negate for all finite d. Ordering note: abs-then-clamp to [0,1] is equivalent to clamp[-1,1]-then-abs since abs maps [-1,1] to [0,1]. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.summary: Cone recomputes new float2(dimensions.x,-dimensions.y) twice and computes ca/cb/tip which are dead, plus recomputes the clamp expression inline.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.currentCost: Two constructions of new float2(dimensions.x,-dimensions.y) (lines 69-70) whose results (ca, cb) are never used in the return. 'tip' (line 68) is computed but only tip.x/tip.y feed 'd' = max(tip.x,tip.y) = max(q.x-dimensions.x, q.y-dimensions.y). The dead float2 builds plus unused locals waste registers/instructions even after DCE may not fully remove the constructor side-effect-free float2.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.proposedChange: Delete the dead locals: remove 'float2 tip = q - dimensions;' if you instead write 'float d = math.max(q.x - dimensions.x, q.y - dimensions.y);' (keep tip if preferred but drop ca/cb entirely). Remove lines 69-70 ('ca','cb') completely. Precompute 'float2 dd = dimensions;' is unnecessary; just keep the single 'side' expression.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.rationale: Removes two float2 vector constructions and two unused float loads per call; shorter dependency chain and fewer SSA values for Burst to schedule. Pure dead-code removal — no numeric change.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.risk: None for ca/cb (provably unused). 'tip' removal must keep d = max(q.x-dimensions.x, q.y-dimensions.y) identical to math.max(tip.x,tip.y), which it is by definition of tip = q - dimensions.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.summary: Ellipsoid divides p by radii twice (scaled = p/radii, then k1V = scaled/radii) creating a long dependency chain through two vector reciprocals.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.currentCost: Two vector divides: scaled = p/radii (3 div), k1V = scaled/radii (3 div), then two math.length (2 sqrt). The second divide depends on the first, lengthening the critical path.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.proposedChange: Precompute 'float3 inv = math.rcp(radii);' once, then 'float3 scaled = p * inv;' and 'float3 k1V = scaled * inv;'. This replaces 6 divides with 3 (rcp) + 6 muls; muls are far cheaper and the two scaled products both depend only on inv, shortening the chain. Burst vectorizes rcp+mul well.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.rationale: div is ~4-5x the latency/throughput of mul on most targets; computing reciprocal once and multiplying twice cuts divide count from 6 to 3 and breaks the serial div->div chain into rcp then two independent-ish muls.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.risk: math.rcp is an approximation-free 1.0f/x in Unity.Mathematics for scalar/float3 (full-precision divide), so result is bit-identical to p/radii / scaled/radii within float rounding of the same operations. If exact bit-reproducibility with the original division order is contractually required, note rcp(x)*y may round differently than x/y; for SDF distance fields this tolerance is acceptable but flag it.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.summary: Cylinder builds new float2(p.x,p.z) and an inner length, then abs and subtract via temporaries; layout is fine but the construction of two float2 literals can be fused.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.currentCost: new float2(radius, halfHeight) is constructed every call though it is purely a function of the two scalar args; same for the inner new float2(p.x,p.z).
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.proposedChange: This is minor; the main real win is ensuring the intermediate 'd' stays in vector regs. No semantic change available beyond what Burst already does. Consider leaving as-is — already near optimal.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.rationale: Burst already SROAs float2 literals into scalars; constant-factor only. Listed for completeness, low confidence of measurable gain.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfPrimitive.cs.risk: None; effectively a no-op cleanup. Could be skipped entirely.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfBoolean.cs.summary: The three Smooth* functions divide by k each call; if k is constant across many evaluations the reciprocal cannot be hoisted at this granularity, but the (d2-d1)/k pattern can use rcp once per call.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfBoolean.cs.currentCost: Each Smooth* does (d2 - d1) / k (one divide) plus a math.lerp and k*h*(1-h). The divide is the highest-latency op in the body.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfBoolean.cs.proposedChange: Add an overload (or expose) that takes 'float invK' precomputed by the caller when k is loop-invariant (common: same blend factor for a whole scene). Inside the existing functions, leaving as-is is fine for single calls, but document/offer Run-style variants taking invK to let callers hoist the 1/k out of hot march loops. Keeps current signature for ergonomics.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfBoolean.cs.rationale: In ray-march loops the same k is reused thousands of times; hoisting 1/k to an invK passed in removes one divide per SDF evaluation per blend node. Pure caller-side hoist — no numeric change when invK == 1/k.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfBoolean.cs.risk: Adding an overload changes API surface only (additive). Numeric: (d2-d1)*invK rounds identically enough; if strict bit-match to /k is required, note the rounding caveat.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.summary: SdfFunction is a managed delegate; invoking it (sdf(p)) on the hot march/normal/AO loops defeats Burst (managed call, no inlining, no vectorization) and is not blittable.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.currentCost: Every March step, every EstimateNormal (4 calls), and every AmbientOcclusion step invokes a managed delegate. Managed delegate dispatch in Burst is unsupported or extremely slow (virtual-style indirect call, GC type, blocks inlining of the SDF body into the loop).
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.proposedChange: Replace 'public delegate float SdfFunction(float3 p);' usage with Burst-friendly 'FunctionPointer<SdfFunction>' (Unity.Burst) and invoke via .Invoke, or better, make March/EstimateNormal/AmbientOcclusion generic over an unmanaged 'ISdf' struct constraint 'where T : unmanaged, ISdf' and call sdf.Evaluate(p) so Burst can inline the concrete SDF into the loop. Mark the delegate [BurstCompile] if using FunctionPointer.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.rationale: Generic-struct dispatch lets Burst specialize and inline the distance function directly into the march loop, eliminating per-step indirect calls and enabling vectorization/constant folding; FunctionPointer at minimum makes it Burst-callable. This is the single biggest perf lever in the module.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.risk: API change. Generic-struct approach requires an ISdf interface used only as a generic constraint (allowed for Burst, resolved statically — not a managed virtual call). House rule forbids interfaces in src; if strictly enforced, use FunctionPointer<SdfFunction> instead, which keeps a delegate type for the signature but is Burst-invocable. Confirm which path the codebase permits.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.summary: EstimateNormal uses 4 SDF evaluations (center d + 3 forward differences). A tetrahedral 4-tap scheme also uses 4 but the forward-difference here is fine; however math.normalize re-derives length with a sqrt that could short-circuit degenerate gradients.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.currentCost: 4 SDF calls (1 center + 3). math.normalize does dot+rsqrt; if grad is near-zero (point exactly on a flat region) normalize produces NaN/inf silently.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.proposedChange: Keep 4 taps (changing to tetrahedral alters which samples are taken => different numeric normal, not semantics-preserving). Real win: the three offset float3 literals new float3(NormalEpsilon,0,0) etc. are compile-time constants — ensure they are 'static readonly'/const-folded; they already are literals so Burst folds them. Optionally route the final normalize through SafeNormalize(grad) to remove the NaN edge case (behavior change for degenerate input only).
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.rationale: No free tap reduction without changing output. The only concrete, low-risk note is the optional SafeNormalize swap to harden degenerate gradients; otherwise this function is already minimal.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.risk: Switching math.normalize -> SafeNormalize changes output for zero-gradient inputs (returns (0,1,0) instead of NaN) — a semantics change at the edge; only adopt if that hardening is desired. Pure-tap changes (tetrahedral) are rejected as they change results.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.summary: AmbientOcclusion computes dist = (float)i * stepSize each iteration via int->float convert + multiply; can be strength-reduced to an additive accumulator.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.currentCost: Per iteration: int-to-float conversion of i, then multiply by stepSize. The convert + mul is a small dependency each loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.proposedChange: Replace the loop counter math: keep 'float dist = stepSize;' before the loop and do 'dist += stepSize;' at the end of each iteration (starting i=1 => first dist=stepSize). Removes the (float)i cast and the multiply, replacing with one add.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.rationale: Strength-reduces a per-iteration int->float convert + fmul into a single fadd, shortening the loop body. For small step counts the win is tiny but real and free.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfRayMarch.cs.risk: Floating-point accumulation order changes: i*stepSize vs repeated addition can differ in the last ULP for large step counts. For AO (a clamped 0..1 aesthetic term, few steps) this is imperceptible, but it is a bit-level semantics change — flag if exact reproduction required.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.summary: Scale does p / scale (3 divides); if the same scale is reused across a march loop the reciprocal could be hoisted by the caller.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.currentCost: 3 vector divides per call. In a ray-march, the same scale vector is typically constant for an object, so dividing every evaluation is redundant work.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.proposedChange: Offer a companion that takes a precomputed inverse: 'public static float3 Scale(float3 p, float3 invScale) => p * invScale;' or document that callers hoist math.rcp(scale). Keep existing div-based overload for ergonomics.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.rationale: Multiply-by-reciprocal hoisted out of the hot loop removes 3 divides per SDF evaluation. Additive API; the existing semantics are unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.risk: Additive overload only; p*rcp(scale) vs p/scale may differ by one ULP. Note rounding caveat if bit-exactness required.

src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.summary: Repeat computes p / cellSize then multiplies cellSize back; uses a divide that becomes mul-by-reciprocal if invCellSize is supplied.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.currentCost: 3 divides (p/cellSize) plus round plus mul. The divide is the costly part and is loop-invariant in cellSize across a tiled domain.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.proposedChange: Add overload taking invCellSize: 'p - cellSize * math.round(p * invCellSize)'. Caller hoists math.rcp(cellSize) once. Keep current overload.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.rationale: Removes 3 divides per evaluation in tiled/instanced SDF scenes where cellSize is constant; replaced by precomputed rcp and muls.
src/IAFahim.Math.Sdf/SdfTransform.cs.risk: Additive overload; rounding of round(p*invCellSize) vs round(p/cellSize) could land on a different integer exactly at cell boundaries (where p/cellSize is an exact .5). This is a genuine edge-case semantics risk at tile seams — guard by keeping the divide-based version as default and only using the rcp variant where seam exactness is not critical.

src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.summary: Fuse basis evaluation directly into the accumulation loop to eliminate the stackalloc scratch buffer round-trip and the redundant constant store.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.currentCost: Per sample: EvaluateL2 writes 9 floats to a stackalloc buffer, then an inner j-loop reads them back and does 9 FMAs. That's an extra 9 stores + 9 loads per sample plus a store/load dependency chain that blocks the FMA from issuing until the basis store retires. For sampleCount samples this is 9*sampleCount redundant memory ops.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.proposedChange: Drop 'float* basis = stackalloc float[9]'. Inside the per-sample loop, compute v = values[i], x/y/z from directions[i], then directly accumulate: outCoeffs[0] += v*0.28209479f; outCoeffs[1] += v*(-0.48860251f*y); ... outCoeffs[8] += v*0.54627421f*(x*x - y*y). This inlines BasisLxMy without the scratch buffer.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.rationale: Removes 9 stores + 9 loads per sample and the store-to-load forwarding stall, letting the FMA chain issue from registers. Same float arithmetic in the same order preserves bit-exact results.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.risk: Must preserve evaluation order of the multiply (value*basis) and the exact float constants to keep bit-identical output. The constant BasisL0M0 term 0.28209479f*v replaces the buffered constant; identical result. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.summary: Inline basis evaluation into the dot product to remove the stackalloc buffer and store/load round-trip on this AggressiveInlining hot leaf.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.currentCost: Writes 9 basis floats to stackalloc, then loops reading them back for 9 FMAs. This is a hot, inlined evaluation path (typical per-pixel/per-probe shading); the scratch buffer adds 9 stores + 9 loads and a store-to-load dependency before the dot product can begin.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.proposedChange: Compute x/y/z once and form the result directly: float result = coeffs[0]*0.28209479f + coeffs[1]*(-0.48860251f*y) + coeffs[2]*(0.48860251f*z) + coeffs[3]*(-0.48860251f*x) + coeffs[4]*(1.09254843f*x*y) + coeffs[5]*(-1.09254843f*y*z) + coeffs[6]*(0.31539157f*(3.0f*z*z-1.0f)) + coeffs[7]*(-1.09254843f*x*z) + coeffs[8]*(0.54627421f*(x*x-y*y)); No stackalloc needed.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.rationale: Eliminates the scratch buffer entirely so the whole evaluation stays in registers, shortens the dependency chain, and lets Burst fold/vectorize the FMA tree. With AggressiveInlining at call sites this removes a stack frame's scratch traffic per call.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.risk: Floating point is not associative; to stay bit-exact keep the same left-to-right accumulation order as the current i-loop (result += coeffs[i]*basis[i] for i=0..8). Writing it as a single + expression must respect that ordering, or accept the tiny ULP difference. State as left-associative sum to be safe.

src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.summary: Replace magic literals/loop bounds with named constants for the L2 coefficient count and the 4*Pi normalization.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.currentCost: The literal 9 appears in four loops and 4.0f*Pi is recomputed inline; the coefficient count is implicit and the normalization constant is unnamed.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.proposedChange: Add private const int CoeffCountL2 = 9; and private const float FourPi = 12.5663706f; (or 4.0f*Pi folded by the compiler). Use CoeffCountL2 in all loop bounds and weight = FourPi / (float)sampleCount.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.rationale: Improves discoverability and prevents drift if higher SH bands are added later; the compiler already folds 4.0f*Pi so no perf change, this is purely clarity within house style (named constants).
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.risk: None — pure refactor, identical codegen. 4.0f*Pi already constant-folds so the float value is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.summary: The per-band Basis* helpers accept unused x/y/z parameters (e.g. BasisL1M1 uses only y, BasisL2M0 uses only z), passed by value every call.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.currentCost: Each call passes 3 floats even when 1-2 are unused. With AggressiveInlining the dead args are optimized away at the EvaluateL2 call site, so cost is effectively zero there; but the uniform signature can mislead and prevents using these as function pointers efficiently.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.proposedChange: Keep the uniform (x,y,z) signature ONLY if function-pointer dispatch over a table is intended; otherwise these helpers are already fully inlined by EvaluateL2 and the unused params are free. No change needed unless a fn-pointer table is desired — in which case the uniform signature is correct and this is optimal.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.rationale: Documents that the apparent redundancy is harmless under inlining; flags it as already-optimal rather than inventing a rewrite. Burst/JIT drops unused inlined args.
src/IAFahim.Math.SphericalHarmonics/SHEv.risk: None. Changing signatures would break the uniform table-dispatch use case; leaving as-is is correct. Reported for completeness, not as an action item.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.summary: Factor the Hermite basis polynomials by Horner form on the scalar coefficients to cut multiplies before the float3 SIMD combine.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.currentCost: Computes tt and ttt (2 mul), then each of h00,h10,h01,h11 with explicit Two*ttt, Three*tt etc. ~10 scalar muls + adds, plus 4 float3 scalar-vector muls and 3 float3 adds.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.proposedChange: Note h00+h01 and h10/h11 share structure. h00 = ((Two*t - Three)*tt + One) via Horner: h00 = One + tt*(Two*t - Three). h01 = -h00 + One? Actually h01 = -Two*ttt+Three*tt = -(h00 - One) = One - h00. So compute h00 once and set h01 = One - h00, removing the second cubic. Similarly h11 = ttt - tt = tt*(t - One); h10 = h11 + (t - tt) so h10 = ttt - Two*tt + t = h11 - tt + t. Reuse subexpressions to remove ~3-4 scalar muls.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.rationale: h01 = 1 - h00 is an exact algebraic identity (2t^3-3t^2+1 + (-2t^3+3t^2) = 1), so one cubic evaluation and a subtract replaces a full second polynomial. Fewer scalar ops shorten the dependency chain feeding the float3 FMA combine; Burst still vectorizes the final accumulate.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.risk: Pure float reassociation: 1 - h00 vs -Two*ttt+Three*tt are not bit-identical under IEEE rounding, so output can differ in the last ULP. Acceptable for a spline evaluator but technically not bit-exact; reject if bit-exact reproducibility is required.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant float-to-step setup and replace per-iteration (float)i * step with an additive accumulator; inline-expand Evaluate's invariant basis-independent work.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.currentCost: Per iteration: int->float cast of i, one mul for t, a full Evaluate call (10+ scalar muls, 4 vector muls, 3 vector adds), a math.distance (sub, dot, sqrt). The (float)i*step recompute and int conversion are redundant each loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.proposedChange: Replace `float t = (float)i * step;` with an accumulator `t += step;` initialized to step before the loop, removing the int->float conversion and using one add instead of cast+mul per iteration. Keep last t snapped to 1.0f if exactness at endpoint matters.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.rationale: Removes one int-to-float conversion and converts a multiply into an add on the loop's critical scalar path each iteration (sampleCount iterations). Lower-latency dependency chain for the t value feeding Evaluate.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.risk: Accumulating t += step drifts from i*step by accumulated rounding (~sampleCount ULPs), shifting sample positions slightly and thus the summed arc length. For a numerical-integration estimate this is within tolerance, but it is not bit-identical to the multiply form. Guard: if endpoint t must be exactly 1.0, set t = One on the final iteration.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.summary: Add a guard or document that sampleCount must be >= 1; division by sampleCount is unchecked.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.currentCost: step = One / (float)sampleCount produces +Inf/NaN for sampleCount==0 and a negative/garbage walk for negative input, with no Try* variant or documented precondition.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.proposedChange: Either rename to a Run-style unchecked contract documenting sampleCount>=1, or add a TryIntegrateArcLength that returns false for sampleCount<=0, consistent with the library's Run/Try* convention.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.rationale: Matches the stated Run/Try* API convention and makes the precondition discoverable without changing the hot-path cost of the existing method.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/CubicHermite.cs.risk: Pure API/documentation change; no behavior change for valid inputs (sampleCount>=1).

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.summary: Apply Horner factoring to the cubic B-spline basis to shorten the scalar dependency chain before the SIMD combine.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.currentCost: ttt computed (2 mul), then b0,b1,b2 each rebuild powers with explicit Three*tt, Six*tt etc. (~9 scalar muls). The OneSixth scale is applied once at the end (good).
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.proposedChange: Evaluate b0..b3 in Horner form, e.g. b0 = One + t*(-Three + t*(Three - t)), b1 = Four + ttt*Three - tt*Six, b2 = One + t*(Three + t*(Three - ... )). Reuses t-products and reduces independent multiplies feeding the accumulate.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.rationale: Horner form replaces repeated power reconstruction with fused multiply-adds, trimming a few scalar muls and shortening latency before the four scalar*float3 FMAs that Burst vectorizes.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.risk: Reassociation of float arithmetic changes last-ULP rounding versus the current expanded form; not bit-exact. Acceptable for spline sampling but reject if bit-reproducibility across the expanded form is contractually required.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.summary: Replace per-iteration (float)i*step in the LUT build and the resample loop with additive accumulators, and snap endpoint t to exact 1.0.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.currentCost: LUT loop and resample loop each do an int->float cast plus a multiply per iteration to form t / targetDist. The endpoint position is computed separately (good) but the interior t and targetDist recompute the cast+mul every step.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.proposedChange: In the LUT loop use `t += step` (init t=step). In the resample loop use `targetDist += targetStep` (init = targetStep). Removes int->float conversion and converts a mul into an add per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.rationale: Drops one conversion and turns a multiply into an add on each loop's scalar critical path; over lutSamples + count iterations this is a real constant-factor saving feeding the dependent Evaluate/distance/FindT chain.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.risk: Accumulator drifts from i*step by accumulated float rounding, slightly perturbing LUT distances and resampled t values; for an arc-length resampler this is within tolerance but not bit-identical. The exact endpoints (indices 0 and count-1) already use literal 0.0/1.0 so they are unaffected.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.summary: Hoist redundant endpoint Evaluate/EvaluateTangent: outPositions[0] and its tangent are computed twice.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.currentCost: Evaluate(...,0.0f) is called at line 62 (prev) and again at line 74 (outPositions[0]); EvaluateTangent(...,0.0f) once. The line-62 result equals the line-74 result, so one full B-spline Evaluate (4 scalar*float3 FMAs + basis polynomial) is recomputed.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.proposedChange: Reuse `prev` for outPositions[0]: set `outPositions[0] = prev;` instead of recomputing Evaluate(...,0.0f) at line 74. prev already holds Evaluate(p0,p1,p2,p3,0.0f).
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.rationale: Eliminates one full Evaluate call (basis poly + four float3 FMAs) per UniformSample invocation by reusing an already-computed identical value. Bit-exact since it is the same expression with the same inputs.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.risk: None: prev is assigned Evaluate(p0,p1,p2,p3,0.0f) at line 62 and not mutated before line 74, so outPositions[0]=prev is bit-identical to the recompute.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.summary: stackalloc of lutSamples+1 floats is unbounded by caller-supplied lutSamples and risks stack overflow on mobile; document/bound it.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.currentCost: float* lut = stackalloc float[lutSamples + 1] allocates 4*(lutSamples+1) bytes on the stack with no upper bound. A large lutSamples (e.g. 100k) overflows the thread stack, especially on mobile where Burst job stacks are small.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.proposedChange: Document a hard precondition/named-constant cap (e.g. MaxLutSamples) on lutSamples, or accept the LUT as a caller-provided float* buffer so allocation strategy is the caller's choice (consistent with outPositions/outTangents already being caller pointers).
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.rationale: Moving the buffer out to the caller removes an unbounded per-call stack allocation and lets the caller reuse a pooled buffer, reducing stack pressure and matching the existing pointer-out API style.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.risk: API signature change (add a float* lut parameter) breaks callers; if only documenting a cap, no signature change but the precondition must be enforced by the caller. No numerical behavior change either way.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.summary: The binary search recomputes lut[low]/lut[high] after the loop and the comparison reloads lut[mid]; loads are fine but the segmentLength guard branch can be made branchless.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.currentCost: factor = segmentLength > 1e-6f ? (targetDist-d0)/segmentLength : 0.0f uses a branch per FindT call (count-2 calls). The division is already guarded, which is correct.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.proposedChange: Keep the divide-by-zero guard but compute it branchlessly with math.select on the condition, or rcp with select. Burst can compile the ternary to a select already, so verify codegen; if it does, no change needed. Primary real win here is ensuring `lut` reads hit L1 (LUT is contiguous, already good).
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.rationale: Removing a data-dependent branch in a per-sample inner function reduces mispredict risk; math.select maps to a blend on SIMD/scalar select on the target. Low impact because lutSamples is typically small so the search is short.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.risk: math.select evaluates both operands, so (targetDist-d0)/segmentLength would execute even when segmentLength<=1e-6f, producing Inf/NaN that select then discards. This is safe only if the NaN is never used (it is selected away), but generating NaN can raise FP exceptions if traps are enabled. Keep the guarded divide unless Burst already emits a branchless select for the ternary.

src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.summary: Constant-fold the compile-time products (Two*Three, Three*Three) into named float constants instead of leaving them as source multiplies.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.currentCost: db0 uses `Two * Three * t`, db2 uses `-Three * Three * tt` and `Two * Three * t`. These are constant*constant that the compiler should fold, but they read as runtime multiplies and rely on the JIT/Burst folding them.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.proposedChange: Introduce named constants (e.g. Six already exists for Two*Three; add Negative... or reuse Nine for Three*Three) and write db0 = -Three*tt + Six*t - Three; db2 = -Nine*tt + Six*t + Three. Nine and Six already exist as constants in this class.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.rationale: Uses the already-defined Six and Nine constants directly, guaranteeing the fold and improving readability/consistency without relying on the compiler to collapse Two*Three and Three*Three.
src/IAFahim.Math.Spline/UniformBSpline.c.risk: None: Two*Three==Six and Three*Three==Nine exactly in float; bit-identical, purely a source-clarity and fold-guarantee change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.summary: Eliminate the ta/tb scratch buffers and the redundant second copy in InitializeNttArrays by reducing-mod directly into fa/fb.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.currentCost: ConvolveWithMod allocates ta[n]+tb[m] on the stack, fills them with a[i]%mod / b[i]%mod, then NttConvolutionSimple allocates fa[size]+fb[size] and InitializeNttArrays copies ta->fa, tb->fb again. That is two full passes over the data plus an extra n+m longs of stack per modulus, times 3 moduli.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.proposedChange: Drop ta/tb entirely. Pass the raw a,b,mod into NttConvolutionSimple and let InitializeNttArrays write fa[i]=a[i]%mod (i<n), 0 otherwise, and fb[i]=b[i]%mod (i<m), 0 otherwise. This fuses the modular reduction and the zero-padded copy into a single pass and removes the ta/tb stack allocation.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.rationale: Removes one full read/write pass over n+m elements and (n+m) longs of stackalloc per call. Fewer memory ops and a smaller working set improve cache behavior; the % is already paid once either way, just folded into the existing copy loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.risk: Semantics-preserving: a[i]%mod for the small NTT moduli (all < 2^31) on long inputs yields identical residues whether reduced in ta first or in fa directly. No signed-mod edge issue because results feed only into NTT arithmetic that already normalizes. Burst-friendly (still blittable pointers).

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.summary: Index the precomputed twiddle table instead of carrying the wn = wn*w%mod multiply chain inside the butterfly loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.currentCost: The inner loop maintains wn with 'wn = wn * w % mod' each iteration: a serial 64-bit multiply + modulo on the critical path per butterfly, plus 'long w = roots[n/len]' bootstrapping. This is a true dependency chain that serializes the inner loop and blocks vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.proposedChange: The full roots[] table of 'size' primitive-root powers is already built in NttConvolutionSimple. Inside PerformNtt use the stride form: for stage with 'half', the twiddle for column j is roots[j * (n/len)] (i.e. roots[j * step] where step = n/len). Compute step once per stage and index roots[j*step] (or carry an additive index 'idx += step') instead of multiplying/modding wn. This replaces a mul+mod dependency with a load + add.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.rationale: Removes a 64-bit multiply and 64-bit modulo from the inner-loop dependency chain, replacing them with a precomputed table load and an integer add. Shorter recurrence latency and friendlier to Burst/SIMD; the roots table is already resident.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.risk: roots[] must be sized >= n (it is built with 'size' entries == n here). Must ensure the precomputed table is passed/visible to every stage (it is). Numerically identical: roots[j*step] equals the wn produced by repeated multiplication. Only valid because the single shared roots table spans the whole transform length.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.summary: Reuse/reverse the forward roots table for the inverse transform instead of recomputing invRoot powers via a fresh stackalloc + power chain.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.currentCost: PerformInverseNtt calls FastPow(root, mod-2, mod) (a full ~30-iteration modpow), then allocates invRoots[n] and rebuilds the entire inverse twiddle table with n multiply+mod operations. This duplicates the roots table work already done in the forward path.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.proposedChange: The inverse roots are just the forward roots in reverse order: invRoots[0]=roots[0]=1 and invRoots[i]=roots[n-i] for i>0 (since root^(n-i) == (root^-1)^i mod p for an n-th primitive root). Pass the existing forward roots[] into PerformInverseNtt and index roots[(n-i)&(n-1)] instead of building invRoots and computing invRoot. This removes the FastPow(root,mod-2) call and the n-element invRoots fill.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.rationale: Eliminates one modular exponentiation (~30 mul+mod) and an entire n-length table-build pass plus n longs of stackalloc, replacing them with O(1) index arithmetic against an already-resident table. n is a power of two so (n-i) wraps with & (n-1).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.risk: Requires roots[] be the size-length table from NttConvolutionSimple (it is, length == n). The identity root^(n-i) = invRoot^i holds because root is a primitive n-th root of unity mod p. invN scaling at the end is unchanged. Index 0 must map to roots[0]=1 (handle i==0 explicitly or rely on (n-0)&(n-1)==0).

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant 'm12 % MOD3' out of the per-element CRT loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.currentCost: Inside the for-loop, 'x3 = (r3[i] - x1 - (m12 % MOD3) * (x2 % MOD3)) * invM12Mod3 % MOD3' recomputes 'm12 % MOD3' every iteration. m12 and MOD3 are both compile-time-ish constants for the loop, so this is a redundant 64-bit modulo per element.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.proposedChange: Compute 'long m12ModM3 = m12 % MOD3;' once before the loop (next to the existing m12/invM1Mod2/invM12Mod3 setup) and use m12ModM3 inside the loop. Optionally also keep '(x2 % MOD3)' but x2 is already in [0,MOD2) so x2%MOD3 is still needed.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.rationale: Removes one 64-bit modulo from every iteration of the CRT combine loop (len iterations). The value is loop-invariant; JIT/Burst may not hoist a div/mod across a memory-dependent expression reliably, so do it manually.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.risk: None. Pure invariant hoist; identical results. m12=MOD1*MOD2 fits in long (167772161*469762049 ~ 7.9e16 < 9.2e18), so no overflow in the existing computation either.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.summary: Size the CRT scratch buffers r1/r2/r3 to n+m-1 instead of n+m.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.currentCost: r1,r2,r3 are stackalloc'd as long[n+m] but only indices [0, n+m-1) are ever written (by NttConvolutionSimple's final copy) and read (by CombineCrt with len=n+m-1). One extra long per buffer = 3 wasted longs of stack.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.proposedChange: Allocate 'stackalloc long[n + m - 1]' for r1, r2, r3 (guard n+m-1 >= 1, which holds for any valid n>=1,m>=1). Keeps stack footprint exactly at the used size.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.rationale: Minor stack working-set reduction; tightens the footprint for deep/recursive callers on mobile. Constant-factor only.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.risk: Must hold n>=1 and m>=1 (valid convolution inputs) so n+m-1>=1; for n==m==0 the size would be -1. The unchecked Run already assumes valid input. NttConvolutionSimple writes exactly n+m-1 entries, so no out-of-bounds.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.summary: Dead code: ExtGcd is never called; ModInverse uses its own iterative loop. Remove it.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.currentCost: ExtGcd is a private recursive method with out params that nothing in the file references (ModInverse implements extended Euclid inline). It is unused code that can confuse maintainers and, if ever Burst-compiled, recursion is undesirable.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.proposedChange: Delete the ExtGcd method entirely. If extended-gcd reuse is desired, refactor ModInverse to call a single iterative (non-recursive) gcd helper instead, but the minimal change is removal.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.rationale: Removes dead, recursive code from a Burst module (recursion is a Burst red flag and bloats IL). No behavioral change since it is never invoked.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.risk: None as long as it truly has no callers in the module (confirmed: only ModInverse's inline loop is used). Purely additive-removal.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to the hot leaf helpers (FastPow, ModInverse) and mark the small per-stage twiddle setup for inlining.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.currentCost: FastPow and ModInverse are small leaf methods called from setup paths (root computation, invN, invRoot, CRT inverses). Without an inlining hint the JIT/Burst may keep call overhead, and a call boundary can block constant propagation of 'mod'.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.proposedChange: Annotate FastPow and ModInverse with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]. The using for System.Runtime.CompilerServices is already present.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.rationale: Enables Burst to propagate the constant mod and fuse the modpow into callers, shrinking call overhead on the setup path. Low impact since these are O(log mod) and not in the innermost butterfly, but free.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.AnyMod/AnyMod.risk: None functionally. Inlining a loop-containing method may not always be honored by the compiler, but the hint is harmless and cannot change semantics.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.summary: Twiddle factor recurrence accumulates floating-point error and creates a long serial dependency chain; for accuracy-tolerant use it is fine, but the per-iteration complex multiply for w is 4 mults + 2 adds purely to advance the angle.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.currentCost: Per butterfly pair: the w-update (lines 30-31) costs 4 mul + 2 add on the critical path and serializes the inner loop (each j depends on prior w). This dependency chain prevents the inner loop from being vectorized/pipelined by Burst.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.proposedChange: Precompute a twiddle table per FFT size once (cos/sin for indices 0..n/2-1) into a stackalloc/caller-provided buffer, then index it: wRe = tw[k], wIm = tw[k+stride]. This removes the serial w-recurrence, letting Burst SIMD the butterfly body and breaking the dependency chain. Alternatively expose a Run overload taking a precomputed twiddle pointer so repeated same-size transforms (the convolution case) reuse it.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.rationale: Replacing a 6-op serial recurrence with a table load removes the loop-carried dependency, enabling vectorization and pipelining; for repeated transforms of identical n (FftConvolution calls Forward 3x at the same size) the trig table is computed once instead of recomputed each call.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.risk: Table approach changes rounding slightly vs the recurrence (different but generally MORE accurate); observable double values may differ in low bits. If bit-exact parity with current output is required this is not semantics-preserving. Needs extra RAM (n/2 complex doubles) — acceptable via stackalloc for typical sizes but large n on mobile stack is a concern; prefer caller-provided buffer.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.summary: Inverse() negates imaginary parts before and after a full Forward, but the convolution discards the imaginary result entirely (line 72 reads only faRe), so the post-Inverse re-negation of im and its multiply are wasted work.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.currentCost: FftTransform.Inverse runs two full O(size) passes over im: pre-negate (line 37) and post-scale+negate (line 40, im[i] = -im[i]*invN). In Run the final imaginary array is never read, so the line-40 imaginary multiply/negate (size mul + size negate + size store) is pure waste, plus the line-37 pre-negate touches im.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.proposedChange: In Run, inline the inverse instead of calling Inverse: negate im once, call Forward, then scale only re by invN (skip all im work on the way out). I.e. for(i<size) faRe[i]*=invN. Saves one O(size) pass writing im plus the per-element imaginary mul/negate.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.rationale: Eliminates one full sweep over the imaginary buffer and ~size multiplies/negations/stores that produce a value the caller never consumes. Pure dead-store elimination the compiler cannot do across the pointer-aliased call boundary.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.risk: None for correctness — the discarded im values are provably unused (only faRe[0..n+m-2] is read). Burst/JIT cannot prove this itself because Inverse writes through pointers that could alias; doing it manually in Run is safe by construction.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.summary: Four stackalloc buffers of `size` doubles (faIm, fbRe, fbIm in addition to faRe) total 4*size*8 bytes on the stack; size is rounded up to the next power of two, so worst case nearly doubles the needed memory and risks stack overflow for large inputs on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.currentCost: 4 * size * 8 bytes stackalloc where size can be ~2*(n+m-1). For n+m-1 around 64k this is ~4MB on the stack — exceeds typical mobile thread stack and is undefined-behavior/crash territory; even moderate sizes pressure L1/L2.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.proposedChange: Provide a Run overload that takes a caller-supplied scratch pointer (4*size doubles) so the allocation strategy is the caller's choice (pooled/native buffer), and/or document a max safe size. At minimum keep the imaginary input buffers but note that faIm/fbIm start all-zero and could be folded with a real-input FFT path (real FFT halves storage and work).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.rationale: Moving large transient allocations off the stack avoids stack-overflow risk and lets callers reuse a single native buffer across calls (no repeated stackalloc cost, better cache reuse). A real-input FFT specialization would cut transform work and storage roughly in half since inputs are real.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.risk: API change (new overload) — keep the existing one for ergonomics. Real-FFT specialization is a larger algorithmic change and must reproduce identical outputs; only worth it if convolution is hot. No correctness risk in simply exposing a scratch-buffer overload.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.summary: `len / 2` is recomputed and passed each outer iteration and inside the inner loop `i + j + half` recomputes the base each j; minor strength-reduction and invariant hoisting available, and Cos/Sin are recomputed per len though the set of angles is fixed for a given n.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.currentCost: len/2 (a shift, cheap) recomputed per outer iter; Math.Cos/Math.Sin called log2(n) times per Forward — for FftConvolution's 3 same-size transforms that is 3*log2(n) trig evaluations of an identical angle set.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `half = len >> 1` (use shift, semantically identical for positive len). For the convolution path, precompute the per-stage (wlenRe,wlenIm) pairs once into a small stackalloc[2*log2(size)] and reuse across the 3 Forward calls, avoiding redundant Cos/Sin. In the inner butterfly, advance pointers (re+idx) instead of recomputing idx1/idx2 = i+j(+half) each iteration to shorten address arithmetic.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.rationale: Removes redundant transcendental calls (Cos/Sin are tens of cycles each) across repeated transforms, and converts repeated index additions into pointer increments that Burst lowers to cheaper addressing.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.risk: len is always a positive power of two so len>>1 == len/2 exactly — no signed-division pitfall. Caching wlen across Forward calls requires threading a buffer through the API (only beneficial in the convolution path); standalone Forward already only computes log2(n) trig values so the win there is marginal.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.summary: Small hot leaf helpers (Swap, and arguably PerformButterflyStep) lack [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]; relying on JIT/Burst inlining heuristics for a ref-double swap in the bit-reversal hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.currentCost: Swap is called 2x per bit-reversal pair inside the i<n loop; without forced inlining there is a (potential) call overhead and the using-directive for MethodImpl is already imported but unused on leaf methods.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to Swap (and consider it on PerformButterflyStep). Burst typically inlines these anyway, but the attribute makes intent explicit and guarantees inlining under managed-IL fallback.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.rationale: Guarantees elimination of call/ref-arg overhead in the bit-reverse loop and removes reliance on heuristics, with zero behavioral change.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Fft/Fft.cs.risk: None — inlining a trivial swap is always safe; AggressiveInlining on the larger PerformButterflyStep could increase code size, so apply only to Swap with confidence.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.summary: Compute inverse roots as the reverse permutation of forward roots instead of n separate modular exponentiations.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.currentCost: Line 12 loops i=0..n-1 calling FastPow(roots[i], mod-2, mod), each O(log mod) modmuls => O(n log mod) total just to build invRoots.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.proposedChange: invRoots[i] = roots[(n - i) & (n - 1)] for i in 0..n-1 (i.e. invRoots[0]=roots[0]=1, invRoots[i]=roots[n-i] for i>=1). This is O(n) with no FastPow calls. The forward generator gPow = g^((mod-1)/n) has order n, so its inverse power is g^((mod-1)/n*(n-i)) = roots[n-i], which equals (roots[i])^{-1}.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.rationale: Replaces O(n log mod) modular exponentiation (~30 iterations of FastPow per element) with an O(n) array read/index. roots is already fully populated by line 11, so each invRoots[i] is a single load.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.risk: Correctness rests on roots[i] being exactly g^((mod-1)/n * i) and gPow having order n (true since g is a primitive root and n | mod-1). n is a power of two so (n-i)&(n-1) is the exact wraparound for i=0. Verify FastPow((mod-1)/n) path unchanged. No overflow change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.summary: Index the precomputed roots array directly for the twiddle instead of maintaining the serial wn multiply chain.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.currentCost: Lines 37-43: each butterfly does wn = wn * w % mod (one 64-bit mul + one mod) and carries wn as a loop-carried dependency, serializing the inner loop and the dependency chain v = a[..]*wn%mod -> wn update.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.proposedChange: Pass the roots base pointer and the stride step = n/len into the butterfly. Replace wn with a direct read: long wn = roots[step * j] (or maintain idx += step). Then v = a[i+j+half] * roots[step*j] % mod. This removes the wn*w%mod update entirely (one mul + one mod per butterfly) and breaks the loop-carried dependency on wn, exposing ILP and Burst vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.rationale: roots[n/len * j] == (roots[n/len])^j == wn by construction, so the value is identical. Eliminates one multiply and one modulo per butterfly across all O(n log n) butterflies, and the now-independent iterations let Burst pipeline/vectorize the v computation.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.risk: roots must contain all n powers (it does: NttInit fills 0..n-1, and NttConvolution builds a size-length roots table). The signature of PerformButterflyStep changes (add roots pointer + step), an internal private method so no public API break. Index step*j stays < n for j<half since (n/len)*(len/2) = n/2 < n. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.summary: Avoid the redundant per-butterfly modular twiddle by reusing the already-built roots/invRoots tables, and drop the dead inverse-roots table if reverse-permutation is used.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.currentCost: Lines 80-90 build full roots and invRoots tables (good), but Forward still recomputes twiddles via the wn chain (see PerformButterflyStep). invRoots is also a second size-length stackalloc that could be derived from roots by reverse indexing.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.proposedChange: Once PerformButterflyStep reads roots directly, the convolution's prebuilt roots table is consumed with no per-element twiddle modmuls. Additionally invRoots[i] can be set as roots[(size - i) & (size - 1)] (single pass, no FastPow at line 88 and no second cur-chain loop at lines 89-90), saving one FastPow plus one O(size) modmul loop and one stackalloc of size longs.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.rationale: Removes one FastPow (O(log mod)) and an O(size) modular-multiply chain; with the direct-index butterfly it also removes O(size log size) twiddle modmuls. Fewer modmuls and less stack pressure improves cache behavior on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.risk: size is a power of two so (size-i)&(size-1) wraps correctly; root has order size since size | mod-1. Keeping invRoots as a separate buffer is optional — reverse-indexing roots in place during Inverse would remove the buffer but changes access pattern; safest is to fill invRoots once from roots. No observable output change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.summary: The copy/zero-pad loop branches per element; split into copy range + zero range to make it branchless and vectorizable.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.currentCost: Line 78: for i in 0..size-1 does fa[i] = i<n ? a[i] : 0 and fb[i] = i<m ? b[i] : 0 — a per-element ternary/branch over the whole padded length, and n,m differ so two independent conditions.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.proposedChange: Copy fa[0..n) from a then zero fa[n..size); copy fb[0..m) from b then zero fb[m..size). Two contiguous memcpy-like loops plus two zeroing loops (or UnsafeUtility.MemClear / a simple zero loop Burst vectorizes).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.rationale: Removes the predicated select per element; contiguous copy and contiguous zero are both vectorizable and avoid mispredict on the i<n / i<m boundary. Same writes, just partitioned.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.risk: None semantically — identical contents. Ensure size>=n and size>=m (guaranteed since size>=n+m-1). Pure layout/loop-structure change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.summary: Replace '1 % mod' initializer with constant 1 and inline/share FastPow; mod is always > 1 here.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.currentCost: FastPow line 17/99 computes res = 1 % mod every call. mod is an NTT prime (>1), so 1 % mod is always 1 — a wasted 64-bit division on a non-hot but frequently-called helper. FastPow is duplicated verbatim in NttInit and NttConvolution.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.proposedChange: Use long res = 1; (drop the modulo) given the documented precondition mod > 1 for NTT primes. Mark FastPow with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] and consolidate the two identical copies into one internal static helper to aid Burst inlining/codegen.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.rationale: Eliminates one 64-bit idiv per FastPow invocation; AggressiveInlining lets Burst fold the exponent loop where e is a compile-time-ish constant pattern (mod-2). Deduplication reduces code size.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform.Ntt/Ntt.cs.risk: Dropping '1 % mod' assumes mod > 1, which holds for all valid NTT moduli (the smallest meaningful prime modulus is far above 1); if a caller could pass mod==1 the result would change from 0 to 1, so guard by documenting the mod>1 precondition (already implied by 'Unchecked Run assumes valid input'). Sharing the helper across static classes is a refactor with no behavioral change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.summary: Hoist the inverse/forward branch out of the innermost loop so the per-butterfly path is branchless.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.currentCost: Inside the O(n log n) innermost loop, every butterfly evaluates `if (!inverse)`. Although `inverse` is loop-invariant, it is re-tested n*log n times; the branch also obstructs Burst auto-vectorization of the modular add/sub.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.proposedChange: Split each method into two straight-line variants (or branch once on `inverse` before the `len` loop), e.g. an internal FwtOrForward / FwtOrInverse, each containing the triple loop with a single fixed expression `(v+u)%mod` or `(v-u+mod)%mod`. The public RunOr/RunAnd already know the direction at the call site, so dispatch there.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.rationale: Removes log n * n/2 branch evaluations and a per-iteration data dependency on a constant, exposing a clean uniform-stride loop body that Burst can SIMD-vectorize (no control flow). Code size grows trivially but I-cache cost is negligible vs. the inner-loop win.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.risk: None — identical arithmetic per branch; only the dispatch site moves. Keep `mod` and overflow behavior unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.summary: The `% mod` per butterfly is the dominant cost; it can be replaced by conditional subtraction since operands are already reduced.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.currentCost: RunOr/RunAnd/RunXor pre-reduce inputs to [0,mod). A 64-bit hardware integer division (`%`) per butterfly costs ~20-40 cycles and is the single most expensive op in the O(n log n) transform.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.proposedChange: For additions where u,v in [0,mod): replace `(u+v)%mod` with `long s=u+v; if(s>=mod) s-=mod;` (or branchless `s -= (mod & -(long)(s>=mod ? 0 : ... ))` form `s -= mod & ((s - mod) >> 63 ^ -1)` — simplest is the conditional-subtract). For subtraction `(u-v+mod)%mod` use `long d=u-v; d += mod & (d>>63);`. The Or-inverse `(v-u+mod)%mod` similarly. Requires u,v already in [0,mod), which the Run* wrappers guarantee, and the transform preserves that invariant (each output is again a single conditional-reduced add/sub).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.rationale: Sums of two reduced values are < 2*mod, so at most one subtraction restores range — turning a 20-40 cycle division into a 1-3 cycle add+predicated-subtract. With mod=1e9+7 this is exact; no overflow (2*mod < 2^31).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.risk: Only valid because Run* pre-reduces (lines 105-109, etc.) and the butterfly preserves [0,mod). If callers were ever to pass non-reduced data straight into FwtXor (it is private, so they cannot), the invariant could break. The branchless mask form depends on arithmetic right shift of negative longs (well-defined in C#).

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.summary: Fold the inverse 1/n scaling into the existing pointwise-multiply pass instead of a separate full sweep.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.currentCost: RunXor does a pointwise multiply loop (lines 146-149), then FwtXor on c, then a third O(n) loop multiplying by invN (lines 152-155). The final loop is a separate pass over c with its own `* invN % mod`.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.proposedChange: The 1/n factor is linear and commutes with the (already-final) state only after the transform, so it cannot fold into the pre-transform multiply. But it CAN be fused: compute invN once, then in the final FwtXor's last layer... simpler and safe: leave as is OR pre-scale by multiplying one operand's pointwise product by invN is invalid. Reject fusing into pre-multiply; instead just confirm the standalone scale loop is minimal. Lower-impact alternative: precompute invN before the transforms so the value is ready (no dependency stall), and mark it const-like.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.rationale: Marginal; the scaling must stay post-transform. Listing for completeness — the only real saving is ensuring invN computation (an ExtGcd recursion) is hoisted before the transforms so it overlaps, which it already effectively is.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.risk: Do NOT fold invN into the pointwise multiply — that would scale before the inverse transform and change results. Keep the separate post-pass.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.summary: ModInverse(n, mod) where n is a power of two and mod is prime can use a closed-form / Fermat path, but ExtGcd recursion is cheap and called once.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.currentCost: Recursive ExtGcd is called once per RunXor for invN. Recursion has call overhead and is not Burst-friendly (deep recursion), though depth is ~log mod ≈ 30.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.proposedChange: Make ExtGcd iterative (standard loop form with running coefficients) to remove recursion — Burst handles loops far better than recursion and it eliminates stack frames. Single call per RunXor, so impact is small, but recursion is a Burst smell worth removing here and in Fwht.cs.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.rationale: Iterative extended-Euclid is the same asymptotics with no call overhead and is Burst-compileable without stack-depth concerns.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/OrAndXorConvo.risk: Behavior identical if the iterative version returns the same canonical (x,y); ensure the final `(x%mod+mod)%mod` normalization is kept.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.summary: Uses `out` parameters and recursion; convert to pointer/iterative to match the unmanaged-Burst convention used elsewhere.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.currentCost: ExtGcd here uses managed `out long` and recursion, unlike OrAndXorConvolution which already uses `long*`. `out` on a static unmanaged path is fine but recursion is a Burst smell, and the two copies diverge stylistically.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.proposedChange: Replace recursive ExtGcd with an iterative loop and pointer outputs (mirror OrAndXorConvolution.ExtGcd). Called once per Inverse(), so the win is Burst-compatibility and consistency, not hot-loop cycles.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.rationale: Removes recursion stack frames and keeps the API uniform with the sibling file; iterative extended-Euclid is the same cost without call overhead.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.risk: Keep the g!=1 fallback returning 1 and the final normalization to preserve exact outputs.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.summary: Xor Forward accumulates without modular reduction, forcing the convolution to risk overflow and preventing the cheap-reduction path the Or/And variants use.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.currentCost: Forward does raw `u+v` / `u-v` with no `% mod`, so after log(size) layers values can reach size * max_input. FwhtConvolution.Run then computes `a[i]*b[i] % mod` on these unreduced longs (line 125), which can overflow 64-bit for large inputs and also means each product needs a full division.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.proposedChange: If the intended semantics is modular (the Or/And variants and Inverse use 1e9+7), reduce inside Forward like the OrAndXorConvolution.FwtXor: `f[i+j]=(u+v)%mod; f[i+j+len]=(u-v+mod)%mod;` — or better, the conditional-subtract form once inputs are pre-reduced. This keeps every intermediate in [0,mod), removing the overflow hazard in Run and enabling conditional-subtract instead of division.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.rationale: Bounded intermediates eliminate the multiply-overflow risk in Run and let the butterfly use cheap reduction; it also matches the documented modular contract used by Inverse (which divides by n mod 1e9+7).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.risk: This CHANGES observable output if any caller relied on the current non-reduced integer FWHT (true Hadamard transform over Z, not Z_p). The test only checks small reduced cases. Treat as a semantics decision: either Fwht.cs is a pure-integer transform (then Inverse's mod-inverse is wrong) or modular (then Forward must reduce). Flag for owner; do not apply blindly.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.summary: Three near-identical branches differing only by which static class is called; and unused `using` directives across the module.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.currentCost: Run duplicates the forward/pointwise/inverse body three times (Xor/Or/And). Maintenance hazard and code bloat, though each path is selected once per call (no hot-loop cost). Also `using System;` / `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;` are imported in files that don't use them.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.proposedChange: Keep the per-type static classes (Burst-friendly, no function pointers needed) but factor the shared pointwise-multiply loop. Or accept duplication for inlining. Remove unused usings (System / CompilerServices) where no attribute or type is referenced to keep the translation unit minimal.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.rationale: Reduces duplication and trims unused imports; no runtime effect but improves maintainability and avoids accidental divergence between the three modular contracts (note Xor.Forward currently does NOT reduce while Or/And do — a real inconsistency this consolidation would surface).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/Fwht.cs.risk: Purely cosmetic if the three transforms keep their distinct math; do not unify the butterfly bodies since Xor/Or/And differ. Removing usings is safe only after confirming no attribute (e.g. MethodImpl) is used in that file.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.summary: Inner loop iterates all i in [0,aLen) and branches on j-range; restrict the loop to the valid i-window to drop the per-iteration bounds branch and halve average iterations.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.currentCost: For each k it loops i from 0..aLen-1 and tests `if (j>=0 && j<bLen)`, so for boundary k most iterations are wasted and every iteration pays two compares + a branch that blocks vectorization. Total work is O(aLen*(aLen+bLen)) including dead iterations.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.proposedChange: Precompute the valid range once per k: `int iLo = k - (bLen-1); if (iLo < 0) iLo = 0; int iHi = k; if (iHi > aLen-1) iHi = aLen-1;` then loop `for (int i=iLo; i<=iHi; i++){ long sum=a[i]+b[k-i]; best = sum<best?sum:best; }`.
