Use branchless min: `best = math.min(best,sum)` (Unity.Mathematics) or `best = sum + ((best-sum)&((best-sum)>>63));`.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.rationale: Eliminates the in-loop range branch entirely (precomputed window), removing a hard-to-predict branch and letting Burst vectorize the min-reduction; also skips the dead iterations, reducing real work by roughly half on the boundary columns.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.risk: Window math must be exact: i ranges where 0<=k-i<bLen ⇔ k-bLen+1<=i<=k, intersected with [0,aLen-1]. Branchless min via mask relies on arithmetic right-shift of (best-sum); guard against overflow of the subtraction when values span the full long range — if inputs can be near ±2^63 keep the comparison form `sum<best?sum:best` which is overflow-safe.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.summary: Fuse the pointwise-product pass and the adjacent-difference pass into a single loop to cut one full O(n) sweep and its memory traffic.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.currentCost: MinIndex writes sc[i]=sa*sb%mod in one loop (17-20), then reads sc[i] and sc[i+1] in a second loop (21-25). Two passes over the sc array => extra n loads/stores and a second cache traversal.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.proposedChange: Combine: in one descending or paired loop compute sc[i] on the fly and immediately form c[i]=(sc[i]-sc[i+1]+mod)%mod, keeping sc[i+1] in a register. E.g. compute scNext = sa[n-1]*sb[n-1]%mod; c[n-1]=scNext; for i=n-2..0: scCur=sa[i]*sb[i]%mod; c[i]=(scCur-scNext+mod)%mod; scNext=scCur. Removes the sc array entirely (also a RAM win) when sc is only an intermediate.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.rationale: Single pass halves memory traffic over sc and removes the sc scratch buffer from the working set, improving cache behavior; the carried scNext register removes the redundant reload of sc[i+1].
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.risk: Must preserve c[n-1]=sc[n-1] (no subtraction) and the +mod before %mod. Reversing iteration order changes write order only, not values. If callers inspect sc after the call, removing it breaks them — but sc/sb/sa are passed as scratch, so verify they are not read post-call (they appear to be pure scratch).

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.summary: Already optimal O(n+m) merge; only micro-opt is hoisting the repeated diff subtraction, no asymptotic change available.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.currentCost: Each iteration recomputes a[i+1]-a[i] and b[j+1]-b[j]; the tail loops recompute one diff per step. Minor redundant subtraction but no wasted asymptotics.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.proposedChange: Optional: precompute difference arrays once is NOT a win (would add O(n) RAM). Leave as-is; this is already the linear convex-min-plus merge. No change recommended.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.rationale: The Minkowski-sum merge of two convex sequences is provably O(n+m); nothing faster exists. Listed to document that it was reviewed and is optimal.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.summary: Divide-and-conquer SMAWK-style recursion is the right O((n+m) log) algorithm but recursion is a Burst smell; the Math.Max/Min calls are fine but the dead-input guards add per-iteration branches.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.currentCost: Recursion depth O(log(n+m)) and the inner loop tests `candA != long.MaxValue && candB != long.MaxValue` every j. If sentinel-infinity inputs are not actually used by callers, these two compares per j are pure overhead in the hot scan.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.proposedChange: Keep the divide-and-conquer (correct asymptotics). If callers never pass long.MaxValue/MinValue sentinels, drop the sentinel checks. Replace Math.Max/Math.Min on ints with branchless or keep (Burst lowers Math.Min(int) well). Consider an explicit manual stack instead of recursion for Burst friendliness if depth matters.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.rationale: Removing the sentinel compares (when unused) strips two branches per inner iteration; iterative stack avoids recursion frames under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/MinMaxConvolu.risk: Dropping sentinel checks changes behavior if callers DO pass infinities — must confirm the contract. Math.Max/Min on int are deterministic and Burst-supported, so leaving them is safe.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.summary: Per-call branch `isPart` and `sign` recompute, plus modular multiply, dominate the inner pentagonal loop; specialize and strength-reduce.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.currentCost: UpdateVal is called O(n*sqrt(n)) times. Each call: computes `j%2` branch, an `isPart` branch (loop-invariant per outer call but passed as a runtime bool), and two `sign * c[...] % mod` 64-bit multiplies+divisions. The `sign` and `isPart` logic is recomputed every call though it only depends on j parity and the fixed caller.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.proposedChange: Inline UpdateVal into each caller (it is a tiny leaf — add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] at minimum). Hoist `isPart` out (two specialized bodies, since ConvolveWithPartition always passes true and ConvolveWithPentagonal always passes false — the bool is a compile-time constant per caller). Track sign by toggling: start sign=1 and flip `sign = mod - sign` each j instead of recomputing parity. The pentagonal case can also avoid the multiply since sign is ±1: use add/subtract `(val + c[...]) ` vs `(val - c[...] + mod)` instead of `sign * c[...]`, eliminating a 64-bit multiply and division per term.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.rationale: sign is always 1 or mod-1, so `sign * c[k] % mod` is just ±c[k] mod — replacing the multiply+div with a conditional add/subtract (already-reduced operands => conditional subtract) removes the single most expensive op in the loop. Toggling sign removes the parity branch. Constant-folding isPart removes a branch and a `(mod-sign)%mod`.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.risk: Must preserve the isPart sign convention exactly: ConvolveWithPentagonal flips sign via `(mod-sign)%mod`. Verify the toggled sign sequence matches the original parity mapping for the inner j and the additional flip. c[i-g1]/a[i-g1] are in [0,mod) only if inputs pre-reduced (a[i]%mod is taken; c is built reduced), enabling conditional-subtract; otherwise reduce first.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.summary: Recompute g1,g2 from scratch each (i,j); they are independent of i, so precompute the pentagonal offsets once.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.currentCost: Inside the i loop, for each j it recomputes `j*(3j-1)/2` and `j*(3j+1)/2` (two multiplies, two more multiplies, two divides) every time — but these generalized-pentagonal numbers depend only on j, not i, so they are recomputed n times each.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.proposedChange: Precompute the pentagonal offsets g1(j),g2(j) into a small stackalloc array (or generate incrementally) up to the max j where g<=n-1 (j ~ sqrt(2n/3)). Then the inner loop just indexes them. Alternatively generate g1/g2 incrementally with running deltas (g1 increases by 3j-2, etc.) to avoid the multiply/divide entirely.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.rationale: Moves O(n*sqrt n) pentagonal-number computations (each 4 mul + 2 div) down to O(sqrt n) precompute, replacing them with cheap array loads or incremental adds. The divides by 2 are exact (one of consecutive integers is even) and can already be a shift, but eliminating them entirely is better.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PartitionConv.risk: stackalloc size = number of valid j ≈ sqrt(2n/3); must bound it safely (cap and assert). Incremental generation must reproduce exact g1/g2; the early-break condition `g1>i && g2>i` still applies per i. Division by 2 is exact only because j*(3j∓1) is always even — true for all integer j, so >>1 is safe.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.summary: relation[x*n+y] index recomputes x*n each j; the column index y is fixed per outer i, so hoist y and stride relation by rows or precompute base.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.currentCost: Inner loop computes `relation[x*n + y]` with x varying and y fixed — the multiply x*n happens per element, and the access pattern is column-major (stride n) over the relation matrix, causing a cache miss roughly every element for large n.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.proposedChange: Since y is fixed in the inner loop, the natural fix is to store/access relation transposed for this kernel (relation[y_row * n + x] = 'x relates to y') so the inner loop walks a contiguous row relation[y*n + ...], turning stride-n column access into stride-1. If the matrix layout is fixed, at minimum hoist `int yn = y` and rely on x*n; but the cache win requires the transposed access. Also the `relation` bool* could be a bitset to cut the working set 8x.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.rationale: Column-major bool access at stride n thrashes cache for n beyond a few hundred; a contiguous row walk is the single biggest real-world speedup here. A bitset packs 64 relations per long, shrinking the matrix from n^2 bytes to n^2/8 and improving cache residency dramatically.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.risk: Transposing relation changes the data contract with callers and with LatticeMeet/Join/MobiusTransform which also index relation[x*n+y] vs [z*n+x]; any layout change must be applied consistently across ALL users or it breaks correctness. Bitset packing changes the public signature (bool* -> ulong*). Treat as a coordinated refactor, not a local edit.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.summary: Zeroing the mu matrix uses `(long)n*n` recomputed in the loop condition and writes every cell though only the upper triangle is populated.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.currentCost: `for (int i=0; i<(long)n*n; i++)` recomputes n*n as a long each iteration (the compiler likely hoists it, but the long compare is wider than needed) and zeroes all n^2 entries even though only reachable (x,y) pairs are later set.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.proposedChange: Hoist `long total = (long)n*n;` before the loop (or use `int` since n^2 fits int for realistic n and is faster), and consider memset via Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned for the zero-fill rather than a scalar loop. The scalar zero loop is O(n^2) of pure stores — a block clear is far faster and Burst/JIT-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.rationale: Block-clearing n^2 longs with InitBlock is memory-bandwidth-bound and several times faster than a scalar store loop; hoisting the bound removes a redundant widening multiply per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.risk: InitBlock zeroes bytes — valid since 0L is all-zero bytes. If n^2 longs exceeds int range the byte count must stay long; for realistic poset sizes n^2 fits int comfortably. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.summary: Hand-rolled popcount loop can be replaced by the intrinsic / AggressiveInlining leaf.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.currentCost: `while(x>0){x&=x-1;c++;}` is a data-dependent loop of up to 32 iterations with an unpredictable trip count, where a single hardware POPCNT exists.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.proposedChange: Use System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount((uint)x) (Burst lowers to popcnt) or math.countbits in Unity.Mathematics. Mark the method [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]. Cast to uint to match the intended non-negative semantics.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.rationale: Replaces an up-to-32-iteration dependency chain with one instruction; Burst and modern CPUs have native popcount, eliminating the loop and its branch.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.risk: x is int; the current loop treats x as the bit pattern of the positive value (x>0 guard skips the sign bit case). PopCount((uint)x) counts all 32 bits including bit 31 — for x>=0 this matches exactly; for negative x the old loop's `x>0` would... actually `x&(x-1)` on negative x loops oddly. Confirm callers only pass non-negative x (lattice ranks are >=0); then (uint) cast is exact.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.summary: O(n^2) per query with column-stride relation access; minor hoist of x,y indices and early-exit already present.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.currentCost: For each candidate z, an inner w-loop scans n entries at stride n (relation[w*n+x]) — column-major, cache-unfriendly. Two such matrix reads per w.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.proposedChange: These are inherently O(n^2) per query. Cache benefit again comes from a transposed/bitset relation (see ZetaTransform note) so the w-loop is contiguous and can AND two bitset rows 64 lanes at a time, finding mismatches with a single masked compare instead of per-w branches.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.rationale: A bitset relation lets `relation_row_x & relation_row_y & ~relation_row_z == 0` be checked 64 elements per long, collapsing the inner n-loop by 64x and removing per-w branches.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/PosetTransfor.risk: Same coordinated-layout-change risk as the ZetaTransform bitset proposal; only worthwhile if the whole module adopts the packed representation. Otherwise leave as-is.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.summary: Hoist invariant shifts out of the inner loop in the long-path Zeta step (and mirror it in SubsetMobius)
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.currentCost: The inner mask loop recomputes (1 << i) twice and the loop bound (1 << n) once per iteration. For a length-2^n array that is 2^n redundant shifts for the bit plus a re-evaluation of the bound expression every iteration, across n outer passes. The RunInt32 sibling already hoists 'bit' and proves this is the intended pattern.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.proposedChange: In PerformZetaStep compute 'int size = 1 << n; int bit = 1 << i;' once before the mask loop, use 'mask < size' as the bound, and replace (1 << i) with 'bit' in both the test and the XOR. Apply the identical change to SubsetMobius.PerformMobiusStep, SupersetZeta.PerformSupersetZetaStep, and SupersetMobius.PerformSupersetMobiusStep.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.rationale: Removes 2^n*n shift instructions and a per-iteration bound recomputation, shortening the dependency chain of the inner loop and matching the already-optimized RunInt32 path. Pure register hoist, no algorithmic change.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.risk: None. (1 << i) and (1 << n) are loop-invariant within their loops; values are identical. Note JIT may already hoist these, but Burst codegen benefits from making it explicit and it guarantees the optimization on all backends.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.summary: Inline the per-step helper into Run for the long variants to match the RunInt32 structure and enable cross-loop hoisting
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.currentCost: Run delegates to a private PerformZetaStep helper per outer i, which prevents hoisting 'size = 1 << n' to a single computation outside the outer loop and creates an inconsistent shape vs RunInt32 (which inlines everything).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.proposedChange: Fold PerformZetaStep's body directly into Run's outer loop (as RunInt32 already does), computing 'int size = 1 << n;' once before the outer i-loop and 'int bit = 1 << i;' once per outer iteration.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.rationale: Single computation of size for all n passes, consistent API surface between long and int32 paths, and removes the (already-likely-inlined but not guaranteed) call boundary that can block Burst hoisting.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetTransfo.risk: None observable; same arithmetic. Keep method names/signatures of Run unchanged so callers are unaffected; only the private helpers are removed.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.summary: Hoist (1 << i) in the rank-wise zeta/mobius inner loops
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.currentCost: In the zeta loop (lines 39-49) and mobius loop (lines 70-79), '(1 << i)' is recomputed up to three times per mask iteration: once for the mask test and twice for 'mask ^ (1 << i)'. This runs across numRanks * logN * n iterations, the dominant work of the routine.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.proposedChange: Inside the 'for i' loop and before the 'for mask' loop, compute 'int bit = 1 << i;' once and reuse it in the '(mask & bit) != 0' test and the 'mask ^ bit' index.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.rationale: Eliminates O(numRanks*logN*n) redundant shift instructions and shortens the address-computation dependency chain in the hottest loops of the method.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.risk: None. bit is invariant within the mask loop and the value is identical to (1 << i).

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.summary: Branchless predication of the conditional add/subtract in the zeta/mobius rank loops to avoid masked-iteration waste and enable vectorization
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.currentCost: The zeta and mobius loops iterate over all n masks but act on only half (those with bit i set), gated by a data-dependent branch 'if ((mask & bit) != 0)'. Half the iterations do nothing yet still pay loop overhead, and the branch defeats Burst vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.proposedChange: Restructure to iterate only over the relevant masks: 'for (int block = 0; block < n; block += bit << 1) for (int j = 0; j < bit; j++) { int hi = block + bit + j; fRow[hi] = (fRow[hi] + fRow[hi - bit]) % mod; ... }'. This visits exactly the n/2 active indices with no branch, the standard SOS-transform layout.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.rationale: Removes the n/2 idle iterations and the unpredictable branch, halving loop trip count for the active work and presenting straight-line contiguous-pair access that Burst can vectorize. Same asymptotic class but ~2x fewer iterations and branchless.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.risk: Must preserve modular semantics exactly (the % mod on each add/sub). The '+mod' before %mod in the mobius pass must be retained for the long-typed subtraction. Verify index arithmetic against the original mask^bit pairing; behavior identical for all valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.summary: Replace the magic-number modulus passed as 'long mod' usage and avoid repeated 64-bit modulo where the operand is known small
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.currentCost: The rank-product loop (lines 52-65) does 'sum = (sum + valF*valG) % mod' for every (i,j,mask) triple: O(numRanks^2 * n) 64-bit multiplies and modulo. 64-bit idiv is ~20-40+ cycles and is the costliest op here. Each valF/valG is already reduced to [0,mod), so partial sums can be deferred.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.proposedChange: Hoist the modulo: accumulate into the 64-bit sum across the small j-range and reduce less often, or use a wider __int128-style split is not available — instead note that since valF,valG < mod and mod fits in 32 bits in typical usage, products fit in 63 bits and at most numRanks(<=~31) of them can be summed before overflow only if mod <= ~2^31.5/sqrt(numRanks). If the contract guarantees mod < 2^31 (common for NTT-style mods like 1e9+7), reduce 'sum %= mod' once after the inner j-loop instead of every term.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.rationale: Cuts the number of 64-bit idiv operations in the rank-product step from O(numRanks^2*n) to O(numRanks*n), replacing the dominant divide cost with cheap 64-bit mul-add accumulation.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.risk: Overflow-sensitive: valid only if (i+1)*(mod-1)^2 < 2^63 for the largest i (numRanks-1). For mod=1e9+7 and numRanks up to ~31, (mod-1)^2 ~ 1e18 already nears 2^63 (~9.2e18), so only ~9 terms are safe — guard by reducing every K terms where K*(mod-1)^2 < 2^63, or keep per-term modulo if mod can be large. Document the mod bound; reject if mod may exceed ~3e9.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.summary: Precompute pc*n offset and replace per-element (long) index multiplies with running pointers in init/scatter/gather loops
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.currentCost: Lines 31-32, 59-60, 63, 85 compute '(long)pc*n + mask' or '(long)j*n+mask' with a 64-bit multiply per element. The init loop (21-26) zeroes via three separate indexed writes.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.proposedChange: For the scatter (28-33) and gather (82-86) loops the pc*n term needs a multiply only because pc varies per mask, so that is unavoidable, but cast can be int when totalSize fits int. For the rank-product loop hoist 'long baseI = (long)i*n' style row pointers (f + j*n) once per row rather than recomputing j*n+mask each j. Replace the three-array zero loop with per-array pointer increments or a single memset-style clear per array (f,g,h are contiguous rows).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.rationale: Turns per-element 64-bit multiplies into pointer increments and lets the zero-init become a tight contiguous store loop (Burst can vectorize/store-wide), reducing instruction count in setup and the inner product loop.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/SubsetConvolu.risk: Index type narrowing to int is only safe if numRanks*n <= int.MaxValue; logN<=26 keeps totalSize within int. Keep long indexing if logN can exceed ~26. Pointer-walking must preserve exact element order; no semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.summary: Hoist the (63 - i) shift amount and the per-iteration (1 << (cnt-1-i)) in the triangulation and reconstruction loops
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.currentCost: In the triangulation double loop (78-85), '63 - i' is recomputed for vec[i]'s pivot test on every j, and the bit-extract '>> (63-i) & 1' is evaluated for vec[i] redundantly across the whole inner j-loop though it is invariant in j. In the reconstruction loop (87-91), '1 << (cnt-1-i)' is recomputed each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.proposedChange: Before the inner j-loop compute 'int sh = 63 - i; long pivotI = (vec[i] >> sh) & 1; if (pivotI == 0) continue;' then test only '(vec[j] >> sh) & 1'. In the reconstruction loop replace with a single bit that shifts: iterate so the k-bit is derived by a running shift rather than recomputing 1 << (cnt-1-i).
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.rationale: Removes invariant recomputation from the inner loop (the vec[i] pivot test and the shift amount are constant across j) and turns a per-iteration variable-shift into a constant operation, reducing instructions in the O(cnt^2) triangulation.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.risk: None. The hoisted values are loop-invariant in j; if pivotI is 0 the original inner condition is always false so 'continue' is equivalent to doing nothing for that i. Behavior identical for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.summary: Use a single descending bit mask instead of recomputing (1L << i) each iteration, and skip directly to the top set bit
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.currentCost: Both loops compute '(1L << i)' every iteration over 64 positions and test against x. Many high iterations are wasted when x has few high bits set.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.proposedChange: Maintain 'long bitMask = 1L << i' updated by '>>= 1' per step, or better, drive the loop from the highest set bit of x using a leading-zero-count intrinsic (System.Numerics.BitOperations.LeadingZeroCount) so only the set-bit positions that matter are visited; for each, index basis[i] directly.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.rationale: Replaces 64 variable shifts with either a single running shift or, via LZCNT, jumps straight to relevant bits, cutting iteration count when x is sparse. Constant-factor win on a hot small-loop primitive.
src/IAFahim.Math.Transform/XorBasis.cs.risk: LeadingZeroCount path changes loop structure; must reproduce exact reduction order (process bits high-to-low, XOR with basis[i], recompute next-highest bit of the updated x). Equivalent result since elimination is high-to-low regardless of skipped zero bits. Ensure BitOperations is Burst-supported in the target Unity version; if not, keep the running-shift variant which is unconditionally safe.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.summary: Replace the UnsafeParallelHashSet<Ptr> free-list with an intrusive stack-of-free-indices (or embedded free-list inside the buffer), turning Alloc/Free into O(1) pointer arithmetic and removing all hashing/iterator overhead.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.currentCost: Alloc() does freeIndex.Count()==0 check, allocates an Enumerator (GetEnumerator + MoveNext over an open-addressed hash table that may probe many empty buckets to find the first occupied slot), reads Current, then Remove() which re-hashes the pointer and re-probes. Free() Add() re-hashes. Each op is several hash computations + random-access probes into a separate heap-allocated bucket array = guaranteed cache misses, far more than a pool needs. Construction also inserts maxItems pointers one-by-one into the hash set (maxItems hash+probe), and the set itself is a second large allocation duplicating information already implied by the contiguous buffer.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.proposedChange: Store a free list as an int* stack (size maxItems) allocated once, plus a freeCount int. Constructor fills stack[i]=i for i in [0,maxItems) and sets freeCount=maxItems (a tight, vectorizable/sequential write). Alloc(): if(freeCount==0) return null; return (T*)buffer + stack[--freeCount];. Free(p): stack[freeCount++] = (int)((T*)p - (T*)buffer);. Alternatively, since the slots themselves are free when not in use, embed an intrusive singly-linked free list head index inside the unused T slots (store next-index in the first 4 bytes of each free slot) and keep only an int freeHead — zero extra allocation. Both make Alloc/Free branch-light, allocation-free, and cache-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.rationale: An index/pointer stack or intrusive free list is the canonical O(1) pool design with no hashing, no probing, and sequential memory access. It eliminates the Enumerator object churn on every Alloc, removes two hash computations and two random-probe sequences per Alloc and one per Free, and (for the intrusive variant) removes the entire second heap allocation (UnsafeParallelHashSet bucket array), halving the allocator's working set and cache footprint. Construction drops from maxItems hash inserts to a single linear fill.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.risk: Behavior preserved for valid callers (Alloc still returns a distinct free slot or null when exhausted; Free returns a slot). Edge: a plain LIFO stack returns the most-recently-freed pointer rather than hash-set iteration order, but no documented ordering contract exists, so observable behavior to valid callers is preserved. Double-free / foreign-pointer detection currently provided by freeIndex.Contains must be reimplemented in the ENABLE_UNITY_COLLECTIONS_CHECKS-guarded ValidatePtr (e.g. a separate per-slot in-use bitset under checks only) so debug diagnostics are not lost; release builds are unaffected since ValidatePtr is [Conditional].

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.summary: Even keeping the hash set, drop the redundant freeIndex.Count()==0 pre-check — the subsequent e.MoveNext() already reports emptiness.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.currentCost: Alloc() calls Count() (a full field/derived read) then constructs an Enumerator and calls MoveNext(); when the set is empty both report empty, so Count() is pure redundant work on every call, and when non-empty Count() is wasted entirely. Two emptiness checks for one decision.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.proposedChange: Remove the leading `if (this.freeIndex.Count() == 0) return null;` block and rely solely on `if (!e.MoveNext()) return null;` inside the using. This collapses two emptiness tests into one.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.rationale: Fewer instructions and one fewer dependent load on the hot Alloc path; MoveNext()==false is exactly the empty condition, so the Count() call is strictly redundant.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeFixe.risk: None — observable result identical (returns null iff no free slot). This is moot if the intrusive-free-list rewrite above is adopted, but it is a safe standalone micro-win otherwise.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.summary: Replace the integer-division `64 / UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>()` with a precomputed/branchless minimum-capacity expression and avoid the div in the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.currentCost: CreateList computes `64 / UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>()` — an integer division (20-40+ cycle latency, not pipelined) — on every call, even though SizeOf<T>() is a compile-time-constant per specialization under Burst. Then math.ceilpow2 runs on the result.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.proposedChange: SizeOf<T>() is constant per generic instantiation, so Burst can already fold `64 / SizeOf<T>()` to a constant; ensure that by keeping it as `const`-foldable. If Burst does not fold it (managed/IL2CPP path), hoist it: compute `int minCap = 64 / sizeOf;` once is unavoidable, but you can replace the division with `(64 >> log2(sizeOf))` only when sizeOf is a power of two — not guaranteed. Safer: since the only goal is 'at least one cache line of elements', compute `math.max(capacity, (64 + sizeOf - 1) / sizeOf)` is still a div; the real win is to mark intent and let Burst constant-fold, and to drop ceilpow2 work when capacity already dominates. Concretely: `int minCap = 64 / sizeOf; int newCapacity = math.ceilpow2(math.max(capacity, minCap));` keeps one div but removes the double assignment to newCapacity (currently two statements / two writes).
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.rationale: Folding the per-type constant removes a true integer division from a list-creation path; collapsing the two-statement `newCapacity` assignment into one nested expression removes a redundant store and lets the optimizer keep the value in a register. Under Burst with constant SizeOf<T> the entire min/div folds away.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.risk: Low. math.ceilpow2 of a value <=0 is undefined, but maxItems/capacity here are >=1 and minCap>=1 (64/sizeOf, sizeOf<=64 typical), so the existing domain is preserved. If sizeOf>64 (large structs) minCap becomes 0 and ceilpow2(max(capacity,0)) — same as today's code, so no regression. Do not switch the div to a shift unless sizeOf is provably power-of-two.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.summary: Tracking every allocation in a NativeHashSet<Ptr> doubles bookkeeping memory and adds a hash+probe per Allocate; a growable UnsafeList<Ptr> (append-only) is sufficient since FreeAll iterates all entries anyway.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.currentCost: Every Allocate() does this.allocated.Add(ptr) = hash(ptr) + open-addressed probe + possible rehash/resize; the hash set stores buckets+slots (sparse, ~2x load-factor overhead) for pointers that are only ever bulk-freed. FreeAll() then copies the whole set to a NativeArray<Ptr>(Temp) (a second allocation + full copy) just to iterate it.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.proposedChange: Replace `NativeHashSet<Ptr> allocated` with `UnsafeList<Ptr> allocated`. Allocate() does allocated.Add(ptr) (amortized O(1) tail write, sequential, no hashing). FreeAll() iterates allocated.Ptr[0..Length] directly freeing each, then allocated.Clear() — no ToNativeArray(Temp) copy and no Temp allocation. This removes per-allocation hashing, the set's bucket overhead, and the FreeAll scratch array.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.rationale: The set's uniqueness guarantee is unused: AllocatorManager.Allocate never returns a duplicate live pointer, so dedup is dead work. A contiguous list gives sequential append (cache-friendly, branch-light), eliminates the hash computation per Allocate, removes the FreeAll Temp NativeArray allocation+copy, and frees in allocation order (sequential pointer walk) instead of hash order (random walk) — better for the OS/allocator free path too.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/MemoryAllo.risk: Medium. If any caller relied on FreeAll being safe under accidental double-registration of the same pointer (set would dedup), a list would free it twice — but Allocate is the only writer and returns unique pointers, so this cannot occur for valid use. Free of individual pointers is not supported by this type today (only FreeAll), so no removal semantics are lost. Keep Ptr.GetHashCode for other users.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.summary: Per-thread UnsafePoolAllocator structs are packed contiguously, inviting false sharing on the hot Alloc/Free path across threads; pad each per-thread pool to a cache-line boundary.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.currentCost: pools is an array of UnsafePoolAllocator<T> laid out back-to-back. Alloc()/Free() on thread i mutate pools[i] (its head/count fields). If sizeof(UnsafePoolAllocator<T>) < 64 bytes (or not a cache-line multiple), pools[i] and pools[i+1] share a cache line, so concurrent Alloc/Free from adjacent threads cause cache-line ping-pong (false sharing) — a severe scalability cost on the exact hot path this type exists to make parallel.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.proposedChange: Allocate each per-thread pool on its own cache line: either wrap UnsafePoolAllocator<T> in a struct padded to 64 bytes (or JobsUtility cache-line size) before laying them out, or over-allocate with stride = align-up(sizeof(UnsafePoolAllocator<T>), 64) and index pools via byte offset. Indexing in Alloc/Free becomes `*(UnsafePoolAllocator<T>*)((byte*)pools + threadIndex * stride)`.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.rationale: Eliminating false sharing is the single biggest determinant of scaling for a sharded/per-thread allocator. Padding to a cache line makes each thread's Alloc/Free touch a private line, removing inter-core coherence traffic; the cost is a few KB of padding (threadCount * <64B), negligible versus the throughput gain under contention.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.risk: Low on correctness (same pool per thread, same results). Costs a bit more RAM (padding). Stride indexing must use the same cache-line constant on alloc and free; recommend a named constant (e.g. JobsUtility.CacheLineSize). Verify UnsafePoolAllocator<T> has no internal pointer that assumes contiguous packing (it does not — pools are independent).

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.summary: Hoist JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount out of the loop conditions; it is read on every iteration in the constructor, Dispose, and Allocated.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.currentCost: `for (int i = 0; i < JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount; i++)` re-evaluates JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount (a property/static accessor, potentially a non-inlined call returning a SharedStatic-backed value) every iteration in three loops. Burst may not prove it loop-invariant if it is a property with a method body, so it can become a per-iteration call that also blocks vectorization/unrolling of the simple accumulate loop in Allocated().
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.proposedChange: Cache `int threadCount = JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount;` once at the top of each method (or store it as a readonly field set in the constructor, since it is fixed for the lifetime of the allocator) and use it in the loop bound. For Allocated(), this also exposes a clean reduction `for(i=0;i<threadCount;i++) acc += pools[i].Allocated();` the optimizer can unroll.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.rationale: Removes a repeated static-property read from each loop iteration, shortens the loop's dependency/bookkeeping chain, and gives Burst a constant trip count to unroll/vectorize the Allocated reduction. Storing it as a readonly field also removes the assumption that ThreadIndexCount is identical at construct vs dispose time (purity/determinism).
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePara.risk: None for correctness as long as ThreadIndexCount is stable across the allocator's lifetime (it is fixed per process for Jobs). Caching it in a field actually hardens against it changing between construct and dispose. Trivial.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/Ptr.cs.summary: The pointer hash `(int)(long)Value` discards the high 32 bits and the low ~3-4 alignment bits, clustering aligned allocations into few buckets; mix the full 64-bit value to a 32-bit hash to cut collisions.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/Ptr.cs.currentCost: GetHashCode returns the low 32 bits of the pointer. Heap allocations are typically 8/16-byte aligned, so the low 3-4 bits are constant, and contiguous allocations differ only in low bits — producing long open-addressing probe chains in any NativeHashSet<Ptr> (used by MemoryAllocator and previously by the pool), degrading Add/Contains/Remove toward O(n) under clustering.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/Ptr.cs.proposedChange: Mix the full 64-bit address, e.g. `ulong x = (ulong)Value; x ^= x >> 32; return unchecked((int)(x * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15UL >> 32));` (a fibonacci/xorshift finalizer), or at minimum `(int)((long)Value ^ ((long)Value >> 32))`. This spreads both halves and avoids alignment clustering.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/Ptr.cs.rationale: A well-mixed hash shortens probe chains in open-addressed Unity hash sets, directly speeding every Add/Contains/Remove that uses Ptr as a key. Low constant cost (a multiply + shift) for materially fewer cache-missing probes when the set is the data structure in play.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/Ptr.cs.risk: Behavior preserved: Equals is unchanged (still pointer identity), and GetHashCode only needs equal objects to hash equal — they still do. This becomes irrelevant if MemoryAllocator switches off the hash set (other ram opportunity) and the pool drops its set, so weigh against those; if any hash-set-of-Ptr remains, this is a clear win. Keep it unchecked to preserve wrap semantics.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.summary: Replace the UnsafeParallelHashSet free list with an intrusive singly-linked LIFO free stack.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.currentCost: Every Free hashes the pointer and inserts into a hash set (bucket probe + possible resize). Every Alloc, on the fast path, constructs an enumerator, calls MoveNext, reads Current, then calls Remove which re-hashes and re-probes for the SAME key — two full hash operations plus enumerator setup/teardown per allocation. The hash set also stores keys in scattered buckets (cache misses) and duplicates pointer storage entirely separate from the slab memory.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.proposedChange: Since each freed block is at least sizeof(T) (T:unmanaged) and these blocks are dead while free, store the free list intrusively: keep a single `T* freeHead`. Free(p): `*(T**)p = freeHead; freeHead = p;`. Alloc(): if freeHead != null, `T* r = freeHead; freeHead = *(T**)r; return r;` else slabAllocator.Alloc(). This requires sizeof(T) >= sizeof(void*); guard with a Debug.Assert in the ctor (true for any T big enough to be worth pooling). Removes the UnsafeParallelHashSet field entirely.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.rationale: Alloc/Free become a handful of pointer loads/stores with zero hashing, zero probing, zero allocation, and perfect temporal/spatial locality (the link is in the block being reused, which is about to be touched anyway). O(1) worst case vs amortized-with-resize hashing. Also frees the RAM the hash set's bucket/next arrays consumed.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.risk: Changes internal representation only; Alloc/Free observable contract (returns a free block, marks block free) is preserved. Reusing the freed block's first 8 bytes as the link is safe because the block is unowned while free. Requires sizeof(T) >= sizeof(void*) (8 on 64-bit); add Debug.Assert(UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() >= sizeof(void*)). LIFO vs the hash set's arbitrary order is not an observable guarantee. Loses the parallel-write capability, which is unused here and not part of the single-threaded contract.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.summary: If a hash-based free list must be kept, use UnsafeHashSet not UnsafeParallelHashSet, and avoid the double lookup.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.currentCost: UnsafeParallelHashSet carries per-thread-block bookkeeping for concurrent writers; this allocator is single-threaded, so that machinery (extra indirection, padded per-thread data) is pure overhead in cache footprint and per-op cost. Additionally Alloc does MoveNext+Current then Remove(ptr), re-hashing the same key.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.proposedChange: Swap to UnsafeHashSet<Ptr>. Better: expose/emulate a 'remove one element' that reuses the located slot. At minimum, the enumerator-then-Remove pattern should be replaced by a method that pops-and-removes in one hash probe. (Preferred fix is the intrusive list above; this is the fallback if hash semantics are required.)
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.rationale: Eliminates parallel-set per-thread overhead and one redundant hash+probe per Alloc, reducing both cycles and working-set size.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafePool.risk: Behavior identical for single-threaded use. Only safe because no concurrent Add/Remove occur; the parallel set is not needed by the documented API.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.summary: Cache the current slab base pointer and free counter to remove repeated dereferences and index recomputation on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.currentCost: Every Alloc dereferences `*this.count` up to three times (compare, reset, post-increment) through a heap pointer, and on the common (non-grow) path computes `this.slabs->Length - 1` and indexes the UnsafeList `(*this.slabs)[...]` via its bounds-aware indexer to fetch the last slab. The count lives behind a separate heap allocation, so each access is a potential cache miss and creates a long load-store dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.proposedChange: Hold the active slab base directly in the struct, e.g. add `T* current;` updated whenever a new slab is pushed. Then Alloc fast path is: `int c = *this.count; if (c == countPerSlab) { grow; c = 0; } *this.count = c + 1; return this.current + c;`. This reads count once, reuses it, and avoids re-indexing slabs->Length-1 entirely on the common path.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.rationale: Cuts the per-Alloc dependency chain (single load of count, single store), removes the UnsafeList indexer call and Length-1 arithmetic from the hot path, and replaces an extra pointer chase with a register-held base pointer. Fewer cache misses and a shorter critical path improve throughput in tight allocation loops.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.risk: Must keep `current` in sync in Clear() (set to null) and on grow. Observable results unchanged: same pointers returned, same counts. The count==countPerSlab initial sentinel that forces first-Alloc growth must be preserved so the first Alloc still allocates a slab before using current.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.summary: Precompute and cache sizeof(T) (and stride) instead of calling UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() per call.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.currentCost: Alloc, AllocationCount, and Allocated each call UnsafeUtility.SizeOf<T>() at runtime. Under Burst this is typically folded to a constant, but the slab byte size `(long)countPerSlab * SizeOf<T>()` is recomputed on every grow, and Allocated()/AllocationCount recompute products every call.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.proposedChange: Store a readonly `int sizeOfT` (and optionally `long slabBytes = (long)countPerSlab * sizeOfT`) computed once in the ctor; use them in Alloc's grow path and the count methods. sizeof(T) is invariant for a closed generic.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.rationale: Removes a repeated multiply/intrinsic on the grow path and in count queries; makes the slab byte size a precomputed constant. Cheap, always-correct invariant hoisting.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.risk: None semantically; SizeOf<T> is constant for a given T. Under Burst the SizeOf call is already a constant so the multiply is the only real saving; impact is low but real for non-Burst/managed mono fallback.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.summary: Allocated() reports total reserved bytes, not bytes actually handed out — name/semantics are misleading versus AllocationCount.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.currentCost: Allocated() returns slabs->Length * countPerSlab * sizeof(T) (total capacity across all slabs), while AllocationCount returns the number of live objects. The Pool's Allocated() forwards to it. A caller reasonably expects 'Allocated' to mean live/used bytes, mirroring AllocationCount.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.proposedChange: Rename to ReservedBytes()/CapacityBytes(), or add AllocatedBytes() = AllocationCount * sizeof(T) for live usage. Keep one consistent vocabulary (Count for objects, Bytes for memory). This is a naming/discoverability fix, not a perf change.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.rationale: Reduces caller error and aligns the API with the Count/Bytes distinction the type already implies, without affecting the perf model.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.risk: API rename is a breaking change for callers; provide it additively or coordinate the rename. No correctness/runtime risk.

src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.summary: Store the count inline in the struct instead of behind a separate 4-byte heap allocation.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.currentCost: The ctor does a dedicated Unmanaged.Allocate for a single int (the count), adding an allocation, a free in Dispose, a pointer field, and a guaranteed cache miss on every Alloc/AllocationCount access since count lives in unrelated heap memory. The [NativeDisableUnsafePtrRestriction] attribute and extra alloc/free exist solely to support this.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.proposedChange: Make count a plain `int count;` field in the struct (initialized to countPerSlab) and use IsCreated based on `slabs != null` instead of `count != null`. This removes the Allocate/Free pair, the pointer indirection, the cache miss, and the attribute.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.rationale: Inline field is register/L1-resident, removing a heap allocation, a free, and a per-Alloc cache miss; shrinks both the allocation count and the critical-path latency of Alloc.
src/IAFahim.Memory.Allocators/UnsafeSlab.risk: Reason for the heap-allocated count is likely that the struct is copied by value and copies must share mutable state (the original code shares count and slabs by pointer so copies see each other's mutations). If the design relies on value copies aliasing the same allocator state, count must stay heap-allocated; verify usage before inlining. If copies are never expected to alias, inlining is safe and strictly better. Flag this aliasing requirement explicitly before applying.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.summary: points[j] % prime is recomputed n times for every j; precompute the reduced points array once, turning O(n^2) modulo ops into O(n).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.currentCost: Inner loop computes points[j] % prime on every (i,j) pair, in both the lhs and rhs passes. That is 2*n*n modulo operations (the most expensive integer op, ~20-40 cycles each), plus the dependency the value never changes across i.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.proposedChange: Before the i-loops, allocate long* p = stackalloc long[n]; for (int j=0;j<n;j++) p[j] = points[j] % prime; then in the hot loop use p[j] directly: pow = (pow * p[j]) % prime;
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.rationale: Hoists a loop-invariant (independent of i) out of the doubly-nested loop, collapsing 2*n^2 divisions to n divisions plus n^2 multiply+mod. Cuts the dominant cost roughly in half and removes a redundant load+div from the inner dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.risk: None. points[j] % prime depends only on j, so the value is identical for every i. stackalloc long[n] is consistent with house style. Assumes prime>0 (same precondition as existing code).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.summary: (1 << j) is recomputed each inner iteration; it can be a single shifting mask variable, and poly[i*n+j] row base i*n is loop-invariant in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.currentCost: Each inner iteration computes 1<<j (shift), i*n+j (multiply-add for index), and tests against poly. i*n is recomputed every inner step.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.proposedChange: Hoist int rowBase = i * n; before the j-loop and index poly[rowBase + j]. Optionally maintain int bit = 1; advancing bit <<= 1; each iteration instead of recomputing 1<<j.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.rationale: Removes a multiply from the inner index computation (replaced by a single add) and turns a variable-distance shift into an incremental shift, shortening the inner-loop instruction count and dependency.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.risk: None for rowBase. For the incremental bit, j<32 is required so the shift does not overflow; the existing (1<<j) already assumes j<32, so semantics are unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.summary: The lhs and rhs passes are byte-identical except for the source matrix; factor into a private helper to shrink code size and improve I-cache/inlining behavior.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.currentCost: Two copies of the same triple-nested reduction body bloat the method, hurting I-cache and making the AggressiveInlining attribute expand a large body at every call site.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.proposedChange: Extract private static long EvalSum(int* mat, int n, long* reducedPoints, int prime) and call it twice: return EvalSum(poly,...) == EvalSum(eval,...). Keep AggressiveInlining on the leaf helper only if small.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.rationale: Single code path improves maintainability and lets the compiler optimize one body; reduces duplicated instruction footprint. Combined with the precomputed points array, the helper is the natural home for the hoisted work.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/S.risk: None functionally. Re-evaluate AggressiveInlining: inlining a large triple-loop body twice may bloat callers; consider dropping it from Test and keeping the helper non-inlined.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.summary: The entire method body is dead: cur is unused, the loop only multiplies temp (a local) and returns best = state[0] regardless. The loop is pure waste.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.currentCost: Up to 1000 iterations of a double multiply (temp *= cooling) plus a double comparison per call, all of which are discarded. cur is computed and never used. Net effect: hundreds of wasted FP ops and a misleading API.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.proposedChange: If the intent is a placeholder, reduce to return state[0]; and delete the loop, cur, temp, cooling, target, n usage. If real annealing is intended, the loop must actually evaluate candidate states against target using temp/cooling; flag this as incomplete rather than micro-optimize.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.rationale: Eliminating provably-dead computation removes 100% of the loop cost. The compiler may already DCE the loop since temp is local and unused after the loop, but the source is misleading and the unused parameters defeat the stated API contract.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.risk: Behavior is observably unchanged (return value is always state[0]). The real risk is semantic: the function does not implement simulated annealing at all, so 'optimizing' it should be paired with confirming intended behavior before shipping.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.summary: sum / n is a 64-bit signed division; if n is known/constant or a power of two it can be strength-reduced, and the running sum risks overflow for large n.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.currentCost: One 64-bit signed idiv per call (~20-90 cycles). Also sum can overflow long if n*max(sample) exceeds 2^63.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.proposedChange: Keep the divide (n is runtime-variable so general strength reduction is not possible), but document/guard overflow. If callers commonly pass power-of-two n, expose an overload taking a shift count. Otherwise leave as-is; this is near-optimal.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.rationale: A single trailing division over an O(n) accumulation is already optimal asymptotically; only the constant-factor idiv and overflow envelope are improvable, and only with caller-side knowledge.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/M.risk: Strength-reducing / to >> only valid when n is a known power of two AND sum is non-negative (signed >> rounds toward -inf, differing from / for negative sums). Do not apply blindly.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.summary: i*n is recomputed every inner iteration; hoist the row base pointer to remove a multiply from the inner loop and shorten the address dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.currentCost: Inner loop indexes mat[i*n + j], recomputing i*n (a multiply) on each of the n*n iterations across both overloads.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.proposedChange: Before the inner loop: int* row = mat + i * n; (or long*) then sum += (long)row[j] * vec[j];. The compiler may already strength-reduce this, but the explicit row pointer guarantees a single add-stride access pattern Burst vectorizes cleanly.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.rationale: Replaces an inner-loop multiply with a hoisted base-plus-stride pointer, improving the chance Burst emits a contiguous SIMD load over row[j]. Same applies to both int* and long* overloads.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.risk: None. Pure index reassociation; identical results for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.summary: Three stackalloc long[n] buffers are allocated on every PerformCheck call (once per Freivalds iteration); the br/cr intermediate buffers can be reused and the allocation hoisted out of the iters loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.currentCost: Per iteration: 3*n*8 bytes of fresh stack frame setup. Across iters iterations this re-stack-allocates repeatedly. cr is only needed transiently for the final compare.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.proposedChange: Allocate ar/br/cr once in Verify (outside the it-loop) and pass them in, reusing across iterations. Additionally, fold the c*r==a*(b*r) compare to avoid materializing cr fully: compute cr[i] inline and compare against ar[i] in one fused pass, dropping one buffer (2*n*8 bytes instead of 3).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.rationale: Hoisting stackalloc out of the loop removes repeated frame adjustment; fusing the final MatrixVectorMultiply(c) with the comparison eliminates the cr buffer and one full pass over results, cutting working set by a third and saving n stores+loads.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.risk: stackalloc inside a loop is technically reused frame space in C#, so RAM may already be constant; the real win is the fused c-multiply/compare dropping a buffer and a pass. Behavior identical: ar[i] != (c row . r) is the same test as ar[i] != cr[i].

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.summary: r[i] = (int)((*seed & 1) * 2 - 1) repeatedly dereferences seed and uses a multiply; load seed into a local register for the whole loop and use a branchless bit-to-sign.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.currentCost: Each iteration reloads *seed (pointer dereference, no register caching across the xorshift) and computes a multiply-subtract to map {0,1}->{-1,1}.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.proposedChange: uint s = *seed; inside loop update s with the xorshift, write r[i] = (int)((s & 1u) << 1) - 1; and store *seed = s; once after the loop. The <<1 replaces the *2.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.rationale: Caching seed in a local removes a pointer round-trip per iteration and enables register allocation of the xorshift state; <<1 is a strength reduction of *2. Shortens the per-element dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Approximation/F.risk: None. (s&1)<<1 - 1 yields exactly -1/1 as before. Writing seed back once preserves the same final RNG state, so subsequent iterations are identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.summary: Branchless accumulation in the hot inner loop removes a data-dependent branch per element.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.currentCost: Inner loop runs n times per binary-search iteration (O(n log(hi-lo)) total). Each iteration has a data-dependent branch `if (v > 0) sum += v;` that the compiler cannot perfectly predict for arbitrary w[i], causing branch mispredicts and breaking auto-vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.proposedChange: Replace `long v = w[i] - mid; if (v > 0) sum += v;` with a branchless form: `long v = w[i] - mid; sum += v & ~(v >> 63);`. For 64-bit signed v, `v >> 63` is 0 when v>=0 and all-ones (-1) when v<0, so `v & ~(v>>63)` yields v for v>0 and 0 for v<=0 (note v==0 gives 0, matching the original which only adds when v>0).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.rationale: Eliminates the per-element conditional branch and produces a straight-line dependency that Burst/LLVM can vectorize into SIMD masked-add across the w[] array, turning a scalar branchy loop into a vectorizable reduction. Fewer mispredicts, higher ILP.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.risk: Relies on arithmetic right shift of signed long (guaranteed in C#). w[i]-mid must not overflow long; this overflow risk already exists in the current code (w[i] and mid are long), so semantics are unchanged. v==0 contributes 0 in both versions, so behavior is identical for all inputs.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.summary: Early-exit once sum >= k lets the inner reduction stop short on large-k-satisfying mids.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.currentCost: The inner loop always scans all n elements even after `sum` has already exceeded k, so the >= k decision is known. For large n this wastes work when the threshold is crossed early.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.proposedChange: Add `if (sum >= k) { /* mark satisfied */ break; }` inside the loop (or hoist the comparison so the loop terminates as soon as sum>=k), then branch lo/hi on the satisfied flag. Keep the branchless body for the common not-yet-satisfied case.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.rationale: Reduces average inner-loop trip count; the predicate is monotone in the partial sum (all added terms are non-negative), so once sum>=k the final answer is fixed regardless of remaining elements.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/L.risk: Adds a branch back into the loop, which can defeat vectorization; this is a tradeoff vs the branchless win above. Only beneficial when k is frequently crossed early. Behavior preserved because remaining terms are >=0 and cannot lower sum below k.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.summary: Cache *head/*tail in locals and hoist repeated Eval(deque[*head], i) to cut pointer derefs and redundant recomputation per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.currentCost: *head and *tail are dereferenced through int* on every comparison and update inside both while loops (3-6 pointer loads/stores per element). Also `Eval(quads[deque[*head]], i)` is computed in the first while-loop condition and then recomputed again for `dp[i]` on line 32.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.proposedChange: Load `int h = *head; int t = *tail;` at function entry, operate on the locals throughout both while loops and the push, and write `*head = h; *tail = t;` once at the end of each iteration (or once after the loop, updating locals in-loop). Additionally, after the head-advance loop, reuse the already-computed `Eval(quads[deque[h]], i)` value for `dp[i]` instead of calling Eval a second time.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.rationale: Promotes head/tail to registers, removing aliasing-forced reloads (the compiler cannot assume *head/*tail don't alias dp/deque/quads through int*/long*). Reusing the front Eval removes one multiply-heavy Eval (2 muls + 2 adds) per element from the n-length outer loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.risk: Must ensure the cached front-Eval value corresponds to the final deque[h] after the advance loop (it does: the loop exits when front is no longer dominated, so the surviving deque[h] is the one evaluated). No aliasing concern because head/tail are scalars passed by pointer and not written through other pointers in the loop. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.summary: Factor Eval to one fewer multiply via Horner form.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.currentCost: `q.A * x * x + q.B * x + q.C` issues 3 multiplies and 2 adds.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.proposedChange: Use Horner: `(q.A * x + q.B) * x + q.C` — 2 multiplies, 2 adds, and a shorter dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.rationale: Strength-reduces one 64-bit multiply and shortens the critical path (the two muls now chain but total mul count drops from 3 to 2). Eval is called in the innermost deque loop, so per-element savings compound.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/D.risk: Integer multiply is associative/distributive in two's-complement wraparound arithmetic, so `A*x*x` and `(A*x+B)*x + C` produce bit-identical results including on overflow. Fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.summary: Hoist the `j > 0` test out of the inner candidate loop by special-casing j==0.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.currentCost: The inner loop evaluates `calc(mid, j) + (j > 0 ? dp[j-1] : 0)` for every j in [start,end]; the `j > 0` ternary is checked every iteration even though it is false at most once (only when start==0).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.proposedChange: Compute the j==0 candidate (if start==0) once before the loop, then run the loop from `max(start,1)` to end with the unconditional body `calc(mid, j) + dp[j-1]`. Keeps best/bestPos tracking identical.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.rationale: Removes a per-iteration branch from the divide-and-conquer inner loop (total work O((r-l) * k) across recursion), improving the candidate loop's straight-line throughput and predictability.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.risk: Must preserve tie-breaking: original picks the first j achieving best (strict `<`). Evaluating j==0 first then iterating j>=1 keeps the same scan order and strict-less comparison, so bestPos ties resolve identically. Behavior preserved.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.summary: Tail-call / iterative conversion of one recursion arm to cap stack depth and avoid recursion overhead.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.currentCost: Two recursive self-calls per node; recursion depth is O(log(r-l)) which is fine, but each call has frame setup and the `delegate*` is passed by value each time. Burst supports recursion but deep call frames hurt mobile stack and inlining.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.proposedChange: Convert the second recursive call (`Recompute(dp, mid+1, r, bestPos, optR, k, calc)`) into a loop by reassigning l=mid+1, optL=bestPos and looping, keeping only the first arm recursive. Standard half-iterative D&C transform.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.rationale: Halves recursion frame count and shortens the call dependency chain; the delegate* and bounds stay in registers across the iterative arm instead of being re-marshalled per call. Lower stack pressure matters on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/O.risk: Must keep the first arm (l..mid-1) recursive and the second iterative to preserve the [optL,bestPos]/[bestPos,optR] monotonic-opt invariant. Pure refactor; outputs in dp[] are unchanged. Verify mid/optR recomputation order matches original.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.summary: Sift-down does two compares + possible swap per level; use a single-store hole/percolate to halve writes, and precompute child indices without redundant bounds work.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.currentCost: Each sift-down level performs up to 2 comparisons and a 3-assignment swap (`tmp; heap[idx]=...; heap[largest]=...`). With swaps, the moved-up element is written then potentially overwritten again next level, doubling memory writes along the path (O(log size) per pop, called once per AddAbsWithHeaps).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.proposedChange: Use the classic 'hole' technique: hold the displaced value in a register `long item = heap[size]` (after `size--`), walk down comparing children and writing only the larger child up into the hole each level, then write `item` once into the final hole. This replaces ~2 writes/level with 1 write/level plus one final store.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.rationale: Halves the store traffic along the sift path and removes the temp-swap dependency chain, improving the heap operation that sits in the AddAbsWithHeaps hot path. Same comparison count, fewer writes -> fewer dependent stores.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.risk: Must replicate exact comparison direction (`>` for max-heap, `<` for min-heap) and the `left<size`/`right<size` bounds so identical elements land in identical positions; heap is not a canonical structure but the resulting heap-order property and peek results are identical. Apply symmetrically to MinHeapPop.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.summary: Unused `size` parameter on MaxHeapPeek/MinHeapPeek widens the signature without benefit.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.currentCost: `MaxHeapPeek(long* heap, int size)` and `MinHeapPeek(long* heap, int size)` take a `size` they never use; it just returns heap[0]. Minor: an extra argument set up at each (inlined) call site and a misleading API.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.proposedChange: Drop the `size` parameter: `private static long MaxHeapPeek(long* heap) => heap[0];` (likewise MinHeapPeek). Update the two call sites in AdjustHeaps.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.rationale: Cleaner, honest signature; with AggressiveInlining the codegen is already heap[0], so this is purely API/ergonomics clarity with zero perf regression and a tiny chance of removing an arg-marshal if inlining ever fails.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.risk: None functionally; private method, two internal call sites. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.summary: Replace `idx * 2 + 1` / `idx * 2 + 2` with shift to express child index as a true shift+or.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.currentCost: Child index computed as `idx * 2 + 1` and `idx * 2 + 2`. A multiply-by-2 is typically lowered to a shift already, but writing it explicitly guarantees the cheap form and avoids any reliance on the optimizer for the +2 case.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.proposedChange: Use `int left = (idx << 1) + 1; int right = left + 1;` — compute right as left+1 instead of a second `idx*2+2`, saving the redundant shift/mul.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.rationale: Removes one shift/multiply per sift level by deriving right from left. Trivial but free; applies to both Pop functions.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/S.risk: Pure arithmetic identity (right = idx*2+2 = left+1). No overflow concern for realistic heap sizes (idx < int range/2). Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.summary: Precompute m*n once and guard against int overflow of the flattened index for large matrices.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.currentCost: `m * n - 1` is computed once (fine), but the search index `mid` is int; for m*n near or above 2^31 the multiply `m*n` overflows int silently. Not a perf issue but a correctness ceiling; also `lo + ((hi-lo)>>1)` is already optimal.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.proposedChange: Either document the m*n < 2^31 precondition explicitly (matching the 'Unchecked Run assumes valid input' convention) or, if large matrices are in scope, widen the index arithmetic to long for the bound while keeping the pointer offset computation correct. No change needed if precondition is acceptable.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.rationale: Avoids a latent silent-overflow correctness bug on very large flattened arrays; otherwise the binary search is already optimal (branchless-friendly, single load per step).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.risk: If m*n is guaranteed < 2^31 by caller contract, leave as-is — this is informational. Do not widen to long if it forces 64-bit index math on mobile where 32-bit indices are cheaper. State the precondition rather than changing code.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.summary: Maintain a running row-base pointer to avoid the `row * n` multiply each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.currentCost: Inner loop computes `a[row * n + col]` every step, doing a multiply `row*n` on each iteration even though row changes by at most +1 per loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.proposedChange: Track `int base = 0;` (= row*n) and update `base += n;` when incrementing row, indexing `a[base + col]`. Replaces a per-iteration multiply with an occasional add.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.rationale: Strength-reduces the multiply to an add along the staircase walk (O(m+n) iterations). Multiplies are cheap on PC but this removes a dependency on the multiplier unit per step, marginally better on mobile cores.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.DivideConquer/M.risk: base must update only on the row++ branch, not the col-- branch, to stay equal to row*n. Index a[base+col] equals a[row*n+col] exactly. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.summary: Skip masks whose bit 0 (start vertex) is unset; the start vertex 0 is the only valid DP base, so any subset not containing vertex 0 is dead state.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.currentCost: The outer loop iterates all 2^n masks and ProcessCycleMask scans all n last-vertices for each. Roughly half of all masks (those without bit 0) can never be reached from dp[(1<<0)*n+0]=0 yet are fully scanned.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.proposedChange: In ProcessCycleMask (or before calling it) skip masks with (mask & 1) == 0: `if ((mask & 1) == 0) continue;`. Equivalently iterate `for (int mask = 1; mask < size; mask += 2)` -- but a simple guard is cleaner and keeps the index meaning.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.rationale: Halves the number of (mask,last) inner scans. The Held-Karp DP only ever populates states whose mask includes the fixed start vertex 0, so masks without bit 0 contain only inf entries that fail the `dp[mask*n+last] >= inf` guard anyway -- pure wasted iteration of the inner n-loop and the branch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.risk: Must keep dp init for those masks as inf (it already is via the full init loop) and FindMinBestCycle uses fullMask which has bit 0 set, so unaffected. Semantics preserved exactly: skipped masks produce no transitions today either.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant base value dp[mask*n+last] and the row base w[last*n] out of the inner u-loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.currentCost: Each iteration recomputes mask*n+last for the dp read and last*n+u; dp[mask*n+last] is reloaded from memory n times though it is invariant across u.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.proposedChange: Add `long baseDp = dp[mask * n + last]; long* wRow = w + last * n; long* dpBase = dp;` before the loop, then use `wRow[u]` and `baseDp + wRow[u]`. Compute `int withU = mask | (1 << u);` once.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.rationale: Removes a redundant load and an index multiply from the hot inner loop, shortening the dependency chain. Burst/LLVM may already hoist the invariant load, but strengthening w into a row pointer removes the last*n multiply from every iteration deterministically.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.risk: None; dp[mask*n+last] is not written inside this loop (writes target (mask|bit)*n+u with the bit set, so a different slot), so the hoisted value stays valid.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.summary: Hoist invariant dp[mask*n+v] load and w[v*n] row base out of the inner u-loop, same as the cycle variant.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.currentCost: dp[mask*n+v] is reloaded n times though invariant; w[v*n+u] recomputes v*n each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.proposedChange: `long baseDp = dp[mask * n + v]; long* wRow = w + v * n;` before the loop; use `baseDp + wRow[u]` and `wRow[u] >= inf`.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.rationale: Shorter dependency chain and one fewer multiply per inner iteration in the dominant O(2^n * n^2) loop; deterministic invariant hoisting independent of optimizer.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/Hamiltoni.risk: None; the write target (mask|bit)*n+u differs from mask*n+v since bit u is newly set, so baseDp is not invalidated.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.summary: Only scan already-decided neighbors u < v instead of all n; used[u] is only ever 1 for u already processed in this DFS branch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.currentCost: CanIncludeNode loops u from 0..n-1 checking adj[v*n+u] && used[u]. But used[u] can only be set for u<v (DFS assigns in increasing v and resets on backtrack), so iterations u>=v always have used[u]==0 and are wasted work in the innermost hot check.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.proposedChange: Change the loop bound to `for (int u = 0; u < v; u++)` and use a row pointer `bool* row = adj + v * n;` with `row[u]`.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.rationale: Halves the average inner-loop length of the most-called leaf function in an exponential branch-and-bound, and removes the v*n multiply per iteration. used[u]!=0 implies u was included earlier, which only happens for u<v.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.risk: Relies on the invariant that used[] is zero for all indices >= v at the time CanIncludeNode(v) runs. This holds because Run zeroes nothing explicitly -- caller must pass used[] pre-zeroed (already assumed) and the DFS only sets used[v]=1 then resets to 0 on unwind, touching index v only. Safe given the increasing-v traversal. Add a comment documenting the invariant.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.summary: Add a bound to prune: if cur + (n - v) <= *best, the remaining vertices cannot beat best, so return early.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.currentCost: The search explores the full include/exclude binary tree of depth n with no upper-bound pruning, giving worst-case 2^n leaves even when best is already large.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.proposedChange: At the top of Search add `if (cur + (n - v) <= *best) return;` before the v==n check (or right after). This is an admissible bound: at most n-v more vertices can be added.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.rationale: Trivial branch that cuts entire subtrees once a good solution is found, often reducing the effective branching dramatically on dense graphs. Pure cycles/asymptotic win with no semantic change -- it only prunes branches that provably cannot improve *best.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.risk: None for correctness: cur+(n-v) is a true upper bound on the achievable set size in this subtree, so pruning when it cannot exceed *best preserves the optimum. Edge: when cur+(n-v)==*best pruning is correct since we need strictly greater (cur > *best) to update.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.summary: The depth and tmp parameters are entirely unused dead weight threaded through every recursive call.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.currentCost: depth and tmp are passed and incremented/forwarded on every recursion but never read; extra register/stack traffic and a misleading signature.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.proposedChange: Remove the `int depth` and `int* tmp` parameters from Search (and tmp from Run's signature if the public API allows, else keep Run signature and drop internally). Stop threading depth+1.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.rationale: Fewer arguments shorten the recursive call's prologue and reduce stack/register pressure in a hot exponential recursion; clearer API. The increment `depth+1` is also wasted ALU work per node.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaxIndepe.risk: tmp is part of the public Run signature; removing it there is a breaking API change -- only safe to drop internally from Search. depth removal is purely internal and safe.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.summary: The bound check `solSize + candSize <= *best` is duplicated: once in ShouldStop (called at entry) and again inside the while loop; and timer++ runs every node via a ref-passed counter.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.currentCost: ShouldStop is a non-inlined call at every Search entry doing timer++ plus the same bound the while-loop re-checks. The redundant bound costs an extra load of *best and compare per node.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.proposedChange: Mark ShouldStop with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] (the using is already imported). Optionally fold the entry bound into the existing while-loop guard `if (solSize + candSize <= *best) return 0;` which already runs first iteration, removing the duplicate compare at entry.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.rationale: Inlining removes call overhead on the hottest path of an exponential search; eliminating the duplicate *best load/compare shortens the per-node critical path. AggressiveInlining on hot leaf methods is exactly the prescribed pattern.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.risk: The timer cutoff (timer > 100000000) must still fire; if folding the bound, keep timer++ and the timer check intact. Note: candSize==0 path returns before the while loop, so the entry bound is needed only when candSize>0 -- which the while guard covers. Verify the candSize==0 success path is still reached before any bound return (it is: the `if (candSize == 0)` check precedes the loop).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.summary: RemoveCandidate does an O(candSize) linear search for v, but v is always currentTmp[0] (the just-processed pivot), so removal is O(1).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.currentCost: After processing, v was read as currentTmp[0]. RemoveCandidate then scans the whole array to find v and swap-with-last, an O(candSize) pass per node, redundantly re-locating a known position 0.
