src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.proposedChange: Since v == currentTmp[0] at the call site, replace RemoveCandidate's loop with `candSize--; currentTmp[0] = currentTmp[candSize];` (swap-remove index 0 with last). Pass the known index 0 instead of searching by value.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.rationale: Turns an O(k) removal into O(1), removing an entire linear pass per recursion node in an exponential algorithm -- a real asymptotic-per-node improvement of the maintenance cost.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.risk: Correctness hinges on v being exactly currentTmp[0] and unique. FilterNeighbors reads from currentTmp and writes to nextCand (cand), not modifying currentTmp, so currentTmp[0] is still v at removal time. Candidates are distinct vertex ids, so value v occurs once. Order of remaining candidates changes but the algorithm is order-insensitive (it just enumerates), so the visited set is identical. Safe.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.summary: Hoist the adjacency row base adj + v*n out of the loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.currentCost: adj[v*n + currentTmp[i]] recomputes v*n each iteration of the candidate-filter loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.proposedChange: `bool* row = adj + v * n;` before the loop, then `if (row[currentTmp[i]])`.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.rationale: Removes one multiply per inner iteration in a loop that runs for every recursion node; strengthens to a single base add + indexed load that Burst lowers cleanly.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.risk: None; adj is read-only and v is constant within the call.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.summary: The dp parameter is never read or written anywhere in the file -- it is pure dead weight threaded through every recursive call.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.currentCost: long* dp is passed to Run and forwarded through every Search recursion but never dereferenced; extra register/stack slot per recursive frame.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.proposedChange: Remove dp from Search's parameter list (and from Run if the public API can change). If Run's signature must stay stable for callers, at least stop forwarding it into Search.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.rationale: One fewer pointer argument per recursive call reduces prologue/spill cost in the hot exponential recursion and clarifies the contract. Confirmed unused by full-file read.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MaximumCl.risk: dp is in the public Run signature; dropping it there is a breaking change. Dropping from the private Search is safe and behavior-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.summary: Restrict the neighbor scan to already-colored vertices (u < v) when checking color legality.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.currentCost: CanUseColor scans all n vertices testing adj[v*n+u] && colors[u]==c, but colors[u] is -1 for all u>v (not yet assigned in this DFS path), so those iterations can never return false.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.proposedChange: Change loop to `for (int u = 0; u < v; u++)` with a hoisted row pointer `bool* row = adj + v*n;`. Vertices are colored in increasing index order, so only u<v have a non-negative color.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.rationale: Halves the average scan length of this per-candidate-color check and drops the v*n multiply per iteration; this is called once per (vertex,candidate color) in an exponential branch-and-bound.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.risk: Depends on the invariant that vertices are assigned colors strictly in increasing index order (Search advances v -> v+1, and colors[v] is set to -1 initially and reset on backtrack). Holds in this code. If a future caller seeds colors out of order this breaks -- document the invariant.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.summary: Hoist row/column base offsets (v*n) out of the per-u loops in TryNewColor and UpdateSaturation.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.currentCost: TryNewColor's loop computes both v*n+u and u*n+v each iteration (one multiply each, two total); UpdateSaturation recomputes v*n+u and u*n+c per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.proposedChange: In TryNewColor: `int* satRow = sat + v*n;` for the v*n+u term; the u*n+v term still needs per-u u*n but can be carried as a running pointer `sat + v` advanced by n. In UpdateSaturation: `bool* adjRow = adj + v*n;`.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.rationale: Removes redundant index multiplies from the saturation bookkeeping that runs on every color try/backtrack; strided pointer walks are Burst-vectorizer friendly.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/GraphColo.risk: The u*n+v access pattern is column-strided; converting to a pointer incremented by n per step is equivalent. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.summary: The submask enumeration loop has dead branches and iterates every (sub, other) ordered pair, doing twice the necessary work.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.currentCost: while-loop at lines 21-28 contains two provably-dead branches: 'if (sub == mask)' can never fire because sub starts at (mask-1)&mask which is strictly < mask, and 'if (sub == 0) break' is unreachable because the loop condition '> 0' already excludes 0. Worse, it visits all proper non-empty submasks sub, so each unordered split {sub, mask^sub} is processed twice (once as sub, once as other), doubling the inner work.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.proposedChange: Drop both dead branches. Iterate only the canonical half of splits, e.g. enumerate sub over proper submasks but only process when sub < (mask ^ sub) (or sub <= mask^sub for the symmetric case), halving the dp[sub*n+v]+dp[other*n+v] evaluations. Loop becomes: 'int sub=(mask-1)&mask; while(sub>0){ int other=mask^sub; if(sub<other){ long cand=dp[sub*n+v]+dp[other*n+v]; if(cand<best)best=cand;} sub=(sub-1)&mask; }'
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.rationale: Removes 2 unpredictable branches per iteration and halves the number of dp loads/adds/compares in the inner split loop. The cand for {sub,other} equals cand for {other,sub}, so skipping one is semantics-preserving; best is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.risk: None: the two removed branches are provably unreachable, and add is commutative so dp[sub]+dp[other]==dp[other]+dp[sub]. Must guard with sub<other (not <=) only if every split has sub!=other, which holds because mask has >=2 bits here (singletons are 'continue'd at line 16), so sub==other would require sub==mask^sub, impossible for a partition of a >=2-bit mask.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.summary: The O(n^3) two-edge relaxation per mask is an order of n more work than the standard Dreyfus-Wagner single-source relaxation needs.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.currentCost: For each of 2^m masks, the i/j/k triple loop (lines 31-43) costs n^3 multiply-add-compare with 3 inf-checks, giving total O(2^m * n^3). It relaxes dp[mask][k] via two graph edges i->j->k, but standard DW only needs a single-source shortest-path relaxation (Dijkstra/Bellman) over the contracted dp[mask][*] as sources, which is O(2^m * n^2) on a dense graph.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.proposedChange: Replace the i,j,k triple loop with a single-edge relaxation: treat dp[mask*n+v] as initial distances and run one round of all-pairs single-edge relaxation to fixpoint (Bellman over dense matrix is O(n^2) per pass, O(n^2) passes worst case, but for the metric closure precompute all-pairs shortest paths apsp[i][k] ONCE via Floyd-Warshall outside the mask loop, then inner step is dp[mask*n+k]=min over i of dp[mask*n+i]+apsp[i*n+k], which is O(n^2) per mask).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.rationale: Precomputing the metric closure apsp once (O(n^3) total, not per-mask) collapses the per-mask merge from O(n^3) to O(n^2), reducing the dominant term from 2^m*n^3 to n^3 + 2^m*n^2 — an n-fold asymptotic win for the hot exponential loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.risk: Must verify the current two-edge form was not intentionally limited to paths of exactly <=2 edges; for shortest-path Steiner it should be the full closure, so using apsp is the correct (and equivalent-or-better) relaxation. Provide w as already-closed metric, or compute closure once. Keep inf-saturating adds to avoid long overflow (inf+w must not wrap).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.summary: (1<<m) and (1<<m)*n are recomputed in loop bounds and the init pass; hoist them.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.currentCost: Line 9 computes (1<<m)*n inside the loop condition each iteration; line 14 recomputes (1<<m) each mask-loop test. These are cheap shifts but re-evaluated every iteration of large loops.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.proposedChange: Hoist 'int full = 1 << m;' and 'int dpLen = full * n;' once at the top; use them in the init loop bound, the mask loop bound, and the final return index '((full-1)*n)'.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.rationale: Eliminates a redundant shift+multiply from each iteration of the 2^m*n init loop and each mask-loop condition; lets Burst keep the bound in a register and reason about loop trip count.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.risk: None; m is constant within the call so 1<<m is loop-invariant.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.summary: The d1!=inf && w1!=inf && w2!=inf triple guard adds three branches per innermost iteration to avoid overflow; a saturating/clamped add or single combined check is cheaper.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.currentCost: Innermost i,j,k body (lines 38-42) evaluates up to three branch conditions before the actual add/compare, on the hottest loop in the file (2^m*n^3 iterations).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.proposedChange: If inf is chosen with headroom (e.g. inf <= long.MaxValue/4), drop the per-term inf guards and instead clamp: 'long cand = d1 + w1 + w2;' then compare 'cand < dp[...]' — since any path through an inf edge yields >= inf and won't beat a real value. Alternatively hoist the d1!=inf check out of the j,k loops (it's invariant in j and k).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.rationale: Removes two/three branch evaluations from the innermost loop; if guards are kept, hoisting 'd1 != inf' (invariant over j,k) out of the inner two loops removes one compare from n^2 iterations per i.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/SteinerDr.risk: Saturating-add variant requires inf to have sufficient headroom against long overflow; state that explicitly. The hoist of d1!=inf is unconditionally safe and semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.summary: Domination is tracked with int counts over a bool adjacency matrix scanned row-by-row; using ulong bitmask closed-neighborhoods collapses the inner O(n) neighbor loops to O(n/64) and makes the final all-dominated check O(1).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.currentCost: Each branch where a vertex is chosen scans the full adjacency row twice (lines 32-33 and 36-37), O(n) increments/decrements per node added/removed, plus the leaf check (lines 20-21) scans all n dom[] counts. Over a backtracking tree this is the dominant cost.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.proposedChange: Precompute per-vertex closed-neighborhood bitmasks N[v] (ulong[ceil(n/64)] per vertex, or a single ulong when n<=64). Represent the dominated set as a bitset 'dominated'. Choosing v sets dominated |= N[v]; the leaf test becomes popcount(dominated)==n (or dominated==full). Backtracking needs the previous dominated value saved on the recursion stack instead of decrementing counts.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.rationale: Replaces two O(n) row scans and an O(n) leaf scan with O(n/64) OR operations and an O(1) full-mask compare, an up-to-64x constant-factor reduction on the hottest path; bitset ops are branch-free and Burst-vectorizable.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.risk: Counts allow per-vertex domination multiplicity (dom[u] can exceed 1) but only the >0 predicate is ever observed (lines 21,26), so a boolean/bitset is behaviorally equivalent. Backtracking must restore the saved prior bitset rather than subtract; store it in a local (stack) per recursion frame. For n>64 use a small fixed ulong array and stackalloc/scratch — keep it unmanaged.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.summary: Bound pruning is missing: search recurses to idx==n before testing 'used < *best', exploring branches that cannot improve the incumbent.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.currentCost: The 'used < *best' comparison only happens at the leaf (line 22). Branches that have already used >= *best vertices keep recursing pointlessly through the full O(n) row updates at each level.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.proposedChange: Add an early cutoff at the top of Search: 'if (used >= *best) return;' (mirrors the pattern already used in MinSetCover.Search line 23). Optionally also prune when used+1 >= *best before taking the 'include v' branch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.rationale: Prunes entire subtrees of the backtracking tree, each of which would otherwise perform O(n) work per level — a real reduction in explored nodes, not just a constant factor.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.risk: Semantics-preserving: any leaf reachable from a node with used>=*best would set *best only if used<*best, which is already impossible, so pruning cannot discard an improving solution.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.summary: adj[vi2 * n + u] base offset (vi2*n) is recomputed each iteration of both neighbor loops.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.currentCost: Lines 32-33 and 36-37 index adj[vi2*n+u] inside the loop; the multiply vi2*n is loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.proposedChange: Hoist 'bool* row = adj + vi2 * n;' once before each loop and index row[u]. (Moot if the bitset rewrite above is adopted.)
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.rationale: Removes a multiply from each of n iterations; gives Burst a clean linear pointer walk that vectorizes better.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinDomina.risk: None; vi2 and n are invariant across the loop.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.summary: covCount==remain only succeeds when ALL elements are covered, but remain is total element-occurrences (with multiplicity) while covCount counts distinct newly-covered — the universe size is the real target and should be precomputed, and set-membership should use bitmasks for O(1) cover/uncover.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.currentCost: CoverSet/UncoverSet iterate every element of a set (O(setSize)) on every recursive visit, and covered[] is an int multiplicity array. The termination 'covCount == remain' uses 'remain' = sum of set sizes (line 9, total), which only equals the number of distinct universe elements when sets are disjoint — for overlapping sets covCount (distinct) can never reach remain (with-multiplicity), so the exact-cover shortcut at line 24 may never trigger and the search degrades to full enumeration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.proposedChange: Compute the universe size U = number of distinct elements once, and terminate when covCount==U. Represent covered as a ulong bitset (when |universe|<=64) so CoverSet is 'added = popcount(setMask & ~covered); covered |= setMask' and UncoverSet restores a saved mask — O(1) instead of O(setSize).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.rationale: Fixes a likely-missed termination (correctness/perf: search currently can't early-exit on overlapping inputs) and replaces per-element O(setSize) scans with single-word bitset ops; the saved-mask restore removes the second full element scan in UncoverSet.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.risk: Confirm intended semantics of 'remain': if the library contractually requires disjoint sets then current code is correct and only the bitset speedup applies; otherwise using distinct-universe-size U is the correct target. Bitset form requires elem ids < 64 (or a small ulong array for larger universes) — keep unmanaged via stackalloc/caller buffer.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.summary: setSizes[i] is reloaded as the loop bound on every iteration, and sets[i] base pointer is re-derived.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.currentCost: Line 42 'j < setSizes[i]' reloads setSizes[i] each iteration; sets[i][j] re-derives the inner pointer per access.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.proposedChange: Hoist 'int sz = setSizes[i];' and 'int* s = sets[i];' before each loop; iterate j<sz over s[j]. Apply in both CoverSet and UncoverSet.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.rationale: Removes a dependent load from the loop condition and a pointer indirection per element, enabling Burst to treat s as a flat array for vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/MinSetCov.risk: None; setSizes[i] and sets[i] are invariant within the call.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.summary: Dist recomputes sqrt of integer-truncated Euclidean distances repeatedly; the same pair distances are recomputed across the DP and can be precomputed once, and Dist should be AggressiveInlined.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.currentCost: Dist does a double subtract, two mults, an add, a sqrt and a (long) truncation. It is called inside the i,j,k DP (the k-loop at lines 30-37 calls Dist(k->i) for every k each time j==i-1, i.e. O(n^2) sqrt total) and again at line 43. sqrt is ~15-40 cycles and dominates.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.proposedChange: Precompute a lower-triangular (or full) distance matrix 'long* d = ...; d[a*n+b]=Dist(...)' once at the start of Run (O(n^2) sqrts), then index d[k*n+i], d[(i-1)*n+i], d[0*n+(n-1)] instead of recomputing. Also add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] to Dist (the using is already imported).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.rationale: The DP body re-evaluates Dist for the same coordinate pairs across iterations; caching makes each distance computed exactly once, turning O(n^2)+ sqrt calls into O(n^2) total with the DP doing pure long loads. AggressiveInlining removes call overhead and lets Burst hoist the sqrt.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.risk: None for correctness: distances are pure functions of coordinates. Extra O(n^2) long buffer (8 bytes/pair) — acceptable given dp is already O(n^2); the caller must supply the scratch (house style passes buffers in). Truncation order is unchanged since each pair is truncated identically.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.summary: Dist(xs[i-1],ys[i-1],xs[i],ys[i]) at line 43 is invariant in j but recomputed for every j in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.currentCost: For each i, the else branch (j != i-1) at line 43 recomputes the same Dist(i-1, i) for every j from 0..i-2 — O(n) redundant sqrt per i, O(n^2) total redundant sqrts.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.proposedChange: Hoist 'long step = Dist(xs[i-1],ys[i-1],xs[i],ys[i]);' once per i (before the j loop) and use it in line 43. (Subsumed if the full distance matrix from the previous item is adopted.)
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.rationale: Removes O(n^2) redundant sqrt evaluations from the DP — sqrt is the most expensive op in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.risk: None; the value depends only on i, not j.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.summary: long.MaxValue sentinel arithmetic (prev + Dist) risks overflow and forces per-cell !=MaxValue branches; row-base offsets j*n and i*n are recomputed.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.currentCost: Init loop fills dp with long.MaxValue; lines 41-43 add Dist to prev guarded by !=MaxValue. Indexing dp[j*n+i] and dp[i*n+j] recomputes j*n / i*n each access.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.proposedChange: Hoist row bases ('long* rowI = dp + i*n;') and reuse; keep the !=MaxValue guard (it prevents overflow of MaxValue+Dist, so it is load-bearing and must NOT be removed). Optionally use a named INF < MaxValue/2 sentinel to make the guard's overflow intent explicit and allow saturating compares.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.rationale: Removes repeated index multiplies; documents that the MaxValue guard exists to avoid signed overflow.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspBitoni.risk: Do NOT drop the !=MaxValue checks — long.MaxValue + Dist overflows to negative and would corrupt the min. Changing the sentinel to INF<MaxValue/2 is safe only if all real distances stay below INF.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.summary: Replace the per-mask popcount loop (lines 19-21) with the branchless bit-count idiom / intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.currentCost: For every mask (up to 2^half iterations), an inner loop of `half` iterations does `(mask & (1<<b)) != 0` test-and-increment to compute `bits`. That is O(half) per mask, with a 1<<b shift, an AND, and a data-dependent branch each step. Over all masks this is O(half * 2^half) just to count bits.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.proposedChange: Use a hardware popcount: `int bits = System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount((uint)mask);`. Burst lowers PopCount to a single POPCNT/equivalent instruction. If BitOperations is undesirable under the house pointer rules, use the SWAR popcount (5 ops, branchless) instead of the loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.rationale: Collapses an O(half) branch-laden inner loop to a single (or ~5) branchless instruction(s), removing a data-dependent branch in the hottest loop and shrinking the dependency chain from `half` serial adds to a log-depth or single-op reduction.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.risk: Semantics identical (popcount of a non-negative int). `mask` is in [1, 2^half), always fits in uint with no sign issue. BitOperations.PopCount is a static intrinsic with no managed allocation, Burst-friendly; confirm Burst version supports it, otherwise fall back to SWAR.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.summary: Hoist the repeated `left[sub * half + j]` and `left[mask * half + i]` index computations out of the inner loop / cache the loaded value.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.currentCost: Inside the j-loop, `left[sub * half + j]` is computed and loaded twice (lines 28 and 30) for the same j, and `left[mask * half + i]` is recomputed at line 31 every iteration though `mask`, `half`, `i` are loop-invariant. Each is an imul + add for the address plus a load.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.proposedChange: Compute `long* maskRow = left + mask * half;` and `long* subRow = left + sub * half;` once before the j-loop. Then `long cur = subRow[j];` loaded once, and update `maskRow[i]`. Hoist `long best = maskRow[i];` before the loop, take the min into the register, and store `maskRow[i] = best;` once after the loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.rationale: Removes a redundant load of subRow[j], eliminates per-iteration recomputation of the invariant `mask*half+i` address, and turns a load-modify-store on maskRow[i] into a single register min reduction with one final store — shorter dependency chain and fewer memory ops in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.risk: Semantics-preserving: maskRow[i] is only written within this j-loop for this mask, so accumulating the min in a register and storing once is equivalent. inf-sentinel comparisons are unchanged (still `< best`). No overflow concern beyond what already exists.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.summary: Replace `n / 2` and `mask ^ (1 << i)` invariants and precompute bit masks; iterate set bits via bit-tricks instead of scanning all `half` positions.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.currentCost: The j-loop (lines 24-26) scans all `half` positions and `continue`s on the ~half that are zero in `sub`, wasting iterations and branching on `(sub & (1<<j)) == 0`. `1 << j` and `1 << i` are recomputed.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.proposedChange: Iterate only set bits: `for (int s = sub; s != 0; s &= s - 1) { int j = BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(s); ... }`. This visits exactly popcount(sub) positions with no skipped/branched iterations and no `1<<j` reconstruction for the membership test.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.rationale: Reduces inner-loop trip count from `half` to popcount(sub) and removes the per-position membership branch (`s & (s-1)` clears the lowest set bit branchlessly). Fewer iterations, fewer mispredicts, shorter shifts.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.risk: Behavior identical — same set of j values processed. TrailingZeroCount/`s & (s-1)` are well-defined for the non-zero `s` here. Burst-friendly intrinsics; if unavailable, the `s &= s-1` walk with a manual ctz is still branch-light. Note: the surrounding result is currently discarded (Run returns inf), so this optimizes dead computation only.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.summary: The entire `left` DP (lines 12-34) is dead: Run unconditionally returns `inf`, so the O(half * 2^half) computation and its O(half * 2^half) stackalloc init can be removed without changing observable output.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.currentCost: Allocates `maxMask*half` longs on the stack (up to 2^10 * 10 = ~10240 longs = ~80 KB for half=10) and initializes them to inf, then runs a full subset DP — all of which is discarded because the method returns `inf` at line 35, never the computed table.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.proposedChange: As an optimization (not a feature fix): since observable output is `inf` for all n>2 and `0` for n<=2, the whole body for `n<=20` is unnecessary; `Run` reduces to `return n <= 2 ? 0 : inf;`. This eliminates the ~80 KB stackalloc (a real mobile stack-pressure concern) and the dominant DP loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.rationale: Removing provably-dead work is the ultimate strength reduction: zero cycles, zero RAM. The large stackalloc on `half=10` is a genuine mobile stack risk for no benefit.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.risk: This is only safe if the method is genuinely intended to return inf (i.e., the DP is incomplete/unused). It almost certainly indicates an unfinished implementation that SHOULD return the tour cost — so this 'optimization' would lock in a bug. Flag for the author: the DP result must be wired into the return before any of the cycle/ram micro-opts above matter. Do NOT apply blindly.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.summary: Initialization loop (line 15) fills the whole table with inf then immediately overwrites left[0]=0; fine, but the fill can use a wider/vectorizable pattern and the table size can use narrower addressing.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.currentCost: Scalar loop writes `maxMask*half` longs one-by-one with `left[i] = inf`. Burst may auto-vectorize, but the explicit scalar form plus the `maxMask*half` recomputed bound (line 15 vs line 14) is a missed hoist.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.proposedChange: Hoist `int total = maxMask * half;` once and reuse for both the stackalloc and the fill bound. Keep the fill as a simple `for` over `total` (Burst vectorizes a constant-store loop well), avoiding the duplicated multiply.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.rationale: Removes a duplicated imul and gives Burst a clean constant-store loop to vectorize (wide SIMD stores of the inf pattern). Minor but free.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Exact/TspMeetIn.risk: Semantics identical. Only meaningful if the DP body is kept (see the dead-code finding); if the body is removed, this disappears.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant reward term out of the innermost sp-loop in the Q-value accumulation.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.currentCost: The innermost loop `q += trans[...] * (reward[s*m+a] + gamma * v[sp])` recomputes `reward[s*m+a]` (an index multiply-add + load) on every one of n iterations, and folds reward into every term so it cannot be factored. This is n*m*n*iters iterations, the dominant cost. Each iteration does an extra add and the reward expression mixes a per-(s,a) constant into the dot product.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.proposedChange: Split the sum: compute `double dot = 0; for(sp) dot += trans[base + sp] * v[sp];` then `double q = reward[s*m+a] * transSum + gamma_dot` — more precisely `q = sum_sp(trans*reward) + gamma*sum_sp(trans*v)`. Since reward is constant over sp, `q = reward[s*m+a]*(sum_sp trans) + gamma*(sum_sp trans*v)`. Precompute `rsa = reward[s*m+a]` once per (s,a), and let `tbase = s*m*n + a*n`. Then inner loop is `dot += trans[tbase+sp]*v[sp]` and after loop `q = rsa*rowSum + gamma*dot`. If transition rows are stochastic (sum to 1, the MDP convention), rowSum==1 and q = rsa + gamma*dot, removing reward from the hot loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.rationale: Removes a per-iteration load and add from the n*m*n*iters hot loop, shortens the FMA dependency chain (pure trans*v accumulation vectorizes/FMAs cleanly under Burst), and hoists the reward load to the (s,a) level (n*m*iters). With the stochastic-row assumption it also removes a multiply.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.risk: Strict factoring `reward*rowSum + gamma*dot` is algebraically identical in real arithmetic but floating-point addition reordering changes rounding, so bitwise-identical output is not guaranteed; observable behavior changes only at ULP level. The rowSum==1 simplification additionally assumes rows are probability distributions — only valid if that is a documented precondition; otherwise keep the explicit `rsa*rowSum` form (compute rowSum in the same pass).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.summary: Eliminate the separate copy-back pass `for(s) v[s]=newV[s]` by double-buffering with a pointer swap.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.currentCost: After each iteration an extra O(n) pass copies newV into v, costing n*iters loads+stores plus a full extra memory sweep that evicts cache.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.proposedChange: Read into `cur` and write into `nxt`, then swap the two pointers at the end of each iteration instead of copying: `double* tmp = v; v = newV; newV = tmp;`. After the loop, if `iters` is odd the result lives in the other buffer — either require even-iteration semantics or copy once at the very end. Both v and newV are caller-provided scratch of equal size, so swapping is safe.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.rationale: Replaces iters full O(n) copy passes with a single pointer swap (constant). Reduces total memory traffic and cache pressure in the outer loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.risk: After the loop the final values may reside in the `newV` buffer rather than `v` depending on parity of iters; caller currently expects results in `v`. Needs a single final conditional copy when (iters & 1)==1 to preserve the observable contract.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.summary: Hoist reward out of both inner sp-loops and precompute the (s,a) base index, same as ValueIteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.currentCost: Both the evaluation loop (line 41) and the improvement loop (line 53) recompute `reward[s*m+a]` and the flat index `s*m*n + a*n + sp` inside the innermost sp-loop, adding redundant index arithmetic and a load per iteration across the policy-iteration sweeps.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.proposedChange: Per (s,a) compute `long rsa=reward[s*m+a]` (double) and `tbase=s*m*n+a*n` once, then inner loop accumulates `dot += trans[tbase+sp]*v[sp]` and forms `q = rsa*rowSum + gamma*dot` (or `rsa + gamma*dot` under the stochastic-row precondition). Apply identically in the evaluation pass where a=policy[s].
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.rationale: Cuts a load and a multiply-add from the hot dot-product loops and strength-reduces the index computation to a single base + sp add, which Burst lowers to contiguous loads it can vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Mdp.cs.risk: Same floating-point reassociation caveat as ValueIteration: identical in exact arithmetic, may differ at ULP. rowSum==1 shortcut only valid if rows are guaranteed stochastic.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.summary: Replace the magic literal stride 10 with a named constant and pass it as a parameter, and hoist counts[i] out of the inner loop bound.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.currentCost: `moves[i * 10 + j]` hardcodes the per-state move stride as the literal 10, which is an undocumented coupling between caller layout and this function (ergonomics/correctness hazard). `counts[i]` is reloaded as the loop bound on every j iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.proposedChange: Introduce `const int MovesStride = 10;` (or better, add an `int stride` parameter so the layout is explicit), and cache `int c = counts[i]; int rowBase = i * MovesStride;` before the j-loop so the bound and base are loaded once. Inner: `scratch[j] = g[moves[rowBase + j]];`.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.rationale: Named constant removes a silent magic number and the brittle assumption; hoisting counts[i] and the row base removes a redundant load and a multiply per inner iteration. Pure constant-factor and clarity win with no behavior change.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.risk: None for the hoist (counts[i] and i*10 are invariant across j). Adding a stride parameter is a signature change (ergonomics) — if avoided, the named-constant + hoist alone is fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.summary: The clear loop and the membership test can use a bitset to shrink the stackalloc and let the compiler vectorize the clear.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.currentCost: `stackalloc bool[n+1]` plus an explicit `for(i<=n) seen[i]=false` byte-by-byte clear. For large n this is n+1 bytes of stack and an n+1 store loop before any useful work.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.proposedChange: Keep bool[] for small n (current code is fine), but for the clear specifically prefer `Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(seen, 0, (uint)(n+1))` to zero the buffer in one vectorized memset instead of a scalar per-byte loop. Optionally pack into `ulong` words ((n>>6)+1 longs) and clear with a short word loop — 8x fewer stores and the final scan tests 64 candidates per load via `~word` bit-scan.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.rationale: InitBlock lowers to a vectorized fill (fewer cycles than the scalar loop); the bitset variant cuts stack footprint 8x and lets the missing-value scan skip 64 present values per word with a trailing-zero-count, improving the common dense case.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Grundy.cs.risk: Bitset version changes index math (word = v>>6, bit = v&63) and the final scan logic — must preserve the exact 'smallest non-negative int in [0,n] not present, else n+1' semantics and the `0<=v<=n` guard. InitBlock alone is a drop-in with no semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MeanPayof.summary: Branchless / fused relaxation and early-exit are fine, but the final feasibility check repeats the relaxation expression; compute potential[v]+w[e] once.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MeanPayof.currentCost: In the relax loop `potential[v] + w[e]` is computed into nxt (good). In the final check loop (line 30) `potential[v] + w[e]` is recomputed inline; minor. More importantly each edge does two array index loads for from/to every Bellman-Ford pass (n*m total).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MeanPayof.proposedChange: This is textbook Bellman-Ford and largely optimal. The only real win: there is no need to special-case — the structure is already tight. If `from`/`to`/`w` are frequently co-iterated, consider a struct-of-arrays-to-AoS packed edge `{int from; int to; long w;}` so each edge is one cache line load instead of three separate streams, improving locality across the n passes.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MeanPayof.rationale: Packing the three parallel arrays into one contiguous edge array turns three independent strided loads per edge into one sequential load, cutting cache misses across the O(n*m) relaxation. The repeated final-check expression is negligible.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MeanPayof.risk: Changing the parameter layout from three pointers to one packed pointer is an API/ergonomics change and requires the caller to build the AoS buffer; only worth it if callers can adopt it. Behavior is identical. Without the layout change, the function is already near-optimal — report as low-priority.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.summary: The min-mean-cycle comparison `cycle < minCycle * len` is both a correctness hazard (overflow) and does integer division per candidate; the algorithm also relabels via a non-standard test.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.currentCost: `if (cycle < minCycle * len)` multiplies minCycle by len (line 68) and then `minCycle = cycle / len` divides (line 69). `minCycle` starts at long.MaxValue, so `minCycle * len` overflows for any len>1 on the first candidate, producing undefined ordering. The per-candidate `cycle / len` is also a 64-bit integer division (tens of cycles) inside the edge loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.proposedChange: Compare ratios without overflow by cross-multiplying with the running best stored as a fraction (bestNum/bestDen): replace `cycle < minCycle*len` with `cycle * bestDen < bestNum * len` using __int128-style widening or a guard `len>0 && bestDen>0`, and seed best lazily on the first valid candidate instead of long.MaxValue. Defer the single division to the very end (compute minCycle = bestNum/bestDen once after the loop). This removes the per-candidate division and the overflowing multiply.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.rationale: Eliminates a 64-bit idiv from the O(m) candidate loop and removes the long.MaxValue*len overflow that can corrupt the result, while keeping one final division. Fewer cycles and actually correct.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.risk: This touches correctness: the current `minCycle*len` overflow means the existing output is already wrong for the general case, so 'semantics-preserving' here means preserving the INTENDED min-mean-cycle value, not the buggy one. Cross-multiplication needs an overflow-safe widening (cycle and bestNum can be large); guard len>0 and handle the no-cycle sentinel (return long.MaxValue when no candidate found). Flag this for a correctness review, not a blind micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.summary: dist/cnt init loop can use InitBlock, and the dist array is never seeded to +inf so all-zero init is intentional (Karp); fine, but the clear can vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.currentCost: `for(i<n){dist[i]=0;cnt[i]=0;}` is a scalar two-store loop over n.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.proposedChange: Zero both buffers with `Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(dist,0,(uint)(n*sizeof(long)))` and likewise for cnt, replacing the scalar loop with a vectorized memset.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.rationale: One vectorized fill instead of n scalar iterations; trivial but free cycle reduction at setup.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.risk: None — zeroing long/int buffers via InitBlock is bit-identical to assigning 0. Only valid because the intended init value is 0 (which it is).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.summary: Cache w[inEdge[v]] to avoid a double indirect load in the relaxation comparison.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.currentCost: `if (inEdge[v] < 0 || w[e] < w[inEdge[v]])` performs two dependent loads (inEdge[v] then w[inEdge[v]]) per edge in the selection loop. The same indirect load recurs.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.proposedChange: Maintain a parallel `long* bestW = stackalloc long[n]` initialized to a sentinel, so the comparison is `inEdge[v] < 0 || w[e] < bestW[v]` (one direct load) and update bestW[v]=w[e] alongside inEdge[v]=e. The summation loop then reads bestW[v] directly instead of w[inEdge[v]].
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.rationale: Removes a level of pointer indirection (the dependent w[inEdge[v]] load) from the per-edge comparison and from the final sum, shortening the load dependency chain at the cost of n longs of scratch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/MinCostFl.risk: Adds n*8 bytes of stack. Behavior identical provided bestW is kept perfectly in sync with inEdge and the no-incoming-edge case (inEdge[v]<0) still returns long.MaxValue. Note this is a simplified arborescence (no contraction of cycles, just min-incoming-edge per vertex) — the opt does not change that semantics, correct or not.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.summary: Replace the O(V*E) edge rescan in the BFS loop with a precomputed reverse (predecessor) adjacency list to get O(V+E).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.currentCost: For every dequeued vertex v (up to n times), the inner `for (int e=0;e<m;e++)` scans ALL m edges and skips those where to[e]!=v. Total work is O(n*m). On a graph with thousands of states/edges this is quadratic and dominates runtime; nearly all of the m iterations per dequeue are wasted `if (to[e]!=v) continue;` branches.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.proposedChange: Build a CSR-style reverse adjacency from the `to` array using stackalloc: int* outdeg=stackalloc int[n] counting how many edges point INTO each node (i.e. group edges by to[e]); int* radjStart=stackalloc int[n+1] as prefix sums; int* radjFrom=stackalloc int[m] holding the from[] endpoints bucketed by to[]. Also compute indeg[u] = number of outgoing edges of u (count of edges with from[e]==u) in the same first pass. Then in the BFS, replace the inner edge scan with: for (int k=radjStart[v]; k<radjStart[v+1]; k++) { int u=radjFrom[k]; if (win[u]) continue; if (--indeg[u]==0){ win[u]=true; q[tail++]=u; } }. This visits each edge exactly once across the whole BFS.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.rationale: Retrograde analysis is linear in V+E. The current code recomputes the predecessor set of v by full scan on every pop, turning a linear algorithm quadratic. Bucketing edges once (two O(m) passes for counts + fill, O(n) prefix sum) removes the inner rescan entirely, cutting asymptotics from O(V*E) to O(V+E) and eliminating the per-edge mispredicted branch `to[e]!=v`.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.risk: Semantics preserved: the original indeg[] counts edges INTO each node (indeg[to[e]]++) but the BFS decrements indeg[u] where u=from[e] for edges entering v — so the original 'indeg' is actually used as the count of OUTGOING edges of u that have not yet been resolved. Must preserve that exact meaning: initialize the decremented counter as out-degree of u (number of edges with from[e]==u), NOT in-degree. Re-read the original carefully: original indeg[to[e]]++ counts in-degree, but it decrements indeg[from[e]]; this is a latent inconsistency in the original. To preserve OBSERVABLE behavior exactly, replicate the original counter semantics bit-for-bit (count via indeg[to[e]]++ and decrement indeg[from[e]]) while only changing HOW predecessors are enumerated. Extra stackalloc of ~ (2n+1+m) ints raises stack usage; for large n,m a caller-provided scratch buffer may be needed to avoid stack overflow.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.summary: Use a single combined stackalloc / memset instead of separate per-element zeroing loop for indeg.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.currentCost: `for (int i=0;i<n;i++) indeg[i]=0;` is a scalar zeroing loop. stackalloc int[n] is not guaranteed zero-initialized so the loop is needed, but a manual scalar loop is slower than a bulk clear and Burst may not always vectorize it.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.proposedChange: Replace the zeroing loop with Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(indeg, 0, (uint)(n*sizeof(int))) (or memset-equivalent) which Burst lowers to a vectorized/optimized clear. Same for the q buffer only the used prefix matters so it needs no clear.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.rationale: A bulk block-clear is a single intrinsic the JIT/Burst turns into wide SIMD stores, reducing the loop's instruction count and dependency chain versus n scalar stores. Fewer cycles on the setup phase.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Retrograd.risk: InitBlockUnaligned is unmanaged-safe and Burst-compatible. Must ensure n>0 before calling (n*sizeof(int) must not overflow uint for huge n — guard if n can exceed ~536M, otherwise safe).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.summary: Replace the scalar tableau zeroing loop with a bulk block-clear.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.currentCost: `for (int i=0;i<rows*cols;i++) tab[i]=0;` zeroes the entire (m+2)*(n+m+2) tableau scalar-by-scalar of doubles. For a 50x50 problem that is ~2700 scalar stores before any real work.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.proposedChange: Use Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(tab, 0, (uint)(rows*cols*sizeof(double))) to clear in one vectorized pass.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.rationale: A single block-clear intrinsic is lowered to wide SIMD stores by Burst, far fewer instructions and a shorter dependency chain than rows*cols scalar zero stores.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.risk: Burst- and unmanaged-safe. Guard against rows*cols*8 overflowing uint only for pathologically huge tableaus; for normal LP sizes it is safe.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.summary: Strength-reduce division to a single reciprocal multiply, hoist the pivot-row base pointer, and skip near-zero pivot factors.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.currentCost: `tab[r*cols+j] /= v` performs a double division for every j (cols divisions per pivot). Division is ~20-40x the latency of multiply. The inner elimination loop recomputes `tab[r*cols+j]` (the normalized pivot row) for every non-pivot row i, re-indexing r*cols each time, and runs the full subtract even when f==0.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.proposedChange: Compute double inv = 1.0/v once; then in the normalize loop do tab[r*cols+j]*=inv. Hoist `double* prow = tab + r*cols;` and `double* row_i = tab + i*cols;` to base pointers so indexing is a single add, not a multiply, per element. In the elimination loop add `if (f==0.0 || (f<eps && f>-eps)) continue;` to skip rows whose pivot-column entry is already zero (common in sparse-ish tableaus), avoiding cols multiply-subtracts. Iterate j over the pointer directly.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.rationale: One reciprocal + cols multiplies replaces cols divisions: division latency is dominant, so this is a large win in the hottest routine (Pivot runs once per simplex iteration over the whole tableau). Hoisting the row base pointer removes a multiply per element and shortens the address dependency chain, enabling Burst to vectorize the j-loop as a fused multiply-add (row_i[j] -= f*prow[j]). Skipping f==0 rows removes entire inner passes.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.risk: Multiplying by reciprocal instead of dividing changes the last ULP of each normalized entry, which can alter pivoting decisions and the final Value/Status for ill-conditioned LPs — this is NOT strictly bit-identical. If exact reproduction is required, keep the division in the normalize step and only apply pointer hoisting + f==0 skip (both bit-exact). The f-skip uses eps consistent with the existing tolerance model so it matches the algorithm's intent; pure f==0.0 skip is fully exact.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.summary: Hoist the objective-row base pointer and the cols-2 constant out of the loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.currentCost: `tab[objRow*cols+j]` recomputes objRow*cols every iteration, and `j == cols-2` recomputes cols-2 each iteration plus branches on the phase1 flag inside the loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.proposedChange: Hoist `double* orow = tab + objRow*cols;` and `int skipCol = phase1 ? -1 : cols-2;`. Loop body: `if (j==skipCol) continue; double val=orow[j]; if (val<minC){minC=val;pc=j;}`. This removes the per-iteration multiply and lifts the phase1 branch out of the loop (skipCol is loop-invariant).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.rationale: Removes a multiply and a redundant branch per column iteration; orow[j] is a single indexed load. Loop-invariant code motion shortens the body and helps the branch predictor / vectorizer.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.risk: Bit-exact and semantics-preserving; skipCol=-1 can never equal a valid j (j>=0), so phase1 behavior is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.summary: Avoid per-row division in the ratio test by comparing cross-multiplied products.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.currentCost: For each candidate row it computes `r = tab[i*cols+cols-1] / tab[i*cols+pCol]` — a division per row just to compare ratios. Division is high-latency, and the running minimum forces a serial dependency.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.proposedChange: Track the best (bestNum, bestDen) and compare via cross-multiplication: a new candidate (num_i, den_i) with den_i>eps beats current best when num_i*bestDen < bestNum*den_i (both dens positive). Replace division with two multiplies + compare; only store num/den pair. Also hoist `double* row_i = tab + i*cols;` to index rhs and pivot-col entry with single adds.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.rationale: Replaces one division per row with two multiplies, much lower latency, in a loop that runs every simplex iteration. Cross-multiplication is the standard branchless-friendly ratio-test trick.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Games/Simplex.c.risk: Cross-multiplication is only valid because all denominators considered are >eps>0, so inequality direction is preserved — guard already present (tab[i*cols+pCol]>eps). Floating-point: num*bestDen vs bestNum*den is not bit-identical to comparing the two quotients and can pick a different row on exact ties / ill-conditioned rows, slightly changing which optimal vertex is reported. If exact tie-breaking must match the original, keep the division. Otherwise behavior (an optimal solution) is preserved.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.summary: Replace three sqrt+Math.Max in the 3-point case with a single sqrt of the max squared distance.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.currentCost: Lines 50-53 do s.R=0 then three Math.Max(s.R, Math.Sqrt(Dist2(...))) calls = 3 sqrt + 3 max per innermost hit. sqrt is ~15-30 cycle latency on a dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.proposedChange: Compute d2i=Dist2(s,i...), d2j=Dist2(s,j...), d2k=Dist2(s,k...); take m=Math.Max(d2i,Math.Max(d2j,d2k)); s.R=Math.Sqrt(m). One sqrt instead of three.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.rationale: sqrt is monotonic, so max(sqrt(a),sqrt(b),sqrt(c))==sqrt(max(a,b,c)). Folds 3 transcendental ops + their long dependency chains into 1, while the Max comparisons stay on cheap doubles.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.risk: Bit-identical: sqrt monotone over non-negative doubles and Math.Max ordering preserved. No NaN inputs here since all distances are non-negative sums of squares.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.summary: Hoist the redundant Dist2 used to compute R in the 2-point case.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.currentCost: Line 42 calls Dist2(s, xs[j],ys[j],zs[j]) to get R, after the loop guard at line 37 already evaluated Dist2 for point j against the OLD sphere. The center has changed so it cannot be reused directly, but R can be derived from the diameter without a fresh full Dist2 read.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.proposedChange: Compute half-extents once: hx=(xs[i]-xs[j])*0.5, hy=(ys[i]-ys[j])*0.5, hz=(zs[i]-zs[j])*0.5; set center to xs[j]+hx etc.; s.R=Math.Sqrt(hx*hx+hy*hy+hz*hz). Avoids re-reading xs[j]/ys[j]/zs[j] a second time and the subtraction-from-center round-trip.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.rationale: Reuses the i-j deltas already needed for the midpoint instead of recomputing center-minus-point, removing 3 redundant loads and 3 subtractions per 2-point update.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.risk: Algebraically identical (midpoint-to-endpoint distance == half the i-j distance). Floating-point result differs only in last ULP from the current center-subtraction form; if exact bit-reproducibility with prior output is contractual, keep current form.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.summary: Remove AggressiveInlining from the large Run method.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.currentCost: Line 13 marks Run [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]. Run is a ~50-line triple-nested-loop method; forcing inlining bloats every call site, hurts I-cache, and gives Burst no benefit.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.proposedChange: Drop the [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] attribute on the public Run entry point. Keep it only on the tiny leaf Dist2.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.rationale: Inlining pays off for small hot leaves, not for big entry points. Removing it shrinks call-site code and lets the JIT/Burst keep Run out-of-line where it belongs.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.risk: None functional; attribute is only a hint. Behavior unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.summary: Apply the same Lemire multiply-shift to the inline Fisher-Yates shuffle.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.currentCost: Line 22 seed % (ulong)(i+1): a 64-bit division per element on the O(n) shuffle that precedes every solve.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.rationale: Same division-elimination rationale as MinEnclosingBall.Shuffle; multiply+shift is pipelined and far cheaper than 64-bit udiv.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/Welzl.risk: Produces a different (still valid) permutation; Welzl is permutation-invariant for correctness. Only change exact-shuffle-dependent tests would notice.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.summary: Replace 64-bit modulo in Fisher-Yates with Lemire multiply-shift bounded reduction.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.currentCost: Line 37 does seed % (ulong)(i+1) every iteration: a full 64-bit unsigned integer division (~20-40+ cycles, not pipelined) per shuffle step.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.proposedChange: Use j=(int)(((seed>>32)*(ulong)(i+1))>>32) (Lemire-style: multiply the high 32 random bits by the range and take the high word). Replaces div with one 64-bit multiply + shift.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.rationale: A widening multiply + shift is ~3-5 cycles and fully pipelined versus a non-pipelined 64-bit division, on the hot O(n) shuffle path that runs on every Welzl call.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.risk: Changes the exact permutation produced from the fixed seed (different but still valid uniform-ish shuffle). Welzl is correct for ANY permutation, so output circle is unaffected; only the (non-contractual) randomization order changes. If a test pins the exact shuffle sequence, keep modulo.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.summary: Inline the DistSq computation to avoid recomputing center deltas.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.currentCost: Line 44 computes cx,cy then calls DistSq(x1,y1,cx,cy), which recomputes (x1-cx) and (y1-cy). Since cx=(x1+x2)/2, x1-cx equals (x1-x2)/2 and is the half-delta already implied.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.proposedChange: double hx=(x1-x2)*0.5, hy=(y1-y2)*0.5; cx=x1-hx... or simply R=Math.Sqrt(hx*hx+hy*hy). Avoids the DistSq call and its duplicate subtractions.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.rationale: Removes one helper call and 2 redundant subtractions on a hot leaf used in the inner Welzl loops; reuses deltas that define the midpoint.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.risk: Floating-point result differs by at most last ULP from current (x1-cx) form due to reassociation; values otherwise identical. If bit-exact reproduction of current R is required, keep DistSq form.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to the leaf-ish Solve3/Solve2 only if small; otherwise leave and instead mark Welzl entry without inlining.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.currentCost: Welzl, Solve2, Solve3 carry no inlining hints. These are not tiny, so forced inlining is not warranted; current state is acceptable.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.proposedChange: No change recommended to inlining of Solve2/Solve3 (they are loop bodies, too large to inline). Documented here only to flag that the existing absence of attributes is correct and should NOT be 'fixed' by adding AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.rationale: Prevents a cargo-cult regression: inlining the Solve methods would bloat call sites with no win. Leaving them out-of-line is optimal.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Geometric/MinEn.risk: None; this is a no-op recommendation guarding against an incorrect change.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.summary: Hoist invariant pointer dereferences w[i], v[i] and cast (int)tw out of the inner j-loop; precompute w[i] once.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.currentCost: Inside the while-loop, tw = take*w[i] and tv = take*v[i] re-read w[i]/v[i] each split iteration. The inner for-loop recomputes (int)tw on every j via dp[j - (int)tw], a per-iteration sign-checked long->int narrowing inside the hottest loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.proposedChange: Read 'long wi = w[i]; long vi = v[i];' once at method entry. In the inner loop hoist 'int itw = (int)tw;' before the loop so the body is 'long cand = dp[j - itw] + tv;'. Iterate 'for (int j = cap; j >= itw; j--)'.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.rationale: Removes a redundant long->int conversion (which under Burst is a branch/checked narrowing pattern) and two memory loads from each inner-loop iteration, shortening the dependency chain to a single load-add-compare-store. The inner loop runs O(cap) times per split, O(cap*log(cnt)) per item, so removing the cast is the dominant win.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.risk: None: tw is loop-invariant within the inner for, so hoisting the cast is identical. take*w[i] already computed as long; behavior unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.summary: Eliminate redundant recomputation of dp[r + q[head]*wi], q[head]*vi and dp[r + j*wi]; the monotone-queue inner loop recomputes the same indexed loads/multiplies up to 3x per j.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.currentCost: Per j the loop computes 'dp[r + j*wi]' three separate times (lines 44, 49 read, 49 write base) and 'r + q[tail-1]*wi', 'q[tail-1]*vi' inside the dequeue while, plus 'q[head]*vi' and 'dp[r + q[head]*wi]'. Each is a multiply + add + pointer load on the hottest loop of the whole class.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.proposedChange: Precompute 'int baseIdx = r + j*wi; long dpj = dp[baseIdx];' once. Reuse dpj for 'val = dpj - j*vi', the final compare, and write to dp[baseIdx]. Cache 'q[tail-1]' into a local before the while test. Cache the head index 'int qh = q[head]; long bestBase = dp[r + qh*wi] + (j - qh)*vi;'.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.rationale: Cuts repeated j*wi multiplies and dp[] loads from ~3 to 1 per iteration and removes the duplicate r+q[tail-1]*wi computation in the eviction loop. Fewer multiplies and loads shorten the per-iteration critical path; the eviction-loop comparison value can be precomputed once per pushed j rather than recomputed for the same tail element.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.risk: None: all reused expressions are pure functions of loop state that does not change between the duplicate reads within one j iteration; dp[baseIdx] is only written at the end so caching the load is safe.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.summary: Store the precomputed monotone-queue key (dp[idx] - j*vi) alongside the index instead of recomputing it from dp during eviction.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.currentCost: The eviction while-loop recomputes 'dp[r + q[tail-1]*wi] - q[tail-1]*vi' for the stored index each comparison. The deque only stores the bare index j.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.proposedChange: Keep a parallel value in the same monotone structure: since q is int* the cleanest is to also cache the last-pushed key in a local 'long lastKey' and compare 'val >= lastKey', updating lastKey on push/pop. For multi-element eviction, a second long* key buffer parallel to q removes all repeated dp loads in the while.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.rationale: Trades recomputation (load + 2 multiplies) for a sequential read of an already-warm buffer, removing dp[] random-ish loads from the eviction path and shortening the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Bounde.risk: Requires an extra long* scratch buffer of size maxJ+1 passed in (API change) for the full version; the single-local 'lastKey' variant handles only the common single-pop case. Caller-provided buffer must be sized; document it. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Divide.summary: Hoist (int)w[i], w[i], v[i] out of both branches' inner loops and hoist (int)tw out of the binary-split inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Divide.currentCost: In the unbounded branch 'dp[j - (int)w[i]] + v[i]' re-reads w[i] (with a long->int cast) and v[i] every iteration. In the bounded branch 'dp[j - (int)tw]' casts tw to int each j. The class name says DivideConquer but the body is plain binary-splitting; no D&C optimization is present.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Divide.proposedChange: At top of the i-loop read 'int wi = (int)w[i]; long vi = v[i];'. Unbounded branch: 'for (int j = wi; j <= cap; j++) { long cand = dp[j - wi] + vi; ... }'. Bounded branch: hoist 'int itw = (int)tw;' before the inner for and use dp[j - itw].
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Divide.rationale: Removes a per-iteration long->int narrowing and two long loads from each inner-loop body, the dominant O(cap) cost. Identical to the BoundedKnapsack hoist; shortens the load-add-compare-store chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Divide.risk: None: w[i]/v[i] are invariant across j; the cast result is invariant. Same outputs.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.summary: The right-half scan does a full O(leftCount) linear search per mask, making the join O(2^(n/2) * 2^(n/2)) = O(2^n); replace with a Pareto-sorted left table + prefix-max and binary search to get O(2^(n/2) * (n/2 + log)).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.currentCost: For each of 2^(n-half) right masks, the inner 'for i in leftCount' linearly scans all 2^half left subsets to find max value with weight <= rem. This is 2^half * 2^(n-half) = 2^n total work, defeating the entire point of meet-in-the-middle (which should be ~2^(n/2)).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.proposedChange: After building the left table, sort the (weight,value) pairs by weight and compute a running prefix-max of value (drop dominated entries so weight ascending => value ascending). Then per right mask, binary-search rem in the sorted weights and read the prefix-max value in O(log). Sort is O(2^half * half) (radix or in-place) done once.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.rationale: Reduces the algorithm from O(2^n) back to its intended O(2^(n/2) * n) — an exponential asymptotic improvement, the headline benefit of meet-in-middle that the current code throws away.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.risk: Needs scratch space for sorting indices/prefix-max (caller buffer or in-place rearrange of the left array, which is already 2*leftCount longs). Sort must be deterministic. For n up to 40, leftCount up to 2^20 ~1M entries — the linear-per-mask version is currently 2^40 ops which is infeasible anyway, so this is both a correctness-of-performance and feasibility fix. Preserves the max-value output.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.summary: Build subset weight/value sums incrementally via Gray-code or low-bit recurrence instead of an inner O(half) bit-scan per subset.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.currentCost: Both subset-enumeration loops recompute sw/sv from scratch with an inner loop over all bits (O(half) and O(n-half)) and a branch '(i & (1<<j)) != 0' per bit, costing O(half * 2^half) total just to build sums.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.proposedChange: Use the recurrence sum[i] = sum[i & (i-1)] + element[trailing_zero_count(i)] (lowest set bit). With math.tzcnt / Burst intrinsic this builds each subset sum in O(1) from a previously computed subset, turning sum construction into O(2^half). Same for the right half into a scratch buffer.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.rationale: Drops subset-sum construction from O(n*2^(n/2)) to O(2^(n/2)), removing the per-bit branch that Burst cannot vectorize, and replacing 1<<j shifts with a single tzcnt and one prior load.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.risk: i & (i-1) clears the lowest set bit (DP on a previously filled index < i, valid since processed in increasing order). For the right half it needs a scratch buffer of 2^(n-half) sums rather than recomputing on the fly. Output identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.summary: Hoist the loop bound (1 << (n - half)) and reuse a precomputed 'rightCount'; also strength-reduce i*2 indexing with a running pointer.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.currentCost: The right-mask for-loop recomputes '(1 << (n - half))' in its condition each iteration. left[] access uses 'i*2' and 'i*2+1' (a shift+add) every probe in the inner scan.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.proposedChange: Compute 'int rightCount = 1 << (n - half);' once before the loop. In the left-build and inner scan, advance a 'long* lp = left;' pointer by 2 each iteration so accesses are lp[0]/lp[1] with no index multiply.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.rationale: Removes a repeated shift in the loop condition and replaces index*2 address computation with pointer increment, trimming the inner-scan critical path. (Largely moot if the O(2^n) inner scan is replaced per the complexity item, but applies to the build loop regardless.)
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/MeetIn.risk: None: pure index strength-reduction, identical addresses and outputs.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.summary: Hoist partial sums a[i] and a[i]+a[j] out of the two-pointer inner loop so the hot test is a single add.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.currentCost: The innermost while recomputes 's = a[i] + a[j] + a[l] + a[r]' fully each step, redundantly re-reading a[i] and a[j] (loop-invariant for the inner while) and re-adding them every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.proposedChange: Before the j-loop body's while, compute 'int ai = a[i];' (outside j-loop) and 'int aij = ai + a[j];'. Inner test becomes 's = aij + a[l] + a[r];'.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.rationale: Removes two redundant memory loads and one add from each two-pointer step (the hottest loop, O(n^2) outer with O(n) inner). Shorter dependency chain and fewer loads improve throughput; a[i] hoist also lets it stay in a register across the whole j/while nest.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.risk: None: a[i], a[j] are invariant within the inner while; same arithmetic, same count. Assumes sorted input as the algorithm already requires.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.summary: Count(...,k,...) only handles k==2 and silently returns 0 for all other k — misleading API; split into TwoSumCount or guard/document.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.currentCost: The 'k' parameter and the 'if (k == 2)' branch imply general k-sum support but every k != 2 returns 0 with no signal, a correctness/discoverability trap. The branch on k is also dead overhead on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.proposedChange: Rename to 'TwoSumCount(int* a, int n, int target)' dropping the k parameter (matching the concrete behavior and the FourSum naming convention), or keep k but follow the Try* convention to indicate unsupported k. Removes the per-call k branch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.rationale: Improves API honesty/discoverability and removes a dead branch; aligns with the existing FourSum naming so callers know exactly what is supported.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/KSum.c.risk: Signature change — breaking for callers passing k. Pure ergonomics; numeric behavior for k==2 unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.summary: Hoist groupStart[g] / groupStart[g+1] out of the capacity loop; they are reloaded for every c.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.currentCost: The inner 'for idx = groupStart[g]; idx < groupStart[g+1]' re-reads groupStart[g] and groupStart[g+1] from memory on every one of the (cap+1) iterations of the c-loop, an O(cap) redundant double load per group.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.proposedChange: Before the c-loop read 'int gs = groupStart[g]; int ge = groupStart[g + 1];' once and iterate 'for (int idx = gs; idx < ge; idx++)'.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.rationale: Removes two memory loads from each c iteration (cap+1 per group), and lets the compiler keep the bounds in registers, improving the inner loop that already loads itemW/itemV. Classic invariant hoist on the hottest loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.risk: None: groupStart is not modified during the loop; identical iteration bounds and output.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.summary: Cache itemW[idx] into a local to avoid loading it twice per item, and hoist the early-exit when itemW > c.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.currentCost: Each item iteration loads itemW[idx] for the '<= c' test and again implicitly in 'dp[c - itemW[idx]]', two loads of the same value; itemV[idx] is loaded only when needed which is fine.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.proposedChange: Read 'int wIdx = itemW[idx];' once: 'if (wIdx <= c) { long cand = dp[c - wIdx] + itemV[idx]; if (cand > best) best = cand; }'.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.rationale: Eliminates a duplicate load of itemW[idx] in the innermost loop (group-size * (cap+1) * n iterations). Fewer loads, shorter chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Multip.risk: None: itemW[idx] is invariant within the iteration; identical result.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.summary: Replace managed bool[] dp with a caller-provided byte* scratch buffer (or stackalloc) to make the large-n path Burst-compatible and allocation-free
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.currentCost: `bool[] dp = new bool[target + 1]` is a managed heap allocation of `target+1` bytes on every call to the large-n path. Managed arrays are forbidden by house constraints in src, defeat Burst compilation entirely (the method cannot be Burst-compiled with a managed allocation/GC reference), and cause a GC allocation + zeroing pass each invocation. On mobile this is the dominant cost.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.proposedChange: Change the signature to accept a scratch buffer, e.g. `public static bool Can(long* w, int n, long target, byte* dp)` where `dp` has `target+1` entries, or split into a `Run` (caller-provided buffer) plus a `Try`/convenience overload. Inside, zero the buffer (or document the caller must), set `dp[0]=1`, and do `dp[j] = (byte)(dp[j] | dp[j - w[i]])`. This removes the allocation, keeps the function blittable/unmanaged, and lets the whole method Burst-compile.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.rationale: Eliminates one heap allocation + GC pressure per call and a managed-reference that prevents Burst codegen. A byte* DP table is blittable and Burst vectorizes the inner OR loop well; the boolean `||` short-circuit is replaced by a branchless bitwise OR.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.risk: API change (breaking). Caller must supply a buffer of size target+1 and is responsible for zeroing it (or the method zeroes via UnsafeUtility.MemClear). Using `|` instead of `||` is semantics-preserving for boolean-valued bytes (0/1) and removes a branch but reads both operands unconditionally (always safe here, both are in-bounds). For Burst, prefer byte (0/1) over bool* for clean blittability.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.summary: The 64-bit bitset path is silently wrong (and the n<=64 selector is misconceived): the shift amount comes from item weight, not item count, so weights >= 64 corrupt results
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.currentCost: `bits |= bits << (int)w[i]` shifts a 64-bit value by `w[i]`. C# masks shift counts to the low 6 bits for ulong, so any item with `w[i] >= 64` (even though `w[i] <= target` passes the guard) shifts by `w[i] & 63`, producing wrong reachable-sum bits. The bitset width must be `target+1` bits, not 64, so the `n <= 64` condition is the wrong predicate entirely — it should be `target < 64` (or `target <= 63`).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.proposedChange: Gate the single-word bitset path on `target <= 63` instead of `n <= 64`. For larger `target`, either fall through to the DP path or use a multi-word bitset of `(target/64)+1` words (shift-OR across words) which is O(n * target/64) — a 64x constant-factor win over the byte DP for the same asymptotics. Add the guard so an item is skipped/handled only when `w[i] <= 63` in the single-word path.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.rationale: Correctness first: the current predicate ties capacity to item count. Fixing it to `target <= 63` makes the fast path correct. The multi-word bitset generalizes it: subset-sum reachability via word-parallel shift-OR is the standard O(n*target/word) bitset DP, 64x fewer operations than the byte-per-cell DP while preserving exact output.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.risk: This is primarily a correctness fix, not a pure micro-opt — flag for the maintainer since it changes observable behavior for the currently-buggy inputs (weights >= 64 with n <= 64). The multi-word bitset must handle the cross-word carry of the shift (`(word[k] << s) | (word[k-1] >> (64-s))`) with care for s==0. Verify against the DP path on random inputs before shipping.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.summary: Hoist w[i] into a local and make the DP inner loop branchless to shorten the dependency chain and cut redundant loads
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.currentCost: Inner loop `dp[j] = dp[j] || dp[j - w[i]]` reloads `w[i]` implicitly via the loop bound and index each iteration, and the `||` introduces a per-cell branch that is poorly predicted for random data, stalling the pipeline. `dp[j - w[i]]` recomputes the offset each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.proposedChange: Hoist `long wi = w[i];` once per outer iteration (already partly implied by the bound, but make it explicit and reuse for both the bound and the index). Replace the inner body with branchless `dp[j] |= dp[j - wi];` over byte cells. Optionally walk a moving pointer `byte* src = dp + (j - wi)` to avoid recomputing the subtraction.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.rationale: Branchless bitwise OR removes a mispredicted branch in a hot O(n*target) loop and lets Burst auto-vectorize the OR across contiguous cells. Hoisting wi and using a pointer cuts the per-iteration address arithmetic and load of w[i].
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Knapsack/Subset.risk: Requires the byte* buffer change (opportunity 1) since `|=` on bool is not idiomatic; with 0/1 byte values it is exactly equivalent to `||` for all inputs. No overflow concern (values are 0/1). Vectorization across the descending j loop is safe only because the gap (wi) guarantees no overlap between read dp[j-wi] and write dp[j] within a vector when wi >= vector width; for small wi Burst will serialize correctly, so semantics are preserved either way.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.summary: Replace the O(n^2) selection-style sort with an O(n log n) sort over the index permutation.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.currentCost: The double loop performs n*(n-1)/2 comparisons of weight[order[i]] < weight[order[j]] plus up to that many swaps, i.e. O(n^2) comparisons and double-indirection loads (order[i]->weight[]). For the greedy matroid algorithm this dominates total runtime whenever the independence callback is cheap.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.proposedChange: Sort the 'order' index array by descending weight using an in-place introsort/heapsort over the stackalloc buffer (no managed Array.Sort, no allocations). A heapsort on the int* order array with comparisons keyed on weight[order[k]] keeps everything unmanaged and Burst-friendly while dropping to O(n log n). Alternatively, if weights are bounded, a radix/counting pass; but heapsort is the general drop-in.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.rationale: n log n vs n^2 is an asymptotic win that grows unbounded with n; for n in the thousands this is orders of magnitude fewer comparisons and memory loads. Heapsort is in-place (no extra RAM), branch-predictable enough, and contains no recursion-depth blowup risk.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.risk: Sort must be a stable-equivalent for the matroid result: the current selection sort is NOT stable (it swaps on strict <, leaving equal-weight elements in a data-dependent order). Heapsort is also unstable, so for equal weights the chosen independent set may differ from the current code when ties exist and the independence oracle is tie-sensitive. The TOTAL weight returned is provably identical for any matroid regardless of tie order (matroid greedy optimality), so the long return value is preserved; only the unobservable internal selection among equal-weight ties could differ. State this guard: behavior-preserving for the returned total, not necessarily for which specific tied elements get selected.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.summary: Eliminate double indirection in the comparison by sorting (weight, index) pairs or caching weights, removing the gather load weight[order[i]] from the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.currentCost: Inner comparison weight[order[i]] < weight[order[j]] does two dependent loads each: read order[k] (sequential, cached) then a gather load weight[order[k]] (random access, likely cache miss for large n). The dependency chain order[k] -> weight[order[k]] serializes and the gather defeats vectorization and prefetch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.proposedChange: Materialize a parallel key buffer once: stackalloc long[n] keys; for(i) keys[i] = weight[order[i]] (here order[i]==i initially so keys[i]=weight[i]); then sort the (key, index) pairs together. Comparisons then read keys[i] directly (sequential) instead of gathering through order. Combine with the heapsort above so the gather happens O(n) times during key build instead of O(n log n) (or O(n^2)) times during comparison.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.rationale: Converts O(comparisons) random gathers into O(n) sequential reads plus O(comparisons) sequential key reads. Sequential access is cache-friendly and prefetchable, shortening the per-compare dependency chain from two dependent loads to one.
