src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Matroid.risk: Costs an extra n*8 bytes of stack (long keys) plus optionally keeping order in sync during swaps (swap both arrays). Stack pressure: n longs + existing 3 int arrays = ~ n*20 bytes on stack; for large n this could approach stack limits, so for very large n a caller-provided scratch buffer would be safer. Semantics preserved (same key values, ties handled identically to whatever sort is chosen).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.summary: Vectorize the GF(2) row XOR (a[r*m+j] ^= a[pivot*m+j]) over wider words; it is the inner hot loop and is trivially SIMD-able.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.currentCost: The inner 'for j: a[r*m+j] ^= a[pivot*m+j]' runs over the full width m for every eliminated row, giving O(n*m) int XORs per pivot and O(rank*n*m) overall. As written, int-at-a-time XOR is one operation per 4 bytes; Burst can auto-vectorize but the row-major int layout wastes 31/32 of each int when the matrix is over GF(2) (entries are 0/1).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.proposedChange: Hoist the row base pointers out of the inner loop: int* rowR = a + r*m; int* rowP = a + pivotRow*m; then loop 'rowR[j] ^= rowP[j]'. This removes the repeated r*m and pivotRow*m multiplies/address computations from every iteration and gives Burst a clean two-pointer XOR loop it vectorizes cleanly. Higher-impact (separate, larger-API change): pack GF(2) rows as bitsets (ulong words, m/64 words) so each XOR processes 64 entries at once, cutting the inner loop length by 64x and shrinking RAM 32x.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.rationale: Pointer hoisting removes two integer multiplies and an add from the address calculation of every inner iteration, shortening the address-gen dependency chain and helping the vectorizer prove contiguity. The bitset packing is an asymptotic constant-factor win (64x fewer word ops, 32x less memory, far fewer cache lines touched) — decisive for large matroids.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.risk: Pointer hoisting is purely semantics-preserving. The bitset repacking changes the public matrix representation (a[] layout and the basis/Rank contract) and the FindPivotRow/SwapRows code, so it is an API-level change, not a drop-in; flag as a larger refactor. Both keep GF(2) XOR semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to the tiny leaf helpers (FindPivotRow, SwapRows, EliminateOtherRows) and drop the unused 'using' directives.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.currentCost: FindPivotRow, SwapRows, EliminateOtherRows are private leaf helpers called inside the column loop. Without an inlining hint the JIT/Burst may keep call overhead (frame setup, parameter marshaling of the many int args). Also 'using System;' is unused in both files and System.Runtime.CompilerServices is unused unless attributes are added.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.proposedChange: Annotate the three private helpers with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] so the hot column loop inlines them and the compiler can keep n,m,a in registers across the merged body, exposing the inner XOR/pivot loops to fusion. Remove the unused 'using System;'.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.rationale: Inlining these small, frequently-called helpers removes call overhead and lets the optimizer hoist invariants (e.g., a+pivotRow*m) across what are currently separate function boundaries. Burst already inlines aggressively, so impact is low, but the hint is free and the using cleanup reduces noise.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/LinearM.risk: Inlining a leaf with two nested loops (EliminateOtherRows) can grow code size; Burst may already do this. Purely a hint — no semantic change. Removing an unused using is safe.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Elimina.summary: Skip XOR-ing the columns already known to be zero/processed: start the inner XOR at column 'col' (or track a leading-zero offset) since columns < current pivot columns are already reduced.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Elimina.currentCost: The inner loop always sweeps j from 0..m-1, re-touching the leading basis columns that are already in reduced echelon form (those columns are 0 in row r for r != pivot, so XOR with pivot row either re-touches a 0 or only the pivot column itself). For matrices much wider than their rank, much of each sweep is wasted work on columns that cannot change the outcome relative to a tighter start.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Elimina.proposedChange: Because elimination produces reduced row echelon form, in row r (r != pivotRow) all previously-pivoted columns are already 0, and the current pivot column is the leftmost nonzero. You can start the XOR sweep at j = col instead of j = 0 for the elimination of rows whose leading nonzero is at 'col'. Guard: this is only valid if rows below 'rank' have zeros in columns < col, which holds for the rows being eliminated at-or-after the pivot but NOT necessarily for rows above (already-reduced rows can have set bits only in their own pivot column, which is < col and already 0 elsewhere). Safest correct version: start sweep at the column index 'col' only for r >= rank; keep full sweep for r < rank.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Elimina.rationale: Avoids touching O(col) already-zero columns per eliminated row, reducing inner-loop length as the algorithm progresses, especially beneficial for tall reductions.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Matroid/Elimina.risk: Correctness hinges on the echelon invariant: above-pivot rows may hold their own earlier pivot bit at a column < col, and XOR-ing the pivot row (which is 0 in those columns) wouldn't change them anyway — so skipping is safe there too, but ONLY because pivot row is zero in columns < col. Must verify pivot row really is zero in all columns < col (true in reduced echelon). If the algorithm is not maintaining full RREF (only forward elimination), this optimization is unsafe — verify the invariant before applying; otherwise reject.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: Hoist the repeated queryIdx[i] load and the post-increment-with-aliased-store into locals to cut redundant memory traffic in the hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: Each iteration loads queryIdx[i] twice (once for Mid args, once for the bucket store), and reads/writes bucketSize[0] through a pointer that the compiler cannot prove is non-aliasing with buckets/lo/hi/queryIdx, forcing a load+store of bucketSize[0] every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: Read int q = queryIdx[i]; once, compute int mid = Mid(lo[q], hi[q]); keep the running offset in a register local (int pos = bucketSize[0]; ... buckets[mid + pos] = q; pos++;) and write bucketSize[0] = pos; once after the loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: Removes a duplicate load of queryIdx[i] and converts a memory-resident counter (forced through pointer aliasing) into a register, eliminating one dependent load+store per iteration and shortening the loop-carried dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: Semantics-preserving only if buckets does not alias bucketSize during the loop; given the algorithm, bucketSize is a separate scalar counter, so caching it is safe. The final write-back reproduces the same final bucketSize[0] value.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: Init writes two interleaved constant streams; splitting into two tight loops (or a single loop with constants hoisted) lets Burst vectorize each store stream.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: The loop stores constants 0 and -1 to two distinct arrays per iteration; interleaved scalar stores to lo[] and hi[] are harder for Burst to widen into vector stores than two homogeneous streams.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: Either keep one loop (already fine) but mark the constants explicitly, or split into for(i) lo[i]=0; and for(i) hi[i]=-1; so each becomes a memset-like vectorizable fill.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: Two homogeneous constant-fill loops map cleanly to vectorized/widened stores (or memset for the 0 case), whereas the interleaved version may stay scalar.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: None functionally; lo and hi are distinct buffers, so order of fills is irrelevant. Splitting doubles loop overhead but each loop is trivially vectorizable, a net win for large n.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: Replace per-query checkFn indirect call inside the add/remove loops with a tighter contiguous scan, and hoist queryK[idx] into a local across the two while-loops.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: queryK[idx] is read/written through a pointer every loop iteration of both while loops; idx is just i (the line int idx = i; is redundant aliasing). Each step also makes an indirect call checkFn(context, queryK[idx]) whose result gates an add/remove, creating a long dependency chain via the function pointer.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: Use int k = queryK[i]; iterate on local k in both while loops, then write back queryK[i] = k; once. Drop int idx = i;. If checkFn is a membership test that is monotone over the contiguous [old..mid) range, document/restructure so the indirect call can be hoisted or batched; at minimum keep k in a register to remove the load/store dependency through the pointer.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: Removes a redundant local alias, replaces repeated dependent pointer load/stores of queryK[idx] with a register, shortening the loop-carried chain and reducing memory traffic per advanced position.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: Caching queryK[i] in a register is safe as long as addFn/removeFn/checkFn do not read or write queryK (they take context + an int key, not queryK), which holds for the parallel-binary-search/divide-conquer pattern. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: Solve is structurally incomplete/incorrect for divide-and-conquer offline: it never recurses and never partitions queries into left/right child sets, so leftCount/rightCount are dead and mid-based work is not amortized.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: leftCount and rightCount are computed-never (always 0) dead variables; the two empty branches (queryR<lo||queryL>hi and the trailing else) do nothing; there is no recursion into [lo,mid] and [mid+1,hi], so the intended O((n+V)log V) divide-and-conquer is not realized — the routine only advances each fully-covering query's pointer to mid once at the top level.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: Either (a) implement the real CDQ/parallel-binary-search recursion: partition queries by whether their answer lies in [lo,mid] vs [mid+1,hi] using checkFn at mid, recurse on both halves with the add/remove state restored, and store the converged answer into answers[]; or (b) if this is a stub, remove the dead leftCount/rightCount and empty branches to make intent and cost explicit.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: As written the asymptotic structure the class name promises is absent; completing the recursion changes per-query cost from un-amortized scans to the intended logarithmic divide-and-conquer, and removing dead vars eliminates wasted register/stack slots and clarifies the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: This is a behavioral/correctness gap, not a micro-opt; changing it alters observable output. Flagged as high-impact design issue — must be validated against intended algorithm before applying. The dead-variable/empty-branch removal alone is semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: The final copy-back loop (idx[i]=tmp[i]) can be eliminated by ping-ponging buffers, and the index loads idx[i]/idx[j] feed double-indirection x[idx[i]] that hurts cache locality.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: Every merge level copies the whole [l,r] range from tmp back into idx (an extra n log n element copies overall), and the comparison x[idx[i]]<=x[idx[j]] does two dependent loads (gather) per compare due to indirection through idx.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: Implement classic ping-pong merge sort: alternate src/dst between idx and tmp by recursion depth (or copy once at the end if depth parity is wrong), removing the per-level copy-back. Optionally sort a precomputed key array (xKey[i]=x[idx[i]]) in lockstep so the inner compare is a single contiguous load instead of a gather.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: Ping-pong removes ~n per merge level of redundant copies (a constant-factor but real reduction of total memory writes and a full extra pass per level); sorting flattened keys turns dependent gather loads into sequential loads, improving cache behavior and enabling vectorized compares.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: Ping-pong requires careful depth-parity handling so the final sorted data lands in idx; getting parity wrong changes output. The key-array variant needs an extra n-sized buffer (RAM trade-off) and must keep keys and indices in lockstep. Apply only with the parity guard verified.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: Hoist repeated double-indirection loads (idx[i], idx[j], z[idx[i]]) into locals and cache idx[j]'s y-value across the inner while.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: The inner while reloads y[idx[i]] and y[idx[j]] each iteration; y[idx[j]] is loop-invariant for the duration of the inner while (j fixed) yet recomputed via two dependent loads every inner iteration. bitAdd indirect call gates on these gathered loads.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: Before the inner while, compute int yj = y[idx[j]]; and compare y[idx[i]] <= yj. Inside, read int ii = idx[i]; once and use z[ii]. After the inner loop completes for this j, j++ as before.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: y[idx[j]] is invariant across the inner loop; hoisting removes two dependent gather loads per inner iteration. Caching idx[i] removes a duplicate indirect load shared by the compare and the bitAdd(z[idx[i]]) call.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: bitAdd mutates bit[] (the Fenwick tree), not x/y/z/idx, so yj and idx[i] remain valid across the call. Semantics-preserving for the standard CDQ pattern where the partition arrays are immutable during the merge.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: The expression prevVersion > 0 ? ... : ... is evaluated up to five times per node (children, sum, and again inside each recursive call), and leftChild[prevVersion]/rightChild[prevVersion] are loaded twice; hoist into locals.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: Per node: prevVersion>0 branch tested 3x in the body plus once more in whichever recursive-call argument fires; leftChild[prevVersion] is read once for leftChild[node] and again as the recursive prevVersion argument (same for rightChild). These are redundant dependent loads plus repeated branches.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: int hasPrev = prevVersion > 0 ? 1 : 0; int pl = hasPrev != 0 ? leftChild[prevVersion] : 0; int pr = hasPrev != 0 ? rightChild[prevVersion] : 0; leftChild[node]=pl; rightChild[node]=pr; sum[node] = hasPrev != 0 ? sum[prevVersion]+1 : 1; then pass pl/pr directly as the child prevVersion in recursion, avoiding the re-load and re-test.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: Collapses 3-4 evaluations of the same predicate and 2 loads of leftChild[prevVersion]/rightChild[prevVersion] into one each, shortening the per-node work in this recursively hot tree-build.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: None: prevVersion is constant within the call, and the body reads leftChild[prevVersion] before any write to leftChild[node] (node != prevVersion since node = ++allocCnt is freshly allocated), so hoisting reproduces identical values. Behavior preserved.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: leftChild[node] is loaded twice (for the != 0 test and for the recursive descent argument); hoist into a local.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: Per recursion level: leftChild[node] read once for the leftCount guard and again as the QueryKth argument in the k<=leftCount branch; sum[leftChild[node]] re-indexes. Two dependent loads of the same address.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: int lc = leftChild[node]; int leftCount = lc != 0 ? sum[lc] : 0; ... if (k <= leftCount) return QueryKth(..., lc, l, mid, k);
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: Removes a redundant load of leftChild[node] on the hot path of an O(log n) descent and lets the compiler keep the child pointer in a register across the branch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: None: node is unchanged within the call and no writes occur, so caching leftChild[node] is exact. Semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.summary: Convert the tail-recursive QueryKth (and the descent in BuildPersistentSegTree) into an iterative loop to remove call overhead and stack growth on deep trees.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.currentCost: QueryKth is purely tail-recursive (both returns are direct recursive calls); each level pays a function-call prologue/epilogue and stack frame. Under Burst, tail-call optimization is not guaranteed, so deep trees (log n ~ 20-30) incur real call overhead.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.proposedChange: Rewrite as a while loop: update node/l/r/k in place until l==r, then return l. Same for the single-path descent shape; BuildPersistentSegTree is harder (it writes child links) but its descent can also be flattened with an explicit walk.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.rationale: Eliminates per-level call overhead and frame setup, keeps node/l/r/k in registers across iterations, and bounds stack usage to O(1) for the query path.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Offline/Offline.risk: QueryKth conversion is mechanical and semantics-preserving (pure tail recursion). BuildPersistentSegTree must still update parent child pointers, so only its descent (not the link writes) can be iterated; apply carefully to preserve the persistent-tree wiring.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.summary: Inner edge scan makes each improvement sweep O(n*m); precomputing per-vertex adjacency or scanning edges once per sweep yields O(m) per sweep instead of O(n*m).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.currentCost: For every vertex v (n of them) the code rescans ALL m edges to find incident ones, so one sweep is O(n*m). With a dense graph m~n^2 this is O(n^3) per sweep, and the outer while may run many sweeps.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.proposedChange: Build a CSR-style adjacency (offset array of length n+1 + neighbor/weight arrays of length 2m) once into caller-provided scratch (or stackalloc), then in the sweep iterate only the edges incident to v via adj[off[v]..off[v+1]]. This makes a full sweep O(n + sum(deg)) = O(n+2m). Alternatively, maintain a per-vertex 'inCut-outCut' delta array updated incrementally when a vertex flips, so each flip costs O(deg(v)) instead of an O(m) rescan.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.rationale: Removes the redundant full-edge rescan per vertex. For dense graphs this is an asymptotic drop from O(n*m) to O(n+m) per sweep; even sparse graphs avoid touching non-incident edges. Fewer total memory reads dominates the runtime here.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.risk: CSR build needs scratch memory (2m ints + 2m longs + n+1 offsets); must be unmanaged (stackalloc or caller buffer) to stay Burst/house-rule compliant. Behavior is identical: same in/out cut sums, same greedy flip order, same tie-breaking (outCut>inCut strict). Edge self-loops (from==to) are currently counted into neither branch via the if/else-if (u set once) — adjacency build must preserve that: a self-loop contributes once where from==v matches first, so replicate the same single-match semantics.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.summary: Per-edge incidence test uses two branches and a sentinel; restructure to branchless/early classification and hoist partition[v].
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.currentCost: Inner loop does `if(from[e]==v) u=to[e]; else if(to[e]==v) u=from[e]; if(u<0) continue;` plus a data-dependent `partition[v]!=partition[u]` branch every edge — 3-4 unpredictable branches per edge, and partition[v] is reloaded each edge.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.proposedChange: Hoist `int pv = partition[v];` out of the edge loop. Compute incidence as `int fe=from[e], te=to[e]; bool inc = (fe==v)|(te==v); int u = (fe==v)?te:fe;` then `if(!inc) continue;`. Accumulate branchlessly: `long contrib=w[e]; bool diff = partition[u]!=pv; inCut += diff?contrib:0; outCut += diff?0:contrib;` (compiler/Burst lowers ternary to cmov/select). This keeps the same single-incidence semantics and removes the else-if dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.rationale: Fewer mispredicted branches and a shorter dependency chain per edge; hoisting partition[v] removes a redundant load on every edge iteration. Burst vectorizes select-style accumulation better than divergent branches.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.risk: Must preserve that an edge with from==v and to==v (self-loop) is treated exactly as before. With `inc=(fe==v)|(te==v)` and `u=(fe==v)?te:fe`, a self-loop gives u==v, diff=false, adds to outCut — same as original (original set u=to=v, partition[v]!=partition[v] false -> outCut). Semantics preserved. No overflow change.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.summary: Misleading name and unused parameter: it does not run GW SDP rounding, ignores alpha, and hardcodes 1.138.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.currentCost: Method named GoemansWilliamson takes a `double alpha` that is never used and multiplies a local-search cut by a magic literal 1.138, allocating a stackalloc partition that is discarded. The name implies an SDP-based algorithm that is not implemented.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.proposedChange: Either remove the unused `alpha` parameter and rename to reflect that it returns a scaled local-search bound (e.g. LocalSearchScaledBound), or honor `alpha` by using it as the multiplier instead of the hardcoded 1.138. Promote 1.138 to a named const (e.g. GwApproxRatioInverse). Also let the caller pass the partition buffer rather than stackalloc-and-discard so the assignment is observable/reusable.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.rationale: Removes a dead parameter (smaller signature, no wasted arg setup) and a magic number; clarifies the perf/semantic contract. The stackalloc int[n] is currently pure waste since the partition is never returned.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/MaxC.risk: Renaming/removing the parameter is a public API change — only do if callers permit. The numeric result for given inputs is unchanged if alpha continues to be ignored and 1.138 retained as a named const.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.summary: `new Random(42)` allocates a managed System.Random inside the method, defeating Burst and breaking the unmanaged/no-managed-types house rule.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.currentCost: System.Random is a managed reference type; constructing it on the hot path causes a heap allocation, is not blittable, and cannot be Burst-compiled. It also hardcodes seed 42, making the method non-configurable and hiding mutable RNG state inside the function.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.proposedChange: Replace with an unmanaged xorshift/PCG state passed in by the caller (e.g. `ulong* rngState` or a `ref Xorshift rng` unmanaged struct) consistent with how Rounding.Random already takes an rng. Provide a small static `NextDouble(ref ulong state)` helper. This keeps the method Burst-compatible and pure w.r.t. a caller-owned seed.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.rationale: Eliminates a managed allocation and makes the routine Burst-jittable and deterministic via an explicit seed argument. xorshift NextDouble is a few ALU ops vs. System.Random's heavier managed implementation.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.risk: Changes the exact random sequence (different RNG), so outputs differ from the current seed-42 sequence — acceptable since the result is already random, but it is an observable change for fixed-seed reproducers. Signature change is a public API change; mirror the existing `Random(...)` rng-parameter convention to stay consistent.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.summary: Outer k-loop rescans the full frac array each pick (O(k*n)) and recomputes a prefix sum from scratch every time.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.currentCost: For each of k picks it walks all n elements accumulating `acc` until r<acc. Each pick is O(n) -> O(k*n) total, and the running `acc` prefix is rebuilt from index 0 every pick even though earlier zeroed entries contribute nothing.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.proposedChange: Maintain the prefix structure incrementally: since a chosen j sets frac[j]=0 and sum-=frac[j], you can skip already-zeroed entries, or use a Fenwick/BIT (the repo already has a Fenwick module) over frac to do each weighted draw in O(log n), giving O(k log n). For small n keep the linear scan but break early and start accumulation from the first nonzero index to cut constant factor.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.rationale: Replaces O(k*n) with O(k log n) for the weighted sampling without replacement, reusing existing Fenwick infrastructure; for the linear fallback, skipping zeroed prefixes reduces redundant additions.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Roun.risk: A Fenwick-based draw must reproduce the same selection probabilities/semantics as the linear `r<acc` scan (first index where cumulative exceeds r). Floating-point cumulative-sum order differs between linear scan and tree query, so the exact element chosen for a given r can differ at tie boundaries — acceptable for a randomized rounding but technically an observable change at FP boundaries; note this if exact reproducibility is required.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.summary: `iter*n` is recomputed as a loop-invariant multiply in Run and inside FindBestItem's inner loop and the total accumulation.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.currentCost: Each iteration computes `gain[iter*n+best]` (a multiply) and FindBestItem recomputes `gain[iter*n+i]` with the `iter*n` multiply folded into every inner-loop index. The base offset `iter*n` is invariant across the inner i-loop but the indexing pattern hides it from some JITs.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.proposedChange: Hoist `long* row = gain + (long)iter*n;` once per outer iteration and pass `row` to FindBestItem so the inner loop indexes `row[i]` (pure pointer add, no multiply). In Run use `total += row[best];`. Use a 64-bit offset for the multiply to avoid int overflow when iter*n exceeds 2^31.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.rationale: Removes a multiply from every inner-loop iteration (turns row[i] into base+i*8 addressing the hardware does for free) and shortens the address-computation dependency chain. Burst/JIT may already strength-reduce this, but passing the row pointer guarantees it.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.risk: Must use 64-bit arithmetic for the offset (`(long)iter*n`) to match/exceed current behavior; the current code uses int `iter*n` which already overflows for large iter*n, so switching to long is a safe correctness improvement, not a behavior change within the valid (non-overflowing) input range.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.summary: Return type truncates a long `total` to int, and total is computed but the function's contract (count vs value) is ambiguous.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.currentCost: `total` is accumulated as long across k picks but returned as `(int)total`, silently truncating/overflowing for large submodular gains. The cast hides potential overflow on the very metric the greedy is optimizing.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.proposedChange: Change the return type to `long` to match the accumulator (and the gain element type long*). If the intended return is the number of selected items, return the pick count instead; but given it sums gains, long is the correct width.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.rationale: Avoids a lossy narrowing on the hot result; long matches the gain element type and the accumulator with zero extra cost.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.risk: Return-type change is a public API change. Numerically identical for inputs whose total fits in int; only differs (more correct) when total exceeds int range, which is currently a silent bug.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.summary: Each of up to m rounds recomputes new-coverage for every set from scratch over its full element list -> O(m^2 * avgSetSize); lazy-greedy or incremental decrement is far cheaper.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.currentCost: FindBestSet calls CountNewCoverage on all m sets every round, each scanning the set's elements -> O(m * totalElems) per round, O(m^2 * totalElems / m) overall. Coverage counts are fully recomputed even though only newly-covered elements change between rounds.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.proposedChange: Maintain a per-set live-uncovered count; when MarkCovered marks element e, decrement the count of every set containing e (requires an element->sets incidence list), or use the classic lazy-greedy (priority queue with stale-marginal revalidation) so most sets are not re-evaluated each round. Both reduce repeated full rescans.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.rationale: Submodular marginal gains are monotonically non-increasing, so lazy evaluation skips re-scoring most sets; an incidence-list decrement makes each MarkCovered update O(elem*setsPerElem) total across the run instead of O(m) full rescans per round.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Submodular/Subm.risk: Lazy-greedy must revalidate the top candidate's marginal before committing to preserve exact greedy choice (same set selected each round, same tie-breaking: strict `curNew>bestNew` keeps the lowest index on ties). Incidence-list approach needs extra unmanaged storage (element->set lists). Behavior preserved only if tie-breaking order is kept identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/CutAn.summary: Entire O(bagSize^2) double loop computes conn/cut then is discarded; method unconditionally returns 1. Dead code.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/CutAn.currentCost: O(bagSize^2) memory reads of adj[bag[i]*n+bag[j]] plus two increments per pair, all results thrown away; the dp pointer is never touched.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/CutAn.proposedChange: Either implement the intended cut-and-count recurrence (use conn/cut to index dp), or, if 1 is genuinely the contract, delete the loop and the unused n/adj/bag/bagSize/dp parameters so the call collapses to a constant. As written the whole body is removable with no observable change since it returns the literal 1.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/CutAn.rationale: Removing a fully dead O(bagSize^2) loop eliminates all cycles and the bag/adj cache traffic for free; no output depends on it.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/CutAn.risk: If callers expect this to mutate dp or this is an unfinished stub, deleting changes intended (future) behavior. Observable behavior today (return value only, no side effects) is preserved either way. Confirm whether the return-1 is a placeholder before deleting vs implementing.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.summary: (1 << k) is recomputed in the loop condition and in every index expression; row base i*(1<<k) and the f[row+mask] target are recomputed repeatedly inside the submask loop.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.currentCost: Per innermost iteration: two shifts for the two (1<<k) factors in f[i*(1<<k)+sub] and g[sub*(1<<k)+mask], plus i*(1<<k) and the f[...+mask] load/compare each repeated though mask is fixed across the sub-loop. The for-mask condition reevaluates (1<<k) every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.proposedChange: Hoist int size = 1 << k; once. Precompute long* fRow = f + i*size; long* gBase = g; before the mask loop. Inside the mask loop hoist long* fTarget = fRow + mask; long best = *fTarget; then in the sub loop compute long val = fRow[sub] + g[sub*size + mask]; if (val < best) best = val; and write *fTarget = best; once after the sub loop. Compare against 2^k literal-free bound.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.rationale: Replaces repeated shifts/multiplies with hoisted invariants, turns the read-modify-write of f[row+mask] (which has a memory dependency chain) into a single register accumulator written once, and removes the (1<<k) recompute in the loop bound. Fewer ops and a shorter dependency chain in the hottest loop of an O(3^k) algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.risk: Caching best in a register and writing once is safe because f[i*size+mask] is not read elsewhere within this mask iteration (sub<mask guarantees the read indices fRow[sub] and the column g[...+mask] are distinct cells from the written cell). Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.summary: The branch `if (sub < mask)` inside the submask enumeration is always true for proper submasks generated by `sub = (mask-1)&mask` then `(sub-1)&mask`, except it guards equality which never occurs in this enumeration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.currentCost: One compare+branch per innermost iteration across O(3^k) iterations.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.proposedChange: The standard submask enumeration `for (sub = mask; sub > 0; sub = (sub-1)&mask)` starting from `(mask-1)&mask` never yields sub==mask, so sub<mask is implied by sub>0 here (the loop already starts strictly below mask). Drop the `if (sub < mask)` guard, or if the intent is to exclude only sub==mask, note it is already excluded. Verify k small enough that sub stays positive.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.rationale: Removes a predictably-taken branch from the innermost loop, shortening the per-iteration critical path and helping Burst keep the loop tight/vectorizable-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/FastS.risk: Must confirm the enumeration never produces sub>=mask. Since sub is seeded with (mask-1)&mask (strictly a proper submask) and each step masks with mask while decrementing, sub is always a proper submask < mask. If any reachable mask makes the guard meaningful, keep it. Default to keeping unless verified.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.summary: edgeW[order[i]*n + order[j]] is loaded twice per j (once in the != 0 test, once in the add), and order[i]*n is recomputed every iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.currentCost: Per j: two pointer derefs into edgeW for the same cell, plus order[i]*n multiply, plus a branch. The branch is also pointless: adding 0 when the value is 0 yields the same sum.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.proposedChange: Hoist int oi = order[i]; long* row = edgeW + (long)oi * n; before the loop. Then `for (int j = i+1; j < n; j++) sum += row[order[j]];` — drop the != 0 test entirely (adding zero is a no-op) and read each cell once.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.rationale: Halves edgeW loads, removes a multiply per iteration via row-base hoisting, and removes a branch since the conditional add is semantically identical to unconditional add of a possibly-zero value. Tighter loop, better for Burst auto-vectorization (pure load+add reduction).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.risk: Only safe if edgeW entries cannot be a sentinel where 'absent' is encoded as a nonzero value that must be skipped — but the current code sums exactly the nonzero entries and adding zero entries changes nothing, so the sum is identical. Watch long overflow is unchanged (same accumulation order).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.summary: dp[order[i]] is read after parent check; order[i] and parent[i] indexed without hoisting; the n-element zero init can be combined but is already minimal.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.currentCost: Per i: parent[i] load, branch, then order[i] load and dp[order[i]] load plus dp[parent[i]] read-modify-write. order[i] is recomputed implicitly.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.proposedChange: Hoist int p = parent[i]; int oi = order[i]; once per iteration: `if (p >= 0) dp[p] += dp[oi] + wSum;` where ComputeEdgeSum is also passed oi to avoid re-reading order[i] inside it (or inline the hoisted oi).
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.rationale: Removes duplicate order[i] indexing shared between Run and ComputeEdgeSum and shortens the dependency on parent[i]. Minor constant-factor win in an O(n^2) routine dominated by ComputeEdgeSum.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankD.risk: None; pure reindexing of the same values, identical results and accumulation order.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.summary: Uses an O(n^2) selection-style sort to rank-transform; can be O(n log n) or, if value domain is bounded, O(n + range) counting sort.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.currentCost: n(n-1)/2 compares and up to that many 3-assignment swaps for the sort phase — quadratic, dominating for larger n.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.proposedChange: Replace the nested-loop sort with an in-place heapsort or insertion-into-sorted over the stackalloc 'sorted' buffer for O(n log n) worst case (heapsort needs no extra RAM, stays unmanaged/Burst-friendly). If x values fit a known small int range, prefer counting sort: stackalloc int[range+1], tally, prefix-sum, assign ranks directly without sorting — O(n+range) and branch-light.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.rationale: Lower asymptotic complexity is the single biggest win here; the current sort is the bottleneck. Heapsort keeps the no-extra-allocation property; counting sort additionally vectorizes the tally/prefix passes well under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.risk: Heapsort changes element movement but produces the same sorted order, so identical ranks. Counting sort requires a known/bounded value range and nonnegative-or-offset indices; if x can be arbitrary int, use heapsort instead. Must preserve stable rank assignment for duplicates (rank increments only on value change), which both alternatives respect since ranks are assigned from the sorted sequence.

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.summary: stackalloc int[n] copy buffer 'sorted' could be avoided if x is allowed to be mutated, or kept but is fine; the i==0 special-case in the ranking loop is a per-iteration branch.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.currentCost: n ints of stack scratch plus an `i == 0 || ...` branch evaluated every iteration of the ranking pass.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.proposedChange: Peel the first iteration: r=1; rank[sorted[0]]=1; then loop i from 1 with only the sorted[i]!=sorted[i-1] test, dropping the i==0 disjunct. Optionally, if callers don't need x preserved, sort x in place and drop the 'sorted' stackalloc entirely.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.rationale: Loop-peeling removes a per-iteration branch; dropping the scratch buffer halves stack working set and removes the initial copy pass (n stores). Smaller working set reduces stack cache pressure on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/RankT.risk: In-place sort destroys input x — only safe if the API contract permits it; otherwise keep the copy. Loop-peel is always safe (n>=1 must be guaranteed by caller, which the unchecked Run convention assumes).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.summary: Row bases i*n and (i+1)*n are recomputed for all four array accesses every inner iteration; column index j+1 recomputed.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.currentCost: Per (i,j): two multiplies (i*n, (i+1)*n) folded into four index expressions plus repeated +j / +(j+1) address arithmetic, and four dependent loads feeding two adds and a compare.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.proposedChange: Hoist long* row0 = a + (long)i*n; long* row1 = a + (long)(i+1)*n; outside the j loop. Inner: `long lhs = row0[j] + row1[j+1]; long rhs = row0[j+1] + row1[j]; if (lhs > rhs) return false;`. row1 for iteration i becomes row0 for i+1, so you can carry the pointer and avoid one multiply per outer step.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.rationale: Eliminates the i*n / (i+1)*n multiplies from the inner loop, reducing address-generation work and shortening the index dependency chain; pointer-walking is friendlier to Burst's addressing and SIMD recognition.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.risk: None; identical loads and comparison. Use long for the base offset to avoid int overflow if m*n exceeds int range (matches the existing implicit widening).

src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.summary: Same row-base recomputation as CheckMonge: i*n and (i+1)*n folded into four index expressions per inner iteration.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.currentCost: Per (i,j): two row-base multiplies and four address computations feeding a 3-operation arithmetic chain plus a sign compare.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.proposedChange: Hoist long* row0 = a + (long)i*n; long* row1 = a + (long)(i+1)*n; before the j loop; inner becomes `long d = row0[j] - row1[j] - row0[j+1] + row1[j+1]; if (d < 0) return false;`. Carry row1 into the next outer iteration's row0 to save one multiply per row.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.rationale: Removes the per-inner-iteration multiplies and tightens address generation; pure load/arith pattern auto-vectorizes better under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Optimization.Treewidth/Conve.risk: None; identical arithmetic and branch. Widen base offset to long to preserve indexing semantics for large m*n.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Recompute of polygon edge-counting and detail-vertex counting walks the polygon arrays multiple times; the vertCount-per-poly is recomputed yet again in the storage pass.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: The Polys array (PolyCount * nvp * 2 ushorts) is scanned to count edges/portals (lines 133-154), scanned AGAIN to count unique detail verts or detail-tri count (lines 165-205), and the actual per-poly vertCount is later recomputed implicitly in the store loop (lines 300-340) and again read via navPolys[i].vertCount. That is 3-4 separate passes over the same large pointer array, each a fresh stream of cache lines.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Fuse the edge/portal counting and the no-detail triCount counting into a single pass over Polys (both only need to walk j until MeshNullIDX). When DetailMeshes==null the loop at 189-205 computes nv exactly like the loop at 133-154 already does; merge them so the array is touched once. Keep the detail-mesh branch separate only where it must read DetailMeshes.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Halves the number of streaming passes over the largest input array before any allocation, reducing cache-line fetches and loop overhead. Same arithmetic, same outputs.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Low. Must preserve that edgeCount/portalCount are accumulated regardless of detail branch, while detailTriCount (no-detail case) accumulates nv-2. Carefully keep the two accumulators independent so behavior is identical.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Per-vertex world-space transform recomputes Bmin and Cs/Ch reads from the pointer each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: In the vertex store loop (lines 266-273) createParams->Bmin.x/.y/.z, createParams->Cs and createParams->Ch are reloaded through the pointer for every vertex (VertCount iterations). The pointer dereference plus field offset is repeated though the values are loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Hoist float3 bmin = createParams->Bmin; float cs = createParams->Cs; float ch = createParams->Ch; into locals before the loop and use them. Same for the hmin/hmax estimation loop (lines 79-85) which reloads Bmin.y and Ch each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Removes repeated pointer-relative loads inside a hot per-vertex loop; lets Burst keep the constants in registers and vectorize the scale/offset. Pure register hoisting, identical results.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: None functionally; createParams is not mutated between hoist and use.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: The same offMeshConClass start-classification predicate (== 0xff) is re-tested in four separate passes over OffMeshConCount.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: offMeshConClass[(i*2)+0]==0xff gating is evaluated in the off-mesh vertex pass (277-288), the off-mesh poly pass (347-361), and the off-mesh connection pass (437-460) - three extra full scans of OffMeshConCount beyond the classification loop, each only acting on the stored subset.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: During the classification loop (95-123), record the indices (or a packed stored-flag plus running n) of stored connections into the offMeshConClass scratch (already allocated 2*count) or a small Temp index buffer, then the three later passes iterate only over storedOffMeshConCount entries instead of re-scanning and re-branching over all connections.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Off-mesh counts are usually small, but this removes three redundant branch-heavy scans and the repeated *2 index math. Constant-factor; only worthwhile if OffMeshConCount is non-trivial.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Low. Must preserve the exact ordering of n (stored index) which all three passes rely on; a recorded index list preserves order trivially.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: BV-tree construction sorts each node's full item range with O(n^2) insertion sort, giving O(n^2 log n)-ish total build cost on large tiles.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: Subdivide picks the longest axis then runs insertion sort (SortItemsX/Y/Z) over the whole [imin,imax) range, which is O(inum^2). Across the recursion this is super-linear per level; for a tile with many polys (PolyCount large) the top-level sort alone is O(PolyCount^2).
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Replace the full insertion sort with nth_element-style partitioning (median-of-three quickselect) around isplit = imin + inum/2 on the chosen axis key. Only the split position needs to be correct, not a full sort, reducing each Subdivide level to O(inum) average. Keep insertion sort as the small-range fallback (inum below ~16) for cache friendliness.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: The recursive median split only requires the array partitioned about its midpoint, not fully sorted. Quickselect is O(n) average vs O(n^2), turning total tree build from O(n^2) toward O(n log n). This is the dominant cost for large-tile navmesh builds.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Medium. Original recast uses qsort here so partial-order is acceptable; however the deterministic tie-breaking of insertion sort changes, which can alter the resulting (still valid) tree shape and node->i escape indices. Acceptable only if BV-tree shape is not part of observable contract (it is an internal acceleration structure). If serialized output must be byte-identical, reject.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Three near-identical insertion-sort functions copy a full BVItem (16+ bytes) on each shift and differ only by which key field is compared.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: Each sort moves whole BVItem structs (ushort3 BMin + ushort3 BMax + int = 16 bytes) per shift; three code copies bloat I-cache and the only difference is .BMin.x/.y/.z. The struct copies in the inner while-shift move 16 bytes per step.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Unify into one SortItems(BVItem* items, int num, int axis) that selects the key via a branch hoisted outside the inner loop (or three specialized internal generics over a key selector struct/function pointer that Burst inlines). Keeps one code path; optionally sort indices/keys instead of moving full structs when num is large.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Reduces instruction footprint (better I-cache in the recursive build) and centralizes the hot comparison. Moving keys+index rather than full structs cuts per-shift memory traffic for wide tiles.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Low for the merge. If switching to index sort, the caller (CalcExtends/leaf write) must dereference through the index, changing access patterns; keep struct-move version unless num is large.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Branchy outcode build and switch-based mapping can be made branchless.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: Four ternary branches build outcode, then an 8-case switch maps it to a side. On hot off-mesh-heavy builds this is several unpredictable branches per point.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Build outcode branchlessly via comparison-to-int (e.g. (-(pt.x>=bmax.x)) & xp) and replace the switch with a tiny 16-entry static const lookup table (byte[16] semantics via a stackalloc/const-indexed expression) mapping outcode to side, defaulting 0xff. Note x cannot be simultaneously >=bmax and <bmin so the 0x05/0x0a illegal combos just map to 0xff.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Removes per-point branch misprediction and the jump table; a single masked table index. Same mapping for all valid outcodes.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Low. Must ensure the table has 0xff for the impossible xp|xm and zp|zm combinations to match the switch default. House rule forbids managed arrays; use a const-indexed expression or stackalloc-once, not a static managed array.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Magic-number portal/edge flags (0x8000, 0xf, 0xff) are duplicated across counting and storing passes instead of using the existing named constants.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: DTExtLink (0x8000) exists as a constant but the counting pass uses literal 0x8000 (line 145, 308); MeshNullIDX is used but the dir mask 0xf and sentinel 0xf are bare literals. Divergence risk between the two passes that must agree.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Introduce named constants (e.g. DTPortalDirMask=0xf, DTBorderDir=0xf) and use DTExtLink consistently in both the count loop (145) and store loop (308) so the maxLinkCount estimate and actual storage can never drift.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Prevents a class of bugs where the two passes use different masks, and improves readability without any perf cost (constants fold).
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: None; pure constant substitution, values identical.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Per-edge DistancePtSegSqr2D call recomputes pq = vi-vj and its length, while the inside-test already loads both vertices; the division (vj.z-vi.z) is redundant with segment work.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: For each edge the loop computes the crossing test using (vj.x-vi.x), (vj.z-vi.z) and a divide, then calls DistancePtSegSqr2D(pt, vj, vi,...) which recomputes pq = vi.xz - vj.xz and lengthsq(pq). The edge vector and its squared length are computed twice per edge.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Inline the segment-distance math into the loop reusing the already-loaded vi, vj and the edge delta. Compute pq=vi.xz-vj.xz once, reuse for both the parametric t and (if needed) the inside test. Avoid the second function-call frame and duplicate subtraction.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Eliminates a redundant vector subtract and lengthsq per edge in a function called per polygon-edge during point-location queries (hot in pathfinding). Fewer ops, shorter dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Low. DistancePtSegSqr2D is AggressiveInlining-absent; inlining manually must preserve the pqLenSqr>0 guard and clamp exactly to keep identical t/distance for degenerate edges.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Triangle areas are computed and stored into a scratch buffer, then re-read in a second loop; the two passes can be fused.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: First loop fills areas[i] and accumulates areasum; second loop re-reads areas[i] to find the weighted triangle. Two passes plus a scratch buffer write/read of npts floats.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Note the selection needs areasum (total) before thresholding, so a single pass cannot pick the triangle without the total. But the max(0.001f, area) clamp used in the sum is NOT applied when reading areas[i] in the second loop (it uses raw areas[i] for dacc) - this is a latent inconsistency. If intended, keep two passes but store the clamped value to avoid recomputation; if not, document. At minimum hoist pts[0] load out of TriArea2D calls.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Reduces scratch traffic and clarifies the clamp semantics; storing the clamped area makes the second-loop dacc consistent with the running sum, avoiding selection skew. Flagged primarily for correctness-of-intent.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Medium: changing dacc to the clamped value alters which triangle/u is selected for degenerate (near-zero-area) triangles - that is a semantics change. Only apply if the clamp inconsistency is confirmed a bug; otherwise leave as-is. Reported as a flag, not a blind edit.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: The point-in-polygon crossing test reloads verts[i] and verts[j] each iteration though verts[j] equals verts[i] of the previous iteration.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: With the j=i++ idiom, vj at iteration i is vi from iteration i-1, but the code reloads verts[j] from memory each time (a redundant load of a float3 = 12 bytes per edge).
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Carry the previous vertex in a local: load vi once per iteration, set vj=prev, then prev=vi at loop end. Saves one float3 load per edge.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Removes a redundant 12-byte load per polygon edge in hot per-poly geometry tests. Pure load elimination, identical math.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: None; the algebraic relation vj_i == vi_{i-1} holds for the standard edge walk. Initialize prev = verts[nverts-1] before the loop.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Hand-rolled de-Bruijn-style log2 ladder can be replaced by a single hardware bit-scan intrinsic under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: Five conditional-shift stages (~10 dependent ops) to compute floor(log2). On Burst/SIMD targets this is a serial dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Use math.lzcnt: floor(log2(value)) == 31u - (uint)math.lzcnt(value) for value>0. Burst lowers lzcnt to a single LZCNT/CLZ instruction. Guard value==0 to preserve current behavior (current code returns 0 for input 0).
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Replaces a ~10-op dependency chain with one hardware instruction, shrinking latency and code size for a method used in tile/index sizing.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Low. Must match edge behavior: current code for value=0 yields 0 (since all shifts produce 0). 31-lzcnt(0) is undefined/31, so add an explicit value==0 -> 0 guard. Confirm math.lzcnt is Burst-intrinsic on target ABIs.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Bit-smear next-power-of-two can use lzcnt-based shift on Burst.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: For value>1: return 1u << (32 - math.lzcnt(value-1)); keep value<=1 -> 1 (and preserve current value==0 -> 0 behavior with a guard). Single shift after one lzcnt.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Shorter dependency chain via hardware CLZ vs six serial smears.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Low/medium. Current code maps 0->0 (value-- underflows to 0xffffffff, smears to 0xffffffff, ++ -> 0) - the lzcnt form must replicate the 0->0 and 1->1 edge cases explicitly or it diverges. Only worthwhile if these are hot; otherwise leave the portable smear.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: DtStraightPathOptions lacks an explicit underlying type, defaulting to int while every sibling flags enum in this file is explicitly typed (uint or byte).
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: Enum implicitly backed by System.Int32 (4 bytes). Inconsistent with DtStraightPathFlags (: byte), DtStatus/DtFindPathOptions/DtRaycastOptions (: uint) and DtDetailTriEdgeFlags (: byte) in the same file.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Declare 'public enum DtStraightPathOptions : byte' (values are 0x01/0x02/0x04, all fit in a byte) to match the codebase convention for small flag enums. If ABI/interop with native Detour expects a wider type, use ': uint' instead to match the other Dt* flag enums.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Consistency makes the intended storage width explicit and avoids accidental signed-vs-unsigned semantics on bit operations. It is currently passed only as a method argument (DtNavMeshQuery), never stored in a blittable struct, so this is API hygiene, not a layout win.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: None observable for the bit-test usages (& / != 0) found in DtNavMeshQuery. Only matters if the type is ever marshalled to native code with a fixed-width expectation; pick the width (byte vs uint) that matches that ABI. No behavior change for the current managed callers.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.summary: Detail flags (WrongMagic..AlreadyOccupied) use signed int literals (1 << n) inside a uint-backed [Flags] enum, mixing signed and unsigned literal forms.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.currentCost: Mixed literal styles: high bits use '1u << 31', detail bits use '1 << 0'. The signed literals are implicitly converted to uint at compile time; correct today but stylistically inconsistent and a latent hazard if a future flag uses bit 31 with the signed form.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.proposedChange: Write all flag values with unsigned literals: 1u << 0, 1u << 1, ... 1u << 7, matching the Failure/Success/InProgress entries and the enum's ': uint' base.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.rationale: Uniform unsigned literals eliminate any implicit signed->unsigned narrowing and make the all-uint intent explicit, reducing the chance of a sign-extension surprise on a future high-bit flag.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/De.risk: Zero behavior change for the current values (all in bits 0-7, identical numerically). Pure source-level consistency fix.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Stack pop-front shifts the entire array every iteration, making the BFS O(n^2) in nodes processed.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: Both methods pop the front of a stackalloc'd DtNode* array with `var curNode = stack[0]; for (i=0;i<nStack-1;++i) stack[i]=stack[i+1]; nStack--;` (lines ~2594-2600 and ~3965-3971). Each pop is an O(nStack) memmove; with maxStack=48 and full traversals this is up to ~48x redundant pointer copies per pop, a quadratic dependency chain that Burst cannot elide.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Treat the buffer as a ring/queue with a head index instead of shifting: keep `int head=0,tail=0`; push at `stack[tail++ % maxStack]` (or just `stack[nStack++]` with a separate `head` read cursor `var curNode = stack[head++];`). Since both already cap pushes at maxStack and never wrap (BFS bounded), the simplest fix is a monotonic `head` cursor: replace the shift with `var curNode = stack[front++];` and test `front < nStack` for loop continuation; reset front/nStack together. No element is moved.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Removes the inner O(n) shift, turning each pop from O(n) into O(1); total work drops from O(n^2) to O(n) memory traffic. Eliminates a long serial copy chain that stalls the pipeline and pollutes cache lines holding live DtNode*.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Must preserve FIFO order (these are breadth-first 'pop front' searches, so ordering is observable for tie-breaking and result order). A head-cursor preserves exact FIFO order. Watch that pushes stop at maxStack as before so head never overruns tail; current code already guards `nStack < maxStack`.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: When fromPoly is an off-mesh connection, the link list is scanned twice for the same target ref.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: Lines ~1131-1158: the first loop walks fromPoly->firstLink to find the link to `to` and stores it in `link`. Then the off-mesh branch (line ~1150) walks fromPoly->firstLink AGAIN searching for the identical `polyRef == to` to read `edge`. Two full linked-list traversals where one suffices.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Reuse the `link` already found in the first loop: in the off-mesh branch read `var v = link->edge; left = right = fromTile->verts[fromPoly->verts[v]];` directly, deleting the second for-loop. The first loop already guarantees `link != null` reached this point.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Removes a second pointer-chasing traversal (links are a freelist, so each hop is a likely cache miss). Halves the link-walk cost on off-mesh portals, which are hit on every path that crosses a jump link.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Must confirm the first loop's matched link is the same one the second loop would select (both match `polyRef == to`); it is — the second loop's first match is identical. Behavior preserved exactly.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Recomputes two line slopes with divisions even when the horizontal-overlap test fails early, and divides redundantly.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: Lines ~2505-2541: after the `minx>maxx` early-out, it always computes `ad = (amax.y-amin.y)/(amax.x-amin.x)` and `bd = (bmax.y-bmin.y)/(bmax.x-bmin.x)` — two float divides — then four multiply-adds. Called per candidate edge inside FindConnectingPolys' O(polyCount * vertCount) loop during tile stitching.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: The early-out is already present (good). Additional win: amin/amax come from CalcSlabEndPoints which guarantees amin.x<=amax.x, so the denominators are the slab spans; hoist `1/(amax.x-amin.x)` and `1/(bmax.x-bmin.x)` as reciprocals computed once and reuse via multiply (slope*x). Also fuse the four interpolations: dmin/dmax only need (bd*minx+bk)-(ad*minx+ak) which simplifies to `(bd-ad)*minx + (bk-ak)`; compute the line `((bd-ad)*x + (bk-ak))` at minx and maxx — 2 mul-adds instead of 4 plus two subtractions.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Cuts two divides to (optionally) reciprocal-multiplies and halves the interpolation FLOPs by algebraically combining the two lines before evaluating. Division latency (~20+ cycles) dominates this routine; reducing count matters during AddTile stitching.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Algebraic refactor of dmin/dmax preserves IEEE results only approximately (reassociation changes rounding). Since this feeds a tolerance test against `py*py*4`, the tiny rounding delta is within the existing epsilon, but to be strictly semantics-preserving keep the same evaluation order and only hoist the reciprocal (mul vs div is itself a rounding change too). Flag as low-impact / verify-with-tests.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Polygon edge wrap-around uses integer modulo in many hot loops though it only ever wraps by at most 1.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: Numerous sites compute the next vertex as `(j + 1) % nv` or `(link->edge + 1) % poly->vertCount` (e.g. ConnectExternalLinks line ~1765, FindConnectingPolys ~2409, GetPortalPoints ~1180, Raycast ~2442/~2495, FindDistanceToWall ~3841). vertCount is small and not power-of-two, so `%` emits a hardware divide (~20-30 cycles) where the value can only be `j+1` or 0.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Replace `(j + 1) % nv` with a branchless/cheap wrap `var jn = j + 1; if (jn == nv) jn = 0;` or `var jn = j + 1 == nv ? 0 : j + 1;`. The Raycast code already uses the conditional form at line ~2510 (`segMax+1 < nv ? segMax+1 : 0`) — apply that pattern consistently.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: A compare+cmov replaces an integer division. Since the increment is always 1 and the loop guarantees j in [0,nv), the conditional is exactly equivalent and ~10x cheaper, and removes a divider dependency from tight per-edge loops executed across every link/portal walk.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Exactly equivalent for the only reachable inputs (0 <= j < nv). No signed/overflow concern since j+1 <= nv. Purely faster.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: For each candidate-vs-result overlap check it re-walks curPoly's link list to decide if the pair is connected, inside a doubly-nested result loop.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: Lines ~4044-4058: the overlap loop over the n stored results, for each `pastRef`, walks `curPoly->firstLink` again to test connectivity. That is O(results * links) per popped node, redundantly re-traversing the same link list `n` times per node.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Hoist the connected-set out of the inner loop: before the `for j` loop, scan curPoly's links once into a small stackalloc set/bitset of neighbour refs (the link count is bounded), then the inner test becomes a membership check instead of a full re-walk. Given DTVertsPerPolygon=6 the link count is tiny, so a linear scan of a cached stack array is fine and removes the repeated firstLink chase.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Turns O(n * linkCount) link-list pointer-chasing per node into O(linkCount) once plus O(n * linkCount) cheap array scans over contiguous memory, avoiding repeated freelist cache misses. Lower asymptotic constant on the neighbourhood query.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Must collect the same set of refs the inline walk compares against (all link->polyRef of curPoly). Equivalent results. Bound the cached array by the max links per poly to avoid overflow.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Triangle vertex selection uses a 3-way `j switch { 0=>tri->x, 1=>tri->y, _=>tri->z }` inside the innermost loops, generating branchy non-vectorizable code.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: In ClosestPointOnDetailEdges (lines ~1286, ~1301-1302) and GetPolyHeight (line ~1394) every triangle vertex fetch evaluates a switch on a loop index to pick x/y/z from a byte4 `tri`. This is 2-3 compares/branches per vertex per triangle, repeated over triCount*3, defeating Burst's ability to keep the triangle indices in a vector register.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Load the triangle once into a local `byte4 t = *tri;` and index it positionally via a fixed-size local array or the byte4's component accessor by stuffing `(&t.x)[j]` (byte4 is a sequential struct of bytes), or precompute `int3 idx = new int3(tri->x, tri->y, tri->z);` and read `idx[j]`. Unity.Mathematics int3 indexer is branchless. Same for the k/jLoop pair in the edge loop.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Replaces a data-dependent branch ladder with a single indexed load (int3 indexer compiles to a shuffle/extract), shortening the dependency chain and letting Burst vectorize the surrounding triangle iteration. Fewer mispredicted branches on irregular detail meshes.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: byte4 raw-pointer indexing relies on sequential layout (it is [StructLayout? confirm] a plain x,y,z,w struct, so `(&t.x)[j]` is valid only if no padding — int3 path avoids that concern). Use the int3 local to stay fully safe; semantics identical since it only reorders the same reads.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.symbol: GetPolyHeight (stackalloc verts + double work on fallback)
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: On the edge-fallback path GetPolyHeight re-walks all detail triangles via ClosestPointOnDetailEdges after already walking them once, and re-fetches poly verts it already gathered.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: Lines ~1361-1418: GetPolyHeight gathers poly verts into a stackalloc Span (PointInPolygon), then loops all detail tris calling ClosestHeightPointTriangle; if none succeed it calls ClosestPointOnDetailEdges which loops the SAME detail tris again and re-derives the SAME triangle vertices from scratch. The poly->verts gather is also redundant with what ClosestPointOnDetailEdges recomputes.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: The fallback is documented as rare, so the double-walk is acceptable, but the per-triangle vertex derivation (the j-switch from the other finding) is shared; factoring a single `GetDetailTriVerts(tile, poly, pd, tri, out float3x3 v)` AggressiveInlining helper removes duplicated index logic and lets both the height loop and edge loop reuse identical, branch-reduced code. No extra correctness risk since it is a pure extraction.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Deduplicates the hottest inner computation (vertex fetch) into one inlinable unit, reducing code size / I-cache pressure and giving Burst one well-shaped loop body to optimize instead of two divergent copies.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Pure refactor; must keep the `triIndex < poly->vertCount` branch semantics identical (main verts vs detail verts). No numeric change.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Per-call recomputation of constant bit masks in the non-DT_POLYREF32 (default 64-bit) decode path.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: In the #else branch, DecodePolyId (lines ~1156-1161) and the single-field decoders recompute `(1ul << Detour.DTSaltBits)-1` etc. on every call. These are compile-time constants (DTSaltBits/DTTileBits/DTPolyBits are consts), so the JIT/Burst should fold them, but the shifts are written as runtime expressions. DecodePolyId is called on essentially every link/neighbour visit in every search (GetTileAndPolyByRef* hot path).
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Promote the masks to `private const DtPolyRef SaltMask64 = (1ul << Detour.DTSaltBits) - 1;` (and TileMask64/PolyMask64) named constants and use them directly. This guarantees constant-folding regardless of Burst const-propagation and documents intent. The methods already carry AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Removes any residual shift/sub from the decode and guarantees the masks are immediates. Even if Burst already folds them, making them named consts removes risk of de-optimization and tidies the hottest decode used by GetTileAndPolyByRefUnsafe in every A* expansion.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: None functional; constants equal the current expressions. Only applies to the 64-bit branch (the shipped default per code layout).

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Each section pointer getter re-reads this.Header and re-derives all prior section offsets, so chained access in AddTile recomputes the same prefix repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: Properties chain: Polygons reads Vertices (which reads Header), Links reads Polygons, DetailMeshes reads Links+Header, etc. In AddTile (DtNavMesh.cs ~310-318) eight section pointers are fetched in sequence; because each getter recomputes the whole prefix from data+header fields, the same header field loads and pointer arithmetic are repeated O(sections^2) times. Header is `(DtMeshHeader*)data` re-cast each time.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Add a single method `void GetSections(out float3* verts, out DtPoly* polys, ...)` (or have AddTile compute the running offset once) that walks the layout linearly with one accumulating pointer, assigning all eight tile fields in one pass. Keep the individual properties for ergonomic single-field access. AddTile is one-shot per tile load, so impact is small but it removes quadratic offset recompute and repeated header dereferences.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Single linear pass computes each section base from the previous one with one add, instead of re-deriving the prefix per property. Fewer header loads, fewer multiplies, smaller code at the call site.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Layout order must match exactly the existing property chain (verts, polys, links, detailMeshes, detailVerts, detailTris, bvTree, offMeshCons). Any mismatch corrupts tile pointers — mechanical but verify against the property definitions.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Replace signed (i-1)/2 parent computation with unsigned shift to drop the signed-division sign-correction sequence in the A* heap hot path.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: `parent = (i - 1) / 2` divides a signed int by 2. Because the compiler cannot prove (i-1) is non-negative, it emits the full signed-divide-by-constant idiom (shift + sign-bit add/cmov), roughly 3-4 extra ops per loop iteration, executed once per heap level on every Push and every Pop's final BubbleUp.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Compute the parent as `int parent = (int)((uint)(i - 1) >> 1);` (or keep `i` and write `(i - 1) >> 1` only once i>0 is guaranteed). Since the loop body only runs while `i > 0`, `i - 1 >= 0`, so an unsigned `>> 1` is exactly `(i-1)/2`. Hoist the first `parent` computation inside/after the `i>0` guard so the initial pre-loop computation (where i could be 0 -> (i-1) = -1) is never division-corrected.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: For non-negative operands, arithmetic `/2` and logical `>>1` produce identical results, but `>>1` is a single-cycle op versus the multi-op signed-division-by-constant lowering. This runs O(log n) times per heap operation and the heap operation count dominates A* search.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Pre-loop `parent = (i-1)/2` with i==0 yields (-1)/2 == 0 in signed, but `(uint)(-1)>>1` == 0x7FFFFFFF. That value is only consumed inside the loop guarded by `i>0`, so it is never dereferenced — still, to be safe, only compute parent after confirming i>0 (move it to loop end / use the guarded form). With that guard the change is exactly semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Replace signed (i*2)+1 child index with unsigned shift, and reduce the dependency chain on heap[child]->total reloads.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: `child = (i * 2) + 1` uses signed multiply (cheap) but pairs with the BubbleUp signed-div issue; more importantly each iteration does two pointer-chasing loads `heap[child]->total` and `heap[child+1]->total` that feed a branch. Runs O(log n) per Pop.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Use `int child = ((int)((uint)i << 1)) | 1;` (i>=0 so `i<<1` cannot overflow into sign within valid heap sizes). Cache `float tChild = this.heap[child]->total;` once and compare against `this.heap[child+1]->total` so the chosen child's total is reused by the subsequent `BubbleUp(i, node)` comparison path where possible; at minimum avoid recomputing `i*2+1` twice by reusing a local.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: `<<1 | 1` is branch-free integer arithmetic matching `i*2+1` for non-negative i. Caching the total of the selected child removes a redundant dependent load before the swap store. Both shave fixed cycles per heap level on the Pop critical path.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Multiplication semantics are identical for in-range i; the only caveat is overflow if i were near int.MAX, which is impossible since child<size<=capacity (a reasonable node count). No observable behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Mark the private heap helpers (and Push/Pop) AggressiveInlining so the hot A* loop avoids call overhead.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: `BubbleUp` and `TrickleDown` are private leaf-ish methods called from Push/Pop/Modify with no inlining hint. Top() has the hint but Push/Pop/BubbleUp/TrickleDown do not. Each Push/Pop incurs a call frame plus the helper call frame.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to `BubbleUp` and `TrickleDown` (and optionally Push/Pop). Under Burst these become straight-line code with the loop bodies inlined into the caller, enabling register allocation of `size`/`heap` across the boundary.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Removing the call boundary lets Burst/LLVM keep `this.heap`, `this.size`, and the node pointer in registers and fuse the BubbleUp tail-call inside TrickleDown, cutting prologue/epilogue and spill traffic on the search hot path.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Pure inlining hint; no semantic change. Slight code-size growth, acceptable on the A* hot path.

src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.summary: Modify is an O(n) linear scan over the heap to locate a node before re-bubbling; flag as a structural cost.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.currentCost: `for i in 0..size: if heap[i]==node` is O(n) per call. In A* with node re-relaxation this is called per improved neighbor, making the queue-update path O(n) instead of O(log n).
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.proposedChange: Store the heap slot index back into the DtNode (it already has spare reserved bits in packedData, or use State-adjacent storage) so Modify can jump directly to the node's slot and call BubbleUp in O(log n). Maintaining the index requires updating it on every store in BubbleUp/TrickleDown. If the API/struct cannot change, leave as-is — this is a design tradeoff, not a free win.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.rationale: Reduces Modify from O(n) to O(log n), turning the dominant re-relaxation cost in dense graphs from linear to logarithmic.
src/IAFahim.Pathfinding.Recast/Detour/Dt.risk: Requires writing the slot index on every heap store (extra writes in BubbleUp/TrickleDown) and a free bit in DtNode; if those stores outweigh the scan for small heaps it can regress.
