src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.risk: Must use unsigned-style logical reasoning, but XOR/right-shift here is on the bit pattern only; the standard 6-step parallel-prefix XOR is exactly equivalent to the iterative inverse-Gray for all 64-bit inputs. For signed long use the arithmetic-vs-logical shift caveat: since we XOR the value with shifted copies, a sign-extending '>>' on negative g produces extra high bits; cast to ulong for the shifts (or shift then mask) to guarantee identity with the loop, which treats g as a magnitude that decays to 0. Guard: perform the prefix XOR on (ulong)g and cast back.

src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.summary: Repeated 'for i: seen[i]=false' init loops over stackalloc bool[n]; stackalloc is already zero-initialized in C#, so the loops are redundant.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.currentCost: An extra full O(n) write pass over the bool[] (and long[] used[]) arrays purely to set them to false/zero, which stackalloc already guarantees in C#.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.proposedChange: Drop the explicit 'for (...) seen[i] = false;' / 'used[i] = false;' loops - C# zero-initializes stackalloc memory by default. If the project ever compiles with [SkipLocalsInit], keep the loops or use a single memset; otherwise remove them.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.rationale: Eliminates an O(n) initialization pass per call with no behavioral change (false == default(bool) == 0).
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.risk: ONLY safe if [SkipLocalsInit] / module-level SkipLocalsInit is NOT applied to this assembly. Verify no SkipLocalsInit attribute before removing; under Burst, stackalloc is likewise zeroed unless localsinit is stripped. State the guard explicitly: keep loops if SkipLocalsInit is present.

src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.summary: ComposeInto writes to tmp then MemoryCopy's tmp back into a every call; ping-pong buffers to skip the copy.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.currentCost: Each composition does an O(n) compute into tmp plus an O(n) Buffer.MemoryCopy back into a - doubling memory traffic per multiply. PermPower performs up to 2*log2(k) compositions.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.proposedChange: Use double-buffering: alternate between two scratch buffers for result and basePerm so each ComposeInto writes the new permutation into the spare buffer and swaps pointers (swap is free) instead of copying. Eliminates the per-call MemoryCopy entirely.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.rationale: Halves the memory bandwidth of the hot exponentiation loop (compute pass only, no copy-back pass). Pointer swap is O(1) vs O(n) copy.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/Permutation.cs.risk: Requires tracking which buffer currently holds the live value and ensuring result/basePerm point to the right buffer at loop exit (may need one final copy into the caller's result if parity lands on the scratch buffer). Behavior identical if final destination is reconciled. Slightly more bookkeeping.

src/IAFahim.Permutation/NextPermutation..summary: Cache ptr[i] in the descending j-scan instead of re-loading and re-comparing through CompareTo each iteration.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/NextPermutation..currentCost: The j-loop calls ptr[j].CompareTo(ptr[i]) each step, reloading ptr[i] (the pivot) every iteration and going through the IComparable<T> interface comparison.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/NextPermutation..proposedChange: T pivot = ptr[i]; while (ptr[j].CompareTo(pivot) <= 0) j--; - hoist the invariant pivot load out of the loop. Same pattern applies to the i-scan where ptr[i+1] vs ptr[i] could reuse one loaded value across steps.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/NextPermutation..rationale: Removes a redundant load per iteration and shortens the dependency chain on the pivot; the value of ptr[i] is loop-invariant in the j-scan.
src/IAFahim.Permutation/NextPermutation..risk: None for the j-scan (ptr[i] is not modified there). For T being a generic unmanaged struct, CompareTo on IComparable<T> may still not inline under Burst; consider an il2cpp/Burst-friendly constrained call, but that is orthogonal. Identical results.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.summary: The local matrix s (the 3x3 symmetric A^T*A) is fully computed but never used; the method returns apq instead. ~18 mul + 18 add of dead work per call.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.currentCost: Builds a full 9-element float3x3 s (each element a 3-term dot product => 27 muls / 18 adds) on every call, then discards it and returns apq.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.proposedChange: Delete the entire 'float3x3 s = new float3x3(...)' construction and just keep/return apq. (Also note the method does NOT actually polar-decompose to a rotation; it returns the raw Apq covariance. If extracting a true rotation was intended, that is a correctness gap, but for pure dead-code removal just drop s.)
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.rationale: Removing a never-read computation eliminates ~45 float ops per ComputeOptimalRotation call with zero observable change, since s is local and unused.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.risk: None for behavior: s is a local that is never returned or read, so removing it is semantics-preserving. Separately flag to the author that the function name promises a rotation but returns the covariance matrix Apq.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.summary: mass = 1/invMass is recomputed via division three separate times per particle across three passes, and positions/restPositions are streamed three times.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.currentCost: For each particle: ComputeCenterOfMass(positions) divides once, ComputeCenterOfMass(restPositions) divides once, ComputeOptimalRotation divides once => 3 float divisions plus 3 separate read passes over the same N elements (3x memory traffic, 3 loop overheads).
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.proposedChange: Precompute mass[i] once (or fuse the two center-of-mass passes and the Apq pass). At minimum, since ComputeOptimalRotation already has the per-i mass, and the rest masses equal the live masses (same invMasses array), compute totalMass and both weighted sums (positions and restPositions) in a single loop, then a single division per particle reused for the Apq accumulation. Reduces 3N divisions to N and 3 passes to 2 (one for centers, one for Apq, or fully fused if centers are needed first).
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.rationale: Division is ~10-20x the cost of mul on most targets and is on the dependency-critical path; collapsing 3N divs to N and 3 streaming passes to fewer cuts both ALU and cache traffic. Fewer loop bodies also help Burst vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.risk: Apq needs the centers first, so full single-pass fusion isn't possible without a two-pass structure; keep centers in pass 1 and Apq in pass 2. Reusing mass requires a scratch buffer (stackalloc/caller-provided) — acceptable under house rules, or just hoist the two CoM loops into one to avoid double-streaming without extra storage.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.summary: alpha is loop-invariant and w=1/(invMass+alpha) plus min(1,w) can be simplified; division per particle is on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.currentCost: Per particle: one division 1/(invMasses[i]+alpha) then math.min(1,w). The min(1,w) clamp means when w>=1 the division result is partly wasted.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.proposedChange: Keep the per-i division (it depends on invMasses[i]) but note alpha is already hoisted — fine. Consider that w>1 only when invMasses[i] < 1-alpha; the math.min is a cheap branchless clamp so leave it. Primary win here is reusing the mass/division from the fused pass above rather than a fresh divide.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.rationale: Avoids an extra reciprocal per particle when the value is already derivable; min stays branchless.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/ShapeMatchingCo.risk: invMasses[i]+alpha could be ~0 only if both are ~0; restitution-free here, but division by near-zero is the same risk as current code, so no new edge case.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/BendingConstrai.summary: Two math.length calls each do a sqrt then code divides by len; using rsqrt-style normalize and reusing 1/len avoids redundant divides, and grad1/grad2 share subexpressions with grad0.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/BendingConstrai.currentCost: len1,len2 via 2 sqrt; then 4 divisions by len1/len2 (n1=d1/len1, n2=d2/len2, and grad terms /len1 and /len2). grad0 recomputes (-n2+cos*n1) and (-n1+cos*n2) which are exactly -grad1*len1-style negations of grad1 and grad2 numerators.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/BendingConstrai.proposedChange: Compute invLen1=1/len1, invLen2=1/len2 once; n1=d1*invLen1, n2=d2*invLen2. Note grad1 = (n2 - cos*n1)*invLen1 and grad2 = (n1 - cos*n2)*invLen2, and grad0 = -( (n2-cos*n1)*invLen1 + (n1-cos*n2)*invLen2 ) = -(grad1+grad2). So replace the explicit grad0 expression with grad0 = -(grad1+grad2), removing two vector adds/subs and a redundant division group.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/BendingConstrai.rationale: grad0 = -(grad1+grad2) is an algebraic identity from the constraint gradient (sum of gradients is zero for a translation-invariant constraint), saving ~2 float3 builds and 2 divisions; reusing invLen turns 4 divides into 2 mul-by-reciprocal groups.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/BendingConstrai.risk: Identity holds exactly in real arithmetic; in float it changes rounding of grad0 slightly (not bit-identical). If exact bit-reproducibility is required this is a behavior change — gate behind a 'fast' variant. The reciprocal reuse (mul by 1/len vs divide) is also not bit-identical to division.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/VolumeConstrain.summary: OneSixth is multiplied into volume and into each of three gradients, then squared in lengthsq; the 1/6 factors can be factored out of w and folded.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/VolumeConstrain.currentCost: 4 separate '* OneSixth' multiplies (volume, grad1, grad2, grad3) plus grad0 sum; then w uses lengthsq of the already-scaled grads (each lengthsq re-multiplies). The 1/6 appears squared inside w and linearly in c.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/VolumeConstrain.proposedChange: Compute raw cross products g1=cross(d2,d3), g2=cross(d3,d1), g3=cross(d1,d2), g0=-(g1+g2+g3) WITHOUT the 1/6. Then volume=dot(g1,d1)*OneSixth (or dot(cross(d1,d2),d3)*OneSixth). w_raw = invMass0*lengthsq(g0)+...; the true w = w_raw*OneSixth*OneSixth. c = volume-restVolume. lambda = -c/(w_raw*(1/36) + alpha). Final position update uses grad_i = g_i*OneSixth, i.e. delta = invMass_i*lambda*OneSixth*g_i — fold OneSixth*lambda into a scalar k once. Removes 3 vector scalings from the gradient construction.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/VolumeConstrain.rationale: Folds four float3 scalar-multiplies into scalar constant folding (1/36 precomputed as a named const), trimming vector ALU ops on the hot path while keeping the same math.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/VolumeConstrain.risk: Floating-point: factoring 1/6 out of squared terms changes rounding (w_raw*1/36 vs scaling-then-square). Not bit-identical. Precompute OneThirtySixth as a named const to satisfy house rules. Behavior preserved to rounding tolerance only.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.summary: dist uses math.length (sqrt) but the early-out only needs dist vs minDist; and invMassA/totalInvMass plus invMassB/totalInvMass are two divisions where one reciprocal suffices.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.currentCost: math.length = sqrt; then two divisions invMassA/totalInvMass and invMassB/totalInvMass; n=delta/dist is another division.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.proposedChange: Compute invTotal = 1.0f/totalInvMass once and multiply (invMassA*invTotal, invMassB*invTotal), replacing 2 divisions with 1 division + 2 muls. The squared-distance early-out is not applicable since n and overlap need the true dist, but n=delta/dist can reuse invDist=1/dist: n=delta*invDist (1 division reused as reciprocal). Keep sqrt since overlap=minDist-dist needs real distance.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.rationale: Replaces 3 divisions (n, two mass splits) with 1 (dist) + 1 reciprocal(totalInvMass) + muls; division is the dominant-latency op here.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.risk: Reordering totalInvMass check: currently dist/minDist check happens before totalInvMass check, so reciprocal of totalInvMass is only taken after the <1e-12 guard — preserve that ordering to avoid div-by-zero. Reciprocal-mul is not bit-identical to division.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.summary: Files import System but none of these files use any System type; the using is dead across all five files.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.currentCost: 'using System;' present in BendingConstraint, CollisionConstraint, DistanceConstraint, ShapeMatchingConstraint, VolumeConstraint with no System reference.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.proposedChange: Remove 'using System;' from all five files (only System.Runtime.CompilerServices and Unity.Mathematics are used).
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.rationale: Pure hygiene; no runtime effect but reduces noise and avoids accidental reliance on System managed types in a Burst module.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.risk: None — if any file later needs System it can be re-added. Confirm no System.* usage (verified: none in the five files).

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.summary: vt (tangential) is computed unconditionally but only used inside the restitution branch.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.currentCost: float3 vn and float3 vt = *vel - vn computed before the 'if (dot(vn,planeNormal) < 0)' branch; when that branch is not taken (separating velocity), vt subtraction is wasted.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.proposedChange: Move the 'float3 vt = *vel - vn;' (and the vn build) inside the if-block, or compute vn lazily, so the tangential subtraction only runs when a velocity response is applied. The position correction *pos -= d*planeNormal does not need vn/vt.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.rationale: Avoids a float3 subtract (and the vn projection) on the common separating-velocity path; pure hoist-into-branch.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/CollisionConstr.risk: None — vn/vt are only read inside the branch; moving them in is semantics-preserving. Slight code-size increase but no behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.summary: n=delta/dist divides a vector by sqrt; lambda then multiplies n. The division and normalization can fuse using a reciprocal, and alpha/(dt*dt) division is loop-invariant per call only.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.currentCost: sqrt (length) + 1 vector division (delta/dist) + scalar division (compliance/(dt*dt)) + scalar division (-c/(w+alpha)).
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.proposedChange: correction = lambda * n = (-c/(w+alpha)) * (delta/dist). Combine into scalar k = -c / ((w+alpha)*dist) then correction = k*delta, removing the separate vector normalization division (delta/dist) — one scalar division instead of a vector division plus reuse. invDt2 could be passed precomputed by caller, but within one call dt*dt is cheap.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.rationale: Folds the vector divide-by-dist and the lambda scalar divide into a single scalar division k, then a vector*scalar — fewer divisions, shorter dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.risk: Not bit-identical (reassociation of divisions). w+alpha and dist are both already guarded > small epsilon, so no new div-by-zero. dist>=1e-8 guard already present.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.summary: Replace length()+divide-by-dist with a single rsqrt to normalize delta, avoiding one sqrt and one vector divide.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.currentCost: math.length(delta) = sqrt(dot(delta,delta)) (one sqrt), then n = delta / dist is a 3-component divide (reciprocal + 3 muls, or 3 divides). The high-latency sqrt feeds directly into the divide, forming a long dependency chain. c = dist - restLength also needs the actual dist.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.proposedChange: float lenSq = math.dot(delta, delta); guard if (lenSq < 1e-16f) return; float invDist = math.rsqrt(lenSq); float dist = lenSq * invDist; float3 n = delta * invDist; This produces n with one rsqrt + muls instead of sqrt + divide, and still yields dist for c = dist - restLength.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.rationale: rsqrt is lower-latency than sqrt+div on most targets and lets normalization use multiplies (vectorizable) instead of a divide. Shortens the critical dependency chain delta->dist->n into delta->invDist->{dist,n} computed in parallel.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/DistanceConstra.risk: rsqrt may be slightly less precise than 1/sqrt on some hardware; for a relaxation solver this is acceptable but is NOT bit-identical to math.length, so it is a semantics-approximating change, not strictly bit-preserving. The early-out threshold must be squared (1e-16f vs 1e-8f) to keep the same cutoff. On mobile some GPUs/CPUs differ in rsqrt accuracy; if exact parity with the current build is required, reject this opt.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..summary: Drop the unused velocity arrays/pointers from the per-constraint solve call: they are dead loads and dead arguments.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..currentCost: Each loop iteration computes two extra pointer addresses (&velocities[idxA], &velocities[idxB]) and pushes the velocities base pointer plus two pointer args into DistanceConstraint.Solve, which never reads *velA/*velB. That is 2 extra LEA/address computations and 3 extra argument moves per constraint, plus a dependency on idxA/idxB before the call even though the velocities are irrelevant.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..proposedChange: Remove the velocities parameter from SolveDistanceConstraints (and velA/velB from DistanceConstraint.Solve), so the loop only forms &positions[idxA]/&positions[idxB]. Since Solve is AggressiveInlining the compiler MAY eliminate the dead args after inlining, but trimming the signature guarantees it and shrinks the public API to only what is used.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..rationale: Eliminates redundant address arithmetic and argument register/stack traffic in the hottest loop of the solver. Fewer live values reduces register pressure inside the (large constraintCount) loop and shortens the dependency chain to the actual position update.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..risk: Signature change is API-breaking; callers passing velocities must be updated. Observable position output is unchanged because velA/velB are provably unused in Solve. If the velocity arrays are intended for a future velocity-projection step, keep them but still drop the per-iteration &velocities indexing until used.

src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..summary: Hoist the dt*dt reciprocal out of the per-constraint loop and pass it to Solve as a precomputed invDtSq.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..currentCost: Inside DistanceConstraint.Solve, alpha = compliance / (dt*dt) recomputes dt*dt and a divide for every constraint, even though dt is constant for the whole SolveDistanceConstraints call. That is one mul + one divide per constraint that depends only on a loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..proposedChange: Compute float invDtSq = 1.0f / (dt * dt); once before the loop in SolveDistanceConstraints (guarding dt below threshold once), and pass invDtSq into a Solve overload that does alpha = compliance * invDtSq. This turns a per-constraint divide into a per-constraint multiply.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..rationale: Strength-reduces a per-iteration division to a multiplication and removes a redundant invariant computation from the hot loop, lowering throughput cost across constraintCount iterations.
src/IAFahim.Physics.Xpbd/XpbdIntegrator..risk: Changes Solve's signature/overload. Numerically compliance*(1/(dt*dt)) is not always bit-identical to compliance/(dt*dt) due to rounding of the reciprocal; for an iterative solver this is negligible but not bit-exact. If dt can be ~0, the single hoisted reciprocal must reproduce the existing per-call behavior (currently Solve would produce inf alpha and then return via the w+alpha guard only if alpha is finite); verify the dt<1e-8 path is handled at the caller as it is in UpdateVelocity.

src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.summary: Hoist b-column access into row-major form and reduce modulo frequency to cut the modulo-per-multiply cost and improve cache behavior in the innermost k-loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.currentCost: Inner loop does b[k*n+j] (column-strided, cache-unfriendly: stride n*8 bytes) plus one 64-bit modulo per k iteration. For n^3 inner iterations that is n^3 divisions and n^3 strided loads -> heavy DIV-port pressure and TLB/cache misses.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.proposedChange: Reorder loops to i-k-j (cache-friendly: stream b row b[k*n+j] sequentially, accumulate into tmp row tmp[i*n+j]). Compute aik=a[i*n+k] once per (i,k), and apply % mod once after the j-accumulation pass per element rather than every k step where the running sum cannot overflow. Concretely: since mod fits in long and inputs are already reduced (< mod), if mod <= ~3037000499 (sqrt(2^63)) then a[i*n+k]*b[k*n+j] < 2^63 and sum stays bounded by reducing only when sum could overflow; otherwise keep per-step %. Minimum safe win: keep per-step % but switch to i-k-j ordering with aik hoisted, eliminating the column-strided b access and the repeated a[i*n+k] index recomputation.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.rationale: i-k-j ordering turns the inner loop into two sequential streams (b row, tmp row) that Burst/SLP can vectorize and the prefetcher loves, versus the current i-j-k which reads a column of b with stride n. Hoisting aik removes one multiply-add address computation per inner iteration. Both lower cycles and cache misses with identical numeric results when % is kept per step.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.risk: i-k-j reordering with per-step % is bit-exact identical to i-j-k per-step % because (sum + x) % mod is applied after each add regardless of accumulation order ONLY IF the same set of products is summed in the same order; i-k-j changes summation order. Modular addition is associative/commutative so the final residue is identical, but intermediate values differ — final result provably equal mod p. Deferring the % (the overflow-conditional variant) is only safe when mod*mod + mod < 2^63 (mod < ~3.03e9) AND inputs pre-reduced; must guard with a named constant MaxDeferMod or reject. Signed long products of pre-reduced non-negative residues stay non-negative, no signed-% pitfall.

src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.summary: Eliminate the per-call stackalloc scratch buffer and the trailing MemoryCopy by writing the product into a caller-provided ping-pong buffer.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.currentCost: Each MultiplyMatrices does stackalloc long[n*n] (grows stack per call inside a loop-driven recursion-free path; repeated stackalloc in the squaring loop reuses frame but still zero-inits cost is avoided, yet the n*n*8-byte MemoryCopy at the end is a full extra pass over the matrix every multiply).
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.proposedChange: Hoist two n*n buffers in Run (src/dst) and ping-pong: MultiplyMatrices writes result into dst and the caller swaps pointers, removing the final Buffer.MemoryCopy(tmp,a,...) entirely. Pass dst as an out pointer; Run already owns temp and result, just add a second temp for squaring.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.rationale: Removes one full n*n*8-byte memory pass (the copy-back) per matrix multiply. In matrix-pow there are O(log exp) squarings plus up to log exp products, so eliminating the copy saves O(n^2 log exp) writes. Also avoids re-stackallocing scratch on every call.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.risk: Pointer ping-pong must keep result semantics: final answer must end up in the caller's result buffer. Need a final conditional copy only if the last write landed in the scratch buffer (one copy total vs one-per-multiply). Behavior identical; care needed that MultiplyMatrices(temp,temp,...) self-multiply still reads consistent source (already needs scratch because output overlaps input — ping-pong naturally fixes the aliasing).

src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.summary: Replace the branchy double loop with a zero-fill plus diagonal write to remove n^2 branches.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.currentCost: n^2 iterations each evaluating (i==j)?1:0 — a data-dependent branch/cmov per element across the whole matrix.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.proposedChange: memset/loop-zero the n*n block (or Unsafe.InitBlock / a tight for writing 0), then a single diagonal loop: for(int i=0;i<n;i++) res[i*n+i]=1. Diagonal index i*n+i can be strength-reduced with an accumulator idx+=n+1.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.rationale: Turns n^2 conditional writes into a branchless contiguous zero-fill (vectorizable / single InitBlock) plus n diagonal writes. Fewer instructions, no per-element compare, prefetcher-friendly contiguous store.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.risk: None — output identical. InitBlock requires byte count n*n*sizeof(long); ensure no overflow of the int byte-count argument for large n (n*n*8 must fit int; guard or use loop for very large n).

src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.summary: Hoist the repeated trans[f*alphabetSize+i] and fail[next] computations and force inlining of this hot per-edge helper.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.currentCost: trans[f*alphabetSize+i] is computed twice (loop condition and after the loop at line 75), and fail[next] is read twice (lines 75-76: fail[next] is written then re-read). state*alphabetSize+i recomputed at lines 70 and 81. The method is a non-inlined call invoked alphabetSize times per dequeued state in the BFS hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] to ProcessTransition (and InitializeRootTransitions). Cache long baseIdx=state*alphabetSize+i once. After the while loop, store the resolved target t=trans[f*alphabetSize+i] in a local, write fail[next]=t and use t (not a re-read of fail[next]) for output[next]|=output[t].
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.rationale: Removes a redundant load+multiply-add per edge, shortens the dependency chain (output|= no longer waits on a reload of fail[next]), and inlining eliminates call overhead and lets Burst keep base indices in registers across the whole alphabet loop. Asymptotics unchanged but constant factor on the dominant BFS edge loop drops.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.risk: Behavior-preserving: fail[next] is set to exactly trans[f*alphabetSize+i] so reusing the local t for output is identical. Inlining a recursive-free leaf is safe under Burst. No aliasing issue since next!=state in Aho-Corasick goto edges (next is a distinct child state).

src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.summary: The else-branch mutates trans in place to build the goto-automaton, mixing two responsibilities; splitting the failure-link build from the goto-completion would clarify the API but is optional.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.currentCost: Single helper both (a) computes failure links for real edges and (b) path-compresses missing edges via trans[state*A+i]=trans[fail[state]*A+i]. The dual role makes the hot method harder to reason about and prevents the compiler from specializing each path.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.proposedChange: Keep the perf model but consider documenting that this is the standard Aho-Corasick BFS goto-completion; optionally precompute fail[state] into a local fs once at method entry (used in both branches) to avoid two fail[state] loads.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.rationale: fail[state] is loaded in both branches (line 73 and 81); hoisting it to a single local at entry removes one load on the else path and clarifies intent. Minor cycle + readability win.
src/IAFahim.Search.Automaton/Automaton.c.risk: None — fail[state] is not modified within the method, so a single cached load is identical to two loads.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.summary: Replace the iterative w &= w-1 popcount loop with a hardware popcount intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.currentCost: PopCountWord loops once per SET bit (Kernighan), so up to 64 iterations per 64-bit word, each a dependent AND + decrement + branch. For a dense bitset this is ~64 cycles/word and a hard-to-predict branch.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.proposedChange: Use Unity.Mathematics math.countbits((ulong)w) (or System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount on platforms where available). Under Burst this lowers to a single POPCNT/CNT instruction; delete the helper. Sum into count over the wordCount loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.rationale: One fixed-latency instruction replaces a data-dependent loop of up to 64 dependent iterations: ~1 cycle vs tens, with no branch misprediction and far shorter dependency chain. The outer accumulation also vectorizes/pipelines better.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.risk: Bit-identical result; popcount is exact. Requires Unity.Mathematics reference (already used in sibling modules). If neither intrinsic is guaranteed, keep a SWAR fallback (parallel bit-count) which is still branchless and ~12 ops vs the current loop.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.summary: Replace the manual 6-step binary-search trailing-zero count with a tzcnt intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.currentCost: BitIndex does 6 sequential compare/shift/add steps (a dependency chain of ~6 dependent branches+shifts) to compute the trailing-zero count of the masked word, on every NextSet hit.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.proposedChange: Use math.tzcnt((ulong)w) (Unity.Mathematics) — returns count of trailing zeros directly. Replace both call sites in Run with from + math.tzcnt(...) and (i<<6) + math.tzcnt(...). Delete BitIndex.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.rationale: TZCNT/CTZ is a single ~3-cycle instruction versus a 6-deep dependency chain of branchy shifts. Shorter critical path, no branches.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.risk: Behavior identical for nonzero w (the only values passed: callers guard w != 0 and bitset[i] != 0). tzcnt of zero is undefined/64 but is never reached here. Requires Unity.Mathematics; otherwise keep current code or use BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.summary: Replace the manual 6-step leading-zero search with an lzcnt intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.currentCost: BitIndexRev runs 6 sequential masked compares with shifts to find the highest set bit index — a long dependent branch chain executed on every PrevSet hit.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.proposedChange: Compute the highest set bit as 63 - math.lzcnt((ulong)x). Replace both call sites and delete BitIndexRev.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.rationale: LZCNT/CLZ is one ~3-cycle instruction; replaces a 6-deep branchy chain. Same result for all nonzero x (the only inputs, since callers guard w != 0 / bitset[i] != 0).
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.risk: lzcnt(0) is 64 -> would give 63-64 = -1, but x is never zero at call sites. Bit-identical otherwise. Requires Unity.Mathematics or BitOperations.Log2/LeadingZeroCount.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.summary: Per-iteration branch 'if (i > wordShift)' to skip the carry-in only matters on the final word; peel it out of the loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.currentCost: Every iteration of the descending loop tests i > wordShift even though it is false for exactly one iteration (i == wordShift), adding a predictable but real compare+branch to each word.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.proposedChange: Loop i from wordCount-1 down to wordShift+1 doing dst[i] = (src[i-wordShift] << bitShift) | (src[i-wordShift-1] >> invShift); then handle the single i == wordShift word after the loop as dst[wordShift] = src[0] << bitShift. Removes the in-loop branch.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.rationale: Eliminates a branch and an index recomputation from the hot per-word body, shortening the loop body and improving the chance Burst keeps the two shifts/OR in a tight pipeline.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.risk: Behavior identical: the peeled iteration reproduces exactly the i==wordShift case (no carry-in). Guard the peeled write only runs when wordCount > wordShift, which the loop already requires.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.summary: wordsPerRow parameter is accepted but unused; wordCount is derived from n instead — dead/misleading parameter.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.currentCost: No runtime cost, but the unused parameter is a correctness/clarity hazard: callers may pass a row stride expecting it to be honored, and it diverges from the Set/Get/Count signatures that also ignore wordsPerRow.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.proposedChange: Either remove wordsPerRow from these signatures, or use it as the loop bound consistently (wordCount = wordsPerRow) across the whole Bitset API. Make the convention uniform so the parameter is either always meaningful or absent.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.rationale: Reduces API misuse risk and signature inconsistency without changing the perf model; an unused parameter is pure overhead in the ABI and a discoverability trap.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bitset.cs.risk: Removing the parameter is a public-API change; keep it only if some caller relies on the signature. No behavioral change to the OR/AND result for current usage since the parameter is ignored today.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.summary: temp buffer is long[n] but only ever holds int values copied back as int — use int[n] to halve scratch RAM.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.currentCost: stackalloc long[n] = 8*n bytes of stack; values written are arr[i]/arr[j] (int) and read back via (int)temp[i]. Doubles the working set and halves cache-line density (4 ints/line vs 8), increasing cache misses on the merge passes for large n.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.proposedChange: Change temp to int* temp = stackalloc int[n]; store temp[k++] = arr[...]; copy back arr[i] = temp[i] (no cast). The inversion counter cnt stays long (return type unchanged).
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.rationale: Halves stack footprint and doubles elements per cache line, reducing cache misses across the O(n log n) merge copies. The cast to long was never needed since stored values are ints; cnt's long-ness is independent of buffer width.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.risk: Semantics-preserving: stored values are the original int array elements, round-tripped through (int) anyway. cnt += m - i + 1 remains long-accumulated, so the inversion total still cannot overflow. No signedness change.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.summary: Counting loop body has a branch per element; make it branchless and the inner loop is the dominant cost.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.currentCost: Inner loop runs n times per binary-search step (~32 steps over the int32 value range), each iteration doing a compare + conditional increment (data-dependent branch that mispredicts on unsorted data).
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.proposedChange: Replace 'if (arr[i] <= mid) cnt++;' with cnt += -(arr[i] <= mid ? 1 : 0) style or 'cnt += (int)((uint)(mid - arr[i]) >> 31 ^ 1)'-type branchless predicate; simplest portable form: cnt += (arr[i] <= mid) ? 1 : 0 compiles branchless, but force it via integer mask. Burst vectorizes the branchless compare-and-add over the array.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.rationale: Removes a per-element mispredictable branch from a loop executed ~32*n times; branchless compare+add lets Burst SIMD-accumulate counts (e.g. 8 lanes), cutting the dominant cost several-fold.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/BitSearch.cs.risk: Must avoid signed overflow in any (mid - arr[i]) trick since both are int and can span the full range; the safe form is the ternary-to-mask (arr[i] <= mid) which has no arithmetic overflow. Result identical.

src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bit.cs.summary: Generic constraint IComparable<T> uses CompareTo for a not-equal-to-default test, risking an interface/virtual call and boxing under non-Burst paths.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bit.cs.currentCost: ptr[mid].CompareTo(default(T)) is an interface-method invocation on a generic; if the JIT/Burst fails to devirtualize (or T's CompareTo allocates), this becomes a virtual call per binary-search step. The intent is merely 'is this element non-zero/true'.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bit.cs.proposedChange: Constrain to where T : unmanaged, IEquatable<T> and use !ptr[mid].Equals(default(T)), or provide specialized overloads (byte*/long*) doing ptr[mid] != 0. Equality is cheaper than ordering and more directly expresses the truthiness test; the typed overloads are fully Burst-friendly and branchless-comparable.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bit.cs.rationale: Equals/!= avoids the three-way ordering computation and is more reliably inlined; concrete-typed overloads eliminate any interface dispatch entirely, which is the only thing that could defeat Burst here.
src/IAFahim.Search.Bit/Bit.cs.risk: Behavior preserved: CompareTo(default) != 0 is equivalent to !Equals(default) for any total order. Changing the constraint is an API change; the safest non-breaking route is adding typed overloads alongside the generic one.

src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.summary: Redundant recomputation of end+1 and a missing strength-reduction opportunity on the bounds branch.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.currentCost: end+1 is computed twice (once for the compare 'end + 1 < len', once for the index 'diff[end + 1]'). The compiler/Burst will almost certainly CSE this, so the win is essentially zero in optimized builds.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.proposedChange: Optionally compute 'int next = end + 1;' once and reuse it for both the comparison and the index. Cosmetic only.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.rationale: Eliminates a textual duplicate sub-expression; makes intent explicit. No real cycle reduction expected because Burst/LLVM already performs common-subexpression elimination on end+1.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.risk: None. end is int; end+1 cannot overflow for any valid len-bounded index reachable past the (uint)end>=(uint)len guard (end < len <= int.MaxVALUE implies end+1 <= int.MaxValue). Semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.summary: prefix[i+1] store uses a +1-offset index each iteration; hoist the output pointer to remove the per-iteration offset add.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.currentCost: Each iteration computes the address prefix + (i+1) for the store. The address generation includes a constant +1 fused into the index; on most targets this folds into the addressing mode so the real cost is ~0. The carried dependency 'cur += diff[i]' is the true bottleneck and is inherent to prefix sum (cannot be SIMD-vectorized without a parallel-scan rewrite).
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.proposedChange: Optionally write 'int* out1 = prefix + 1;' before the loop and store 'out1[i] = cur;'. Keeps prefix[0]=len as-is. Equivalent codegen on Burst; purely stylistic.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.rationale: Removes the textual +1 from the hot index; lets the addressing mode use a plain base+i*4. In practice LLVM already folds the +1 into the displacement, so expect no measurable change.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.risk: None. Behavior identical: prefix[0]=len, prefix[1..len]=running sums. The dependency chain remains, so this does not change asymptotics or vectorizability.

src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.summary: Name 'RangeSum' is misleading: it returns the single prefix value at idx, not a sum over a range; and the length is stored in-band at prefix[0], coupling layout to PrefixFromDiff.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.currentCost: No cycle cost (it is already a branchless-friendly bounds check + one load). The issue is API clarity/discoverability and the hidden contract that prefix[0] holds the length (a non-obvious in-band length encoding).
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.proposedChange: Rename to PrefixAt (or PointQuery) to match what it returns, and document that prefix[0] stores len as written by PrefixFromDiff. If a true range sum is intended, expose 'RangeSum(prefix, lo, hi) => prefix[hi+1] - prefix[lo]' which is the natural use of the +1-offset prefix layout.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.rationale: Aligns the name with observable behavior and exploits the existing offset-by-one prefix layout (prefix[i+1]=sum of diff[0..i]) so a real range sum is a single subtraction with no extra storage.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.risk: Pure rename/addition; no behavior change to existing callers if the old method is kept. The proposed RangeSum(lo,hi) assumes 0<=lo<=hi<len (unchecked-by-design); guard with the same (uint) trick if a checked variant is wanted.

src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.summary: Build and PrefixFromDiff duplicate the identical prefix-sum loop; PrefixFromDiff already computes a superset of what Build produces.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.currentCost: Two near-identical inclusive-scan loops are maintained. Functionally Build(output,diff,len) == PrefixFromDiff writing to output-1 region shifted; the running-sum logic is duplicated, increasing maintenance surface (not runtime cost).
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.proposedChange: Keep both public entry points for ergonomics, but note that output[i] from Build equals prefix[i+1] from PrefixFromDiff. No code merge is needed for perf; if dedup is desired, have Build call an internal scan helper shared with PrefixFromDiff's body. Do NOT add indirection on the hot path without inlining.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.rationale: Single source of truth for the scan; avoids divergent bug fixes. Runtime is unchanged since both are O(len) sequential scans with the same carried dependency.
src/IAFahim.Search.DifferenceArray/Diffe.risk: If refactored into a shared helper, ensure it stays AggressiveInlining so Burst still emits a tight loop; otherwise leave as-is. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.summary: Replace the variable-length 'val' bit-position loop with a single trailing-zero-count intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.currentCost: Each iteration of every backtracking inner loop runs `int val = 0; int tmp = lsb; while (tmp > 1) { tmp >>= 1; val++; }` — a data-dependent loop of up to ~9 (n) iterations (shift + compare + increment + branch each step), on the hottest path of the solver. Identical code is duplicated in 4 methods (lines 34, 39, 94, 97).
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.proposedChange: Since `lsb = allowed & -allowed` is always exactly `1 << val`, compute `int val = System.Numerics.BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(lsb);` (or `Log2(lsb)`). This is one `tzcnt`/`bsf` machine instruction. Factor it into a private `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] static int BitIndex(int x) => BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount(x);` reused by all four sites.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.rationale: Strength-reduces an O(val) dependency-chained loop with a per-step branch into a single fixed-latency instruction Burst lowers to native tzcnt. Removes a hard-to-predict loop branch from the hottest recursion and shrinks the dependency chain feeding the recursive call's `col|lsb` etc.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.risk: lsb is guaranteed a single set bit (isolated low bit of a non-negative mask), so TrailingZeroCount(lsb)==old val exactly; TrailingZeroCount(0) is never hit because lsb!=0 inside the while(allowed!=0) body. BitOperations is Burst-intrinsic; if BitOperations is disallowed by the managed-type policy, use Unity.Mathematics math.tzcnt((uint)lsb). No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.summary: Managed `int[]` literal violates house constraints and defeats Burst; replace with direct unrolled writes.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.currentCost: Line 47 allocates a managed array `int[] res = { 9,5,6,7,1,0,8,2 };` on the GC heap every call, then copies it element-by-element into resultDigits. Managed array allocation is not Burst-compilable and not blittable, so this method cannot run under Burst at all and incurs a heap allocation + GC pressure.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.proposedChange: Write the 8 constants straight into resultDigits: `resultDigits[0]=9; resultDigits[1]=5; ... resultDigits[7]=2;` (or stackalloc + loop). Remove the managed array entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.rationale: Eliminates the only managed allocation in the file, making the method Burst/unmanaged-compatible and removing per-call GC allocation. Direct stores are also fewer instructions than allocate+initialize+copy.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.risk: None — output is identical for the (numLetters==8,numWords==2) case; all other inputs still return false. Note this function is a hard-coded stub regardless, so behavior is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.summary: Zeroing the full 729*324 dense matrix dominates cost while the matrix is sparse.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.currentCost: Line 28 runs `for (int i=0;i<729*324;i++) m[i]=0;` clearing 236,196 ints (~921 KB) on every call before BuildSudokuMatrix writes at most 4 ones per row. The clear is the dominant memory-bandwidth cost and thrashes L2/L3, especially on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.proposedChange: Either (a) use the existing zero-init guarantee of stackalloc-with-no-explicit-init under Burst is NOT available, so instead clear only the rows actually built: after BuildSudokuMatrix, only `rc` rows are used, and only 4 columns per row are set — but the unset columns within used rows must be 0. Better: clear per-row lazily inside AddSudokuMatrixRow by memset-ing the `324` ints of that row to 0 right before setting its 4 ones, so only `rc*324` (rc<=729, typically far fewer when many cells are pre-filled... actually rc can be up to 729) — so the real win is using Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned / a SIMD-friendly clear instead of the scalar element loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.rationale: Replacing the scalar `for` clear with a block-clear (Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned over rc*324 ints) lets Burst/runtime emit vectorized stores (8-16 ints/instruction) instead of one store per iteration, cutting the clear instruction count ~8-16x. Clearing only `rc*324` instead of `729*324` further skips untouched tail rows when fewer than 729 candidate rows exist.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.risk: Must clear exactly the bytes that BuildSudokuMatrix will read as columns of valid rows; clearing rc*324 is safe only if SolveDlx reads only rows [0,rc). It does (BuildDlxMatrix loops r in [0,rows)). InitBlockUnaligned size must be rc*324*sizeof(int). If house policy forbids Unsafe, keep the loop but bound it to rc*324 instead of 729*324 (still a strict win when rc<729).

src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.summary: Recompute repeated subexpressions r*9 and r*9+c once.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.currentCost: Line 30 computes `r*9+c` (cell index) and `r*9+v`, `c*9+v` with `r*9` evaluated twice and the box index recomputes `(r/3)*3 + c/3`. Per candidate row (up to 729) these are redundant multiplies/divides.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.proposedChange: Hoist `int rc9 = r*9; int cell = rc9 + c; int box = (r/3)*3 + c/3;` and reuse: `rm[rc] = cell*9 + v` is wrong layout (keep r*81+c*9+v), but reuse box for the 4th constraint and cell for the 1st. Pass `box` in from the caller (BuildSudokuMatrix already iterates r,c) to avoid recomputing the two integer divisions per call.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.rationale: Removes redundant integer multiply and two integer divisions (div is ~20+ cycle latency on some mobile cores) from a loop executed up to 729 times per solve. Box index is loop-invariant per (r,c) and can be computed once in the caller.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.risk: Pure index-arithmetic refactor; identical addresses written. No overflow concern (max index 729*324 fits int). Verify the 4th-constraint offset still uses (r/3)*3+c/3 exactly.

src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.summary: Strength-reduce cell/9 and cell%9 using a shared quotient.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.currentCost: Line 34 computes `r = cell/9` and `c = cell%9` as two separate integer division operations per cell visit, plus `box=(r/3)*3+c/3` (two more divisions). Backtracking visits cells extremely frequently.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.proposedChange: Compute one division: `int r = cell/9; int c = cell - r*9;` (replaces the %9 div with a mul+sub). Likewise reuse r for box. Optionally pass r,c,box as recursion parameters incremented along the fixed cell order instead of recomputing from `cell` each call.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.rationale: `%` after `/` is a redundant second division; `cell - r*9` reuses the already-computed quotient with a cheap imul+sub, removing one ~20-cycle integer division per visited cell. Carrying r/c/box through recursion would eliminate all four divisions per node.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.risk: cell is always in [0,81), so quotient/remainder identities hold exactly; no signed-edge issue since cell>=0. Passing precomputed indices changes signature only on a private method — verify all four backtrackers stay consistent if generalized.

src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.summary: Mark the tiny hot leaf helpers AggressiveInlining to cut call overhead in the DLX inner loops.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.currentCost: Cover/Uncover/CoverRow/UncoverRow/SelectBestColumn are small, called in tight per-node loops inside SearchDlx, with many pointer args passed by value on each call (12 pointer parameters). Without inlining hints the JIT/Burst may keep them as calls, paying prologue/epilogue + argument shuffling per invocation.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to Cover, Uncover, CoverRow, UncoverRow, SelectBestColumn, and the BitIndex helper. (System.Runtime.CompilerServices is already imported.)
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.rationale: Inlining these leaf routines removes per-call argument marshaling of the 8-12 pointers and lets Burst keep the shared pointer base values in registers across the cover/uncover sweeps, shortening dependency chains and enabling cross-call optimization.
src/IAFahim.Search.ExactCover/ExactCover.risk: Inlining is a hint; only risk is code-size growth (Cover/Uncover contain nested loops, so the compiler may decline — acceptable). No semantic change. Keep recursive SearchDlx un-inlined (recursion can't inline).

src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.summary: Fuse the initial copy pass into the horizontal prefix-sum pass to eliminate one full O(width*height) sweep over the array.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.currentCost: Three full passes: (1) a copy loop dst[i]=diff[i] over width*height elements, (2) horizontal prefix, (3) vertical prefix. The copy pass is a redundant read+write of the whole grid (2*width*height memory ops) plus loop overhead, and it streams the whole array through cache once before the horizontal pass re-reads it.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.proposedChange: Drop the standalone copy loop. In the horizontal pass, for each row do dst[r*width+0]=diff[r*width+0]; then for c=1..width-1 dst[r*width+c]=dst[r*width+c-1]+diff[r*width+c]. This reads diff once and writes dst once, computing the row prefix in the same sweep. The vertical pass stays as-is reading/writing dst.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.rationale: Removes an entire width*height read+write pass and one cache traversal of the array; the horizontal accumulation becomes the first writer of dst, so total memory traffic drops from ~ (copy:2N) + (horiz:read+write of dst ~2N) to a single read of diff + write of dst (~2N) for the horizontal stage. Fewer instructions retired and fewer cache lines touched, especially impactful for large grids on mobile where bandwidth is scarce.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.risk: Semantics identical: dst still ends as the 2D prefix sum of diff, and diff is read-only so reading diff[c] instead of the just-copied dst[c] yields the same value. Requires width>=1 (already implied by the loops). No overflow change.

src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.summary: Hoist the row-base index r*width out of the inner horizontal and vertical loops to strength-reduce repeated multiplies into pointer/offset increments.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.currentCost: Inner loops recompute r*width+c (and (r-1)*width+c) each iteration: a multiply plus adds per element. width*height multiplies in the horizontal pass and another width*height in the vertical pass.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int rowBase = r * width; before each inner loop and index dst[rowBase + c]; in the vertical pass also hoist int prevBase = (r-1)*width; (or keep a moving pointer long* row = dst + rowBase). This converts the per-element multiply into a single multiply per row plus an add.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.rationale: Replaces O(width*height) multiplies with O(height) multiplies; the inner step becomes pure additions/increments that Burst can fold into addressing and vectorize. Shortens the dependency chain on the index computation.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos2D.cs.risk: None; identical addresses computed. Burst/JIT may already hoist this, but making it explicit guarantees it and aids readability.

src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.summary: Hoist row-base indices and avoid the per-element branch on i>0 by special-casing the first row.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.currentCost: Inner loop recomputes i*width+j and (i-1)*width+j each iteration (two multiplies) and tests if (i>0) on every element, a branch that is taken for all rows except the first yet evaluated width*height times.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.proposedChange: Compute int rowBase = i*width; int prevBase = rowBase - width; once per row. Handle i==0 with a dedicated loop (just the rowAcc running sum, no vertical add) and i>=1 with a loop that always adds res[prevBase+j]. This removes the i>0 branch from the hot inner loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.rationale: Eliminates width*height index multiplies (down to O(height)) and removes a width*height-count branch whose outcome is loop-invariant per row. The two resulting straight-line inner loops vectorize cleanly under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.risk: None; output identical. First-row loop writes res=rowAcc, subsequent rows add the row above, exactly as the original conditional did.

src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.summary: Hoist the per-row stack stackalloc out of the height loop to allocate it once.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.currentCost: int* stack = stackalloc int[width]; sits inside the for(i) loop. While stackalloc inside a loop in C# does not grow the frame each iteration (the frame is reserved once), placing it in-loop can defeat that guarantee depending on codegen and obscures intent; the stack contents are fully overwritten each row anyway since top resets to 0.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.proposedChange: Move int* stack = stackalloc int[width]; and the heights buffer init above the for(i) loop; reset int top=0; at the start of each row iteration. heights is already hoisted; do the same for stack.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.rationale: Guarantees a single frame reservation, removes any per-iteration stackalloc setup, and makes the working set explicit. No correctness change since each row re-initializes top=0 and only reads stack entries it wrote this row.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.risk: None functionally. Stack is fully rewritten per row before reads (entries pushed before popped), so hoisting is safe.

src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.summary: The interval sort uses O(n^2) selection-style swap sort; replace with an O(n log n) sort to fix the asymptotic bottleneck.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.currentCost: The double loop for(i){for(j=i+1..){if res[j]<res[i] swap}} is an O(n^2) sort of the intervals by start. For large n this dominates the whole routine (the merge pass is O(n)).
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.proposedChange: Sort the n (start,end) pairs with an O(n log n) in-place sort over the pointer array — e.g. an unmanaged heapsort or introsort on indices/pairs keyed by res[k*2]. Keep it allocation-free using stackalloc/in-place swaps to respect house constraints (no managed Array.Sort).
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.rationale: Lowers complexity from O(n^2) to O(n log n); for n in the thousands this is orders of magnitude fewer comparisons/swaps. Same final merged output since the merge step only requires intervals sorted by start.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.risk: Must keep the sort stable-enough only in the sense that ties by start don't change the union result (they don't, since merge takes max end). Implementing heapsort in unmanaged C# is more code/complexity; verify the pair-swap keeps start and end paired. Behavior preserved for all valid n>=1 (n==0 would read res[0] in the original too, so no new edge case).

src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.summary: Replace the inner j-1 underflow ternary with a branchless first-column special-case and hoist row base.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.currentCost: dp[j - 1 < 0 ? 0 : j - 1] evaluates a branch every cell of every row (width*height branches), and grid[i*width+j] recomputes i*width+j per cell. For j==0 the expression dp[0] is also semantically a corner the loop handles awkwardly.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long* row = grid + i*width; (or int rowBase). Handle j==0 outside the inner loop (left neighbor contributes 0), then loop j=1..width-1 using dp[j-1] directly with no bounds ternary. Use a branchless min via Math.Min already present; the key is removing the j-1<0 test.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.rationale: Removes width*height branch evaluations from the hot loop and O(width*height) index multiplies (down to O(height)), tightening the dependency chain and helping Burst vectorize the steady-state inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos.cs.risk: Must preserve the j==0 case exactly: original uses dp[max(0,j-1)]=dp[0] when j==0, i.e. it reads dp[0] (the cell itself's previous value via temp logic). Carefully reproduce: at j==0 the min is over (dp[0]_old, dp[0]_old, prev=0) -> result is 1 when grid==1 (since prev starts 0). Reproduce that as dp[0] = grid==1 ? 1 : 0. Verify against original before applying.

src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos1D.cs.summary: Remove the unused 'using System;' (and in Imos2D) to keep translation units clean; not a perf change but reduces noise. The Build loop itself is already an optimal single-pass prefix sum.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos1D.cs.currentCost: using System; is imported but System is unused in Imos1D.cs; harmless but unnecessary. The prefix-sum loop is already minimal (one read, one write, one add per element) and correct.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos1D.cs.proposedChange: Drop the unused using. No change to the loop — it is already the canonical scalar prefix sum. Note: prefix sums are inherently serial (carry dependency), so SIMD would require a parallel-prefix rewrite that is usually not worth it for int on mobile; leaving scalar is the right call.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos1D.cs.rationale: Purely hygiene/ergonomics; confirms the hot loop is already optimal so no cycles are left on the table here.
src/IAFahim.Search.Imos/Imos1D.cs.risk: None. This is the lowest-value item; included only to certify Imos1D.Build needs no algorithmic change.

src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.summary: Insertion sort is O(n^2); the dependent searches (FindFirstOverlapping/CountOverlapping) and MergeIntervals all assume sorted-by-start input, so an O(n log n) sort would dominate cost on large arrays.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.currentCost: O(n^2) comparisons/moves worst case. For n in the thousands this is the dominant cost of any pipeline that sorts then searches.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.proposedChange: Replace the insertion sort with an in-place dual-array heapsort (or introsort) keying on starts[] and carrying ends[] in lockstep. Keep the signature identical (int* starts, int* ends, int len). Heapsort needs no scratch buffer, stays unmanaged/Burst-friendly, and is O(n log n) worst case.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.rationale: Asymptotic improvement from O(n^2) to O(n log n). For already-near-sorted input insertion sort wins, but as a general-purpose primitive the quadratic blowup is the real risk on adversarial/large inputs.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.risk: Heapsort is not stable; if any caller relies on stable ordering of equal-start intervals (e.g. a secondary order of ends), behavior changes. Insertion sort here is already not preserving end-order beyond start, so stability is likely not contractual — but confirm no caller depends on it. If stability is required, this opt must be rejected.

src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.summary: Both are O(n) linear scans. If starts[]/ends[] are sorted by start (the SortByStart primitive in the same class implies this is the intended pre-state), overlap queries can be bounded by binary search.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.currentCost: O(n) per query. For repeated queries against a fixed sorted interval set this is wasteful.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.proposedChange: Add sorted variants (e.g. CountOverlappingSorted) that binary-search the upper bound i where starts[i] < targetEnd, scanning only the prefix, and for non-overlapping-set cases binary-search both ends. Keep the existing unsorted Run methods for the general case to preserve current semantics.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.rationale: When inputs are sorted, a binary-search bound turns O(n) per query into O(log n + k). This is additive API (new methods), not a behavior change to existing ones.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.risk: Only valid when the array is sorted by start; the unsorted methods must stay for general input. New method, so no observable change to existing callers. Must document the sorted precondition clearly to avoid silent wrong answers.

src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.summary: Branch-counting loop can be made branchless to help Burst auto-vectorize the SoA (separate starts[]/ends[]) layout.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.currentCost: One unpredictable conditional branch per element; count++ is control-dependent, blocking vectorization of the reduction.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.proposedChange: Accumulate without a branch: count += (-(starts[i] < targetEnd & targetStart < ends[i])) & 1, or count += (starts[i] < targetEnd ? 1 : 0) folded as a mask. In C# write it as: int hit = (starts[i] < targetEnd && targetStart < ends[i]) ? 1 : 0; count += hit; — Burst lowers the ternary to a setcc/mask and can vectorize the add-reduction over the SoA arrays.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.rationale: Removing the data-dependent branch turns the loop into a maskable reduction; Burst/LLVM can vectorize comparisons + masked add across the contiguous starts[]/ends[] arrays, cutting cycles several-fold and eliminating branch mispredicts.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/IntervalSear.risk: Semantics identical for all inputs (same boolean condition). Note short-circuit && becomes non-short-circuit at the vector level, but both operands are pure pointer loads with no side effects, so no observable difference and no extra fault risk (same indices were already accessed).

src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.summary: Redundant re-derefs of a[i].End and b[j].End: the advance test recomputes ends already loaded for the hi/lo computation.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.currentCost: a[i].End and b[j].End are loaded once for Math.Min(hi) and again for the if (a[i].End < b[j].End) advance test — up to 4 pointer-offset loads per iteration where 2 cached values suffice.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.proposedChange: Hoist per-iteration: int aEnd = a[i].End; int bEnd = b[j].End; int aStart = a[i].Start; int bStart = b[j].Start; then lo = aStart>bStart?aStart:bStart; hi = aEnd<bEnd?aEnd:bEnd; and advance with if (aEnd < bEnd) i++; else j++;.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.rationale: Cuts redundant loads and lets the comparator reuse register values, shortening the dependency chain. Also makes the min/max explicit branchless ternaries instead of Math.Min/Max calls (Burst inlines those anyway, so neutral there, but the load hoisting is a real win).
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.risk: Behavior identical; a[i]/b[j] are not mutated within the iteration so cached values equal re-reads. No aliasing concern (dst is the output and not read). Pure refactor.

src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.summary: Interval struct lacks explicit layout/readonly-blittable annotations; relies on implicit sequential layout. It is already blittable (two ints) but could be made explicit for guaranteed packing and intent.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.currentCost: No runtime cost today, but layout is implicit. 8-byte struct of two ints is naturally packed, so this is purely a robustness/intent note.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.proposedChange: Optionally add [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] for explicit, ABI-stable packing. The struct is already optimal at 8 bytes; no change needed for correctness. Document that it is intentionally blittable for Burst/interop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.rationale: Two contiguous ints are already the minimal layout; explicit Sequential guarantees no reordering across compilers and signals Burst-compatibility intent. This is a near-no-op flagged for completeness, not a cycle/RAM win.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.risk: None functionally. Adding StructLayout has zero effect on a 2-int struct's existing layout. Low value; include only if codifying blittability is desired.

src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.summary: ptr[outIdx] is re-dereferenced multiple times per iteration in the overlap branch; caching the current merged End reduces repeated offset loads.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.currentCost: ptr[outIdx].End is loaded for the compare (>= ptr[i].Start), again for the inner compare (ptr[i].End > ptr[outIdx].End), and written. Each ptr[outIdx] access recomputes outIdx*sizeof(Interval) offset.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.proposedChange: Cache the running interval: track int curEnd = ptr[0].End; compare ptr[i].Start <= curEnd; on merge curEnd = ptr[i].End > curEnd ? ptr[i].End : curEnd and write ptr[outIdx].End = curEnd; on new segment set curEnd = ptr[i].End. This removes repeated outIdx offset arithmetic and end reloads from the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.rationale: Keeps the merged End in a register, removing redundant indexed loads and the multiply for the offset on the dominant (overlap) path, shortening the loop's critical dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Search.Interval/Interval.cs.risk: Behavior identical: curEnd mirrors ptr[outIdx].End exactly. Must ensure curEnd is written back to ptr[outIdx].End before/when outIdx advances so the array reflects the merge (it already does on the merge branch; on the new-segment copy ptr[outIdx]=ptr[i] sets End correctly). Pure refactor if writes are kept in sync.

src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.summary: The O(n) initialization loop is entirely dead work — all three buffers are fully written before being read in the main loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.currentCost: One full pass over len writing tail[i]=0, prev[i]=-1, idx[i]=0 for every i: 3 stores per element, len iterations, plus the loop overhead. On large inputs this is a second O(n) streaming pass that pollutes cache before the real work.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.proposedChange: Delete the `for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) { tail[i] = 0; prev[i] = -1; idx[i] = 0; }` line. tail[pos] and idx[pos] are always written (line 20-21) before any read of tail/idx at that position (LowerBound only reads tail[0..lisLen), and a slot at index==lisLen is written the same iteration it is first reached). prev[i] is written for every i in [0,len) at line 22 before the reconstruction loop reads prev[cur].
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.rationale: Removes an entire O(n) pass and 3*len stores. Eliminates touching pages of stackalloc memory that the algorithm overwrites anyway, reducing cache footprint and total cycles.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.risk: Must confirm no read precedes a write. tail/idx: LowerBound(tail,lisLen,...) only reads indices < lisLen; the slot tail[lisLen]/idx[lisLen] is written in the iteration where pos==lisLen (and lisLen then grows), so every read-back is of a previously-written slot. prev: every i in [0,len) is assigned prev[i] in the main loop; reconstruction only follows indices reachable via idx[lisLen-1] and prev-chain, all of which were assigned. Safe and semantics-preserving. (Note: stackalloc is NOT zero-init-guaranteed to be relied upon, but the algorithm never reads uninitialized slots, so this is fine.)

src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.summary: Same dead initialization loop as Run; tail (long), prev, idx are all overwritten before read.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.currentCost: An O(n) pass writing tail[i]=long.MaxValue (8-byte store), prev[i]=-1, idx[i]=0 per element before any useful work.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.proposedChange: Delete `for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) { tail[i] = long.MaxValue; prev[i] = -1; idx[i] = 0; }`. The MaxValue sentinel is never needed because LowerBoundLong only scans indices < lisLen, all of which hold real written values; idx and prev are written before read identically to Run.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.rationale: Removes an O(n) prepass and len 8-byte + 2*len 4-byte stores, shrinking cache footprint and cycle count.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.risk: Identical reasoning to Run: every read of tail/idx/prev is of a slot written earlier in the algorithm. The long.MaxValue sentinel only mattered if LowerBoundLong could read an unwritten slot, which it cannot (hi=lisLen). Safe.

src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.summary: When result==null the caller only wants the LIS length, but Run still allocates and maintains prev and idx buffers.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.currentCost: stackalloc of prev[len] and idx[len] plus the per-iteration stores idx[pos]=i and prev[i]=... even on the length-only path where they are never consumed.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.proposedChange: Provide a fast length-only path (or a separate `RunLength(int* ptr, int len)` returning int) that maintains only the `tail` array and skips prev/idx entirely: drop the idx[pos]/prev[i] stores and the two extra stackalloc buffers. Keep current Run for the reconstruction case. This halves stackalloc working set and removes two stores per element when the caller passes result==null.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.rationale: Cuts stack memory from 3*len to 1*len and removes 2 stores/element on the common length-only query. Lower cache pressure, fewer dependency-carrying stores. Pure win on that path, and a cleaner Try*/Run-split API.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.risk: Ergonomic/API change if exposed as a new method (additive, non-breaking). If instead branched inside Run on result==null, the per-iteration branch is loop-invariant and the JIT/Burst will hoist it, but a cleaner separate method avoids any branch. No semantic change to outputs.

src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.summary: Binary search has a data-dependent branch per step; can be made branchless to remove mispredict cost on random data.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.currentCost: Per midpoint: a compare feeding an unpredictable branch that assigns either hi or lo. On random inputs this branch mispredicts ~50% of the time, stalling the pipeline each of the ~log2(len) steps.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.proposedChange: Rewrite as a branchless predicated update, e.g. keep a base+count form: `int baseIdx=0; int n=len; while(n>1){ int half=n>>1; int t=tail[baseIdx+half-1]; baseIdx += (t < val) ? half : 0; n -= half; }` then a final fixup, OR use the cmov-friendly `lo = cond ? mid+1 : lo` pattern so Burst/LLVM emits a conditional move instead of a branch.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.rationale: Replaces a hard-to-predict branch with a conditional move, removing branch-mispredict penalties on each of the log2(len) iterations of the hottest inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.risk: Must preserve lower-bound semantics (first index with tail[i] >= val) exactly, including the tail[mid] >= val (not >) comparison that makes LIS strictly increasing. Branchless rewrites are easy to get off-by-one; verify against the current contract. Whether LLVM/Burst actually emits cmov is not guaranteed, so the win is conditional — keep the current form if codegen already produces a cmov.

src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.summary: idx and prev could use a narrower index type when len is known small, but house rules favor int; the real packing win is noting idx duplicates information.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.currentCost: Three separate len-sized buffers (tail,prev,idx) — 3*len*4 bytes for int / (8+4+4)*len for long.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.proposedChange: No safe narrowing under house constraints (len is int, indices need int range). Leave as-is. Flagging that idx[pos]=i stores the array index of the tail's owner; this is necessary for reconstruction and cannot be folded into prev without extra work, so no change recommended.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.rationale: Documenting that the layout is already near-minimal for the reconstruction algorithm; no further safe RAM reduction beyond the result==null path above.
src/IAFahim.Search.LIS/Lis.cs.risk: None — this is a non-action (rejecting a tempting but unsafe narrowing).

src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.summary: Replace O(n^2) insertion sort of the right half with an O(n log n) sort; it is the asymptotic bottleneck of the whole algorithm.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.currentCost: Insertion sort is O(rightCount^2) = O(4^(len-half)). For len=40, rightCount=2^20 (~1.05M) and the sort performs on the order of 10^12 comparisons/moves, dwarfing the O(2^(len-half)*(len-half)) enumeration and O(2^half*log) query phases. Meet-in-the-middle's entire value (turning 2^n into ~2^(n/2)) is destroyed by an O(4^(n/2)) sort, making it effectively O(2^n) again.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.proposedChange: Implement an in-place iterative (non-recursive, to stay Burst/stack-friendly) heapsort or bottom-up mergesort over long*. Heapsort needs no scratch buffer and is fully in-place: sift-down to build the heap, then repeatedly swap arr[0] with arr[i--] and sift-down. This keeps the stackalloc layout unchanged and restores true O(rightCount*log rightCount).
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.rationale: O(n log n) vs O(n^2): for n=2^20 that is ~20*n vs n^2, a ~50000x reduction in the dominant term. This single change moves the method from impractical to practical for len in the 30-40 range, which is exactly the regime meet-in-the-middle targets.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.risk: Must produce a fully ascending order identical to insertion sort so the subsequent LowerBoundLong/UpperBoundLong binary searches remain valid (they require sorted input). Heapsort/mergesort are not stable, but stability is irrelevant here since only values (not original indices) are compared. Use iterative heapsort (no recursion) to avoid Burst stack-depth/recursion concerns. No signed/overflow caveats.

src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.summary: Build the left and right subset-sum tables incrementally (DP over the lowest set bit) instead of recomputing each subset sum from scratch.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.currentCost: For each of 2^k masks the inner loop scans all k bits (testing (mask & (1<<i)) and branching), giving O(k*2^k) adds/branches per half, with a data-dependent branch per bit that mispredicts often.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.proposedChange: Set sums[0]=0, then for mask=1..count-1: long low = mask & (-mask); int bit = trailing-zero-count(low); sums[mask] = sums[mask ^ (int)low] + values[base + bit];. mask ^ low < mask so the dependency is already filled. Get the bit index via Unity.Mathematics math.tzcnt or a 64-entry De Bruijn lookup table (constant, blittable) to stay Burst-friendly.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.rationale: Reduces table construction from O(k*2^k) to O(2^k): exactly one load, one add, one store per mask, with no per-bit inner loop and no data-dependent branch. Removes the (1<<i) shift and the masked-branch entirely, shrinking the dependency chain and eliminating branch mispredicts. Applies to both the left and right enumeration loops.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.risk: mask & (-mask) is the standard lowest-set-bit idiom and is correct for the positive int range used here (mask>=1, count<=2^(len-half) fits in int as long as len<=~60). tzcnt of a power of two is exact. Semantics identical (same multiset of subset sums, just produced in a different mask order, which does not matter because the right table is sorted and the left table is only iterated). De Bruijn table must be marked const/static readonly blittable to avoid managed access under Burst.

src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.summary: Same incremental subset-sum table construction as SubsetSumCount, and the two methods duplicate the entire enumeration+sort body.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.currentCost: Identical O(k*2^k) per-bit recomputation as SubsetSumCount, plus full source duplication of the left/right build and sort across both public methods (maintenance/code-size cost, and Burst compiles two large copies).
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.proposedChange: Apply the same lowest-set-bit incremental DP. Additionally factor the shared 'enumerate halves + sort right' work into one private static helper (e.g. BuildTables(int* values,int len,long** leftOut,int* leftCountOut,long** rightOut,int* rightCountOut) operating on caller-provided stackalloc, since stackalloc cannot be returned across frames) so both Count and Has reuse one implementation.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.rationale: Cuts table build to O(2^k) as above, and removes a full duplicate of the hot enumeration/sort path. Since stackalloc must live in the public method's frame, the helper should take the two buffers as parameters and only fill them, preserving the no-heap/no-managed contract.
