src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.risk: Refactor must keep the buffers stackalloc'd in the public caller (stackalloc cannot escape its frame). Observable behavior unchanged; HasSubsetSum still short-circuits on first match. No overflow/signedness change.

src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.summary: Per-left-element double binary search (LowerBound + UpperBound) can be merged, and the equal-range count can avoid two independent O(log n) descents.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.currentCost: For each of 2^half left masks the code does TWO full binary searches over rightSums (LowerBoundLong then UpperBoundLong), i.e. 2*log2(rightCount) comparisons per left element.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.proposedChange: Either (a) compute lo once with LowerBoundLong, then run UpperBoundLong restricted to the subrange [lo,len) so the second search is over a smaller window; or (b) since target-leftSums[i] is monotonic as leftSums is also sorted, sort leftSums too and sweep both arrays with two monotone pointers in O(2^half + 2^(len-half)) total instead of O(2^half * log).
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.rationale: Option (b) replaces the O(2^half * log(2^(len-half))) query phase with a single linear two-pointer merge after sorting both halves, removing the log factor entirely and turning random binary-search memory access (cache-unfriendly) into two sequential streaming scans (cache- and prefetch-friendly, Burst-vectorizable comparisons).
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.risk: Two-pointer requires leftSums sorted ascending; since rem = target - leftSums[i] decreases as leftSums increases, the matching window in rightSums moves monotonically, so a classic descending/ascending sweep is valid. Must handle duplicate sums on both sides correctly when counting (multiply run-lengths). Adds an O(2^half log) sort of the left side, which is still asymptotically below the right-side sort, so net complexity does not regress.

src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.summary: AggressiveInlining on the two large public methods (and on the loop-heavy SortLongs) is counterproductive.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.currentCost: [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] on SubsetSumCount/HasSubsetSum forces inlining of methods containing stackalloc and nested loops into every call site, bloating caller code size, hurting i-cache, and providing no leaf-call benefit. SortLongs is a loop body, not a leaf, so inlining it is also wasted.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.proposedChange: Remove AggressiveInlining from SubsetSumCount, HasSubsetSum, and SortLongs. Keep it only on the genuine hot leaves LowerBoundLong/UpperBoundLong (and any new tzcnt helper), where inlining into the per-element query loop actually removes call overhead.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.rationale: Inlining helps tiny hot leaves called in tight loops; it hurts large frames (code bloat, register pressure, i-cache pressure). Stackalloc-bearing methods especially should not be force-inlined into callers. Right-sizing inlining improves overall i-cache behavior under Burst without changing semantics.
src/IAFahim.Search.MeetInMiddle/MeetInMi.risk: Pure compilation-hint change; no observable behavior change. Burst may already ignore the attribute, but removing it documents intent and avoids pessimization on the managed/Mono path used in tests.

src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.summary: stackalloc inside the iteration loop allocates newState every iteration
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.currentCost: `double* newState = stackalloc double[dim];` is on line 15 inside the `for (int iter ...)` loop. Although the C# spec lets the runtime reuse the slot, the canonical/portable expectation is one stackalloc per loop iteration; under some JIT/Burst codegen this can re-zero or re-reserve stack each iteration, and it bloats the frame conceptually each pass.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.proposedChange: Hoist a single `double* newState = stackalloc double[dim];` to before the `for (int iter...)` loop (right after `*bestValue = currentVal;`). The buffer is fully overwritten each iteration (line 16 writes all dim entries unconditionally before any read), so reusing one allocation is semantics-preserving.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.rationale: One stack reservation instead of `iterations` reservations; removes any per-iteration stack-pointer adjustment / implicit zeroing and shortens the dependency chain at loop entry. Working set is identical (dim doubles) but allocated once.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.risk: None for semantics: every element of newState is written (line 16) before being read (line 17/20). Caller already assumes dim>0 valid. Keep stackalloc outside the loop but still inside Run so frame size is bounded by dim.

src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.summary: Math.Exp is evaluated eagerly and the accepted-state copy can be avoided by mutating state in place
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.currentCost: Line 18 `if (delta > 0 || Rand(seed) < Math.Exp(delta / temp))` always relies on short-circuit (Exp only runs when delta<=0, which is fine). But line 20 copies newState back into state with a full loop after the candidate was built into a separate buffer. Two full dim-length copies of work per accepted step.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.proposedChange: Eliminate the separate newState buffer entirely: keep a single scratch `cand` built from `state`, and on acceptance swap the `state`/`cand` pointers instead of element-wise copying (`double* tmp = state; state = cand; cand = tmp;`). On rejection, leave state untouched. This removes the dim-length copy on every accepted iteration. Note: since `state` is a caller-owned out buffer, instead keep state as the canonical buffer and only element-copy on the rarer best-improvement path; the candidate copy-back on accept is unavoidable if state must stay the caller's pointer — in that case at least mark `Rand` with [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)].
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.rationale: Pointer swap is O(1) vs O(dim) copy per accepted step; over many iterations with high accept rate this removes the dominant memory traffic. Inlining Rand removes call overhead in the hottest leaf (called 2x/iter).
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.risk: Pointer-swap variant changes which physical buffer `state` points to inside Run; the caller's `state` pointer value is passed by value so the caller still sees its original buffer only if you copy back once at the end. Guard: after the loop, copy the winning buffer into the caller's original `state` pointer once. If that final-state contract is not required by callers, the swap is safe; otherwise keep the in-loop copy and only apply the AggressiveInlining part.

src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.summary: Hot leaf RNG lacks AggressiveInlining and divides by uint.MaxValue each call
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.currentCost: `Rand` is called twice per iteration (lines 16 in a dim-loop, and 18) yet is a non-inlined static method doing a `(double)*seed / uint.MaxValue` division. Division and call overhead in the innermost loop (line 16 runs dim times per iteration).
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to `Rand`. Replace the division `(double)*seed / uint.MaxValue` with a multiply by a precomputed constant: `*seed * (1.0 / 4294967295.0)` (named const `private const double InvUintMax = 1.0 / uint.MaxValue;`).
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.rationale: Reciprocal-multiply replaces a ~20-cycle double division with a ~4-cycle multiply; inlining removes call/return and lets Burst keep `*seed` in a register across the dim-loop body. Multiply-by-reciprocal of the exact same constant yields bit-identical results here because 1.0/4294967295.0 is computed once at compile time — note this is NOT generally bit-identical to division, so see risk.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.risk: x/y vs x*(1/y) are not always bit-identical; results can differ by 1 ULP for some seeds, which slightly changes the random stream and therefore the optimization trajectory (still a valid SA run, but not bit-identical output). If exact reproducibility of *bestValue across versions is required, reject the reciprocal change and keep only AggressiveInlining. AggressiveInlining alone is fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.summary: Massive redundant recomputation of Evaluate at the same points; fMid passed in is ignored and recomputed
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.currentCost: In each call, `Evaluate(f, a)` is computed 3 times (lines 52/54 are separate branches, but line 56 computes `Evaluate(f,a)` and `Evaluate(f,b)` again, and line 54/55 also call `Evaluate(f, (a+b)/2)` as fLeft while the *passed-in* fMid is the midpoint value but the code recomputes the whole-interval Simpson on line 56 using fresh Evaluate calls). `Evaluate(f,a)`, `Evaluate(f,b)` and the midpoint are each evaluated multiple times per node. `(a+b)/2` is recomputed ~5 times. For a depth-d recursion this multiplies the eval count several-fold.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.proposedChange: At the top of the method compute `double mid = (a + b)/2; double fa = Evaluate(f,a); double fb = Evaluate(f,b);` once. Reuse `fMid` (the passed-in midpoint value) instead of recomputing it. Compute `fLeft = Evaluate(f,(a+mid)/2)` and `fRight = Evaluate(f,(mid+b)/2)` (the quarter points — note current line 53 uses (a+b)/2 and b which is a BUG, see risk). Build `whole`, `left`, `right` from these cached values; reuse them in the recursive calls so children receive their fMid (fLeft/fRight) without recomputation.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.rationale: Cuts Evaluate calls per node from ~7-8 to 2 new evaluations per level (the two quarter points), the textbook adaptive-Simpson recurrence. Also removes repeated `(a+b)/2` divisions. Asymptotically same node count but ~3-4x fewer function evals and divisions per node — large constant-factor win on the hot recursive path.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.risk: The current code is mathematically incorrect (line 53 `fLeft = Evaluate(f,(a+b)/2)` is the midpoint not the left-quarter; `fRight = Evaluate(f,b)` is the endpoint not the right-quarter; the recursive children are passed fLeft/fRight as their fMid which is inconsistent). A faithful 'preserve observable behavior' refactor would replicate these wrong points — but that contradicts a correctness fix. Recommend flagging as a correctness bug and, only if behavior must be preserved exactly, cache the *currently-evaluated* points verbatim to remove redundancy without changing which points are sampled.

src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.summary: Per-iteration parity branch and i*h multiply can be strength-reduced; coefficient pattern is branchless
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.currentCost: Line 68 `sum += (i % 2 == 0) ? 2*Evaluate(...) : 4*Evaluate(...)` runs a `%`-based parity test and an unpredictable-ish ternary every iteration, plus `a + i*h` recomputes an integer-to-double multiply each step. n iterations.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.proposedChange: Replace `i % 2 == 0` with `(i & 1) == 0` (i is a non-negative loop counter, so `&` is exact). Hoist the coefficient as a branchless expression: `double coef = 2.0 + 2.0 * (i & 1);` (gives 2 for even, 4 for odd) then `sum += coef * Evaluate(f, x);`. Maintain `x` incrementally: `double x = a + h; for (...) { ...; x += h; }` to replace `a + i*h` with one add per step. Optionally split into two strided loops (even indices coef 2, odd indices coef 4) to make the coefficient a loop-invariant constant and improve vectorization.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.rationale: `& 1` is a single-cycle mask vs `%` (may lower to a longer sequence on some targets); branchless `coef` removes a data-dependent branch the predictor can mispredict; incremental `x += h` removes an int->double conversion and multiply per iteration, shortening the dependency chain. The two-strided-loop form lets Burst hoist the constant coefficient and vectorize cleanly.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.risk: Incremental `x += h` accumulates floating-point rounding differently than `a + i*h`, so results are not bit-identical (typically <1 ULP*n drift). If bit-identical output is required, keep `a + i*h` and apply only the `& 1` and branchless-coef changes, which ARE bit-identical (same products, just reordered selection). `& 1` is safe because i >= 1 and never negative.

src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.summary: Legendre polynomial recurrence divides by (k+1) each step and recomputes invariants
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.currentCost: Inner loop (line 91) runs the full n-term recurrence 50 times (Newton iterations) per root, with a `/(k+1)` division each of the n steps. Line 92 recomputes `n*(...)/(x0*x0 - 1)`. Total ~50*n divisions per root, n roots => O(50*n^2) divisions.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.proposedChange: Note the polynomial recurrence coefficients `(2k+1)/(k+1)` and `k/(k+1)` depend only on k and n, not on x0 or the Newton iteration. Precompute two stackalloc arrays `a_k = (2k+1)/(k+1)` and `b_k = k/(k+1)` once per Run (size n), then the inner loop becomes `p = a_k[k]*x0*p1 - b_k[k]*p2;` with multiplies only. This lifts n divisions out of the 50-iteration Newton loop and out of the per-root loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.rationale: Replaces ~50*n*nroots divisions with n precomputed divisions total, converting the hot inner loop to fused multiply-add friendly form that Burst vectorizes/pipelines far better. Divisions (~20 cyc) dominate this kernel; removing them from the innermost loop is the single biggest cycle win in GaussLegendre.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.risk: Precomputing a_k/b_k and multiplying gives results within 1 ULP of the original divide-in-loop, not necessarily bit-identical, so computed nodes/weights may differ in the last bits and thus the integral. If bit-identical output is mandatory, reject; otherwise the quadrature accuracy is unchanged (well below eps=1e-14 tolerance). Extra 2*n doubles of stack — negligible.

src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.summary: No early-out reuse of converged Newton state and missing AggressiveInlining on Evaluate leaves
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.currentCost: `Evaluate` (lines 43/59/71/96) are tiny leaf methods returning a polynomial; not marked AggressiveInlining. Called in tight loops (SimpsonIntegral line 68 n times, GaussLegendre line 79 n times, AdaptiveSimpson recursively).
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to all four `Evaluate` helpers and to `TernaryReal.Evaluate`. They are 2-3 FLOP leaves in hot loops.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.rationale: Guarantees inlining so the loads of f[0..2] hoist and the polynomial becomes register FMAs, removing call overhead and enabling vectorization across loop iterations. Pure refactor, bit-identical.
src/IAFahim.Search.Numerical/Numerical.c.risk: None — inlining a pure expression-bodied method does not change results. Burst typically inlines these anyway, but the attribute makes it explicit and helps non-Burst managed/IL2CPP builds.

src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.summary: RangeXor reads ptr[r] without bounds context but, more importantly, the l==0 fast-path returns ptr[r] which is the prefix value, yet for l>0 it XORs two prefix entries — semantics are fine, but the type-punning via *(T*)&res defeats Burst vectorization and the sizeof branch is a runtime dispatch on a compile-time constant.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.currentCost: Two runtime if (sizeof(T)==4 / ==8) branches per call plus address-of type punning (*(T*)&res) which forces a stack spill and blocks Burst from keeping the value in a register.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.proposedChange: Replace the type-punning with Unsafe.As or directly compute res in T via System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe.Add/Read on ptr: T res = ptr[r]; then XOR with ptr[l-1] using a generic XOR only valid for integer T — since generic ^ is unavailable, instead provide concrete non-generic overloads RangeXor(int* ,int,int) and RangeXor(long*,int,int) mirroring the existing Run overloads, eliminating the sizeof branch and the *(T*)&res pun entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.rationale: sizeof(T) is a JIT/Burst compile-time constant so the branch is dead-code-eliminated, but the *(T*)&res reinterpret writes res to a stack slot and reloads it as T, adding a store/load dependency the optimizer often cannot remove across the pointer cast. Concrete overloads let Burst keep everything in registers and match the established Run(int*/long*) API convention.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.risk: Behavior identical for int/long. For T whose sizeof is neither 4 nor 8 the current code returns default; concrete overloads simply would not exist for those, which is stricter but matches the rest of the module (only int/long Run overloads exist).

src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.summary: The IComparable<T>.CompareTo constrained-generic call is an interface dispatch on the hot inner loop. Even with where T:unmanaged,IComparable<T>, Burst/IL2CPP may not always devirtualize boxing-free, and it blocks SIMD vectorization of the running min/max scan.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.currentCost: One interface/virtual CompareTo call per element (O(len) calls), each returning an int that is then compared to 0 — a long dependency chain plus potential boxing if devirtualization fails.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.proposedChange: Provide concrete numeric overloads (int*, long*, float*, etc.) using native < / > operators (branchless min/max via math.min/math.max where available), keeping the generic IComparable version as a fallback. The native-comparison loops vectorize and avoid the CompareTo call entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.rationale: Native operator comparison on primitive types is a single CPU compare, branch-predictable or branchless, and Burst auto-vectorizes a running-min reduction; CompareTo is opaque to the vectorizer and adds call overhead per element.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.risk: Must replicate the exact tie-break semantics: Run uses > 0 (keep previous on equal) and < 0; MinIndex uses strict < (keeps earliest index on ties), MaxIndex strict > (earliest on ties). Concrete overloads must use the same strict/non-strict operators to preserve identical outputs including NaN handling for float (CompareTo orders NaN; native < does not — for float, keep CompareTo or define explicit NaN policy).

src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.summary: The serial running-sum/xor recurrence ptr[i]+=ptr[i-1] has a loop-carried dependency that prevents vectorization; a log-step (Hillis-Steele) or blocked prefix scan exposes parallelism for large len.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.currentCost: Strict serial dependency chain of length len: each iteration waits on the previous store/load, ~1 add per cycle best case, no ILP across iterations.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.proposedChange: For large len, use a two-pass blocked prefix scan: compute per-block local prefix sums (vectorizable within independent blocks), then add carried block offsets. Or document that this is intentionally serial and gate the blocked path behind a len threshold so small inputs keep the cheap loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.rationale: In-place blocked scan breaks the single long dependency chain into independent SIMD-friendly chunks, raising throughput on large arrays where the recurrence latency dominates; small-len keeps current code via threshold.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/Prefix.cs.risk: Adds branch/complexity; only wins for large len (cache-resident, len in the thousands+). For small typical inputs the extra setup is a net loss, so it must be threshold-gated. Output must be bit-identical, which it is for integer add/xor (associative); fine for long/int.

src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.summary: LCP compares one byte per iteration; for long common prefixes this is 8x slower than a word-at-a-time compare.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.currentCost: One byte load + compare + branch per matching byte; O(maxLen) byte ops with a per-byte branch that the predictor handles but still one iteration per byte.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.proposedChange: Compare 8 bytes at a time by loading (long*)a and (long*)b while i+8<=maxLen; on the first differing 8-byte chunk, XOR the two longs and use math.tzcnt (trailing-zero count, /8) to locate the exact mismatching byte; fall back to byte loop for the tail. Add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] retained.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.rationale: Word-wide compares cut loop trip count by 8x and tzcnt pinpoints the mismatch byte in one instruction; this is the standard memcmp/LCP fast path and Burst maps tzcnt to a single intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.risk: Endianness: trailing-zero on the XOR gives the lowest-address mismatching byte only on little-endian (PC x86/x64 and ARM in normal config are LE). Must guard for unaligned loads (raw pointer loads of long are fine on x86/ARMv8). Tail handling must not read past maxLen.

src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.summary: All three use the naive O(textLen*patLen) double-loop search. A first-byte-skip (memchr-style) on the inner alignment, or a proper sublinear algorithm, cuts the dominant cost.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.currentCost: Worst case O((textLen-patLen+1)*patLen) byte comparisons; for the common case the outer loop probes every position even when text[i] != pattern[0].
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.proposedChange: Add a cheap first-byte filter: before the inner j-loop, scan i forward to the next position where text[i]==pattern[0] (a tight single-byte loop the compiler vectorizes), then verify the rest. For high-impact, offer a Boyer-Moore-Horspool bad-character variant: precompute a 256-entry stackalloc skip table once (shared across FindFirst/CountOccurrences) giving expected sublinear scanning.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.rationale: The first-byte filter skips the expensive inner loop setup for the ~255/256 of positions that fail on byte 0, and a vectorizable single-byte scan-to-match is far faster than per-position bool ok=true bookkeeping. Horspool gives O(textLen/patLen) expected on typical inputs versus O(textLen*patLen).
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.risk: Horspool needs a 256-byte stackalloc skip table (allowed by house rules) and patLen<=255 fits byte shifts but shift values up to patLen need int storage; for patLen up to textLen use int[256] stackalloc. Match/FindFirst/CountOccurrences must keep identical found-position semantics (FindFirst returns first index, CountOccurrences counts all overlapping occurrences). The simple first-byte filter is zero-risk and preserves exact semantics.

src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.summary: Match duplicates FindFirst's entire body but only needs a boolean. It can delegate to FindFirst to remove duplicated code and benefit from any single optimization site.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.currentCost: Duplicated double-loop maintenance burden; Match and FindFirst can drift. No runtime cost difference today.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.proposedChange: Implement Match as return FindFirst(text,textLen,pattern,patLen) >= 0; (note: FindFirst returns -1 for patLen==0 whereas Match currently does NOT special-case patLen==0 — see risk). Centralizes the search algorithm so future fast-path work (first-byte filter, Horspool) lands in one place.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.rationale: Single source of truth lowers complexity and ensures both paths get the same optimized scanner; the JIT inlines FindFirst into Match given AggressiveInlining, so no added call cost.
src/IAFahim.Search.Prefix/PrefixSearch.c.risk: Semantics differ for patLen==0: current Match returns true (empty pattern matches at i=0 because the inner loop never executes and ok stays true), while FindFirst returns -1 for patLen==0. Delegating would flip Match's empty-pattern result from true to false. Either keep an explicit if(patLen==0) return true; guard in Match, or do not delegate.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.summary: Replace O(n*k) sliding-window membership rescan with an O(n) 64-bucket counter array.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.currentCost: For each window slide, when removing an element it does an inner loop `for (j=i; j<i+k; j++)` scanning up to k elements to test if the removed value is still present. Total cost is O(n*k); for large windows this dominates and is a quadratic blow-up versus the intended O(n) sliding window.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.proposedChange: Maintain `int* cnt` of length 64 (stackalloc or caller-provided scratch) counting occurrences of each value in [0,64) currently in the window. On add: `if(++cnt[add]==1) seen|=1L<<add;`. On remove: `if(--cnt[remove]==0) seen&=~(1L<<remove);`. Initialize cnt during the first k-element fill. This removes the inner stillPresent scan entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.rationale: Turns the per-slide membership test from O(k) into O(1), making the whole routine O(n) instead of O(n*k). Counter updates are branch-light increments/decrements that Burst vectorizes/pipelines well, and bitmask updates stay O(1).
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.risk: Requires 64 ints of scratch (256 bytes). Values outside [0,64) are ignored exactly as today, so observable mex output is unchanged. Must zero the counter array before first fill. Behavior identical for all valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.summary: mex can decrease when an element is removed, but the loop only ever increments mex, which is already correct for incremental add but the recompute-from-current-mex after removal can be wrong — verify or reset.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.currentCost: After a removal that clears a bit below the current mex, `mex` is never decreased; the subsequent `while ((seen & (1L<<mex))!=0 && mex<64) mex++` only advances. If the removed value was < current mex, the reported mex is stale/too large.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.proposedChange: On any removal that clears bit `remove` where `remove < mex`, set `mex = remove` before the while-advance loop, so mex is recomputed from the now-missing slot. (This is a correctness guard, not purely perf; flag for caller review.)
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.rationale: Avoids redundant/incorrect state; also keeps the while-advance loop tight by starting at the lowest cleared index rather than rescanning from 0.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.risk: This changes output for windows where a sub-mex value leaves the window — but the current output is arguably already wrong there. If the 'Run' methods assume valid input only, confirm intended semantics before applying; treat as semantics-clarifying, not blind micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.summary: Dead `left <= right` guard in the mex-advance while condition; left is never mutated.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.currentCost: `while ((seen & (1L<<mex))!=0 && left<=right) mex++;` evaluates `left<=right` every iteration, but `left` stays 0 for the whole function, so the term is always true. It is a wasted compare plus a live but unused variable.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.proposedChange: Remove the `left` variable and the `&& left<=right` term: `while ((seen & (1L<<mex))!=0) mex++;`. Add `&& mex<64` to match RunWindow and avoid shifting by 64 (1L<<64 is UB-ish / wraps) if seen could ever be all-ones.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.rationale: Eliminates a dead variable and a per-iteration comparison from the hot inner loop, and removes a potential out-of-range shift when all 64 bits are set.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.risk: None for the dead-variable removal. The `mex<64` guard is a defensive fix: with values in [0,64) seen can become -1 (all bits), and `1L<<64` is implementation-defined; guarding makes it deterministic without changing valid-input behavior.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.summary: Loop bound `i<=r && i<n` recomputes two comparisons each iteration; hoist the min.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.currentCost: `for (int i=l; i<=r && i<n; i++)` does two bound checks per element. Minor, but the upper bound is loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.proposedChange: Precompute `int hi = r < n-1 ? r : n-1;` (branchless: `int hi = r + (((n-1-r)>>31)&((n-1)-r));`) then loop `for (int i=l; i<=hi; i++)`. Also guard the final mex while with `mex<64`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.rationale: Single comparison per iteration instead of two; the min is computed once. Branchless min avoids a predictable-but-real branch.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/Mex.cs.risk: n-1 underflows if n==0; guard with the existing l>r early-out plus `n>0`. With valid input (l<=r within bounds) behavior is identical.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.summary: Hoist the `(k-1)*len` and `k*len` row-base offsets and `1<<k` out of the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.currentCost: Inner loop recomputes `(k-1)*len`, `k*len` (two multiplies) and the `i + (1<<k) <= len` bound each iteration. These are loop-invariant across the inner `i` loop, costing redundant multiplies/shifts on every element.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.proposedChange: Before the inner loop: `int prevBase = (k-1)*len; int curBase = k*len; int step = 1<<k;` then index `dst[i+prevBase]`, `dst[i+half+prevBase]`, `dst[i+curBase]`, bound `i+step<=len`. Use pointer rows `int* prev = dst+prevBase; int* cur = dst+curBase;` to drop the per-element add entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.rationale: Removes two integer multiplies and a shift from the inner loop body, shortening the dependency chain and exposing a clean strided access Burst can vectorize. The branchless `a>b?a:b` is already vectorizer-friendly via max.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.risk: None; pure invariant hoisting, identical results. Note RangeMin already hoists `step`/`half` but still recomputes the `*len` bases — same fix applies there.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.summary: Reuse the shift `1<<k` and consider a precomputed log table to drop the per-query log loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.currentCost: `while ((1<<(k+1))<=range) k++;` is an O(log range) loop per query, and `1<<k` is recomputed in the two index expressions. For many small queries the log loop dominates.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int k = 31 - lzcnt((uint)range);` (or `BitOperations.Log2`) to get floor(log2(range)) in one instruction, then reuse `int sk = 1<<k;` in both index expressions. Same applies to RangeMin.Query and the BuildSparse `log` computation.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.rationale: Replaces an O(log n) software loop with a single LZCNT, removing a data-dependent branch loop from the hot query path; reusing `sk` avoids recomputing the shift.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMax.cs.risk: range>=1 required (start<=end), already guaranteed for valid queries. lzcnt(0) is undefined — guard or rely on range>=1. Burst maps lzcnt to a native instruction on supported targets.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.summary: Hoist `(k-1)*len` and `k*len` row bases out of the inner loop (use pointer rows).
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.currentCost: Inner loop recomputes `(k-1)*len` and `k*len` (two multiplies) per element even though `step` and `half` are already hoisted. The row bases are invariant across i.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.proposedChange: Add `int* prev = dst + (k-1)*len; int* cur = dst + k*len;` before the inner loop, then `int a = prev[i]; int b = prev[i+half]; cur[i] = a<b?a:b;`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.rationale: Eliminates two multiplies per element and converts to contiguous pointer-relative loads, which Burst lowers to vectorized min on the strided row.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.risk: None; identical output. Same memory layout assumptions as current code.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.summary: Unused `int* src` parameter; remove for API consistency with RangeMax.Query.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.currentCost: `Query(int* sparse, int* src, int len, int start, int end)` never references `src`. It costs an extra argument register/stack slot at every call site and diverges from RangeMax.Query's signature, hurting discoverability and forcing callers to pass a redundant pointer.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.proposedChange: Drop the `src` parameter so the signature matches RangeMax.Query: `Query(int* sparse, int len, int start, int end)`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.rationale: Cleaner, consistent API and one fewer argument to marshal; no behavioral change since src is dead.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeMin.cs.risk: Source-breaking signature change for existing callers — update call sites. Pure ergonomics; no runtime semantics change.

src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeAdd.cs.summary: Sequential prefix-sum has a loop-carried dependency that blocks vectorization; acceptable but flaggable.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeAdd.cs.currentCost: `cur += diff[i]; dst[i]=cur;` carries a dependency through `cur`, so Burst cannot auto-vectorize the scan; throughput is one add per cycle at best.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeAdd.cs.proposedChange: Leave as-is for small len (dependency chain is cheap and code is clear). For large len only, a two-pass blocked/SIMD prefix-sum (partial sums per lane then offset) can be ~2-4x faster, but it adds complexity and a scratch pass — recommend only if profiling shows this is hot.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeAdd.cs.rationale: Documents the inherent serialization; the blocked-scan trades the dependency chain for parallel partial sums. Constant-factor only, not asymptotic.
src/IAFahim.Search.Range/RangeAdd.cs.risk: Blocked prefix-sum is easy to get wrong (lane offsets, overflow into int). Output must stay int with identical wraparound semantics. Only worth it for large arrays; default keep the simple form.

src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.summary: Replace the O(len^2) rank computation and O(len) Fenwick walks with proper coordinate compression plus logarithmic Fenwick operations, reducing the whole method from O(len^2) to O(len log len).
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.currentCost: For each of len elements it (a) scans all len elements to compute rank: O(len) -> O(len^2) total; (b) walks bit[rank..len] to accumulate inv: O(len); (c) walks bit[rank..len] to increment: O(len). Both Fenwick loops are linear instead of logarithmic, so the entire routine is O(len^2). This defeats the purpose of using a Fenwick tree at all.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.proposedChange: After insertion-sorting `sorted`, compute each element's rank with a binary search into the dedup'd sorted array (lower_bound) instead of the inner O(len) count loop. Then use real Fenwick update/prefix-sum: update via `for (int j = rank; j <= len; j += j & -j) bit[j]++;` and query via `for (int j = rank-1; j > 0; j -= j & -j) sum += bit[j];`, counting already-inserted elements with value > current. This yields O(len log len).
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.rationale: Inversions over a range is fundamentally O(len log len) with a Fenwick tree; the current code does O(len) work per Fenwick operation and an extra O(len) rank scan, collapsing to O(len^2) — asymptotically no better than the naive double loop in Run, while using extra memory and being far more complex. A logarithmic Fenwick plus binary-search rank restores the intended complexity.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.risk: Must preserve tie-handling semantics: current code counts inversions where equal values are NOT inversions (rank uses strict `<` plus index tie-break, and counts bit[rank..len] i.e. strictly greater ranks). With distinct ranks per element (stable via index tie-break) the binary-search lower_bound must replicate the same strict ordering. Bit array must be zeroed by caller across the [1..len] window actually used; with the smaller log-walk footprint the same [1..len] indices are touched, so zeroing contract is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.summary: The `long* compressed` stackalloc is allocated but never used; remove it.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.currentCost: `long* compressed = stackalloc long[len];` reserves 8*len bytes of stack that is never read or written, inflating the stack frame and risking stack overflow for large `len` on mobile where stack is tighter.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.proposedChange: Delete the line `long* compressed = stackalloc long[len];` entirely. It has no readers.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.rationale: Dead stackalloc consumes stack and zero-init cost (Burst/IL zero-inits stackalloc) for nothing; removing it shrinks the working set by 8*len bytes and eliminates the implicit memset.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.risk: None — the pointer is never referenced after allocation, so removal is purely subtractive and semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.summary: Add an early-exit when the running result reaches the absorbing element (gcd==1, or lcm overflow/0) and mark Gcd/Lcm with AggressiveInlining.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.currentCost: RangeGcdQuery.Run keeps calling Gcd even after res==1 (gcd can never drop below 1 for positive inputs), wasting a full Euclid call per remaining element. RangeLcmQuery.Run keeps multiplying after res becomes 0. Gcd/Lcm are hot leaf functions called once per element but are not inlined.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.proposedChange: In RangeGcdQuery.Run add `if (res == 1) return 1;` inside the loop (guarding for arr containing 1). In RangeLcmQuery.Run add `if (res == 0) return 0;`. Annotate Gcd and Lcm with `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]`.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.rationale: Early-out turns an O(len) sweep into O(distance-to-absorbing-element) in common cases (a 1 in a gcd range, a 0 in an lcm range). Inlining removes call overhead and lets Burst hoist the Euclid loop into the caller for register allocation.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.risk: For Gcd early-exit, valid only if all values are non-negative such that gcd>=1; if zeros/negatives are possible the absorbing value is not necessarily 1, so guard as `res==1` specifically (gcd of 1 with anything is 1, always safe regardless of sign since |gcd|=1). For Lcm, res==0 stays 0 only when Lcm(0,x)=0 which the code already guarantees — safe.

src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.summary: Hoist the repeated `node*2` / `(l+r)>>1` subexpressions into locals to cut redundant integer ops on the hot segment-tree recursion paths.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.currentCost: Each Run/Apply/Push computes `node * 2` and `node * 2 + 1` two-to-four times per call (e.g. RunMin lines 112-114 recompute node*2 and node*2+1 three times; ApplyMin recomputes them twice). PushMin/PushMax recompute `(l + r) >> 1` twice in the same statement (lines 127-128, 153-154). These are in the per-node recursion executed O(log n) times per query but with a large constant.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.proposedChange: Introduce `int left = node << 1; int right = left | 1; int mid = (l + r) >> 1;` once at the top of each recursive/apply/push method and reuse. Use `node << 1` (equivalent to *2 for valid 1-based node indices well below INT_MAX).
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.rationale: Removes 2-4 redundant integer multiplies/adds and a duplicated shift per node visit; shortens the dependency chain and gives Burst CSE-friendly form. `left | 1` for the right child is one op vs `left + 1` and identical since left is even.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.risk: `node << 1` equals `node * 2` only while node stays non-negative and < 2^30; segment-tree node indices are bounded by ~2n, far below that, so safe. `left | 1` == `left + 1` requires left even (node>=1 even product) — always true. No observable change.

src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.summary: Skip the verification pass when no candidate can be a majority, and avoid re-reading arr[start+i] by advancing a pointer.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.currentCost: Always runs a second full O(len) verification loop even when len==0 trivially has no majority. Both loops recompute `arr[start + i]` (base+index add) each iteration instead of walking a pointer.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.proposedChange: Compute `int* p = arr + start;` and index `p[i]` (or post-increment a cursor) in both loops to drop the per-iteration `start + i` addition. Optionally short-circuit `if (len == 0) return -1;` at entry.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.rationale: Pointer walking removes one add per element across two passes (2*len adds saved); minor but free. Burst auto-vectorizes the simple count-compare verification loop better when the base is a single pointer.
src/IAFahim.Search.RangeQueries/RangeQue.risk: Semantics identical: Boyer-Moore still needs the verification pass for correctness in the general case; only the redundant address arithmetic is removed. len==0 guard preserves the `count > 0` false result (returns -1) exactly.

src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.summary: Replace `(maxSize + minSize) % 2 == 0` parity test with a bitwise AND on the low bit.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.currentCost: Each of the n-1 loop iterations computes an integer addition plus a signed `%` (modulo) against the constant 2 and compares to 0. Signed `%` against 2 emits an idiv-style sequence or sign-correction code; it runs every iteration in the hot loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.proposedChange: Use `((maxSize + minSize) & 1) == 0` (even when low bit is 0). Since maxSize+minSize is always >= 1 and non-negative, `& 1` is exactly equivalent to `% 2 == 0` here.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.rationale: `& 1` is a single ALU op with no sign-correction branch, vs the longer signed-modulo sequence. Sum is a count so it is always >= 0, making the mask provably equivalent. Saves a few cycles per iteration across n-1 iterations.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.risk: Equivalent only for non-negative operands; maxSize+minSize is a heap-size count >= 1, so the guard is satisfied. No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.summary: Final `return res[(n - 1) / 2]` uses signed integer division; use `(n - 1) >> 1`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.currentCost: One signed `/ 2` at function exit, which the JIT lowers to a shift plus a sign-fixup add (because dividend could be negative in general).
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.proposedChange: Return `res[(n - 1) >> 1]`. This also matches the existing `(i - 1) >> 1` parent-index convention already used in SiftUp.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.rationale: For n >= 1, n-1 >= 0, so arithmetic shift equals the division with no sign correction. Consistent with the >> idiom used elsewhere in this struct.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.risk: n must be >= 1 for n-1 to be non-negative; the method already dereferences a[0] and writes res[0] unconditionally, so n >= 1 is a precondition. No behavior change for valid input.

src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.summary: Compute child indices with shift/OR instead of `2 * i + 1` and `2 * i + 2`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.currentCost: Each sift-down step does two multiplies (`2 * i`) and two adds to form left/right child indices. SiftDown runs O(log n) per insertion across the whole stream.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.proposedChange: Compute `int l = (i << 1) + 1; int r = l + 1;` — one shift, one increment, and reuse l to derive r (r = l+1) instead of recomputing 2*i+2.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.rationale: Removes a redundant multiply and a redundant add: r is simply l+1, so the second child index needs no separate 2*i. Shorter dependency chain in the tight heap loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.risk: Pure index arithmetic; i is a non-negative heap index so the shift is safe. Identical results.

src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.summary: Add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] to the hot leaf partition/insertion helpers (and the sift helpers).
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.currentCost: Partition/PartitionLong are the innermost workhorses of SelectTopK, TryGetKth and TopK.Run; SiftUp/SiftDown are the workhorses of MedianMaintain. As ordinary (non-inlined) static calls there is call overhead and the optimizer cannot fuse them with their single call sites or keep loop state in registers across the call boundary.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.proposedChange: Annotate Partition, PartitionLong, InsertionSort, SiftUpMax/Min and SiftDownMax/Min with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)], matching the convention already applied to MedianIndex.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.rationale: Inlining the partition into the quickselect loop lets Burst/LLVM keep left/right/idx and the pivot in registers and removes per-call stack setup; these are leaf methods so inlining has bounded code-size cost. Consistent with the AggressiveInlining already used on MedianIndex.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.risk: Pure inlining hint; no semantic change. Mild code-size growth (acceptable for leaf helpers); Burst generally honors and benefits from this.

src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.summary: Eliminate the full `stackalloc long[n]` copy of the input; partition the result region in place or copy only when caller aliasing is a concern.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.currentCost: Allocates n longs on the stack (8*n bytes) and does a full n-element copy loop before partitioning. For large n this is a large stack footprint (stack-overflow risk on mobile) plus an O(n) memcpy, when the algorithm only needs the first k elements out.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.proposedChange: If the contract allows mutating/consuming `a`, run PartitionLong directly on `a` and copy the first `count` results to `res`, dropping `temp` entirely. If `a` must be preserved but `res` has capacity n, partition into `res` instead of a separate `temp`. At minimum replace the manual copy loop with UnsafeUtility.MemCpy / Buffer.MemoryCopy.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.rationale: Removes an 8*n-byte stackalloc and an entire O(n) element-by-element copy pass; quickselect is in-place by nature, so the scratch buffer is pure overhead. Large stackalloc on mobile threads is a real overflow hazard.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.risk: Changes whether the caller's input array is mutated. The 'Run' convention here assumes valid caller input but not necessarily input immutability — gate behind the module's mutation contract. If preserving `a` is required, the partition-into-res variant keeps semantics identical while still removing temp.

src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.summary: Missing k>=n short-circuit: when k >= n the quickselect loop does needless partitioning work to return the whole array.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.currentCost: When k >= n, the desired output is simply all n elements; yet the while loop still runs full quickselect partitions (O(n) work and swaps) before `count = Min(k,n)` clamps it. Also `if (idx == k)` can never trigger usefully when k == n since indices are < n.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.proposedChange: Add `if (k >= n) { for (int i=0;i<n;i++) res[i]=a[i]; return n; }` early-out (or copy and return before the loop). Mirrors the `k >= len` early return already present in Selection.SelectTopK.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.rationale: Avoids an entire quickselect pass plus its swaps when the result is trivially the whole input. Brings TopK.Run in line with the guard SelectTopK already has.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.risk: None for valid input; result set (first n elements) is identical. Order within the returned k is already unspecified by quickselect, so copying as-is preserves the contract.

src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.summary: Inconsistent quickselect update rule: TopK.Run uses `left = idx` on the `idx < k` branch while SelectTopK/TryGetKth use `left = idx + 1`, which can cause non-termination/extra iterations.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.currentCost: In TopK.Run, on `idx < k` it sets `left = idx` (not `idx + 1`). Since element at `idx` is already in its final partitioned position, re-including it wastes an iteration and, in degenerate equal-key runs, can stall progress; the two code paths solving the same problem disagree.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.proposedChange: Use `left = idx + 1` on the `idx < k` branch to match SelectTopK/TryGetKth, since position `idx` is fixed after partitioning. Unify the three loops into one shared helper to keep them consistent.
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.rationale: The pivot lands at its sorted index `idx`, so the next search range starts at idx+1; `left = idx` redundantly reconsiders a settled element and reduces progress guarantees. Sharing one implementation removes the divergence (also a maintainability/ergonomics win).
src/IAFahim.Search.Selection/Selection.c.risk: PartitionLong partitions in descending order and TopK currently never sets result via `idx==k` break path differently — verify the descending-partition invariant still places element idx finally (it does). Behavior for the top-k SET is preserved; only iteration count and worst-case progress improve. Validate against existing tests before applying.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/BinarySea.summary: Three-way compare uses two dependent loads/branches per iteration; collapse to a single comparison per step (lower-bound style) plus one equality check at the end.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/BinarySea.currentCost: Each loop iteration does two comparisons against ptr[mid] (< key, then > key). On a non-found path the loop body has up to 2 branches per step, lengthening the dependency chain and adding branch-prediction pressure on random keys.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/BinarySea.proposedChange: Convert to a lower-bound search: while(lo<hi){int mid=lo+((hi-lo)>>1); if(ptr[mid]<key) lo=mid+1; else hi=mid;} then after the loop test if(lo<len && ptr[lo]==key){index=lo; return true;}. This is one comparison per iteration plus a single final equality test.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/BinarySea.rationale: Classic three-way binary search averages ~1.5 comparisons/iteration but has an early-exit; the lower-bound variant does exactly one comparison per iteration with a tighter, more predictable branch and a shorter dependency chain (mid->load->compare->update), which Burst/branch-predictors handle better for the common not-found and duplicate-key cases. One extra load at the end is amortized over log2(n) iterations.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/BinarySea.risk: Behavior changes for duplicate keys: three-way TryFind returns an arbitrary matching index, lower-bound returns the FIRST match. If callers rely on returning any match this is fine; if a specific (non-first) match index is contractually required, reject. For all-distinct arrays the returned index is identical. Need len>0 guard already implicit since lo<len handles len==0.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.summary: Open-addressing probe recomputes (idx+i)%cap every iteration; replace modulo with an incrementing index that wraps by subtraction.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.currentCost: Inner loop executes `int c=(idx+i)%cap` each probe — an integer division/remainder (10-40 cycles on many targets, not vectorizable) on every step of a linear probe.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.proposedChange: Compute idx once, then iterate: `int c=idx; for(int i=0;i<cap;i++){ ... if(occ[c]==0)return false; if(CompareKeys...){...} c++; if(c==cap)c-=cap; }`. The wrap is a single compare+subtract, no division.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.rationale: Removes one integer remainder per probe iteration, replacing ~20-cycle div with a 1-cycle predictable compare/sub. Linear probing already walks contiguous memory; the branch `c==cap` is taken at most once per full scan so prediction is near-perfect.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.risk: None semantically: idx is already in [0,cap), and c increments by 1 each step wrapping at cap, producing the exact same probe sequence (idx, idx+1, ..., mod cap). cap must be >0 (already required for the original % cap).

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.summary: Initial bucket uses signed `h % cap`; the masked-positive hash means an unsigned reduction is valid and avoids signed-remainder overhead.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.currentCost: `int idx = h % cap` is a signed remainder; signed % emits extra instructions to handle the sign of the dividend even though h is already non-negative (GetUnmanagedHash returns h & 0x7FFFFFFF).
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.proposedChange: Use `int idx = (int)((uint)h % (uint)cap);` so the JIT/Burst emits an unsigned remainder, or if cap is constrained to a power of two by the caller, expose a masked variant `idx = h & (cap-1)`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.rationale: h is guaranteed in [0, 2^31-1], so unsigned reduction is identical in value but the codegen for unsigned % is cheaper (no sign-correction). A power-of-two mask path would strength-reduce the only remaining division entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.risk: Value-identical because h>=0 and cap>0, so signed and unsigned remainder agree. The mask variant is only valid when cap is a power of two — gate it behind a separate method or a documented precondition; do not silently apply.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.summary: Byte-by-byte hash and compare defeat vectorization for common blittable key sizes (4/8/16 bytes); special-case word-sized keys.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.currentCost: Both loops iterate sizeof(T) times one byte at a time. For a 16-byte key that is 16 load+branch iterations for compare and 16 mul-add iterations for hash, far more than the data warrants; the per-byte loop is a serial dependency chain (h=h*31+p[i]) that Burst cannot SIMD.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.proposedChange: Branch on sizeof(T): for sizeof(T)==4 compare/hash via *(uint*)a; for ==8 via *(ulong*); for ==16 via two ulongs. CompareKeys becomes a single (or two) word comparisons; hashing can mix words with a multiply-xor finalizer. Fall back to the byte loop for odd sizes. Since sizeof(T) is a JIT-time constant per generic instantiation, Burst will dead-code-eliminate the wrong branches.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.rationale: Word-wide loads cut the compare from N byte-loads to N/8 word-loads and remove the per-byte branch; the equality early-out on mismatch is rarely hit for full-key compares anyway. Fewer loads, shorter dependency chain, better for Burst which specializes per generic type.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.risk: Hash VALUE will differ from the current byte-polynomial hash. That is acceptable only if no external contract depends on the exact hash value (it is an internal probe index). The compare must remain a full bitwise equality (same observable result). Unaligned word loads are fine on the supported targets but note it for strict-alignment platforms; CompareKeys result is bit-identical so observable behavior of QueryCacheGet is preserved.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.summary: qt/2 is recomputed repeatedly inside FindBestCentroid's nested loops; hoist the half-size and reuse.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.currentCost: FindBestCentroid evaluates `qt/2` once per outer node for the `ok` test and again per incident edge in the inner condition `sz[v] > qt/2`. qt is loop-invariant for the whole call, so this is a redundant signed division (qt/2) executed O(edges) times.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.proposedChange: At the top of FindBestCentroid compute `int half = qt >> 1;` (qt is the queue tail count, always >=0, so arithmetic shift == /2) and use `half` in both the outer and inner comparisons.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.rationale: Removes a division (or at least a redundant recompute) from the innermost edge-scan loop, replacing it with a single hoisted shift. The centroid scan touches every edge of the component, so this is the hot inner loop of each decomposition level.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.risk: None: qt is a count of enqueued nodes, strictly >=0, so qt>>1 equals qt/2 exactly. Pure hoist, no behavior change.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.summary: FindBestCentroid re-scans every node's edges to validate the centroid, an O(V+E) pass that duplicates information already derivable from subtree sizes in O(V).
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.currentCost: After ComputeSubtreeSizes, FindBestCentroid does a second full edge walk per candidate to find the max child subtree, making centroid finding O(V+E) with an extra adjacency traversal each decomposition level.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.proposedChange: During the reverse pass in ComputeSubtreeSizes, also accumulate per-node maxChildSize[u] (the largest sz over children) by updating maxChildSize[p]=max(maxChildSize[p], sz[u]). Then the centroid test is purely sz-based: node u is a centroid iff max(maxChildSize[u], qt - sz[u]) <= qt/2, evaluated in a single O(V) forward scan with no adjacency walk.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.rationale: Eliminates the second adjacency traversal (the dominant edge-touching loop) and replaces it with an O(1) test per node using an array filled during the existing size pass — same total info, strictly fewer edge visits, lower constant and no extra asymptotic term beyond the unavoidable size computation.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.risk: Requires one more stackalloc int[numNodes] (maxChildSize), increasing stack working set by 4*numNodes bytes — acceptable given numNodes already drives several such buffers; on deeply recursive decomposition the stackalloc is per-call so verify total stack budget. The selected centroid is equivalent (same definition: no subtree, including the parent side qt-sz[u], exceeds qt/2). Init maxChildSize to 0 each level.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.summary: The `queue` scratch buffer duplicates traversal order that `parent` already encodes; but more concretely, removed[] init loop can be fused and buffers right-sized.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.currentCost: Four stackalloc int[numNodes] plus a byte[numNodes] are allocated every call; the removed[] zero-init is a separate loop from the others. On mobile with large numNodes this is a sizable per-call stack footprint and an extra init pass.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.proposedChange: Allocate the int buffers in one stackalloc int[numNodes*3] block and slice (sz/parent/queue) to improve locality, and zero removed[] with a single Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned/Burst memset rather than a scalar loop. Keep removed as the only persistent-across-iterations buffer.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.rationale: A single contiguous allocation improves cache locality and a vectorized memset clears removed[] faster than a scalar byte loop (which Burst may not auto-vectorize across the function boundary). Reduces setup overhead per outer decomposition call.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Interacti.risk: Pointer slicing must keep correct alignment (int* slices of an int block are naturally aligned). InitBlock semantics identical to the zero loop. Low impact; mainly setup-phase, not the inner loop.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.summary: The per-round team rotation is an O(numTeams) array shift; the entire schedule can be generated by index arithmetic with no rotation buffer.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.currentCost: Each of `rounds` rounds does a backward copy loop shifting teams[1..numTeams-1], i.e. O(numTeams) memory moves per round => O(numTeams^2) total writes plus the match emission, and the rotation creates a serial dependency that Burst cannot vectorize.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.proposedChange: Replace the rotation with the standard circle method closed form: team 0 is fixed; for round r and slot i, the opponent indices are computed as (r + i) mod (numTeams-1) and (r - i mod (numTeams-1)) with the fixed slot handled separately, writing matches directly. This removes the teams[] buffer and the shift loop entirely.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.rationale: Turns O(numTeams^2) data movement into O(numTeams^2) pure index math with zero memory shuffling and no loop-carried dependency on the teams array, which Burst vectorizes/pipelines far better and drops a stackalloc.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.risk: The closed-form must reproduce the EXACT same pairing and the same t1/t2 ordering and the same -1 bye encoding as the current rotation, otherwise observable output (schedule[] contents/order) changes. This requires careful derivation and a parity check against the current algorithm before adopting; if exact-order parity cannot be guaranteed, keep the rotation. Flagged as a candidate, not a drop-in.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.summary: isOdd bye-substitution branches run inside the hot match loop even though the bye team index (numTeams-1) is known per round position.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.currentCost: For odd n, every emitted match tests `t1==numTeams-1` and `t2==numTeams-1`. Only one slot per round ever holds the phantom team, so most of these branches are wasted work in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.proposedChange: Hoist the odd-n handling: the phantom team (index numTeams-1) only ever appears as t2 of slot i==0 or rotates predictably; compute which single slot contains it per round and patch that one match to -1 after the inner loop, leaving the inner loop branch-free.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.rationale: Removes two comparisons per match from the inner loop for the odd-n case, converting them into a single post-loop fix-up. Smaller inner-loop body, better vectorization of the common emit path.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.risk: Must correctly identify the phantom slot each round to preserve identical -1 placement; if mis-derived, byes land on wrong matches. Low impact and only benefits odd n; verify slot mapping against current output before applying.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.summary: Inner loop recomputes (r+c)%n and a multiply r*n per cell; replace modulo with a running counter and strength-reduce the row base.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.currentCost: Each of n^2 cells does `grid[r*n+c] = (r+c)%n + 1` — a multiply (r*n) recomputable as a running base, and a remainder per cell. n^2 remainders dominate for large n and are not vectorizable.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.proposedChange: Hoist row base: `int* row = grid + r*n;` (or maintain `int baseIdx` incremented by n each row). For the value, maintain `int v = (r % n); for(c...){ row[c] = v + 1; v++; if(v==n) v=0; }`. This removes the per-cell modulo (replaced by compare+reset) and the per-cell multiply.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.rationale: (r+c)%n increases by 1 each step and wraps at n, so a running counter with a single compare/reset reproduces it exactly while eliminating n^2 integer remainders and n^2 multiplies. The resulting loop is a simple increment Burst can pipeline well.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/Schedulin.risk: None semantically: v starts at r%n and steps identically to (r+c)%n, wrapping at n; +1 offset preserved. n>=1 assumed (n==0 writes nothing, same as original). Pure strength reduction.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.summary: Ternary search on a sorted array is strictly worse than binary search; it does more comparisons per the same log-base reduction.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.currentCost: Each iteration computes two thirds (two divisions by 3) and up to 4 comparisons to cut the range to 1/3. Information-theoretically, comparison search on sorted data is optimal at binary (1 comparison -> halve); ternary uses ~2 comparisons to cut to 1/3, giving worst-case ~2*log3(n) = ~1.26*log2(n) comparisons vs log2(n) for binary — more comparisons AND two divisions by 3 (not power-of-two, not shiftable) per step.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.proposedChange: If the contract is just 'find key in sorted int array, return index or ~insertionPoint', replace the body with a binary search returning ~lo on miss. If ternary is required for API/teaching reasons, at minimum compute `third=(hi-lo)/3` once and reuse for both mid1=lo+third and mid2=hi-third to avoid the second division.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.rationale: Binary search dominates ternary on sorted-array membership: fewer comparisons, and mid via (hi-lo)>>1 is a shift versus /3 which is a real division (~20+ cycles, twice per ternary step). Even keeping ternary, hoisting `third` removes one division per iteration.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.risk: Switching to binary changes internal probe order but preserves the observable contract IF return value is index-on-hit and ~lo (insertion point) on miss — binary search yields the same insertion point. For arrays with duplicate keys the returned hit index may differ from ternary's (neither guarantees first/last), so only safe if callers accept any matching index. The `third` hoist is fully behavior-preserving and unconditional.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.summary: (hi-lo)/3 is computed twice per iteration for mid1 and mid2.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.currentCost: mid1 = lo + (hi-lo)/3 and mid2 = hi - (hi-lo)/3 each evaluate the integer division (hi-lo)/3 independently => two divisions per loop iteration.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.proposedChange: Hoist `int third = (hi - lo) / 3;` then `int mid1 = lo + third; int mid2 = hi - third;`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.rationale: Halves the number of (non-strength-reducible) integer divisions per iteration from 2 to 1; division is the most expensive arithmetic op here and sits on the critical path of every step.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/TernarySe.risk: None: identical values, single behavior-preserving CSE the JIT may or may not already perform across the two uses; making it explicit guarantees it under Burst.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.summary: Convert the data-dependent branch in the search loop to a branchless predicated update to eliminate branch mispredictions on random keys.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.currentCost: Each of the ~log2(len) iterations executes an unpredictable conditional branch (ptr[mid] > key). For random/uniform keys this branch mispredicts ~50% of the time; on PC and especially in-order/short-pipeline mobile cores each misprediction costs ~10-20 cycles, dominating the loop body which otherwise is a load + compare + a couple of adds/shifts.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.rationale: The classic lower_bound/upper_bound restructured as base+half is the standard branchless form: it removes the only unpredictable branch from the hot loop, turning each iteration into a fixed-latency sequence (load, compare, conditional-move, add, shift) with no speculation penalty. Total cycle count becomes deterministic ~log2(len) iterations regardless of key distribution, which is a net win whenever the original branch is not highly biased.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.risk: Semantics must be verified to match exactly: upper_bound returns the count of elements <= key, i.e. first index where ptr[index] > key. The proposed loop must terminate with n==1 then do one final ptr[baseIdx] <= key correction; off-by-one in the final correction or the half/n update would change results. Must also preserve behavior for len==0 (return 0) and for keys outside the array. Reduces instruction-level branch predictability dependence but introduces a loop-carried dependency through baseIdx (cmov result feeds next address) which can slightly lengthen the critical path on wide OoO cores when the branch was actually well-predicted; the win holds for unpredictable keys, the common case for a general search primitive. No signed/overflow change: baseIdx+half stays within [0,len] as before.

src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.currentCost: 'using System;' is imported but no System type is referenced in the file (only System.Runtime.CompilerServices.MethodImplOptions is used). It is dead source clutter, mirrored identically in LowerBound.cs.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.proposedChange: Delete line 1 'using System;'. Keep only 'using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;'.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.rationale: Zero runtime cost either way (unused usings are elided by the compiler), but removing it improves readability/consistency and avoids a misleading signal that System types are in play. Pure hygiene.
src/IAFahim.Search.Specialized/UpperBoun.risk: None. No behavioral change; the build still compiles since no System.* symbol is referenced. Purely cosmetic.

src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.summary: Strength-reduce the integer division in Gosper's hack to a shift, since the divisor is always a power of two.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.currentCost: One hardware integer division (idiv) per call: `(((r ^ mask) >> 2) / c)`. idiv is ~20-40 cycles and is not pipelined, dominating the cost of this otherwise-cheap leaf method that is called once per enumeration step in tight loops.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.proposedChange: c = mask & -mask is by construction the lowest set bit, i.e. always a power of two. Replace `/ c` with a right shift by trailing-zero-count of c. Under Burst, use Unity.Mathematics: `int tz = math.tzcnt(c); return (((r ^ mask) >> 2) >> tz) | r;`. If Unity.Mathematics is unavailable here, compute tz via De Bruijn or `System.Numerics.BitOperations.TrailingZeroCount`. The shifted dividend `(r ^ mask) >> 2` is non-negative on the valid (mask != 0) path, so signed >> equals the division exactly.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.rationale: Division by a power-of-two known only at runtime still compiles to a full idiv because the compiler cannot prove c is a power of two. tzcnt + shr is ~3 cycles total vs ~20-40 for idiv, and both feed a much shorter dependency chain, improving throughput in the enumeration loop.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.risk: Semantics-preserving only because the dividend is non-negative for valid inputs (mask != 0): for c == 0 (mask == 0) the original `/ c` divides by zero (already UB/exception in the current code), and tzcnt(0)==32 would shift everything out — same precondition (mask != 0) as the original, so no new valid-input regression. Must confirm `(r ^ mask) >> 2 >= 0`: with mask != 0, r = mask + c never overflows for masks not using bit 31 in this enumeration, keeping the value non-negative; if bit 31 can be set, guard or document that mask must be < 2^31 (the same constraint under which the original division behaves).

src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.summary: Replace the Kernighan popcount loop with the hardware popcount intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.currentCost: Loop runs once per set bit (O(popcount) iterations), each iteration a subtract + and + branch with a loop-carried dependency on m. Up to 32 dependent iterations for a full mask.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.proposedChange: Return `math.countbits(mask)` (Unity.Mathematics) or `System.Numerics.BitOperations.PopCount((uint)mask)`. Burst lowers math.countbits to a single POPCNT instruction on supporting targets.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.rationale: A single POPCNT (or a short SWAR fallback on targets without it) is constant-time (~1-3 cycles) versus an O(set bits) dependent loop. Removes the data-dependent branch entirely, which also helps when this is inlined into hot enumeration code.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.risk: Behavior identical for all 32-bit inputs. On mobile/ARM targets without a popcount instruction, Burst emits a branchless SWAR sequence which is still faster and branch-free than the current loop. Cast to uint avoids any sign concerns; result range 0..32 is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.summary: Parameter ordering inconsistency: dst-first vs dst-last across the module's Run methods.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.currentCost: EnumerateMasks.Run is (dst, bits) and EnumerateSubsets.Run is (superMask, dst) / EnumerateSupersets.Run is (subMask, maxMask, dst). Mixed dst position hurts discoverability and call-site consistency, raising the chance of argument-order mistakes (no compile error since both are pointer/int-shaped distinct types here, but still error-prone for callers).
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.proposedChange: Standardize on input-args-first, dst-last (the convention used by the other two files): change EnumerateMasks.Run to `Run(int bits, int* dst)`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.rationale: Consistent signatures reduce caller cognitive load and argument-swap bugs without any change to the generated code or perf model.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateMasks.risk: Source-breaking signature change for existing callers; purely an API consistency decision. No runtime/semantic impact once call sites are updated.

src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateSuper.summary: Remove the dead local `remaining`, which is computed but never used.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateSuper.currentCost: `int remaining = maxMask ^ subMask;` performs an xor and occupies a register/stack slot but is never read. A good optimizer (and Burst) will usually dead-code-eliminate it, but it is dead source that obscures intent.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateSuper.proposedChange: Delete the line `int remaining = maxMask ^ subMask;`.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateSuper.rationale: Eliminates a guaranteed-dead computation and clarifies the algorithm; zero behavioral effect, smaller readable surface, and removes reliance on DCE.
src/IAFahim.Search.Subset/EnumerateSuper.risk: None. The variable has no readers, so removal cannot change observable behavior.

src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.summary: Reverse in-place suffix-sum loop is a strict serial dependency chain; reading ptr[i+1] then writing ptr[i] each iteration prevents vectorization and exposes full load-add-store latency per element.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.currentCost: len-1 iterations, each with a loop-carried dependency (ptr[i] depends on ptr[i+1] just written). ~1 add + 1 load + 1 store per element on the critical path, no ILP, no SIMD.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.proposedChange: Keep the running scalar accumulator out of memory: 'long acc = 0; for (int i = len-1; i >= 0; i--) { acc += ptr[i]; ptr[i] = acc; }'. The accumulator lives in a register, so the store to ptr[i] is no longer a dependency for the next read (next read is ptr[i-1], independent of the store).
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.rationale: Breaks the memory load->store->load dependency chain into a register accumulator chain (add latency only, ~1 cycle), and removes the dependence of each load on the previous store, letting the CPU overlap loads. Same arithmetic, same in-place result.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.risk: None for behavior: produces identical suffix sums and ptr[0] return. Overflow behavior is identical (same unchecked long/int add order).

src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.summary: The sizeof(T)==4 / ==8 branches type-pun via '*(T*)&sum', which forces a stack spill of the accumulator to take its address; a union-free reinterpret avoids the address-taken local.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.currentCost: Taking '&sum' marks the accumulator address-exposed, which can inhibit keeping it purely in a register and forces a store/reload at the return; minor but on a hot leaf method.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.proposedChange: Return via a typed cast directly: for the 4-byte path 'int r = sum; return *(T*)&r;' is the same; better, since sizeof(T) is a compile-time constant under Burst specialization, the unused branch is dead-code-eliminated already — keep as is, but mark the local with the pattern that avoids re-taking address inside the loop (it already is outside the loop, so impact is low).
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.rationale: sizeof(T) is constant per Burst monomorphization so the branch folds away; the only residual cost is the address-of on the accumulator at return. Confirming the accumulator is written once after the loop (already true) keeps this near-optimal.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.risk: Reinterpret of a 4/8-byte integer to T is only valid when sizeof(T) matches; guarded by the sizeof(T) checks already. No change to semantics.

src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.summary: Naming/contract inconsistency: the typed Run overloads (int*/long*) build an in-place suffix-sum array and return ptr[0]; the generic Run<T> instead computes only the total sum without writing the suffix array, yet Sum<T> returns ptr[0] assuming the suffix array was built. Callers using Run<T> then Sum<T>/RangeSum<T> get inconsistent results.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.currentCost: Run<T> does a forward total-sum and never populates the suffix array, so a subsequent Sum<T> (returns ptr[0]) yields the full sum only by coincidence, while RangeSum<T> re-scans O(r-l) instead of using O(1) suffix differences ptr[l]-ptr[r+1].
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.proposedChange: Make generic Run<T> match the typed overloads: build the in-place suffix sums (acc-accumulator reverse loop), return ptr[0]. Then RangeSum<T> can become O(1): 'ptr[l] - ptr[r+1]' (with ptr[r+1] treated as 0 when r==len-1), instead of an O(n) rescan.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.rationale: Aligns the generic with the specialized overloads (consistent observable contract across the class) AND turns RangeSum from O(n) into O(1) once the suffix array exists — an asymptotic win for range queries, which is the entire point of a suffix-sum structure.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.risk: This CHANGES observable behavior of Run<T>/RangeSum<T> (Run<T> currently leaves the array untouched). It is a contract fix, not a semantics-preserving micro-opt: only adopt if the intended contract is 'Run builds the suffix array' as the typed overloads imply. RangeSum O(1) form requires the array to be a valid suffix-sum array and bounds r+1<=len.

src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.summary: IComparable<T>.CompareTo is an interface-dispatched call inside the hot loop; for the common blittable numeric types this defeats branchless SIMD min/max and risks a non-devirtualized virtual/interface call.
