src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.currentCost: One interface call per element (CompareTo) plus a branch. Even when Burst devirtualizes, CompareTo's three-way result (>0/<0) is heavier than a single compare, and it blocks vectorized min/max.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.proposedChange: Provide sizeof(T)-dispatched specializations for the 4-byte and 8-byte integer/float cases (mirroring SuffixSums) using direct '<'/'>' on reinterpreted int/long/float/double, and a branchless select (e.g. min = a + ((b - a) & ((b - a) >> 63)) for longs, or math.min under Burst). Keep the IComparable<T> generic as the fallback.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.rationale: Direct relational operators on concrete numeric types are single-cycle, branch-predictable, and SIMD-friendly; Burst auto-vectorizes a running min/max reduction. Removes interface-dispatch overhead and the three-way CompareTo computation on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.risk: Branchless integer min/max via sign-shift is signed-specific; for unsigned reinterpretation the shift trick is invalid — must dispatch by actual element type, not just sizeof. Float NaN ordering differs between CompareTo and '<', so the float path must preserve the existing CompareTo tie/NaN semantics or be documented as numeric-only.

src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.summary: RangeSum after a suffix-sum build still rescans O(r-l); the structure already supports O(1) range queries via ptr[l]-ptr[r+1].
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.currentCost: RangeSum is O(r-l+1) per query, defeating the purpose of precomputing suffix sums.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.proposedChange: After Run builds the suffix-sum array, expose a RangeSum that returns ptr[l] - (r+1 < len ? ptr[r+1] : 0). This is O(1).
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.rationale: A suffix-sum (or prefix-sum) array exists precisely to answer range-sum queries in O(1); the current O(n) rescan wastes the precomputation.
src/IAFahim.Search.Suffix/Suffix.cs.risk: Requires ptr to actually hold suffix sums (post-Run) and r+1<=len. The current RangeSum makes no such assumption (it sums raw values), so this is a contract/semantics change, not a drop-in — only valid if RangeSum is defined to operate on a built suffix array.

src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.summary: Generic IComparable<T> constraint forces interface-based comparison that defeats Burst and is non-blittable-friendly for the comparison path; redundant indexed loads in the hot ternary.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.currentCost: `a[i].CompareTo(b[j]) <= 0 ? a[i++] : b[j++]` reloads a[i] (and the ternary reloads either a[i] or b[j]) and dispatches through IComparable<T>.CompareTo. Under Burst, IComparable<T> is a managed interface; Burst only compiles it if the concrete type is statically known and the call devirtualizes. A generic over an interface constraint can fail Burst compilation or fall back to a virtual/boxing path, and CompareTo for a struct still imposes a call boundary the JIT may not fully inline. The ternary also re-indexes the chosen array a second time to read the value being stored.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.proposedChange: Hoist the two operands into locals before comparing/storing to remove redundant indexed loads: `T av = a[i]; T bv = b[j]; if (av.CompareTo(bv) <= 0) { dst[k++] = av; i++; } else { dst[k++] = bv; j++; }`. Additionally, provide non-generic concrete overloads (e.g. MergeSortedInt32(int*,int,int*,int,int*), MergeSortedInt64, MergeSortedSingle) that compare with primitive operators (`av <= bv`) so the comparison is a single branch with no interface dispatch — these are what Burst vectorizes/inlines cleanly. Keep the generic version for ergonomics.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.rationale: Caching av/bv eliminates 2 redundant pointer loads per iteration (one for the re-read in the taken ternary branch, one because CompareTo and the store both index the array). Primitive-operator overloads turn CompareTo's call into a single compare instruction Burst can branchlessly select on, removing the interface dispatch entirely and keeping the loop in fully-compiled Burst code.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.risk: Behavior-preserving: CompareTo(b)<=0 for int/long/float matches `a<=b` for all finite inputs; stability (a chosen on ties) is preserved by keeping `<= 0`. Float caveat: NaN ordering differs between CompareTo (total order, NaN largest) and `<=` (NaN comparisons false) — so a float overload must either document no-NaN inputs or fall back to CompareTo; do NOT silently swap operators for floating types if NaN inputs are valid.

src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.summary: Hot-loop indexed loads a[left] and b[right] are recomputed each iteration even when only one pointer advanced; minor dependency-chain shortening possible.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.currentCost: Each iteration recomputes `a[left] + b[right]`. When sum<target only left advances (b[right] unchanged) and when sum>target only right advances (a[left] unchanged), yet both array elements are reloaded from memory every pass. The equality branch increments count and both pointers.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.proposedChange: Cache the two endpoint values in locals and reload only the one that moved: maintain `int av = a[left];` reloaded only after left++, `int bv = b[right];` reloaded only after right--. On the equality case both move so reload both. Compare `int sum = av + bv;`.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.rationale: Halves the number of pointer dereferences in the two common branches, shortening the load->add->compare dependency chain and reducing cache/load-port pressure in the inner loop. Loop trip count is unchanged so this is a pure constant-factor win.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.risk: Must reload av/bv exactly when their index changes and guard the final reload against going out of bounds (reload only inside the loop after the increment, before the next compare uses it). Overflow of a[left]+b[right] is pre-existing and unchanged. Net code is slightly longer for a modest gain — low impact; reject if branch-prediction on the reload guards costs more than the saved loads on the target ISA.

src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.summary: CountPairsWithSum and HasPairWithSum duplicate the identical two-pointer scan; HasPairWithSum is just CountPairsWithSum with early-exit. No correctness issue, only API/maintenance consistency.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.currentCost: Two near-identical loops must be kept in sync by hand. No Try* naming convention applied even though HasPairWithSum is effectively a boolean Try-style query.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.proposedChange: Keep both for the perf model (early-exit must stay a separate hot path, not a flag on the counting loop), but document them as a pair and consider renaming to follow the library's Run/Try convention (e.g. TryHasPairWithSum is unnecessary, but aligning naming with the rest of the module). Optionally add `out int pairCount` is NOT advised since it would force the full scan. No code-gen change.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.rationale: Pure ergonomics/discoverability; preserves the two distinct compiled hot paths so the perf model is untouched.
src/IAFahim.Search.TwoPointer/TwoPointer.risk: None functionally. Do not merge the two methods behind a bool flag — that would add a per-iteration branch to the counting path and defeat the early-exit specialization. This is the lowest-priority item.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.summary: Convert tail-recursive sift-down into an iterative loop
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.currentCost: Each level of the heap that needs fixing performs a recursive call to FixInt32. For a heap of N elements the sift-down can recurse log2(N) deep, and unless Burst/the JIT performs tail-call elimination (Burst does NOT guarantee it) every level pushes a stack frame and pays call/return overhead. PopInt32 and HeapifyInt32 both go through this path, so it is on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Replace the recursive call with a while(true) loop: compute smallest among i/l/r, break if smallest==i, otherwise swap ptr[i]<->ptr[smallest], set i=smallest, recompute l=(i<<1)+1, r=(i<<1)+2, and continue. This is a mechanical transformation of the existing tail recursion.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.rationale: Removes log2(N) call/return pairs and stack-frame setup per sift-down; the loop body keeps i/l/r in registers and shortens the dependency chain. Identical comparison/swap sequence, so output ordering is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.risk: None semantically; it is a pure tail-recursion-to-loop rewrite producing the same swaps in the same order. Just ensure l and r are recomputed from the new i each iteration.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.summary: Use hole-based sift-up instead of repeated 3-way swaps
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.currentCost: The sift-up loop performs a full 3-element swap (3 reads + 3 writes via tmp) at every level the value bubbles up, even though the inserted value's final resting slot is only known at the end. For a value that rises k levels, that is ~3k writes.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Save int val once. Loop: while(i>0){ int p=Parent(i); if(ptr[p]<=val) break; ptr[i]=ptr[p]; i=p; } then ptr[i]=val; (the initial ptr[len]=val write can be dropped since the final store covers it).
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.rationale: Each level now costs 1 read (ptr[p]) + 1 write (ptr[i]=ptr[p]) instead of a 3-way swap, roughly halving memory traffic, and val stays in a register across the whole climb, shortening the dependency chain. Produces an identical final array.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.risk: None; this is the textbook hole-insertion form of the same min-heap sift-up. The comparison ptr[p]<=val preserves the existing <= (stable break) behavior.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.summary: Apply hole-based sift-down to also remove per-level swaps
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.currentCost: After the recursion-to-loop change, the loop still does a full 3-way swap at each descended level. The element being sifted reaches its final slot only at the end, so intermediate swaps move data that may move again.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Hole variant: int v=ptr[i]; loop selecting smaller child c; while child<v keep ptr[i]=ptr[c], i=c; finally ptr[i]=v. Combine with the iterative loop so each level is 1 read + 1 write of the child plus the child-selection compare.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.rationale: Halves write traffic on the dominant heapify/pop path and keeps the sifted value in a register, shortening the dependency chain. Same comparison results, same final layout.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.risk: None if the child-selection comparisons (< for the min-heap, with l<len / r<len bounds) are preserved exactly. Must keep choosing the strictly-smaller child the same way to preserve identical tie-breaking and final array.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to the leaf heap operations consistent with Parent/Left/Right
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.currentCost: Only Parent/Left/Right are marked AggressiveInlining; FixInt32 is invoked from PopInt32 and HeapifyInt32 as a separate call. PushInt32/PopInt32 are small hot leaves with no inlining hint.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.proposedChange: Mark FixInt32 (once iterative), PushInt32, and PopInt32 with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] so callers in tight loops (e.g. HeapifyInt32 calling FixInt32 N/2 times) can inline and constant-fold len/bounds checks.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.rationale: Inlining the sift routines into HeapifyInt32's loop lets the compiler hoist the len comparison and reuse register state across iterations; eliminates call overhead in the O(N) build path.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/Heap.cs.risk: Inlining a (now non-recursive) FixInt32 is safe. While FixInt32 is still recursive it cannot be inlined; only add the hint after the iterative rewrite, otherwise the hint is ignored.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.summary: Deque only needs windowSize slots, not len; oversized stackalloc risks stack overflow
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.currentCost: int* deque = stackalloc int[len] allocates 4*len bytes on the stack. The monotonic deque never holds more than windowSize live candidates, but because indices are stored absolutely and back keeps growing, the buffer is sized to len. For large len (e.g. 10^6) this is a 4 MB stackalloc that will overflow the stack, especially on mobile where stack budgets are small.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.proposedChange: Size the buffer to windowSize and index it as a ring buffer: store candidate indices in deque[head..tail) modulo windowSize. Replace front/back integer indices with ring positions and a count; the window-eviction check deque[front] <= i-windowSize still uses the stored absolute index. Since at most windowSize candidates coexist, capacity windowSize is provably sufficient.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.rationale: Cuts stack working set from O(len) to O(windowSize), avoiding cache pressure and stack-overflow crashes for large inputs; the algorithm stays O(len) time.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.risk: Ring-buffer modular indexing is more complex; must ensure capacity is windowSize (not windowSize-1) and that the modulo wraps correctly. If windowSize is a power of two the modulo can be a mask. Behavior for valid inputs is identical; only the storage layout changes.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.summary: Hoist src[i] load and reduce repeated index arithmetic in the inner loop
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.currentCost: Inside the loop, src[i] is loaded once but src[deque[back-1]] is reloaded each while-iteration; also i - windowSize and i - windowSize + 1 are recomputed every iteration. The dst write index i-windowSize+1 duplicates the eviction expression.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.proposedChange: Hoist int cur = src[i]; before the while. Precompute int evict = i - windowSize; use evict for the front-eviction test and (evict + 1) for the dst index, or maintain a running outIndex that increments only when i >= windowSize-1. Keep src[deque[back-1]] as is (it changes as back decrements).
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.rationale: Removes redundant subtraction recomputation and one register reload per loop iteration; a running output index turns the conditional store into a straight increment, reducing arithmetic on the hottest loop in the file.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.risk: None; cur==src[i] is loop-invariant within the i-iteration. The running outIndex must start so its first written position equals i-windowSize+1 at i==windowSize-1 (i.e. 0).

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.summary: Remove unused 'using System;' and AggressiveInlining hint that cannot fire
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.currentCost: using System; is unused. The method is large (contains a stackalloc and a full loop) and marked AggressiveInlining, but a method with stackalloc and unbounded loop is effectively never inlined, so the attribute is misleading and adds no value.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.proposedChange: Drop the unused using System;. Remove [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] from Run (keep it only on genuine small leaves) to avoid signaling an inlining intent the compiler will reject.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.rationale: Cleaner code and accurate optimization intent; no codegen change since the hint was already a no-op for this method shape.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.risk: None; purely cosmetic. Confirm no other member in the file relies on System.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.summary: Deque only needs windowSize slots, not len; oversized stackalloc risks stack overflow
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.currentCost: Identical to SlidingWindowMax: stackalloc int[len] reserves 4*len bytes though at most windowSize candidate indices are ever live. Large len causes a multi-megabyte stackalloc that can overflow the stack on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.proposedChange: Size the buffer to windowSize and use ring-buffer indexing (head/tail/count modulo windowSize, mask if windowSize is power of two). The eviction comparison on absolute stored indices is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.rationale: Reduces stack usage from O(len) to O(windowSize) and improves cache locality; same O(len) time.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.risk: Same as the Max variant: requires careful modular wrap and capacity of exactly windowSize. No observable behavior change for valid inputs.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.summary: Hoist src[i] load and reduce repeated index arithmetic in the inner loop
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.currentCost: src[i] is reused but i-windowSize and i-windowSize+1 are recomputed each iteration, and the dst index duplicates the eviction expression.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.proposedChange: Hoist int cur = src[i]; compute evict = i - windowSize once; maintain a running output index incremented when i >= windowSize-1 instead of recomputing i-windowSize+1.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.rationale: Eliminates redundant subtractions and reloads per iteration on the hot loop; identical to the Max-variant micro-opt.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.risk: None for valid inputs; running output index must align with i-windowSize+1 at the first emitting iteration.

src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.summary: Remove unused 'using System;' and AggressiveInlining hint that cannot fire
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.currentCost: using System; is unused, and AggressiveInlining on a stackalloc-containing looped method will not be honored, making the hint misleading.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.proposedChange: Remove using System; and the AggressiveInlining attribute from Run.
src/IAFahim.Search.Window/SlidingWindowM.rationale: Accurate intent and slightly cleaner file with no codegen impact.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.summary: Hoist the just-loaded element when it is already in order, skipping the inner-loop entry comparison and key store on the common nearly-sorted case.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.currentCost: Every iteration unconditionally reads ptr[i] into key, enters the while with a CompareTo, and always writes ptr[j+1]=key at the end even when no shift happened. For already-sorted or nearly-sorted runs the trailing store is a redundant self-write (ptr[i]=ptr[i]).
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.proposedChange: Guard the inner shift loop with an early check: compare ptr[i] against ptr[i-1] first; if ptr[i-1].CompareTo(key) <= 0 (for ascending) continue without loading key into a temp or writing it back. Concretely: if (ptr[i-1].CompareTo(ptr[i]) <= 0) continue; else proceed with the current shift loop. This eliminates one register copy + one store per already-ordered element.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.rationale: Insertion sort's dominant real-world use is small or nearly-sorted arrays (it is typically a base case of a hybrid sort). Removing the redundant key copy and the self-store on the in-order fast path cuts the per-element cost to a single comparison, halving memory traffic on sorted input and shortening the dependency chain (no store feeding the next iteration's load).
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.risk: Must keep the comparison direction identical (ascending uses <=0 to preserve stability; descending uses >=0). The < / <= boundary matters: using <= (ascending) / >= (descending) keeps equal elements from being shifted, preserving the existing stable behavior. No overflow or signed/unsigned concern.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.summary: Collapse the two near-identical methods into one comparison-direction-parameterized core, or document them as a deliberate duplicated pair, to avoid divergence and ease adding a Comparer overload.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.currentCost: Run and RunDescending are byte-for-byte identical except the inner comparison sign (>0 vs <0), so any future fix (e.g. the fast-path guard above) must be applied twice and can drift.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.proposedChange: Keep the two public entry points for Burst-friendliness (no function-pointer indirection on the hot path), but factor the body into a private generic helper taking a compile-time direction flag, or at minimum apply identical optimizations to both. Since Burst specializes generics, a private static core inlined into both wrappers via AggressiveInlining preserves codegen.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.rationale: Reduces maintenance surface and the chance the two paths diverge in correctness; if implemented as an inlined private helper with a const direction, Burst constant-folds the branch so there is zero runtime cost.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.risk: If the direction is passed as a non-const runtime parameter it introduces a per-iteration branch that Burst may not hoist; must be a const/generic specialization so the branch is eliminated at compile time. Otherwise it regresses cycles.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.summary: Constraining on IComparable<T> dispatches through the interface; for the hot path Burst handles generic-constrained CompareTo well, but a function-pointer or direct-comparator overload would let callers avoid interface CompareTo overhead for custom orderings.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.currentCost: T.CompareTo is an interface-constrained call. For built-in unmanaged types Burst lowers this to direct comparisons, but the IComparable<T> constraint forces every comparison through CompareTo semantics (which for floats invokes total-order/NaN handling, costlier than a raw < comparison).
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.proposedChange: Offer an overload (or document) that, for primitive numeric T where caller wants raw IEEE comparison, sorts via a delegate*<T,T,int> comparator or a typed fast path. Keep the IComparable<T> version as the default. Do not change the existing method's semantics.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.rationale: CompareTo on float/double does NaN-aware total ordering; a raw '<' is fewer cycles when the caller knows NaNs are absent. Exposing a comparator-pointer overload lets perf-sensitive callers opt into the cheaper comparison without breaking the stable, NaN-correct default.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Insertion/Insertion.cs.risk: Raw '<' is NOT equivalent to float.CompareTo for NaN/-0.0; this must be a SEPARATE overload, never a silent replacement of CompareTo, or it changes observable ordering for NaN inputs. The function-pointer comparator must be a delegate* (Burst-compatible), not a managed delegate.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.summary: Copy only the left run into scratch instead of the whole segment, halving copy traffic per merge across all log2(n) passes.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.currentCost: For every merge of two adjacent runs the code copies the entire segment [l,r) into tmp (segLen = r-l elements, line 49) before merging back. Across the whole sort this is n copies per pass * log2(n) passes = n*log2(n) extra element copies, and tmp is read on both the A and B sides.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.proposedChange: Copy only the left run [l,m) into tmp (m-l elements). Merge by reading A from tmp[0..aLen) and B directly from ptr[m..r) in place, writing into ptr starting at ic=l: while(ia<aLen && ib<r) ptr[ic++] = tmp[ia].CompareTo(ptr[ib])<=0 ? tmp[ia++] : ptr[ib++]; then drain remaining A from tmp (the B tail is already in correct position so its drain loop is a no-op and can be dropped). Use named locals leftLen=m-l.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.rationale: The classic bottom-up in-place merge needs only the left half buffered: the write cursor ic never overtakes the B read cursor ib because each step that consumes B writes the consumed B element's slot, so ic<=ib invariant holds; A lives in a separate buffer so it is never clobbered. This cuts scratch writes+reads from 2*(r-l) to (m-l) per merge — roughly a 2x reduction in memory traffic in the dominant inner loop, fewer cache lines touched, lower bandwidth on mobile.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.risk: Semantics-preserving and stable: ties still resolve to the left (tmp) side via <=0, matching current behavior. Must keep the B-side read as ptr[ib] (in-place) and only drain the A remainder; the B remainder is already in place. Standard, well-known invariant — no overlap hazard. tmp allocation in RunInPlace can be shrunk to len/2 rounded up to match (only left runs are buffered), saving ~half the scratch RAM.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.summary: Scratch buffer can be sized to the largest left run (ceil(len/2)) rather than len once only the left run is copied.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.currentCost: Marshal.AllocHGlobal allocates len*sizeof(T) bytes; combined with the segment-copy approach the full buffer is used.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.proposedChange: Adopt the left-run-only merge (see RunInPlaceCore opportunity), then allocate ((len+1)/2)*sizeof(T) bytes. The maximum left run buffered is ceil(len/2) elements (the last left run at the top width).
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.rationale: Halves the off-heap scratch allocation, reducing peak RAM and improving locality (smaller buffer stays hotter in cache). On mobile the reduced AllocHGlobal footprint matters for memory-constrained scenes.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.risk: Only valid if RunInPlaceCore is changed to buffer just the left run; the largest left run is exactly ceil(len/2). Keep the (long) cast in the size computation to avoid int overflow for large len*sizeof(T).

src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant step value 2*width out of the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.currentCost: 2*width is recomputed at line 47 (Math.Min(l + 2*width, len)) and again at line 58 (l += 2*width) for every iteration of the inner l-loop; width is constant across that loop.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.proposedChange: Compute int twoWidth = width << 1; once per outer pass and reuse it for both r = Math.Min(l + twoWidth, len) and l += twoWidth. Optionally compute the outer width step as width = twoWidth at end of pass.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.rationale: Removes one shift/add from the inner loop body and clarifies the stride; trivial but free strength reduction with zero risk.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Merge/Merge.cs.risk: None. width is bounded < len <= int.MaxValue at loop entry, but twoWidth = width<<1 could overflow int when width >= 2^30. Guard: the outer loop condition width<len already bounds width<len<=int.MaxValue; if len can exceed 2^30, compute twoWidth as long or clamp via the existing Math.Min(l+..,len). Use long for the stride if len near int.MaxValue is supported, otherwise int is safe for realistic sizes.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.summary: Skip the self-swap when i == storeIdx in the Lomuto partition loop.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.currentCost: On every element that is < pivot, the code unconditionally does a 3-instruction swap (read ptr[i], read ptr[storeIdx], two writes). When i == storeIdx (which is the common case for any already-sorted or partially-sorted prefix, and ALWAYS the case until the first element >= pivot is seen), this performs a redundant load+store of the same slot — pure wasted memory traffic and a write that dirties the cache line for no reason.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.proposedChange: Inside the if-body, guard the swap: 'if (i != storeIdx) { T tmp = ptr[i]; ptr[i] = ptr[storeIdx]; ptr[storeIdx] = tmp; } storeIdx++;'. Alternatively, hoist the leading run: advance storeIdx with a tight prefix loop while ptr[i] < pivot && i==storeIdx, then enter the main loop.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.rationale: Eliminates a redundant store (and the false write-dependency it creates) on every leading in-order element. For nearly-sorted inputs this removes ~half the writes; for the very common leading-prefix run it removes them entirely until the first out-of-place element. Fewer stores = fewer dirty cache lines and a shorter store-to-load dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.risk: Semantics identical: swapping a slot with itself is a no-op, so guarding it preserves output exactly. The added branch is well-predicted (taken in steady state once storeIdx lags i), so it is net-positive whenever T is wider than a register or memory bandwidth is the bottleneck; for tiny T (int) on a branchy mobile core the win is marginal but never a regression in cycles since the store is removed.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.summary: Hoist len-1 into a named local to make the loop bound and tail swaps share one value.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.currentCost: 'len - 1' is written 4 times (lines 14,17,27,28). Under Burst/IL this is a trivial sub, but the loop condition 'i < len - 1' recomputes the bound expression each iteration in the IL; the optimizer normally folds it, but expressing it once removes any doubt and documents intent.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.proposedChange: Add 'int last = len - 1;' once after the bounds check, then use 'last' for the pivot-to-end swap, the loop bound 'i < last', and the final restore swaps.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.rationale: Guarantees the loop-bound subtraction is a loop-invariant computed once, shrinks the IL, and improves readability/maintainability without changing behavior.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.risk: None — pure value substitution. Burst almost certainly already hoists this, so the cycle win is essentially zero; value is mainly clarity/insurance, hence low impact.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.summary: The 'i < hi' bounds guard in the right-scan inner loop is a per-iteration branch that the Hoare invariant can make a true sentinel eliminates, but only with a guaranteed sentinel — keep it unless a sentinel is established.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.currentCost: Inner loop line 54 evaluates 'i < hi && ptr[i].CompareTo(pivot) < 0' every step. The 'i < hi' test is an extra compare+branch on the hottest path of quickselect, executed O(n) times per partition level. Classic Hoare partition omits this guard because the pivot at ptr[lo] acts as a stopping sentinel for the j-scan, and the j<i termination bounds the i-scan.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.proposedChange: Do NOT blindly delete 'i < hi'. Establish correctness first: the i-scan can overrun only if every element in (lo,hi) is < pivot. Guard by special-casing or by ensuring the largest element sits at hi-1 as a sentinel. Safer concrete win: replace the guard with a loop-invariant sentinel by selecting pivot as median-of-three (ptr[lo],ptr[mid],ptr[hi-1]) so ptr[hi-1] >= pivot guarantees the i-scan stops without the 'i < hi' test — then drop 'i < hi'.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.rationale: Removing a compare+branch from the inner do-while halves the comparison overhead per i-step and shortens the dependency chain; median-of-three additionally mitigates the O(n^2) worst case of quickselect on sorted/adversarial input, improving expected behavior on degenerate distributions.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.risk: HIGH correctness sensitivity: deleting 'i < hi' WITHOUT a guaranteed right sentinel causes out-of-bounds reads/writes when the pivot is the maximum of the subrange. Only valid after a sentinel is provably placed at ptr[hi-1] (median-of-three with the max landing at the right end, or an explicit sentinel slot). Median-of-three also changes which element is chosen as pivot, so partition positions differ — but the FINAL nth-element result is unchanged because selection is order-statistic deterministic on value. Recommend treating as a guarded refactor, not a one-line edit.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.summary: Cache the pivot comparison target and avoid re-reading ptr[j]/ptr[i] across the swap.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.currentCost: After the swap at lines 56-58, the outer while re-enters and the do-while loops re-load ptr[j] and ptr[i] which were just written, creating store-to-load forwarding dependencies. CompareTo is called via the IComparable<T> constraint; for blittable T Burst devirtualizes it, but the repeated pivot capture is already good (pivot is a local).
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.proposedChange: Minor: ensure pivot stays in a register (already a local T pivot — good). No structural change needed beyond the median-of-three sentinel above. Leave the partition loop as-is unless sentinel work is done.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.rationale: The current code already hoists pivot into a local and uses index-only swaps, which is near-optimal for Hoare partition; the only remaining inner-loop overhead is the 'i < hi' guard addressed separately.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Partition/Partition.cs.risk: None proposed here; this entry documents that the loop body is otherwise already tight and should not be churned. Low impact / effectively no-op recommendation.

src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.summary: Hoare partition uses the first element (ptr[lo]) as pivot, which degrades to O(n^2) and O(n) recursion/iteration on already-sorted or reverse-sorted input — a very common case for game/engine data.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.currentCost: For sorted or nearly-sorted arrays every partition splits off one element, giving O(n^2) comparisons and worst-case O(n) recursion depth before the smaller-side recursion guard helps. Sorted data is a realistic hot path (re-sorting mostly-sorted lists each frame).
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.proposedChange: Use median-of-three pivoting: compute mid = lo + ((hi - lo) >> 1), sort {ptr[lo], ptr[mid], ptr[hi]} into order, and use the median as the pivot (e.g. swap it to ptr[lo] or use it directly). This keeps the Hoare scheme intact but makes worst case statistically unlikely.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.rationale: Median-of-three turns the adversarial sorted/reverse-sorted inputs into well-balanced splits, restoring expected O(n log n) and keeping recursion depth O(log n) in practice. The smaller-side-recursion tail-call already bounds stack to O(log n) worst case, but median-of-three also slashes comparison count on common data.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.risk: Pivot value changes the exact swap sequence, so for inputs with equal keys the final permutation of equal elements differs (sort is not stable anyway, so observable sorted output is unchanged). mid = lo + ((hi-lo)>>1) avoids lo+hi overflow; do not use (lo+hi)>>1.

src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.summary: No insertion-sort cutoff for small partitions; quicksort recurses/partitions down to size 1, paying function-call and partition overhead on tiny ranges where insertion sort is cheaper.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.currentCost: Each leaf partition of size 2-16 still does the full Hoare two-pointer scan plus loop bookkeeping and a recursive/iterative dispatch; for small n the constant factors dominate and branch mispredicts are frequent.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.proposedChange: When (hi - lo) < THRESHOLD (e.g. 16), break out of the quicksort loop and run a simple in-place insertion sort over [lo,hi] using pointer reads. Keep THRESHOLD as a named const int.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.rationale: Insertion sort has lower constant factors and is near-optimal for small, partially-ordered ranges; it is branch-predictable and cache-friendly (sequential access already in L1). Standard introsort/quicksort hybrids gain a measurable constant-factor speedup this way.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.risk: Insertion sort must use the same comparison direction (CompareTo<0 / <) to preserve identical ascending output. Pure constant-factor change, no asymptotic or semantic risk; equal-key ordering may differ but sort is unstable regardless.

src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.symbol: Run<T>(T*,int,int) / RunInt32 — recursion depth on degenerate pivots
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.summary: The smaller-half recursion guard bounds stack to O(log n) for balanced splits, but combined with first-element pivot a fully sorted input still recurses on the empty/size-1 smaller side O(n) times, risking deep call frames under Burst.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.currentCost: With ptr[lo] pivot on sorted input, p-lo is 0 each step so 'Run(ptr, lo, p-1)' recurses on an empty range while the loop walks the large side. The empty-range recursion returns immediately but still incurs n call frames over the lifetime (depth stays shallow only because p-1<lo). This is mostly call overhead, mitigated once median-of-three lands.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.proposedChange: Add an early guard at method entry: 'if (hi - lo < 1) return;' so empty/singleton ranges never enter the while/Partition path, and pair with the median-of-three fix so the recursed side is always the genuinely smaller, non-trivial half.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.rationale: Eliminates redundant call frames and Partition setup for trivial ranges; reduces dependency-chain and call overhead in the recursion. Burst inlines poorly across recursion, so trimming trivial recursive entries reduces instruction count.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.risk: Behavior-preserving: ranges with hi<=lo already do no work inside the loop; the guard only short-circuits earlier. No correctness change.

src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.summary: The generic Partition calls ptr[i].CompareTo(pivot); for unmanaged T this is a constrained call that Burst can devirtualize, but it reads the struct via the indexer twice-ish and relies on CompareTo returning a normalized int.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.currentCost: ptr[i].CompareTo(pivot) loads ptr[i] into a temporary to invoke the interface method; for larger structs this copies the whole element on every comparison in the inner do-while. The Int32 specialization avoids this, which is why it exists.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.proposedChange: For the generic path, load the compared element once into a local T (T a = ptr[i];) before the CompareTo when T is large, or document that callers of large structs should provide a specialized comparator path like RunInt32. At minimum keep the specialized numeric overloads (already done) and consider adding RunInt64/RunSingle to avoid the constrained-call copy for common primitives.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.rationale: Constrained interface calls on value types are devirtualized by Burst but still copy the receiver struct; for primitive-keyed sorts the specialized overloads compile to register comparisons with no struct copy, fewer loads, and better vectorizable inner loops.
src/IAFahim.Sort.QuickSort/QuickSort.cs.risk: Adding overloads is purely additive (no behavior change). Caching ptr[i] into a local before CompareTo is semantics-preserving since ptr[i] is not mutated between the read and the compare within one do-while iteration.

src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.summary: Fuse the count and prefix-sum into a single combined-histogram pass over all 4 bytes to eliminate redundant src[i] reloads and 3 of 4 scatter-dependent reads.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.currentCost: Each of the 4 LSD passes does an independent count loop (read src[i], shift, mask, increment) AND a scatter loop (re-read src[i], shift, mask, indexed store). The byte extraction (src[i]>>shift)&0xFF is computed twice per element per pass: 2 reads of src[i] x 4 passes = 8 loads per element. Counting is also serialized with scattering.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.proposedChange: Build all 4 histograms in one initial pass: int* cnt = stackalloc int[256*4]; loop once over ptr extracting all four bytes of each value and incrementing cnt[0*256+b0], cnt[1*256+b1], etc. Then prefix-sum each 256-block and run only the 4 scatter passes. This removes the 4 separate count loops (one pass instead of four count passes) and reads each source element once for counting instead of four times.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.rationale: Reduces histogram-building memory traffic from 4 full array reads to 1, cutting total element loads from 8/elem to 5/elem (1 combined count + 4 scatter). Fewer passes over the array means fewer cache fills of the data when len exceeds L1. The combined histogram (4KB) still fits comfortably in L1.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.risk: Combined histogram is 4*256*4 = 4KB of stackalloc, slightly more stack but trivial. Semantics identical (stable LSD radix). Burst handles the larger stackalloc fine; ensure the 4 count increments per element don't create false aliasing — they target distinct 256-blocks so no hazard.

src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.summary: Skip passes whose byte is uniform (all elements share the same value in that byte position) to early-out on small-range data.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.currentCost: Always performs all 4 byte passes even when, e.g., all values fit in 16 bits (top two byte passes are no-ops that still scatter the whole array twice).
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.proposedChange: During the single combined-histogram pass, also track min/max or detect per-byte uniformity. For each byte position, if cnt[block] has a single nonzero bucket equal to len, skip that pass's scatter. Maintain the src/dst swap parity correctly (if an odd number of real passes run, do the final copy as already done in Run).
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.rationale: For common real-world data (small positive integers, counts, indices) the upper 1-2 bytes are constant, so 1-2 of the 4 scatter passes become pure no-ops. Skipping them halves the scatter traffic for such inputs at the cost of a cheap O(256) check per byte.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.risk: Must preserve final buffer parity: the existing 'if (src != ptr) copy' already handles odd pass counts, but skipping passes changes parity, so the copy-back guard must remain based on the actual final src pointer (it already is). RunWithResult lacks the copy-back, so applying skip there requires adding a final copy when src != result. Stability preserved.

src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.summary: Reuse a single count buffer across passes instead of re-stackalloc'ing inside the loop, and zero it with a tight memset-style clear.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.currentCost: int* cnt = stackalloc int[256] sits inside the shift loop. While the compiler typically hoists the allocation, the manual zero loop (256 stores) runs 4 times and is written as a scalar loop.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int* cnt = stackalloc int[256] above the shift loop (single 1KB region reused), and clear it each pass with Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned(cnt, 0, 1024) which Burst lowers to a vectorized clear, instead of the scalar for-loop.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.rationale: Guarantees one stack region rather than relying on the JIT to coalesce per-iteration stackallocs, and InitBlock is wider/branch-free vs a 256-iteration scalar store loop. Lower instruction count for the clear.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.risk: None for correctness; stackalloc inside a loop is legal but hoisting is strictly clearer and removes any chance of repeated stack-pointer adjustment. Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned requires System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe which is available under Burst; constant byte 0 fill is safe.

src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.summary: RunLong only sorts on the low 32 bits and indexes longs as ints, so it neither produces a correct sort nor a working pass structure; the intended 8-pass long radix must read 8 distinct bytes of each long.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.currentCost: Inside the loop it does ((int*)ptr)[i] which reads the low 32-bit half of long i (and for i>=1 actually re-reads halves of earlier longs because int indexing strides 4 bytes, not 8). The pointer swap at the end (t=src,tt=dst,dst=t,t=tt) is also a no-op that never updates src. Effectively the routine does 8 passes all keyed on the same low int bits and never scatters into a usable result.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.proposedChange: Operate on long* directly: extract bytes via (int)((ptr[i] >> shift) & 0xFFL) with a long* src/long* dst pair, run shift 0..56 step 8 (8 passes), swap src/dst each pass, and copy back if final src != ptr. This makes it an actual 8-pass 64-bit LSD radix with one read+one scatter per element per pass.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.rationale: Fixes the asymptotics/work: current code does wasted passes on the wrong data and an inert swap. A correct long* implementation does the minimal 8 passes with proper 8-byte striding and a single copy-back, which is both correct and the optimal pass count for 64-bit keys.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.risk: This changes observable output, but the current output is degenerate/incorrect, so this is a correctness fix rather than a behavior-preserving micro-opt; flagged because the perf structure (int-casting, inert swap) is inseparable from the bug. The shift mask must be 0xFFL (long) to avoid sign extension into the byte; (int) cast after masking to 8 bits is safe.

src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.summary: RunWithResult ping-pongs between result and temp but only writes the final sorted data into result when the pass parity lands there; with 4 passes it happens to end in result, but the contract is fragile and undocumented.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.currentCost: src starts at ptr, dst at result; after 4 swaps src==result, but there is no copy-back guard. If pass count ever changes (e.g., the skip-pass optimization or RunLong-style reuse) the result buffer would silently hold stale/half-sorted data. Also ptr is mutated as scratch on pass 1 (src=ptr write target? no — ptr is only read pass 1, then temp/result alternate), but the parity coupling is implicit.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.proposedChange: Add an explicit final guard: if (src != result) { for (int i=0;i<len;i++) result[i]=src[i]; } mirroring Run, and document that ptr is read-only. This makes the routine robust to any change in pass count and matches the Run/Try* convention.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.rationale: Robustness and consistency with Run at near-zero cost (the copy only executes when parity is wrong). Decouples correctness from the magic '4 passes is even' assumption, enabling the pass-skipping optimization without breaking output.
src/IAFahim.Sort.RadixSort/RadixSort.cs.risk: With exactly 4 passes today src==result so the guard is a no-op (zero extra cost on the current path). No semantic change for current input; purely defensive and enabling.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInt64s..summary: Insertion sort is O(n^2); for the unbounded len contract this degrades badly. A specialized integer sort (e.g. LSD radix sort on 64-bit keys, or an introsort/heapsort hybrid) gives O(n) / O(n log n) worst case.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInt64s..currentCost: O(n^2) comparisons+moves in the worst/average case. For len in the thousands this is millions of ops; the inner while is a serial dependency chain (each ptr[j+1]=ptr[j] depends on the prior), so it cannot vectorize and stalls the pipeline.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInt64s..proposedChange: Provide a threshold-dispatched Run: keep insertion sort for small len (e.g. len <= 32 or 64), and for larger len run an LSD radix sort over the 8 bytes of the long (8 passes of 256-bucket counting sort, flipping the sign bit of the top byte to handle signed ordering). Radix needs one scratch buffer of len longs; reuse a caller-provided buffer to honor the no-managed-alloc constraint (Run(long* ptr, long* scratch, int len)).
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInt64s..rationale: Radix sort is O(8n) = O(n) for 64-bit keys vs O(n^2). Counting passes are branchless and cache-friendly (sequential reads, histogram in stackalloc int[256]). Removes the long serial dependency chain of insertion sort. Keeping insertion for tiny len preserves its low constant-factor advantage where radix's 8 passes lose.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInt64s..risk: Signed ordering: must XOR the most-significant byte with 0x80 (flip sign bit) so two's-complement negatives sort before positives; do it only on the top-byte pass and reverse on read, or pre/post transform. Stability differs from insertion sort but sort is not documented as stable for scalars. Requires an API change to take scratch (or stackalloc only when len is small) — flag as additive overload, not a silent break.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.summary: Same O(n^2) insertion sort on int keys; a 4-pass LSD radix sort sorts 32-bit ints in O(n) and dominates for non-tiny len.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.currentCost: O(n^2) average/worst, serial move chain that defeats Burst vectorization and stresses the store-forwarding pipeline.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.proposedChange: Threshold dispatch: insertion sort for small len, else 4-pass LSD radix (256-bucket counting sort per byte) with sign-bit flip on the high byte for signed correctness, using a caller-supplied scratch buffer.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.rationale: 4*n vs n^2. Histograms live in stackalloc int[256] (1 KiB, fits L1). Sequential scatter/gather is cache-predictable. Branchless counting passes Burst-vectorizes far better than the data-dependent insertion inner loop.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.risk: Signed key handling via top-byte XOR 0x80000000 as above. Additive overload to pass scratch; do not break existing unchecked Run signature. Stability not currently guaranteed so reordering equal keys is acceptable.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.summary: Inner loop does two index computations (ptr[j+1], ptr[j]) per iteration; walk with two running pointers/indices to cut address arithmetic and shorten the move-store dependency.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.currentCost: Each inner iteration recomputes ptr+j and ptr+j+1 and re-reads ptr[j]; the compiler usually folds this but it is not guaranteed under Burst with aliasing assumptions.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.proposedChange: Hoist key's insertion as a memmove-style shift: cache the value being shifted in a register pattern, or restructure to `long t = ptr[j]; ptr[j+1] = t;` reusing the load. Minor; main win is the algorithmic change above.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.rationale: Removes a redundant load of ptr[j] (it is loaded once for the compare and could be reused for the store), trimming one memory op per inner iteration.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortInts.cs.risk: Pure micro-opt, semantics-identical. Low impact because Burst/LLVM likely already CSEs the load; only worth doing if profiling the IR shows the redundant load survives.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.summary: O(n^2) insertion sort over 8-byte Pair structs; each shift moves the whole 8-byte struct. Radix sort on the Key with a parallel value array, or sorting an index, gives O(n) and moves less data.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.currentCost: O(n^2) struct moves; each ptr[j+1]=ptr[j] copies 8 bytes (Key+Value). Doubles the memory traffic of a key-only sort and keeps the serial dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.proposedChange: For non-tiny len, LSD radix sort by Key (4 passes) writing whole Pair entries into a scratch Pair buffer; sign-flip the top byte of Key for signed correctness. Alternatively radix-sort an int[] permutation of indices to avoid moving the 8-byte payload during intermediate passes, applying the permutation once at the end.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.rationale: O(4n) vs O(n^2). The index-permutation variant moves only 4-byte indices during the 4 passes and writes the final 8-byte payload exactly once, halving payload memory traffic versus shuffling Pairs every pass.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.risk: Signed Key ordering via top-byte XOR 0x80000000. Radix is not stable across the chosen byte order unless implemented LSD (it is) so equal Keys retain input order — actually LSD radix IS stable, which insertion sort also is on Key, so behavior is preserved for ties (good). Needs scratch buffer: additive overload, do not break unchecked Run.

src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.summary: Pair is implicitly auto-layout; add [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] (and it is already naturally 8-byte aligned/blittable) to lock layout for interop and Burst SoA reasoning.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.currentCost: Default struct layout is sequential for blittable structs in practice, but unannotated layout can theoretically be reordered and is less self-documenting for a type passed via raw pointers.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.proposedChange: Annotate `[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] public struct Pair`. No size change (two ints = 8 bytes, no padding).
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.rationale: Guarantees Key-then-Value byte order so callers can blit/upload buffers and so radix passes can index the Key field by known offset. Documents blittability for Burst.
src/IAFahim.Sort.Specialized/SortPairs.c.risk: None semantically; layout is already what callers expect. Purely a hardening/clarity change.

src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.summary: Remove the dead tempNext allocation that is allocated and freed but never read or written.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.currentCost: One Marshal.AllocHGlobal of maxDfaStates*4 bytes (up to ~8GB when nfaStates approaches 31) plus a FreeHGlobal, with zero uses. Pure wasted heap traffic, page commits, and two syscalls per call.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.proposedChange: Delete the tempNext allocation (line 38), its tempBytes computation (line 36), and the corresponding FreeHGlobal in the finally block (line 103). tempNext is never referenced anywhere in the body.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.rationale: Eliminates a large, fully unused allocation/free pair. Fewer cycles (two fewer P/Invoke transitions), and for large nfaStates it halves committed scratch memory, reducing the chance of an allocation failure / OOM on mobile.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.risk: None. Static analysis shows tempNext has no reads or writes; removing it is behavior-preserving.

src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.summary: Fuse the BFS discovery pass and the transition-table rebuild pass; the subset-transition bitmask for every reachable state is computed twice identically.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.currentCost: The O(maxDfaStates * sigma * nfaStates) inner triple loop is executed twice: once during BFS (lines 51-65) to discover states, and again in the rebuild loop (lines 76-98). For reachable states this is fully redundant work, doubling the dominant cost. The rebuild loop also scans ALL maxDfaStates masks (including unreachable ones, skipped via stateMap[mask]==-1) instead of only the reachable subsets already enqueued.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.proposedChange: During BFS, store each computed transition target 'next' directly into dfa->Transitions[stateMap[subset]][c] = (will be patched) and remember the raw next-mask, OR keep a parallel per-(state,c) next-mask buffer produced in the BFS so the rebuild loop only maps masks to ids via stateMap[next] without recomputing the OR-reduction. Also iterate only over the 'queue' of reachable subsets (head 0..stateCount) rather than 0..maxDfaStates, eliminating the stateMap[mask]==-1 scan over up to 2^nfaStates entries.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.rationale: Removes a full duplicate of the asymptotically dominant computation and removes a sweep over up to 2^nfaStates unreachable masks. For automata with sparse reachable subsets (the common case) this changes the rebuild from O(2^n * sigma * n) to O(reachable * sigma * n), a potentially exponential reduction, plus a 2x constant-factor win on the rest.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.risk: Must preserve identical Transitions and IsAccept contents. Storing the raw next-masks needs a buffer of stateCount*sigma ints; tempNext (after repurposing) could hold per-state next ids. Accept flags must still be computed per reachable subset. Ordering of stateMap assignment must remain so ids match the original BFS numbering.

src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.summary: Iterate only set bits of the subset using bit-tricks instead of scanning all nfaStates bits.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.currentCost: Inner loop 'for s in 0..nfaStates' tests (subset & (1<<s)) for every bit, so cost is O(nfaStates) per (subset,c) regardless of population count. Most subsets have far fewer set bits than nfaStates.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.proposedChange: Replace the per-bit scan with a popcount-driven loop: for (int m = subset; m != 0; m &= m - 1) { int s = TrailingZeroCount(m); if (nfaTrans[s][c] >= 0) next |= 1 << nfaTrans[s][c]; }. Burst lowers tzcnt/blsr to single instructions (math.tzcnt / Bmi1).
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.rationale: Cost drops from O(nfaStates) to O(popcount(subset)) per (subset,c), and removes the per-bit branch on the mask test, shortening the dependency chain to one blsr + tzcnt per active state.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.risk: Hoist this transition computation into a shared helper so the BFS and rebuild passes (or the fused pass) stay identical. 1<<nfaTrans[s][c] requires nfaTrans[s][c] < 32, which the existing 1<<s scheme already assumes. Semantics-identical for valid NFAs with <32 states.

src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.summary: Hoist the 1<<s and nfaTrans[s] row pointer out of the alphabet loop, or swap loop nesting so the NFA row is loaded once per state.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.currentCost: In both inner passes, for each (c,s) the code recomputes (1<<s) and dereferences nfaTrans[s][c] through two pointer indirections, with the s-loop nested inside the c-loop so nfaTrans[s] is re-fetched sigma times per state.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.proposedChange: Cache int* row = nfaTrans[s] once per s, and precompute bit = 1<<s. If the transition OR is restructured per-state (loop s outer, accumulate into a small per-c next array of size sigma in registers/stack), nfaTrans[s] is dereferenced once per state instead of once per (state,c).
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.rationale: Removes redundant outer-pointer loads (nfaTrans[s]) and shift recomputation; improves spatial locality by reading each NFA transition row contiguously across c.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/FiniteAutoma.risk: Restructuring needs a sigma-sized scratch for the per-c next masks; with sigma typically small (e.g. 26 or 256) this fits in stackalloc. Behavior identical as long as all c are accumulated before mapping.

src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.summary: Replace the modulo in the hot DP accumulation with a branchless/conditional subtraction since operands are already reduced.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.currentCost: dp[nxt] = (dp[nxt] + dp[i]) % MOD runs inside the O(len*sigma) inner loop, performing a 64-bit integer division (high-latency, ~20-90 cycles, not vectorizable) on every transition.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.proposedChange: Maintain the invariant 0 <= dp[k] < MOD. Then dp[nxt]+dp[i] < 2*MOD, so replace % with: long v = dp[nxt] + dp[i]; dp[nxt] = v >= MOD ? v - MOD : v; (or branchless: v - (MOD & -(long)(v >= MOD))). Apply the same to the final 'total' accumulation loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.rationale: Eliminates a 64-bit div per inner-loop iteration, replacing it with an add + compare + conditional subtract that Burst can render branchless. Massive constant-factor win on the dominant loop since dp values are provably < MOD by construction.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.risk: Correctness depends on MOD <= 2^62 so that dp[nxt]+dp[i] does not overflow long (true for typical MODs like 1e9+7). If MOD could exceed 2^62 the add could overflow; guard by documenting MOD < 2^62. Otherwise exactly equal to the % result because both operands are in [0,MOD).

src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.summary: Drop the explicit dp zeroing loop; stackalloc memory can be cleared more cheaply or fused.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.currentCost: A separate for-loop writes dp[0..len]=0 before the algorithm, a full pass over len+1 longs distinct from the compute loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.proposedChange: Use 'long* dp = stackalloc long[len + 1]; ' with an initializer-free clear via Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned / a single memset-style fill, or rely on the fact only dp[0] needs a known value if you restructure to read-before-write. Set dp[0]=1 then clear dp[1..len] in one InitBlock.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.rationale: Replaces an element-by-element store loop with a single bulk clear that Burst/JIT lowers to vectorized stores, reducing instruction count and improving the clear's memory bandwidth utilization.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.risk: Must still guarantee dp[1..len] are zero before accumulation. InitBlock over the tail is equivalent. Low impact since it is an O(len) pass dwarfed by the O(len*sigma) main loop.

src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.summary: Hoist patLen==0 handling / guard and cache the sigma stride; minor but the state*sigma multiply repeats each iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.currentCost: Each iteration computes next[state * sigma + pattern[i]], a multiply by sigma plus add per step. The first access uses 0*sigma which is dead arithmetic.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.proposedChange: Drop the 0*sigma (use next[pattern[0]]). The state*sigma multiply is inherent to the row-major layout, but it could be strength-reduced if sigma is a known power of two via shift; otherwise leave as-is. The dead 0 multiply removal is free.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.rationale: Removes one constant-folding-resistant multiply-by-zero expression and clarifies intent. If callers always pass a power-of-two sigma (e.g. 256 for byte alphabet), a sigma-as-shift overload would turn the per-step multiply into a shift.
src/IAFahim.String.Automata/SubsequenceA.risk: 0*sigma is already folded by any optimizer, so this is cosmetic unless a power-of-two-stride specialization is added. No semantic change. patLen>=1 is assumed by Run convention (pattern[0] dereferenced unconditionally).

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant `precision / BaseTwo` (and `precision / AlphabetSize`-style divisors) out of the hot per-symbol and per-bit renormalization loops.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.currentCost: `precision / BaseTwo` is recomputed on every iteration of the inner `while(true)` renormalization loop (lines 31,37,40,41 in Encode; 94,105,107,114 in Decode). That is a 64-bit integer divide (tens of cycles, not pipelined) executed potentially many times per symbol, even though `precision` never changes.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.proposedChange: Compute `long half = precision >> 1;` (precision is the bound `1L<<K`, a power of two by construction, so >>1 is exact) once before the outer loop, and reference `half` everywhere `precision / BaseTwo` appears. Likewise `range / AlphabetSize` can become `range >> 8` since AlphabetSize==256 is a power of two and `range = hi-lo >= 0`.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.rationale: Replaces a long divide (~20-40 cycles, serializing) on the critical dependency chain with a precomputed value / single shift (1 cycle). The renorm loop is the innermost hot path, so this is a large constant-factor win and shortens the lo/hi dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.risk: `range >> 8` is only valid because range is non-negative (hi>=lo) and 256 is a power of two; for non-negative operands `x/256 == x>>8` exactly. `precision>>1` is exact because precision is set to a value `>= 1L<<K`; if a caller passes a non-power-of-two precision, `precision/2` floor-division differs from `precision>>1` only for odd precision — guard by documenting/asserting precision is even (it is, since it equals `1L<<K` whenever used as the renorm midpoint). If callers may pass odd precision, keep `(precision >> 1)` still equals floor division for even and for the `1L<<K` contract holds.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.summary: Replace the `while ((1L << K) < precision) K++;` linear bit-count loop with a leading-zero / Log2 intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.currentCost: Up to ~63 iterations of a branch + shift to compute K = ceil(log2(precision)). Done once per call, so minor, but it is pure scalar serial work.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.proposedChange: Use `int K = 64 - System.Numerics.BitOperations.LeadingZeroCount((ulong)(precision - 1));` (Burst lowers LeadingZeroCount to lzcnt/clz). For exact power-of-two precision this yields the same K the loop produces.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.rationale: Single CPU instruction vs a 63-iteration dependency-carried loop; Burst-friendly intrinsic.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Arithmetic.c.risk: Off-by-one on the ceil-vs-floor boundary: the loop computes the smallest K with `(1L<<K) >= precision`. `64 - lzcnt(precision-1)` gives exactly that for precision>=1. Validate the precision==1 / precision power-of-two edge before adopting; keep the loop if precision can be 0.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.summary: `Huffman.Decode` is an empty stub: it fills `buffer` from input but never emits any output byte, never advances `opos`, and never writes `*outLen`.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.currentCost: The method consumes input into `buffer`/`bits` in the inner while but has no bit-to-symbol decoding, no output writes, and the outer `while` condition `opos < *outLen` never changes so it loops on the inner refill then exits with zero work. Observable behavior: produces no output. This is a correctness gap, not just perf.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.proposedChange: Implement actual canonical/tree-walk decoding (walk the Huffman tree or a decode LUT bit by bit, emitting `output[opos++]` until `opos == *outLen`), and set `*outLen = opos`. Until implemented, no perf optimization is meaningful here.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.rationale: A no-op decoder makes the encoder output unusable; any downstream perf tuning is moot. Flagging because the task is to find concrete issues in these files.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.risk: Implementing decode changes behavior from 'produces nothing' to 'produces correct output' — intended. Must mirror Encode's MSB-first bit packing (`buffer << code.Length | bits`, flush `buffer >> (bits-32)`).

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.summary: Remove `[MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]` from `Build`; it is a large method with stackalloc, a heap-allocating struct, try/finally, and a recursive call — inlining is harmful, not helpful.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.currentCost: AggressiveInlining on a big method bloats every call site's I-cache footprint and the `stackalloc Node[2*sigma]` + Marshal.AllocHGlobal make it un-inlinable in practice anyway, so the attribute is at best ignored and at worst forces I-cache pressure if honored.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.proposedChange: Drop the attribute on `Build`. Reserve AggressiveInlining for the small hot leaf methods (`Push`, `Pop` already aren't attributed — those are the real inline candidates).
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.rationale: Inlining hints belong on small hot leaves; on cold setup methods they only cost code size. Build is called once per frequency table, not in a hot loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.risk: None — purely a hint removal; cannot change semantics.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.summary: Convert recursive `Traverse` to an explicit stackalloc'd stack (iterative) to bound stack usage and avoid recursion in Burst.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.currentCost: Recursion depth equals the Huffman tree height (up to sigma-1 in the degenerate skewed-frequency case), each frame carrying Node*/length/bits/codes — unbounded native stack growth and a hidden call/return dependency chain. Burst is unfriendly to recursion.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.proposedChange: Use an explicit `int* stackId = stackalloc int[2*sigma]` plus parallel length/bits arrays (or pack into a small struct) and iterate. Tree has at most 2*sigma nodes so the bound is known.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.rationale: Removes call overhead and unbounded native-stack risk; makes the function a straight-line loop Burst can compile without recursion. Same traversal order/output.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.risk: Must preserve left-before-right ordering so emitted codes match (left = bits<<1, right = (bits<<1)|1). Push right then left if using a LIFO to keep left processed first.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.summary: Strength-reduce heap index math `(idx-1)/2`, `idx*2+1`, `idx*2+2` to shifts.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.currentCost: `(idx-1)/2` is a signed divide (idx>=1 in that branch so non-negative) and `idx*2+1`/`idx*2+2` are mul-by-2; the signed `/2` emits extra sign-correction instructions versus a shift.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.proposedChange: Parent: `int p = (idx - 1) >> 1;` (idx>0 guaranteed by the while, so idx-1>=0, shift == divide). Children: `int left = (idx << 1) + 1; int right = left + 1;` (saves recomputing idx*2).
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.rationale: Avoids the signed-division sign-fixup sequence and one redundant multiply; tiny but on the sift loop's critical path.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Huffman.cs.risk: `>>1` equals `/2` only for non-negative dividend — guaranteed here since idx>0 in Push's loop. AggressiveInlining-add these tiny leaves to encourage inlining.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.summary: Replace the O(n * window * matchLen) brute-force window scan with a hash-chain (or 3-byte rolling-hash bucket) match finder to get near-O(n) average behavior.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.currentCost: For every position i, it rescans all up to `windowSize` prior positions and re-extends each match byte-by-byte: worst/typical cost is O(n · windowSize · avgMatchLen). On highly repetitive input this is quadratic-ish and dominates runtime.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.proposedChange: Maintain a hash table keyed on the next 3 (or 4) bytes mapping to a chain of recent positions; at each i, only probe positions in that chain (bounded by a max-chain constant), extending matches from there. All buffers are stackalloc/native — fits house constraints.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.rationale: Standard LZ77 acceleration: cuts candidate positions from O(window) to O(chain-length constant), turning the encoder from quadratic to near-linear on real data — the single biggest win in this module.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.risk: Greedy match selection can differ from the exhaustive 'longest of all window positions' if chain depth is capped, changing which equally/less-optimal token is chosen — output stays a valid LZ77 stream and decodes identically, but the exact tokenization may differ from the brute-force version. If bit-exact output is a contract, cap-chain must be unbounded (still faster via hashing) to preserve 'first longest' selection.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.summary: Branchless window start and early-out when a match already reaches the 255 cap; also hoist `len`/`input` and lift the `l>255` cap test.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.currentCost: `Math.Max(0, i - windowSize)` is a call/branch per outer iteration. The inner match loop re-checks `l > 255` every byte. When `bestLen` already equals 255 (max), the outer loop keeps scanning remaining window positions pointlessly.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int start = i - windowSize; if (start < 0) start = 0;` (or `start = (i - windowSize) & ~((i - windowSize) >> 31)` branchless). Add `if (bestLen == 255) break;` after updating bestLen to stop scanning once the cap is hit. Bound the inner loop with `int maxL = (len - i) < 256 ? len - i : 256;` so the per-byte `if (l>255) break;` disappears.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.rationale: Removes a per-byte branch from the innermost loop, removes a per-position call, and prunes the candidate scan once the maximum encodable length is found — fewer comparisons on the hottest loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.risk: Early-out on bestLen==255 changes which position wins ties only among matches all of length 255 (Offset differs); if exact bestPos tie-breaking is a contract this alters output. The original keeps the first j giving 255 too (since `l > bestLen` is strict), so breaking on first 255 preserves the same bestPos — behavior-preserving.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.summary: Shrink the Token struct: Length is capped at 255 (fits byte) and Literal is already byte; pack to reduce per-token footprint and improve cache density of the output stream.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.currentCost: Token is two `int` (8 bytes) + `byte` + 3 padding = 12 bytes. Length never exceeds 255 by the encoder's own cap, so 4 bytes of it are wasted; Offset is bounded by windowSize.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.proposedChange: If windowSize <= 65535, use `ushort Offset; byte Length; byte Literal` (4 bytes) — a 3x reduction. Otherwise keep Offset int but make `Length` a byte. Decode reads the same fields.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.rationale: Smaller tokens mean the Decode pass (and any serialization) touches 3x fewer cache lines; the token array is the primary output working set.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.risk: Narrowing Offset to ushort breaks if windowSize>65535; gate on a const or keep int Offset + byte Length (still 8->? saves padding). Changes the public struct layout — an API/ABI change for callers reading Token fields, so it is a breaking change to weigh against the ergonomic contract.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.summary: The byte-by-byte copy loop for matches can be widened, and when Offset >= Length the run is non-overlapping and can use a bulk memmove/word copy.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.currentCost: `for j in [0,Length): output[pos+j] = output[pos-Offset+j]` copies one byte per iteration with a load-store dependency, even when source and dest don't overlap (Offset >= Length), where a vectorized/word copy is legal.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.proposedChange: When `input[i].Offset >= input[i].Length`, copy via `Buffer.MemoryCopy(output+pos-Offset, output+pos, Length, Length)` or an 8-byte-at-a-time loop. Keep the byte loop only for the overlapping (Offset < Length) RLE case. Hoist `input[i]` into a local Token to avoid re-deref of the struct fields each iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.rationale: Removes the per-byte dependency chain for the common non-overlapping case, letting Burst emit wide loads/stores; loading the Token once avoids repeated pointer arithmetic into the input array.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz77.cs.risk: Overlapping copies (Offset < Length, i.e. RLE-style self-reference) MUST stay byte-sequential — memmove semantics would corrupt them, so the `Offset >= Length` guard is mandatory. With the guard, output is identical.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.summary: Encode is O(outCount^2 · phraseLen) due to walking the phrase chain for every dictionary entry at every position, with repeated GetByte chain re-walks; replace with a trie-based dictionary.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.currentCost: For each position it loops over all `outCount` phrases (line 23); for each it walks the parent chain to compute pLen (lines 28-32), then for each byte calls `GetByte` (line 36) which itself re-walks the chain from scratch up to 256 deep with a fresh stackalloc[256]. This is roughly O(outCount · phraseLen^2) per position — cubic-ish overall.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.proposedChange: Maintain an explicit LZ78 trie (children keyed by byte) in stackalloc native arrays: at each position, descend the trie matching input bytes in O(matchLen) and emit the (phrase, literal) at the first miss. This is the textbook LZ78 encoder.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.rationale: Reduces per-position work from O(outCount · phraseLen^2) to O(matchLen), turning a cubic algorithm into linear. By far the dominant cost in this file.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.risk: LZ78 dictionary construction order must match so phrase indices are identical; a correct trie reproduces the same phrase numbering and thus the same token stream — behavior-preserving when implemented faithfully. The current `GetByte` stackalloc[256] inside a double loop also means a fresh 1KB stackalloc per inner iteration (see separate item).

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.summary: `GetByte` does a `stackalloc int[256]` on every single call, and it is called inside the Encode double loop's inner byte loop — enormous redundant stack traffic and repeated chain re-walks.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.currentCost: Each GetByte call allocates 256 ints (1 KiB) of stack and re-walks the phrase chain from the leaf to compute the byte at a given offset. It is invoked per (phrase, k) inside the per-position loop, so the same chain is rebuilt O(phraseLen) times per phrase per position.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.proposedChange: Eliminate GetByte entirely by adopting the trie (previous item), which yields bytes directly during descent. If keeping the chain approach short-term, hoist one scratch buffer outside the loops and pass it in, and reverse-index without re-walking (precompute the phrase's byte sequence once per phrase candidate).
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.rationale: Removes repeated 1 KiB stackallocs (stack pointer churn, no reuse) and O(phraseLen) re-walks per byte access, collapsing redundant work.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.risk: Behavior identical: GetByte returns the byte at `chainLen-1-offset` (0 if out of range); the trie/precompute must reproduce the same out-of-range->0 semantics. stackalloc inside a method called in a loop is allocated once per call (not leaked) but still wasteful.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.summary: `stackalloc int[count]` is performed inside the per-token loop and uses int (4 bytes) to store byte values; hoist it out and narrow to byte.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.currentCost: Line 64 allocates `int[count]` on every iteration where idx>=0 — O(count) stack per token, and the chain holds only byte literals yet stores them as 4-byte ints (4x the needed RAM, worse cache use).
