src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.proposedChange: Hoist a single `byte* chain = stackalloc byte[maxPhraseLen]` (or `byte[count]`) before the loop and reuse it across tokens; store `input[cur].Literal` directly as byte. Bound the size by the max possible phrase length rather than `count` if known.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.rationale: One stackalloc instead of per-token; 4x smaller scratch (byte vs int) improves cache footprint and reduces stack pointer adjustment in the hot decode loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/Lz78.cs.risk: Reused buffer is fully overwritten each token (chainLen reset), so no cross-token contamination — behavior preserved. `(byte)chain[j]` cast already implies byte values; narrowing the storage type is safe since literals are bytes.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.summary: Brute-force O(n^2 · matchLen) longest-previous-factor search; replace with a suffix-automaton / suffix-array LPF or hash-chain to reach near-linear LZ factorization.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.currentCost: For each i it scans all j<i (line 24) and extends byte-by-byte (line 27), giving O(n^2 · avgMatchLen) — the classic quadratic LZ factorization. Dominant cost.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.proposedChange: Compute the LZ factorization via a suffix automaton or the LPF array from a suffix array + LCP (Crochemore/Ilie), or a bounded hash-chain match finder, all expressible with native stackalloc arrays.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.rationale: Drops the asymptotic from quadratic to O(n) or O(n log n), the single largest improvement for this routine on non-trivial inputs.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.risk: The current code selects the longest match and ties break to the smallest j (first found, strict `>`). An LPF/automaton must reproduce the same length and the same chosen position to keep output bit-identical; if only length-equivalence is required (any valid factor of max length), the constraint relaxes. State which contract holds before swapping.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.summary: Hoist invariant bound and remove redundant per-byte comparison in the inner extend loop; remove misleading AggressiveInlining on this large method.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.currentCost: Inner loop tests `i + l < len && j + l < i` each byte; `len` and the `j < i` cap are loop-invariant-derivable into a single `maxL = min(len - i, i - j)` bound, halving the per-byte comparisons. Also `[MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)]` on this large method only bloats I-cache.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.proposedChange: Precompute `int maxL = (len - i) < (i - j) ? (len - i) : (i - j); int l = 0; while (l < maxL && input[j+l] == input[i+l]) l++;` and drop the AggressiveInlining attribute.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.rationale: One bound compare per byte instead of two, with the bound branchless-min'd once per j; fewer instructions on the hottest loop. Attribute removal avoids needless code-size growth.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/LzFactorizat.risk: min(len-i, i-j) exactly reproduces the original two-condition termination, so output unchanged. AggressiveInlining removal is a hint-only change.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..summary: Replace Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal scratch list with stackalloc; the P/Invoke heap calls defeat Burst and add per-call overhead
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..currentCost: Two managed P/Invoke transitions (AllocHGlobal + FreeHGlobal) per call. These are managed-runtime calls that Burst cannot compile, forcing the whole method onto the non-Burst path. Also a heap allocation + free on every invocation (latency, fragmentation, no caller pooling).
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..proposedChange: Since `list` holds values `(byte)i` for i in [0,sigma) and is indexed by byte symbols, sigma is provably <= 256. Use `byte* list = stackalloc byte[256];` (or stackalloc byte[sigma] if Burst allows variable-length; fixed 256 is safest/blittable) and drop both Marshal calls. The list never escapes the function.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..rationale: stackalloc is a single stack-pointer bump (effectively free) versus a heap alloc/free pair, and it keeps the method Burst-compilable and branch/exception-free. 256 bytes on the stack is trivial and fully within one cache line set, improving locality vs. a fresh heap block.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..risk: sigma must be <= 256 (guaranteed: list values are byte and inputs index it as byte, so any sigma>256 is already semantically broken/truncating in current code). Using a fixed 256 wastes a few bytes when sigma is smaller but is fully safe and avoids variable-length-stackalloc concerns under Burst.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..summary: Replace the byte-at-a-time backward shift loop with a single overlapping memmove (Buffer.MemoryCopy)
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..currentCost: `for (int j = pos; j > 0; j--) list[j] = list[j-1];` is `pos` dependent load/store iterations with a per-byte loop branch and a serial dependency chain; for large alphabets and high positions this dominates.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..proposedChange: Shift `list[0..pos-1]` up by one with a single overlapping move: `Buffer.MemoryCopy(list, list + 1, sigma - 1, pos);` then `list[0] = symbol;`. (Direction is high-to-low / non-overlapping-destructive but MemoryCopy handles overlap correctly for dst>src copying low->... use the overlap-safe move semantics.)
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..rationale: Collapses `pos` scalar iterations into one bulk move the JIT/Burst can vectorize, removing the per-element loop branch and shortening the dependency chain. For typical MTF where recently-used symbols cluster near front pos is small, but the worst case (cold symbols, pos~sigma) becomes a single SIMD-friendly copy.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..risk: Buffer.MemoryCopy is a managed BCL method and may not be Burst-intrinsic; under Burst prefer UnsafeUtility.MemMove. Overlap direction must be handled (dst = src+1 overlapping forward); use a guaranteed overlap-safe memmove, not memcpy. If neither memmove intrinsic is available under Burst, keep the scalar loop. Net: only apply if an overlap-safe, Burst-friendly move primitive exists in the project.

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..summary: Inconsistent AggressiveInlining: Encode is marked, Decode is not, and neither is a hot leaf
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..currentCost: Encode carries [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] but is a multi-loop, allocation-bearing method — inlining it bloats the caller with no benefit and is asymmetric with Decode which has no attribute. Inconsistent API surface.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..proposedChange: Either remove AggressiveInlining from Encode (it is not a small leaf), or add it to Decode for symmetry. Recommended: remove from both; let the compiler decide for these larger routines.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..rationale: Inlining large bodies increases instruction-cache pressure at every call site without speeding the inner loops (the cost is in the O(len*sigma) loops, not call overhead). Consistency aids discoverability and avoids surprising codegen.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..risk: None semantically; purely codegen-size/consistency. Verify no caller relies on inlining for a measured win (unlikely given the body size).

src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..summary: List-initialization loop is loop-invariant per call and the linear search rescans from 0 each symbol; both are inherent O(sigma) but the init can use a fill primitive
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..currentCost: `for (i=0;i<sigma;i++) list[i]=(byte)i;` is a scalar identity fill each call. The encode search `while (list[pos]!=input[i]) pos++;` is an unavoidable O(pos) probe but the cast `(byte)pos` and reload of input[i] in the shift epilogue are minor redundancies.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..proposedChange: Hoist `byte sym = input[i];` once per outer iteration and reuse it for the compare, output, and `list[0]=sym` (avoids reloading input[i] after pointer-aliasing the compiler may not prove non-aliased with output). The identity-fill is fundamental; leave as-is or keep scalar (Burst vectorizes the simple `(byte)i` pattern poorly anyway).
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..rationale: Caching `input[i]` in a local removes a potential reload that the compiler cannot elide because `output` and `input` are unrelated pointers it must assume may alias `list` writes; the local breaks that conservative reload.
src/IAFahim.String.Compress/MoveToFront..risk: None — `input[i]` does not change within the iteration (input and list/output are distinct buffers by contract). Purely removes a redundant load.

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.summary: Replace per-iteration modulo with a branch/conditional-subtract to avoid an integer division in the hot loop.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.currentCost: `text[(sa[i] - 1 + len) % len]` executes one integer % (a multi-cycle hardware divide, ~20-40 cycles on mobile ARM) per element, len times.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.proposedChange: Since sa[i] is in [0,len) and len>=1, (sa[i]-1+len) is in [len-1, 2*len-2), so the modulo result is either sa[i]-1 (when sa[i]>=1) or len-1 (when sa[i]==0). Replace with: `int p = sa[i]; bwt[i] = text[p != 0 ? p - 1 : len - 1];` or branchless `int p = sa[i] - 1; bwt[i] = text[p + (len & (p >> 31))];` (p>>31 is -1 when p<0 i.e. sa[i]==0, masking len; 0 otherwise).
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.rationale: Eliminates the divide entirely, replacing it with a compare+select or a shift+and+add. Divides are the most expensive integer op and block the pipeline; the branchless form is fully data-parallel and Burst can vectorize the gather. Net ~20-40 cycles saved per element.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.risk: Branchless form relies on signed arithmetic shift (sa[i]-1 only ever -1 at minimum, so p>>31 is safe). Semantics identical for all valid sa in [0,len). No overflow since len fits in int and sa[i]<len.

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.summary: The LF[] scratch buffer is unnecessary; the text can be reconstructed in a single backward pass using count[] directly, removing one len-sized buffer from the working set.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.currentCost: Two len-length passes plus a separate len-sized LF[] buffer (4*len bytes) that is written in one loop and read in another, doubling memory traffic over bwt and adding a cache-resident array.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.proposedChange: Drop the LF parameter and the LF-building loop. In the final loop, compute the next position inline: `for (int i = len - 1; i >= 0; i--){ int b = bwt[pos]; text[i] = b; pos = count[b]++; }`. This fuses the LF computation into the reconstruction walk. (count[] must hold cumulative starts at this point, which it already does after the prefix-sum.)
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.rationale: Removes a 4*len-byte allocation and an entire len-length read/write pass, halving memory traffic in this phase and shrinking the cache footprint. Fewer passes = fewer cache misses on large len.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.risk: Changes the public method signature (drops LF*), an API/ergonomics break — callers must be updated. Behavior is identical: count[b]++ during the walk reproduces exactly the LF values that the separate loop precomputed, since the walk visits positions in the same relative order the prefix counts assume. If the LF param must stay for ABI reasons, reject; otherwise this is strictly better.

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.summary: maxChar is hardcoded to 256 and zeroed/prefix-summed every call regardless of the actual alphabet; accept a sigma parameter to bound these O(256) loops to the real alphabet size.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.currentCost: Two fixed 256-iteration loops (zeroing count[] and prefix-sum) run unconditionally even when the text uses a small alphabet (e.g. DNA sigma=4), wasting ~512 iterations and touching 1KB of count[] memory per call.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.proposedChange: Add an `int sigma` parameter and use it in place of the literal 256 for the zero-init and prefix-sum loops: `for (int c = 0; c < sigma; c++)`. Keep 256 as a named default constant if a no-sigma overload is desired.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.rationale: For small alphabets this turns two 256-iteration loops into sigma-iteration loops, cutting fixed overhead and the count[] cache footprint. For sigma=256 it is identical.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/Bwt.cs.risk: API change (adds parameter). Caller must pass sigma >= max(bwt[i])+1 or results are wrong; document as unchecked-Run contract. The count loop `count[bwt[i]]++` already assumes bwt values < sigma.

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.summary: The occ table is stored column-major (stride len+1 per symbol) and rebuilt with an inner per-symbol copy loop, making Build O(len*sigma) with cache-hostile strided writes; switch to row-major prefix layout so each step writes one contiguous row.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.currentCost: Inner loop `for c in sigma: occ[c*(len+1)+i+1] = occ[c*(len+1)+i]` does sigma strided loads+stores per text position (O(len*sigma) total). Each access jumps len+1 ints, so every symbol's column is a separate cache line — sigma cache misses per position.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.proposedChange: Store occ row-major: occ[i*sigma + c] = number of occurrences of c in text[0..i). Then per position copy the previous row contiguously and bump one counter: `int* prev = occ + i*sigma; int* cur = occ + (i+1)*sigma; for(int c=0;c<sigma;c++) cur[c]=prev[c]; cur[text[i]]++;`. The contiguous sigma-int copy is vectorizable by Burst (memcpy-like) versus sigma strided scalar stores. Adjust all occ readers (rank queries) to the new index formula c -> i*sigma+c.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.rationale: Same asymptotic O(len*sigma) work but turns sigma cache-line-straddling stores into one contiguous, Burst-vectorizable row copy, drastically cutting cache misses and enabling SIMD. The recomputed stride `c*(len+1)` (a multiply per inner iter) is also eliminated.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.risk: Changes the occ memory layout, so every consumer of occ must use the new indexing. occ is currently unused by Count/Locate in this file (they use SA), so the blast radius is external rank-query code; coordinate the layout change everywhere. Behavior of stored counts is identical, only layout changes.

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.summary: If the column-major layout must be kept, at least hoist the c*(len+1) stride multiply and the +i+1 base out of the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.currentCost: Inner loop recomputes `c*(len+1)` (an imul) and `+ i + 1` / `+ i` address arithmetic every iteration of the sigma loop.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.proposedChange: Precompute `int stride = len + 1;` once. Maintain a running base per column or, simpler, iterate `int* col = occ + i; int* coln = occ + i + 1; for(int c=0;c<sigma;c++){ coln[c*stride] = col[c*stride]; }` so the loop-invariant `len+1` is a register and only one multiply by c remains; or accumulate `base += stride` to make it an add instead of a multiply: `int idx = i; for(int c=0;c<sigma;c++){ occ[idx+1]=occ[idx]; idx += stride; }`.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.rationale: Replaces a per-iteration multiply with a single add (strength reduction) and keeps len+1 in a register. Cheaper than the current code even without changing layout.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.risk: None semantically; pure address-arithmetic refactor. Only worth doing if the row-major rewrite is rejected (that one is strictly better).

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.summary: Locate recomputes both binary-search bounds via two full FindBound calls; the second search can be narrowed using the first result and the comparison work is duplicated.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.currentCost: Two FindBound calls, each O(log len * patLen) comparisons over the whole [0,len) range. The lower-bound and upper-bound searches independently re-compare the same suffixes near the boundary.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.proposedChange: Seed the upper-bound search with the lower bound: `int start = FindBound(...,true); int end = FindBoundFrom(text,len,pattern,patLen,sa,start,len);` where FindBoundFrom takes an initial l=start (all positions < start already compare < pattern, so cmp>0 cannot occur below start). This shrinks the second search range from len to len-start.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.rationale: The upper bound is always >= the lower bound, so the lower-half of the second binary search is provably useless. Narrowing l to start removes up to log2(start) comparison rounds, each costing up to patLen integer compares.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.risk: Correct only because for any mid<start, CompareWithSa returns cmp<=0 in the lower sense already established; passing l=start preserves the invariant since end>=start. No semantic change to returned count/results.

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.summary: Add AggressiveInlining to the leaf comparison helpers so the binary-search inner loop is one flat function Burst can optimize and auto-vectorize.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.currentCost: CompareRange and CompareWithSa are private leaf methods called O(log len) times per query inside FindBound; without inlining hints there is call overhead and the comparison loop is opaque to the surrounding binary search.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.proposedChange: Annotate CompareRange and CompareWithSa with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] (matching the convention already used in Bwt.cs). The early-return scalar loop in CompareRange is already branch-predictable; inlining lets Burst hoist len-saPos and Math.Min.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.rationale: Removes call overhead in a logarithmically-hot path and exposes the compare loop to the optimizer for hoisting and potential SIMD on the equality scan. Matches existing inlining convention in the module.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.risk: None; pure hint. Larger code size is negligible for these tiny methods.

src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.summary: Replace Math.Min with a branchless/inline min and avoid the redundant `patLen > cmpLen` recheck.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.currentCost: `Math.Min(patLen, len - saPos)` is a call (usually inlined, but worth ensuring) and then `patLen > cmpLen` re-tests the same relation Math.Min just resolved.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.proposedChange: `int rem = len - saPos; int cmpLen = patLen < rem ? patLen : rem; int cmp = CompareRange(text+saPos, pattern, cmpLen); if (cmp == 0 && cmpLen == rem && patLen != rem) return -1;` — or simply keep `patLen > cmpLen` which is equivalent to `cmpLen == rem` after the min; the point is to compute min inline once. Since cmpLen<patLen iff rem<patLen, `patLen > cmpLen` is already the cheapest test, so just inline the min.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.rationale: Inlining the min avoids any chance of an un-inlined Math.Min call under Burst and keeps the value in a register; the existing `patLen > cmpLen` is fine. Minor cycle save in a log-hot path.
src/IAFahim.String.FMIndex/FMIndex.cs.risk: None; ternary min is identical to Math.Min for ints. Pure refactor.

src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.summary: The most-frequent-pair search is O(workLen^2) per rule due to a redundant inner freq-count over the whole buffer, and the early-exit makes it select a near-arbitrary pair rather than the true max; a single linear-ish pass can both fix the cost and be deterministic.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.currentCost: For each i, the j-loop scans for a duplicate of pair (work[i],work[i+1]); on the FIRST duplicate found it runs a full O(workLen) freq count, records it, then breaks out of the j-loop. With `if (bestFreq > 1) break;` after, the outer loop exits at the first i whose pair repeats. Net: O(workLen) freq scans, but the selection is order-dependent (first repeating pair wins, not the globally most frequent). Across all rules this is O(maxRules * workLen) at best, O(maxRules * workLen^2) if early pairs are unique.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.proposedChange: Replace the i/j/k triple structure. Since values are bytes (0..255), the distinct-pair space is 256*256. Do ONE pass computing the frequency of each adjacent pair into a stackalloc count buffer (or a small hash over 65536 ushort/int slots) keyed by (work[k]<<8 | work[k+1]), tracking the max as you go. This is a single O(workLen) pass that yields the GLOBAL argmax pair. If you must preserve the existing 'first pair with freq>1, by position' tie/selection rule for behavioral parity, instead keep the i-loop but hoist the freq count: count occurrences of the pair at position i in the SAME left-to-right scan and stop at the first i with freq>1 (eliminates the separate j-loop entirely, since j only existed to detect 'has a duplicate', which freq>1 already proves).
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.rationale: The j-loop is pure redundancy: it only checks whether a duplicate exists, which the subsequent freq count already determines (freq>1). Removing it drops a whole O(workLen) inner scan. A pair-frequency histogram over the 65536 possible byte-pairs turns per-rule selection into one linear pass, removing the quadratic worst case and removing the data-dependent branch mispredicts of the nested search.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.risk: The histogram version changes WHICH pair is chosen when multiple pairs tie or when a later pair is globally more frequent than the first-repeating one, so it changes observable output. Only adopt it if 'most frequent pair' (not 'first repeating pair') is the intended contract. The j-loop-removal version preserves exact current selection and output and is safe. Byte-pair key (k<<8|k+1) is exact since both operands are bytes; no signed/overflow issue.

src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.summary: work[i], work[i+1], and workLen-1 are reloaded on every iteration of the inner loops though invariant within them.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.currentCost: Inside the i-loop, the j-loop reads work[i] and work[i+1] on every j; the k-loop reads work[i] and work[i+1] on every k. work[i]/work[i+1] are invariant for fixed i but are re-dereferenced through the pointer each time, defeating register allocation across the pointer alias. workLen-1 is recomputed in three loop bounds.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.proposedChange: Hoist `byte a = work[i]; byte b = work[i+1];` before the j-loop and compare against a,b. Hoist `int lastIdx = workLen - 1;` once per outer-while iteration and use it in the i, j, and k loop bounds. In the replacement/rewrite loop, similarly cache pair0/pair1 (already done) and use a single `int limit = workLen - 1` instead of recomputing `k < workLen - 1` each iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.rationale: Removes repeated pointer dereferences and the redundant subtraction in hot loop conditions, shortening the dependency chain and freeing the compiler/Burst to keep a,b in registers. Burst cannot always prove work[i] is invariant across the k-loop because writes to work[newLen++] in the rewrite phase create potential aliasing; explicit locals make the invariance unconditional.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.risk: None. a/b are read before any write to work in that scan; lastIdx equals workLen-1 exactly. Pure constant-factor win, identical output.

src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.summary: newSym = (byte)(254 - ruleCount) silently collides with real byte data once ruleCount > 254 and with symbols already emitted; the type also wastes the upper symbol space. Worth a named constant and a tighter maxRules guard for safety and clarity.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.currentCost: With maxRules large, (254 - ruleCount) underflows past 0 and wraps to 255,254,... reusing byte values that may equal literal input bytes or earlier new symbols, producing silent mis-compression. No named constant documents that 255 is reserved and new symbols grow downward from 254.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.proposedChange: Introduce `const int FirstNewSymbol = 254;` and clamp the while condition to also stop when ruleCount would make the symbol collide with the input alphabet, or assert maxRules <= 254 as a documented Unchecked precondition. At minimum replace the magic 254 with a named constant.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.rationale: Prevents a silent-correctness landmine and documents the symbol-allocation scheme; named constant aids Burst constant-folding and readability. No throughput cost.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/GrammarCompre.risk: If callers already pass maxRules <= 254 by the Unchecked contract, this is purely defensive/ergonomic and changes nothing observable. Do not add a runtime exception (house rule); use a const + comment or a benign loop-exit guard.

src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.summary: IsNewRule is O(n^2) per call and is invoked at every position inside Build's scan, making Build up to O(len^3); the period/repetition test it performs can be answered far more cheaply.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.currentCost: For each start, IsNewRule loops l=1..(len-start)/2 and for each l does an inner k-loop up to l, i.e. ~ (len-start)^2/4 byte comparisons. Build calls it inside the inner `while (j < len && !IsNewRule(s,j,len))` for growing j, so worst case the total is cubic in len. Each call also re-scans from scratch with no memoization across adjacent positions.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.proposedChange: IsNewRule(start) returns true iff there exists l in [1,(len-start)/2] with s[start..start+l) == s[start+l..start+2l), i.e. the suffix beginning at start has a 'square' (period l) prefix of length 2l. Compute the Z-array (or prefix-function) of the suffix once and detect the smallest square in O(n); or, since you only need 'does ANY square prefix exist', the prefix-function pi of the prefix: a square prefix of length 2l exists iff for some position p, 2*(p+1 - pi[p]) ... — use the standard 'smallest period' test: position p has a border giving period d=p+1-pi[p]; a square prefix exists when d divides some prefix length and the repeat count >=2. At minimum, hoist the per-call recomputation by computing the prefix-function/Z-array of s once outside Build and indexing into it, turning each IsNewRule into O(1)/O(small).
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.rationale: Replaces nested O(n^2)-per-call square detection with linear-preprocessing + O(1) queries, dropping Build from cubic toward linear/near-linear. Far fewer byte comparisons and branch mispredicts in the hot scan.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.risk: Must reproduce IsNewRule's exact predicate (existence of any l with equal halves, l<=(len-start)/2) including the boundary l=(len-start)/2 to preserve where Build splits, hence identical rule boundaries and ruleCount. Verify the square-detection condition matches the brute force on small inputs before adopting. Prefix-function buffer needs O(len) stackalloc/work memory (caller-provided per house rules).

src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.summary: The half-length bound (len-start)/2 is recomputed and the first-mismatch inner loop can be reordered to fail faster; also l only needs candidates where s[start]==s[start+l].
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.currentCost: `(len - start) / 2` is recomputed each l iteration of the outer loop (it is loop-invariant). The inner k-loop tests positions 0..l in order; for typical data the first byte (k=0) is the discriminator, but more importantly l values where s[start]!=s[start+l] can never match and still pay the k-loop entry/setup.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int half = (len - start) / 2;` before the loop. Guard the inner comparison with a cheap precheck: `if (s[start] != s[start+l]) continue;` before entering the k-loop (it would fail at k=0 anyway but this skips loop setup). Use `(len - start) >> 1` since (len-start) is non-negative in this context.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.rationale: Removes a per-iteration division, and `>>1` is exact for non-negative operands (cheaper than a signed div which emits the add-sign-bit sequence). The precheck cuts loop-setup overhead for the common non-matching l.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.risk: `>>1` is only equivalent to `/2` when (len-start)>=0; here start ranges within [0,len) so len-start>0, safe. The s[start]!=s[start+l] precheck is semantically identical to the k=0 iteration of the existing loop. No output change.

src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.summary: Query has a dead branch: both arms of the IsTerminal test return rules[ruleId].Char, and the pos parameter is unused, so the function is a constant-time field read masquerading as a recursive/dispatch query.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.currentCost: `if (rules[ruleId].IsTerminal) return rules[ruleId].Char; return rules[ruleId].Char;` loads IsTerminal, branches, then returns the same field either way — a wasted load and an unpredictable branch on a leaf accessor. `pos` is dead. This signals the function is unfinished rather than optimal.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.proposedChange: Collapse to `return rules[ruleId].Char;` and mark `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]`. If the intended behavior is true SLP expansion (recursing through Left/Right by pos), that is a functional bug to flag separately — as written, drop the branch and the unused pos (or keep pos in signature for API stability but remove the branch).
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.rationale: Eliminates a branch and a redundant field load on a hot leaf accessor; inlining lets Burst fold it into callers. Removes an unpredictable branch with zero behavioral effect since both arms are identical.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.risk: Removing the IsTerminal branch is behavior-preserving ONLY because both arms already return the identical value today. If the dead branch is a placeholder for future non-terminal expansion, document that; do not silently bake in the no-op. Removing pos changes the signature (ergonomics/API break) — keep pos if callers exist.

src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.summary: Rule packs two int + byte + bool with default layout, costing 12 bytes payload that pads to 12-16; reordering or narrowing improves cache density when arrays of rules are scanned linearly in FindOrCreateRule.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.currentCost: Fields: int Left, int Right, byte Char, bool IsTerminal. Natural layout is 4+4+1+1 = 10 bytes, padded to 12 (or 16 under some alignment). FindOrCreateRule scans rules[i].IsTerminal/Left/Right linearly, so each rule touched pulls its full padded footprint into cache.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.proposedChange: Apply [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential, Pack=1)] or [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit)] to pack to 10 bytes, or fold IsTerminal into a flag bit if Char's range permits, shrinking the per-rule footprint and improving the rules[] scan cache-line utilization. Keep blittable/unmanaged for Burst.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.rationale: Tighter struct -> more rules per cache line -> fewer misses during the linear FindOrCreateRule scan, which is on the build hot path. Pack=1 is acceptable here because access is via Burst-generated code and fields are read individually, not requiring natural alignment for SIMD.
src/IAFahim.String.Grammar/Slp.cs.risk: Pack=1 can slow unaligned int loads on some mobile architectures (ARM tolerates unaligned but with a penalty); measure-by-reasoning suggests the cache-density win dominates for linear scans but this is the one place alignment-vs-density could go either way, so treat as low-impact and architecture-dependent. Must remain blittable for Burst (it does).

src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.summary: Find calls EditDistance.Levenshtein which does Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal twice per call; this allocates+frees the heap (textLen - patLen + 1) times and is not Burst-compilable.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.currentCost: Two Marshal.AllocHGlobal + two FreeHGlobal + a try/finally per text position. For n positions that is O(n) heap alloc/free pairs on the hot path, plus Marshal is a managed P/Invoke that Burst rejects entirely.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.proposedChange: Add scratch-buffer parameters (int* prev, int* curr) to Find and pass them through to a pointer-based Levenshtein overload that takes caller-provided buffers instead of allocating. Reuse the same two buffers across all positions (size patLen+1). This matches the existing library convention already used by LandauVishkin (curr/prev passed in).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.rationale: Eliminates O(n) heap allocations entirely (zero allocs on hot path), removes the managed Marshal calls so the method becomes Burst-compilable, and removes the try/finally exception machinery from the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.risk: Caller must allocate buffers of size patLen+1. Behavior identical for valid inputs. The current Levenshtein early-exit (maxDist+1) semantics must be preserved in the buffer-based overload.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.summary: Find recomputes a full O(patLen^2) Levenshtein table at every window even though only a band of width 2k+1 can ever stay <= k.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.currentCost: O(n * m^2) total: for each of ~n positions, Levenshtein fills an m x m DP. Most of that work is wasted because cells outside the diagonal band of width 2k+1 are guaranteed to exceed k.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.proposedChange: Use a banded edit-distance evaluation restricted to columns [i-k, i+k] (Ukkonen-style banding), or route Find through the existing LandauVishkin path which already amortizes across positions with a single forward DP using curr/prev. The banded inner loop drops per-window cost from O(m^2) to O(m*k).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.rationale: Reduces asymptotic work from O(n*m^2) to O(n*m*k); for small k (the common approximate-match case) this is a large constant- and order-factor win, with far fewer cache lines touched per window.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ApproximateMatc.risk: Banding must clamp band edges and treat out-of-band cells as +infinity to preserve the exact <= k decision. For k >= m the band degenerates to the full table (same result).

src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.summary: states[v * 256 + text[i]] is recomputed up to four times per character and v * 256 uses a multiply where a shift suffices.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.currentCost: Per character: text[i] re-read multiple times, v*256 recomputed in the while-condition body and twice more after, and states[v*256+text[i]] indexed 3x. That is several redundant integer multiplies/loads on the hottest loop in the matcher.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int b = text[i]; once per iteration. Replace v * 256 with v << 8 (define const int StateStride = 256, const int LinkSlot = 255, const int OutSlot = 254). Compute int* row = states + (v << 8); load int nxt = row[b]; once and reuse it in the while/if instead of re-indexing. After updating v, recompute the row pointer once.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.rationale: Cuts the per-character work to a single load of nxt plus one base-pointer add; removes 2-3 redundant array index computations and the multiply (shift is 1 cycle, multiply 3-4). Burst auto-vectorizes nothing here but the scalar dependency chain shortens, helping the gather-bound inner loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.risk: v*256 == v<<8 exactly for non-negative v (state ids are always >= 0). Named constants change no values. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.summary: Magic constants 256 (stride), 255 (fail/link slot), and 254 (output slot) are unnamed, and the parameter stateCount is unused.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.currentCost: Readability/maintenance cost; the layout contract (254/255 reserved slots) is implicit. stateCount is dead.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.proposedChange: Introduce const int Sigma = 256, const int FailSlot = 255, const int OutSlot = 254. Either remove the unused stateCount parameter or use it to bound-check in a Try* variant per house convention.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.rationale: Self-documenting layout reduces the chance of an off-by-one when this packed table format is reused; no codegen change.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoOffline.cs.risk: Removing a parameter is a signature/API change; if external callers exist, keep it or add a parallel overload. No behavioral change otherwise.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.summary: The inner while loop computes run % period for every character compared, a division on the hottest path.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.currentCost: Per comparison: an integer modulo (run % period), ~20-40 cycles on many mobile cores, plus an add for i+(run%period). This runs O(n) times per (period,i) pair.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.proposedChange: Maintain a rolling index m that tracks run % period without division: start m = 0; compare s[i+run] == s[i+m]; after each step do run++ and m++ then if (m == period) m = 0;. This replaces the modulo with an increment and a single compare/branch (or branchless: m = (m + 1 == period ? 0 : m + 1)).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.rationale: Replaces a div by an add+compare, eliminating the longest-latency op in the inner loop; the compare is well-predicted (taken once per period), and s[i+m] base offset is now incremental.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.risk: Rolling counter must reset to 0 exactly when it reaches period, reproducing run % period for all run >= 0. Result identical.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.summary: AggressiveInlining is applied to a large doubly-nested-loop method where inlining cannot help and may hurt.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.currentCost: The attribute forces the JIT/Burst to consider inlining a big function body into every caller, bloating call sites and instruction cache with no benefit since the cost is inside the loops, not the call.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.proposedChange: Remove [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] from Find. Reserve AggressiveInlining for the small leaf helpers (GetNext/SetNext style), not loop-bearing entry points.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.rationale: Inlining a hot leaf saves a call; inlining a multi-loop driver only grows code size and I-cache pressure. Removing it lets the optimizer keep the loop body tight and out-of-line.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.risk: None functionally; this is a codegen hint only. Same output.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.summary: Loop bound period * 2 <= n recomputes the multiply each outer iteration and the inner bound n - 2*period each entry.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.currentCost: A multiply (period*2) in the outer condition and 2*period recomputed for the inner loop bound; minor but per outer iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int twoP = period << 1; reuse in both the outer guard (twoP <= n) and inner bound (i <= n - twoP). Strength-reduce *2 to <<1.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.rationale: Removes a redundant multiply and reuses a single shifted value; trivial but free and clarifies intent.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Crochemore.cs.risk: period is positive so <<1 == *2 exactly. No change in behavior.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.summary: patLens[p] is reloaded every inner-loop iteration and patterns[p] is re-dereferenced per character instead of being hoisted.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.currentCost: Inner char loop re-reads patLens[p] (loop bound) and indexes patterns[p][j] through a double indirection each iteration; the bound check j < patLens[p] re-loads from memory every step.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.proposedChange: Hoist int pl = patLens[p]; byte* pat = patterns[p]; byte* tw = text + i; before the j-loop, then compare tw[j] != pat[j] with bound j < pl. Also hoist the early-out i + pl > textLen using pl.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.rationale: Removes a memory load from the inner-loop bound and collapses the double pointer indirection to a single base+offset, shortening the per-character dependency chain in the brute-force matcher.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.risk: None; pat and pl are loop-invariant within the j-loop. Identical results.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.summary: Match is brute force O(textLen * patCount * maxPatLen); for many patterns an Aho-Corasick pass (already present in this module) is asymptotically better.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.currentCost: Every text position is compared against every pattern fully. With P patterns of length up to L over text n, worst case O(n*P*L).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.proposedChange: Document/redirect multi-pattern callers to the AhoCorasick path (Build/AddPattern/BuildLinks/Search) which runs in O(n + total matches) after an O(sum of pattern lengths) build. Keep Match only as a small-P fallback.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.rationale: Aho-Corasick removes the per-position per-pattern rescan, turning O(n*P*L) into O(n) search; the module already implements it, so this is wiring not new code.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DictionaryMatch.risk: Aho-Corasick reports matches by pattern id at end positions; the brute-force Match reports id at start positions per (i,p). Caller-facing match coordinate semantics differ and must be reconciled, so this is a guarded recommendation, not a drop-in swap.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.summary: GetNext(st, link, c) is evaluated up to three times for the same (link, c) in the link-assignment expression.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.currentCost: Line 69 calls GetNext(st, link, c) twice plus the while loop's final probe; each is a st[link].Next[c] load. The ternary recomputes the same value it just tested.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int viaLink = GetNext(st, link, c); after the while loop, then st[u].Link = (v == 0) ? 0 : (viaLink != -1 ? viaLink : 0);. Build runs once so impact is on construction time, but it removes 2 redundant gathers per edge.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.rationale: Eliminates duplicate fixed-buffer indexing; one load instead of three. Construction is not the hot search path, hence medium not high.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.risk: viaLink captures the post-loop value of GetNext(st,link,c); identical to current. No behavior change.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.summary: Search re-reads st[v].Out and st[v].ExitLink as separate indexed loads when a single State* sv = &st[v] base pointer would serve both.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.currentCost: Per character: Transition plus st[v].Out, st[v].ExitLink each re-index the State array; the exit-link walk re-indexes st[exit] twice per node (Out and ExitLink).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.proposedChange: After v = Transition(...), take State* sv = st + v; use sv->Out and sv->ExitLink. In the exit walk, State* se = st + exit; read se->Out and se->ExitLink from the one base. Optionally mark Transition AggressiveInlining (it is a small leaf).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.rationale: Reduces repeated address computation into the State array (each State is large: 256*4 + 12 bytes, so indexing is a shift+add per access); caching the base pointer trims the dependency chain in the per-character loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.risk: Pure pointer-strength reduction; same loads, fewer recomputations. Identical output.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.summary: State always reserves fixed int Next[256] (1024 bytes) even when sigma is much smaller, and uses int per transition where the trie rarely needs 31 bits.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.currentCost: sizeof(State) ~= 1036 bytes regardless of sigma; for a DNA/byte-subset alphabet (sigma=4 or sigma small) over 99% of each State is unused, wrecking cache locality across states during Search/BuildLinks.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.proposedChange: If sigma is known small and fixed at compile sites, template/duplicate the struct with fixed int Next[Sigma], or store transitions in a separately sized flat int* table (size*sigma) indexed as table[v*sigma + c] so memory scales with sigma. Where state counts fit, use short/int32 is already minimal; the win is the 256 stride.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.rationale: Shrinking the per-state stride from 1KB to sigma*4 bytes dramatically improves cache-line utilization in the BFS and search loops (more states per line, fewer misses), which dominates this gather-bound algorithm.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/AhoCorasick.cs.risk: Requires sigma to be fixed/known for the flat layout; the fixed[256] form is simplest if sigma can exceed compile-time bounds. Indexing math (v*sigma+c) must match Build/Search consistently. Behavior identical when sigma is respected.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.summary: Two heap allocations (AllocHGlobal) per call defeat Burst and add syscall-level overhead; the unchecked/Run convention in this library uses caller-provided scratch buffers instead.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.currentCost: Two Marshal.AllocHGlobal calls + try/finally with two FreeHGlobal per invocation. Marshal interop and try/finally are not Burst-compatible and serialize on the allocator.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.proposedChange: Change the signature to accept two caller-provided int* scratch buffers (prev, curr) of size lenB+1, matching the buffer-passing convention used by DynamicKmp/PatternMatch/PrefixFunction. Drop the try/finally entirely. Caller can stackalloc.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.rationale: Removes per-call heap allocation and the managed Marshal/try-finally path, making the method Burst-compilable and eliminating allocator dependency chains. Same numeric result.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.risk: API change (adds parameters) — breaks existing callers. Behavior identical for all valid inputs; caller must supply buffers of at least lenB+1 ints, consistent with the unchecked Run convention.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.summary: The early-break on row-min > maxDist returns prev[lenB] from a stale (partially computed) row, which can return a distance that is not the true value but is also not consistently maxDist+1; the band can also be shrunk to O(lenA*maxDist).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.currentCost: Inner row is full width O(lenB) even when only the diagonal band of width 2*maxDist+1 can hold values <= maxDist. Columns outside the band are wasted work.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.proposedChange: Restrict the inner j-loop to the band [max(1, i-maxDist), min(lenB, i+maxDist)], initializing out-of-band cells to maxDist+1. This yields O(lenA*maxDist) instead of O(lenA*lenB).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.rationale: When maxDist << lenB this is a large asymptotic reduction in cycles and touches far fewer cache lines per row.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.risk: Must initialize band boundary cells to maxDist+1 so min() never reads uninitialized/out-of-band neighbors. Preserves the clamped result (return value capped at maxDist+1 semantics) only if the existing early-break semantics are also tightened; verify intended return contract first.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.summary: cost is computed with a branch and Math.Min nesting builds a longer dependency chain than necessary.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.currentCost: Ternary `a[i-1]==b[j-1]?0:1` is a data-dependent branch per cell; three-way Math.Min nests sequentially.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.proposedChange: Compute cost branchlessly: `int cost = (a[i - 1] != b[j - 1]) ? 1 : 0` can be `(int)(a[i-1] != b[j-1])`-style via subtraction trick, or hoist `a[i-1]` out of the j-loop into a local since it is loop-invariant across j.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.rationale: Hoisting a[i-1] removes one redundant load per inner iteration; branchless cost lets Burst vectorize the comparison. Inner loop runs lenA*lenB times so per-cell savings compound.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.risk: Branchless cost must produce exactly 0/1; the bool-to-int cast is well-defined. Hoisting a[i-1] is purely a CSE with no semantic change.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.summary: AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal + try/finally per call defeats Burst and allocates; should take a caller-provided v buffer.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.currentCost: One Marshal.AllocHGlobal + try/finally + FreeHGlobal per call; managed interop path blocks Burst.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.proposedChange: Pass `int* v` (size m+1) as a parameter like the other methods; remove try/finally. Caller stackallocs.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.rationale: Eliminates heap allocation and managed Marshal path, enabling Burst compilation and removing allocator serialization.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.risk: Signature change breaks callers. Numerically identical; caller must size v to lenB+1.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.summary: Loop-invariant `m + 1` (trace row stride) is recomputed each iteration, and the `d > 0` test inside the while is loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.currentCost: `d * (m + 1) + i` recomputes m+1 and the multiply each iteration; `d > 0` re-evaluated every while step though it cannot change within the call.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int stride = m + 1; int rowBase = d * stride;` before the i-loop and index `trace[rowBase + i]`. Lift the `d > 0` guard out of the while by skipping the extend loop entirely when d == 0.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.rationale: Removes a multiply and add from the trace store path and removes an invariant compare from the hot extend loop, shortening the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.risk: None — pure invariant hoisting. d does not change during the call.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.summary: Branchful per-byte mismatch count prevents wide vectorization; a branchless accumulate lets Burst SIMD it.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.currentCost: `if (a[i] != b[i]) dist++;` is a data-dependent branch per byte, serializing and hard to vectorize.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.proposedChange: Accumulate branchlessly: `dist += (a[i] != b[i]) ? 1 : 0;` (bool-to-int) so Burst can vectorize the compare-and-sum, or process in word-sized chunks comparing 8 bytes via XOR and popcount of nonzero byte lanes.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.rationale: Removes the per-byte branch, enabling SIMD horizontal sum over the comparison mask; on long inputs this is several-x fewer cycles.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/EditDistance.cs.risk: Branchless form yields identical count. Word-chunk variant needs careful tail handling and byte-lane nonzero detection to match exact per-byte count.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.summary: Three separate passes (zero cntA/cntB, fill cntA, fill cntB) plus a full 256-entry compare; can fuse and early-out.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.currentCost: 256 zeroing iterations writing two arrays, then two length-n fill loops, then a 256 compare loop — multiple passes over the histograms.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.proposedChange: Fuse the two fill loops into one (lenA==lenB so iterate i once: cntA[a[i]]++, cntB[b[i]]++). Optionally use a single int* histogram of 256: increment for a[i], decrement for b[i], then verify all 256 are zero — halves histogram RAM and the compare touches one array.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.rationale: Single fused fill loop has better locality and fewer loop overheads; single signed histogram halves the working set (1KB vs 2KB) and the final scan reads one cache-resident array. Same boolean result.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.risk: Single-histogram variant changes the buffer contract (one int* of 256 instead of two). With signed counts no overflow for realistic lengths (< 2^31). Final check `cnt[i] != 0` is equivalent to cntA[i] != cntB[i].

src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.summary: First-occurrence detection is O(n^2) via an inner linear scan over prior characters; a 256-entry last-seen table makes it O(n).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.currentCost: For each i an inner loop `for j in [0,i)` scans for a prior equal byte — quadratic in lenA/lenB.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.proposedChange: Use a 256-int table `firstId[c]` initialized to 0 (meaning unseen). For each i: if firstId[a[i]]==0 assign firstId[a[i]]=nextId++ ; mapA[i]=firstId[a[i]]. Reset the table between the a and b passes. This is the standard parameterized-match canonical form in O(n).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.rationale: Drops the algorithm from O(n^2) to O(n) with a fixed 256-int scratch (1KB). Large win for non-trivial lengths.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/PatternMatch.cs.risk: Adds a 256-int scratch buffer (use caller-provided int* per library convention, or stackalloc). Must clear it (or use a generation stamp) before the second pass. Produces identical canonical id sequence: id assigned on first occurrence in order, reused thereafter.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.summary: The whole routine is O(n^2) per period (O(n^3) total in the worst case) plus an O(count) subsumption scan; the genuine Main-Lorentz algorithm finds all maximal repetitions in O(n log n).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.currentCost: Outer period loop O(n), inner start loop O(n), inner k-compare O(period), and an extra O(count) subsumption scan per found run. Worst case approaches O(n^3).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.proposedChange: Replace the brute-force scan with the actual Main-Lorentz divide-and-conquer using Z-function / prefix-function on prefix and reversed suffix to find runs crossing the midpoint, giving O(n log n). At minimum, replace the O(count) linear subsumption check with an indexing keyed by period.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.rationale: This file is named MainLorentz but implements brute force; the named algorithm is asymptotically far better and is the intended contract. Massive cycle reduction for large n.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.risk: Significant rewrite; must preserve the exact set/ordering of Run outputs the current code emits (it emits the first non-subsumed run per period via the `break`). The true algorithm enumerates maximal repetitions which may differ in count/representation — confirm the intended output contract before changing.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.summary: The extension loop computes `len % period` every iteration; since len starts at 2*period it equals len-period region and can be tracked with a running index instead of a modulo.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.currentCost: `s[start + len % period]` performs an integer division/modulo per extension step — div is ~20+ cycles and is on the hot extension path.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.proposedChange: Maintain a cyclic index `int m = period` (since at len==2*period, len%period==0... actually track `int m = (2*period) % period == 0`), incrementing m each step and resetting to 0 when m==period: `if (++m == period) m = 0;` then compare `s[start+len] == s[start+m]`.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.rationale: Replaces a hardware division with an increment-and-compare (branch predictable, ~1 cycle), removing the div from the inner extension loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.risk: Must seed m correctly: at len==2*period the index is len%period==0, so start m at 0 before the first compare. Strength reduction of % to a counter is exact for non-negative len.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.summary: `period * 2` and `2 * period` are recomputed in loop headers/bodies; minor invariant hoist.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.currentCost: `period * 2 <= n` in the outer header and `start + 2 * period <= n` plus `len = 2 * period` each recompute the doubling.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `int twoP = period << 1;` once per outer iteration and reuse for the header bound, the inner start bound, and the initial len.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.rationale: Shift instead of multiply and a single CSE per period; trims a few ops from inner-loop bound checks.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/MainLorentz.cs.risk: None — period is positive, period<<1 == period*2 exactly with no overflow for valid n.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/DynamicKmp.cs.summary: Build duplicates PrefixFunction.Run verbatim; consolidating removes duplicate code and a second I-cache footprint.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DynamicKmp.cs.currentCost: Two identical prefix-function implementations (DynamicKmp.Build and PrefixFunction.Run) maintained separately; duplicate instruction-cache pressure and divergence risk.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DynamicKmp.cs.proposedChange: Have DynamicKmp.Build call PrefixFunction.Run (both AggressiveInlining) instead of reimplementing the loop, or delete Build and document that callers use PrefixFunction.Run.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DynamicKmp.cs.rationale: Eliminates code duplication; with AggressiveInlining the abstraction is free at runtime and reduces maintenance/divergence risk.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/DynamicKmp.cs.risk: None functionally — the loops are byte-for-byte equivalent (fail vs piPtr naming only).

src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.summary: Dead constant MOD = ulong.MaxValue is never referenced; hashing uses natural mod-2^64 ulong overflow.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.currentCost: An unused private const that misleads readers into thinking the hash is computed mod (2^64 - 1) (a Mersenne-style modulus), when in fact Compute/Build/Query all rely on plain ulong wraparound (mod 2^64).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.proposedChange: Remove the `private const ulong MOD = ulong.MaxValue;` line, or, if a true Mersenne modulus was intended, document the discrepancy. As-is it is purely dead and should be deleted. Also drop the unused `using System;` in all three files (no System type is referenced).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.rationale: Eliminates a dead symbol and removes the false implication that any modular reduction is happening. No codegen change (const is already folded away / unused), but it removes a correctness trap: a future edit that 'restores' `% MOD` with MOD=ulong.MaxValue would silently break Query, since Query's identity prefix[r]-prefix[l]*power[r-l] only holds for the ring Z/2^64 (power-of-two modulus), not for mod (2^64-1).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.risk: None for removal. If instead someone wires MOD into the arithmetic, Query breaks because subtraction-based range hashing requires a consistent ring and ulong.MaxValue is not 2^64; must NOT introduce % MOD. Pure deletion is fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.summary: Per-iteration multiply-add chain has a serial dependency on `hash`; widening the byte load and unrolling can shorten the critical path, but the dependency is inherent to polynomial hashing.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.currentCost: Compute's loop body `hash = hash * Base + ptr[i]` is a strict serial dependency chain: one 64-bit multiply + add per byte, latency-bound (~3-4 cycles/byte on the mul), no ILP because each iteration needs the previous hash. Build is the same but emits two independent streams (prefix and power) which already overlap.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.proposedChange: For Compute, process the data in K independent lanes using horner blocking: maintain K partial hashes h0..h3 each consuming every 4th byte, then combine with precomputed Base^k powers at the end (h = ((h0*B + h1)*B + h2)*B + h3 style, with the correct Base^4 stride multipliers). This breaks the single latency chain into 4 parallel chains, trading a few extra multiplies for ~4x more ILP. Keep AggressiveInlining only if call sites are few; otherwise the unrolled body may bloat callers.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.rationale: The current loop is latency-bound, not throughput-bound, so parallel Horner lanes hide multiply latency and let Burst/the CPU issue independent muls every cycle. This is a real constant-factor win on long strings (the typical RollingHash use case).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/RollingHash.cs.risk: Must use modular-arithmetic-consistent stride powers of Base under the SAME mod-2^64 ring (ulong overflow), which is associative/commutative, so the lane-combine yields bit-identical results to sequential Horner. Tail handling for len not divisible by K must replicate the exact left-to-right weighting. Build cannot be lane-split (it must materialize every prefix), so leave Build unchanged.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.summary: Caller only tests Compare(...)==0, so the subtraction a[i]-b[i] and full lexical ordering are wasted work; an equality-only scan is cheaper and vectorizable.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.currentCost: Compare returns a[i]-b[i] computing a signed difference (an extra subtract per mismatch), but its only caller FindLyndonRuns does `Compare(...) == 0`. The byte-at-a-time equality loop also defeats wide-load vectorization that Burst could apply to a memcmp-style equality test.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.proposedChange: Add a dedicated `private static bool Equals(byte* a, byte* b, int len)` that returns false on first mismatch (no subtraction) and have FindLyndonRuns call it. Internally compare in machine-word chunks (read ulong via *(ulong*)(a+i) vs *(ulong*)(b+i)) for the bulk, with a byte tail, since only equality (not ordering) is needed. Keep the ordering-returning Compare only if some external caller needs it; otherwise replace it.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.rationale: Removes a per-mismatch subtract and, more importantly, enables 8-bytes-per-iteration equality comparison instead of 1, cutting the inner-loop trip count ~8x for the (common) long-match case inside the O(n*p) Lyndon scan. Equality via word loads is exactly what Burst vectorizes well.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.risk: Word-wide loads require the comparison to be pure equality (it is) and that reads of up to 7 bytes past the logical end stay within the allocated buffer; since a/b point inside s+i and s+i+p with i+2p<=n guaranteed by the guard, a word read at offset i may overrun the p-length window into valid in-bounds bytes only if i+p+8<=n — guard the word path with a length check and fall back to the byte loop for the tail/short cases. Endianness does not matter for equality. Behavior is identical because only ==0 is observed.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.summary: Count is O(n^2): for every i it linearly expands left/right over the LCP array; this can be reduced to O(n) with a monotonic-stack / nearest-smaller-value precomputation.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.currentCost: For each i in [1,n), two inner while-loops walk outward over lcp[] as long as neighbors are >= h = lcp[i]. On a flat or slowly-decreasing LCP array (e.g. lcp all equal), each i scans O(n), giving O(n^2) total time and O(n^2) memory traffic over lcp[].
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.proposedChange: Precompute, in O(n) using a monotonic stack, the nearest index to the left with lcp < h (prevSmaller[i]) and nearest to the right with lcp < h (nextSmaller[i]). Then left = prevSmaller[i]+1, right = nextSmaller[i]-1, and the maximal interval width is (right-left+1) in O(1) per i. Note the current code uses strict bounds (left>1, right<n-1) — the stack version must replicate those exact boundary conditions and the `>= h` vs `< h` tie-breaking to stay identical.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.rationale: Reduces the asymptotic from O(n^2) to O(n) time and O(n) extra scratch, the classic 'largest rectangle / NSV' transformation. For large suffix arrays this is the dominant cost and the single biggest win in this module.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/Runs.cs.risk: Tie handling is subtle: the original expands while neighbors are `>= h`, meaning equal-height neighbors are absorbed into the interval for EVERY i sharing that height, so multiple i's report overlapping/duplicate intervals and the result counts those repeats. The NSV reformulation must keep the same counting semantics (it counts per-i, not per-distinct-interval), so use a consistent strict-on-one-side / non-strict-on-the-other convention that reproduces `>= h` outward expansion exactly; otherwise the returned `runs` count changes. Needs two int* scratch buffers (allowed under house rules via caller-provided pointers or stackalloc). Verify against the existing NUnit tests before shipping.

src/IAFahim.String.Match/ZAlgorithm.cs.summary: Inner Z-box loop repeatedly reloads zPtr[i] from memory each iteration; caching it in a local register and writing back once removes a store-load dependency per step.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ZAlgorithm.cs.currentCost: The while-loop `while (i + zPtr[i] < len && ptr[zPtr[i]] == ptr[i + zPtr[i]]) zPtr[i]++;` reads and writes zPtr[i] (a memory location) every iteration, creating a store-to-load round-trip on the dependency chain and inhibiting keeping the counter in a register. The subsequent `if (i + zPtr[i] - 1 > r)` re-reads it again.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ZAlgorithm.cs.proposedChange: Hoist into a local: `int z = (i <= r) ? min(zPtr[i-l], r-i+1) : 0; while (i + z < len && ptr[z] == ptr[i + z]) z++; zPtr[i] = z; if (i + z - 1 > r) { l = i; r = i + z - 1; }`. This keeps the hot counter in a register and stores to zPtr[i] exactly once. Also consider replacing `zPtr[k] < rem ? zPtr[k] : rem` with a branchless math.min, and reconsider AggressiveInlining on these large, non-leaf loop bodies (they bloat every call site for little benefit since the function is already a top-level entry point).
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ZAlgorithm.cs.rationale: Eliminates n redundant loads + stores on the hottest path of the Z-algorithm and shortens the dependency chain (register increment vs memory increment), a clean constant-factor improvement. min as a branchless select avoids a mispredictable branch on the comparison. Removing AggressiveInlining from a large body avoids icache pressure at call sites.
src/IAFahim.String.Match/ZAlgorithm.cs.risk: Pure register-vs-memory transformation — observable output identical. The min/select substitution is on two non-negative ints (rem = r-i+1 >= 1 when i<=r, zPtr[k] >= 0), so no signed-overflow concern. Identical change applies to both the byte* and int* overloads (which are duplicated and could be unified via a generic where T : unmanaged + IEquatable, but that risks Burst/equality-codegen quality, so keep two specializations).

src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.summary: The stackalloc int[len*2] failure buffer 'f' is allocated and zero-initialized but never read or written after init; remove it entirely.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.currentCost: 8*len bytes of stack per call plus a len*2-iteration zeroing loop (2*len stores). For large len this can overflow the limited stack on mobile and pollutes cache with a buffer that is pure dead state.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.proposedChange: Delete the lines 'int* f = stackalloc int[len * 2];' and the following 'for (int i = 0; i < len * 2; i++) f[i] = 0;'. The algorithm as written (Booth's with i2/j/k pointers) never references f.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.rationale: Eliminates an entire O(len) memory write pass and 8*len bytes of stack working set with zero behavioral change, since f is write-once-dead. Fewer cache misses, no stack-overflow risk on mobile.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.risk: None. f is provably never read. The int* overload (line 26) already omits this buffer, confirming it is vestigial. Pure dead-code removal, semantics identical.

src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.summary: Replace the two modulo operations (i2+k)%len and (j+k)%len in the hot loop with branchless conditional subtraction.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.currentCost: Two integer div/mod per loop iteration. Idiv on x86/ARM is ~20-40 cycles and cannot be vectorized; this is the dominant cost in the inner loop and Burst cannot strength-reduce a non-constant len.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.proposedChange: Both indices are in [0, 2*len-2). Compute 'int ia = i2+k; if (ia>=len) ia-=len;' and 'int jb=j+k; if (jb>=len) jb-=len;' then index s[ia], s[jb]. Equivalently branchless: 'ia -= (ia>=len ? len : 0)'. Since i2,j,k each < len, the sum is < 2*len so a single subtraction always normalizes.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.rationale: A single compare-and-subtract (predicated, ~1-2 cycles) replaces a full integer division (~20-40 cycles), removing the longest dependency-chain operation from the hot path. len need not be a power of two for this to be valid.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.risk: Valid only because each of i2,j,k is strictly < len at the point of use (loop guard ensures it), so i2+k and j+k are < 2*len, meaning one subtraction suffices. If invariants changed (k could reach len), a while/loop would be needed; here single subtraction is provably sufficient.

src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.summary: Same modulo-to-conditional-subtraction strength reduction as the byte* overload for (i2+k)%len and (j+k)%len.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.currentCost: Two non-constant idiv per inner-loop iteration dominate the loop; Burst cannot turn a runtime len into a multiply-shift.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.proposedChange: Replace s[(i2+k)%len] / s[(j+k)%len] with normalized indices: 'int ia=i2+k; ia-=(ia>=len?len:0); int jb=j+k; jb-=(jb>=len?len:0);' then s[ia], s[jb].
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.rationale: Eliminates the heaviest arithmetic op (division) from the hot loop, shortening the per-iteration dependency chain by ~20-40 cycles each.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.risk: Same guard: i2,j,k < len so sums < 2*len, one subtraction normalizes. Behavior identical.

src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.summary: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] is NOT warranted for these (they contain loops), but the unused 'using System;' should be removed and the missing attribute on a future leaf helper noted; primarily flag that System import is dead.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.currentCost: 'using System;' (line 3) is unused after the dead f-buffer removal; no runtime cost but signals leftover scaffolding. AggressiveInlining on a looped method gives no benefit.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.proposedChange: Remove 'using System;' (nothing from System namespace is referenced). Keep 'using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;' only if an inlining attribute is actually added elsewhere; otherwise it is also unused and can be removed.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.rationale: Both using directives are currently unused (no Math, no MethodImpl attribute present). Removing dead imports is a zero-risk cleanup; neither method should be force-inlined since both contain a while loop.
src/IAFahim.String.MinRotation/MinRotati.risk: None — purely removing unreferenced imports. Confirm no attribute usage before removing System.Runtime.CompilerServices.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.summary: Recomputed transition-slot address pointer arithmetic up to 3 times per Add; hoist into a local.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.currentCost: The expression ((int*)((IntPtr)_node + cur * sizeof(PalindromicTree.Node) + sizeof(int))) is computed once on line 42, then identically again on line 44, and a structurally identical one on line 70. Each is an int->IntPtr mul/add chain. The line 42 read and line 44 read recompute the same base and re-index [c].
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.proposedChange: Compute int* curTrans = (int*)((byte*)_node + cur * sizeof(PalindromicTree.Node) + sizeof(int)); once after the first while-loop, then use int next = curTrans[c]; for the existence check, reuse next in the early-return branch, and curTrans[c] = state; on line 70. This removes one full address computation and one redundant load of curTrans[c].
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.rationale: Eliminates a redundant memory load (the value read on line 42 is re-read on line 44) and one duplicate multiply/add address computation, shortening the dependency chain on the hot per-character path. Burst/JIT may not CSE through the IntPtr cast reliably.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.risk: None; identical addresses and identical reads. Prefer (byte*) over (IntPtr) cast for clarity but arithmetic is the same.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.summary: Cast Link to int redundantly; Link is already int in the Node struct.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.currentCost: Lines 40, 60, 66 do cur = (int)_node[cur].Link and link = (int)_node[cur].Link / (int)_node[link].Link. PalindromicTree.Node.Link is declared as int, so the (int) cast is a no-op that adds visual noise and signals a possible type-confusion that could mask a future widening bug.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.proposedChange: Drop the (int) casts: cur = _node[cur].Link; and link = _node[link].Link; since Link is int.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.rationale: No cycle change but removes dead casts; improves readability and prevents accidental reliance on truncation semantics. House style requires explicit types, which are already satisfied.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.risk: None — Link field type is int; cast is identity.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.summary: Two near-identical suffix-link walk loops (lines 35-41 and 61-67) recompute _pos-1-checkLen each iteration; hoist _pos-1 and cache _s[].
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.currentCost: Both walk loops compute _pos - 1 - checkLen and load _node[cur].Len then index _s each iteration. _pos is a static field reloaded each iteration; the subtraction base (_pos-1) is loop-invariant.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.proposedChange: Hoist int posM1 = _pos - 1; before each loop and test posM1 - checkLen >= 0 && _s[posM1 - checkLen] == c. Optionally factor the shared walk into a private static AggressiveInlined helper int FindLink(int start, int posM1, byte c) to remove duplicated code and let the JIT inline one tight version.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.rationale: Removes a per-iteration reload of the _pos static and a redundant decrement from the dependency chain inside the hottest inner loop; factoring also shrinks I-cache footprint and code duplication.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.risk: None; _pos is not modified inside either walk loop, so _pos-1 is invariant there.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.summary: No AggressiveInlining attribute and no Try/Run naming; transition addressing duplicated instead of using PalindromicTree.GetNext/SetNext style helpers.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.currentCost: Add manually inlines the GetNext/SetNext pointer math that PalindromicTree already encapsulates in helpers, duplicating the addressing logic and the risk of one diverging from the other.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.proposedChange: Introduce private static AggressiveInlined GetNext(int v, int c)/SetNext(int v, int c, int x) mirroring PalindromicTree, and call them from Add. This deduplicates the addressing trick and centralizes the Next0-overlay convention in one place.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.rationale: Same codegen after inlining but eliminates copy-paste of the overlay arithmetic, reducing maintenance/correctness risk and matching the sibling class's API shape.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/DynamicPal.risk: None if helpers compile to identical arithmetic and are AggressiveInlined under Burst.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Node struct (Next0:int, Len:int, Link:int, Occ:long) is 24 bytes due to long forcing 8-byte alignment with no padding issue, but the int,int,int,long layout already wastes no bytes; however Occ as long may be oversized.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: sizeof(Node) is 24 bytes (3 ints = 12, then 8-byte aligned long at offset 16 -> 4 bytes padding after the three ints, total 24). For len up to ~2^31 characters Occ counts cannot exceed n which fits in int for any realistic Burst/mobile workload; the long doubles the field and forces 4 bytes of padding.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: If maximum occurrence count is bounded by string length (always true: a substring occurs at most n times), change Occ to int. Layout becomes 4 ints = 16 bytes, eliminating the 4 bytes of alignment padding AND 4 bytes of width = 24->16 bytes per node (33% smaller), improving cache density of the node array that both Build and Add stream through.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: Occurrence count of any palindrome is at most n; for n <= 2^31-1 (the addressable limit here, since indices are int) Occ never overflows int. Shrinking the hot Node from 24 to 16 bytes is a large working-set/cache-miss win on the pointer-chasing suffix-link walks.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: Semantics change ONLY if a caller needs occurrence counts > int.MaxValue, impossible when n is an int. Verify no external API exposes Occ as long; if it does, keep long or expose via a widening accessor. Also re-check the overlay trick in DynamicPalindromicTree: the transition array indexes [c] starting at offset sizeof(int); with 4 ints the in-struct overlay still spans Len/Link/Occ as 3 int slots — confirm alphabet size used via this overlay never indexes c>=3, otherwise it reads out of the node. (This caveat already applies to the current code.)

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Replace IntPtr-based byte-offset address arithmetic with typed pointer indexing to cut the per-call instruction count and improve Burst codegen.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: Each GetNext/SetNext does ((IntPtr)_node + v*sizeof(Node) + sizeof(int)) then casts to int* and indexes [c]. This forces a load of the global _node, an integer multiply by 24 (non-power-of-two, not strength-reducible to a shift), an add, and a cast through IntPtr. These are the two hottest leaf methods, called inside both inner while-loops of Extend for every character.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: Cache the global pointer once into a local Node* at the top of Extend (and Build), and pass it down or index directly: e.g. int* row = (int*)((byte*)node + (nint)v*sizeof(Node) + sizeof(int)); return row[c]; Using (byte*) avoids the IntPtr round-trip.
