Better, precompute a stride and keep the base as Node*; the multiply by 24 stays but the IntPtr boxing-of-pointer-arithmetic pattern is removed, which Burst lowers more cleanly.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: IntPtr arithmetic mixes managed-pointer semantics that Burst/JIT handle less efficiently than raw byte*/typed-pointer indexing. Removing the IntPtr intermediary and the repeated global-field load (replaced by a register-resident local) shortens the dependency chain in the tightest loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: Pure address-arithmetic refactor; identical bytes accessed. No semantic change. Must keep the same sizeof(Node) stride and +sizeof(int) base offset exactly.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Mutable static global state makes the type non-reentrant, non-thread-safe, and leaks the AllocHGlobal buffer; convert to an unmanaged struct context passed by pointer/ref.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: _node, _size, _last, _len are static. Build() overwrites them and AllocHGlobals a new buffer every call with no Free, leaking memory on each Build. Two concurrent or nested Builds corrupt each other. Every GetNext/SetNext re-loads the static _node global from memory.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: Introduce a blittable struct PalindromicTreeState { public Node* Node; public int Size; public int Last; public int Len; } and make Build/Extend/DistinctCount take PalindromicTreeState* (or ref). Provide a Free(PalindromicTreeState*) that calls Marshal.FreeHGlobal. This also lets GetNext/SetNext read the pointer from a register-resident local rather than a global.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: Removes hidden mutable global state (purity/determinism), fixes the per-call memory leak, enables reentrancy/Burst job usage, and lets the compiler keep the base pointer in a register across the hot loops instead of reloading a static field.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: API-breaking change (signatures change). Behavior for a single sequential Build call is preserved. Caller must now own/free the buffer.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: The Node struct stores only one int (Next0) but GetNext/SetNext index [c] for c in 0..255, reading/writing 256 ints per node; the storage model and the (len+3) allocation are inconsistent and massively under-allocated.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: sizeof(Node)=24 bytes (one transition slot Next0). GetNext(v,c)=((int*)(base+v*24+4))[c] accesses offset v*24+4+c*4, up to +1024 bytes past the node base — i.e. each node's transition row overruns into ~42 following nodes. The buffer is only (len+3)*24 bytes, so for non-trivial input this reads/writes out of bounds and nodes clobber each other.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: Decide the real alphabet. If the input is a small alphabet (e.g. lowercase letters, K<=26), store a fixed transition array fixed int Next[K] inside Node and size the allocation accordingly; index with c-base. If full byte alphabet is required, allocate a separate int[256] transition table per node (256*4=1024 bytes/node) explicitly and size the buffer as (len+2)*(256 ints) — and consider a hash/sparse map since most rows are empty to save RAM/cache. Either way make the per-node stride match the indexed range so accesses stay in bounds.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: Correct, bounds-consistent storage is a prerequisite for any perf claim. A right-sized fixed array also makes the struct blittable and the access a single base+ (c<<2) load with no overlap, and a sparse/hashed alphabet cuts 1KB/node of mostly-zero memory (huge cache-miss reduction for large len).
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: This is the load-bearing correctness issue, not a micro-opt: current code is out-of-bounds for any meaningful input. Fixing it changes the memory layout and allocation size; observable behavior changes only in that it stops corrupting memory. Choose alphabet size to match the documented contract.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Zero-initialize the transition rows in bulk instead of relying on per-node Next0=-1 (which only clears one of the many transition slots).
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: Build sets _node[0/1].Next0=-1 and Extend sets _node[cur].Next0=-1, initializing only the single Next0 field; the remaining 255 transition ints per node are left as whatever AllocHGlobal returned (uninitialized), so GetNext on an unset (v,c) does not reliably return -1.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: After AllocHGlobal, initialize the entire transition region to -1 once (e.g. a typed fill loop or, if rows are contiguous, Unsafe.InitBlock with 0xFF over the transition bytes), then drop the per-node single-field reset. A single linear memset-style pass is cache-friendly and removes a redundant per-Extend write.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: GetNext relies on -1 sentinel for absent transitions; only a full-region init makes that correct. Doing it once linearly is cheaper and more vectorizer-friendly than scattered per-node writes, and removes one store per Extend.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: Depends on resolving the storage-model decision above. Once the transition array size is fixed, a 0xFF fill yields -1 for every int (two's complement), which matches the sentinel exactly.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Hoist repeated _node[p].* and GetNext(p,c) loads into locals across the suffix-link walk loops to shrink the dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: In both while-loops, GetNext(p,c) is evaluated in the loop condition and then SetNext(p,c,...) re-derives the same row address; _node[p].Link is loaded separately. The second loop compares GetNext(p,c)==q then SetNext(p,c,clone), recomputing the row base twice per iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: Compute the row base int* row = &transition[p] once per iteration, read row[c] into a local for the condition, and write row[c] in the body using the same local pointer; load _node[p].Link from a cached Node* local. Cache c-adjusted index once.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: Eliminates duplicate address computation (the v*24 multiply + base add) per loop iteration and the duplicate row[c] load, shortening the critical dependency chain of the inner loop that dominates eertree construction.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: Pure reassociation of identical memory accesses; preserves behavior provided the row pointer is recomputed each iteration after p changes.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Adopt the library Run/Try convention and return the constructed handle instead of mutating globals, and expose Occ-propagation / suffix-link results explicitly.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: Build returns void and writes hidden state; callers cannot run it as a pure function, and Occ counts are set to 1 per node but never propagated down suffix links (DistinctCount is the only query). The API is harder to discover and inconsistent with the rest of the library's unchecked-Run style.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: Rename to RunBuild(PalindromicTreeState* state, byte* s, int len) returning the node count (or void) with state passed in, and add a RunPropagateOccurrences(state) that walks nodes in reverse creation order adding Occ to node[Link].Occ, so Occ is actually meaningful. Keep DistinctCount(state*).
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: Matches the library's Run/Try naming and pointer-context convention, improves discoverability, and makes the Occ field (currently dead/initialized-but-unused) actually usable without changing the hot path.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: API naming/shape change only; construction semantics unchanged. Occ propagation is additive (opt-in method), not altering existing outputs of DistinctCount.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.summary: Branchy mirror init and redundant null-window guard; the i<=r test is subsumed by l<=r when r is the active window, and Math.Min reads d[] then branches.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.currentCost: Per i: ternary l<=r && i<=r ? Math.Min(d[l+r-i], r-i+1) : 1. Two comparisons plus a Math.Min (which on int is a compare+cmov but Burst may emit a branch). The l<=r check is loop-invariant-ish but evaluated every iteration; mirror index l+r-i is recomputed.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.proposedChange: Hoist int center = l + r into nothing useful but instead: since r starts at -1 and only grows, replace l<=r with a single r>=i test after ensuring r initialized; compute int k = i <= r ? Math.Min(d[l + r - i], r - i + 1) : 1; (the l<=r is implied because whenever r>=0 we have l<=r by construction). This drops one comparison per iteration on the hot O(n) loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.rationale: Removes one branch from every iteration of the linear scan. The invariant l<=r holds whenever r>=0 because (l,r) are only assigned together as a valid window, so testing only i<=r is sufficient and equivalent.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.risk: Must verify the window invariant l<=r holds at all r>=0 (it does: l=i-k, r=i+k with k>=1 in Odd so l<=r). If r==-1, i<=r is false so the else branch (1) is taken, matching original. Equivalent.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.summary: Same redundant l<=r guard as Odd; drop to single i<=r comparison.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.currentCost: Per i: l<=r && i<=r ? Math.Min(d[l+r-i+1], r-i+1) : 0 evaluates two comparisons every iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.proposedChange: int k = i <= r ? Math.Min(d[l + r - i + 1], r - i + 1) : 0; relying on the window invariant l<=r whenever r>=0. Saves one comparison per iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.rationale: Identical reasoning to Odd: (l,r) are assigned together as a valid window so l<=r is implied by r>=0; removing the redundant test shortens the per-iteration critical path of the O(n) scan.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.risk: For Even, k can be 0 so l=i-k-1 = i-1, r=i+k=i; l<=r holds (i-1<=i). When r==-1 the else (0) is taken. Equivalent — verify the d[l+r-i+1] index stays in-bounds, which it does because i<=r implies the mirror index is within [l,r].

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.summary: Math.Min(int,int) may not be recognized by Burst as branchless; use math.min or manual cmov pattern.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.currentCost: Math.Min from System.Math; under Burst the System.Math.Min(int,int) intrinsic is usually fine but not guaranteed to vectorize/branchless across versions, and pulling System.Math into a Burst hot path is less idiomatic than Unity.Mathematics math.min.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.proposedChange: If Unity.Mathematics is available in this module, use math.min(a,b) which Burst lowers to a branchless min. Otherwise replace with a manual branchless form: int m = b + ((a - b) & ((a - b) >> 31)); for a<b style min (with care on overflow). Keep Math.Min if it already lowers to cmov.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.rationale: Guarantees branchless min in the hot O(n) inner expression, avoiding a potential mispredicted branch per character.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Manacher.c.risk: Manual branchless min can overflow on a-b for extreme int ranges; here both operands are bounded by n (string length) so a-b cannot overflow. Prefer math.min to avoid the overflow caveat entirely.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.summary: Two separate stackalloc int[n] scratch buffers and two separate sum loops; reuse one buffer and fuse the accumulation into Manacher to avoid the buffer entirely.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.currentCost: Allocates 2*n ints on the stack (8*n bytes) and runs four O(n) passes: Odd fill, sum, Even fill, sum. On mobile, 8*n stack bytes risks stack overflow for large n and doubles the working set; the two sum loops re-stream the just-written arrays (cache reload).
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.proposedChange: 1) Reuse a single int* d = stackalloc int[n]: run Odd into d, accumulate count, then run Even into the SAME d and accumulate again — halving stack to 4*n bytes. 2) Better: add Manacher overloads (or a SumOdd/SumEven) that accumulate sum(d[i]) inline as they compute each d[i], eliminating the scratch buffer and the second pass entirely — O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.rationale: Halves (or eliminates) the stackalloc footprint, removes two full O(n) re-read passes by fusing the sum into the producer loop, cutting cache traffic roughly in half and removing stack-overflow risk on mobile for large n.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.risk: Fusing requires Manacher to expose a sum-accumulating variant; the standalone d[] is still needed internally by Manacher because each d[i] depends on previously written d[] (mirror reads). So the buffer cannot be fully removed without restructuring — but a single shared buffer (option 1) is safe and trivially equivalent. The fused-sum variant must keep writing d[] for the mirror reads; only the extra summation pass is removed.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.summary: int accumulator may overflow for large n; total palindrome count can be ~n^2/2 which exceeds int.MaxValue around n~65536.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.currentCost: count is int and sums sum(odd[i]) + sum(even[i]) which equals the total number of palindromic substrings (with multiplicity of radii), bounded by ~n*(n+1)/2. For n >= ~92682 this overflows int silently, producing wrong results.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.proposedChange: Change return type and accumulator to long. count becomes long count = 0; return long. Matches PalindromicTree.Occ being long and is the only overflow-safe type for this quantity.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.rationale: Correctness for large inputs; the sum of palindrome radii is quadratic in n, so int is provably insufficient. This is a semantics-preservation fix for valid large inputs, not a slowdown (one extra register width).
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Occurrence.risk: Changes the public return type int->long, an API break. If callers depend on int, provide a long-returning method and keep int as a checked/documented small-n variant. Strictly, current behavior is buggy for n>~92k so this restores intended semantics.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Reloads linkPtr[link] and diffPtr[v]/diffPtr[link] with an extra dependent load; minor branch reduction possible but loop is already tight.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: Per v: load linkPtr[v]; load linkPtr[link]; load diffPtr[v]; load diffPtr[link]; branch. The diffPtr[v]==diffPtr[link] compare and linkPtr[link]!=-1 are two conditions joined by &&, causing a short-circuit branch in addition to the if-branch.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: Combine into branch-light form: int link = linkPtr[v]; int dl = diffPtr[link]; int slink = (linkPtr[link] != -1 & diffPtr[v] == dl) ? slinkPtr[link] : link; slinkPtr[v] = slink; using non-short-circuit & to fuse the two predicates into one branch (both loads are cheap and always needed). This removes one conditional branch per iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: Replaces a short-circuit && (two branches) with a single bitwise-and predicate (one branch), and the loads are always performed anyway, so there is no wasted work. Tighter dependency chain in the O(stateCount) loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: Using & instead of && always evaluates diffPtr[v]==diffPtr[link]; diffPtr[link] is a valid read for any link>=0 (link=linkPtr[v] is a real state index, links never -1 for v>=2 since the imaginary roots are 0/1). Safe given the automaton invariant that linkPtr[v] for v>=2 is a valid in-range index.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.summary: Returns stateCount unchanged — a no-op return value that adds no information.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.currentCost: The method always returns its stateCount argument, so callers gain nothing; it pretends to be a Try/Run-with-count convention but the count is just echoed.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.proposedChange: Make it return void (it mutates slinkPtr in place), or if the Run convention requires a count, document that it equals input. Changing to void removes a pointless move on return.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.rationale: Clarifies the API contract and removes a meaningless return; aligns with in-place-mutation Run convention.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/Palindromi.risk: API change; only do if no caller relies on the echoed return. Trivial otherwise.

src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/LyndonFact.summary: Inner Duval loop reloads s[k] and s[j] and recomputes nothing reducible; already optimal O(n), but the s[k]<=s[j] then s[k]<s[j] does two compares where one branchless update suffices.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/LyndonFact.currentCost: Inner loop: while (s[k]<=s[j]) { if (s[k]<s[j]) k=i; else k++; j++; }. This loads s[k] and s[j] twice (once for <=, once for <). Two comparisons of the same pair per iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/LyndonFact.proposedChange: Load both once: byte sk = s[k], sj = s[j]; if (sk > sj) break;-style restructure, or: int cmp = sk - sj; then k = cmp < 0 ? i : k+1; with the loop guard on cmp<=0. This loads each byte once and reuses the comparison result, halving the byte loads in the hot inner loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/LyndonFact.rationale: Removes one redundant byte load and one redundant comparison per inner iteration of the Duval scan; the comparison result is reused for both the loop condition and the k-update branch.
src/IAFahim.String.Palindrome/LyndonFact.risk: None; s[k] and s[j] are unchanged between the two original comparisons, so caching them is equivalent. Keep the k=i vs k++ branch (data-dependent, hard to make branchless cheaply).

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.summary: Replace the jagged bool*** triple-pointer DP table with a single flat bool[n*n*256] allocation.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.currentCost: n*n separate AllocHGlobal calls (each 256 bytes) plus n AllocHGlobal for the row pointer arrays plus 1 for the top array = n^2 + n + 1 heap allocations and the same number of frees. Every dp[i][j][s] access is a triple pointer-chase (3 dependent loads) which serializes and thrashes cache; the inner production loop does dp[i][k][left] and dp[k+1][j][right] each costing 3 chained loads.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.proposedChange: Allocate one block: bool* dp = (bool*)Marshal.AllocHGlobal((long)n*n*256); index as dp[((i*n)+j)*256 + s]. Free with a single FreeHGlobal. Precompute row base offsets (i*n+j)*256 once per cell.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.rationale: Collapses O(n^2) allocations to 1, eliminating malloc/free overhead and pointer-array storage (n^2 pointers + n pointers of 8 bytes each = ~8*n^2 extra bytes). Triple dependent load becomes a single base+offset computed load, shortening the dependency chain in the hottest inner loop (4 nested loops) and giving contiguous, cache/vectorizer-friendly memory.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.risk: n*n*256 can overflow int; use long for the byte count and size_t-style nint indexing. Behavior identical for valid inputs. Semantics preserved exactly.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.summary: Hoist production-table field loads out of the innermost (i,k,p) loops by precomputing left/mid/right per production once.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.currentCost: left=productions[p*3], mid=productions[p*3+1], right=productions[p*3+2] are reloaded for every (i,k) pair inside the O(n^3 * prodCount) loop. The p*3 multiply and three loads repeat n^3 times per production.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.proposedChange: Iterate productions in the inner loop but read productions[] via a precomputed pointer (prod = productions + p*3; left=prod[0]; mid=prod[1]; right=prod[2]) and consider restructuring so the (i,k) loops sit inside the p loop only where it helps; at minimum compute the p*3 base once and reuse. Combined with the flat dp array, dp[i][k][left] base for row (i,k) is loop-invariant across p and can be hoisted to a pointer rowIK = dp + ((i*n+k)*256).
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.rationale: Removes a multiply and converts three indexed loads into pointer-relative loads; hoisting the (i,k) and (k+1,j) row base pointers out of the p loop turns two 3-term address computations per production into one add per production. Fewer integer ops in the tightest loop of an O(n^3) algorithm.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.risk: None; pure reassociation of address arithmetic. Output identical.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.summary: The 256-wide variable axis assumes nonterminal ids < 256 but uses a full byte-per-bool dense array; pack into bitset or use the actual variable count.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.currentCost: Each cell stores 256 bytes regardless of how many nonterminals exist; total n*n*256 bytes. Inner loop zero-inits 256 bools per diagonal cell.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.proposedChange: If the grammar variable count V is known/passable, size the third axis to V instead of 256, or pack booleans into a ulong bitset (256 bits = 32 bytes, 8x smaller). Bitset also enables testing dp[i][k][left] via (word >> bit)&1 and lets the production loop be partially vectorized.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.rationale: 8x smaller working set (32 vs 256 bytes/cell) dramatically lowers cache pressure for the O(n^2) table; fewer bytes to zero-init. Better fit in L1/L2 for medium n.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.risk: Requires variable-id range guarantee (<256) which the code already assumes via the literal 256. Bitset indexing must use unsigned shifts. API may need a variable-count parameter to be fully safe; otherwise keep 256-bit bitset.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.summary: Drop the redundant explicit zero-init of diagonal cells when the allocation can be zeroed in bulk.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.currentCost: Inner loop `for (int s=0;s<256;s++) dp[i][i][s]=false;` runs n*256 stores; off-diagonal cells are never explicitly zeroed and rely on... actually they ARE only written true, so they need zeroing too.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.proposedChange: After a single flat AllocHGlobal, memset the whole block to 0 once (e.g. Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned / a tight loop) instead of per-cell loops. This both fixes the latent correctness assumption (off-diagonal cells must start false) and replaces scattered zeroing with one linear pass the prefetcher/vectorizer handles well.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.rationale: One contiguous zeroing pass is faster than scattered per-cell loops and is auto-vectorizable; removes the per-diagonal 256-store loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Parsing.cs.risk: Must ensure ALL cells are zeroed (current code only zeroes diagonal explicitly; off-diagonal correctness depends on AllocHGlobal not zeroing — bulk memset makes it correct and explicit). Verify no cell is read before being conditionally set.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.summary: maxStates = len*ruleCount*4 over-allocates the column dimension; the S buffer is (len*ruleCount*4)*(len+1)*12 bytes which is O(len^2) and frequently huge.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.currentCost: byteCount = len*ruleCount*4 * (len+1) * sizeof(State)=12. For len=1000, ruleCount=50 that is 200000*1001*12 ~ 2.4 GB single allocation — impractical on mobile and mostly untouched memory.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.proposedChange: Per Earley theory the number of states in any column is bounded by ruleCount*(maxRuleLen+1), independent of len. Cap maxStates at a grammar-derived bound (e.g. ruleCount * (maxDot+1) or a passed capacity) rather than scaling by len. Keep counts[] guards as-is.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.rationale: Reduces allocation from O(len^2 * ruleCount) to O(len * ruleCount * constant), an asymptotic memory reduction. Smaller footprint = fewer page faults, fits mobile.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.risk: Must not under-size: the bound must hold for the grammar. Since rules here have a fixed 3-int layout (single RHS slot per dot via rule*3+dot+1), dot is small; a safe cap needs the max RHS length. State as required guard: cap must be >= max states per column for the given grammar.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.summary: Hoist the k*maxStates row base and counts[k] into locals inside the main scan loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.currentCost: Each iteration recomputes k*maxStates + i three times (lines 36-38) and re-reads counts[k] as the loop bound and counts[k]++ inside the predictor; the predictor also recomputes k*maxStates+counts[k] four times per added state.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.proposedChange: Compute int baseK = k*maxStates once per k; use State* row = S + baseK; read fields via row[i]. In the predictor, cache int c = counts[k] and write row[c] fields then store counts[k]=c after the loop (re-reading length each iter is required since it grows, but the multiply k*maxStates is invariant).
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.rationale: Removes repeated k*maxStates multiplies (a multiply + add per access) from the hot scan; converts 3 indexed struct loads into pointer-relative loads with a shared base. Fewer integer ops and a shorter address-dependency chain.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.risk: counts[k] grows during the predictor loop (states added to same column), so the loop bound i<counts[k] must keep re-reading counts[k]; only the k*maxStates base is invariant. Preserve that re-read. Otherwise identical.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.summary: The predictor scans all ruleCount rules to find rules whose LHS == symbol; this O(ruleCount) per prediction can be an index lookup.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.currentCost: For every state whose next symbol is a nonterminal (>=256), the inner loop iterates all ruleCount rules testing rules[r*3]==symbol. Total predictor work is O(states * ruleCount).
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.proposedChange: Precompute (once, or caller-provided) a CSR-style index mapping nonterminal symbol -> list of rule ids with that LHS (start offsets + flat rule-id array). Predictor then iterates only the matching rules.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.rationale: Reduces predictor from O(ruleCount) per call to O(rulesForThatLHS), lowering total from O(S*R) toward O(S * avgRulesPerLHS). Asymptotic win for grammars with many rules.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.risk: Requires an auxiliary index structure (extra allocation or an added parameter). Behavior identical. Also de-dup of predicted states is still absent (already not done), so no semantic change.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.summary: State struct (3 ints = 12 bytes) can be narrowed and the counts init loop replaced with a bulk zero.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.currentCost: counts init is a scalar loop `for i<=len counts[i]=0`. State holds three 32-bit ints even though Dot and often Rule/Origin are small.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.proposedChange: Zero counts via Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned over (len+1)*4 bytes. If rule/dot/origin ranges permit, pack State into smaller fields (e.g. Dot as short) and add [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential, Pack=...)] — but only if provably within range.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.rationale: Bulk zero is vectorizable; narrower State shrinks the O(len^2) S buffer proportionally, improving cache behavior.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/Earley.cs.risk: Narrowing fields needs proven bounds on rule/dot/origin (origin up to len can exceed short for len>32767). Keep ints unless bounds known. Bulk zero of counts is always safe.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.summary: The per-rule `int* rhs = stackalloc int[rhsLen]` inside the while loop stack-allocates repeatedly in a loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.currentCost: stackalloc inside a loop body: in C# the stack space is not freed until method return, so each iteration grows the frame — effectively unbounded stack growth proportional to number of expansions, risking stack overflow and defeating the bounded-frame assumption. The rhs copy is also redundant.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.proposedChange: Eliminate the rhs temporary entirely: push directly from the table in reverse order: for (int i = rhsLen-1; i>=0; i--) stack[top++] = table[rhsStart + i]. No stackalloc, no copy.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.rationale: Removes a stackalloc-in-loop (potential unbounded frame growth and stack overflow) and an O(rhsLen) copy pass per expansion. Burst/JIT will not hoist a loop-body stackalloc, so this is a real frame-size and cycle win.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.risk: None — table[rhsStart+i] is read in the same reverse order the copy produced; observable behavior identical. Strictly safer.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.summary: AggressiveInlining on a method containing stackalloc and an unbounded parse loop is unlikely to help and may bloat callers.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.currentCost: [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] on a large method with stackalloc; inlining a stackalloc into the caller can enlarge the caller frame and is often ignored by the JIT/Burst for big bodies.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.proposedChange: Drop AggressiveInlining here (keep it on genuine hot leaf methods like SuffixOracle.Contains). After removing the in-loop stackalloc, the remaining stackalloc[len*2+2] is the only frame allocation.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.rationale: Avoids code-size bloat at call sites and misleading intent; inlining a top-level parser entry point rarely pays off. Keeps Burst codegen focused.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LlParse.cs.risk: Purely an attribute change; no semantic effect. Verify no caller relied on inlining for a measured win (none expected for an entry point).

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.summary: Module-global mutable static pointer state makes Build/Contains non-reentrant, non-thread-safe, and leaks the prior allocation on re-Build.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.currentCost: Six mutable statics; calling Build twice overwrites _link/_len/_trans without freeing the previous AllocHGlobal (memory leak), and concurrent Build/Contains race. No Free method exists at all — every Build leaks three native blocks.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.proposedChange: Introduce an unmanaged `Oracle` struct holding the pointers and sizes; Build returns/initializes it, Contains takes it by pointer/ref. Add a Free(ref Oracle) that releases the three blocks. This matches the house unmanaged-struct convention and removes hidden global state.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.rationale: Makes the API pure/reentrant/deterministic and plugs a guaranteed native memory leak on repeated Build. No per-call cost change; structurally enables multiple oracles and Burst function-pointer use without shared statics.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.risk: API signature change (Build/Contains gain an Oracle parameter). Behavior of a single Build+Contains sequence is identical. Callers must be updated; add Free to release memory.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.summary: The _trans init loop writes states*sigma ints to -1 scalarly; clone copy and Extend loops index with repeated p*_sigma multiplies.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.currentCost: Init: `for i<states*sigma _trans[i]=-1` is a scalar store loop. In Extend, `_trans[p*_sigma + c]` recomputes p*_sigma multiple times per while iteration; the clone copy loops `_trans[clone*_sigma+i]` / `_trans[q*_sigma+i]` recompute the base each iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.proposedChange: Hoist row bases: int* pRow = _trans + p*_sigma; reuse pRow[c]. For the clone copy use int* dst = _trans + clone*_sigma, src = _trans + q*_sigma and copy via a pointer loop (or Unsafe.CopyBlock since both are int rows of _sigma). For init, fill -1 in a vectorizable manner.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.rationale: Removes repeated multiplies from the SAM construction inner loops and turns the clone copy into a contiguous block copy that Burst can vectorize. Net fewer integer ops and better memory throughput during Build.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.risk: None functionally; pure address-arithmetic hoisting. Block-copy of _sigma ints is equivalent to the elementwise loop.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.summary: Hoist _sigma and _trans into locals to avoid reloading mutable statics each iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.currentCost: Inside the loop `v = _trans[v*_sigma + pattern[i]]` reads two statics (_trans, _sigma) every iteration; since they are static fields the JIT may reload them (cannot prove they don't change).
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.proposedChange: int sigma = _sigma; int* trans = _trans; before the loop, then v = trans[v*sigma + pattern[i]].
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.rationale: Caches static-field loads in registers, removing two memory loads per pattern character and enabling the multiply to use a register operand. Tightens the dependency chain of the match loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/SuffixOracle.cs.risk: Safe because Contains does not mutate these statics; values are loop-invariant. If the struct refactor (above) lands, this becomes reading struct fields once.

src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LrParse.cs.summary: Cache state via top-1 read and avoid recomputing state*symbolCount; already tight but minor hoist possible.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LrParse.cs.currentCost: Each loop iteration computes stack[top-1] then state*symbolCount + (terminal+1). On a shift, the next iteration reloads stack[top-1] (the just-pushed value). Small redundancy.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LrParse.cs.proposedChange: Keep the current top-of-stack state in a local `int state` and update it on shift (state = action.Target) and on reduce (state = gotos[...]) instead of re-reading stack[top-1] each iteration. The stack still records states for reduce pops.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LrParse.cs.rationale: Eliminates one dependent load (stack[top-1]) per LR step, shortening the per-token critical path in the hot driver loop.
src/IAFahim.String.Parse/LrParse.cs.risk: On reduce, after `top -= rhsLen`, the new top state is stack[top-1] which must be re-read (it is older, not tracked) — so keep that read on the reduce path; only the shift path benefits from the cached local. Ensure state local is refreshed correctly on both paths to preserve semantics.

src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.summary: Iterate only set bits of activeMask instead of scanning all 32 bit positions, and hoist the per-bit work out of the wasted iterations.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.currentCost: The outer loop runs a fixed 32 iterations regardless of how many patterns sets are active; each does a (1<<bit) shift and a branch. When only a few doubling-levels are active (typical: log2(numPatterns) <= ~20 active bits, often far fewer), most of the 32 iterations are pure branch overhead.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.proposedChange: Replace `for (int bit=0; bit<32; bit++){ if((activeMask&(1<<bit))!=0){...}}` with a popcount-style walk over set bits: `int m = activeMask; while (m != 0){ int bit = math.tzcnt(m) (or Unity Burst intrinsic / De Bruijn); m &= m-1; int u = roots[bit]; ... }`. This visits exactly popcount(activeMask) levels with no shift/AND per skipped slot.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.rationale: Reduces outer-loop trip count from constant 32 to popcount(activeMask), removing wasted branch+shift work. `m &= m-1` clears the lowest set bit branchlessly; tzcnt is a single instruction under Burst. Inner per-character work is unchanged so the asymptotic text scan cost is identical, but constant overhead per query drops.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.risk: Behavior-identical: same set of roots processed, order of summation into totalMatches is commutative (long addition), no overflow change. Must ensure tzcnt/De Bruijn handles only nonzero m (loop guard m!=0 guarantees it).

src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.summary: Hoist baseChar into a local and strength-reduce the per-character dependency chain; consider passing/using a row pointer base to cut the `u * sigma` multiply.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.currentCost: Inner loop body `int c = text[i]-baseChar; u = nexts[u*sigma+c]; totalMatches += counts[u];` has a multiply `u*sigma` on the serial dependency chain (each u depends on the previous load). With sigma=26 (non-power-of-two) this is a real IMUL feeding directly into the load address, lengthening the loop-carried latency.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.proposedChange: Compute the row base once per step: `int* row = nexts + u*sigma; u = row[c];`. This does not remove the multiply but lets the compiler fold it into the load's addressing (base+index*1) and keeps c off the multiply path. Alternatively, if a row-major layout with a precomputed `int* nextRow = nexts + u*sigma` stored per node were available it would eliminate the multiply entirely, but within current layout the framing as `nexts + u*sigma` plus `[c]` is the cleanest hint to the JIT/Burst address generator.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.rationale: `u*sigma` is loop-carried (u from previous iteration). Expressing the access as a pointer add + scaled index helps Burst emit a single addressing-mode load and overlaps the `counts[u]` load. The text[i]-baseChar subtraction is independent of u and can be computed ahead. Net: shorter critical path per character.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.risk: Semantics identical (same index arithmetic). No bounds change. Only an addressing-form hint; if Burst already does this the win is zero, so impact is medium not high.

src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.summary: Cache `nexts[u*sigma+c]` index once instead of recomputing `u*sigma+c` three times per trie-descent step.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.currentCost: Lines 34/40/42: the expression `nexts[u * sigma + c]` (i.e. the index `u*sigma+c`) is evaluated up to 3 times in one iteration — twice in the `if` condition (34) and again on line 42, plus the store on 40. Each is a multiply + add and a separate load.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.proposedChange: Compute `int idx = u*sigma + c;` once, load `int cur = nexts[idx];` once, then test `if (cur == root || cur == 0){ ... nexts[idx] = v; cur = v; } u = cur;`. This collapses three index computations and up to two reloads to a single index calc and load.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.rationale: Removes redundant IMUL+add and redundant memory loads of the same cell on the build hot path. The cell value can't change between the test and the use except via the store we control, so one load suffices.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.risk: Behavior-identical. The original re-reads nexts[idx] on line 42 after possibly storing v on line 40; the rewrite assigns cur=v in that branch so u gets the same value. No aliasing concern since idx is a single fixed cell.

src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.summary: Fuse the node-initialization loop with the structure by hoisting `root*sigma`, `u*sigma`, `v*sigma` base pointers; also reuse a single `1<<bit` value.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.currentCost: Lines 24, 37 init loops compute `root*sigma+i` / `v*sigma+k` inside the loop (multiply hoistable to a base add). Lines 18/20/77 recompute `1<<bit` multiple times. The fail-link BFS (50-74) recomputes `u*sigma+i`, `fails[u]*sigma+i`, `nexts[root*sigma+i]` repeatedly.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.proposedChange: Hoist `int rootBase = root*sigma;` and iterate `int* rrow = nexts+rootBase;` filling `rrow[i]=root`. In the create branch use `int* vrow = nexts + v*sigma;` for the fill. In BFS hoist `int uBase=u*sigma; int fBase=fails[u]*sigma;` once per node so `nexts[u*sigma+i]` becomes `urow[i]` and `nexts[fails[u]*sigma+i]` becomes `frow[i]`. Compute `int onebit = 1<<bit;` once and reuse on lines 20 and 77.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.rationale: Each multiply hoisted out of a sigma-length inner loop saves sigma-1 multiplies per node. fails[u] is loaded once per node instead of sigma times. These are constant-factor wins over the whole trie (O(total nodes * sigma)).
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.risk: Semantics identical — pure loop-invariant code motion. fails[u] is not modified inside the i-loop of the BFS body (only fails of children are written), so hoisting fBase=fails[u]*sigma is safe.

src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.summary: `int* q = stackalloc int[nodeCount - root + 1]` sizes the BFS queue to the global node count delta but the queue only needs the nodes in THIS level's trie; verify and tighten to avoid large stack frames on mobile.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.currentCost: After the trie-build, nodeCount-root+1 equals exactly the number of nodes created in this Insert (root was ++nodeCount before the build, nodeCount after). That is correct and tight here, so the size is fine — but note this stackalloc grows with the merged-level pattern-set size (up to total length of all patterns in the doubling group). On a deep merge (largest bit) this can be a large stack allocation on mobile.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.proposedChange: Document the worst-case bound (sum of pattern lengths in the largest doubling group) so callers can budget stack; or accept an external scratch buffer pointer (Try*/Run convention) instead of stackalloc so the queue memory is caller-controlled and reusable across inserts, eliminating per-call stack-frame growth and stack-overflow risk on mobile for large pattern sets.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.rationale: Burst/mobile stacks are limited; a stackalloc whose size scales with input can overflow. Passing a reusable scratch pointer removes the unbounded stack frame and avoids re-zeroing/realloc per call.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.risk: Changing the signature to take a scratch buffer is an API/ergonomics change (breaking). The stackalloc itself is correctly sized; this is a robustness/RAM-locality note, hence low impact. No correctness bug in current code.

src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.summary: Add [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] is already imported but unused; mark hot leaf accessors / keep Run non-inlined but ensure the per-char step can inline. Also follow Try*/Run naming consistently (Build.Insert vs Query.Run).
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.currentCost: `using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;` is imported but no [MethodImpl] attributes are applied. Run is the hot entry; Insert is named Insert not Run despite both being the public 'do-it' methods, a minor API inconsistency.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.proposedChange: Either remove the unused CompilerServices using, or apply [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] where a small helper is extracted (e.g. a step function). For API consistency consider AhoPersistentBuild.Run mirroring AhoPersistentQuery.Run, or document why Insert keeps its name.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.rationale: Removes a dead import (clarity) and aligns with the house Run convention, improving discoverability without affecting the perf model.
src/IAFahim.String.Pattern/AhoPersistent.risk: None functionally. Naming change would be source-breaking for callers, so treat as optional/low.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.summary: Replace Marshal.AllocHGlobal/FreeHGlobal scratch stack with stackalloc or a caller-provided buffer to make the method Burst-compatible and allocation-free.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.currentCost: Two P/Invoke transitions per call (AllocHGlobal + FreeHGlobal) plus a heap allocation of (n+1)*4 bytes. Marshal.* are managed interop calls that Burst cannot compile, so the whole method falls off the Burst-compiled path; on mobile the per-call malloc/free is a real cost in any locate/build loop.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.proposedChange: Either accept an `int* stack` scratch buffer parameter sized n+1 like SuffixArray.Build does for its scratch arrays, or `int* stack = stackalloc int[n + 1];` when n is provably bounded. Drop the Marshal calls entirely. This matches the house pattern (raw pointers / stackalloc, no managed APIs).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.rationale: Eliminates two interop calls and a heap allocation per invocation, and removes the only thing preventing Burst from compiling this function. Stack/scratch reuse keeps the working set hot in cache.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.risk: stackalloc requires n bounded to avoid stack overflow; for unbounded n prefer the caller-buffer form (consistent with the rest of the module). Behavior is identical since the stack is purely internal scratch.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.summary: Dead branch: `int prevLcp = i < n ? lcp[i] : 0;` always takes the true side because i ranges over [1, n).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.currentCost: A redundant compare-and-select per loop iteration computing a condition that is invariably true inside `for (int i = 1; i < n; i++)`.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.proposedChange: Replace with `int prevLcp = lcp[i];` (drop the ternary). Removes one branch/cmov per iteration.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.rationale: Fewer instructions in the inner loop; the condition `i < n` is a loop invariant guaranteed true by the loop bound, so the select is pure overhead.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.risk: None — i is strictly less than n for every iteration, so the value is unchanged. (Note: the surrounding tree-building logic never links Child/Sibling and never pushes the popped parents; that is a correctness concern, not part of this perf pass, but flagging since the scratch-stack churn may be masking it.)

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.summary: The rank-clear loop writes 2*len entries to -1, but the first len are unconditionally overwritten on the next line; only the sentinel half [len, 2*len) needs clearing.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.currentCost: len redundant stores: `for (i in 0..2*len) rank[i] = -1` then `for (i in 0..len) rank[i] = ptr[i]` rewrites the lower half. That is len wasted writes plus the dirtied cache lines.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.proposedChange: Clear only the sentinel region: `for (int i = len; i < len * 2; i++) rank[i] = -1;`. The lower half is fully initialized by the subsequent `rank[i] = ptr[i]` loop.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.rationale: Halves the store traffic of the clear and avoids touching/dirtying cache lines that are immediately rewritten, lowering memory bandwidth — meaningful for large len on mobile.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.risk: None for valid input: every rank[0..len) is assigned ptr[i] before any read. The +h sentinel reads (rank[sa[i]+h]) only index into [len, 2*len), which is still cleared. Requires rank buffer length >= 2*len, which the existing code already assumes.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.summary: The trailing `for (i) rank[i] = tmpRank[i]` full copy can be eliminated by ping-ponging the rank and tmpRank buffers across doubling rounds.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.currentCost: O(len) copy every doubling round (~log len rounds), i.e. an extra len*log(len) stores plus a full second buffer read each round, purely to move the new ranks back into `rank`.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.proposedChange: Have Build swap the `rank`/`tmpRank` pointers after UpdateRank instead of copying, and write the new ranks into tmpRank (already done). On loop exit ensure `rank` points at the final buffer (one conditional copy or swap-count parity fixup at the end). Keep SortByRank reading from whichever pointer currently holds the live ranks.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.rationale: Removes a full O(len) pass per round, turning ~log(len) memcpys into pointer swaps. Reduces both instruction count and L1/L2 traffic on the hottest loop of the construction.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/SuffixArr.risk: Caller-visible: which physical buffer holds the result changes per parity. Must guarantee on exit that `rank` (the buffer the caller expects to read) holds the final ranks — do a single final copy if the swap parity left them in tmpRank, or document the parity. Use Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned for the final copy. Semantics preserved as long as the final ranks land in the caller's rank buffer.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.summary: rightSize is computed via GetSize(node->Right) after rightHash already dereferenced node->Right; redundant null-check and field reload.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.currentCost: GetSize(node->Right) reloads node->Right and re-tests it for null even though GetHash(node->Right) just did the same dereference; an extra load + branch on the hottest treap primitive (Pull runs on every Split/Merge step).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.proposedChange: Hoist the right pointer once: `DynamicStringNode* r = node->Right; ulong rightHash = r == null ? 0 : r->Hash; int rightSize = r == null ? 0 : r->Size;` and likewise cache node->Left for GetSize(node->Left). Lets the compiler share the single null test.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.rationale: Pull is called on every treap rotation/split/merge; shaving a redundant pointer load and branch per call compounds over O(log n) recursion per operation. Caching the child pointer also shortens the dependency chain feeding the Hash multiply.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.risk: None — single-threaded treap, node->Left/Right are not mutated between the reads within Pull. Same arithmetic, same result.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.summary: The `mid == 0` special-case is re-tested every binary-search iteration though it can only fire when low==0; restructure so the loop never evaluates mid==0.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.currentCost: Per iteration: a branch `if (mid == 0)` plus a `continue` that wastes the whole iteration when it fires. More importantly each non-trivial iteration does TWO full O(log n) GetSubstringHash calls (each = two Splits + two Merges + Pull chain), so the binary search itself is the cost driver.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.proposedChange: Start the search at low=1 (lcp of length 0 always matches, ans stays 0 as the base case) so `mid` is never 0, removing the in-loop check and the wasted iteration. Additionally, hoist `int n = GetSize(root)` already done; consider caching that GetSubstringHash(i..i+mid-1) shares prefixes across iterations — but at minimum drop the mid==0 guard.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.rationale: Removes a per-iteration branch and an entirely wasted loop iteration (when mid==0 it just sets low=1 and recomputes). Fewer treap traversals directly cut the dominant cost since each iteration triggers four Split/Merge passes.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.risk: Must preserve ans=0 when no common prefix: initializing ans=0 and low=1 keeps that base case. high=Min(n-i,n-j) bound unchanged. Behavior identical for all i,j.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.summary: Each Lcp binary-search step calls GetSubstringHash, which Splits the treap out and Merges it back (O(log n) restructuring with Pull on every node) — O(log^2 n) treap mutations per Lcp, and the splits churn the structure.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.currentCost: GetSubstringHash performs two Splits + two Merges (each O(log n) with a Pull allocation-free but pointer-rewriting chain) per call, called O(log n) times in the binary search => O(log^2 n) full treap rebuilds, mutating the tree repeatedly just to read a hash.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.proposedChange: Add a non-mutating range-hash query that walks the treap by accumulated subtree sizes and combines precomputed subtree hashes without Split/Merge (a read-only `RangeHash(root, l, r, powers)` using the stored Size/Hash fields). Use it inside Lcp/CompareSuffix instead of GetSubstringHash. Splits are only needed for Insert/Erase.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.rationale: Turns each hash query from O(log n) structural mutation into an O(log n) read-only descent with no pointer writes and no Pull recomputation, and removes the repeated tear-down/rebuild of the tree per binary-search step. Far fewer writes, better cache behavior, lower constant factor and no transient structural churn.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/DynamicSu.risk: Requires writing a correct order-statistics range-hash descent that reproduces GetSubstringHash's polynomial combination exactly (same BASE/powers convention). Must match the existing hash formula bit-for-bit to preserve CompareSuffix results. Higher implementation effort; verify against the Split-based version on a fuzz corpus.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.summary: After the binary search lands at l, a linear scan counts matching lcp entries, degrading to O(len) when the matching interval is large.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.currentCost: The `for (i = l; i < len; i++)` linear count can scan up to len entries when many suffixes share the prefix length, making the function O(len) instead of O(log len) for wide intervals.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.proposedChange: Replace the linear forward scan with a second binary search for the last index where lcp[i] >= queryLen, then return that index - l + 1 (mirroring the existing right-bound binary search). Both bounds become O(log len).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.rationale: Restores O(log len) worst case for the whole query; the current linear tail dominates for common-prefix-heavy data (e.g. repetitive text), which is exactly where suffix-array locate is used.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/LcpInterv.risk: Must reproduce the exact same count: the current loop counts contiguous entries from l with lcp>=queryLen, so the upper-bound binary search must use the identical comparison (>=) and inclusive bounds. Verify off-by-one against the loop on edge cases (l==len-1, all-match, none-match).

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/Locate.cs.summary: Math.Min(patLen, textLen - sa[mid]) is computed, then the result patLen <= textLen - sa[mid] re-derives the same comparison; fold into one branch.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/Locate.cs.currentCost: Per binary-search iteration: a Math.Min plus a redundant second comparison `patLen <= textLen - sa[mid]` that recomputes textLen - sa[mid] and re-compares against patLen.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/Locate.cs.proposedChange: Compute `int rem = textLen - sa[mid];` once, `int n = patLen < rem ? patLen : rem;` (branchless min), call Compare, and reuse `patLen <= rem` for the full-match test. Avoids recomputing textLen - sa[mid] and the Math.Min call overhead.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/Locate.cs.rationale: Cuts a duplicate subtraction and comparison per iteration of the O(log saLen * patLen) search and replaces Math.Min with an inlinable conditional Burst lowers to a cmov.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixArray/Locate.cs.risk: None — same values, same control flow. byte difference a[i]-b[i] already returns correct int sign for unsigned bytes.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.summary: Memoization dp is reset and fully recomputed on every CountSubstrings call, turning the outer Find loop into a quadratic/exponential blowup over states.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.currentCost: Find walks the suffix-link chain and for each of up to 256 transitions calls CountSubstrings, which (a) does an O(stateCount) reset of dp[i]=-1 and (b) recomputes the entire Dfs subtree from scratch. The substring counts are a fixed function of the automaton, so this recomputes identical values O(states*256) times. Each Find call therefore costs O(stateCount^2 * 256) or worse.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.proposedChange: Compute the dp[] count array ONCE before the Find loop (single Dfs over the DAG with the dp[i]=-1 sentinel), then in Find read cnt = dp[next] directly instead of calling CountSubstrings/resetting. Pass the already-populated dp in. Reset dp once at entry, not per-call.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.rationale: The count of substrings reachable from each state is invariant across the whole query; computing it once is O(states + edges) instead of O(states) per transition per chain node. Eliminates the redundant O(stateCount) memset and the repeated DAG traversals, dropping total cost by a factor of ~stateCount*256.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.risk: Semantics-preserving as long as dp is fully populated before first read; the existing -1 sentinel already guarantees each state is computed exactly once. No edge-case change. (Note: GetNext's pointer math assumes an inline 256-int transition table immediately after the first int of State, which does not match the {Link,Len,Head} layout in SuffixAutomaton.cs — flag separately as a likely pre-existing correctness bug, not part of this opt.)

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.summary: Dfs is unbounded recursion over the automaton DAG; deep chains risk stack overflow and Burst dislikes deep recursion on hot paths.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.currentCost: Recursion depth can reach stateCount (a long path automaton), one stack frame per state plus a 256-iteration loop each. Recursion also blocks some Burst optimizations and inlining.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.proposedChange: Convert Dfs to an explicit-stack iterative post-order over the DAG using the dp[] sentinel (already available as scratch) plus a small explicit int* worklist, computing counts bottom-up. Combine with the compute-once change above.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.rationale: Iterative traversal has bounded, caller-controlled memory, no per-call frame setup, and is more Burst/vectorizer friendly. Same asymptotic work, lower constant and no native-stack blowup.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.risk: Must preserve the exact +1 (empty/own contribution) accumulation per node and the DAG-memoized single visit. Need an explicit worklist buffer sized to stateCount; document it as caller-provided to stay within the no-managed-alloc constraint.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.summary: Inner transition probe loops c over all 256 codes calling GetNext even when most slots are empty.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.currentCost: For every chain node, 256 GetNext calls (each a pointer recompute + load) regardless of actual out-degree. Suffix-automaton states are typically sparse, so most of these 256 loads miss/return -1.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.proposedChange: Iterate actual outgoing edges via the linked Head/Next edge list (as SuffixAutomaton.GetNext already does) instead of dense c in [0,256). If lexicographic order by Char is required (it is, to satisfy 'k-th'), collect present (Char,To) pairs once and sort, or keep a per-state sorted edge order at build time.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.rationale: Replaces a fixed 256-iteration dense scan with iteration proportional to real out-degree, cutting both branch count and cache traffic. For sparse states this is a large constant-factor win.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.risk: Ordering matters: the k-th-substring result depends on ascending character order, so edges must be visited in ascending Char. The linked edge list is in insertion order, so a one-time sort or build-time ordering is required to preserve output semantics.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.summary: GetNext does IntPtr arithmetic with sizeof recomputed per call and is not inlined.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.currentCost: Each call recomputes v*sizeof(State)+sizeof(int) through IntPtr conversions; called 256x per chain node per query. No AggressiveInlining attribute.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.proposedChange: Add [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] and index via a typed pointer (e.g. ((int*)(state + v))[1 + c]) so the offset folds to a constant scale; better, fold it into the edge-list iteration from the previous item and delete this dense accessor.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.rationale: Inlining removes call overhead on a hot leaf; typed indexing lets the JIT/Burst emit a single scaled load instead of IntPtr add chains. Lower dependency-chain length per probe.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/KthSu.risk: Pointer/offset semantics must match the actual State memory layout; the current implementation assumes an inline transition array that the {Link,Len,Head} struct does not provide, so this accessor appears already inconsistent with the build format — verify layout before micro-tuning.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/LinkT.summary: Each popped node rescans all states to find children, making link-tree traversal O(stateCount^2).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/LinkT.currentCost: For every node popped (stateCount of them) the inner loop scans linkPtr[0..stateCount) to find i with linkPtr[i]==v. Total O(stateCount^2) loads and branches even though the link tree has exactly stateCount-1 edges.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/LinkT.proposedChange: Precompute a children adjacency in CSR form once: count children per parent (one pass over linkPtr), prefix-sum into head offsets, scatter child indices into a flat int* childBuf. Then traversal visits each node and iterates only its real children -> O(stateCount). Accept the two scratch buffers (childHead[stateCount+1], childBuf[stateCount]) as caller-provided pointers to honor the no-alloc rule.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/LinkT.rationale: Reduces traversal from O(n^2) to O(n) with two linear passes; for n in the thousands this is orders of magnitude fewer memory accesses and far better cache behavior (sequential CSR scans vs repeated full-array sweeps).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/LinkT.risk: Pure restructuring of iteration order; DFS visit set is identical. Visit ORDER changes (children grouped by parent rather than reverse-scan order) — if callback ordering is observable to callers, document it. Requires extra scratch buffers passed in by the caller.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Occur.summary: Same O(stateCount^2) child rescan as LinkTree, plus it stackallocs a per-call buffer and stores a constant value.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Occur.currentCost: For each popped node the inner loop scans all stateCount link entries to find children: O(stateCount^2). Also `int* stack = stackalloc int[stateCount]` allocates per call (fine but could be caller-provided), and `outPos[count++] = lenPtr[v]` stores lenPtr[v] which is guaranteed == targetLen inside the matching branch, so it always writes the constant targetLen.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Occur.proposedChange: Reuse the CSR children adjacency from the LinkTree fix to get O(stateCount) traversal. Take the stack/scratch as a caller-provided int* to remove the per-call stackalloc (matches LinkTree's signature convention and the library's no-hidden-alloc model). Write outPos[count++] = targetLen directly (or, more likely the intended semantic, write the state index v rather than lenPtr[v]).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Occur.rationale: O(n) instead of O(n^2) traversal; removing per-call stackalloc avoids stack-pointer adjustment and large frame growth for big automata. Writing the constant directly removes a redundant load.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Occur.risk: The current store outPos[count++]=lenPtr[v] only ever records targetLen repeated count times, which looks like a bug (occurrence *positions* should be state ids / end positions). Changing the stored value would alter observable output, so treat the value fix as a correctness question to confirm with the caller, separate from the O(n)->traversal optimization which is behavior-preserving on the count return.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Lexic.summary: Brute-force enumerates all O(n^2) substrings counting duplicates; defeats the entire point of having a suffix automaton in this module.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Lexic.currentCost: Double loop over (len, start) counts every substring occurrence including duplicates up to k, O(n^2) work and counting with multiplicity rather than distinct substrings. For the k-th DISTINCT substring this is also semantically different from an automaton-based answer.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Lexic.proposedChange: If the goal is the k-th lexicographically-smallest DISTINCT substring, walk the suffix automaton transitions in ascending character order using the per-state distinct-substring counts (the same dp[] count machinery in KthSubstring), emitting characters greedily — O(answer length * sigma) instead of O(n^2). If duplicates are intentionally counted, at minimum break out of the outer len loop early once count would exceed achievable totals, and reuse the automaton rather than the raw text.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Lexic.rationale: Automaton-driven k-th-substring is linear in the output length, not quadratic in input length; it also dedups naturally. This both fixes asymptotics and aligns the function with the module's data structure.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Lexic.risk: Distinct-vs-multiplicity is an observable semantic choice: the current code counts WITH multiplicity, an automaton counts DISTINCT. Switching changes outputs, so confirm intended definition before replacing. If multiplicity is required as-is, only the early-exit micro-opts apply (behavior-preserving).

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Gener.summary: Inner copy loop reloads lengths[i] and strings[i] each iteration and does scalar element copies that could be hoisted/widened.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Gener.currentCost: `for (j; j<lengths[i]; j++) intText[pos++]=strings[i][j]` re-reads lengths[i] (bounds the loop) and indexes strings[i] each iteration; widening byte->int is inherently scalar here but the base pointer and length are loop-invariant and reloaded.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Gener.proposedChange: Hoist `int len = lengths[i]; byte* s = strings[i]; int* dst = intText + pos;` before the inner loop, copy with `for (j=0;j<len;j++) dst[j]=s[j];` then advance pos += len. This gives the JIT/Burst a clean invariant base+count loop it can vectorize (byte->int widening unpack).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Gener.rationale: Removes repeated indirect loads of lengths[i]/strings[i] from the dependency chain and exposes a contiguous widening copy that Burst can SIMD-vectorize, instead of a pos-carried scalar store chain.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Gener.risk: None — identical output. Pure loop-invariant hoisting and induction-variable cleanup; pos arithmetic stays equivalent.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.summary: Eliminate the redundant GetNext recomputation at line 65 by reusing the transition value already found by the loop's exit condition.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.currentCost: The first while loop (line 53) calls GetNext(st,e,p,c) every iteration. When it exits (p!=-1 branch), line 65 calls GetNext(st,e,p,c) a SECOND time over the same (p,c) to obtain q. GetNext is an O(deg(p)) linked-list scan, so this doubles the scan cost on the state that exits the loop — paid on every Extend that takes the else branch (the common case for a new transition that already exists).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.proposedChange: Restructure the loop to compute the transition once per iteration into a local: 'int nx; while (p != -1 && (nx = GetNext(st,e,p,c)) == -1) { SetNext(...); p = st[p].Link; }'. Then in the else branch use that captured 'nx' as q instead of calling GetNext again ('int q = nx;'). Because the loop exits precisely when GetNext(p,c) != -1, the last captured nx equals the q that line 65 would recompute — identical value, one fewer scan.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.rationale: Removes one full edge-list traversal per Extend call along the suffix-link chain transition lookup; halves GetNext work for the hot else-path. Same arithmetic and control flow otherwise, so output is bit-identical.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.risk: Must ensure 'nx' is only read in the branch where p != -1 (where it is guaranteed assigned to the non- -1 value). When p == -1 the loop ran GetNext on the last valid p before p became -1, so nx must not be used in the p==-1 branch (it already isn't). No semantic change.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.summary: The clone-redirect loop (line 77) re-scans the full edge list of each p via GetNext just to compare against the known q.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.currentCost: Inside 'while (p != -1 && GetNext(st,e,p,c) == q)' each iteration scans p's entire edge linked list to find the (p,c) transition, then compares To against q. Since SetNext prepends, and we only follow links while the transition still equals q, this repeats an O(deg) scan per chain step where a direct edge-node lookup would suffice.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.proposedChange: Introduce a helper GetNextEdge(st,e,p,c) returning the edge index (not the To). Walk the chain by locating the edge once, reading e[edge].To to test == q, and if so rewrite e[edge].To = clone IN PLACE instead of SetNext prepending a new shadowing edge. This both avoids the recompute and stops growing the edge array (no new edges appended in the redirect loop), shrinking edgeCount growth and the per-state list length scanned by all future GetNext calls.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.rationale: In-place To rewrite is O(deg) once per chain node and removes the append, so subsequent GetNext scans over these states stay shorter (lower constant on every later transition lookup and less edge RAM). Standard SAM clone-redirect rewrites the existing edge rather than shadowing it.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.risk: Behavior-preserving ONLY if every reader resolves a transition via first-match on the prepended list. Current GetNext returns the FIRST matching edge; SetNext prepends, so a shadowing edge currently overrides the old one and GetNext already returns the new target — so in-place rewrite yields the same observed transition. EnumerateTransitions, however, currently emits BOTH the stale and new edge (duplicate char) after a redirect; switching to in-place rewrite changes EnumerateTransitions output (removes the duplicate). If any caller depends on seeing duplicate chars, this is observable — verify EnumerateTransitions contract before applying. If kept conservative (recompute avoided but still SetNext-prepend), only the cycles win applies with zero observable change.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.summary: Edge is 12 bytes (3x int); Char and the index fields could be narrowed to shrink the edge array footprint and improve cache density of GetNext scans.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.currentCost: Each Edge is 12 bytes. GetNext is a pointer-chasing linked-list walk whose cost is dominated by cache misses across the edge array; larger nodes mean fewer edges per cache line. For a SAM over a small alphabet (e.g. byte/char input), Char never needs 32 bits.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.proposedChange: If alphabet fits in 16 bits, change Edge.Char to short/ushort. To/Next remain int (state and edge counts can exceed 65535). With explicit [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] and ordering {int To; int Next; short Char;} the struct packs to 12 (still padded) — the real win requires also narrowing index types, so only adopt if the index domain is provably <=2^16 or accept To/Next stay int. Alternatively, store transitions in a parallel SoA (separate To[]/Char[]/Next[] arrays) so a GetNext scan touches only the Char[] and Next[] streams, not To, until a match.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.rationale: Narrower Char and SoA splitting reduce bytes touched per linked-list hop, lowering cache-miss pressure in the hottest inner loop (GetNext) on both PC and mobile where memory bandwidth is the bottleneck.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.risk: Narrowing Char to 16 bits breaks correctness if alphabet exceeds 65535 (e.g. full int code points) — only safe with a documented alphabet bound. SoA changes the public struct API (Edge no longer the storage unit), an ergonomics/compat break; flag and confirm no external dependency on the Edge layout. Default to no-change unless the alphabet bound is confirmed.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.summary: The 'using System;' directive is unused in this file.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.currentCost: Dead using directive: no System type is referenced (only System.Runtime.CompilerServices.MethodImpl is used). Zero runtime cost but adds noise and can mask accidental dependencies.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.rationale: Cleaner compilation unit, no behavioral impact; keeps the file minimal and makes the actual dependency surface explicit.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.risk: None — purely cosmetic; verify no source-generator or partial file in the same namespace relies on the transitively-imported namespace (it does not here).

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.summary: Transition lookup is O(deg(state)) linked-list scan; for large/dense alphabets a different transition representation lowers asymptotics, at a RAM cost.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.currentCost: GetNext/Transition/Contains all do a per-state singly-linked edge scan, so a single transition query is O(out-degree), and Build's Extend incurs O(sum of degrees) total — fine for sparse small alphabets but O(alphabet) worst case per query for dense states (especially the initial state which accumulates one edge per distinct first-character).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.proposedChange: Offer an alternative dense-transition mode: a fixed-size int[alphabetSize] transition table per state (state-major flat array trans[state*ALPHA + c]) selected when the alphabet is small and known. GetNext becomes O(1) array index instead of a list walk; Burst vectorizes nothing here but removes pointer chasing entirely. Keep the linked-list path as the sparse default.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.rationale: Converts the dominant inner-loop cost from O(deg) pointer-chasing with random cache misses to a single O(1) indexed load, a large constant-factor and worst-case asymptotic win for small alphabets (DNA, bytes). This is the standard SAM speed/memory tradeoff.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Suffi.risk: Dense table costs O(numStates * alphabetSize) RAM, prohibitive for large alphabets / int code points — must be gated on a small alphabet bound and is a new API surface (not a drop-in). Output identical (same transitions); only storage and lookup mechanism change. Treat as an additive variant, not a replacement, to preserve the existing sparse contract.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.summary: PushVersion takes a 'len' parameter that is completely ignored, and the Version struct it implies is never populated — dead/misleading API.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.currentCost: PushVersion(int* roots, ref int versionCount, int root, int len) writes only roots[versionCount++] = root; the 'len' argument is silently discarded. The Version struct (Root, Len) is declared but never stored or returned, so callers pass len believing it is recorded. This is a correctness/ergonomics hazard, not a perf cost.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.proposedChange: Either (a) remove the unused 'len' parameter and the Version struct if length-per-version is not a feature, or (b) actually store versions as Version*/SoA so GetVersion can return both Root and Len. Pick one to make the API honest. Current signature should not advertise a parameter it drops.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.rationale: Removes a silently-ignored argument that callers pay to compute and pass for no effect; makes the persistent-SAM version API self-consistent. No hot loop here, but it eliminates wasted argument setup and a misleading contract.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.risk: Changing the public signature is a source-break for any external caller. Grep of src shows no in-repo callers of PushVersion/GetVersion, so internal break risk is nil; confirm no Unity-side consumer before removing the parameter.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.summary: Both using directives in PersistentSam.cs are unused.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.currentCost: Neither System nor System.Runtime.InteropServices is referenced — there is no StructLayout attribute or System type in the file. Dead directives.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.rationale: Cleaner unit, explicit dependency surface, zero behavioral change. If [StructLayout] was intended on the Version struct for blittable Burst layout, add it explicitly instead of leaving the unused import.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixAutomaton/Persi.risk: None functionally. If the Version struct is meant to be blittable across Burst boundaries, consider adding [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] explicitly (it is already sequential by default for this all-int struct, so no actual change needed).

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.summary: Edge.Min and Edge.Max are dead fields — written but never read; remove them to shrink Edge from 20 to 12 bytes.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.currentCost: Edge is 5 ints = 20 bytes. Build() writes edges[newEdge].Min = i and edges[newEdge].Max = len every insertion, but no code in the file (or struct consumer pattern) ever reads Min/Max. These are 2 dead stores per node insertion and 8 wasted bytes per edge in the edge array.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.proposedChange: Drop Min and Max from the Edge struct: 'public struct Edge { public int To; public int Char; public int Next; }'. Delete the corresponding edges[newEdge].Min = i; and edges[newEdge].Max = len; assignments on lines 48-49.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.rationale: Edge array shrinks 40% (20B -> 12B). The hot inner scan loop (lines 26-30) walks the Next linked list reading Char and Next; a 12-byte Edge packs ~5.3 edges per 64B cache line vs 3.2 today, cutting cache misses during the per-character edge scan that dominates Build cost. Also removes 2 stores/insertion.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.risk: Must confirm no external caller reads Edge.Min/Max — they are public fields. Within this file they are write-only. If Min/Max are part of a documented public API for downstream queries (substring offsets), removing them changes the API surface; in that case keep them but at minimum hoist them out of being recomputed. Given Min==edge insertion index i and Max==len are trivially derivable, they appear vestigial.
