src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.summary: Dead/unused locals: 'int c = s[i]' on line 19 is immediately overwritten, and activeEdge/activeLen (and effectively activeNode) are never used.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.currentCost: Line 19 'int c = s[i]' performs a load that is always overwritten by line 23 'c = s[i + added]' on the first iteration of the inner while (added==0, i+0<len is always true since i<len). activeEdge=-1 and activeLen=0 are declared and never read; activeNode is initialized to 0 and never reassigned, so nodes[activeNode] is always nodes[0].
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.proposedChange: Delete line 19 entirely (move declaration into the inner loop: 'int c = s[i + added];'). Remove activeEdge and activeLen declarations. Replace nodes[activeNode].FirstEdge with nodes[0].FirstEdge (3 sites) and drop activeNode, or keep activeNode as a named constant 0 if clarity is preferred.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.rationale: Eliminates a redundant memory load per outer iteration and removes dead register pressure. Hard-coding root index 0 lets Burst fold nodes[0] address computation as a constant base instead of an indexed load through a variable, shortening the dependency chain in the insertion path.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.risk: None for the dead-load removal — behavior is identical. Replacing activeNode with literal 0 is safe only because this code never descends the tree (it is a root-only suffix trie, not true Ukkonen with active points); confirm no future intent to make activeNode mutable before hard-coding. If preserving the Ukkonen skeleton for later work, keep activeNode but still remove activeEdge/activeLen which are unambiguously dead.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.summary: Per-character edge lookup is an O(alphabet/degree) linear linked-list scan; the root node accumulates one edge per distinct starting character, making total build O(n * sigma) worst case.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.currentCost: Inner loop lines 26-30 walks nodes[0].FirstEdge -> Next chain comparing Char==c. Since every insertion adds an edge off root, the root fan-out grows up to sigma (distinct chars). Each of the n outer steps scans this list, giving O(n*sigma) and a long pointer-chasing dependency chain (each Next load depends on the previous).
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.proposedChange: If the input alphabet is a small bounded range (e.g. mapped to [0,K)), replace the per-node edge linked list with a direct child index table: a K-wide int* children block indexed by char, giving O(1) child lookup. Lookup becomes children[node*K + c] != -1 — branchless, no pointer chasing. Allocate via stackalloc/caller buffer to stay unmanaged.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.rationale: Converts the inner O(degree) scan into a single indexed load, removing the serial Next-chain dependency that stalls the pipeline, and drops asymptotic build cost from O(n*sigma) to O(n*K) with K a compile-time-friendly constant. For DNA/ASCII workloads this is a large constant-factor and latency win.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.risk: Only valid when sigma is small and bounded (otherwise the K-wide table blows up RAM). For arbitrary 32-bit int chars this is infeasible — keep the linked list but consider sorting/hashing edges. Requires caller to provide alphabet bound K; changes the API/buffer-sizing contract, so gate behind a documented precondition.

src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.summary: Hot leaf is fine for Burst but the method lacks [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] hints and the inner Char-match break could be hoisted; node Len/Link writes are dead-store candidates.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.currentCost: nodes[newNode].Len = len - i and nodes[newNode].Link = 0 are written on every insertion. Link is never read in this file (root-only trie has no suffix links used). Len = len-i is also unread here. These are stores Burst cannot elide because the buffers are externally visible through pointers.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.proposedChange: If Node.Link/Len are not consumed by downstream queries, drop them from Node (mirror of the Edge change), shrinking Node from 16 to 8 bytes and removing 2 stores/insertion. Keep Start and FirstEdge which are load-bearing for tree structure.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.rationale: Smaller Node struct improves node-array cache density and removes dead stores in the insertion hot path. Node array halves in size if both fields go.
src/IAFahim.String.SuffixTree/SuffixTree.risk: Node.Start/Len/Link are public and may be the public substring-decoding contract (Start+Len describe the suffix span; Link supports future Ukkonen). Removing them is only safe if no consumer reads them. Lower confidence than the Edge.Min/Max case because Start/Len are the natural substring accessor. Verify external usage before removing; default to keeping if a public tree-query API depends on them.

src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.summary: The overflow/non-overflow if/else branches are byte-for-byte identical, and the per-length limit loop re-multiplies the alphabet power that FindMissing immediately recomputes.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.currentCost: Both branches of the if (overflow || limit > len) statement call FindMissing with the exact same arguments and the same return logic, so the branch and its dead computation are pure overhead. FindMissing then recomputes limit = alphabetSize^subLen from scratch each call (a full subLen-iteration multiply loop) duplicating the work the outer loop just did to detect overflow.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.proposedChange: Collapse the if/else into a single block: compute limit incrementally once (carry it across subLen iterations as runningLimit *= alphabetSize), pass the already-computed limit into FindMissing instead of recomputing it inside, and call FindMissing exactly once per subLen. Remove the dead 'overflow' bool entirely since both paths are identical.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.rationale: Eliminates a redundant branch and the inner subLen-length multiply loop inside FindMissing (called once per length). Passing the precomputed limit removes O(subLen) work per FindMissing invocation. Code size and instruction count drop with no behavioral change.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.risk: None for behavior: the two branches are provably identical so collapsing is semantics-preserving. Passing limit in requires FindMissing to keep its same seen[]-reset and scan loops; ensure limit type stays long to match current overflow semantics.

src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.summary: Inner hash loop recomputes the full subLen-length polynomial hash for every window position instead of using a rolling hash.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.currentCost: For each of (len - subLen + 1) start positions it runs a subLen-iteration loop computing hash = hash*alphabetSize + val, i.e. O(len*subLen) multiply-adds plus a bounds check per char.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.proposedChange: Maintain a rolling base power highPow = alphabetSize^(subLen-1) and slide the window: on advancing i, subtract s[i-1]*highPow and multiply by alphabetSize then add the new char, tracking a count of out-of-range chars in the current window to preserve the 'valid' gate. Falls back to recompute only when a window contains an out-of-alphabet char.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.rationale: Reduces the seen-marking pass from O(len*subLen) to O(len) amortized multiply-adds, a subLen-factor reduction. subLen grows with input so this is a real asymptotic improvement on the dominant pass.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.risk: Must replicate the exact 'valid' semantics: a window is only marked when ALL chars are in [0,alphabetSize). Track inrange-char count in the window; only mark seen when count==subLen. Subtraction term must use the same alphabetSize base and long arithmetic to avoid overflow for large subLen.

src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.summary: nextOcc index expressions recompute (long)i * alphabetSize repeatedly; the row base can be hoisted.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.currentCost: In the backward fill and DP loops, each access computes (long)i * alphabetSize + c with a 64-bit multiply per inner-loop iteration (alphabetSize iterations per i).
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long rowBase = (long)i * alphabetSize (and (long)(i+1)*alphabetSize) outside the c-loop, then index nextOcc[rowBase + c]. Same for the DP path-reconstruction accesses.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.rationale: Removes one 64-bit multiply per inner iteration, turning it into a single add. Over alphabetSize*len iterations this is a measurable constant-factor win and shortens the dependency chain feeding the load.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.risk: None; pure strength reduction of an invariant subexpression. Keep long type to preserve large-index addressing.

src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.summary: DP fill recomputes row-base index products i*cols and (i-1)*cols repeatedly in the inner loop.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.currentCost: Inner j-loop computes dp[i*cols+j], dp[(i-1)*cols+j], dp[i*cols+(j-1)], dp[(i-1)*cols+(j-1)] each with a multiply i*cols or (i-1)*cols per iteration: ~3-4 multiplies per cell over aLen*bLen cells.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.proposedChange: Hoist int rowBase = i*cols and int prevRowBase = (i-1)*cols before the j-loop; index as dp[rowBase+j], dp[prevRowBase+j], etc. Optionally keep a running pointer int* row = dp + rowBase; int* prevRow = dp + prevRowBase.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.rationale: Removes the per-cell multiply, replacing it with additions/index offsets and shortening the address-generation dependency chain. Over O(aLen*bLen) cells this is a clear constant-factor win and helps Burst vectorize the row scan.
src/IAFahim.String/Enumeration.cs.risk: None; pure strength reduction of loop-invariant subexpressions. Same applies to the traceback's dp[(idxA-1)*cols+idxB] accesses (minor, traceback is O(len)).

src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.summary: r[j] is a 0/1 random bit, so the three matrix-vector products do a full multiply+mod per element when they should conditionally add only when r[j]==1.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.currentCost: Each of the three i,j double loops does b[..]*r[j] then a %mod every inner iteration: O(3*n^2) multiplies and O(3*n^2) modulo operations per Freivalds iteration. The mod after every accumulation is the dominant cost (division is ~20-40 cycles).
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.proposedChange: Since r[j] in {0,1}: for the b*r and c*r products, branch 'if (r[j] != 0) sum += matrix[..];' and take a single % mod only when sum could overflow (or accumulate in unsigned/128-bit and mod once per row). For a*br, br[j] is already reduced < mod, so still need the product, but the modulo can be deferred: accumulate into an unchecked long/Int128 and reduce once per row if mod*mod*n fits, else reduce periodically.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.rationale: Replaces n^2 multiplies+mods in two of three products with conditional adds (no multiply, no per-element mod). For the third, deferring mod cuts division count from n^2 to n per iteration. Division elimination is the single biggest cycle win here.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.risk: Deferring mod requires guaranteeing no overflow: matrix entries and br are < mod (~1e9); sum of n such products fits in long only if mod*mod*n < 2^63, i.e. n*1e18 < 9.2e18 => n<=9. For larger n, reduce every K accumulations where K*mod^2 < 2^63. The r[j]==1 conditional-add is exactly equivalent to multiplying by the 0/1 bit, fully semantics-preserving.

src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.summary: The rolling-hash update computes text[i]*pPow%mod and a final %mod with an extra +mod normalization every shift; the modulo count can be reduced.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.currentCost: Per window shift: two %mod operations plus a +mod correction. textHash = (textHash - text[i]*pPow%mod + mod) % mod then (textHash*p + text[i+patternLen]) % mod.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.proposedChange: Combine into fewer reductions: keep textHash in [0,mod); compute removal = text[i]*pPow % mod once, then textHash = (textHash + mod - removal) % mod is needed, but the subsequent multiply-add can fold its reduction. Alternatively precompute pPowModded once (already done) and use Int128/unchecked mul to avoid the intermediate %mod on text[i]*pPow when text[i]<256 and pPow<mod (product < 256*1e9 < 2^63, so text[i]*pPow never overflows long and the inner %mod is unnecessary before the outer subtraction's %mod).
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.rationale: text[i] <= 255 and pPow < mod < 2^30, so text[i]*pPow < 2^38, far below 2^63 — the inner '%mod' on that product is redundant for overflow safety and only needed to keep the subtraction non-negative, which the +mod already guards after one combined reduction. Saves one division per shift.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.risk: Must ensure (textHash - text[i]*pPow) stays representable: textHash<mod~2^30, text[i]*pPow<2^38, so the difference fits in long; add mod*ceil to keep non-negative before the single %mod. Verify the final value equals the original modular result — straightforward since all intermediates are exact.

src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.summary: Binary-lifting index expressions recompute (long)x * logV per access in the hot LCA query loop.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.currentCost: The non-tree-edge loop does, for each of logV levels, multiple up[(long)x*logV+j] and maxEdge[(long)x*logV+j] loads, each recomputing a 64-bit multiply by logV. This is the dominant verification cost: O(numEdges * logV) with ~3-4 multiplies per level.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.proposedChange: Hoist long xBase = (long)x*logV and yBase = (long)y*logV at the top of each level's body (recomputed only when x/y advance), or better, index by row pointers: long* maxRowX = maxEdge + (long)x*logV. Update the base only when x is reassigned via up[]. Same for the binary-lifting table-fill double loop (hoist (long)i*logV and (long)anc*logV).
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.rationale: Eliminates repeated 64-bit multiplies in the innermost lifting loop, replacing index math with a single add per access. Shortens the load-address dependency chain feeding the memory access.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.risk: x and y change inside the loop (x = up[...]); the hoisted base must be recomputed at exactly those reassignment points. Keep long arithmetic for addressing safety.

src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.summary: logV is computed via a shift loop but overshoots by one, sizing binary-lifting tables larger than necessary; also the loop is a trivial closed form.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.currentCost: while ((1<<logV)<=numVertices) logV++ starting at logV=1 yields ceil(log2(numVertices))+1 levels, one more than the LCA needs, inflating the up/maxEdge working set and the table-fill loop by a full pass over numVertices.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.proposedChange: Compute logV directly: int logV = 32 - LeadingZeroCount((uint)numVertices) (or keep the loop but start tighter). Verify whether callers size up/maxEdge to this logV; if the extra level is load-bearing for caller buffer sizing, leave as-is but document. The table-fill and per-edge query loops both iterate logV, so trimming one level removes O(numVertices) fill work and one lifting iteration per edge.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.rationale: One fewer level reduces the binary-lifting table size (RAM/cache) and trims one iteration from every per-edge query loop and the O(numVertices*logV) fill. lzcnt is branchless vs the shift loop.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.risk: Higher risk: callers allocate up/maxEdge sized to whatever logV this routine implies. Changing logV changes the required buffer size and the table stride, so this is only safe if the stride is internal. Flagged low-impact/needs-caller-audit; the safe sub-win is just the lzcnt strength reduction of the count loop.

src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.summary: NextLong uses % diff which is a division; for the Schwartz-Zippel hot path mod is constant per call site but diff varies.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.currentCost: min + (val % diff) does a 64-bit modulo per call. In SchwartzZippelTest this runs numVariables*iterations times.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.proposedChange: Leave as-is unless diff is known power-of-two; document that callers wanting many draws from the same range should hoist a precomputed reciprocal/mask. No safe generic change without changing the value distribution.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.rationale: Modulo reduction here is inherent to uniform sampling; replacing with mask only valid for power-of-two diff which would change observable random values otherwise.
src/IAFahim.String/Probabilistic.cs.risk: Rejected as a generic change: any reciprocal-multiply or masking alters the exact output sequence (observable, since seed is fixed and deterministic). Only note it; do not apply.

src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.summary: The adjacency build does a % numVertices per edge even though (u*k+i) is monotonic and wraps at most once per row.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.currentCost: Inner loop computes adj[u*k+i] = (u*k+i) % numVertices for every edge: numVertices*k modulo operations. Since numVertices = k^(n-1), u*k+i ranges in [0, k^n), and (u*k+i) % k^(n-1) is exactly the low n-1 digits.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.proposedChange: Note that v = (u*k+i) % numVertices = (u*k+i) - (((u*k+i)/numVertices))*numVertices, and since u<numVertices, u*k+i < numVertices*k, the quotient is in [0,k). Precompute base = u*k; for each i the value (base+i) wraps when it reaches a multiple of numVertices. Replace the per-edge division with an incremented counter v that increments alongside and is reset by subtracting numVertices when it reaches it (single compare+conditional-subtract instead of division).
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.rationale: Replaces numVertices*k divisions with a running counter and one branch (or branchless conditional subtract) per edge. For DeBruijn where numVertices grows exponentially this removes the dominant per-edge division cost.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.risk: Must reset the running v=0 at the start of each u-row correctly and handle the wrap: since base+i increases by 1 each inner step and numVertices is the modulus, conditional subtract when v==numVertices is exact. Use unsigned-safe compare; all values non-negative so no signed-% pitfall.

src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.summary: Same per-edge % numVertices in the Hierholzer loop as GraphBuild, plus numVertices is recomputed by a multiply loop already computed by GraphBuild's caller.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.currentCost: Inner step v = (u*k + nextEdge) % numVertices runs once per edge traversal (numEdges times) with a 64-bit modulo. numVertices is also recomputed via an n-1 iteration multiply loop at entry.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.proposedChange: Since nextEdge = edgeIdx[u] is in [0,k) and u in [0,numVertices), u*k+nextEdge < numVertices*k, so v = (u*k+nextEdge) - (u*k+nextEdge >= numVertices ? ... ). The quotient is in [0,k); compute v with a single division-free form: v = (u*k+nextEdge); while loop unnecessary — at most quotient<k so a multiply by k could overflow. Simpler: precompute numVertices via pow with exponentiation-by-squaring or accept the multiply loop (cheap, runs once). Focus: replace per-edge % with the standard De Bruijn successor (u % (numVertices/k))*k ... — but cleanest safe win is hoisting and noting numVertices is small. Recommend leaving % if numVertices not power-of-k-friendly; primary win is replacing the modulo with the identity v = (u*k+nextEdge) - numVertices*((u*k+nextEdge)/numVertices) only if a cheaper successor exists.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.rationale: The modulo is the hottest op in Hierholzer. A De Bruijn successor edge can be computed as nextVertex = (u * k + symbol) mod k^(n-1); when k is a power of two this is a mask/shift. Strength-reduce to shift/mask in the common k=2 (binary De Bruijn) case.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.risk: Power-of-two specialization only valid when k is a power of two (then % numVertices == & (numVertices-1) since numVertices=k^(n-1) is also a power of two and non-negative operands). Guard with a k-is-power-of-two check or a separate Run path; for general k keep the division. Signed operands are all non-negative so &-mask is exact under the guard.

src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.summary: Dead 'allocated'/branch structure: the stackalloc-vs-AllocHGlobal split with a 1024 threshold mixes heap allocation into an otherwise pointer-pure API and adds a try/finally on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.currentCost: The 1024-element threshold triggers Marshal.AllocHGlobal (managed interop, not Burst-friendly) and wraps the whole traversal in try/finally, which Burst cannot compile and which defeats the no-exceptions house rule on the hot path.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.proposedChange: Follow the house pattern used elsewhere (callers pass pre-sized buffers): take int* stack as a caller-provided parameter sized numEdges+1, removing the AllocHGlobal/try/finally entirely. This makes the method Burst-compilable and allocation-free, matching the rest of the module's pointer-buffer convention.
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.rationale: Marshal.AllocHGlobal and try/finally are not Burst-compatible and introduce managed interop + exception scaffolding on the hot path. Moving the buffer to a caller parameter restores purity, removes runtime allocation, and matches the established API style (e.g. SuffixArrayBuild-style caller buffers).
src/IAFahim.String/DeBruijn.cs.risk: API change: adds a parameter, so callers must supply the buffer (numEdges+1 ints). This is a signature break but aligns with house constraints (no heap alloc, no exceptions). Behavior of the traversal is unchanged.

src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.summary: Recursive stackalloc inside the recursion: each XmlTreeHash frame stackallocs node.ChildCount uints, so deep/wide trees can blow the stack and Burst dislikes per-frame variable stackalloc.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.currentCost: uint* tempHashes = stackalloc uint[node.ChildCount] executes on every recursive call; stack usage is sum of childCounts along the deepest path, unbounded by tree shape. Burst's stack frame for recursive stackalloc is hard to bound.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.proposedChange: Reuse the caller-provided calculatedHashes buffer (already O(nodeCount)) as the scratch for child hashes instead of a fresh per-frame stackalloc: gather child hashes by reading calculatedHashes[childIdx] (each child already wrote its hash before returning), and sort indices/hashes using a small region of a single shared scratch buffer passed in once. This removes recursion-local stackalloc.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.rationale: Eliminates O(depth * width) cumulative stack growth and per-frame stackalloc, making stack usage bounded and Burst-friendly. Since each child already stores its hash in calculatedHashes, the temp array is redundant — read from there.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.risk: Insertion sort needs a mutable scratch region; reusing calculatedHashes in place would corrupt stored hashes, so a single caller-provided scratch buffer of max-childCount is needed. The canonical (sorted) ordering of child hashes must be preserved exactly to keep the same output hash.

src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.summary: FNV multiply constant is fine, but the tree-hash insertion sort is O(childCount^2) which dominates for high-fan-out nodes.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.currentCost: Both XmlTreeHash and JsonCanonicalHash sort children with insertion sort: O(childCount^2) comparisons/moves per node. For wide nodes (large ChildCount) this is the bottleneck.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.proposedChange: For uint key sorting in XmlTreeHash, use an in-place radix/counting sort over the 32-bit keys (4 passes of 8-bit buckets) when ChildCount exceeds a small threshold (e.g. 32); keep insertion sort below it. JsonCanonicalHash sorts ChildInfo by KeyHash (int) — same radix approach on the key, carrying the HashVal payload.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.rationale: Drops the per-node sort from O(w^2) to O(w) for wide nodes, an asymptotic win on fan-out-heavy XML/JSON. Insertion sort retained for small w where its low constant wins.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.risk: Radix sort needs a scratch buffer (caller-provided, per house rules) and a stable ordering to match insertion sort's result for equal keys; FNV folding of equal hashes is order-independent for duplicates so stability is not observable, but verify equal-key handling produces identical final folded hash. Threshold must be tuned; below it keep current path to avoid regressions.

src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.summary: ChildInfo struct stores KeyHash redundantly when it equals elements[childIdx].KeyHash already in memory; the gather duplicates data only to sort.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.currentCost: stackalloc ChildInfo[elem.ChildCount] (8 bytes each) duplicates each child's KeyHash and computed HashVal per frame, recursively, growing stack by 8*childCount per level.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.proposedChange: Sort child indices (a single int per child) by elements[childIdx].KeyHash rather than copying KeyHash+HashVal into a parallel struct array, reading KeyHash via the already-resident elements[] and HashVal via calculatedHashes[childIdx]. This halves scratch footprint and reuses existing storage.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.rationale: Reduces per-frame scratch from 8 bytes/child to 4 bytes/child and avoids duplicating data already present in elements[] and calculatedHashes[], shrinking the recursive stack working set and cache pressure.
src/IAFahim.String/SpecialStructures.cs.risk: Sorting indices by an indirect key adds an indirection per comparison (load elements[idx].KeyHash); for small fan-out the extra load may offset the savings. The final fold order must remain by ascending KeyHash exactly as today. Type==1 (object) sorts; Type other (array) preserves order — must keep that distinction.

src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.summary: Replace the two per-iteration `% len` modulo operations (integer divisions) with subtraction-based wraparound.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.currentCost: Each loop iteration computes `s[(i + k) % len]` and `s[(j + k) % len]`. `len` is a runtime value (not a compile-time power of two), so each `%` is a full hardware integer division. Booth's/duval's min-cyclic-shift loop runs O(len) iterations, so this is 2 divisions per hot iteration — divisions are 20-40+ cycles each on mobile ARM and not pipelined well.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.proposedChange: Index can be reduced by subtraction rather than modulo because `i < len`, `j < len`, and `k < len` are loop invariants, so `i + k` and `j + k` are each strictly less than `2*len`. Compute e.g. `int ik = i + k; if (ik >= len) ik -= len;` and likewise `int jk = j + k; if (jk >= len) jk -= len;`, then index `s[ik]` / `s[jk]`. A single conditional subtraction (or branchless `ik - (len & -(ik >= len ? 1 : 0))`) replaces each division.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.rationale: `a + b < 2*len` with `0 <= a,b < len` means `(a+b) % len` equals `(a+b) - len` when `a+b >= len`, else `a+b`. One compare + conditional subtract (~1-3 cycles, branch-predictable since the wrap is infrequent within a run) replaces a 20-40 cycle division, cutting the dominant cost of the inner loop roughly in half.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.risk: Correctness depends on the invariants `i<len`, `j<len`, `k<len` which are exactly the loop guard `while (i < len && j < len && k < len)`. Since the indexing only happens inside that guarded body, `i+k < 2*len` and `j+k < 2*len` always hold, so a single subtraction is provably equivalent to `% len`. No signed-negative concern: all of i,j,k are non-negative. Pure constant-factor, no semantic change.

src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.summary: MinPeriod.Run is a pure forwarding wrapper over StringPeriod.Run; mark it AggressiveInlining (or document it as an alias) so the call is elided.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.currentCost: `MinPeriod.Run` only does `return StringPeriod.Run(s, len);`. Under Burst/IL2CPP the JIT/AOT will usually inline a trivial forwarder, but it is not guaranteed, leaving a redundant call frame and an extra symbol that duplicates intent.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.proposedChange: Add `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` to `MinPeriod.Run` (the `System.Runtime.CompilerServices` using is already present) to force the forward to collapse, or consolidate to a single public name to remove the duplicate API surface.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.rationale: Guarantees zero call-frame overhead for the alias and removes ambiguity about which entry point is canonical, with no behavior change.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.risk: None functionally — identical inputs/outputs. Only an API-surface/discoverability consideration: if both names are intentionally public for clarity, keep both but inline the wrapper.

src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.summary: The KMP prefix-function build is duplicated verbatim across three classes; factor it into one AggressiveInlining helper to avoid divergent maintenance and enable a single optimization point.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.currentCost: The identical loop `for (int i=1,j=0; i<len; i++){ while(j>0 && s[i]!=s[j]) j=fail[j-1]; if(s[i]==s[j]) j++; fail[i]=j; }` appears three times (StringPeriod lines 134-139, Borders 159-164, CountOccurrences 184-189). Triplicated code triples the surface for bugs and means any future micro-opt (e.g. caching `s[j]`) must be applied three times.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.proposedChange: Extract `static void BuildFailure(byte* s, int len, int* fail)` marked `[MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)]` and call it from all three sites. This is a refactor only; with AggressiveInlining the generated code for each caller is unchanged.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.rationale: DRY without cost: inlining keeps the hot loop in-place per caller while collapsing three copies into one canonical, individually-optimizable definition. Lowers complexity/maintenance risk at zero runtime cost.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.risk: Must keep the helper AggressiveInlining and pointer-typed so Burst still vectorizes/inlines exactly as today; otherwise a non-inlined call could add overhead. Semantics identical since the code is copied verbatim.

src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.summary: In the KMP failure-build inner loop, cache `s[i]` once per outer iteration to cut repeated loads in the while/if comparisons.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.currentCost: Inside the build loop, `s[i]` is re-read in both `while (j>0 && s[i]!=s[j])` and `if (s[i]==s[j])`. `s` is a raw pointer the compiler cannot prove is alias-free against the `fail`/`radii` writes, so each `s[i]` may be reloaded from memory rather than kept in a register.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.proposedChange: Hoist `byte ci = s[i];` at the top of the outer loop body and compare `ci != s[j]` / `ci == s[j]`. Same for the matching loops in CountOccurrences (`byte ti = text[i];`).
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.rationale: Removes a potential redundant memory load per iteration (the compiler may not hoist it due to pointer-aliasing uncertainty between `s` and `fail`). Saves a load and shortens the dependency chain in the tightest string-processing loops.
src/IAFahim.String/StringCore.cs.risk: Provably equivalent: `s[i]` does not change within one outer iteration (the body writes only to `fail[i]`/`radii`/output, never to `s`). No aliasing hazard since `s` is read-only by contract. Pure micro-opt.

src/IAFahim.Unique/UniqueInts.cs.summary: Eliminate redundant self-stores while no duplicate has been seen yet (the common all-unique case).
src/IAFahim.Unique/UniqueInts.cs.currentCost: On every iteration that keeps an element, `ptr[dst++] = ptr[i]` executes a store. When the input has no (or few) duplicates, dst==i for the whole prefix, so the loop writes each element back onto itself — len-1 wasted stores plus the dependency on dst++ for an array that is already correct.
src/IAFahim.Unique/UniqueInts.cs.proposedChange: Split into two phases. Phase 1: scan with `for (i=1; i<len && ptr[i]!=ptr[i-1]; i++) {}` doing no stores; this advances over the already-unique prefix. Then set `dst=i`. Phase 2: continue from i with the existing compact loop comparing against ptr[dst-1] (the last kept value) instead of ptr[i-1]. For fully-unique input this does zero stores and returns len; for input with duplicates it matches current behavior.
src/IAFahim.Unique/UniqueInts.cs.rationale: Removes len-1 redundant memory stores on the dominant all-unique path, and on the mixed path removes stores for the leading unique run.
